# Rigveda Samhita, Volume 10 — English Translation

**Source:** `Rig_Vol10.pdf` (728 PDF pages; Kannada commentary of 1950 — Sāyaṇa's Sanskrit bhāṣya with the Kannada explanation of H. P. Venkata Rao; "Bhāga 10", ಭಾಗ ೧೦).
**Covers:** Maṇḍala 1, **Sūktas 122–136**, beginning with the First Adhyāya of the Second Aṣṭaka ("ಎರಡನೆಯ ಅಷ್ಟಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಮೊದಲನೆಯ ಅಧ್ಯಾಯವು"), per the Pīṭhike ("ಪ್ರಥಮಮಂಡಲದ ೧೨೨-೧೩೬ ಸೂಕ್ತಗಳಿವೆ"); the first sūkta is 122 (*pra vaḥ pāntam*), on printed p. 2 (PDF 23). **Reference aids:** the reader's Google-Docs OCR of printed pp. 4–60 (numerals only; words are not used) and the digit-glyph prototype `publish/tools/numeral_pass/glyphs.py`.

## Pīṭhike (Preface) — Kannada, printed pp. i–ix

*(PDF 7–15; printed page = PDF − 6 here, since the Pīṭhike has its own roman numbering. Small-type Sanskrit and numerals in this preface are very small; doubtful letters and numbers are marked `[?]`. The reader's Google-Docs OCR was used only as a cross-check on numerals, never for words.)*

### Printed p. i  (PDF 7)

In this part of the Ṛksaṃhitā there are the Sūktas of Maṇḍala 1, **122–136** (as printed "೧೨೨-೧೩೬"). Of these, Sūktas 122–126 have as their seer Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija, and Sūktas 127–136 have as their seer Parucchepa Daivodāsi.

About the seer Kakṣīvān, the Bṛhaddevatā and other works say this: a king named Kaliṅga had no children. He was old and unable to beget a son. At that time the seer Dīrghatamas, son of Ucathya, came near the king, and the king asked him to beget a son on his behalf, since he had none, in his royal wife. In earlier times, when people had no children for some reason, there was the custom of obtaining sons for the continuance of the line from a qualified Brāhmaṇa; this is described clearly in the Purāṇas and the Mahābhārata. The seer agreed to the king's request, and the king told his chief queen to go to the seer. The queen, being ashamed to have intercourse with a seer who was old and ugly, did not wish it, and in her place she adorned her maidservant named Uśik beautifully with her own clothes and ornaments and sent her to the seer. When the woman Uśik came to him, the seer, knowing that she was a maidservant and not the queen, sprinkled her with mantra-consecrated water, made her pure like a wife, and then had intercourse with her. The son born to Uśik by that seer is the seer Kakṣīvān. It is said of him that he is extremely famous among those who perform sacrificial rites:

> एवं वै पर आट्णारः कक्षीवाँ औशिजो वीतहव्यः श्रायसस्त्रसदस्युः पौरुकुत्स्नः प्रजाकामा अचिन्तयत ॥

> *evaṃ vai para āṭṇāraḥ kakṣīvā~ auśijo vītahavyaḥ śrāyasastrasadasyuḥ paurukutsnaḥ prajākāmā acintayata ‖*

(Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5-6-5-3, as printed "೫-೬-೫-೩"; the same reference is printed clearly on p. 3 and the reader's OCR reads it there.) This is said in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda. Therefore this seer is extremely famous both in composing mantras and among those who perform sacrificial rites. This seer is the seer of the Sūktas 116–125 of Maṇḍala 1 of the Ṛgveda (in all 146 ṛks), of ṛks 1–5 of Sūkta 126 (5 ṛks), and of Sūkta 74 of Maṇḍala 9 (9 ṛks), altogether 160 ṛks (as printed: "೧೧೬-೧೨೫ … ಒಟ್ಟು ೧೪೬ … ೧೨೬ … ೧-೫ … ೫ … ೭೪ … ೯ … ಒಟ್ಟು ೧೬೦"). The name of this seer occurs in the following ṛks of the Ṛgveda (as printed, in small type; the numbers were checked against the reader's OCR, which reads the first two and the last four clearly): Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-126-2; 1-123-3; … eight further references in the middle of the list whose numerals the OCR garbles and that I cannot read reliably from the small type `[?]` (the OCR gives them as "L-IL-N; 2-F-00; nn-394-00; 7-002-2; 0-810-09; n-nn2; F-29-0; 0-03L-4" — letter-shaped substitutes for digits, kept here only as a record); … 1-18-1; 1-112-11; 10-61-16; 10-143-1 — "these ṛks in which it occurs".

### Printed p. ii  (PDF 8)

In the nineteenth Anuvāka of the first Maṇḍala there are the 7 Sūktas from 127 to 133; in the next Anuvāka, the twentieth, there are the Sūktas from 134 to 139 (as printed). For the 13 Sūktas that result from these two Anuvākas, the seer is "Parucchepo Daivodāsiḥ", that is, Parucchepa, son of Divodāsa. We have told about Divodāsa earlier. Divodāsa, or Divodāsa Atithigva, was a king renowned in very ancient (Vedic) times, son of Vadhryaśva and father of Sudāsa. His name occurs in many places in the Ṛgveda. It is said in various places that his chief enemy was Śambara or Dāsa, the leader of the forest people who lived in the hills and mountains. No Sūktas seen by Divodāsa himself occur anywhere in the Ṛgveda; therefore modern scholars differ on whether his son, the seer Parucchepa, is the seer of these Sūktas. Be that as it may, according to the Anukramaṇikā — by the verse *agnim ekādaśa parucchepo daivodāsir āgneyaṃ tu pārucchepaṃ sarvam atyaṣṭi tv atidhṛtiḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ* [as printed; wording not individually verified] — Parucchepa is declared the seer of the 13 Sūktas mentioned above (127–139). Yāska says in his Nirukta:

> परुच्छेप ऋषिः । पर्ववच्छेपः परुषिपरुषि शेपोऽस्येति वा ।

> *parucchepa ṛṣiḥ | parvavacchepaḥ paruṣiparuṣi śepo 'syeti vā |*

(Nirukta 10-42, as printed; the reader's OCR reads it clearly.) That is, he is called so because "he grew up in comfort and was well built in all his joints" — this is the main intention; the etymology of the word *parucchepa* is not so important here. This seer's story is also told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (adhyāya 22, khaṇḍa 5-6, as printed and as read by the OCR) and in the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa (13-4-5, as printed and as read by the OCR). In these 13 Sūktas seen by Parucchepa there are in all 100 ṛks [?: as printed "೧೦೦"]. This seer's son Anānata Pārucchepi is the seer of 3 ṛks of Sūkta 111 of Maṇḍala 9. All these ṛks have one special distinguishing feature: they are in metres named Atyaṣṭi, Atiśakvarī and Atidhṛti. Sūkta 127 is in Atiśakvarī; the remaining Sūktas (except for some ṛks) are composed in Atyaṣṭi. This kind of metre has 7 pādas and in all 68 syllables; in some places one or two syllables more or less are also found. We have described these metres, with their characteristics and examples, in detail in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 1, pp. 221–231. Another special feature of the ṛks seen by Parucchepa is told by Yāska:

> अभ्यासे भूयांसमर्थं मन्यन्ते यथाहो दर्शनीयाहो दर्शनीयेति ।
> तत्परुच्छेपस्य शीलम् ॥

> *abhyāse bhūyāṃsamarthaṃ manyante yathāho darśanīyāho darśanīyeti |*
> *tatparucchepasya śīlam ‖*

(Nirukta 10-42, the same reference again.)

### Printed p. iii  (PDF 9)

That is, in the ṛks seen by this seer repetition (*abhyāsa*, twofold utterance) is especially to be seen. Ordinarily, in the ṛks of metres such as Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh and Jagatī there are only two parts, a first half and a second half. But in the ṛks seen by Parucchepa, in Atyaṣṭi and the like, there are three halves (*ardhas*); in the first and third halves, in the final part of each, one or two words are repeated again and again, like a refrain. For example:

> अग्निं होतारं मन्ये दास्वन्तं वसुं सूनुं सहसो जादवेदसं विप्रं न जातवेदसम् ।

> *agniṃ hotāraṃ manye dāsvantaṃ vasuṃ sūnuṃ sahaso jādavedasaṃ vipraṃ na jātavedasam |*

(printed *jādavedasaṃ* in the first place, *jātavedasaṃ* in the second [sic?]). In this ṛk the word *jātavedasam* is repeated twice; between the repetitions are the words *vipraṃ na*. This repeated word always stands at the end of the sentence.

> निष्ठमानो यमुते नायते धन्वासहा नायते ।

> *niṣṭhamāno yamute nāyate dhanvāsahā nāyate |*

[printed in small type; the first words are read doubtfully, `[?]`]. In this ṛk the words *nāyate* are repeated twice, and between them stands the word *dhanvāsahā*. Yāska explains this matter of repetition by saying "*abhyāse bhūyāṃsam arthaṃ manyante yathāho darśanīyāho darśanīyeti*" and giving its meaning. The commentators on the Nirukta say of this sentence:

> अभ्यासे भूयांसमर्थं मन्यन्ते । शब्दाभ्यासे यत्रान्यो विशेषो नास्ति तत्रैवं विशेषमाचार्या मन्त्रार्थसतत्त्वविदो मन्यन्ते-यदुतार्थ-भूयस्त्वमिति । न हि कस्मात् स एव शब्दः पुनरभ्यस्यते । लोकेऽपि चैतद् दृष्टं शब्दाभ्यासेऽर्थभूयस्त्वमिति । यथा-अहो दर्शनीये! अहो दर्शनीये! इति । गुणातिशये हि स्त्रियाः शब्दाभ्यासः । तस्मान्मन्त्रेष्वपि तद्देवेति [?] न्याय्यम् ॥

> *abhyāse bhūyāṃsamarthaṃ manyante | śabdābhyāse yatrānyo viśeṣo nāsti tatraivaṃ viśeṣamācāryā mantrārthasatattvavido manyante-yadutārtha-bhūyastvamiti | na hi kasmāt sa eva śabdaḥ punarabhyasyate | loke 'pi caitad dṛṣṭaṃ śabdābhyāse 'rthabhūyastvamiti | yathā-aho darśanīye! aho darśanīye! iti | guṇātiśaye hi striyāḥ śabdābhyāsaḥ | tasmānmantreṣvapi taddeveti [?] nyāyyam ‖*

That is, when one word is uttered twice in a sentence, if the pair of utterances do not have two different meanings, the repetition of the word indicates an excess of meaning — that is, it is used to give prominence to the matter that was stated, or to make the matter settle well in the mind. For example, when describing a woman's beauty one says "aho darśanīye, aho darśanīye" ("oh how beautiful, oh how beautiful"). At that point the doubling of the word expresses "ah, what beauty — what beauty!" and so makes the excess of beauty plain; this is a usage in the language of the world. Likewise it should be understood here. But Sāyaṇa ordinarily explains the repeated words of these ṛks by giving them different meanings.

This doubling has another purpose too. Many ṛks of the Ṛgveda were composed so as to be suitable for singing. When songs set to *rāga* and so on are sung …

### Printed p. iv  (PDF 10)

… the refrain and the pallavi and anupallavi are sung again and again, which is a well-known thing to all in the world. Therefore these ṛks, too, must have been composed with the aim of being sung in many ṛks so as to be audible clearly. For that reason it is also said in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa that these Pārucchepa mantras are to be used in the recitation of the Śastra mantras. From this point of view, a large part of the Sāmaveda consists of ṛks of the Ṛgveda.

When one understands Vedic mantras in their meaning and recites or sings them with devotion and faith, with the accents, both the reciter and the listeners hearing the Vedic sound have a joy that cannot be put into words — a matter that has come within the experience of many. Some modern scholars, such as Westerners, look at the Vedic mantras only from the point of view of the primacy of meaning, and so they have no chance to learn the full beauty of the Vedic mantras; nor do they try. Some say that although these ṛks are in metre there are many omissions and violations of grammar, and that they belong to "Prauḍha" (mature, ornate) poetry. But their view is not acceptable. For at that time there was no written language. Everything had to be learned by heart. Therefore it is natural that more attention was given to pronunciation and audibility. And while writing was not known and grammar was little developed, it is natural that the words and idioms in use at that time were used. And we must not forget that the grammars composed by Pāṇini and others were composed on the basis of Vedic words. Grammar comes from language, not language from grammar. Language is the root; grammar follows it. Therefore it is not right to apply today's grammatical rules by force to the forms of the words and so on seen in the Vedic mantras.

We have said before that many ṛks were composed from the point of view of singing; for that reason, in many places short syllables are used as long and long syllables as short; this is seen here and there. For example, in words such as *adha, gha, sma* the long syllable is in the *saṃhitā-pāṭha*; likewise, *ṛtāvṛdhā* is pronounced *ṛtavṛdhā*, and so on. In many places one or two syllables of words are lost, for example *ātmanā* is written *tmanā*, and in place of *bhāvayavyasya* one finds *bhāvyasya*. Such losses and additions are not new to modern language: when singing compositions, singers sing *kṛṣṇamūrti* as "kṛṣṇā mūrati" and *kīrti* as "kīrutī". Such omissions and additions are many; since the Vedic mantras have been handed down, taught by pure utterance alone, such slight faults (which are not really faults) are not unnatural.

### Printed p. v  (PDF 11)

That the Sūktas seen by Parucchepa belong to very ancient mantras there is no doubt on the matter. The meaning of many words and sentences in these ṛks is very obscure and unclear, and so the meaning does not fit well in many places. Most of these mantras have been included among the Śastra mantras. Their details are in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows:

> देवासुरा वा एषु लोकेषु समुयतन्त ते वै देवाः षष्ठेनैवाह्नेभ्यो लोकेभ्योऽसुरान् प्राणुदन्त तेषां यान्यन्तर्हस्तीनानि वसून्यासंस्तान्यादाय समुद्रं प्रास्यन्त [?] त एतेनैव छन्दसानुहायान्तर्हस्तीनानि वसून्यादवत [?] तद्यदेतत्पदं पुनःपदं स एवाङ्कुश आसञ्जनाय । आ द्विषतो वसु वत्त्रे निरेनमेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यो लोकेभ्यो नुदते य एवं वेद ॥

> *devāsurā vā eṣu lokeṣu samuyatanta te vai devāḥ ṣaṣṭhenaivāhnebhyo lokebhyo 'surān prāṇudanta teṣāṃ yānyantarhastīnāni vasūnyāsaṃstānyādāya samudraṃ prāsyanta [?] ta etenaiva chandasānuhāyāntarhastīnāni vasūnyādavata [?] tadyadetatpadaṃ punaḥpadaṃ sa evāṅkuśa āsañjanāya | ā dviṣato vasu vattre nirenamebhyaḥ sarvebhyo lokebhyo nudate ya evaṃ veda ‖*

(Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, as printed "೨೨-೬": Ai. Brā. 22-6.) Once the gods and the Asuras fought in these worlds. Then, on the sixth day of the sacrifice (the "dvādaśāha"), the gods drove the Asuras out of these worlds. Then the Asuras took the wealth they had in their hands and fled and threw it into the ocean. Afterwards the gods pursued the Asuras and, by the power of reciting the ṛks seen by Parucchepa, got back the wealth the Asuras had thrown into the ocean. When getting it back, the seventh pāda of the ṛks seen by Parucchepa (the pāda that is repeated, the *punaḥ-parihita* pāda) helped them. In the world, to pull from a deep place something that has fallen, people use a hook (marginal English word "hook" printed); that is natural. In the same way the seventh pāda of the ṛks seen by this seer (the pāda "*sumṛḻīko na āgahi*" and the like) draws up the wealth in the ocean and makes it come to the gods; that is the meaning. The man who, knowing this matter well, performs the rite by reciting the mantras accordingly, conquers his enemies, drives them from this world and himself gets their wealth.

The application of the ṛks seen by Parucchepa and their inner meaning are told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa in this way (Ai. Brā. 22-25, as read by the reader's OCR; I could not read it in the print):

> पारुच्छेपीरुपदधाति पूर्वयोः सवनयोः [?] पुरस्तात्स्थितयाज्यानां रोहितं वै नामैतच्छन्दो यत्पारुच्छेपमेतेन वा इन्द्रः सप्त स्वर्गाँल्लोकानरोहत् । रोहति सप्त स्वर्गाँल्लोकान्य एवं वेद । तदाहुर्यत्पञ्चपदा एव पञ्चमस्याह्नो रूपं षट्पदाः षष्ठस्याथ कस्मात्सप्तपदाः षष्ठेऽहञ्क्रि [?]-यन्त इति । षड्भिरेव पद्यैः षष्ठमहराप्नुवन्त्यपच्छिद्यैवैतदहर्यत्सप्तमं तदेव सप्तमेन पदेनाभ्यारभ्य वसन्ति वाचमेव तत्पुनरुपयन्ति सन्तत्यै ॥

> *pārucchepīrupadadhāti pūrvayoḥ savanayoḥ [?] purastātsthitayājyānāṃ rohitaṃ vai nāmaitacchando yatpārucchepametena vā indraḥ sapta svargā~llokānarohat | rohati sapta svargā~llokānya evaṃ veda | tadāhuryatpañcapadā eva pañcamasyāhno rūpaṃ ṣaṭpadāḥ ṣaṣṭhasyātha kasmātsaptapadāḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hañkri [?]-yanta iti | ṣaḍbhireva padyaiḥ ṣaṣṭhamaharāpnuvantyapacchidyaivaitadaharyatsaptamaṃ tadeva saptamena padenābhyārabhya vasanti vācameva tatpunarupayanti santatyai ‖*

The Kannada gloss then says: The ṛks seen by Parucchepa are called *rohita* ("ascending"). For by reciting these ṛks Indra ascended, at one time, to the seventh heaven. The seven heavens here are the seven divisions of heaven in the world of heaven, according to differences of excellence. The man who performs the sacrifice in this way, reciting these mantras, attains the seven heavens.

### Printed p. vi  (PDF 12)

On the sixth day of the sacrifice called "dvādaśāha" or "daśarātra", the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) and midday pressing (*mādhyandinasavana*) (*savana* means the rite of extracting the Soma from the creeper), seven priests of the group of *hotṛ* priests recite the *praiṣa*, *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* mantras. That is, first one Pārucchepa ṛk is to be recited, and then one *prasthita-yājyā* mantra is to be recited. In this connection the Pārucchepa mantras to be recited are:

> नृषन्निन्द्र वृषपाणास इन्दवः (ऋ. सं. १-१३९-६)

> *nṛṣannindra vṛṣapāṇāsa indavaḥ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-139-6)*

— and from this ṛk, [the ṛks] up to the last ṛk of this Sūkta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-139-11, as printed); and

> पिबा सोममिन्द्र सुवानमद्रिभिः (ऋ. सं. १-१३०-२)

> *pibā somamindra suvānamadribhiḥ (ṛ. saṃ. 1-130-2)*

— and from this ṛk, [the ṛks] up to the last ṛk of this Sūkta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-10, as printed; the Sūkta numbers 139 and 130 were read with the help of the reader's OCR, since the image's "9" and "4" are easily confused). These ṛks are to be recited one by one. The ṛks seen by Parucchepa have the name *rohita* ("ascending"). For by reciting these ṛks Indra ascended to the seventh heaven at one time or another. Seven heavens here are the seven divisions of heaven, in the world of heaven, by differences of excellence. The man who in this way recites these mantras and performs the sacrifice will also attain the seven heavens.

Here there is one special matter. On the fifth day of this sacrifice it is the custom to recite at the savana-time the ṛks of five pādas (the *paṅkti* metre). So on the sixth day ṛks with six pādas have to be recited. Yet why are the Pārucchepa ṛks, which have seven pādas, recited on that day? — it is said that on all six days, with the six pādas of the ṛk, one crosses the six heavens, and with the seventh pāda one attains the seventh heaven, *saptama-svarga*. For since the seventh pāda is a repetition of the ṛk, it is reckoned, within the ṛk, as six pādas. To the seventh pāda, as it is of excellent praise, it is said that by reciting it one may obtain the best seventh heaven; that is the main intention.

Regarding the use of the Sūktas seen by Parucchepa in the Śastra mantras, the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says the following, which is explained here:

> द्यौर्वै देवता षष्ठमहर्वहति त्रयस्त्रिंशस्तोमो रैवतं सामातिच्छन्दाश्छन्दो यथादेवतमेतेन यथास्तोमं यथासाम यथाच्छन्दसं राध्नोति य एवं वेद ॥

> *dyaurvai devatā ṣaṣṭhamaharvahati trayastriṃśastomo raivataṃ sāmāticchandāśchando yathādevatametena yathāstomaṃ yathāsāma yathācchandasaṃ rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 22-7 [?], as printed "೨೨-೭"; the reader's OCR garbles the last digits, giving "…-2".) The Kannada then explains: on the sixth day of the Daśarātra sacrifice described above, the deity is Dyaus (heaven), the Stoma recited is the *trayastriṃśa*, the Sāman is *Raivata*, and the metre is *Aticchandas*; the man who knows this attains the deity, the Stoma, the Sāman and the metre, each according to what is proper.

### Printed p. vii  (PDF 13)

The details of the *trayastriṃśa Stoma* we have already told. Nevertheless in the Tāṇḍya Brāhmaṇa the description of this Stoma is as follows:

> एकादशभ्यो हिङ्करोति स तिसृभिः स सप्तभिः स एकया । एकादशभ्यो हिङ्करोति स एकया स तिसृभिः स सप्तभिः । एकादशभ्यो हिङ्करोति स सप्तभिः स एकया स तिसृभिरन्तो वै त्रयस्त्रिंशः ॥

> *ekādaśabhyo hiṅkaroti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa saptabhiḥ sa ekayā | ekādaśabhyo hiṅkaroti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa saptabhiḥ | ekādaśabhyo hiṅkaroti sa saptabhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiranto vai trayastriṃśaḥ ‖*

That is: the *tṛca* to be recited (the group of three ṛks) in the first *paryāya*, the first ṛk to be recited three times, the second ṛk seven times, the third ṛk once (so that eleven ṛks are recited). In the second *paryāya* the first ṛk of the *tṛca* is recited once, the second ṛk three times, the third ṛk seven times (altogether 11 ṛks). In the third *paryāya* the first ṛk is recited seven times, the second once, the third three times (altogether 11 ṛks). In this way, since the number of ṛks recited in the three *paryāyas* is three times eleven, that is thirty-three, this Stoma has the name *trayastriṃśa-stoma*. The Sāman produced from the ṛk "*revatīr naḥ sadhamāde*" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-30-13, as printed and as read by the OCR) has the name *Raivata*. A metre with more syllables than Gāyatrī is called *Aticchandas*. On this sixth day the deities are Vāk, Gau and Dyau. The Stoma is to be praised with the *trayastriṃśa*; with the Raivata Sāman it is to be sung. The ṛks of the Aticchandas metre are to be recited (for the Śastra mantras). These are the special programmes of this sixth day.

> यद्वै समानोदर्कं तत्षष्ठस्याह्नो रूपं यद्वैव तृतीय-महस्तदेतत्पुनर्यत्षष्ठं [?] यदश्ववद्यदन्तवद्यत्पुनरावृत्तं यत्पुनर्निवृत्तं यद्रेतवद्यत्पर्यस्तवद्यत्रिवद्यदन्तरूपं [?] यदुत्तमे पदे देवता निरुच्यते यदसौ लोकोऽभ्युदितः ॥

> *yadvai samānodarkaṃ tatṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ yadvaiva tṛtīya-mahastadetatpunaryatṣaṣṭhaṃ [?] yadaśvavadyadantavadyatpunarāvṛttaṃ yatpunarnivṛttaṃ yadretavadyatparyastavadyatrivadyadantarūpaṃ [?] yaduttame pade devatā nirucyate yadasau loko 'bhyuditaḥ ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 22-7 [?], as printed "೨೨-೭"; the second line is in bold small type and a few letters are doubtful.) The programme that is carried out on the third day of this sacrifice is also to be observed on the sixth day. In reciting the mantras on the third day, the *aśvavat*, *antavat* and so on that were said are also to be recited on the sixth day again. But on the sixth day there is one special order.

> यत्पारुच्छेपं यत्सप्तपदं यन्नाराशंसं यन्नाभानेदिष्ठं यद्रैवतं यदतिच्छन्दा यत्कृतं यत्तृतीयस्याह्नो रूपमेतानि वै षष्ठस्याह्नो रूपाणि ।

> *yatpārucchepaṃ yatsaptapadaṃ yannārāśaṃsaṃ yannābhānediṣṭhaṃ yadraivataṃ yadaticchandā yatkṛtaṃ yattṛtīyasyāhno rūpametāni vai ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpāṇi |*

On that day the ṛks seen by Parucchepa with seven pādas, the ṛks seen by Nābhānediṣṭha, and the ṛks praising the deity *Narāśaṃsa* are to be recited; the Sāman called *Raivata*, for singing …

### Printed p. viii  (PDF 14)

… is to be sung. The ṛks of the Aticchandas metre (metres with more syllables than the Gāyatrī) are to be used. The *bhūtakāla* (past-tense) forms of usage are to be present. Whatever special orders have been said to be followed on the third day, or have not been said, are all to be observed on the sixth day too. That doing so — the recitation of the mantras seen by Parucchepa — is the special feature of the programme of the sixth day.

> अयं जायत मनुषो धरीमणीति षष्ठस्याह्न आज्यं भवति पारुच्छेपमतिच्छन्दाः सप्तपदं षष्ठेऽहनि षष्ठस्याह्नो रूपं ।

> *ayaṃ jāyata manuṣo dharīmaṇīti ṣaṣṭhasyāhna ājyaṃ bhavati pārucchepamaticchandāḥ saptapadaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ |*

The *ājya-śastra* mantra recited on the sixth day must be ṛks of the Sūkta seen by Parucchepa, "*ayaṃ jāyata manuṣo dharīmaṇi*". Their metre is Aticchandas; that is, they have more syllables than ordinary metres; and in these ṛks there are seven pādas (3 pādas in the first half, 2 in the middle half, 2 in the last half, altogether 7 pādas). All these are the special features of the sixth day.

> स्तीर्णं बर्हिरुप नो याहि वीतये आ वां रथो नियुत्वान्वक्षदवसे सुषुमा यातमद्रिभिर्युवां स्तोमेभिर्देवयन्तो अश्विनावर्मुह [?] इन्द्र वृषन्निन्द्रास्तु [?] श्रौषळोषूणो अग्ने शृणुहि त्वमीळितो ये देवासो दिव्येकादशस्थेयमददादभसमृणच्युतमिति प्रलुगं पारुच्छेपमतिच्छन्दाः सप्तपदं षष्ठेऽहनि षष्ठस्याह्नो रूपं ॥

> *stīrṇaṃ barhirupa no yāhi vītaye ā vāṃ ratho niyutvānvakṣadavase suṣumā yātamadribhiryuvāṃ stomebhirdevayanto aśvināvarmuha [?] indra vṛṣannindrāstu [?] śrauṣaḷoṣūṇo agne śṛṇuhi tvamīḷito ye devāso divyekādaśastheyamadadādabhasamṛṇacyutamiti pralugaṃ pārucchepamaticchandāḥ saptapadaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 22-7 [?], as printed "೨೨-೭"; a few letters of this long passage are doubtful.) The Śastra mantras called *Praüga* contain the following ṛks. They are ṛks seen by Parucchepa; the metre is Aticchandas with more syllables; they have seven pādas. Their order is (the list below is as printed in the Kannada page; the numerals are read with the help of the reader's OCR, and doubtful ones are marked):

> स्तीर्णं बर्हिरुप नो याहि वीतये

> *stīrṇaṃ barhirupa no yāhi vītaye*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-135-1 and the ṛks up to the third; as printed "೧-೧೩೫-೧ ರಿಂದ ೩ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳು")

> आ वां रथो नियुत्वान्वक्षदवसे [?]

> *ā vāṃ ratho niyutvānvakṣadavase [?]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-135-4 to the 6th ṛk; as printed "… ರಿಂದ ೬ ವರೆಗಿನ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳು"; the reader's OCR reads "೧-೧೩೫೪", with the hyphen lost)

> सुषुमा यातमद्रिभिः

> *suṣumā yātamadribhiḥ*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-137-1 to the 3rd ṛk; the reader's OCR reads "೧-೧೭-೧", which has lost the digit 3, and my own reading of the small type was also "1-13?-1")

> युवां स्तोमेभिर्देवयन्तो अश्विना

> *yuvāṃ stomebhirdevayanto aśvinā*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-139-3 to the 6th ṛk, as read by the reader's OCR)

> अवर्मह इन्द्र दाद्हि श्रुधी नः

> *avarmaha indra dādhi śrudhī naḥ*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-133-6 and the 7th ṛk, as read by the reader's OCR: "೧-೧೩೩-೬ ಮತ್ತು ೭ ನೆಯ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳು") — the first words are read doubtfully.

> अस्तु श्रौषट् पुरो अग्निं धिया दधे

> *astu śrauṣaṭ puro agniṃ dhiyā dadhe*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-136-1, as read by the reader's OCR)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-139-7, as read by the reader's OCR)

### Printed p. ix  (PDF 15)

> ये देवासो दिव्येकादशस्थ (ऋ. सं. १-१३९-११)

> *ye devāso divyekādaśastha (ṛ. saṃ. 1-139-11)*

> इयमददाद्रभसमृणच्युतं (ऋ. सं. ६-६१-१ से ३ ऋक्) [ṛks 3, as printed "೬-೬೧-೧ ರಿಂದ ೩ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳು"]

> *iyamadadādrabhasamṛṇacyutaṃ (ṛ. saṃ. 6-61-1 se 3 ṛk) [ṛks 3, as printed "೬-೬೧-೧ ರಿಂದ ೩ ಋಕ್ಕುಗಳು"]*

The ṛks together with those said above belong to the Praüga-śastra mantras. Of these, only the ṛks beginning "*iyam adadād …*" were seen by Bharadvāja; all the other ṛks were seen by Parucchepa.

> स पूर्व्यो महानां (ऋ. सं. ८-६३-१)

> *sa pūrvyo mahānāṃ (ṛ. saṃ. 8-63-1)*

Also in the Marutvatīya-śastra mantras that begin with the ṛk *sa pūrvyo mahānām* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-63-1) the following alone, seen by Parucchepa —

> यं त्वं रथमिन्द्र मेधसातये (ऋ. सं. १-१२९-१)

> *yaṃ tvaṃ rathamindra medhasātaye (ṛ. saṃ. 1-129-1)*

— that one ṛk only is included. The rest of the ṛks are seen by other seers, and are therefore not described here.

To publish in simple Kannada, with criticism and translation, the Ṛgsaṃhitā — extremely ancient, extremely deep, extremely extensive, the basis of all śāstras, the root of everything — is not an easy task. But with the great aim that all people, great and small, such as scholars, shall have an increase of knowledge and be worthy of God's grace, the Karnāṭaka throne-holder, protector of Vedic learning, self-taught scholar, lover of his subjects and devoted to God, Śrī Jayacāmarājendra Oḍeyar Bahādur, G.C.B., G.C.S.I., the great Prabhu, graciously encourages the publication of this very costly work under his own patronage; this must be called the good fortune of the people of Karnāṭaka. I pray that God, the Lord of all — the Veda-puruṣa — may bestow on such a generous-minded Lord, on his family, and on the princess (named Gāyatrī, the mantra regarded as most important among the Vedic mantras) and on all the people, all the fruits that are the result of long life, health and prosperity, and all riches, and spiritual and supreme knowledge as well.

## Sūkta 122 — *pra vaḥ pāntam* (printed pp. 1–70)

### Printed p. 1  (PDF 22) — title page of the Second Aṣṭaka

*(Ornament: Oṃ in a sun-disc.)*

**॥ श्रीः ॥ ॥ श्री गणाधिपतये नमः ॥** — *Śrīḥ. Śrī Gaṇādhipataye namaḥ* — "Prosperity. Salutation to Śrī Gaṇādhipati."

> वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे ।
> यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननम् ॥
> यस्य निःश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् ।
> निर्ममे तमहं वन्दे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरम् ॥
> प्रक्रिया प्रथमे काण्डे साकल्येनोपवर्णिता ।
> अत ऊर्ध्वं तु [?] ज्ञेया स्मर्यते च क्वचित्क्वचित् ॥
> वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः ।
> तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥

> *vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame |*
> *yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanam ‖*
> *yasya niḥśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat |*
> *nirmame tamahaṃ vande vidyātīrthamaheśvaram ‖*
> *prakriyā prathame kāṇḍe sākalyenopavarṇitā |*
> *ata ūrdhvaṃ tu [?] jñeyā smaryate ca kvacitkvacit ‖*
> *vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ |*
> *tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*

"I bow to Gajānana, bowing to whom, at the beginning of all undertakings, the gods headed by Vāgīśa (Brahmā) are fulfilled." / "I praise Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara, whose breath is the Vedas and who made the whole world out of the Vedas." / "The grammatical process (*prakriyā*) was described completely in the first Kāṇḍa (the First Aṣṭaka); henceforth it is to be known [from the later passages? — the third pāda `[?]`] and is recalled here and there." / "The Veda is Śiva, Śiva is the Veda, one who studies the Veda is Sadāśiva; therefore with all effort one should always recite the Veda alone." *(Sense mine and tentative; the third verse is the author's own note that the grammar notes of the First Aṣṭaka, which came at the end of each Ṛk, will now be given where they arise — compare the Kannada on p. 4 below.)*

**सायणभाष्यसहिता ऋग्वेदसंहिता** — *Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā Ṛgvedasaṃhitā*. **भाग—१०** (Part 10).
**॥ द्वितीयाष्टके प्रथमोऽध्यायः ॥** — *Dvitīyāṣṭake prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ*. Kannada: "The first Adhyāya in the Second Aṣṭaka. In the first Maṇḍala, the hundred-and-twenty-second Sūkta."

**Kannada introduction (begins).** The Sūkta *pra vaḥ pāntam*, which begins in the first Adhyāya of the Second Aṣṭaka, and the four Sūktas after it (Sūktas 122–126) were seen by the seer Kakṣīvān, born to the seer Dīrghatamas in the woman named Uśik. The woman Uśik was a maidservant of the queen of the king of Kaliṅga; the king of Kaliṅga, desiring that a son should be born to him, sent his wife to the seer Dīrghatamas for union; and then the king's wife, not liking it, …

### Printed p. 2  (PDF 23)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 122".)* …secretly sent her own maidservant, named Uśik, to the seer; and from the seer Dīrghatamas this son named Kakṣīvān was born to her, it is said in the Purāṇas and elsewhere. Though this seer Kakṣīvān was born of a Kṣatriya woman, he became famous as a Brāhmaṇa through contact with a Brāhmaṇa. On the matter of this seer's origin Sāyaṇa has told a story in the bhāṣya on the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-13.

Kakṣīvān is the name of a king. The story of his origin is this: long ago the king of the Aṅga country had gone once, with his wives and maidservants, to the river Gaṅgā for water-sport. Just at that time the seer named Dīrghatamas was floating along in a boat. The seer was extremely weak, and so his wife, sons and others, [thinking] "such a weakling is not wanted by us", had put him in a boat and let it go on the Gaṅgā. The king of Aṅga, by chance, saw the seer Dīrghatamas who had come in the boat to the place where he was bathing, was greatly delighted, took him out of the boat and honoured him; and he begged him: "Sir, for a long time I have had no children. Here is this wife of mine; beget one son on her." Then the queen, seeing this seer who was extremely old, did not wish to be with him, and sent in her place a maidservant of hers named Uśik. The all-knowing great seer, sprinkling her with mantra-consecrated water, made that maidservant like the seer's wife; and she conceived. The son born in her was the seer named Kakṣīvān. He performed many sacrifices such as the Rājasūya. Indra, pleased with the sacrifices, graciously gave Kakṣīvān a young woman named Vṛcayā. The word *kakṣya* also means the strap that is tied to a draught animal. *Kakṣīvān* = *kakṣyāvān* (Nirukta 6-10, as printed). So says the Nirukta.

The name of this Kakṣīvān is found in the following ṛks of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā: Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-18-1; 1-21-13; 1-112-1; 1-116-7; 4-26-1; 8-9-10; 9-74-8; 10-25-10; 10-61-16 (as printed; the reader's OCR reads the same), and also in Atharvaveda 4-29-5 (the OCR shows "೪೨೯-೫", the hyphen lost). His family name must have been *Pajra*, because he is called *Pajriya* in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-7 and 1-117-6 (as printed "೧-೧೧೭-೬"), and his descendants are called *Pajrāḥ* in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-126-4. In Sūkta 1-126 of the Ṛ. Saṃ. this seer praises the gifts given to him by a king named Svanayabhāvya; and in the Sāṅkhyāyana Śrauta Sūtra 16-4-5, among the group of mantras called Nārāśaṃsa Sūktas, which praise heroes, there is also included the Dānastuti mantra on the king Svanayabhāvya made by Kakṣīvān, the son of Uśij. When he had grown old he married a maiden named Vṛcayā; this matter is described in the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-13. He is said to have lived a hundred years …

The Western scholar Weber, on the basis of the mantras Tai. Saṃ. 5-6-5-3; Kāṭhakasaṃhitā 13-3; Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa 25-16-3 (all three as read by the reader's OCR), is of the opinion that this Kakṣīvān was first a Kṣatriya, and that therefore his name occurs, in the mantras cited above, together with the names of the kings Para Āṭṇāra, Vītahavya, Śrāyasa, Trasadasyu and Paurukutsa. This seer is the seer of 151 ṛks in all: the 146 ṛks of the Sūktas from 116 to 125 in the first Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda, and ṛks 1–5 of Sūkta 126; besides, he is the seer of the 9 ṛks of Sūkta 74 of the ninth Maṇḍala, "*Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasaḥ*" — and since there the seer is called "Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasaḥ" — that is, Kakṣīvān the son of the seer Dīrghatamas — even though the epithet *Auśija* is lacking there, the seer of the Sūkta now in hand, too, may be said to be the seer of that [Sūkta] as well.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (introduction)**

> अथ द्वितीयाष्टके प्रथमोऽध्याय आरभ्यते । शतर्चिनामाद्ये मण्डले चतुर्विंशत्यनुवाकाः । तेषु कदित्थेत्यष्टादशानुवाके षट् सूक्तानि । तत्र प्र वः पान्तमिति द्वितीयं सूक्तम् । पञ्चोनेत्यनुवर्तमानात्पञ्चदशर्चम् । ऋषिश्चान्यस्मादृषेरिति [?] परिभाषया कक्षीवानृषिः । अनादेशपरिभाषया त्रिष्टुप् । विश्वे देवा देवता । प्र वो वैश्वदेवमित्यनुक्रमणिका । अस्य विशेषविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥

> *atha dvitīyāṣṭake prathamo 'dhyāya ārabhyate | śatarcināmādye maṇḍale caturviṃśatyanuvākāḥ | teṣu kaditthetyaṣṭādaśānuvāke ṣaṭ sūktāni | tatra pra vaḥ pāntamiti dvitīyaṃ sūktam | pañconetyanuvartamānātpañcadaśarcam | ṛṣiścānyasmādṛṣeriti [?] paribhāṣayā kakṣīvānṛṣiḥ | anādeśaparibhāṣayā triṣṭup | viśve devā devatā | pra vo vaiśvadevamityanukramaṇikā | asya viśeṣaviniyogo laiṅgikaḥ ‖*

Now the second Aṣṭaka's first Adhyāya begins. In the first Maṇḍala, belonging to the Śatarcins, there are twenty-four Anuvākas. Among them, in the eighteenth Anuvāka, beginning *kad itthā*, there are six Sūktas. Of these, *pra vaḥ pāntam* is the second Sūkta. It has fifteen ṛks (by the continuing rule "*pañconā …*" [?]). By the rule "the seer is [the same as] the other seer's" [?] the seer is Kakṣīvān; by the rule of the unspecified metre it is Triṣṭubh; the deity is the Viśvedevas; the Anukramaṇikā says "*pra vo vaiśvadevam*"; its special application is *laiṅgika*.

**Anuvāda (Kannada translation).** The first Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda has been completed, so we now begin to write the translation and explanations of the first Adhyāya of the second Aṣṭaka. In the eight Adhyāyas of the first Aṣṭaka the grammatical process (*vyākaraṇa-prakriyā*) that has to be stated for each ṛk was given all together at the end of the bhāṣya of each ṛk. Now we shall give that part here and there, as the occasion requires. We have already said that there are twenty-four Anuvākas in the first Maṇḍala, connected with the seers of the Śatarca. Of those, in the eighteenth Anuvāka there are six Sūktas beginning with *kad itthā*. Since the first Sūkta was completed in the previous Adhyāya, the Sūkta *pra vaḥ pāntam* on which we now comment is the second in the eighteenth Anuvāka. In it there are fifteen ṛks. As said before, the seer of this Sūkta too is Kakṣīvān himself, …

### Printed p. 4  (PDF 25)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 122".)* … the metre is Triṣṭubh, the deities are the Viśvedevas. The Anukramaṇikā begins "*pra vo vaiśvadevam*"; the application of this Sūkta is *laiṅgika* — that is, the application of each ṛk is as the deities propounded in those ṛks are praised, it is to be understood.

**Sūkta 122** — Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 18 ‖ Sūkta 122 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 1 ‖ Vargas 1, 2, 3 ‖ number of ṛks in this Sūkta: 15 ‖ Seer: Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija ‖ Deity: Viśvedevas ‖ Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्र वः पान्तं रघुमन्यवोऽन्धो यज्ञं रुद्राय मीळ्हुषे भरध्वम् ।
> दिवो अस्तोष्यसुरस्य वीरैरिषुध्येव मरुतो रोदस्योः ॥ १ ॥

> *pra vaḥ pāntaṃ raghumanyavo 'ndho yajñaṃ rudrāya mīḷhuṣe bharadhvam |*
> *divo astoṣyasurasya vīrairiṣudhyeva maruto rodasyoḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्र । वः । पान्तम् । रघुऽमन्यवः । अन्धः । यज्ञम् । रुद्राय । मीळ्हुषे । भरध्वम् ॥
> दिवः । अस्तोषि । असुरस्य । वीरैः । इषुध्याऽइव । मरुतः । रोदस्योः ॥ १ ॥

> *pra | vaḥ | pāntam | raghu 'manyavaḥ | andhaḥ | yajñam | rudrāya | mīḷhuṣe | bharadhvam ‖*
> *divaḥ | astoṣi | asurasya | vīraiḥ | iṣudhyā 'iva | marutaḥ | rodasyoḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे रघुमन्यवो लघुक्रोधा अक्रोधन ऋत्विजो वो युष्माकं पान्तं पालनशीलं पातव्यं वा यज्ञं यागसाधनमन्धोऽन्नमाज्यसोमादिलक्षणं रुद्राय । रुद्दुःखं तद्धेतुभूतं दुरितं वा । तस्य द्रावयित्रे । एतन्नामकाय देवाय मीळ्हुषे फलस्य वर्षित्रे तदर्थं प्र भरध्वम् । प्रकर्षेण सम्पादयत ।

> *he raghumanyavo laghukrodhā akrodhana ṛtvijo vo yuṣmākaṃ pāntaṃ pālanaśīlaṃ pātavyaṃ vā yajñaṃ yāgasādhanamandho 'nnamājyasomādilakṣaṇaṃ rudrāya | rudduḥkhaṃ taddhetubhūtaṃ duritaṃ vā | tasya drāvayitre | etannāmakāya devāya mīḷhuṣe phalasya varṣitre tadarthaṃ pra bharadhvam | prakarṣeṇa sampādayata |*

O mild-tempered (*laghu-krodhāḥ*, not angry) priests, bring forth for Rudra — the one who makes run away (*drāvayitṛ*) *rut*, "pain" (or the sin that is the cause of it), the god of this name, the one who rains the fruit (*mīḍhvas*) — the food (*andhas*, consisting of ghee, Soma and the like), the means of sacrifice, your own, protecting (*pāntam*) or to be protected. *Pra bharadhvam*: "offer abundantly".

> अहं चेषुध्येव इषुध्या शरध्या यथा निरस्यति तथा वीरैरमित्राणां विविधमीरकैर्नियोपेतैर्वा [?] तदनुचरैर्मरुदादिभिः सह दिवो द्युलोकसकाशात् । उपलक्षणमेतत् । लोकत्रयादसुरस्य निरसितव्यानामसुराणां निरसितुः । कर्मणि षष्ठी । निरसितारं तमेव देवं रोदस्योर्निरोधनवत्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योर्मध्ये वर्तमानान्मरुतश्चास्तोषि । स्तौमि ॥

> *ahaṃ ceṣudhyeva iṣudhyā śaradhyā yathā nirasyati tathā vīrairamitrāṇāṃ vividhamīrakairniyopetairvā [?] tadanucarairmarudādibhiḥ saha divo dyulokasakāśāt | upalakṣaṇametat | lokatrayādasurasya nirasitavyānāmasurāṇāṃ nirasituḥ | karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī | nirasitāraṃ tameva devaṃ rodasyornirodhanavatyordyāvāpṛthivyormadhye vartamānānmarutaścāstoṣi | staumi ‖*

"And I, as one throws down [enemies] with arrows from a quiver — [so I praise], together with the Maruts and others who are his followers, [those] 'heroes' of the enemies' [side]`[?]` (the middle part of this sentence is doubtful in the small type), from heaven, from the region of the sky (this is only an indication — [it means from] the three worlds), the expeller of the Asuras who are to be expelled (*asurasya*: the genitive is in the sense of the object), that very god (Rudra); and the Maruts who stand in the middle between Heaven and Earth, the two that obstruct [the way] (*rodasyoḥ*), I praise (*astoṣi* = *staumi*)." *(Sense mine and tentative for the doubtful middle.)*

**Grammatical tail (characterised, not transcribed; sūtra wording as printed):** *pāntam* — the root *pā*, the suffix *śatṛ*, which is by an *uṇādi* suffix *ṛ* of the root *pibati*; *mīḷhuṣe* — a *kvasu*-final word by *dāśvān sāhvān*…; in the dative singular the *saṃprasāraṇa* of *vas* by *vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam*; *ṣatva* by *śāsivasi*…; *divaḥ* — the ending gets the udātta by *ūḍidam*…; *astoṣi* — the root *stu*, the Vedic *luṅ*; *iṣudhyā* — *iṣavo dhīyante 'syām*, the suffix *ki* of the root *dhā* by *karmaṇy adhikaraṇe ca*, final udātta by the *kṛt* accent, and the ending's udātta by *udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt*. *(Sūtra numbers are not printed here.)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Raghumanyavaḥ* — O mild-tempered (non-angry) priests; *vaḥ* — you (by you); *pāntam* — protecting (to be protected); *yajñam* — the means of the sacrifice; *andhaḥ* — the food in the form of ghee and the like; *rudrāya* — to Rudra who destroys the sin that is the cause of suffering; *mīḷhuṣe* — in order to rain the fruits; *pra bharadhvam* — offer abundantly; (*aham ca* — and I) *iṣudhyā iva* — as (one who destroys the enemy) with the arrows in the quiver; *vīraiḥ* — with heroes who strike the enemies (with the Maruts who are his followers); *divaḥ* — from the region of the sky (from the three worlds); *asurasya* — of the Rākṣasas (of that Rudra who drives them away); *rodasyoḥ* — of the earth and the sky (standing in the middle); *marutaḥ* — the Marut gods too; *astoṣi* — I praise.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O mild-tempered priests, offer abundantly the oblation in the form of ghee and so on, which protects you and is the means of the sacrifice, to Rudra, who "milks" the fruits (in the form of rain), and who is the remover of the sin that causes suffering. And I praise (that Rudra god) who, with heroic (followers who are his own attendants), as the archer with the arrows in the quiver destroys the enemies, drives the Rākṣasas in the intermediate region from there, and also the Marut gods who are in the sky between earth and heaven.

**Printed English (as printed):** *Present, mild-tempered (priests), the sacrificial viands which you have prepared, to the reward-showering Rudra. I praise him who, with his heroic (followers), as (with shafts) from a quiver, expelled (the Asuras) from heaven: and (I praise) the Maruts, (who abide) between heaven and earth.*

### Printed p. 6  (PDF 27)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 122".)* **Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***raghumanyavaḥ*** — Here *raghu* means *laghu*. In the Ṛgveda *r* is used in many places in place of *l*. For example:

> अश्वं न त्वा वारवन्तं वन्दध्या अग्निं नमोभिः सम्राजन्तमध्वराणाम् ॥

> *aśvaṃ na tvā vāravantaṃ vandadhyā agniṃ namobhiḥ samrājantamadhvarāṇām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-27-1 [?] — as read from the image; the reader's OCR of this reference is garbled.) In this ṛk *vāravantam* means *vālavantam* — a horse that has a tail (hair). Therefore here *raghumanyavaḥ* = *laghumanyavaḥ*: *laghukrodhāḥ, akrodhinaḥ* — "of little anger" (*light or little anger*, as printed in English), that is, those who are without anger — that is the sense.

*Laghukrodhāḥ akrodhinaḥ ṛtvijaḥ* is how Sāyaṇa explained it. He too has shown that it is difficult to state the meaning properly for this word. Ordinarily *raghu* (*laghu*) comes to mean "quick"; the word *manyu* is recorded among the names of anger (*krodha*) (Ni. 3-9, as printed; the OCR reads 3-9). Therefore one ought, strictly, to understand it as "quick-tempered persons"; but this meaning is not so suitable. Sāyaṇa has explained *alpakrodhinaḥ, akrodhinaḥ*. But even that does not make clear the real nature of the priests. Of whom this word is the epithet, and what its right meaning is — that it is not easy to say, the scholar Wilson has said in this way in the preface of his book *The Rig-veda, Translation and Notes*:

*"It may not be always possible to devise unexceptionable and felicitous equivalents for such expressions, but they may be so rendered as to eonvey [sic] with some degree of accuracy the substance of the text: the more unmanageable difficulties are those which are utterly insuperable except by guess ………… thus, as already observed, the substantive is vety [sic] often omitted and the adjective does double duty: the first Verse of the second Ashtaka offers an example: it begins—Raghu-manyavah (रघु मन्यवः)—"oh ye of little wrath"; "ye who are gentle, mild-tempered";but who they are that are so addressed does not appear. The scholiast says, mild-tempered priests, and it would not be easy to suggest a preferable application of the epithet, although, if not traditional. it is only conjectural."* (Vol II Introduction. P. XVII)

From this it is hard to say in what way the epithet "non-angry" shows the real nature of the priests. Along with the meaning *akrodhinaḥ*, this word also has …

### Printed p. 7  (PDF 28)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 1".)* …(the word *raghumanyavaḥ*, continued) another reading, in the sense *śīghrastutayaḥ* ("quick praisers"), is also found: *manyatir arcākarma* — since *manyate* is recorded among the words meaning "to praise" (*arcati-karma-nāmāni*), it is said that *śīghrastutayaḥ* is possible too. But here the word *manyu* shows the definite meaning "anger"; so this variant reading does not look so proper, and "quick-tempered ones" is not right either. Therefore "those without anger" is the right sense.

***mīḷhuṣe*** — *phalasya varṣitre rudrāya*: for Rudra who showers the fruits (the things desired). Here it is the aspect of Rudra as giver that is told; another aspect of Rudra is explained as well, when the derivation of the word *rudrāya* is given: *rut duḥkhaṃ taddhetubhūtaṃ duritaṃ vā | tasya drāvayitre etannāmakāya devāya* — *rut* is sorrow, or the sin that causes it; because he makes this run away, he has the name Rudra. All aspects of Rudra's nature will be explained in the Sūkta addressed to this deity.

***vīraiḥ*** — *amitrāṇāṃ vividhamīrakaiḥ vīryopetaiḥ*: with the Maruts who are endowed with heroism that harms the enemies in many ways. The Maruts, being Rudra's sons, are always his followers.

***rodasyoḥ marutaḥ*** — Sāyaṇa explains: *dyāvāpṛthivyor madhye vartamānān marutaḥ* — the Maruts who stand between Heaven and Earth.

> आ यस्मिन्सूरणानि बिभ्रती सचा मरुत्सु रोदसी ।

> *ā yasminsūraṇāni bibhratī sacā marutsu rodasī |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-56-8, as printed.) In this ṛk it is said that Rodasī is Rudra's wife and the mother of the Maruts. But since the dual number is used in the ṛk in hand, it is right to take it as Heaven and Earth.

***marutaḥ*** — *marutaḥ mitarāviṇo vā mitarociṇo vā mahadravantīti vā* (Ni. 11-13, as printed; the reader's OCR reads the same): either because they make a regular (measured) sound, or because they have regular (measured) light, or because they move greatly and swiftly; hence the name *marutaḥ*. Its explanation was given earlier too.

***iṣudhyā*** — *iṣudhyā (niṣaṅgeṇa) śatrūn yathā nirasyati tathā*: as one drives the enemies away with a quiver (with the arrow from a quiver) easily, so I praise (*staumi*, I will praise) Rudra, the god who comes with the heroic Maruts from the heavenly world to destroy the Asuras — that is the meaning. By himself he has power; to his arrows the help of the Maruts is added. Hence the greatness of his power will be greater still — that is the sense.

> इमा रुद्राय स्थिरधन्वने गिरः क्षिप्रेषवे देवाय स्वधाव्ने ।

> *imā rudrāya sthiradhanvane giraḥ kṣipreṣave devāya svadhāvne |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3[?]-[?], as printed; the numerals are small and I cannot read them reliably.)

### Printed p. 8  (PDF 29)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 122".)*

> शतशीर्षा रुद्रः सहस्राक्षः शतेषुधिरधिज्यधन्वा [?] ।

> *śataśīrṣā rudraḥ sahasrākṣaḥ śateṣudhiradhijyadhanvā [?] |*

(printed with a four-part reference in the small type, "Śa. Brā. 9-1-1-6 [?]" — the first word and the numbers are not reliably read.) In sentences such as this there is a description of Rudra holding quivers full of terrible arrows. Taking this into account Sāyaṇa has said much here, and the idea is made known that Rudra is a destroyer of enemies and terrible, and that this nature of his becomes still more powerful with the help of the Maruts.

***asurasya*** — Here the accusative is used [i.e. a usage in the sense of the object]. For the word *asura* the bhāṣyakāra here gives the meaning *nirasitāraṃ devam* — "the god who defeats (the enemies)". Ordinarily the meaning "Rākṣasas" is current for the word *asura*; but in many places the meaning of this word is in favour of the gods. In this Aṣṭaka this use of the word *asura* occurs in about ten ṛks; everywhere the meaning is in favour of the gods.

> दिवो अस्तोष्यसुरस्य वीरैरिषुध्येव मरुतो रोदस्योः ।

> *divo astoṣyasurasya vīrairiṣudhyeva maruto rodasyoḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-1.) In this ṛk — *asurasya nirasitavyānām asurāṇāṃ nirasituḥ | karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī | nirasitāraṃ tam eva devaṃ (rudram)* — that is, "Rudra, who defeats the Asuras".

> शतं राज्ञो नाधमानस्य निष्काञ्छतमश्वान्प्रयतान्सद्य आदम् ।
> शतं कक्षीवाँ असुरस्य गोनां दिवि श्रवो जरमा ततान ॥

> *śataṃ rājño nādhamānasya niṣkāñchatamaśvānprayatānsadya ādam |*
> *śataṃ kakṣīvā~ asurasya gonāṃ divi śravo jaramā tatāna ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-126-2, as printed; the reader's OCR confirms it on p. 25 as "1-126-1 and 2"; the words of this ṛk are read from the small bold type, and the second line's first words are doubtful.) Here — *asurasya dhanānāṃ nirasitur dānaśīlasya rājñaḥ svanayasya* — "of the king Svanaya, who gives away wealth and so on"; thus the word *asura* is in favour of the king Svanaya.

> इन्द्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नतेन्द्राय मही पृथिवी वरीमभिर्द्युम्न-साता वरीमभिः ॥

> *indrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnatendrāya mahī pṛthivī varīmabhirdyumna-sātā varīmabhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-131-1.) [The first line's last words and the second line are in bold small type; "*dyumnasātā*" is read with doubt `[?]`.] Here the word *asura* is explained as *asuraḥ nirasanaśīlaḥ śatrūṇāṃ puṇyakṛtām eva tanniv āsāt (dyauḥ dyuloka)* [as printed, the reading being partly `[?]`]: "heaven is the dwelling-place of the meritorious who perform sacrifices and the like, and makes no room for their enemies" — thus the word *asura* is an epithet of the word *dyauḥ*, in the sense of heaven.

> प्र सा क्षितिरसुर या महि प्रिय ऋतावानावृतमा घोषतो बृहत् ।

> *pra sā kṣitirasura yā mahi priya ṛtāvānāvṛtamā ghoṣato bṛhat |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-151-4 [?], as read; the OCR is garbled here.)

### Printed p. 9  (PDF 30)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 1".)* …in this ṛk, the word *asura* is an epithet of Mitrāvaruṇa — "*he asurā asurau balavantau mitrāvaruṇau*" ("O Asuras, O strong Mitra and Varuṇa") — and tells of their protective power and strength.

> त्वं राजेन्द्र ये च देवा रक्षा स्नाप्यसुर [?] त्वमस्मान् ।

> *tvaṃ rājendra ye ca devā rakṣā snāpyasura [?] tvamasmān |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-134-1, as printed; the reader's OCR agrees; the middle words of the line are read with doubt `[?]`.) In this ṛk *asura* — *śatrūṇāṃ nirasitaḥ he indra* ("O Indra, who defeat the enemies") — the word *asura* is used with reference to Indra.

> त्वमग्ने रुद्रो असुरो महो दिवस्त्वं शर्धो मारुतं पृक्ष ईशिषे ।

> *tvamagne rudro asuro maho divastvaṃ śardho mārutaṃ pṛkṣa īśiṣe |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-6, as printed.) In this ṛk the meaning given for the word *asura* is: *asuraḥ śatrūṇāṃ nirasitā rudro 'si* — "you are Rudra who conquers the enemy".

> त्वं विश्वेषां वरुणासि राजा ये च देवा असुर ये च मर्ताः ।

> *tvaṃ viśveṣāṃ varuṇāsi rājā ye ca devā asura ye ca martāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [2]-2[7]-10 [?], as printed in small type; the reader's OCR reads "3-32-10", which I do not accept as it stands.) Here for *asura* the meaning is *he asura śatrūṇāṃ kṣepaka varuṇa* ("O Varuṇa, thrower down of the enemies"): "who defeats the enemies"; the word *asura* is in favour of Varuṇa.

> मा नो वधैर्वरुण ये त इष्टावेनः कृण्वन्तमसुर भ्रीणन्ति [?] ।

> *mā no vadhairvaruṇa ye ta iṣṭāvenaḥ kṛṇvantamasura bhrīṇanti [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-28-[?]; the last digit is doubtful.) In this ṛk too: *he asura pāpakṛtāṃ nirasitaḥ varuṇa* ("O Varuṇa, who suppress those who do wrong") — it is in favour of Varuṇa.

> बृहस्पते तपुषाश्मेव विध्य वृकद्वरसो असुरस्य वीरान् ।

> *bṛhaspate tapuṣāśmeva vidhya vṛkadvaraso asurasya vīrān |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-30-4.) In this ṛk the word *asura* is an epithet of *vṛkadvarasaḥ*; "of the Asura who has closed the door" — *saṃvṛtadvārasya asurasya* — "the Asura who shut the door and blocked it": here the ordinary meaning of the word *asura* itself is clear.

> पिता यज्ञानामसुरो विपश्चितां विमानमग्निर्वयुनं च वाघताम् ।

> *pitā yajñānāmasuro vipaścitāṃ vimānamagnirvayunaṃ ca vāghatām |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-2-4 [?], as printed; the reader's OCR reads the same.) In this ṛk, *asuro balapradaḥ* — "Asura, giver of strength" — the word *asura* is used with reference to Agni.

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पत्नीव पूर्वहूतिं वावृधध्या उषासानक्ता पुरुधा विदाने ।
> स्तरीर्नात्कं व्युतं वसाना सूर्यस्य श्रिया सुदृशी हिरण्यैः ॥ २ ॥

> *patnīva pūrvahūtiṃ vāvṛdhadhyā uṣāsānaktā purudhā vidāne |*
> *starīrnātkaṃ vyutaṃ vasānā sūryasya śriyā sudṛśī hiraṇyaiḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पत्नीऽइव । पूर्वऽहूतिम् । ववृधध्यै । उषासानक्ता । पुरुधा । विदाने इति ।
> स्तरीः । न । अत्कम् । विऽउतम् । वसाना । सूर्यस्य । श्रिया । सुऽदृशी । हिरण्यैः ॥ २ ॥

> *patnī 'iva | pūrva 'hūtim | vavṛdhadhyai | uṣāsānaktā | purudhā | vidāne iti |*
> *starīḥ | na | atkam | vi 'utam | vasānā | sūryasya | śriyā | su 'dṛśī | hiraṇyaiḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

*(The Saṃhitā reads* vāvṛdhadhyā *and the Pada* vavṛdhadhyai *as printed; the Pada's *vi-utam* is read with doubt.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> पत्नीव पत्नी यथा पूर्वहूतिं पत्युः पूर्वाह्वानं ववृधध्यै वर्धयितुं शीघ्रगतिर्भवति तद्वदुषासानक्ताहोरात्रे देवते अपि पुरुधा बहुप्रकारं बहुविधैः स्तोत्रैर्विदाने ज्ञायमाने सत्यौ पूर्वहूतिं ववृधध्यै अस्मदीयं पूर्वाह्वानं वर्धयितुं शीघ्रमागच्छतमिति शेषः । यद्वा । ववृधध्यै अस्मद्वर्धनाय पुरुधा बहुप्रकारं विदाने वर्धनोपायो ज्ञानत्यौ [?] भवतमिति शेषः ॥ उषासानक्ता । उषासोषसः (पा. ६-३-३१) इति पूर्वपदस्योषासादेशः । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥ अथ केवलोषा उच्यते । स्तरीः शत्रूणां हिंसकस्तेजसा

> *patnīva patnī yathā pūrvahūtiṃ patyuḥ pūrvāhvānaṃ vavṛdhadhyai vardhayituṃ śīghragatirbhavati tadvaduṣāsānaktāhorātre devate api purudhā bahuprakāraṃ bahuvidhaiḥ stotrairvidāne jñāyamāne satyau pūrvahūtiṃ vavṛdhadhyai asmadīyaṃ pūrvāhvānaṃ vardhayituṃ śīghramāgacchatamiti śeṣaḥ | yadvā | vavṛdhadhyai asmadvardhanāya purudhā bahuprakāraṃ vidāne vardhanopāyo jñānatyau [?] bhavatamiti śeṣaḥ ‖ uṣāsānaktā | uṣāsoṣasaḥ (pā. 6-3-31) iti pūrvapadasyoṣāsādeśaḥ | devatādvandve cetyubhayapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ‖ atha kevaloṣā ucyate | starīḥ śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsakastejasā*

Like a wife who hastens to increase (*vavṛdhadhyai*) her husband's first call (*pūrvahūti*, the first summons), so, you two deities Night and Day (*uṣāsānaktā*), who are known (*vidāne*) in many ways (*purudhā*) by many kinds of praises, come quickly to increase our first summons — that is what must be supplied. Or else: "*vavṛdhadhyai*, for our increase, knowing (*vidāne*) the many means of increase, be [ours]". *Uṣāsānaktā*: by *uṣāsoṣasaḥ* (Pā. 6-3-31, as printed) the first member is replaced by *uṣāsā*; by *devatādvandve ca* both members keep their own accent. Now Dawn alone is spoken of: *starīḥ* — the destroyer of enemies by her radiance, …

> च्छन्नो वादित्यः स इव हिरण्यैर्हिरण्यवर्णै रश्मिभिर्वृतं निततं विशेषेण सम्बद्धमत्कमत्कं [?] सन्ततं वा रूपं वसानाच्छादयन्ती धारयन्ती सूर्यस्य श्रिया शोभया सुदृशी शोभनं दृश्यमाना सूर्यस्य पुरोगामिनी रश्मिभिः खल्वेषा जगद्वासयति । तादृश्युषा अस्मत्पूर्वहूतिं पालयत्वित्यर्थः । यद्वा । हिरण्यैर्हितरमणीयैः प्रकाशैर्धनविशेषैर्वा सहागच्छतु ॥ व्युतं । वेञो निष्ठायां वचिस्वपीत्यादिना सम्प्रसारणम् । स्तरीः । अवितृस्तृतन्त्रिभ्य ईः इतीकारप्रत्ययः ॥

> *cchanno vādityaḥ sa iva hiraṇyairhiraṇyavarṇai raśmibhirvṛtaṃ nitataṃ viśeṣeṇa sambaddhamatkamatkaṃ [?] santataṃ vā rūpaṃ vasānācchādayantī dhārayantī sūryasya śriyā śobhayā sudṛśī śobhanaṃ dṛśyamānā sūryasya purogāminī raśmibhiḥ khalveṣā jagadvāsayati | tādṛśyuṣā asmatpūrvahūtiṃ pālayatvityarthaḥ | yadvā | hiraṇyairhitaramaṇīyaiḥ prakāśairdhanaviśeṣairvā sahāgacchatu ‖ vyutaṃ | veño niṣṭhāyāṃ vacisvapītyādinā samprasāraṇam | starīḥ | avitṛstṛtantribhya īḥ itīkārapratyayaḥ ‖*

(The first words of the line read *tejasā cchanno vāditya[ḥ] sa iva* — "like the Sun, covered with radiance"; the reader's OCR reads *cchanno vāditya* clearly, which replaces my first reading *cainno*.) The sense: "like the Sun, with golden-coloured rays, a form (*atkam*, i.e. *atkam* = a covering or *saṃtatam*, "extended") covered, extended, joined in a special way; wearing (*vasānā*, covering, bearing) the beauty (*śriyā*, with the splendour) of the Sun, well-seen (*sudṛśī*), seen beautifully, going before the Sun — she, by her rays, makes the world dwell (*jagad vāsayati*). Such a Dawn, may she protect our first summons — that is the sense. Or else: let her come together with golden, i.e. beneficial and delightful lights or special treasures." *Vyutam*: from the root *ve*(*ñ*) with the *niṣṭhā* suffix, *saṃprasāraṇa* by *vacisvapi…*. *Starīḥ*: the suffix *ī* by *avitṛstṛ…* [?] — the grammatical tail, only characterised.

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Uṣāsānaktā* — O Day and Night; *purudhā* — [known] by manifold (praises); *vidāne* — [you who are] to be known; *patnī iva* — like a wife (hastening, accepting her husband's first call); *pūrvahūtim* — the first call; *vavṛdhadhyai* — to increase, [come] quickly; [or: *vavṛdhadhyai* — for our welfare; *purudhā vidāne* — you who know the means (of increase); *patnī iva* — like a wife; *pūrvahūtim* — (our) first prayer (aiming at it) come;] *starīḥ na* — like Sūrya, who is of excellent power (the destroyer of enemies); *hiraṇyaiḥ* — with golden-coloured (rays) or with wealth; *vṛtam* — joined in a special way (possessed); *atkam* — the form; *vasānā* — wearing (and); *sūryasya śriyā* — with the lustre of the Sun; *sudṛśī* — the Dawn of lovely form; *(pūrvahūtim* — may she accept our first prayer).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Day and Night! You who are known by many praises, as a wife accepts her husband's first call and comes quickly, accept our first, early praise in the form of an invocation, so that we may prosper (and, knowing the various means of increase for us, accept our first call). And may the Dawn too, lovely in form, and — as the Sun does — endowed with golden rays, wearing the lustre of the Sun and pervading the sky, accept our first invocation.

**Printed English (as printed):** *Animated by our deversified [sic] praise, hasten, Morning and Night, to attend to our first invocation, as a wife (to the first call of her husband); and may the Dawn, beautiful with the lustre of the (rising) Sun, and robing, like the Sun (her) vast expanse with golden rays, (come to our early rite).*

### Printed p. 13  (PDF 34)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 1".)* **Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 2.**

In this ṛk the beauty of the forms of Night and Dawn and their nature as benefactors are described, and their grace is prayed for. Comparing them to a wife shows their affection and sense of ownership. In the first half of this ṛk two kinds of construction are possible. First:

***purudhā vidāne vavṛdhadhyai*** — *bahuprakāraṃ bahuvidhaiḥ stotrair jñāyamāne* — "you who are known by many kinds of praises"; and second:

***vavṛdhadhyai*** — "for our welfare"; ***purudhā*** — by many kinds of ways; ***vidāne*** — "you who know [them]" — so the meaning is. Dawn and Night are, through the succession of the days, the cause of food and other wealth for men, and of joy and comfort. *Vājinīvatī* (giver of food), *sumnāvarī* (giver of comfort), *sūnṛtāvatī* (giver of pleasant words) and similar epithets that point to the nature of Dawn are recorded in the Nirukta as synonymous names of Dawn (2-18, as printed). Since Night and Dawn are the controllers of the whole world in every respect, the second meaning is more fitting.

***patnī iva*** — Here, in the simile, beauty, possession and a sense of ownership are suggested. Comparing the character of Dawn to a lovely woman is a custom; and she is described as one who calls out to the children as a mother, and to the elders as a wife.

***starīḥ*** — *śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsakaḥ; tejasā ācchannor vā ādityaḥ* — "the destroyer of enemies; or the Sun covered with radiance". The word *starī* has been explained as "the destroyer of enemies, or the Sun pervaded by splendour". Ordinarily *starī* means a [cow] that is useless, not giving fruit.

For example:

> स्तरीरु त्वद्भवति सूत उ त्वद्यथावशं तन्वं चक्र एषः ।

> *starīru tvadbhavati sūta u tvadyathāvaśaṃ tanvaṃ cakra eṣaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-101-3, as read — the reader's OCR is garbled here — the Parjanya verse.) In this ṛk the nature of Parjanya is described. One part of him is compared to a barren cow. Just as a barren cow gives no milk, so he is compared, when it is said "not giving rain", and for the word *starīḥ* Sāyaṇa has given the meaning *nivṛttaprasavā gauḥ*, "a cow that has ceased to bear". In just the same way:

> स्तरीर्यत्सूत सद्योऽज्यमाना व्यथिरव्यः कृणुत स्वगोपा ।

> *starīryatsūta sadyo 'jyamānā vyathiravyaḥ kṛṇuta svagopā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-31-10 [?], as read.) In this ṛk too the same meaning follows. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā…

> कदा चन स्तरीरसीत्याह न स्तरीं रात्रिं वसति ।

> *kadā cana starīrasītyāha na starīṃ rātriṃ vasati |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-8, as printed; the reader's OCR gives the same.) In this sentence, for the words *starīṃ rātrim* Sāyaṇa has given the sense "night full of thieves and scorpions and so on"; Bhaṭṭabhāskara has given the sense *starīṃ chādayitrīṃ vināśayitrīṃ rātrim* — "the destroying (night)". That is, the traditional meaning there too is "that which destroys benefit, or is useless". In just the same way in the ṛk in hand also *starīḥ śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsakaḥ*: "destroyer of enemies", the Sun that makes the enemies' effort fruitless, may be said.

***atkaṃ vasānā*** — *rūpaṃ vasānā*: "wearing a form" — i.e. a lovely form; this word is used in many ṛks describing the Dawn (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-29-3; 10-95-8 etc., as read, may be seen). *Sūryasya purogāminī raśmibhiḥ khalv eṣā jagad vāsayati* — Born before the Sun, with golden rays, she awakens and illumines the world — that is the sense.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** *Patnīva* — *patyur no yajñasaṃyoge* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-33), the *nuk* augment and the suffix *ṅīp* in the feminine; accent by the *p* of the suffix. *Pūrvahūtim* — the root *hveñ spardhāyām* …, *striyāṃ ktin* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-94), *saṃprasāraṇa*, lengthening by *halaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-2); accusative singular. *Vavṛdhadhyai* — the root *vṛdhu vṛddhau*; the sense of the infinitive (*tumartha*) by *tumarthe sesenasen…* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-9), the suffix *kadhyai*; *āgamānuśāsanam anityam* — so the augment (*rīk* etc.) is not added to the reduplicative syllable; since the suffix begins with an acute, the *dhai* gets the acute; *kṛn mejantaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-39) — the indeclinable designation; *avyayād āp supaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-82) — *luk* of the case endings. *Uṣāsānaktā* — *uṣā ca naktaṃ ca*; *uṣasaḥ …*: *uṣasoṣasaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-31) — the substitute *uṣāsā* in the first member; *supāṃ sulug…* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39; the OCR prints the same on pp. 20 and 27) — the ending is replaced by *ā*; *devatādvandve ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-41) — both members keep their own accent. (Only the sūtra names and numbers legible in the print are given.)

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ममत्तु नः परिज्मा वसर्हा ममत्तु वातो अपां वृषण्वान् ।
> शिशीतमिन्द्रापर्वता युवं नस्तन्नो विश्वे वरिवस्यन्तु देवाः ॥ ३ ॥

> *mamattu naḥ parijmā vasarhā mamattu vāto apāṃ vṛṣaṇvān |*
> *śiśītamindrāparvatā yuvaṃ nastanno viśve varivasyantu devāḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

### Printed p. 16  (PDF 37)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 122".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ममत्तु । नः । परिज्मा । वसर्हा । ममत्तु । वातः । अपाम् । वृषण्वान् ॥
> शिशीतम् । इन्द्रापर्वता । युवम् । नः । तत् । नः । विश्वे । वरिवस्यन्तु । देवाः ॥ ३ ॥

> *mamattu | naḥ | parijmā | vasarhā | mamattu | vātaḥ | apām | vṛṣaṇvān ‖*
> *śiśītam | indrāparvatā | yuvam | naḥ | tat | naḥ | viśve | varivasyantu | devāḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> नोऽस्मान्वसर्हा वसनार्हो गार्हपत्यादिरूपेण । यद्वा । वासकानामाच्छादकानां वृष्ट्यादीनां हन्ताग्निः । अथवा । वसर्हा वासरो वासरस्य गमयिता । परिज्मा परितो गन्तादित्यो ममत्तु । मादयतु । तथापां वृष्ट्युदकानां वृषण्वान् वर्षणवान् वृष्ट्युत्पादको वातो वायुरस्मान्ममत्तु । किञ्च हे इन्द्रापर्वता । इन्द्रः प्रसिद्धः । पर्वतः पर्ववान् वृष्ट्यादिपूरणवान्पर्जन्यः । तौ युवं युवां नोऽस्मानस्मद्बुद्धिं वा शिशीतं तीक्ष्णीकुरुतम् । शोधयतम् इत्यर्थः । तत्र स्मात् यस्मादहं सर्वान्देवान् स्तौमि तस्माद्विश्वे सर्वेऽपि देवा नोऽस्माकं वरिवस्यन्तु । प्रभूतमन्नं प्रदातुमिच्छन्तु । समृद्धान्नप्रदानेन प्रीणयन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

> *no 'smānvasarhā vasanārho gārhapatyādirūpeṇa | yadvā | vāsakānāmācchādakānāṃ vṛṣṭyādīnāṃ hantāgniḥ | athavā | vasarhā vāsaro vāsarasya gamayitā | parijmā parito gantādityo mamattu | mādayatu | tathāpāṃ vṛṣṭyudakānāṃ vṛṣaṇvān varṣaṇavān vṛṣṭyutpādako vāto vāyurasmānmamattu | kiñca he indrāparvatā | indraḥ prasiddhaḥ | parvataḥ parvavān vṛṣṭyādipūraṇavānparjanyaḥ | tau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ no 'smānasmadbuddhiṃ vā śiśītaṃ tīkṣṇīkurutam | śodhayatam ityarthaḥ | tatra smāt yasmādahaṃ sarvāndevān staumi tasmādviśve sarve 'pi devā no 'smākaṃ varivasyantu | prabhūtamannaṃ pradātumicchantu | samṛddhānnapradānena prīṇayantītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(The remainder of the bhāṣya is the grammatical tail — *mamattu*: the root *madī harṣe*, with the sense of the causative included, in the *loṭ* the Vedic *śluḥ* in place of the vikaraṇa; reduplication; *śiśītam*: … *ī hal̥ghoḥ* …; *indrāparvatā*: by *devatādvandve ca* the former member gets *ānaṅ* — only characterised, not transcribed.)*

May Agni, the wearer of garments (? — *vasarhā*, the one worthy of dwelling, in the form of the Gārhapatya and so on), delight us; or Agni the slayer of the covering rains and so on; or Āditya, who makes the day go; may the one who goes all round (*parijmā*) delight us; and the Wind (*vāta*), rainer (*vṛṣaṇvān*) of waters, giver of rain and so on, delight us. And, O Indra and Parvata (Indra the well known; Parvata — the cloud *parjanya* who has the filling of the rain, etc.), you two sharpen us, or our minds; therefore, since I praise all the gods, may all the gods [grant] us abundant food, wishing to give it — that is, may they please us by generously giving food.

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Naḥ* — to us; *vasarhā* — Agni, [who is in] Gārhapatya and other forms (the destroyer of the covering rains and so on); (*vasarhā* — the one who makes the days go); *parijmā* — the one who moves all around (Āditya); *mamattu* — may he delight [us]; (*tathā* — likewise); *apām* — of the waters (the rain); *vṛṣaṇvān* — the one who makes it rain; *vātaḥ* — the wind; *mamattu* — may he delight (us), (and); *he indrāparvatā* — O Indra and (the one who is full of rain and the like) Parjanya; *yuvam* — you two; *naḥ* — our (minds), or (us); *śiśītam* — sharpen (or purify); *tat* — therefore (since I praise all the gods); *viśve devāḥ* — all the gods; *naḥ* — to us; *varivasyantu* — may they give abundant food.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** May Agni, in the forms Gārhapatya and so on, or the destroyer of the covering rains — and also the Āditya who moves everywhere (the lord of the days) — delight us; and may the Wind that makes the rain delight us; and O Indra and Parjanya, who are (full of rain and so on), purify our minds; may all the gods [being praised by us] graciously give us abundant food.

*(The printed English reads "circumambient divinity. the wearer" with a full stop after "divinity" as printed.)*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 3.**

***vasarhā*** — *vasanārho gārhapatyādirūpeṇa | yadvā vāsakānām ācchādakānāṃ vṛṣṭādīnāṃ hantā agniḥ | athavā vasarhā vāsaro vāsarasya gamayitā parijmā parito gantā ādityaḥ.* "Agni, who takes on many forms such as the Gārhapatya, or the Agni who destroys the clouds [and so on] that cover, or the Āditya who makes the days pass (*vasarhā*, the one who destroys the darkness at the time of dawn?)" — this is what Sāyaṇa says. On this same ṛk, in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (2-1-11), Bhaṭṭabhāskara explains:

> वसर्हा-अग्निहोत्रकरणाभिमुखस्थानार्हो वसनार्हः (पृषोदरादित्वात् न [?] शब्दो लुप्यते) यद्वा छादयित्रीणां काष्ठादीनां हन्ता अग्निः । यद्वा वासरस्य गमयिता आदित्य उच्यते ॥

> *vasarhā-agnihotrakaraṇābhimukhasthānārho vasanārhaḥ (pṛṣodarāditvāt na [?] śabdo lupyate) yadvā chādayitrīṇāṃ kāṣṭhādīnāṃ hantā agniḥ | yadvā vāsarasya gamayitā āditya ucyate ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-11, as printed; the OCR reads the same.) That is, either Agni of the sacrificial house or Āditya; either way the meaning is fitting here.

***vṛṣaṇvān*** — *varṣaṇavān vṛṣṭyutpādakaḥ*: "the one who produces rain" — "wind", says Sāyaṇa; *apāṃ vṛṣā varṣitā parjanyaḥ tadvān vātaḥ* — "the wind accompanied by Parjanya who showers rain"; so too Bhaṭṭabhāskara (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-11).

***indrāparvatā*** — *indraḥ prasiddhaḥ | parvataḥ parvavān vṛṣṭyādipūraṇavān parjanyaḥ* — Sāyaṇa explains *parvata* as the deity Parjanya. Bhaṭṭabhāskara has said that the word *parvataḥ* is also the word *saṃvatsara* (year) — "*parvatas saṃvatsara-ity ete*" [as read, `[?]`]. Whichever sense is taken, it is clear that here the word *parvata* is a synonym of a deity who is to be worshipped. Since this word is used in many places as a synonym of *śatru* (enemy), etc., and it is said "by splitting the *parvata* Indra sent the rain", etc., it is proper to discuss this usage here.

### Printed p. 18  (PDF 39)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 122".)* The use of the word *parvata* is found most in the Sūktas of Indra and the Maruts. The ordinary meaning of it is "mountain (hill)"; but it is common that here it is used as a synonym of "cloud (*megha*)". The Nirukta writer has said: 

> पर्वतः पर्ववान्पर्वतः । पर्व पुनः पृणातेः प्रीणातेर्वा । मेघोऽपि गिरिरेतस्मादेव ।

> *parvataḥ parvavānparvataḥ | parva punaḥ pṛṇāteḥ prīṇātervā | megho 'pi giriretasmādeva |*

(Ni. 1-20, as printed.) *Parvata* from *parvavān*, "having joints"; and *parva*, from the root *pṛ* "to fill" (*pṛṇāti*) or from the root *prī* "to please": thus from the word *parva*, formed from the roots that mean "to fill" or "to please", the word *parvata* is explained as mountain (hill) or cloud (*megha*). The sense of this etymology gives either the idea of filling the region where the mountain is, or the idea of satisfying beings (with the rain and so on). Here one should notice that *parvata* is an obstructing thing and also a benefactor.

Ordinarily the struggle of Indra with the Asuras and with the mountains may be called a struggle of lights with darknesses.

> वि चिद्वृत्रस्य दोधतो वज्रेण शतपर्वणा । शिरो बिभेद वृष्णिना ॥

> *vi cidvṛtrasya dodhato vajreṇa śataparvaṇā | śiro bibheda vṛṣṇinā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-6-6 [?], as read; the OCR is garbled.) In this ṛk, with the thunderbolt that has a hundred joints (*parvans*) and is made of rays, the Asura who is in the form of darkness and a coverer was destroyed. From such examples, words such as *vṛtra* show the darkness-nature that covers the world, and the word *parvata* too may be said to enter into that same darkness. Moreover, if one gives merely the ordinary meaning "hill" or "cloud", the full sense in harmony with the context will not be given. For, by the destruction of *parvata* he released the cows and the waters that had been hidden; and he made the Sun and the Dawn manifest — thus the work is fourfold. Therefore if *parvata* is taken simply as "cloud", that is not in harmony with the context.

> अदर्दरुत्समसृजो वि खानि त्वमर्णवान्बद्बधानाँ अरम्णाः ।
> महान्तमिन्द्र पर्वतं वि यद्वः सृजो वि धारा अव दानवं हन् ॥

> *adardarutsamasṛjo vi khāni tvamarṇavānbadbadhānā~ aramṇāḥ |*
> *mahāntamindra parvataṃ vi yadvaḥ sṛjo vi dhārā ava dānavaṃ han ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-32-1 [?], as read in the small type; the OCR is garbled.) In this ṛk also — *"Śiśuṃ nadīnāṃ harim adribudhnam"* —

> शिशुं नदीनां हरिमद्रिबुध्नमिति गिरिर्वा अद्रिर्गिरिबुध्ना ॥

> *śiśuṃ nadīnāṃ harimadribudhnamiti girirvā adrirgiribudhnā ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 7-3-2-15 [?], as read — a four-part reference in the small type, doubtful.) In this Brāhmaṇa sentence too, the words *parvata* and *megha* have a sense that is extraordinary and not of the world, as is shown …; this is a dark mass (*tamorāśi*) in the form of a mountain, and of the heavenly region …

---


### Printed p. 19  (PDF 40)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 1".)* …(the Brāhmaṇa sentence is understood as) a dark mass in the form of a mountain, and of the heavenly region that conceals the waters and the cows; breaking this darkness Indra, with the Maruts, makes the waters and the light flow.

> अहन्नहिं पर्वते शिश्रियाणं त्वष्टास्मै वज्रं स्वर्यं ततक्ष ।

> *ahannahiṃ parvate śiśriyāṇaṃ tvaṣṭāsmai vajraṃ svaryaṃ tatakṣa |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-2 [?], as read.) In ṛks such as this, Ahi, Śambara, Vṛtra and the like are Asuras that conceal themselves in this mass of darkness in the form of a mountain and block the flowing waters, and so Indra is praised as their destroyer. In the same way, in many places the word *parvata* is described as a synonym of *śatru* (enemy) or as a shelter for enemies. Therefore, in ṛks such as *araṃsta parvataś cit sariṣyan* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1[?]-[?], as read) and *kuhmāc cid asya parvatā bhayante* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1[?]-13 [?]) it is said that the mass of darknesses in the form of mountains fear Indra, who is of the nature of light, as soon as he is visible; and that he shut them up in the underworld.

Contrary to these descriptions, it is said in many places that *parvata* is the thunderbolt of the nature of light, and the presiding deity of the rains and so on, Parjanya.

> प्राक्राद्धाक्राद्धरादुदक्त्रादभि जहि रक्षसः पर्वतेन ।

> *prākrāddhākrāddharādudaktrādabhi jahi rakṣasaḥ parvatena |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-104-19, as printed; the reader's OCR gives the same.)

> अस्मे रुद्रा मेहना पर्वतासो वृत्रहत्ये भरहूतौ सजोषाः ।

> *asme rudrā mehanā parvatāso vṛtrahatye bharahūtau sajoṣāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-63-1[?] [?], as read.) In ṛks such as these the mountains are helpers to Indra in the work of destroying enemies.

> प्र पूषणं विष्णुमग्निं पुरन्धिं सवितारमोषधीः पर्वताँश्च ।

> *pra pūṣaṇaṃ viṣṇumagniṃ purandhiṃ savitāramoṣadhīḥ parvatā~śca |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-5[?]-[?] [?], as read.)

> शं नः पर्वता ध्रुवयो भवन्तु शं नः सिन्धवः शमु सन्त्वापः ।

> *śaṃ naḥ parvatā dhruvayo bhavantu śaṃ naḥ sindhavaḥ śamu santvāpaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-35-4 [?], as read.) In such ṛks *parvata* is invited along with deities such as Mitra, Varuṇa and Pūṣan.

> *yuvaṃ tamindrāparvatā puroyudhā yo naḥ pṛtanyādapa taṃtamiddhataṃ vajreṇa taṃtamiddhatam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-132-6, as read; the OCR gives "…132-…" in the same place.)

### Printed p. 20  (PDF 41)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 122".)*

> इन्द्रापर्वता बृहता रथेन वामीरिष आ वहतं सुवीराः ।

> *indrāparvatā bṛhatā rathena vāmīriṣa ā vahataṃ suvīrāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-53-1 [?], as read.) In these places and in the ṛk in hand there is, jointly for Indra and for Parvata, invocation and praise. Here the Sāyaṇa has said that by *parvata* is meant Parjanya; *parvata* is the deity to be worshipped (*ārādhya devate*).

***śiśītam*** — *tīkṣṇīkurutaṃ, śodhayatam ity arthaḥ* — "make [us] sharp, or make [us] pure" — that is the sense of *śiśītam*; it also has the sense of *tīkṣṇa*, *harita* ("tawny"); it indicates energy, vigour, alertness. Here the sense is *śuddha*, "pure" (Sanskrit as printed).

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** *Mamattu* — the root *madī harṣe*; since the causative action is shown, it is a root with the causative sense included; the suffix *tip* in the 3rd person singular; *eruḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-86) *u*; *bahulaṃ chandasi*, the vikaraṇa gets *śluḥ* by that, and by *ślau* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-10) reduplication of the root, the first consonant remains in the reduplicative syllable, and by *khari ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-55) the root's *d* becomes *t*; since it is at the start of the word, the *nighāta* does not arise, and the root's accent remains because the suffix is *pit*. *Parijmā* — the root *jani prādurbhāve*; with the prefix *pari* before it, formed by *śvanvan… pūṣan…* (Uṇ. Sū. 1-157, as printed; the reader's OCR reads the same) with the suffix *kani*; the elision of the root's penultimate and the *makāra* ending. *Apām* — the word *ap*, feminine, always plural; genitive plural; *ūḍidaṃpadādi* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) gives the ending the acute. *Śiśītam* — the root *śo tanūkaraṇe*, of the *divādi* class; *loṭ*, 2nd person dual, *thas* is replaced by *tam*; by *bahulaṃ chandasi* the vikaraṇa *śyan* is replaced by *śluḥ*; the *ā* in place of the root vowel by *ād eca upadeśe 'śiti* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-45 as read; the OCR prints "6-1-455"); when *ślu* follows, reduplication of the root (*ślau*); by *śābhyastayor ātaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-112) the *ā* of the root becomes *ī*-ish (*itva*); and by *bahulaṃ chandasi* the reduplicative syllable gets *itva*; so the form *śiśītam*; since it stands at the beginning of the word, the *nighāta* does not arise, and the suffix being *pit* the root accent remains (as in *mamattu*). *Indrāparvatā* — *indraś ca parvataś ca*; by *devatādvandve ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-26) the first member takes *ānaṅ*.

Sū. 7-1-39) puts *ā* in its place; by *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) the *nighāta* accent. *Yuvam* — *prathamāyāś ca dvivacane bhāṣāyām* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-88): the *ātva* is done in worldly speech only, so it does not occur in the Chandas; the ending *am*; in the dual *yuvāvau dvivacane* — *yuvā* in place of the *m*-ending. *Viśve* — in the nominative plural when *jas* comes, *jasaḥ śī* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-17) the substitute *śī*; guṇa; *svāṅgakamadantānām* … (Phiṭ-sūtra 29, as printed) — the *adanta* pronoun, the initial udātta. *Varivasyantu* — *varivas* is a nominal stem; when the sense "of that action" is intended, *namovarivaścitraṅaḥ kyac* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-19) the suffix *kyac*; *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-32) — *varivasya* gets the name root; loṭ 3rd plural; being after an *atiṅanta* by *tiṅ atiṅaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) the *nighāta* accent. *Devāḥ* — *dyotanaśīlāḥ devāḥ*; it belongs to the *pacādi* group, so the suffix *ac*; guṇa of the root's light vowel; final udātta by the suffix accent. ‖ 3 ‖

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उत त्या मे यशसा श्वेतनायै व्यन्ता पान्तौशिजो हुवध्यै ।
> प्र वो नपातमपां कृणुध्वं प्र मातरा रास्पिनस्यायोः ॥ ४ ॥

> *uta tyā me yaśasā śvetanāyai vyantā pāntauśijo huvadhyai |*
> *pra vo napātamapāṃ kṛṇudhvaṃ pra mātarā rāspinasyāyoḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत । त्या । मे । यशसा । श्वेतनायै । व्यन्ता । पान्ता । औशिजः । हुवध्यै ।
> प्र । वः । नपातम् । अपाम् । कृणुध्वम् । प्र । मातरा । रास्पिनस्य । आयोः ॥ ४ ॥

> *uta | tyā | me | yaśasā | śvetanāyai | vyantā | pāntā | auśijaḥ | huvadhyai |*
> *pra | vaḥ | napātam | apām | kṛṇudhvam | pra | mātarā | rāspinasya | āyoḥ ‖ 4 ‖*
