*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 3".)* **Special topics, Ṛk 12 (continued).** ***śardham*** (continued):

> इन्द्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमूतये मारुतं शर्धो अदितिं हवामहे ।

> *indraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimūtaye mārutaṃ śardho aditiṃ havāmahe |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-106-1, as read.) In this ṛk *mārutaṃ śardhaḥ* means the strength of the Maruts — a strength in the form of a group-power.

> स हि शर्धो न मारुतं तुविष्वणिरप्नस्वतीषूर्वरास्विष्टनिरार्तनास्विष्टनिः ।

> *sa hi śardho na mārutaṃ tuviṣvaṇirapnasvatīṣūrvarāsviṣṭanirārtanāsviṣṭaniḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-127-6 [?], as read.) In this ṛk *mārutaṃ śardhaḥ* is explained as the strength of the Maruts — or the strength in the form of the group-power of the deities, the Maruts, which ordinarily this word indicates; and in ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-71-8; 1-139-1 it is used of Agni too. Since food, or sustenance, is a strengthener of power, the bhāṣyakāra has taken the word in the ṛk in hand as food that gives strength.

***daśatayasya*** — *daśendriyasaṃvardhakatvena daśāvayavasyānnasya*: "of the food of ten parts, as it increases the ten organs" — that is, food that nourishes the body that has ten organs. In the next ṛk of this same Sūkta [that is, Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-13] this word occurs; there the bhāṣyakāra says *daśatayasya dhāseḥ dāśendriyatṛptisādhanatvena daśāvayavasyānnasya* … *daśacamasagṛhītatvād annasya daśavidhatvam* — he explains it as "ten kinds of food that are the means of satisfying the ten organs". [As] the food (or Soma) is held in ten *camasa* vessels, there are ten kinds. And in

> मा मामेधो दशतयश्चितो धाक् प्र यद्वां बद्धस्त्मनि खादति ष्ठाम् ।

> *mā māmedho daśatayaścito dhāk pra yadvāṃ baddhastmani khādati ṣṭhām |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-158-4 [?], as read.) the bhāṣyakāra has explained the word *daśatayaḥ* as "*daśayaḥ* — dwelling [in the ten]". Hence the word *daśataya* has only the meaning "ten-fold" or "of ten kinds". In the context in hand it is explained, so as to fit it, as "that which is the means of satisfying the ten organs".

***naṃśe*** — *daśatayasya naṃśe* — "to us, [the sacrificers] who offer food in the form of oblation and call [you], give the food that gives strength to bring about the defeat of enemies" — thus the gods speak among themselves; that is the sense.

***dyumnāni*** — Among the twenty-eight names of wealth, *mahaṃ rekṇaḥ* and so on, the word *dyumna* is recorded (Ni. 2-10 [?] — as read by me; the reader's OCR gives "39" for the Nirukta reference here too, the hyphen lost), so *dyumnāni* means "riches". In this ṛk the bhāṣyakāra has explained *dyotamānānnāni*:

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 122".)* "foods that shine, that is, nourishing foods" (Ni. 5-5 [?] — as read by me; the OCR has "39" in this place). Yāska says: *dyumnaṃ dyotateḥ yaśo vā annaṃ vā* — "*dyumna* is from *dyut*, 'to shine': glory, or food" — and with this derivation (of "the glory that shines well, or food"), to support this meaning:

> शतं ते शिप्रिन्नूतयः सुदासे सहस्रं शंसा उत रातिरस्तु ।
> जहि वर्धर्नुषो मर्त्यस्यास्मे द्युम्नमधि रत्नं च धेहि ॥

> *śataṃ te śiprinnūtayaḥ sudāse sahasraṃ śaṃsā uta rātirastu |*
> *jahi vardharnuṣo martyasyāsme dyumnamadhi ratnaṃ ca dhehi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3[?]-[?], as read.) — they have cited this ṛk as an example.

***vasutātiḥ*** — *vasūnāṃ dhanānāṃ tātir vistāraḥ*: "the spread (abundance) of wealth" — wealth in abundance, abundant wealth. The word *vasutāti* occurs in the ṛk that follows and nowhere else. For this word the bhāṣyakāra [says] *vasutātir vasūnāṃ haviḥ-lakṣaṇānāṃ dhanānāṃ vā vistārayitāra ṛtvijaḥ | vacanavyatyayaḥ* — "the priests who spread the wealth in the form of oblations; the number is changed [from plural to singular]"; since the priests offer oblation-wealth, "*vasutātiḥ*" means the priests. Here he has said the singular is used in place of the plural by *vyatyaya*.

***prabhṛtheṣu*** — *prakṛṣṭabharaṇeṣu yāgeṣu*: "in sacrifices which are attended with excellent preparations" — in sacrifices equipped with excellent materials.

As the main intention of the second half of this ṛk, one may say, according to the opinion of the Western scholar Wilson: "all the deities should come and accept the foods in the form of Soma, which the priests offer abundantly in the sacrifice."

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 12, noted briefly; sūtra numbers not reproduced).** *Dhāma* — the root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* — *loṭ*-sense in *luṅ*; in the 1st person plural the suffix *mas*; *nityaṃ ṅitaḥ* — the *s* is dropped; when *cli* comes, *sic*; *gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* — its *luk*; *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi* — the *aṭ* augment does not come; after an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*. *Avocan* — the root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; *luṅ*, 3rd plural, the suffix *jhi*; elision of the *i*; *jhoṃtaḥ* — the *ant*; when *cli* comes, *asyativakti khyātibhyo 'ṅ* — the *aṅ*; *vaca um* — …

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 3".)* **Grammar page, continued (Ṛk 12, noted briefly).** *Avocan* (concluded) — the augment *um* in the root after *aṅ* …; by *mider guṇaḥ* [as printed in part] guṇa; the augment *aṭ* for the stem; after an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*. *Daśatayasya* — *daśa avayavā asya, daśatayan*; *saṅkhyāyā avayave tayap* the suffix *tayap*; since it is *pit*, the suffix *ini*-like is unaccented. *Vasutātiḥ* — *vasūnāṃ tātiḥ vasutātiḥ*; the root *tan vistāre*; in the sense of action by *striyāṃ ktin* the suffix *ktin*; by *vyatyaya* the *ā*-substitution for the root when it follows; *marutvṛdhādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṅkhyānam* — the accent of the end of the first member; or by *sarvadevāt tātil* the suffix *tātil*, which was prescribed [for *sarva* and *deva*], comes by *vyatyaya* in its own sense after this word too; by *liti* the first-member acute. *Rāran* — the root *ramu krīḍāyām*; in the sense of intensity, *dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ* the suffix *yaṅ*; *yaṅo 'ci ca* the *luk*; after a *yaṅluganta* the Vedic present sense *luṅ*; 3rd plural, *jhi*, the *ant*, loss of the *i*; *dīrgha iṇkitaḥ* — the lengthening of the reduplicative syllable; the connection with the word *yeṣu* before it, *yadvṛttānnityam* — the *nighāta* is prevented; the first-syllable acute of the suffix; the augment *aṭ* is not [added] in the Vedic way. In the second explanation, the root *rā dāne*; *leṭ*, 3rd plural, *jhi*; *itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* — the loss of the *i*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* — a substitute for *śap*, *śluḥ*; taking this as the cause, doubling of the root; *chandasy ubhayathā* — since the vikaraṇa has the name *ārdhadhātuka*, *sārvadhātuka*-cause *jit*… *ato lopa iṭi ca* the loss of the root's *ā*; for that reason *abhyastānām ādiḥ* the first-syllable acute does not arise. *Sanvantu* — the root *ṣaṇu dāne*; *loṭ*, 3rd plural; after an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*. In the second explanation, the root *vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau*; as before the suffix *jhi*, the *ut* substitute; *vyatyayo bahulam* — *u* as the vikaraṇa for *śap*; the form as before. ‖ 12 ‖

#### Ṛk 13

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> मन्दामहे दशतयस्य धासेर्द्विर्यत्पञ्च बिभ्रतो यन्त्यन्ना ।
> किमिष्टाश्व इष्टरश्मिरेत ईशानासस्तरुष ऋञ्जते नॄन् ॥ १३ ॥

> *mandāmahe daśatayasya dhāserdviryatpañca bibhrato yantyannā |*
> *kimiṣṭāśva iṣṭaraśmireta īśānāsastaruṣa ṛñjate nṝn ‖ 13 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> मन्दामहे । दशतयस्य । धासेः । द्विः । यत् । पञ्च । बिभ्रतः । यन्ति । अन्ना ।
> किम् । इष्टाश्वः । इष्टरश्मिः । एते । ईशानासः । तरुषः । ऋञ्जते । नॄन् ॥ १३ ॥

> *mandāmahe | daśatayasya | dhāseḥ | dviḥ | yat | pañca | bibhrataḥ | yanti | annā |*
> *kim | iṣṭāśvaḥ | iṣṭaraśmiḥ | ete | īśānāsaḥ | taruṣaḥ | ṛñjate | nṝn ‖ 13 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> मन्दामहे । स्तुमो वयं देवान् । मदि स्तुतौ । इदित्त्वान्नुम् ॥ किमर्थम् । दशतयस्य धासेर्दशेन्द्रियतृप्तिसाधनत्वेन दशावयवस्यान्नस्य यद्यस्माद्द्विः पञ्च दशविधान्यन्नानि । दशचमसगृहीतत्वादन्नस्य दशविधत्वम् । एवंविधमन्नं बिभ्रतो धारयन्तो दश चमसाध्वर्यवो यन्ति होमाय गच्छन्त्याहवनीयं प्रति । यद्वा । आश्वमेधिकानि दशान्नानि जुहोतीत्याम्नातान्याज्यमधुप्रभृतीनि [?] दशविधान्यन्नानि विश्वेभ्यो होतुं धारयन्तो यन्ति यदा तदा मन्दामह इति । न चेष्टाश्वप्रभृतीन्यप्यनिहाय [?] कस्मादस्मान्स्तुत्यागमिष्यन्तीति वाच्यम् । तरुषः शत्रूणां तारकान् । तरतेरौणादिक उसिन् ॥ नॄन् नेतृकर्माणाम् [?] । एवं महानुभावान् वरुणादीन्विश्वांश्च देवानेतन्नामको राजा किमृञ्जते । किं प्रसाधयति । तथेष्वरश्च [?] किमृञ्जते । एते इदानीं वर्तमाना ईशानासः पृथिव्या ईश्वरा राजानश्च किं प्रसाधयन्ति । यद्वा । येषां स्तोतॄणामस्माकमेते स्तुता देवा ईशानासः स्वामिनः किल तादृशांस्तरुषः शत्रूणां तारकान् नॄन् कर्मनिर्वाहकानस्मानिष्टाश्वादयः किं साधयन्ति किमुपद्रवन्ति प्रभवन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

> *mandāmahe | stumo vayaṃ devān | madi stutau | idittvānnum ‖ kimartham | daśatayasya dhāserdaśendriyatṛptisādhanatvena daśāvayavasyānnasya yadyasmāddviḥ pañca daśavidhānyannāni | daśacamasagṛhītatvādannasya daśavidhatvam | evaṃvidhamannaṃ bibhrato dhārayanto daśa camasādhvaryavo yanti homāya gacchantyāhavanīyaṃ prati | yadvā | āśvamedhikāni daśānnāni juhotītyāmnātānyājyamadhuprabhṛtīni [?] daśavidhānyannāni viśvebhyo hotuṃ dhārayanto yanti yadā tadā mandāmaha iti | na ceṣṭāśvaprabhṛtīnyapyanihāya [?] kasmādasmānstutyāgamiṣyantīti vācyam | taruṣaḥ śatrūṇāṃ tārakān | taraterauṇādika usin ‖ nṝn netṛkarmāṇām [?] | evaṃ mahānubhāvān varuṇādīnviśvāṃśca devānetannāmako rājā kimṛñjate | kiṃ prasādhayati | tatheṣvaraśca [?] kimṛñjate | ete idānīṃ vartamānā īśānāsaḥ pṛthivyā īśvarā rājānaśca kiṃ prasādhayanti | yadvā | yeṣāṃ stotṝṇāmasmākamete stutā devā īśānāsaḥ svāminaḥ kila tādṛśāṃstaruṣaḥ śatrūṇāṃ tārakān nṝn karmanirvāhakānasmāniṣṭāśvādayaḥ kiṃ sādhayanti kimupadravanti prabhavantītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(150 dpi; some words doubtful, as marked.)* "*Mandāmahe*: we praise the gods (the root *madi stutau*; the *num* augment because it has the indicatory *i*). For what purpose? *Daśatayasya dhāseḥ* — of the food (*dhāsi*, food) of ten parts, as it is the means of satisfying the ten organs: since there are twice five, ten kinds of food — the food has ten kinds because it is held in ten *camasa* vessels. Bearing food of this kind, the ten *camasa*-priests (*adhvaryus*) go to the *āhavanīya* fire to make the offering. Or else: ten kinds of food — ghee, honey and so on, mentioned in the Āśvamedhika text ["he offers the ten foods"] — they go carrying, to offer to all the gods; when it is so, *mandāmahe*, 'we praise'. It must not be said, 'why will [the gods] come to us, leaving even Iṣṭāśva and the others?' [The gods are] *taruṣaḥ*, 'rescuers (*tāraka*) of enemies' — from the root *tṛ*, the *uṇādi* suffix *usin*. *Nṝn* — 'the leaders of deeds'. 'What does the king of this name (Iṣṭāśva) *ṛñjate*, what does he accomplish [against] such great-souled deities Varuṇa and the rest and all the gods? And so too Iṣṭaraśmi, what do they accomplish? What do these now-existing lords (*īśānāsaḥ*) of the earth, the kings, accomplish?' Or else: 'to us the praisers who have praised these gods, who are indeed lords (*svāmin*), what can Iṣṭāśva and the others accomplish [against] such men, we the *taruṣaḥ* (rescuers of enemies?), the leaders who carry out the sacrificial work — what can they trouble, what power can they have?' — that is the sense."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Yat* — because; *daśatayasya* — (that increases the ten organs) of ten kinds; *dhāseḥ* — of food; *dviḥ pañca* — ten (since it is held in ten *camasa* vessels); *annā* — (in the form of oblation) the foods; *bibhrataḥ* — carrying (the Adhvaryus and others); *yanti* — go (to make the offering).

(How can they harm?)]

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** When (the Adhvaryus and others) go to offer the ten kinds of food, having taken it in the ten *camasas*, we praise the Viśvedevas. What satisfaction can Iṣṭāśva, Iṣṭaraśmi and other kings give, as the Viśvedevas are the rescuers of enemies and the carriers out of sacrificial works? (Having obtained the Viśvedevas as lords, how can Iṣṭāśva and the others harm us, who are rescuers of enemies and workers at the rites?)

**Printed English (as printed):** *we rejoice that for the satisfaction of the ten (organs of sense) the (priests) bearing the twice five (ladles of) sacrificial food, proceed (to the altar). What can Ishtashwa; (what can) Ishtarashmi, (what can) those who are now lords of the earth, achieve (with respect) to the leaders of men, the conquerors of their foes?*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 13.**

***daśatayasya dhāseḥ*** — *daśendriyatṛptisādhanatvena daśāvayavasyānnasya*: the commentator explains it as food which is the means of satisfying the ten organs — the five organs of action and the five organs of knowledge, ten in all. Since *daśatayasya* means "of ten kinds", it can also mean the oblations, Soma, ghee and other materials placed in the ten *camasa* vessels. The word *dhāsi* is recorded among the twenty-eight names of food (Ni. 3-9, as read by the reader's OCR).

***dviḥ pañca*** — that is, ten. *Daśavidhānyannāni* — *daśacamasagṛhītatvād annasya daśavidhatvam*: here the foods placed in the ten *camasa* vessels are called "foods of ten kinds".

***bibhrataḥ yanti annā*** — *ṛtvijaḥ*, that is, the Adhvaryus and the rest, carry in their hands the foods with which the ten vessels are filled, in order to offer them to the gods, and go to the *āhavanīya* fire to make the oblation.

Or else, in the Aśvamedha sacrifice, the commentator gives another meaning: they prepare ten kinds of oblation materials — ghee, honey, food and so on — and go near the fire to offer them to the Viśvedevas.

***iṣṭāśvaḥ, iṣṭaraśmiḥ*** — The commentator has explained these words as kings of these names. Since these words occur nowhere else in the Ṛgveda except in this ṛk, nothing more can be said about them.

***īśānāsaḥ*** — *vartamānā pṛthivyā īśvarā rājānaś ca*: "the present lords of the earth" — that is, kings, chiefs and so on.

The meaning of the second half of this ṛk is obscure; the seer's intention is not clearly understood.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 13, noted briefly; sūtra numbers not reproduced).** *Mandāmahe* — the root *madi stutau*; *idito num dhātoḥ* the *num* augment; *laṭ*, 1st plural, the suffix *mahiṅ*; *ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere* — *e* for the *ṭi*-part; the vikaraṇa *śap*; *ato dīrgho yañi* — lengthening of the stem's *a*; at the beginning of the verse-quarter no *nighāta*; since a *lasārvadhātuka* follows the *a* of the stem, by *tāsyanudāttet…* the *a* is unaccented, so the root accent remains. *Bibhrataḥ* — the root *ḍubhṛñ bharaṇe*; in the sense of *laṭ* the suffix *śatṛ*; the vikaraṇa *śluḥ*; reduplication of the root; *bhṛñām it* — *i* in the reduplicative syllable; since *sārvadhātukam apit* the suffix is *ṅit*-like, no guṇa; *yaṇ* substitution; *nābhyastāc chatuḥ* — in the nominative plural the *num* augment does not come; *abhyastānām ādiḥ* — the first-syllable acute. *Yanti* — the root *iṇ gatau*, *adādi*; *laṭ*, 3rd plural, *jhi*; *jhoṃtaḥ* — *ant*; *iṇo yaṇ* — *yaṇ* for the root; since *yvoḥ…* the *nighāta* does not arise; the suffix's first-syllable acute. *Annā* — in the neuter plural, when *śi* has come, *śeś chandasi bahulam* the *śi* is dropped.

> *hiraṇyakarṇaṃ hiraṇyavikārakuṇḍalādyupetakarṇaṃ maṇigrīvaṃ ratnādyupetakaṇṭham | etaddvayaṃ sarvāvayavasyāpyupalakṣaṇam | evaṃ sarvāṅgābharaṇayuktamarṇaḥ araṇīyaṃ rūpaṃ tatpraśaṃsanaṃ putrādikamityarthaḥ [?] | uktalakṣaṇamasmadīyaṃ rūpaṃ vā no 'smākaṃ viśve sarve devā varivasyantu | paricarantu | prayacchantvityarthaḥ | aryo 'raṇīyo viśleṣāṃ [?] devānāṃ saṅgho jagmuṣīḥ stoturmukhānnirgacchantīrgiraḥ stutīrusrāḥ vikāre prakṛtiśabdaḥ kṣīrājyādīni havīṃṣi ca sadyo 'smadyāgamanānantarameva cākantu kāmayantām | chāndasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ parasmaipadaṃ ca | yadvā | yajurluki nugabhāvaḥ | ā cākantiti vā yojyam | paryāptaṃ kāmayantāmityarthaḥ | keṣviti taducyate | asme asmākaṃ sambandhiṣūbhayeṣu stotreṣu yaṣṭṛṣu ca | yadvā | asmākamubhayeṣvaihikāmuṣmikeṣu phaleṣu ‖*

*(150 dpi; a few words doubtful.)* "*Hiraṇyakarṇam*: one whose ear has golden earrings and the like; *maṇigrīvam*: one whose neck has jewels and the like. These two stand for all the limbs; thus *arṇaḥ* — a form (*araṇīyam rūpam*) adorned with ornaments on all limbs, [that is] children and the like who are to be praised. Or [that] form of ours of the kind described: may all the gods (*viśve devāḥ*) *varivasyantu* — wait upon [us], bestow [it]. *Aryaḥ* — the company of all the deities, worthy to be approached; *jagmuṣīḥ* — the praises coming out of the praiser's mouth; *usrāḥ* — milk, ghee and other oblations (the word for the original [cow] is used for the product): may they at once — immediately after our sacrifice — desire (*cākantu*), 'wish': *śap* with *śluḥ* and *parasmaipada* in the Vedic way; or else the *num* is absent when the *luk* of *yaj*; or *ā cākantu* may be joined: 'let them wish sufficiently'. In what? *Asme*, in our — both the praises and the sacrificers; or, in both our results in this world and the next."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Hiraṇyakarṇam* — one who has golden earrings; *maṇigrīvam* — one who has a jewelled necklace; *arṇaḥ* — one of pleasing form; *tat* — sons and the like; *naḥ* — to us; *viśve devāḥ* — Viśvedevas; *varivasyantu* — may they favour; *aryaḥ* — the company (of the Viśvedevas) worthy of praise; *ā jagmuṣīḥ* — coming from the mouth of the praiser; *giraḥ* — the praising words; *usrāḥ* — the oblations of milk and the like; *asme* — of us (to us); *ubhayeṣu* — in the two kinds of results (the benefits of this world and the next); *sadyaḥ* — at once; *ā cākantu* — may they greatly desire (may they favour strongly).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** May the Viśvedevas favour us with sons and the like, adorned with earrings and jewelled necklaces; may that venerable company [of the gods] accept the praises that issue from the mouth of the praiser, and the oblations given by the sacrificer. May they strongly desire (*apekṣa*, accept) both the results — of this world and of the next — of us who are theirs.

**Printed English (as printed):** *May all the gods favour us with a person decorated with golden earrings and jewel necklace: may the venerable (company of the deities) be propitiated by the praises issuing (from the mouth of the worshipper): may our offerings be acceptable to them, and (may they be pleased) with both (our praises and offerings).*

### Printed p. 63  (PDF 84)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 3".)* **Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 14.**

***hiraṇyakarṇam, maṇigrīvam*** — the prayer is that the deities should bless us with children and others who wear golden ornaments such as earrings in the ears and jewelled necklaces and other ornaments on the neck. Or the prayer is: "Be gracious so that we ourselves may wear earrings and the like and jewelled necklaces on the neck."

***arṇaḥ*** — though the word *arṇa* is recorded among the hundred names of water (Ni. 2-23, as read by the reader's OCR), here the bhāṣyakāra explains *araṇīyaṃ rūpaṃ* — "a son of pleasing form".

***aryaḥ*** — the word *arya* has the meaning of master, lord; here the bhāṣyakāra says "the group of the Viśvedevas".

***gira ā jagmuṣīḥ*** — the praising words coming forth from our mouth.

***usrāḥ*** — *usriyeti gonāma | usrāviśvo 'syāṃ bhogāḥ usreti ca* (Ni. 4-19, as read by the reader's OCR) — "*usriyā* is a name of the cow; *usrā* …". Though the word *usrāḥ* means "cows that give milk", as the bhāṣyakāra says, *vikāre prakṛtiśabdaḥ* — "the name of the original is used for the product": *kṣīrājyādīni haviṃṣi ca* — milk, ghee and the like; by usage the word *usrāḥ* is employed for things made from cows, namely milk, ghee and the like. In some places *usrāḥ* also means "rays" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-171-5 and so on).

***ubhayeṣu*** — two kinds of people, those who praise and those who sacrifice; or, in another sense, this world and the other world.

***asme*** — this word is used in the sense of all seven cases. For example:

(1) *asme te bandhuḥ | vayam ity arthaḥ* — "*asme ity etat padaṃ sarvavibhaktyantam | tasmād ekārtham | ekam eva hy etac chabdarūpaṃ saptasv api vibhaktyartheṣu vartate | prakaraṇādivaśāt tasya niyamo bhavati | tadyathā — prathamāyās tvat — asme te bandhuḥ | vayam ity arthaḥ*" — that is, the word *asme* is used in the sense of the seven cases according to the context; according to the context in each place, any of the seven cases may be given to this word. For example, in the sentence *asme te bandhuḥ* the word *asme* has the sense *vayam*, "we"; this is an example of the meaning of the first case —

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 14, noted briefly; sūtra numbers not reproduced).** *Hiraṇyakarṇam* — *hiraṇyaṃ karṇau yasya saḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*: the accent of the first member; accusative singular. *Arṇaḥ* — the root *ṛ gatau*; *arti iti arṇaḥ*; *udake nuṭ ca* (Uṇ. Sū. 4-636, as read by the reader's OCR) the suffix *asun* and the augment *nuṭ*; guṇa of the root and *ra*; *ñnityādir nityam* — the initial acute. *Varivasyantu* — *varivas* is a nominal stem; when the sense "to do this" is intended, *namovarivaścitrāṅaḥ kyac* the suffix *kyac*; *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* — it takes the name of a root; *loṭ*, 3rd plural, *jhi*, the substitute *ut*, *ant*; after an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*. *Aryaḥ* — the root *ṛ gatau*; *āryaḥ svāmivaiśyayoḥ* — the suffix *yat* by irregular formation; *āryasya svāmyākhyā ceti* (Phiṭ. Sū. 1[?]) the final acute.

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 122".)* **Grammar page, continued (Ṛk 14, noted briefly; sūtra numbers not reproduced).** *Jagmuṣīḥ* — the root *gamḷ gatau*; when *liṭ* comes, *kvasuś ca* the suffix *kvasu*; with it as the cause, guṇa of the root [as printed, in part]; reduplication; the first consonant remains; *kuhoś cuḥ* the *j* for *g*; *gamahanajana…* the loss of the root's penultimate; since it is *ugit*, when the feminine is intended, *ugitaś ca* the suffix *ṅīp*; since it has the name *bha*, *vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam* — *saṃprasāraṇa* of the *v*; *pūrvarūpa*; *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca* — *ṣatva* of the *s* of *vasu*; the *u* of *vasu* takes the acute by the suffix accent; accusative plural. *Cākantu* — the root *kamu kāntau*; *kānti* means wish; *vyatyayo bahulam* — in *loṭ*, 3rd singular, *tu* is the *parasmaipada* suffix and *śap* gets *śluḥ*; *ślau* the reduplication of the root; *tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya* the lengthening of the reduplicative syllable; after an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*. Or: *dhātor ekācaḥ…*, *yaṅ* comes and *yajoc… ci ca* the *luk*; in the Vedic way *nugator anunāsikād…* — the *nuk* augment does not come in the reduplicative syllable; *dīrgha iṇkitaḥ* — the lengthening of the reduplicative syllable. *Asme* — the word *asmad*; when the genitive (locative) ending follows, *supāṃ sulug…* the substitute *śe*; *śeṣe lopaḥ* — the loss of the portion after *m*; the ending takes the acute. ‖ 14 ‖

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> चत्वारो मा मशर्शारस्य शिश्वस्त्रयो राज्ञ आयवसस्य जिष्णोः ।
> रथो वां मित्रावरुणा दीर्घाप्साः स्यूमगभस्तिः सूरो न द्यौत् ॥ १५ ॥

> *catvāro mā maśarśārasya śiśvastrayo rājña āyavasasya jiṣṇoḥ |*
> *ratho vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā dīrghāpsāḥ syūmagabhastiḥ sūro na dyaut ‖ 15 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> चत्वारः । मा । मशर्शारस्य । शिश्वः । त्रयः । राज्ञः । आयवसस्य । जिष्णोः ।
> रथः । वाम् । मित्रावरुणा । दीर्घऽअप्साः । स्यूमऽगभस्तिः । सूरः । न । द्यौत् ॥ १५ ॥

> *catvāraḥ | mā | maśarśārasya | śiśvaḥ | trayaḥ | rājñaḥ | āyavasasya | jiṣṇoḥ |*
> *rathaḥ | vām | mitrāvaruṇā | dīrgha 'apsāḥ | syūma 'gabhastiḥ | sūraḥ | na | dyaut ‖ 15 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> मा मां कक्षीवन्तं मशर्शारस्य । मशकीकृत्य भृशं शृणोति शारयति वामित्रानिति मशर्शारः । एतन्नामकस्य राज्ञः शिश्वः शिशवः शिशुवदप्रबुद्धाश्चत्वारः पुत्रा बाधन्त इति शेषः ॥ शिशुशब्दस्य जसादिषु छन्दसि वावचनमिति गुणाभावः ॥ तथायवसस्य सर्वतः प्राप्तान्नस्यैतन्नाम्नो राज्ञो जिष्णोर्जयशीलस्य पुत्रास्त्रयस्त्रयोऽपि बाधन्त इति शेषः । हे मित्रावरुणैतन्नामानौ देवौ वां युवयोः सम्बन्धी रथो दीर्घाप्साः अतिविस्तृतरूपः स्यूमगभस्तिः स्यूमिति सुखनाम सुखकरदीप्तिः सन् सूरो न सूर्य इवाद्यौत् । द्योतताम् । उक्तानामस्मद्विरोधिनां पुरतः स्फुरन् भयजनको भवत्वित्यर्थः ॥ द्युतेश्छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति लुङ् । द्युद्भ्यो लुङि [?] इति परस्मैपदम् । सिचि वृद्धिः परस्मैपदेषु इति वृद्धिः । बहुलं छन्दसीत्यडभावे हल्ङ्यादिसंयोगान्तलोपौ । यद्वा । द्य अभिगमने आदादिकः । छान्दसे लुङ्यतो वृद्धिर्लुकि हलि इति वृद्धिः ॥

> *mā māṃ kakṣīvantaṃ maśarśārasya | maśakīkṛtya bhṛśaṃ śṛṇoti śārayati vāmitrāniti maśarśāraḥ | etannāmakasya rājñaḥ śiśvaḥ śiśavaḥ śiśuvadaprabuddhāścatvāraḥ putrā bādhanta iti śeṣaḥ ‖ śiśuśabdasya jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanamiti guṇābhāvaḥ ‖ tathāyavasasya sarvataḥ prāptānnasyaitannāmno rājño jiṣṇorjayaśīlasya putrāstrayastrayo 'pi bādhanta iti śeṣaḥ | he mitrāvaruṇaitannāmānau devau vāṃ yuvayoḥ sambandhī ratho dīrghāpsāḥ ativistṛtarūpaḥ syūmagabhastiḥ syūmiti sukhanāma sukhakaradīptiḥ san sūro na sūrya ivādyaut | dyotatām | uktānāmasmadvirodhināṃ purataḥ sphuran bhayajanako bhavatvityarthaḥ ‖ dyuteśchandasi luṅlaṅliṭa iti luṅ | dyudbhyo luṅi [?] iti parasmaipadam | sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu iti vṛddhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasītyaḍabhāve halṅyādisaṃyogāntalopau | yadvā | dya abhigamane ādādikaḥ | chāndase luṅyato vṛddhirluki hali iti vṛddhiḥ ‖*

*(Small type; the grammar tail with its sūtra references is given as read, partly abbreviated in the print.)* "*Mā*: me, Kakṣīvān. *Maśarśāra*: 'he who makes [enemies] into gnats and greatly crushes (*śṛṇoti*, *śārayati*) the foes' — the *śiśvaḥ*, the four children (sons) of the king of this name, immature as babes, trouble [me] — this must be supplied. In the word *śiśu* the lack of guṇa in *jas* etc. is by *chandasi vā vacanam*. Likewise the three sons of the king *āyavasa* — of this name, who has obtained food on all sides — the *jiṣṇu*, 'the victorious' — trouble [me] — this is to be supplied. O Mitra and Varuṇa, deities of these names: your chariot, *dīrghāpsāḥ* ('of very wide form'), *syūmagabhastiḥ* — *syūma* is a name for 'comfort'; being of a comfort-giving radiance, may it shine (*adyaut*) like the Sun. May it shine; that is, may it be dreadful as it flashes before the enemies spoken of, our opponents. The root *dyut*, by *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* a *luṅ*; the *parasmaipada* by *dyudbhyo luṅi*; *vṛddhi* in *sic* before a *parasmaipada* suffix; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives the absence of *aṭ*, and *halṅyābbhyo…* the loss of the final *s* and the conjunct final. Or else: *dya abhigamane* of the *ādādika* class; in the Vedic *luṅ*, *ato vṛddhir luki hali* — *vṛddhi*."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Mā* — me (Kakṣīvān); *maśarśārasya* — of the king named Maśarśāra; *śiśvaḥ* — the immature; *catvāraḥ* — four (sons); and *āyavasasya* — of the one named Āyavasa (who has obtained food); *jiṣṇoḥ* — of the victorious; *rājñaḥ* — of the king; *trayaḥ* — three (sons); (*bādhante* — trouble); *he mitrāvaruṇā* — O Mitra and Varuṇa; *vām* — your; *rathaḥ* — chariot; *dīrghāpsāḥ* — of very wide form; *syūmagabhastiḥ* — of comforting light; *sūro na* — like the Sun; *adyaut* — may it shine (to be fearful to them).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Mitra and Varuṇa, the four immature sons of the king named Maśarśāra and the three sons of the king named Āyavasa trouble me, Kakṣīvān; may your chariot, of vast form and comforting light, shine like the Sun (to be terrifying to them).

### Printed p. 68  (PDF 89)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 122".)* **Printed English of Ṛk 15 (as printed):** *The four (silly) sons of Masarsara, the three of the victorious monarch Ayavasa, (annoy) me. Let your spacious and bright-rayed chariot, Mitra and Varuna, blaze (before them) like the sun, (filling them with fear).*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 15.**

***maśarśārasya, āyavasasya*** — The commentator's explanation is that these are names of two kings. Who are they? Their story is not told. Since their names are not found elsewhere in the Ṛgveda either, more details cannot be learned. A German scholar named Ludwig has held that *Maśarśāra* is *Murmurāra*, *Nāpusasa*; but there is no proper evidence for it.

***dīrghāpsāḥ*** — *apsas* is recorded among the fifteen names of form (Ni. 3-13, as read by the reader's OCR). *Dīrgha* means large, extended; the chariot is "of large, extended form".

***syūmagabhastiḥ*** — *syūmam iti sukhanāma* — "*syūma* means comfort-giving; *gabhasti* — a light or rays": the sense is "with comforting rays".

> रथो वां मित्रावरुणा दीर्घाप्साः स्यूमगभस्तिः सूरो नाद्यौत् ।

> *ratho vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā dīrghāpsāḥ syūmagabhastiḥ sūro nādyaut |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-15.) Mitra and Varuṇa, [we pray], may your chariot, of very bright form, though comforting for the eyes of those who worship, be fierce and terrible, like the light of the Sun, to our enemies — thus Mitra and Varuṇa are prayed.

As to the chariot of Mitra and Varuṇa, whose form is mild to the eyes of the worshippers:

> दर्शं नु विश्वदर्शतं दर्शं रथमधि क्षमि । एता जुषत मे गिरः ॥

> *darśaṃ nu viśvadarśataṃ darśaṃ rathamadhi kṣami | etā juṣata me giraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3?-[?], as read.) Punaḥśepa says that the chariot of Mitra and Varuṇa is seen by all, and that he himself saw it.

> हिरण्यरूपमुषसो व्युष्टावयःस्थूणमुदिता सूर्यस्य ।
> आ रोहथो वरुण मित्र गर्तमतश्चक्षाथे अदितिं दितिं च ॥

> *hiraṇyarūpamuṣaso vyuṣṭāvayaḥsthūṇamuditā sūryasya |*
> *ā rohatho varuṇa mitra gartamataścakṣāthe aditiṃ ditiṃ ca ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-6[?]-[?], as read.) In ṛks such as these the matter of Mitra and Varuṇa mounting the chariot is described.

## Sūkta 123 — *pṛthū rathaḥ* (begins at the foot of printed p. 70; the contents table gives p. 71)

**Heading (Kannada):** *nūra ippattamūraneya sūktavu* — "The hundred-and-twenty-third Sūkta."

This Sūkta, like the one that follows, is addressed to Uṣas. In this first Maṇḍala the following are the only Sūktas addressed to Uṣas: 30th Sūkta, ṛks 20–22 [?]; the 48th Sūkta (15 ṛks) [?], the 49th Sūkta (4 ṛks) [?], the 92nd Sūkta (18 ṛks) [?], the 113th Sūkta (20 ṛks) [?], the 123rd Sūkta (13 ṛks) [?] and the 124th Sūkta (13 ṛks) [?] (the numerals in this passage are small and were read at 150 dpi only). Leaving aside the last two of these, the others were explained in the earlier parts; now we shall comment on the 123rd and 124th Sūktas.

About the deity Uṣas, Yāska says: *uṣāḥ kasmād ucchatīti satyā rātrer aparaḥ kālaḥ* (Ni. 2-19, as read by the reader's OCR): that is, who is the deity Uṣas? What is her nature? What is the reason for this name? Raising such questions he says: *uṣaḥ kasmāt | ucchatīti satyaḥ | ucchī vivāse | vivāsayati hīyaṃ tamāṃsi tasmād ucchatīty enam asyāḥ karttari kārake uṣā ity etad abhidhānaṃ bhavati | kā punar iyam uṣā iti | rātrer aparaḥ kālaḥ sa uṣā ity ucyate* — he explains that the name is formed from the root *ucchī vivāse* ("to shine out"), which has the sense of "to send out". What is sent out? Darkness. Because this deity dispels darkness and spreads light, she is called Uṣas. And that time is what? The last part of the night: the time that has no darkness and is full of light, just before sunrise as the night ends, is named *uṣaḥkāla*, "dawn-time".

"Since the dawn-time arrives after the night passes, the dawn-time is said to be born from the night" — a custom. To support this, Yāska:

*(The verse that Yāska cites continues at the top of p. 71, where it is given in full; it is not written here to avoid reproducing a half-read line.)*

The seers have described the nature of this deity Uṣas in many ways, and have used many epithets according to these descriptions. Of them, sixteen principal words that apply to the deity Uṣas are listed by Yāska in this way (Ni. 2-19, OCR). *(In the lists of Ṛk references below, the reader's OCR often drops hyphens; where I give a number it is the printed one as I read it, confirmed by the OCR unless marked `[?]`.)*

***vibhāvarī*** — *viśeṣaprabhāvayuktā | viśiṣṭaprakāśayuktā* — "possessed of special glory; possessed of special light; very resplendent" — *Resplendent* (as printed in English). This word is recorded in the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-30-20; 1-48-1; 1-48-10; 1-92-14; 4-52-6; 5-79-4; 5-79-10; 8-47-14 (the second and fifth have the hyphens lost in the OCR: "1-481", "4-526").

***bhāsvatī*** — *tejasvatī | viśiṣṭaprakāśanayuktā*: "shining" (*Shining*, as printed). Recorded in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-7; 1-113-4.

***odatī*** — *undī kledane | unatti sarvaṃ nīhāreṇodakī*: "wetting everything with dew; flowing, gushing & c." (as printed). Recorded only in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-48-6; 8-69-2.

***arjunī*** — *śubhravarṇā*: "white" — *the white*. Recorded in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-49-3; 5-84-2.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (introduction to Sūkta 123)**

> कदित्थेत्यष्टादशानुवाके षट् सूक्तानि । तत्र पृथू रथ इति तृतीयं सूक्तं त्रयोदशर्चम् । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । पृथुः सप्तोनोषस्यं तु इति । दीर्घतमसः पुत्रः कक्षीवान्नृषिः शिष्यश्चान्यस्मादृषेरिति परिभाषितत्वात् । अनादेशपरिभाषया त्रिष्टुप् छन्दः । तुशब्दप्रयोगादिदमादिके सूक्ते उषोदेवताके । प्रातरनुवाके उषस्ये क्रतावस्य चोत्तरस्य च विनियोगः । अहोषस्य इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । पृथू रथ इति सूक्ते प्रत्यृचं रित्थ [?] । आश्व० [?] इति । तथाश्वि[?]नशस्त्रस्य इदमादिसूक्तद्वयस्य विनियोगः प्रातरनुवाकन्यायेन । आश्व० [?] इत्यादिसूत्रात् ॥

> *kaditthetyaṣṭādaśānuvāke ṣaṭ sūktāni | tatra pṛthū ratha iti tṛtīyaṃ sūktaṃ trayodaśarcam | atrānukramaṇikā | pṛthuḥ saptonoṣasyaṃ tu iti | dīrghatamasaḥ putraḥ kakṣīvānnṛṣiḥ śiṣyaścānyasmādṛṣeriti paribhāṣitatvāt | anādeśaparibhāṣayā triṣṭup chandaḥ | tuśabdaprayogādidamādike sūkte uṣodevatāke | prātaranuvāke uṣasye kratāvasya cottarasya ca viniyogaḥ | ahoṣasya iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | pṛthū ratha iti sūkte pratyṛcaṃ rittha [?] | āśva0 [?] iti | tathāśvi[?]naśastrasya idamādisūktadvayasya viniyogaḥ prātaranuvākanyāyena | āśva0 [?] ityādisūtrāt ‖*

The seer is Kakṣīvān, the son of Dīrghatamas — by the rule that the seer is the one who has been defined elsewhere; by the rule of the unspecified metre the metre is Triṣṭubh; from the use of the word *tu* this Sūkta and the next have Uṣas as the deity. In the *prātaranuvāka* the Sūkta has its application in the *uṣasya kratu* [the Uṣas rite] and the following; it is prescribed in the section … ; and the two Sūktas beginning with this one are applied in the Aśvina-śastra on the analogy of the *prātaranuvāka*."

### Printed p. 73  (PDF 94)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 4".)* **Anuvāda (Kannada).** Of the six Sūktas of the eighteenth Anuvāka, which begins with *kad itthā*, this Sūkta *pṛthū rathaḥ* is the third. It has thirteen ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā says "*pṛthuḥ saptonoṣasyaṃ tu*" [as read]. The seer of this Sūkta is Kakṣīvān, the son of Dīrghatamas; the metre is Triṣṭubh; since the word *tu* is used in the sūtra, this Sūkta and the next are addressed to Uṣas. At the time of reciting the *prātaranuvāka* mantras, this Sūkta and the following one are applied for the mantras connected with the Uṣas rite (*uṣasya kratu*) — so it is prescribed in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, section *ahoṣasyaḥ*, by the sūtra *pṛthū ratha iti sūkte pratyṛcam ityādi* (Āś. 4-14 [as read; the OCR has "4 14", the hyphen lost]); and for the Aśvina-śastra mantras too these two Sūktas are applied, as stated by the sentence *prātaranuvāka-nyāyena* (Āś. 6-3).

**Sūkta 123** — Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 18 ‖ Sūkta 123 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 1 ‖ Vargas 4, 5, 6 ‖ number of ṛks in this Sūkta: 13 ‖ Seer: Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa Auśija ‖ Deity: Uṣas ‖ Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पृथू रथो दक्षिणाया अयोज्यैनं देवासो अमृतासो अस्थुः ।
> कृष्णादुदस्थादर्या विहाया चिकित्सन्ती मानुषाय क्षयाय ॥ १ ॥

> *pṛthū ratho dakṣiṇāyā ayojyainaṃ devāso amṛtāso asthuḥ |*
> *kṛṣṇādudasthādaryā vihāyā cikitsantī mānuṣāya kṣayāya ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पृथुः । रथः । दक्षिणायाः । अयोजि । आ । एनम् । देवासः । अमृतासः । अस्थुः ।
> कृष्णात् । उत् । अस्थात् । आर्या । विऽहायाः । चिकित्सन्ती । मानुषाय । क्षयाय ॥ १ ॥

> *pṛthuḥ | rathaḥ | dakṣiṇāyāḥ | ayoji | ā | enam | devāsaḥ | amṛtāsaḥ | asthuḥ |*
> *kṛṣṇāt | ut | asthāt | āryā | vi 'hāyāḥ | cikitsantī | mānuṣāya | kṣayāya ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> दक्षिणायाः प्रवृद्धायाः स्वव्यापारकुशलाया उषोदेवतायाः पृथुर्विस्तीर्णो रथोऽयोजि । अश्वैर्युक्तः सन्नद्धोऽभूत् । अत्र यद्यपि देवताविशेषो न श्रुतस्तथापि सूक्तस्योषोदेवताकत्वादुषस इति गम्यते । एनं सन्नद्धं रथममृतासोऽमरणधर्माणो देवासो देवनशीला हविर्भाजो देवा आस्थुः । आस्थितवन्तः । देवयजनं गन्तुमारूढा इत्यर्थः । अनन्तरं सोषाः कृष्णात् कृष्णवर्णाद्रात्रिरूपात्तमसः सकाशादुदस्थात् । उत्थिताभूत् । कृष्णं कृष्यतेर्निकृष्टो वर्णः (नि. २-२०) इति यास्कः । कीदृशी सा । अर्या अरणीया पूजनीया विहाया विविधगमनयुक्ता महती वा । विहाया इति महन्नाम विहायो यह्वः इति तन्नाममु पाठात् । मानुषाय क्षयाय मनुष्याणां निवासाय चिकित्सन्ती अन्धकारनिवारणरूपां चिकित्सां कुर्वती । तमो निवारयन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

> *dakṣiṇāyāḥ pravṛddhāyāḥ svavyāpārakuśalāyā uṣodevatāyāḥ pṛthurvistīrṇo ratho 'yoji | aśvairyuktaḥ sannaddho 'bhūt | atra yadyapi devatāviśeṣo na śrutastathāpi sūktasyoṣodevatākatvāduṣasa iti gamyate | enaṃ sannaddhaṃ rathamamṛtāso 'maraṇadharmāṇo devāso devanaśīlā havirbhājo devā āsthuḥ | āsthitavantaḥ | devayajanaṃ gantumārūḍhā ityarthaḥ | anantaraṃ soṣāḥ kṛṣṇāt kṛṣṇavarṇādrātrirūpāttamasaḥ sakāśādudasthāt | utthitābhūt | kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣyaternikṛṣṭo varṇaḥ (ni. 2-20) iti yāskaḥ | kīdṛśī sā | aryā araṇīyā pūjanīyā vihāyā vividhagamanayuktā mahatī vā | vihāyā iti mahannāma vihāyo yahvaḥ iti tannāmamu pāṭhāt | mānuṣāya kṣayāya manuṣyāṇāṃ nivāsāya cikitsantī andhakāranivāraṇarūpāṃ cikitsāṃ kurvatī | tamo nivārayantītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(The phrase "tasmin sūkte" and the number-reference of Yāska are read as printed: Ni. 2-20, as in the OCR "2-20" on p. 76; at the end the small-type grammar reference is only characterised.)* "Of Dakṣiṇā — the grown (*pravṛddhā*), skilled in her work — the goddess Uṣas, the broad (*pṛthu*, wide) chariot was yoked (*ayoji*): it was made ready, fitted with horses. Here, though no particular deity is named, it is understood to be Uṣas, since the Sūkta is addressed to Uṣas. This ready chariot the immortal (*amṛtāsaḥ*, of deathless nature) gods (*devāsaḥ*, the shining; the gods who partake of oblations) mounted (*āsthuḥ*): that is, they ascended in order to go to the place of the divine sacrifice. Afterwards she, Uṣas, *kṛṣṇāt*, from the black — from the darkness in the form of night — rose up (*udasthāt*). *Kṛṣṇa* [is derived] from the root *kṛṣ*; it is a lower colour (Ni. 2-20), says Yāska. What kind is she? *Āryā*: worthy of approach, worthy of worship; *vihāyāḥ*: of various motion, or great — *vihāyaḥ* is a name of 'great', by its reading among the names of 'great' (*yahvaḥ*). *Mānuṣāya kṣayāya*: for the dwelling of men, *cikitsantī* — making the cure in the form of the removal of darkness: that is, dispelling the darkness."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Dakṣiṇāyāḥ* — of the skilful (Uṣas deity); *pṛthuḥ* — broad; *rathaḥ* — the chariot; *ayoji* — was made ready (yoked with horses); *enam* — this (ready chariot); *amṛtāsaḥ* — immortal; *devāsaḥ* — gods; *ā asthuḥ* — mounted (afterwards); *āryā* — worshipful; *vihāyāḥ* — of manifold motion (Uṣas); *mānuṣāya kṣayāya* — for the dwelling of men; *cikitsantī* — performing the cure in the form of removing darkness; *kṛṣṇāt* — from black (darkness); *ut asthāt* — rose up.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** The broad chariot of the skilful (Uṣas deity) was yoked with horses; the immortal gods mounted it. Afterwards the worshipful and many-moving (Uṣas deity), performing a cure in the form of removing darkness for the dwellings of men, rose up from the black (darkness).

**Printed English (as printed):** *The spacious chariot of the graceful (Dawn) has been harnessed ; the immortal gods have ascended it; the noble and all-pervading Ushas has risen up from the darkness, bringing health to human habitations.*

### Printed p. 75  (PDF 96)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 4".)* **Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 1.**

***dakṣiṇāyāḥ*** — *pravṛddhāyāḥ svavyāpārakuśalāyāḥ*: "of her who is much developed and skilled in carrying out her own work, [the goddess] Uṣas" — the two senses having been given, he has joined this word as an epithet of the deity Uṣas.

Yāska in the Nirukta has given the derivation of the word *dakṣiṇā* in several meanings (Ni. 1-7, as read by the reader's OCR).

> नूनं सा ते प्रति वरं जरित्रे दुहीयदिन्द्र दक्षिणा मघोनी ।
> शिक्षा स्तोतृभ्यो मा ति धग्भगो नो बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥

> *nūnaṃ sā te prati varaṃ jaritre duhīyadindra dakṣiṇā maghonī |*
> *śikṣā stotṛbhyo mā ti dhagbhago no bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1[?]-[?], as read; the OCR is garbled.) For the word *dakṣiṇā* in this ṛk, the Nirukta explains in one way: *dakṣiṇā dakṣateḥ samardhayati karmaṇo vṛddham samardhayatīti* — "*dakṣiṇā* [is so called] because she completes (*samardhayati*) the work, brings the deficient to fullness". Here the vṛttikāra [Sāyaṇa's predecessor] says: *yajñe hi yat kiñcid vigataṛddhikaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati tad iyaṃ samardhayati viśiṣṭaṃ hi yajñasya sādhanam etad iti* — "in the sacrifice, whatever is made deficient in its completeness is made complete by this; hence it is a special means of the sacrifice": whatever in the sacrifice is deficient in the means of completion, this makes perfect; therefore this produces prosperity; hence, in the matter of the completion of a sacrifice this is the means — so the meaning is explained. In the second explanation of the Nirukta: *api vā pradakṣiṇāgamanād diśam abhipretya digdiśasuprakṛtiḥ* [as read, doubtful] — *dakṣiṇa* means the southern direction. Here the vṛttikāra explains that the priests go round the sacrificial altar in a clockwise (*pradakṣiṇa*) circuit; the cause of this going round, namely to go first facing the south — [the sense is] that *dakṣiṇā* in the sense of the southern direction (Ni. 1-2, as read in the OCR). In the third explanation of the Nirukta, *dakṣiṇo hasto dakṣateḥ utsāhakarmaṇaḥ* ("*dakṣiṇa* is the hand, from *dakṣ* in the sense of exertion"): when working, the worker uses the right hand to show his exertion; hence *dakṣiṇā* means "the right hand". Following this meaning also, [*dakṣiṇā*] is derived from the root *dāś* "to give" (*dāśater vā syād dānakarmaṇaḥ*, "or [it comes] from the root *dāś*, in the sense of giving"), so that the word *dakṣiṇā* is formed. Following the three kinds of meaning given by the Nirukta writer, Sāyaṇa explains *pravṛddhāyāḥ*, "of one who has reached excess" (Ni. 1-3 [?], as read).

***kṛṣṇāt*** — *nikṛṣṭavarṇāt naiśāt tamasaḥ* (Ni. 1-7 [?], as read): "from the darkness of night, which is of a low (black) colour"; this is the sense. The Nirukta writer —

> रुशद्वत्सा रुशती श्वेत्यागादारैगु कृष्णा सदनान्यस्याः ।
> समानबन्धू अमृते अनूची द्यावा वर्णं चरत आमिनाने ॥

> *ruśadvatsā ruśatī śvetyāgādāraigu kṛṣṇā sadanānyasyāḥ |*
> *samānabandhū amṛte anūcī dyāvā varṇaṃ carata āmināne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-2, as printed on p. 71.) — citing this ṛk, [he says] *kṛṣṇavarṇā rātriḥ | kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣyater nikṛṣṭo varṇaḥ* (Ni. 2-20) — "*kṛṣṇa* is black-coloured night; [the word] *kṛṣṇa* is formed from the root *kṛṣ*; it means a low, base colour" — thus he has explained it.

***āryā*** — *araṇīyā pūjanīyā* — "worthy of worship": that is, that which is worthy of worship. The word *ārya* is recorded among the four names of Īśvara ("lord") (Ni. 3-11, as read). The Nirukta writer cites a use of the word *ārya* in the sense of Īśvara; but the meaning "lord" is explained as fitting one who deserves praise. For example:

> प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट नामार्यः शंसामि वयुनानि विद्वान् ।
> तं त्वा गृणामि तवसमतव्यान् क्षयन्तमस्य रजसः पराके ॥

> *pra tatte adya śipiviṣṭa nāmāryaḥ śaṃsāmi vayunāni vidvān |*
> *taṃ tvā gṛṇāmi tavasamatavyān kṣayantamasya rajasaḥ parāke ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-100-5 [?], as read; the OCR has "7-10-5".)

> अर्योऽहमीश्वरः स्तोतॄणामर्यस्त्वमसीति वा ।

> *aryo 'hamīśvaraḥ stotṝṇāmaryastvamasīti vā |*

(Ni. 5-9 [?], as read by the OCR.) Here the vṛttikāra says: *yasmād aryo 'hamasmi īśvaraḥ stutīnām udīraṇe* … or *arya asi, ārya īśvaraḥ mad-anugrahāya samarthaḥ* — "since I am a master (*ārya*), able to utter praises, I know well your qualities in order to praise you; therefore you, who are worthy of praise, [I am] able to praise; or, since you are able to show grace, you are (*ārya*) worshipful" — he explains thus. In this ṛk the word *uṣas* does not occur, but from the context he has given the sense *pūjanīyā* for the word *āryā* in describing the qualities of the deity Uṣas.

***vihāyāḥ*** — *vividhagamanayuktā mahatī vā*: "Uṣas moves about in many ways, or is filled with greatness". The word *vihāyāḥ* is recorded in the group of twenty-five names of 'great', beginning with *mahat, brahman* [as read] (Ni. 3-13, as read by the OCR). The Nirukta writer has cited a use of the word *vihāyāḥ* in this same sense (Ni. 10-26, as read by the OCR). For example:

> विश्वकर्मा विमना आद्विहाया धाता विधाता परमोत संदृक् ।
> तेषामिष्टानि समिषा मदन्ति यत्रा सप्तर्षीन् पर एकमाहुः ॥

> *viśvakarmā vimanā ādvihāyā dhātā vidhātā paramota saṃdṛk |*
> *teṣāmiṣṭāni samiṣā madanti yatrā saptarṣīn para ekamāhuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-82-[?], as read.)

### Printed p. 78  (PDF 99)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)* ***ratho āyoji*** — *aśvair yuktaḥ saṃnaddho 'bhūt*: "the chariot was made ready, yoked with horses". Here "horses" does not mean stallions; as Yāska says in the Nirukta, *aruṇo gāva uṣasaḥ* — "the red cows are Uṣas's [horses]" — the horses of Uṣas's chariot are the red-coloured cows (or rays) (Ni. 2-18 [?], as read).

***enaṃ devāso amṛtāso asthuḥ*** — the gods, deathless, mounted Uṣas's chariot. The gods' mounting Uṣas's chariot means that at dawn the sacrificer who begins the sacrifice invokes the gods, so that those gods go to the sacrificial altar at dawn together with Uṣas who is riding in her chariot — that is the sense.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 1, noted briefly; the sūtra numbers listed by the reader's OCR for this page are given in the block at the end).** *Ayoji* — the root *yuji yoge*; *luṅ* in the passive, 3rd singular, the suffix *ta*; *ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ* — *ciṇ* in place of *cli*, with the loss of *ta* by *ciṇo luk* (*ciṇo luk*, as printed); the augment *aṭ*; after an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*. *Devāsaḥ* — the root *divu*; since it is of the *pacādi* group the suffix *ac*; the guṇa of the light penultimate; final acute by *cit*; when *jas* follows, *ājjaser asuk*. *Amṛtāsaḥ* — the root *mṛṅ prāṇatyāge*; the suffix *kta*; with *nañ* in the compound, *ñño jaramarami…* the final acute of the latter member; when *jas* follows, as before the *asuk*. *Asthuḥ* — the root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; *luṅ*, 3rd plural, *jhi*; *cleḥ sic*, and by *gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ* the *luk* of *sic*; *ātaḥ* the substitute *jus* for *jhi*; *usyapadāntāt* the *pararūpa*; since it follows an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*; so too *asthāt* in the 3rd singular. *Cikitsantī* — the root *kita nivāse*; *kitaḥ…* (by the sūtra *kiter vyādhipratīkāre*) the suffix *san*; taking it as the cause, reduplication of the root by *sanyaṅoḥ*; by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* the stem *cikitsa* gets the name of a root; the suffix *śatṛ* in the sense of the present, …

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पूर्वा विश्वस्माद्भुवनादबोधि जयन्ती वाजं बृहती सनुत्री ।
> उच्चा व्यख्ययुवतिः पुनर्भूरोषा अगन्प्रथमा पूर्वहूतौ ॥ २ ॥

> *pūrvā viśvasmādbhuvanādabodhi jayantī vājaṃ bṛhatī sanutrī |*
> *uccā vyakhyayuvatiḥ punarbhūroṣā aganprathamā pūrvahūtau ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पूर्वा । विश्वस्मात् । भुवनात् । अबोधि । जयन्ती । वाजम् । बृहती । सनुत्री ।
> उच्चा । वि । अख्यत् । युवतिः । पुनःऽभूः । आ । उषाः । अगन् । प्रथमा । पूर्वऽहूतौ ॥ २ ॥

> *pūrvā | viśvasmāt | bhuvanāt | abodhi | jayantī | vājam | bṛhatī | sanutrī |*
> *uccā | vi | akhyat | yuvatiḥ | punaḥ 'bhūḥ | ā | uṣāḥ | agan | prathamā | pūrva 'hūtau ‖ 2 ‖*

*(I read the second line's* व्यख्यत्‌ *as* वि अख्यत्; *the Saṃhitā's* ऊर्ध्वा/उच्चा *is as printed* उच्चा.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> विश्वस्माद्भुवनात्सर्वस्मात्सुप्ताद्भूतजातात्पूर्वा प्रथमा सेयमुषा अबोधि । बुद्धाभूत् । उषःकालमुपगम्य हि पश्चात्सर्वे प्राणिनः प्रतिबुध्यन्ते । कीदृशी सा । वाजं गमनशीलं प्रकाशं निर्वर्त्याभकारं [?] जयन्ती पराभवं कुर्वती । यद्वा । वाजशब्दोऽन्ननामसु पठितत्वादन्नं नाम । अन्नं वै वाजः (श. ब्रा. ९-३-४-१) इति श्रुतेः । यजमानार्थमन्नं सम्पादयन्ती । बृहती महती सनुत्री सर्वं जगत्सम्भजन्ती धात्री वा प्रकाशस्य । किञ्च सोषा उच्चैरुच्चैरूर्ध्वप्रदेशेषु स्थिता सती व्यख्यत् । विचष्टे । सर्वं जगत्प्रकृतीत्यर्थः । कीदृशी सा । युवतिर्मिश्रणशीला नित्ययौवना वा पुनर्भूः पुनःपुनर्भवनशीला प्रतिदिनं वर्तमानत्वात् । सोषाः पूर्वहूतौ सत्यां प्रथमा मुख्या प्रकृष्टा सत्यागन् देवयजनदेशं प्रत्यागच्छति । प्रथम इति मुख्यनाम प्रतमो भवतीति यास्कः । नि. २-२२ । इतरदेवेभ्यः पूर्वमाहूता सती शीघ्रमेवागच्छतीत्यर्थः ॥

> *viśvasmādbhuvanātsarvasmātsuptādbhūtajātātpūrvā prathamā seyamuṣā abodhi | buddhābhūt | uṣaḥkālamupagamya hi paścātsarve prāṇinaḥ pratibudhyante | kīdṛśī sā | vājaṃ gamanaśīlaṃ prakāśaṃ nirvartyābhakāraṃ [?] jayantī parābhavaṃ kurvatī | yadvā | vājaśabdo 'nnanāmasu paṭhitatvādannaṃ nāma | annaṃ vai vājaḥ (śa. brā. 9-3-4-1) iti śruteḥ | yajamānārthamannaṃ sampādayantī | bṛhatī mahatī sanutrī sarvaṃ jagatsambhajantī dhātrī vā prakāśasya | kiñca soṣā uccairuccairūrdhvapradeśeṣu sthitā satī vyakhyat | vicaṣṭe | sarvaṃ jagatprakṛtītyarthaḥ | kīdṛśī sā | yuvatirmiśraṇaśīlā nityayauvanā vā punarbhūḥ punaḥpunarbhavanaśīlā pratidinaṃ vartamānatvāt | soṣāḥ pūrvahūtau satyāṃ prathamā mukhyā prakṛṣṭā satyāgan devayajanadeśaṃ pratyāgacchati | prathama iti mukhyanāma pratamo bhavatīti yāskaḥ | ni. 2-22 | itaradevebhyaḥ pūrvamāhūtā satī śīghramevāgacchatītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Small type at 150 dpi; the Śatapatha reference and the Nirukta number are partly doubtful, as marked.)* "From all beings (*viśvasmād bhuvanāt*) — from all creatures that were asleep — she is first (*pūrvā*): this Uṣas awoke (*abodhi*). For after Dawn's arrival all living beings wake. What is she like? *Jayantī vājam* — overcoming (*jayantī*) the *vāja*, the moving light — that is, defeating the darkness [or: *vāja* is among the names of food: 'food is *vāja*' (Śa. Brā. 9-3-4-1, as printed "೯-೩-೪-೧"; the OCR reads it clearly) — providing food for the sacrificer]. *Bṛhatī*: great; *sanutrī*: she who shares out everything to the world, or the supporter of light. And further, she, Uṣas, standing in lofty regions, *vyakhyat*: looks at, sees all the world. What is she like? *Yuvatiḥ* — ever young, or mingling; *punarbhūḥ* — becoming again and again, as she comes each day. She, Uṣas, the first at the first invocation (*pūrvahūtau*), chief, excellent, comes (*agan*) to the place of the divine sacrifice. *Prathama* is a name of 'chief': 'it becomes *pratama*', says Yāska (Ni. 2-22, as read by the reader's OCR). The sense: being invoked before the other gods, she comes at once."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Vājam* — the moving (the darkness that moves away) or [alternatively] food; *jayantī* — she who has conquered (and brings [it] to the sacrificer); *viśvasmāt* — all; *bhuvanāt* — from creatures (those asleep, born beings); *pūrvā* — first; *bṛhatī* — great; *sanutrī* — giving light (to the world) [she]; *uṣāḥ* — the deity Uṣas; *abodhi* — awoke (appeared); (*kiñca* — and); *yuvatiḥ* — ever young; *punarbhūḥ* — she who again and again appears (that [Uṣas]); *uccā* — from the lofty (regions); *vi akhyat* — looks at all the world (gives light); (*sā* — she); *pūrvahūtau* — at the first prayer (of the day); *prathamā* — before all, as excellent; *ā agan* — comes (to the sacrificial region).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Casting off the transient (shadowy) darkness and giving light (to the whole world), the great Uṣas awoke first among all the world (showed herself). Ever young and rising day after day; from a lofty region she looks at the whole world (gives light); at the sacrifice she comes first of all (before all the deities) at the first invocation.

**Printed English (as printed):** *First of all the world is she awake, triumphing over transitory (darkness): the mighty, the giver (of light) from on high, she beholds (all things): ever youthful, ever reviving, she comes first to the invocation.*

### Printed p. 81  (PDF 102)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 4".)* **Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 2.**

***viśvasmāt bhuvanāt pūrvā abodhi*** — *suptāt bhūtajātāt iyam uṣāḥ prathamā abodhi*: "from the sleeping creatures, this Uṣas awoke first". For after the dawn-time comes, all living beings awaken afterwards. The sense is: she wakes before all the creatures that sleep; that is, Uṣas rises. Then all awake — this is the sense. Here Sāyaṇa explains the word *pūrvā* as *prathamā*.

***vājaṃ jayantī*** — *gamanaśīlaṃ prakāśaṃ nirvartya andhakāraṃ parābhavaṃ kurvatī*: "the deity Uṣas, removing the darkness connected with the night, makes light so that beings may move about" — this is one sense. Here Sāyaṇa has explained the word *vāja* as darkness. Then he says *yadvā vājaśabdo 'nnanāmasu paṭhitatvād annanāma* — "or the word *vāja* is recorded among names of food": the word *vāja* is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9), among the names of battle (Ni. 5-9), and as the name of a king (Ni. 1-17); and "oblations" or "water" (Ni. 11-27) (all as read by the reader's OCR, with hyphens partly lost) — he thus gives these meanings, because the Nirukta writer gives them; and since the word is used in the Śruti passages in the sense of food — *annaṃ vai vājaḥ* (Śa. Brā. 9-3-4-1, Tai. Brā. 1-3-6-2, as read by the reader's OCR) — he also gives the meaning "food". Thereby *yajamānārthaṃ annaṃ saṃpādayantī*, "she provides food for the sake of the sacrificer" — another meaning. Thus he has given two meanings.

***bṛhatī sanutrī*** — *mahatī sarvaṃ jagat sambhajantī dātrī vā prakāśasya*: "great, sharing everything with the world, or giver of light". He explains that Uṣas stirs all the creatures in the world to go about their tasks, or that she is endowed with a greatness by which she makes light for the benefit of the whole world: two meanings. The Nirukta writer says that the word *bṛhatī* denotes "filled with greatness".

> रमध्वं मे वचसे सोम्याय ऋतावरीरुप मुहूर्तमेवैः ।
> प्र सिन्धुमच्छा बृहती मनीषावस्युरहवे कुशिकस्य सूनुः ॥

> *ramadhvaṃ me vacase somyāya ṛtāvarīrupa muhūrtamevaiḥ |*
> *pra sindhumacchā bṛhatī manīṣāvasyurahave kuśikasya sūnuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-33-5, as read.) For the word *bṛhatī* in this ṛk he has given the meaning *mahatyā*, "great".

> आ सुष्वयन्ती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ ।
> दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥

> *ā suṣvayantī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yonau |*
> *divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-6 [?], as read.) For the word *bṛhatī* in this ṛk too he has given the meaning *bṛhatyau mahatyau*, "great".

***punarbhūḥ*** — *punaḥ punar bhavanaśīlā pratidinaṃ vartamānatvāt*: "she who becomes again and again, since she is present every day": because Uṣas rises every day, it means she has a nature that stays differently on each day. That is, she is born again and again. Therefore in many ṛks it is said that this deity Uṣas is ever young:

> पुनःपुनर्जायमाना पुराणी समानं वर्णमभि शुम्भमाना ।

> *punaḥpunarjāyamānā purāṇī samānaṃ varṇamabhi śumbhamānā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-10 [?], as read.) In ṛks such as these Uṣas is described as rising again and again.

***pūrvahūtau satyām uṣāḥ prathamā — mukhyā*** — that Uṣas, at the sacrifice, when she is invoked before the other deities for the acceptance of the oblation, comes to the place where the sacrifice is going on, in front of all the deities: that is the sense. *Itaradevebhyaḥ pūrvam āhūtā satī śīghram evāgacchatīty arthaḥ* — this is Sāyaṇa's explanation.

Yāska gives for the word *prathama* the meaning "chief":

> देवानां माने प्रथमा अतिष्ठन् कृन्तत्रादेषामुपरा उदायन् ।
> त्रयस्तपन्ति पृथिवीमनूपा द्वा बर्बूकं वहतः पुरीषम् ॥

> *devānāṃ māne prathamā atiṣṭhan kṛntatrādeṣāmuparā udāyan |*
> *trayastapanti pṛthivīmanūpā dvā barbūkaṃ vahataḥ purīṣam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-27-23, as read by the reader's OCR.) In this ṛk, *prathama iti mukhyanāma pratamo bhavati* (Ni. 2-22, as read by the reader's OCR): for the word *prathama* he gives the sense "chief". In this ṛk the vṛttikāra explains *prathamāḥ* as *prakṛṣṭatamāḥ* — "most excellent" — i.e. "chief".

### Printed p. 83  (PDF 104)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 4".)* **Grammar page, continued (Ṛk 2).** …the light vowel; *ciṇo luk* — the loss of the following *ta*; the augment *aṭ* for the stem; after an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*. *Jayantī* — the root *ji jaye*; *śatṛ* in the sense of the present; the vikaraṇa *śap*; taking it as the cause, guṇa of the root's *i*; *ay*-substitution; in the feminine, *ugitaś ca* the suffix *ṅīp*; since it follows an *anupadeśa* [*śap*-vikaraṇa] and *lasārvadhātuka*, the acute is not on it, so the root accent remains; since *ṅīp* is *pit*, unaccented. *Akhyat* — the root *khyā prakathane*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* — *luṅ* in the sense of the present; *asyativaktikhyātibhyo 'ṅ* — *aṅ* in place of *cli*; *ato lopa iṭi ca* — the loss of the root's *ā*; the augment *aṭ* for the stem; after an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*. *Yuvatiḥ* — the word *yuvan*; when the feminine is intended, *yūnas tiḥ* the suffix *ti*; since *ṭi*-loss is the exception, the *prakṛtibhāva*, *nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya* the *n*-loss; the final acute by the suffix accent. *Agan* — the root *gamḷ gatau*; as before *luṅ* in the sense of the present; in the Vedic way the loss of the *m* of the root; by *vyatyaya* the plural suffix in place of the 3rd person singular; the *nighāta*. *Pūrvahūtau* — the root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *striyāṃ ktin* the suffix *ktin* in the sense of action; *bahulaṃ chandasi* the *saṃprasāraṇa* and *pūrvarūpa* of the root; *halaḥ* the lengthening of the *saṃprasāraṇa*; *tādau ca niti* — the accent of the first member; locative singular. ‖ 2 ‖

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यत् । अद्य । भागम् । विऽभजासि । नृऽभ्यः । उषः । देवि । मर्त्यऽत्रा । सुऽजाते ।
> देवः । नः । अत्र । सविता । दमूनाः । अनागसः । वोचति । सूर्याय ॥ ३ ॥

> *yat | adya | bhāgam | vi 'bhajāsi | nṛ 'bhyaḥ | uṣaḥ | devi | martya 'trā | su 'jāte |*
> *devaḥ | naḥ | atra | savitā | damūnāḥ | anāgasaḥ | vocati | sūryāya ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> सुजाते शोभनजनने देवि देवनशीले हे उषः उषःकालाभिमानिदेवते मर्त्यत्रा मनुष्याणां पालयित्री त्वमद्यास्मिन्काले नृभ्यो मनुष्येभ्यो यदद्य भागं भजनीयं स्वकीयप्रकाशस्यांशं विभजासि विभज्य ददासि । यद्वा । मर्त्येषु मध्ये नृभ्यो यजमानेभ्यो देवानां भागं विभज्य ददासि । उषसि प्रवृत्तायां हविषो दीयमानत्वादुषसो वाऽतृत्वमुपचर्यते । अत्रास्मिन्भागविषये दमूना यजमानेभ्योऽभिमतफलदानमनाः । दमूना दममना वा दानमना वा दान्तमना वेति निरुक्तवचनं (नि. ४-४) तादृशः सविता प्रेरको देवोऽस्मान् अनागसो वोचति । अपापान् याग-योग्यान्स्वेतु । अनुग्रहाया… इत्यर्थः । किमर्थम् । सूर्यायास्माद्यागदेशं प्रति सूर्यस्यागमनार्थम् ॥

> *sujāte śobhanajanane devi devanaśīle he uṣaḥ uṣaḥkālābhimānidevate martyatrā manuṣyāṇāṃ pālayitrī tvamadyāsminkāle nṛbhyo manuṣyebhyo yadadya bhāgaṃ bhajanīyaṃ svakīyaprakāśasyāṃśaṃ vibhajāsi vibhajya dadāsi | yadvā | martyeṣu madhye nṛbhyo yajamānebhyo devānāṃ bhāgaṃ vibhajya dadāsi | uṣasi pravṛttāyāṃ haviṣo dīyamānatvāduṣaso vā 'tṛtvamupacaryate | atrāsminbhāgaviṣaye damūnā yajamānebhyo 'bhimataphaladānamanāḥ | damūnā damamanā vā dānamanā vā dāntamanā veti niruktavacanaṃ (ni. 4-4) tādṛśaḥ savitā prerako devo 'smān anāgaso vocati | apāpān yāga-yogyānsvetu | anugrahāyā… ityarthaḥ | kimartham | sūryāyāsmādyāgadeśaṃ prati sūryasyāgamanārtham ‖*

*(Small type; I could not settle some letters at the end of the passage; the sense as given in the Kannada follows.)* "O well-born, divine Uṣas, deity presiding over the dawn-time, protectress of mortals (*martyatrā*): whatever share (*bhāga*) to be enjoyed, a part of your own light, you apportion (*vibhajāsi*) to men today — or: among mortals, you divide and give the gods' portion to the sacrificers, since the oblation is given once Uṣas has begun, [and hence] the giving is figuratively attributed to Uṣas. In this matter of the share, may the god Savitṛ, the impeller, *damūnāḥ* — whose mind is bent on giving the desired fruit to the sacrificers [*damūnā* is *dama-manāḥ*, 'of subdued mind', or *dāna-manāḥ*, 'of giving mind', or *dānta-manāḥ*, 'of restrained mind' — Nirukta (Ni. 4-4, as read by the reader's OCR)] — declare us (*vocati*) sinless (*anāgasaḥ*), fit for the sacrifice: out of grace. For what purpose? For the sake of the Sun's coming (*sūryāya*) to the sacrificial place."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Sujāte* — O well-born one; *devi* — O one of shining nature; *he uṣaḥ* — O deity Uṣas; *martyatrā* — protectress of men (you); *adya* — now; *nṛbhyaḥ* — for men (for the sacrificers); *yat* — whatever; *bhāgam* — (your) share of light (and the share of oblation); *vibhajāsi* — you apportion (to the gods); *atra* — in this matter of the share; *damūnāḥ* — (disposed to give the desired [fruit] to the sacrificers) or in giving, of good mind; *devaḥ savitā* — the god Savitṛ; *naḥ* — us; *anāgasaḥ* — free from sin (fit for the sacrifice); *sūryāya* — for the Sun (to come to our sacrificial hall); *vocati* — may he tell.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O well-born, divine Uṣas, you who protect men! Whatever portion of your light you now apportion to men — to men who perform sacrifices, the portion of the oblation to the several gods — in that matter may the god Savitṛ, disposed to give what is desired to the sacrificers, declare us sinless and fit for the sacrifice, so that the Sun may come to our sacrificial hall.

### Printed p. 85  (PDF 106)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 4".)* **Printed English (as printed):** *Well-born and divine Ushas, you are the protectress of mortals; whatever share (of light) you apportion to-day to men, may the radiant Savitri be disposed (to confirm) the gift, and declare us free from sin; so that (he) the sun (may come to our sacrificial hall).*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 3.**

***martyatrā bhāgaṃ vibhajāsi nṛbhyaḥ*** — *manuṣyāṇāṃ pālayitrī tvaṃ manuṣyebhyaḥ svakīyaprakāśasyāṃśaṃ vibhajya dadāsi | yadvā martyeṣu madhye yajamānebhyo devānāṃ bhāgaṃ vibhajya dadāsi*: "Uṣas, the protectress of men, gives men separately a part of her light for their benefit — that is one sense." "To the sacrificers, who deserve protection among men, Uṣas gets the gods' respective shares of the oblation distributed separately" — that is another sense. Both meanings are explained by Sāyaṇa in the bhāṣya. In the first meaning the word *martyatrā* is used in the sense "protectress of men"; in the second meaning the word *nṛbhyaḥ*, though a general word for men, indicates a speciality of those who perform sacrifices.

It is Agni himself who apportions the oblation shares to the gods. But since, when the dawn-time has come, the oblation is at once offered in the fire, the character of "giver of the oblation shares" is attributed to Uṣas figuratively (*aupacārika*). He has stated this clearly: *uṣasi pravṛttāyāṃ haviṣo dīyamānatvāt uṣaso dātṛtvam upacaryate*.

***damūnāḥ*** — *yajamānebhyo 'bhimataphaladānamanāḥ*: "one with a mind to grant the desired fruit to the sacrificers". In the Nirukta the word *damūnāḥ* (Ni. 4-4, as read by the reader's OCR) is explained *damanamanāḥ* — one with a cruel/restrained mind [as printed]; or *dānamanāḥ*, one willing to give; or *dāntamanāḥ*, one whose mind is calmed by the restraints (*yama*, *niyama*); or "…

### Printed p. 86  (PDF 107)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)* *(Special topics of Ṛk 3, concluded.)* …[*damūnāḥ*] — having explained four kinds of meaning, he applies the epithet *damūnāḥ gṛhapatir agniḥ* ("the household lord Agni, *damūnāḥ*") to Agni. Here the epithet *damūnāḥ devaḥ savitā*, in the phrase "the god Savitṛ", is applied to Savitṛ; this indicates the identity of Agni (or the Sun) with Savitṛ; or it suggests that, like Agni, the god Savitṛ too has a greatness of the kind that makes him a *damūnas*.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 3; sūtra numbers as read by the reader's OCR).** *Vibhajāsi* — the root *bhaja sevāyām*; *leṭ*, 2nd singular, the suffix *sip*; *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94) the augment *aḍ*; since there is a connection with *yat* the *nighāta* does not arise; since *sip* and *śap* are *pit* they are unaccented, so the root accent remains. *Martyatrā* — in the sense of the seventh case (among men) by *devamanuṣyapuruṣamartyebhyo dvitīyāsaptamībhyāṃ…* (Pā. Sū. 5-4-56) the suffix *trā*; the final acute by the suffix accent. *Sujāte* — *śobhanaṃ jātaṃ jananaṃ yasyāḥ sā sujātā*; the vocative singular form; by *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) the *nighāta*. *Anāgasaḥ* — *na vidyate āgo yeṣāṃ te anāgasaḥ*; *nalopo nañaḥ* — the loss of the *n* of *nañ*; *tasmān nuḍ aci* — the augment *nuṭ* before a vowel; in the indeclinable-prefixed compound the first member's accent; accusative plural. *Vocati* — the root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; *leṭ*, 3rd singular, *tip*; *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* the *luk* of *śap*; *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* — the augment *aḍ* for the stem, by *vyatyaya*; *vaca um* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-20) the augment *um*; since it is *mit* it comes after the last vowel; guṇa; after an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*. *Sūryāya* — the root *sṛ gatau*; *sarati iti sūryaḥ* — *rājasūyasūrya…* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-114) formed with the suffix *kyap* by irregular formation; since it is *pit* it is unaccented, so the root accent remains; dative singular. ‖ 3 ‖

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अहना । उषोनामैतत् । अहना द्योतनेति तन्नाममु पाठात् । सा देवी दिने दिने प्रत्यहं दिवे दिव इत्यहर्नाममु पाठात् । गृहं गृहं तत्तद्यज्ञ-गृहमच्छाभिमुख्येन याति । गच्छति । कीदृशी । अध्यधिकं नाम नमनं प्रह्वत्वमुद्योगं प्रतिगृहमुद्योगं प्रकाशनरूपं दधाना धारयन्ती । यद्वा । अधि दधानाधिकं धारयन्ती । किञ्च सिषासन्ती सम्भक्तुमिच्छन्ती द्योतना कृत्स्नं जगद्द्योतनशीला शश्वत् प्रतिदिनमागात् । आगच्छति । पूर्वं यातीत्युक्तत्वात्पुनरागादिति वचनमावश्यकत्वद्योतनार्थम् । आगत्य च वसूनां धनानां हविर्लक्षणानामग्रमग्रमित् तत्तच्छ्रेष्ठभागं भजते सेवते स्वीकरोतीत्यर्थः ॥

> *ahanā | uṣonāmaitat | ahanā dyotaneti tannāmamu pāṭhāt | sā devī dine dine pratyahaṃ dive diva ityaharnāmamu pāṭhāt | gṛhaṃ gṛhaṃ tattadyajña-gṛhamacchābhimukhyena yāti | gacchati | kīdṛśī | adhyadhikaṃ nāma namanaṃ prahvatvamudyogaṃ pratigṛhamudyogaṃ prakāśanarūpaṃ dadhānā dhārayantī | yadvā | adhi dadhānādhikaṃ dhārayantī | kiñca siṣāsantī sambhaktumicchantī dyotanā kṛtsnaṃ jagaddyotanaśīlā śaśvat pratidinamāgāt | āgacchati | pūrvaṃ yātītyuktatvātpunarāgāditi vacanamāvaśyakatvadyotanārtham | āgatya ca vasūnāṃ dhanānāṃ havirlakṣaṇānāmagramagramit tattacchreṣṭhabhāgaṃ bhajate sevate svīkarotītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Small type; the passage marked `[?]` is a doubtful stretch; the Kannada commentary below confirms the sense.)* "*Ahanā*: this is a name of Uṣas, by its reading among the names *ahanā, dyotanā*. She, the goddess, comes day by day (*dive dive* — read among the names of 'day'). She goes (*yāti*) to house after house — to each sacrificial house — facing it (*accha*). What is she like? *Adhi nāma dadhānā*: bearing an excess of *nāma*, 'bending', that is 'eagerness', 'effort' — bearing for every house an effort in the form of light; or *adhi dadhānā* — bearing more. And, desiring to confer (*siṣāsantī*), illuminating the whole world (*dyotanā*), she has come (*āgāt*), always, every day. Having come, she takes (*bhajate*, serves, accepts) the foremost, the choicest portion (*agram agram*), of the riches — of the wealth in the form of oblations."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Ahanā* — the deity Uṣas; *dive dive* — every day; *adhi* — in excess; *nāma* — the effort (the bending) of the form of light; *dadhānā* — bearing; *gṛhaṃ gṛham* — to every sacrificial house; *accha yāti* — she goes facing; *(kiñca* — and); *siṣāsantī* — wishing to bestow favour; *dyotanā* — illuminating the world; *śaśvat* — always (every day); *āgāt* — she comes (having come); *vasūnām* — of the oblations and the like; *agram agram it* — the choicest portions only; *bhajate* — she accepts.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Uṣas, assuming each day the effort (*udyoga*) in the form of light, goes to every house of sacrifice; wishing to favour (the sacrificers), illuminating the world, she comes always, every day; having come she accepts only the choicest part of the oblations offered.

### Printed p. 88  (PDF 109)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)* **Printed English (as printed):** *Ahana, charged with downward-bending (light), goes daily from house to house; she comes, perpetually diffusing light, and desirous of bestowing (benefits), and accepts the choicest portions of (the sacrificial) treasures.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 4.**

***ahanā*** — "the deity Uṣas": that is the sense. Among the sixteen names of Uṣas beginning *vibhāvarī, sūnarī, bhāsvatī* (Ni. 2-19) the word *ahanā* too is declared (see the introduction of this Sūkta).

***dive dive*** — since this word is declared (Ni. 2-21) among the twelve names of "day" beginning *vasoḥ, dyauḥ, bhānuḥ*, it means "every day".

***accha*** — *acchābhi-rāptam iti śākapūṇiḥ* (Ni. 5-15, as read by the reader's OCR): "the word *accha* is used in the sense of *abhi* and in the sense of *āptam* — so the opinion of the teacher Śākapūṇi". Sāyaṇa here gives for the word *accha* the sense *ābhimukhyena*, "facing". *Gṛhaṃ gṛham accha yāti* — the sense is "the deity Uṣas enters the sacrificial houses with favour".

***adhi nāma dadhānā*** — in this sentence Sāyaṇa explains *adhikaṃ namanaṃ prahvatvam udyogaṃ prakāśanarūpaṃ pratigṛhaṃ dadhānā*: "Uṣas bears in every house her extraordinary light-effort" — that is one explanation; or *adhi dadhānā adhikaṃ dadhānā*: "bearing exceedingly light" — another: thus two explanations.

***gṛhaṃgṛham ahanā yāti*** — "Uṣas shines in every house"; and by saying again *śaśvat āgāt* ("she comes every day"), the necessity of the coming of Uṣas is shown.

***vasūnām agram agram it bhajate*** — *dhanānāṃ havirlakṣaṇānāṃ tattacchreṣṭhabhāgaṃ svīkarotīty arthaḥ*: "the deity Uṣas accepts the several choice portions of the oblations offered by the sacrificers" — that is the sense. The word *vasu* conveys many meanings. This word is declared among the names of rays (Ni. 2-15, as read by the reader's OCR) and among the names of wealth, *maghaṃ rekṇaḥ* and the rest (Ni. 3-9, as read by the OCR; the OCR gives "3, 3-9").

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> सूनृते सुष्ठु मनुष्याणां नेत्र्यृतो हे उषो देवते भगस्य सर्वैर्भजनीयस्यादित्यस्य स्वसासि । स्वसृस्थानीयासि । तेन सहोत्पद्यमानत्वात्प्रसूतत्वाद्वेत्यर्थः । तथा वरुणस्य तमोनिवारकस्य सवितुर्देवस्य जामिरसि । भगिनीस्थानीयासि । एकस्मिन्नेव स्थाने उत्पद्यमानत्वात् । जनयन्त्यपत्यान्यस्यामपत्कमन्य इति जामिः [?] । यद्वा । जमति गच्छति स्वोत्पत्तिस्थानादन्यत्रेति । उक्तनिर्वचनद्वयमभिप्रेत्य यास्क आह । न जामयेभगिन्यै [?] जामिरन्यस्यां जनयन्ति जामिपत्कं जमतेर्वा स्याद्गतिकर्मणो निर्गमनप्राया भवति (नि. ३-६ [?]) इति । तादृशी त्वं प्रथमेतरदेवेभ्यः पूर्वोत्कृष्टा वा सती जरस्व । स्तुता भव । जरतिः स्तुतिकर्मा (नि. १०-८) इति यास्कः । पश्चा पश्चात्त्वत्स्तुतेरनन्तरं योऽघस्य दुःखस्य कस्मिंश्चिद्दुःखस्य कारणस्य वा पापस्य धाता धारयिता [?] अस्ति स सः पापी दध्याः । गच्छतु । वचनव्यत्ययः । दध्य दभ्नोतीति गत्यर्थेषु पाठात् । यदि स पापी बलीयान् तं दक्षिणया प्रवृद्धया सहायभूतया त्वया रथेनास्मदीयरथादिसाधनेन च जयेम ॥

> *sūnṛte suṣṭhu manuṣyāṇāṃ netryṛto he uṣo devate bhagasya sarvairbhajanīyasyādityasya svasāsi | svasṛsthānīyāsi | tena sahotpadyamānatvātprasūtatvādvetyarthaḥ | tathā varuṇasya tamonivārakasya saviturdevasya jāmirasi | bhaginīsthānīyāsi | ekasminneva sthāne utpadyamānatvāt | janayantyapatyānyasyāmapatkamanya iti jāmiḥ [?] | yadvā | jamati gacchati svotpattisthānādanyatreti | uktanirvacanadvayamabhipretya yāska āha | na jāmayebhaginyai [?] jāmiranyasyāṃ janayanti jāmipatkaṃ jamatervā syādgatikarmaṇo nirgamanaprāyā bhavati (ni. 3-6 [?]) iti | tādṛśī tvaṃ prathametaradevebhyaḥ pūrvotkṛṣṭā vā satī jarasva | stutā bhava | jaratiḥ stutikarmā (ni. 10-8) iti yāskaḥ | paścā paścāttvatstuteranantaraṃ yo 'ghasya duḥkhasya kasmiṃścidduḥkhasya kāraṇasya vā pāpasya dhātā dhārayitā [?] asti sa saḥ pāpī dadhyāḥ | gacchatu | vacanavyatyayaḥ | dadhya dabhnotīti gatyartheṣu pāṭhāt | yadi sa pāpī balīyān taṃ dakṣiṇayā pravṛddhayā sahāyabhūtayā tvayā rathenāsmadīyarathādisādhanena ca jayema ‖*

*(Small type; a few words doubtful, the sūtra-like references to the Nirukta as read by me: Ni. 3-6 `[?]` for *jāmi*, Ni. 10-8 `[?]` for *jarati*.)* "O Sūnṛtā — leader of men in a good way — O deity Uṣas, you are the sister (*svasā*) of Bhaga — of the Āditya, who is to be served by all: that is, you stand in the place of a sister, since you were produced together with him. And so, you are the *jāmi* of Varuṇa — of the god Savitṛ, the remover of darkness: you stand in the place of a sister, since you arise in one place. *Jāmi* — [from] *janayanti apatyāni*... or from *jam*, 'to go': 'she goes elsewhere from the place of her birth'. Intending both derivations, Yāska says: *na jāmaye 'bhinai jāmir anyasyāṃ janayanti jāmipatkam jamater vā syād gatikarmaṇo nirgamanaprāyā bhavati* (Ni. 3-6 `[?]`). Such as you are, first (*prathamā*), or excelling the other gods, *jarasva* — be praised (*jaratiḥ stutikarmā*: 'to praise', Ni. 10-8 `[?]`, says Yāska). *Paścā* — afterwards, after your praise: he who is the bearer (*dhātā*) of sin (*agha*) — of some sorrow or of the cause of sorrow — *sa dadhyāḥ*: let that sinner go (the number is changed; the root *dadh*, 'to go'); if that sinner is stronger, we shall conquer him with you, the grown (*dakṣiṇayā*), the helper — with our chariot and other means."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Sūnṛte* — O one who leads men to the good path; *uṣaḥ* — O deity Uṣas (you); *bhagasya* — of Āditya, who is to be served by all; *svasā* — the sister; (*tathā* — likewise); *varuṇasya* — of Savitṛ, the remover of darkness; *jāmiḥ* — the sister (you); *prathamā* — first, before the other deities, best; *jarasva* — be praised (by us); *paścā* — afterwards (when we have been pleased by praising); *yaḥ* — who; *aghasya* — of sin, the cause of sorrow; *dhātā* — the supporter; *saḥ* — he; *dadhyāḥ* — let him go away (from here); *tam* — him; *dakṣiṇayā* — with the helping you; *rathena* — with our chariot; *jayema* — we conquer.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Uṣas, leader of men on the good path, you are the sister of Āditya, who is to be served by all, and the sister of Savitṛ, the dispeller of darkness; first and best among all the gods, you are to be praised by us; so we praise you; let the one who is the cause of sorrow (the sin) go away from here; with your help we conquer him with our chariots.

### Printed p. 92  (PDF 113)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)* **Printed English of Ṛk 5 (as printed):** *Ushas, endowed with truth, you are the sister of Bhaga, the sister of Varuna, you are hymned first (of the gods): then let the worker of iniquity depart, for we shall overcome him with our chariot, through your assistance.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 5.**

***bhagasya svasā*** — *sarvaiḥ bhajanīyasya ādityasya svasā svasṛsthānīyā asi*: "you are the sister of Āditya, who is to be worshipped by all" — Uṣas the deity is worshipped by all as the sister of the Sun. By the connection of being born together with the Āditya, she is, like the Āditya, worthy of worship by reason of greatness: that is the sense. The word *bhaga* has many meanings.

The word *bhaga* is recorded (Ni. 1-7, as read by the reader's OCR) and, in the ṛk "*nūnaṃ sā te*" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-21, as read by the OCR), it is a word for "wealth", and in (Ni. 3-9, as read by the OCR; "39") the meaning "wealth" is also given.

> वामंवामं त आदुरे देवो ददात्वर्यमा ।
> वामं पूषा वामं भगो वामं देवः करूळती ॥

> *vāmaṃvāmaṃ ta ādure devo dadātvaryamā |*
> *vāmaṃ pūṣā vāmaṃ bhago vāmaṃ devaḥ karūḷatī ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-4[?]-[?], as read; the OCR is garbled.) In this ṛk the word *bhaga* refers to a god, one among the Ādityas;

> श्रद्धयाग्निः समिध्यते श्रद्धया हूयते हविः ।
> श्रद्धां भगस्य मूर्धनि वचसा वेदयामसि ॥

> *śraddhayāgniḥ samidhyate śraddhayā hūyate haviḥ |*
> *śraddhāṃ bhagasya mūrdhani vacasā vedayāmasi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-151-1, as printed.) Here the vṛttikāra explains *bhagasya bhāgadheyasya dharmasya* — "of Bhaga, of the *bhāgadheya* [one's allotted portion], of *dharma*": he gives the word *bhaga* the sense *dharma*;

> प्रातर्जितं भगमुग्रं हुवेम वयं पुत्रमदितेर्यो विधर्ता ।
> आध्रश्चिद्यं मन्यमानस्तुरश्चिद्राजा चिद्यं भगं भक्षीत्याह ॥

> *prātarjitaṃ bhagamugraṃ huvema vayaṃ putramaditeryo vidhartā |*
> *ādhraścidyaṃ manyamānasturaścidrājā cidyaṃ bhagaṃ bhakṣītyāha ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-41-2, as read.) — in ṛks such as this *bhaga* is used also as a name of the Sun.

***varuṇasya jāmiḥ*** — *tamo vārakasya savitur devasya bhaginīsthānīyā asi* — "you stand in the place of a sister to the god Savitṛ, who restrains darkness": *janayanty apatyāny asyām apatkam anye iti jāmiḥ* … (the Kannada explains that Uṣas and Savitṛ, the Sun, have one origin; that is why Sāyaṇa says "they are born in one place"; since the root *jam* means 'to go', the word *jāmi* is formed from the root *jan*: in a woman, offspring are born; this woman is called *jāmi* because, since she is born here, the family goes to another house — the second sense.) Both these meanings are stated by Yāska.

### Printed p. 93  (PDF 114)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 5".)*

> न जामये भगिन्यै जामिरन्यस्यां जनयन्ति जामिपत्यं जमतेर्वा स्याद्गतिकर्मणो निर्गमनप्रायो भवति ॥

> *na jāmaye bhaginyai jāmiranyasyāṃ janayanti jāmipatyaṃ jamatervā syādgatikarmaṇo nirgamanaprāyo bhavati ‖*

(Ni. 3-6, as printed "೩-೬"; the Sanskrit as read letter by letter from the large type; I read the first words as *na jāmaye bhaginyai* and the fourth as *jāmipatyam*.) Daughters are not entitled to the funeral oblations (? — *pāyasa-bhāga*) [`[?]` the first sentence of the Kannada gloss: "women are not fit for a share in the inheritance"]. They are not fit for a share in their brother's estate, since they, having nourished children, are given away to a husband. The word *jāmi* is well known in the sense "sister"; or the word *jāmi* formed from the root *jam* meaning 'to go' conveys the sense 'one who joins, from the family where she was born, another family' — such are the two meanings given by Sāyaṇa, in accord with the intention of the Nirukta writer.

***prathamā jarasva*** — *itaradevebhyaḥ pūrvā utkṛṣṭā vā satī stutā bhava*: "Uṣas is praised first in the sacrifice; or, being chief above all other deities, is praised" — he gives these two meanings.

Yāska explains *jarā stutiḥ jaratiḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ* (Ni. 10-8, as read by the OCR) — "*jarā* means praise: from the root *jṝ*, 'to praise'"; since the word *jarate* is recorded among the verbs of praising (Ni. 3-6 `[?]`), the verb *jarati* is explained by Sāyaṇa in the sense of praise.

***yaḥ aghasya dhātā saḥ dadhyāḥ*** — *yaḥ kaścid duḥkhasya tadutpādakapāpasya vā dhārayitā saḥ gacchatu*: "he who holds sorrow — he who has sin that causes sorrow — let him go from here (by your grace) and be conquered by us" — this is the prayer that is explained.

***dadhyāḥ*** — Yāska classes *dadhyati, dabhnoti* (Ni. 3-9, as read by the OCR on p. 93) among the verbs meaning 'to go'; hence here he explains the word *dadhyāḥ* as *gacchatu*.
