### Printed p. 94  (PDF 115)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)* **Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, Ṛk 5; sūtra numbers as read by the reader's OCR for p. 94).** *Jāmiḥ* — the root *jani prādurbhāve*; the suffix *iñ* of the uṇādi class by *bahulagrahaṇa*; *vyatyaya* gives *m* for the *n*; *janayanty asyām apatyam anye iti jāmiḥ* — or *jamati gacchati svotpattisthānād anyatra iti jāmiḥ*; thus in the second sense, taking the root *jam adane*, with the suffix *iñ* as before; since roots have many meanings, it is used in the sense of going. *Sūnṛte* — the root *ūna parihāṇe*; *sutarāṃ ūnayati apriyam iti sūnā*; *vāk* of the pleasant and true; *sūnṛtā* — in the vocative *sūnṛte*; *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) the *nighāta*. *Jarasva* — the root *jṝṣ vayohānau*; here used in the sense of praise; *loṭ*, 2nd singular; by *vyatyaya* no *yak*-type augment in the passive-like middle; *savābhyāṃ vāmau* (…) the *am*; after an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*. *Paścā* — *paścāt* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-33) the substitution *paśca* for the word *apara*, and in the sense of the fifth case [*astāti*], the suffix *āti*, by irregular formation; in the Vedic way the final *t* drops; the first-syllable acute of the suffix. *Dadhyāḥ* — *dadhyati dabhnoti* (Ni. 3-9 and OCR "14-61" `[?]`) says the Nirukta, reading it among the verbs of going; hence here it is used in that sense; *liṅ*, 2nd singular; by *vyatyayo bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85) the *tip*-like singular ending; after an *atiṅanta* the *nighāta*. *Dhātā* — the root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; in the sense of the agent the suffix *tṛc*; since it is *cit*, the final acute; nominative singular. *Jayema* — the root *ji jaye*; *āśīrliṅ* [as printed *vidhiliṅ*], 1st plural, the form *jayema*; since *yat* is connected with the word *yaḥ* before it, *yadvṛttānnityam* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66) prevents the *nighāta*; since the suffix is *lasārvadhātuka*, *tāsyanudāttet* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the root accent remains. *Dakṣiṇayā* — the root *dakṣa vṛddhau*; *druhakṣibhyām inan* (Uṇ. Sū. 2-1[?]-[?], as read) the suffix *inan*; in the feminine, since it ends in *a*, *ṭāp*; since the suffix is *nit*, *ñnityādir nityam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) the first-syllable acute; instrumental singular. ‖ 5 ‖

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उदीरतां सूनृता उत्पुरंधीरुदग्नयः शुशुचानासो अस्थुः ।
> स्पार्हा वसूनि तमसापगूळ्हाविष्कृण्वन्त्युषसो विभातीः ॥ ६ ॥

> *udīratāṃ sūnṛtā utpuraṃdhīrudagnayaḥ śuśucānāso asthuḥ |*
> *spārhā vasūni tamasāpagūḷhāviṣkṛṇvantyuṣaso vibhātīḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत् । ईरताम् । सूनृताः । उत् । पुरंऽधीः । उत् । अग्नयः । शुशुचानासः । अस्थुः ।
> स्पार्हा । वसूनि । तमसा । अपऽगूळ्हा । आविः । कृण्वन्ति । उषसः । विऽभातीः ॥ ६ ॥

> *ut | īratām | sūnṛtāḥ | ut | puraṃ 'dhīḥ | ut | agnayaḥ | śuśucānāsaḥ | asthuḥ |*
> *spārhā | vasūni | tamasā | apa 'gūḷhā | āviḥ | kṛṇvanti | uṣasaḥ | vi 'bhātīḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> सूनृताः प्रियसत्यात्मिका वाच उदीरताम् । उद्गच्छन्तु । हे ऋत्विज उत्कृष्टं यथा भवति तथा स्तोत्रं प्रवर्तयध्वम् । तथा पुरन्धीः पुरन्धयः । पुरं शरीरं यासु धीयते याभिर्वा ताः पुरन्धयः प्रज्ञाः प्रयोगविषयाः । ता उत्तिष्ठन्तु । प्रज्ञोपलक्षितानि कर्माणि प्रवर्तन्तामित्यर्थः । यद्यपि प्राणवायुना शरीरं धार्यते तथापि यो वै प्राणः सा प्रज्ञा या वा प्रज्ञा स प्राण इति श्रुतेः प्राणप्रज्ञयोरेकात्मत्वात्प्रज्ञायाः शरीरधारणमविरुद्धम् । तथाग्नय आहवनीयाद्याः शुशुचानासोऽत्यन्तं दीप्यमाना उदस्थुः । उत्तिष्ठन्तु । प्रज्वलयन्त्वित्यर्थः । किमर्थमेवमिति तदुच्यते । यतो विभातीर्विविधं भासमाना उषस उषो-देवताः तमसापगूळ्हान्धकारेणात्यन्तं गोपितानि स्पार्हा स्पृहणीयानि वसूनि वासयोग्यानि यज्ञसाधनभूतहविरादीन्याविष्कृण्वन्ति यथावस्तु प्रकटीकुर्वन्ति । तस्मात्स्तोत्रादिकं कुर्वन्त्वित्यर्थः ॥

> *sūnṛtāḥ priyasatyātmikā vāca udīratām | udgacchantu | he ṛtvija utkṛṣṭaṃ yathā bhavati tathā stotraṃ pravartayadhvam | tathā purandhīḥ purandhayaḥ | puraṃ śarīraṃ yāsu dhīyate yābhirvā tāḥ purandhayaḥ prajñāḥ prayogaviṣayāḥ | tā uttiṣṭhantu | prajñopalakṣitāni karmāṇi pravartantāmityarthaḥ | yadyapi prāṇavāyunā śarīraṃ dhāryate tathāpi yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā yā vā prajñā sa prāṇa iti śruteḥ prāṇaprajñayorekātmatvātprajñāyāḥ śarīradhāraṇamaviruddham | tathāgnaya āhavanīyādyāḥ śuśucānāso 'tyantaṃ dīpyamānā udasthuḥ | uttiṣṭhantu | prajvalayantvityarthaḥ | kimarthamevamiti taducyate | yato vibhātīrvividhaṃ bhāsamānā uṣasa uṣo-devatāḥ tamasāpagūḷhāndhakāreṇātyantaṃ gopitāni spārhā spṛhaṇīyāni vasūni vāsayogyāni yajñasādhanabhūtahavirādīnyāviṣkṛṇvanti yathāvastu prakaṭīkurvanti | tasmātstotrādikaṃ kurvantvityarthaḥ ‖*

*(Read at 150 dpi; letters that were unclear are marked `[?]` or taken as the Kannada's plain sense.)* "May the pleasant and true words (*sūnṛtāḥ*) rise up (*udīratām*): let them go up. O priests, so recite the praise that it be excellent. Likewise *purandhīḥ* — *purandhayaḥ*: 'those in which the body (*pura*) is placed, or by which it is placed' — the powers of intelligence (*prajñā*), that are the field of operation: let them rise; that is, let acts marked by intelligence go forward. Although the body is held by the vital air, still, by the Śruti *yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā, yā vā prajñā sa prāṇaḥ* (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad 3-3, as read by the reader's OCR), since *prāṇa* and *prajñā* are one in nature, the holding of the body by *prajñā* is not inconsistent. Likewise the fires — Āhavanīya and the others — *śuśucānāsaḥ*, shining intensely, *udasthuḥ*: may they rise, may they blaze. Why so? It is said: because the Uṣases (the Uṣas deities), who shine (*vibhātīḥ*) in various ways, reveal (*āviṣkṛṇvanti*) in their true form the desirable riches (*spārhā vasūni*), the oblations and other means of sacrifice, suitable for dwelling, that were hidden by darkness; therefore they should do their praise and the rest."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Vibhātīḥ* — shining in various forms; *uṣasaḥ* — the Uṣas deities; *tamasā* — by darkness; *apagūḷhā* — well hidden; *spārhā* — desirable; *vasūni* — dwelling-suitable houses (the oblations and the like); *āviḥ kṛṇvanti* — make manifest; (therefore); *sūnṛtāḥ* — the pleasant and true (praise-) words; *ut īratām* — let them rise; …

### Printed p. 96  (PDF 117)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)* **Pratipadārtha, concluded:** …*ut īratām* — let them rise; *purandhīḥ* — (connected with action) the powers of knowledge, the actions marked by knowledge; *ut* [*asthuḥ*] — let them begin (and); *agnayaḥ* — the fires (Āhavanīya and the others); *śuśucānāsaḥ* — blazing; *ut asthuḥ* — let them blaze up.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** When the deities Uṣas arise in diverse forms, the houses — or the oblation materials — that are much desired and had been well hidden by the darkness (so that they were not seen with the eye) become manifest; therefore, O priests, at that time (*ut*) chant in a loud voice good praise-words; begin (acts that are the fruits of sacrificial knowledge); and let the fires (Āhavanīya and others) be kindled so that they shine brightly.

**Printed English (as printed):** *Let words of truth be spoken : let works of wisdom (be performed) : let the blazing fires rise up, so that the many radiant Ushas may make manifest the desirable treasures hidden by the darkness.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 6.**

***sūnṛtāḥ*** — *priyasatyātmikāḥ vācaḥ*: Yāska records the word *sūnṛtā* among the names of speech (Ni. 2-19, as read by the OCR) and among the names of food (Ni. 3-9, as read by the OCR). Sāyaṇa, however, explains that for it the meaning "speech that is beneficial and true" is used in another sense. The idea is: "may the priests recite hymns that are most agreeable, which will give delight to the deities".

***purandhīḥ ut tiṣṭhantu*** — *puraṃ śarīraṃ yāsu dhīyate yābhir vā tāḥ purandhayaḥ prajñāḥ prayogaviṣayāḥ | prajñopalakṣitāni karmāṇi pravartantām ity arthaḥ*: the word *pura* conveys "body"; *purandhi* means *prajñā* ("wisdom") that holds the body properly in place. The sense is "let [acts] done with pure knowledge, or performed with conduct, begin".

In the Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad it is said: *yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā, yā vā prajñā sa prāṇaḥ* (Kau. Upa. 3-3, as read by the OCR). By this sentence the identity of *prāṇa* and *prajñā* is declared: *prāṇa* (vital air) itself holds the body in place; yet "that *prajñā* holds the body" appears to be a contradiction; but it is removed by the identity between *prāṇa* and *prajñā*.

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 5".)* In the bhāṣya, by saying *yadyapi prāṇavāyunā śarīraṃ dhāryate tathāpi prāṇaprajñayor ekatvāt prajñāyāḥ śarīradhāraṇam aviruddham*, Sāyaṇa has described the manner of removing the contradiction, and given for the word *purandhi* the meaning *prajñā* ("[the powers of] knowledge, the acts joined with knowledge").

Yāska reads the two words *purandhi* and *purandhī*, and has shown the difference of their meanings. The word *purandhī* means "Earth and Heaven" [as read: *vyāvāpṛthivīvācaka*] (Ni. 3-22, as read by the OCR).

> *te hi yajñeṣu yajñiyāsa ūmāḥ sadhasthaṃ viśve abhi santi devāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-3[?]-[?], as read.)

> पुरन्धिर्बहुधीस्तत्र कर्मा [?] । पुरन्धिर्भगः पुरस्तात्स्यान्यादेश इत्येकम् । इन्द्र इत्यपरं स बहुकर्मतमः पुरां च दारयितृतमः । वरुण इत्यपरम् ॥

> *purandhirbahudhīstatra karmā [?] | purandhirbhagaḥ purastātsyānyādeśa ityekam | indra ityaparaṃ sa bahukarmatamaḥ purāṃ ca dārayitṛtamaḥ | varuṇa ityaparam ‖*

(Ni. 6-1[?]-[?], as read.) Thus Yāska has said. According to one opinion [of the vṛttikāra Durgācārya], the word *purandhi* means the deity named Bhaga; according to another opinion, since *dhī* means "action", he who does many bold deeds is Indra — [this is] the meaning; and still others say that, since *purandhi* is he who destroys clouds and enemy cities, the word expresses the sense "Indra". Others [say] "Varuṇa":

> इमामू नु कवितमस्य मायां महीं देवस्य नकिरा दधर्ष ।
> एकं यदुद्ना न पृणन्त्येनीरासिञ्चन्तीरवनयः समुद्रम् ॥

> *imāmū nu kavitamasya māyāṃ mahīṃ devasya nakirā dadharṣa |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-4[?]-[?], as read.) In this ṛk the seer of the mantra praises Varuṇa. *Dhīr iti prajñānāma sā yasya pūrvī bahvī sa purandhiḥ | varuṇaś ca prajñayā stūyate kasmāt varuṇaḥ purandhiḥ* — the vṛttikāra explains thus: *dhī* is a word for *prajñā*; since Varuṇa is praised with much *prajñā*, the doer of many things, he says the word *purandhi* has the sense "Varuṇa". That is one opinion.

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-2[?]-[?], as read; the first line has been read doubtfully and is not transcribed as Sanskrit.) In this ṛk they explain the word *purandhi* as *bahuno dhanasya dātā*, "the giver of much wealth".

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अप । अन्यत् । एति । अभि । अन्यत् । एति । विषुरूपे इति विषुऽरूपे । अहनी इति । सम् । चरेते इति ।
> परिऽक्षितोः । तमः । अन्या । गुहा । अकः । अद्यौत् । उषाः । शोशुचता । रथेन ॥ ७ ॥

> *apa | anyat | eti | abhi | anyat | eti | viṣurūpe iti viṣu 'rūpe | ahanī iti | sam | carete iti |*
> *pari 'kṣitoḥ | tamaḥ | anyā | guhā | akaḥ | adyaut | uṣāḥ | śośucatā | rathena ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> इदानीमहोरात्रस्तुतिद्वारोषाः स्तूयते । विषुरूपे वक्ष्यमाणप्रकारेण नानारूपे अहनी अहश्च रात्रिश्चोभे सं चरेते । समित्येकीभावे । सहैवाव्यवधानेन चरतः । अत्राहः साहचर्यात्तत्प्रतियोगित्वाच्च रात्रिरप्यहरित्युच्यते । उत्तरत्र मन्त्रान्तरेऽयमेवार्थः स्पष्ट आम्नातः । अहश्च कृष्णमहरर्जुनं च वि वर्तेते रजसी वेद्याभिः (ऋ. ६-९-१) इति । तयोर्मध्येऽन्यद्रात्रिरूपमहरपैति । अपगच्छति । प्रतिलोमं गच्छति वा । अपेत्येतस्य प्रातिलोम्यम् (नि. १-३) इति यास्कः । अन्यच्च दिवसाख्यमहरभ्येति । अभिमुखेन गच्छति । अभीत्याभिमुख्यम् (नि. १-३) इति यास्कः । रात्र्यां प्रतिनिवृत्तायामहराभिमुखमागच्छतीत्यर्थः । विषुरूपे सं चरेते इति यदुक्तं तदेव स्पष्टीक्रियते । परिक्षितोः पर्यायेण निवसतोः परिक्षपयितोर्वा । प्राणिनामायुः क्षयात्प्रक्षपणं प्रसिद्धं तयोर्मध्येऽन्या रात्रिस्तमस्तमोरूपा गुहा पदार्थानां गूहनमकः करोति । अन्या हरेकदेशभूतोषाः शोशुचता भृशं दीप्येन रथेनाद्यौत् । द्योतते । प्रकाशते प्रकाशयति वा सर्वम् । रात्रिस्तमोरूपत्वात्सर्वं जगदावृणोति । उषास्तु सर्वान्प्राकाश्य-यतीत्युषसः स्तुतिः ॥

> *idānīmahorātrastutidvāroṣāḥ stūyate | viṣurūpe vakṣyamāṇaprakāreṇa nānārūpe ahanī ahaśca rātriścobhe saṃ carete | samityekībhāve | sahaivāvyavadhānena carataḥ | atrāhaḥ sāhacaryāttatpratiyogitvācca rātrirapyaharityucyate | uttaratra mantrāntare 'yamevārthaḥ spaṣṭa āmnātaḥ | ahaśca kṛṣṇamahararjunaṃ ca vi vartete rajasī vedyābhiḥ (ṛ. 6-9-1) iti | tayormadhye 'nyadrātrirūpamaharapaiti | apagacchati | pratilomaṃ gacchati vā | apetyetasya prātilomyam (ni. 1-3) iti yāskaḥ | anyacca divasākhyamaharabhyeti | abhimukhena gacchati | abhītyābhimukhyam (ni. 1-3) iti yāskaḥ | rātryāṃ pratinivṛttāyāmaharābhimukhamāgacchatītyarthaḥ | viṣurūpe saṃ carete iti yaduktaṃ tadeva spaṣṭīkriyate | parikṣitoḥ paryāyeṇa nivasatoḥ parikṣapayitorvā | prāṇināmāyuḥ kṣayātprakṣapaṇaṃ prasiddhaṃ tayormadhye 'nyā rātristamastamorūpā guhā padārthānāṃ gūhanamakaḥ karoti | anyā harekadeśabhūtoṣāḥ śośucatā bhṛśaṃ dīpyena rathenādyaut | dyotate | prakāśate prakāśayati vā sarvam | rātristamorūpatvātsarvaṃ jagadāvṛṇoti | uṣāstu sarvānprākāśya-yatītyuṣasaḥ stutiḥ ‖*

*(Read from 150 dpi; the letters of a few words are marked or approximate, e.g. the compound *prakāśayati* near the end.)* "Now, through the praise of Day and Night, Uṣas is praised. *Viṣurūpe* — two of various forms (in the manner to be told), Day and Night, both *saṃ carete* (*sam* means 'together': they move together, without interval). Here, because of its companionship with day and because it is its counterpart, night too is called *ahar* ('day'). In another mantra later the same sense is clearly handed down: *ahaś ca kṛṣṇam ahar arjunaṃ ca vi vartete rajasī vedyābhiḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-9-1, as printed "೬-೯-೧"). Of the two, one — the night form of the 'day' — *apaiti*: goes away, or goes backward (*pratilomam*): *apety etasya prātilomyam* (Ni. 1-3, as read by the OCR), says Yāska. The other, called day, *abhyeti*: goes facing; *abhīty ābhimukhyam* (Ni. 1-3), says Yāska — when the night has gone back, the day comes facing. What is said — *viṣurūpe saṃ carete* — is now made clear. *Parikṣitoḥ*: of the two that dwell in turn, or that make [life] wane — the waning of the lives of creatures is well known; between them, the other, Night, which has the form of darkness, makes *guhā* — a hiding — of things. The other, the day-portion, Uṣas, brilliantly shining (*śośucatā*) with her chariot, *adyaut*: shines, or illuminates everything. Night, being of the form of darkness, covers the whole world; Uṣas, however, makes everything visible: thus the praise of Uṣas."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Viṣurūpe* — (in the manner told further on) of various forms; *ahanī* — the two, Day and Night; *saṃ carete* — move together; *anyat* — of the two, one (Night); *apa eti* — goes backward (passes); *anyat* — the other (Day); *abhi eti* — goes forward; *parikṣitoḥ* — of the two that dwell in turn (that cause the lives of beings to wane, as they come and go); *anyā* — one (Night); *tamaḥ* — in the form of darkness; *guhā* — (things) concealing; *akaḥ* — does; *anyā* — the other; *uṣāḥ* — Uṣas, the portion of the day; *śośucatā* — brilliantly shining; *rathena* — with her chariot; *adyaut* — illuminates all.

### Printed p. 101  (PDF 122)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 5".)* **॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** The Day and the Night, of various forms, move together; of the two, one (Night) goes backward, the other (Day) goes forward; Night, which destroys the lives of beings, makes things hidden in the form of darkness; the other, the day-portion Uṣas, shines with her radiant chariot and illuminates the whole world, which was covered by darkness.

**Printed English (as printed):** *The twofold day proceeds unseparated; one (part going) forward, one backward; one of these two alternating (periods) effects the concealment (of things); the Dawn illumines them with her radiant chariot.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 7.** In this ṛk Uṣas is praised through the praise of Day and Night. The Day and Night, the two, move one after the other in many forms.

***viṣurūpe*** — *vakṣyamāṇaprakāreṇa nānārūpe | ahaś ca rātriś cobhe sahaiva avyavadhānena carataḥ* — Sāyaṇa explains: "Day and Night both move together without interval". *Atrāhnaḥ sāhacaryāt tatpratiyogitvāc ca rātrir apy ahar ity ucyate* — "here, from association with day and from being its counterpart, night too is called *ahar*":

> अहश्च कृष्णमहरर्जुनं च वि वर्तेते रजसी वेद्याभिः ।
> वैश्वानरो जायमानो न राजावातिरज्ज्योतिषाग्निस्तमांसि ॥

> *ahaśca kṛṣṇamahararjunaṃ ca vi vartete rajasī vedyābhiḥ |*
> *vaiśvānaro jāyamāno na rājāvātirajjyotiṣāgnistamāṃsi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-9-1, as printed.) Citing this ṛk, he describes that from association with day and from being contrary to it, night too is called "day". In the compound word [the Kannada explains], although the word "day" itself has two forms in common usage — as a day consisting of "day and night" — in the name *ahas* the "night" aspect — it is [another of] the many forms; in the day-forms, the night is covered with darkness and conceals all things from the sight of everyone; while it [the day] moves the opposite way … This same idea is explained by Yāska in *tayor madhye 'nyā rātrirūpam aharapaiti prātilomaṃ gacchati vā* [as printed].

### Printed p. 102  (PDF 123)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)* ***apa + eti*** — in this the prefix *apa* is used in the sense of "contrary" (*prātilomya*). Yāska explains: *vyapetyaitasya prātilomyam* (Ni. 1-3, as read by the OCR).

In the same way *anyac ca divasākhyam ahar abhi eti abhimukhena gacchati* — "the other, the 'day' called *divasa*, goes forth facing; the day is [so] named; since Uṣas, in contrast to night, exists in the form of a luminous source, she comes facing [the night] — that is, goes to meet it, after the night has passed."

***abhi + eti*** — the prefix *abhi* is used in the sense of "facing": *abhītyābhimukhyam* (Ni. 1-3, as read by the OCR) is Yāska's description. The sense: after the night has gone, Uṣas comes facing [the world].

***parikṣitoḥ*** — *paryāyeṇa nivasatoḥ parikṣapayitor vā* — "of the two that dwell by turns, or that make [life] wane": the day and the night come one after another; and they reduce (*kṣapayanti*) the lives of beings by their going and coming — that is the sense.

***uṣāḥ śośucatā rathena adyaut*** — *dyotate prakāśate prakāśayati vā sarvam*: "Night covers the whole world with darkness; Uṣas, with her radiance, illuminates the whole world, and shines herself with her own light": thus Uṣas is praised here.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अद्यास्मिन्नहनि सदृशीरित् परस्परं सदृश्य एव । तथा श्व इत् परस्मिन्नहनि सदृशीः परस्परं सदृश्य एव । उशब्दोऽपिकारार्थः । इच्छब्द एवार्थः । अद्यतन्योऽपि श्वस्तनीभिः सदृश्यः श्वस्तन्यश्चाद्यतनीभिः । एवमहरन्तरेण सादृश्यम् । कथं सादृश्यमिति तदुपपाद्यते । यदा नक्षत्राणि न दृश्यन्ते सूर्यश्च नोदेति उषःकालः । स चैकविंशतिघटिकाभिः षड्विंशतिपराभिः [?] सम्मितः । सूर्यो हि प्रतिदिनमेकोनषष्ट्यधिकपञ्चसहस्रयोजनानि [?] मेरुं प्रादक्षिण्येन परिभ्रमति । तथा सति यत्र यत्र लङ्कादिभूप्रदेशे सूर्यो गच्छति तस्य तस्य पुरस्त्रिंशद्योजनमुषा अपि गच्छति । सूर्यो यस्मिन्देशे गच्छति तत्र त्रिंशद्योजनं पुरस्ताद्देशस्थितानामुषो दृश्यते । एवं सर्वप्रदेशेष्वपि । तथोषा अपि यत्र गच्छति ततः पुरस्त्रिंशद्योजनभूभागवर्तिनामुदिता दृश्यते । एवं लङ्कादिसर्वप्रदेशस्थानामुषस उदयो गन्तव्यः । एवं च सत्येकस्मिन्भूभागे यावत्कालं यथोषाः प्रकाशयति तथा भूभागान्तरेऽपि तावन्तं कालं प्रकाशयति । एवमुक्तरीत्यैकस्मिन्नेवाहनि सर्वप्रदेशवर्तिनामुषसः सदृश्यः । प्रदेशबाहुल्यमपेक्ष्योषसां बहुत्वाद्बहुवचनम् । एवमेकरूपा उषसोऽनवद्याः शुद्धाः । तासामुदयात्सर्वे भावा अनवद्या भविष्यन्ति किमु वक्तव्यं तासामनवद्यत्वम् । दीर्घमुक्तरीत्यात्यन्तमायतं वरुणस्य तमोनिवारकस्य सूर्यस्य धाम स्थानं मेरुवलयं सचन्ते । प्रतिदिनं सेवन्ते । कियद्दूरमिति तदुच्यते । त्रिंशतं योजनानि त्रिंशद्योजनानि पुरतः । सूर्यो यत्र यत्रोदेति ततस्त्रिंशद्योजनं पुरस्तादुद्यन्तीत्यर्थः । किञ्चासां मध्य एकैकोषा लङ्कादिकैकभूभागवर्तिनां क्रतुं गमनागमनादिरूपं कर्म तद्विषयां प्रज्ञां वा । तथा च निरुक्तम् । क्रतुं प्रधिकर्म वा प्रज्ञां वा (नि. २-२८ [?]) इति । सद्यस्तदानीमेव हि स्वोदयकाल एव परि यन्ति । परितो गच्छन्ति । निर्वहन्तीत्यर्थः । तत्तद्भूभागविशेषेण सूर्यस्योदयो ज्योतिश्शास्त्रे प्रदर्शितः । उदयो यो

*(As read; the sūtra of the astronomical verse is in small type: "Ārya. 4-13", Āryabhaṭīya, as printed "ಆರ್ಯ. ೪-೧೩", which the reader's OCR reads the same. In the last words I read* सिद्धपुरे *and* यवकोट्यां *as printed; the first word of the sentence, "in Laṅkā", ends the sentence from p. 104.)*

"Today, on this day, the Uṣases (dawns) are all alike with one another; likewise tomorrow they are all alike with one another. The word *u* has the sense of *api* ('also'); *it* has the sense of *eva*. Today's are like tomorrow's, and tomorrow's like today's. In this way there is likeness from day to day. How is the likeness established? When the stars are not seen and the Sun has not yet risen, that is the dawn-time; it is measured by twenty-one *ghaṭikās* or twenty-six [?] beyond them. The Sun goes round Meru each day in a clockwise way [for 5,059 [?] yojanas]; and so in whatever place on the earth, Laṅkā and so on, the Sun goes, the dawn goes thirty yojanas in front of him. In whatever region the Sun goes, to those who are stationed thirty yojanas in front, the dawn is seen. So in all regions. And likewise wherever the dawn goes, she is seen to have risen to those in the part of the earth thirty yojanas ahead. In this way the rising of Uṣas is to be understood for those in all regions, Laṅkā and the rest. And so, as long as Uṣas lights one part of the earth, so long she lights another part. In this way, in one and the same day, the dawns are alike for those in all regions; the plural is used out of regard to the many regions. Thus the dawns are of one form, *anavadyāḥ* — pure: from their rising all things will be blameless — what then need be said of their own blamelessness? *Dīrgham*: in the manner told, very extended: they follow (*sacante*) the region (*dhāma*) of Varuṇa — of the Sun, the remover of darkness — the ring of Meru; day by day they serve it. How far? Thirty yojanas ahead (*puratas*): wherever the Sun rises, thirty yojanas ahead of that they rise — that is the sense. And among them each Uṣas, for each region of the earth, such as Laṅkā, *kratum* — 'action in the form of going and coming', or the intelligence concerning it; thus the Nirukta (*kratuṃ pradhikarma vā prajñāṃ vā*, Ni. 2-28, as read by the OCR) — *sadyas* — just then, at their own rising, *pari yanti*: go round, accomplish. The Sun's rising in each part of the earth is shown in the science of the heavens: 'the rising at Laṅkā is the setting at Siddhapura, at Yavakoṭi it is midday, in the country of Romaka it is midnight' (Āryabhaṭīya 4-13)."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Uṣasaḥ* — the dawns; *adya* — now; *sadṛśīḥ it* — (one to another) alike; *śvaḥ* — tomorrow also; *sadṛśīḥ u* — alike (thus of one form); *anavadyāḥ* — pure ones (they); *dīrgham* — very long (extended); *varuṇasya* — of the remover of darkness (the Sun); *dhāma* — the region (path); *triṃśatam yojanāni* — thirty yojanas distance (rising ahead of the Sun); *sacante* — they follow (they go round); *ekaikā* — each (dawn); *kratum* — the action (of going and coming, as applicable to each part of the earth); *sadyaḥ* — at once (at the time of her rising); *pari yanti* — they accomplish.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** The dawns of today and of tomorrow are alike; they are pure; they go round the very extended region (the path) of the Sun, the remover of darkness, rising thirty yojanas ahead of the Sun; and every dawn at its time of rising performs its action, applying it to the region concerned.

**Printed English (as printed):** *The same to-day, the same tomorrow, the irreproachable (Dawns) precede the distant course of Varuna (Sun) by thirty yojanas, and each in succession revolves in its (appointed) office.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 8.**

***sadṛśīr adya sadṛśīr idu śvaḥ*** — *asminn ahani parasparaṃ sadṛśyaḥ | parasminn ahani api parasparaṃ sadṛśya eva | adyatanyo 'pi śvastanībhiḥ sadṛśyaḥ śvastanyaś cādyatanībhiḥ | evam ahar-antareṇa sādṛśyam* — here the likeness of days to one another is described: "today's day is alike to tomorrow's day; tomorrow's day is alike to today's; yesterday's day is alike to today's; tomorrow's is alike to today's" — a mutual likeness is set out. "On the ground of the equal quality — the same kind of character — produced by the Sun's special motion, it may be said that the likeness holds for the other days too" — that is the sense. This kind of likeness Sāyaṇa has explained.

### Printed p. 106  (PDF 127)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)* *(Special topics of Ṛk 8, continued; from here the Kannada text was read from the page image and cross-checked word by word against the reader's OCR, which for the Kannada prose is good.)* …"…when the stars are not seen and the Sun has not yet risen" — people reckon the time from twenty-one *ghaṭikās* to twenty-six *ghaṭikās* [before sunrise] as the dawn-time (*uṣaḥkāla*), which comes in the last part of the night. The Sun goes round Mount Meru each day in a clockwise circuit of five thousand and fifty-nine [`[?]` "ಐದು ಸಾವಿರದ ಐವತ್ತೊಂಭತ್ತು"] yojanas. Before the Sun rises (in the regions where he rises, Laṅkā and the rest), by the time the Sun comes there, the dawn has already arrived thirty yojanas ahead of him. Hence in the region ahead of where the Sun is, at a distance of thirty yojanas, the rising of the Sun is seen as the dawn. This arrangement holds in all regions.

In the same way the dawn, too, rises in the region thirty yojanas ahead of the region where she herself is. For all who live in all regions, from Laṅkā onward, it is to be understood that the rising of Uṣas is perceived in one and the same manner.

Thus, as the light of Uṣas is seen in one region, so at the same time in all the other regions the same equal light of Uṣas is perceived by all. Therefore, because the days are reckoned as different days beginning from the dawn-time, and because the regions are different, it is to be understood that the one Uṣas is many Uṣases, and the mutual likeness (*sādṛśya*, comparison) of these is here described.

When the regions are not taken into account, Uṣas, rising of her own nature perfectly pure, and since in Uṣas there is a supreme purity that makes all things pure, there is no need to explain at length about Uṣas's purity.

***varuṇasya dīrghaṃ dhāma sacante*** — *atyantam āyataṃ tamonivārakasya sūryasya meruvalayaṃ pratidinaṃ sevante*: "they serve every day the very extended ring of Meru of the Sun, the remover of darkness". Though the Sun's light is far from the region where he is, it destroys darkness, and the pervasion of the Sun's light is perceived. It is described that, just as the Sun goes round Meru in a clockwise circuit, so does Uṣas every day.

***varuṇaḥ vṛṇotīti sataḥ*** (Ni. 10-5, as printed "೧೦-೫", the OCR reads "10-5") — "because he restrains the clouds, the Sun, remover of darkness, is called Varuṇa", and "he who illuminates the light of Varuṇa" is said; and further —

#### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> जानत्यह्नः प्रथमस्य नाम शुक्रा कृष्णादजनिष्ट श्वितीची ।
> ऋतस्य योषा न मिनाति धामाहरहर्निष्कृतमाचरन्ती ॥ ९ ॥

> *jānatyahnaḥ prathamasya nāma śukrā kṛṣṇādajaniṣṭa śvitīcī |*
> *ṛtasya yoṣā na mināti dhāmāharaharniṣkṛtamācarantī ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> जानती । अह्नः । प्रथमस्य । नाम । शुक्रा । कृष्णात् । अजनिष्ट । श्वितीची ।
> ऋतस्य । योषा । न । मिनाति । धाम । अहःऽअहः । निःऽकृतम् । आऽचरन्ती ॥ ९ ॥

> *jānatī | ahnaḥ | prathamasya | nāma | śukrā | kṛṣṇāt | ajaniṣṭa | śvitīcī |*
> *ṛtasya | yoṣā | na | mināti | dhāma | ahaḥ 'ahaḥ | niḥ 'kṛtam | ā 'carantī ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> उषाः प्रथमस्य मुख्यस्य प्रथमानस्य वाह्नो दिवसस्य नाम नमनमागमनं जानत्यवगच्छन्ती । प्राणिनां प्रज्ञापयन्तीत्यर्थः । सोषाः शुक्रा स्वतो दीप्ता अत एव श्वितीची श्वैत्यं गच्छन्ती प्रकाशं प्राप्नुवती कृष्णात् कृष्णवर्णात्तमसः सकाशादजनिष्ट । प्रादुर्भवति । यद्यपि तमसः सकाशान्नोत्पद्यते तथापि तदनन्तरभावित्वात्तत उत्पद्यत इत्युपचर्यते । उत्पन्ना सा ऋतस्य सत्यभूतस्यादित्यस्य धाम तेजोयुक्तं स्थानं योषा मिश्रयन्ती न मिनाति । न हिनस्ति । न तेनेयं तेजो न पराभवति । अपि त्वहरहः सर्वेष्वहःसु निष्कृतमाचरन्ती । अलङ्कारशोभां कुर्वती । यद्वा । ऋतस्य सत्यभूतस्य यज्ञस्य धाम देवयजनाख्यं स्थानं योषा मिश्रणशीला सती न मिनाति । न हिनस्ति । किन्त्वहरहः सर्वेषु यागदिवसेषु निष्कृतं हविरादीनां प्रकाशनरूपमलङ्कारमाचरन्ती कुर्वन्ती । तादृश्युषा अजनिष्टेति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥

> *uṣāḥ prathamasya mukhyasya prathamānasya vāhno divasasya nāma namanamāgamanaṃ jānatyavagacchantī | prāṇināṃ prajñāpayantītyarthaḥ | soṣāḥ śukrā svato dīptā ata eva śvitīcī śvaityaṃ gacchantī prakāśaṃ prāpnuvatī kṛṣṇāt kṛṣṇavarṇāttamasaḥ sakāśādajaniṣṭa | prādurbhavati | yadyapi tamasaḥ sakāśānnotpadyate tathāpi tadanantarabhāvitvāttata utpadyata ityupacaryate | utpannā sā ṛtasya satyabhūtasyādityasya dhāma tejoyuktaṃ sthānaṃ yoṣā miśrayantī na mināti | na hinasti | na teneyaṃ tejo na parābhavati | api tvaharahaḥ sarveṣvahaḥsu niṣkṛtamācarantī | alaṅkāraśobhāṃ kurvatī | yadvā | ṛtasya satyabhūtasya yajñasya dhāma devayajanākhyaṃ sthānaṃ yoṣā miśraṇaśīlā satī na mināti | na hinasti | kintvaharahaḥ sarveṣu yāgadivaseṣu niṣkṛtaṃ havirādīnāṃ prakāśanarūpamalaṅkāramācarantī kurvantī | tādṛśyuṣā ajaniṣṭeti pūrvatrānvayaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; the first half is clear; "nahinasti"/"tejo" in the middle is read as printed.)* "*Uṣas* knows (*jānatī*, understands) the *nāma* — the 'bowing', the coming — of the first (*prathama*), the chief, the beginning day (*ahnaḥ*); that is, she causes living beings to know it. She, Uṣas, *śukrā* (self-shining, of herself bright) and therefore *śvitīcī* (reaching whiteness, getting light), was born (*ajaniṣṭa*) from *kṛṣṇāt* — from the black darkness; that is, she appears. Although she is not born from the darkness, still, because she comes after it, it is said figuratively that she is born from it. Born, she, *yoṣā*, mingling with the *dhāma* (the brilliant place) of the true Āditya (*ṛtasya*), does not harm (*na mināti*) it — [her brightness] does not defeat his brilliance; rather, *aharahaḥ*, day by day on all days, *niṣkṛtam ācarantī*: she makes an ornament, a beauty. Or else: she, mingling with the place of the sacrifice of the true one (*ṛtasya* = of the true sacrifice), the place called the sacrificial ground (*devayajana*), does not harm it; on the contrary, day by day on all days of sacrifice she brings about the ornament in the form of the manifestation of the oblations and the like; may such an Uṣas [be born] — this is connected with what precedes."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Ṛtasya* — of the true Āditya (of the sacrifice); *dhāma* — the brilliant place (the region); *yoṣā* — having joined (Uṣas); *na mināti* — does not defeat (the Āditya's brilliance); (*api tu* — but); *aharahaḥ* — every day; *niṣkṛtam ācarantī* — giving the beauty that is an ornament (making the ornament of manifest oblations and the like); *(uṣāḥ* — the deity Uṣas); *ahnaḥ* — of the day; *prathamasya* — of the first part; *nāma* — the coming; *jānatī* — knowing (making the world know); *śukrā* — self-shining (and therefore); *śvitīcī* — possessed of whiteness; *kṛṣṇāt* — from black darkness; *ajaniṣṭa* — came into being.

### Printed p. 110  (PDF 131)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)* **॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Uṣas, though she joins the place of Āditya (and enters the sacrificial hall), does not diminish his radiance (nor does she cause the sacrifice delay); every day she gives Āditya (and the sacrificial hall) the beauty that is an ornament (an ornament in the form of the manifestation of oblations and the like), makes the world know the first part of the day, and being of herself shining, white, she is born from the black (from the darkness).

**Printed English (as printed):** *The self-illumined Dawn, announcing the declination of the first (portion) of the day, is born white-shining out of the gloom : cleansing (with the radiance) of the sun, she impairs not his splendour, but daily adds embellishment (to his lustre).*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 9.**

***jānatī*** — *avagacchantī prāṇināṃ prajñāpayantī*: "Uṣas knows the beginning of the day and makes all beings know it" — that is the sense.

***kṛṣṇāt ajaniṣṭa*** — *nikṛṣṭāt tamasaḥ sakāśāt prādurbhavati*: "Uṣas appears from base darkness, since the darkness of the night gives difficulty to others; after it has diminished, she is born from the darkness of a lower nature"; because the darkness in the night pervades widely, and because Uṣas rises in the last part of the night, the birth of Uṣas is described as from the darkness; and since she comes up after the darkness has gone, this expression is figurative (*aupacārika*). (See the introduction to this Sūkta.)

***ṛtasya dhāma yoṣā na mināti*** — Sāyaṇa has given two meanings for this sentence. The first meaning: the word *ṛta* means the Āditya, who is truth; the place of his brilliance is joined by Uṣas with her own brilliance, but she does not disparage that brilliance.

The word *ṛta* is recorded among the synonyms of water (Ni. 2-14, as read by the OCR on p. 110);
 it is also recorded among the synonyms of *udaka* (water) — thus stated (as printed on p. 111: "ಋತಶಬ್ದವು ಉದಕ(ಸೂರ್ಯಯ)ನಾಮಗಳಲ್ಲಿ (ನಿ. ೨-೧೪) ಪಠಿತವಾಗಿದೆ"). In the Nirukta (4-19, as read by the OCR) he explains *satyaṃ vā yajñaṃ vā* — "truth or sacrifice" — so, following the meaning "truth", the first meaning has been explained.

*Reference numbers printed on this page as read by the reader's Google-Docs OCR (digits only; hyphens and sometimes a digit may be lost — use only as a check):* 2-14

### Printed p. 111  (PDF 132)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 5.)*

The second meaning: taking the meaning of the word *ṛta* as the sacrificial place in which oblations are offered to the deities — *devayajanākhyaṃ sthānaṃ yoṣā miśraṇaśīlā satī na mināti na hinasti*: Uṣas, mingling with the sacrificial ground, does not harm it; rather *aharahaḥ sarveṣu yāgadivaseṣu niṣkṛtaṃ havirādīnāṃ prakāśanarūpam alaṅkāram ācarantī kurvatī ajaniṣṭa*: on every day of sacrifice she makes the ornament consisting of the manifestation of the oblations and the like, and is born. That is: Uṣas, shedding her light in the sacrificial times of the various sacrifice-days that go on day after day, and making the various oblations manifest, brings the sacrifice to completion — thus the rising of Uṣas is described here.

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> कन्याऽइव । तन्वा । शाशदाना । एषि । देवि । देवम् । इयक्षमाणम् ।
> संस्मयमाना । युवतिः । पुरस्तात् । आविः । वक्षांसि । कृणुषे । विभाती ॥ १० ॥

> *kanyā 'iva | tanvā | śāśadānā | eṣi | devi | devam | iyakṣamāṇam |*
> *saṃsmayamānā | yuvatiḥ | purastāt | āviḥ | vakṣāṃsi | kṛṇuṣe | vibhātī ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> तन्वा शरीरेण शाशदाना शाशद्यमाना स्पष्टतां प्राप्नुवती । शाशदानः शाशद्यमानः । नि. ६-१६ । इति यास्कः । कन्येव कमनीया कन्येव । कन्या कमनीया भवति कैनेयं नेतव्येति वा । नि. ४-१५ । इति यास्कः । सा यथा जनान्तिके विवसना संचरति तथा हे उषः त्वं कन्या कमनीयाप्रगल्भा सती तन्वा शरीरेण शाशदाना स्पष्टतां गच्छन्ती दृश्यसे । पश्चात्प्रगल्भा सती हे देवि देवनशीले इयक्षमाणं यष्टुमिच्छन्तमभिमतं दातुमिच्छन्तं वा देवं द्योतनस्वभावं सूर्यरूपं प्रियमेषि गच्छसि । ततः पश्चात् युवतिर्यौवनोपेता सती पुरस्तात्प्रत्युत सूर्यस्य पुरतः संस्मयमाना समीपदंशं [?] हास्यं कुर्वती विभाती अत्यन्तं भासमाना वक्षांसि वक्षसोऽलक्षितानि नानावर्णान्याविष्कृणुषे । प्रकटीकरोषि । यद्वा । युवतिरिति लुप्तोपमा । यथा लोके प्रगल्भा योषित् पुरस्तात् प्रियतमस्य पुरतः संस्मयमाना दन्तप्रदर्शनाय ईषदसनं कुर्वती वक्षांसि वक्षसोपलक्षितानि गोस्थानि बाहुमूलस्तनादीन्याविष्करोति तथा त्वमित्यर्थः । यद्वा । पुरस्तात् पूर्वस्यां दिशि संस्मयमाना स्मितोषमप्रकाशं कुर्वती युवतिः सर्वेषु भावेषु मिश्रणशीला वक्षांसि । वक्ष इति रूपनाम । वन्त्स्थानीयानि नीलपीतादीनि रूपाण्याविष्करोषि ॥

> *tanvā śarīreṇa śāśadānā śāśadyamānā spaṣṭatāṃ prāpnuvatī | śāśadānaḥ śāśadyamānaḥ | ni. 6-16 | iti yāskaḥ | kanyeva kamanīyā kanyeva | kanyā kamanīyā bhavati kaineyaṃ netavyeti vā | ni. 4-15 | iti yāskaḥ | sā yathā janāntike vivasanā saṃcarati tathā he uṣaḥ tvaṃ kanyā kamanīyāpragalbhā satī tanvā śarīreṇa śāśadānā spaṣṭatāṃ gacchantī dṛśyase | paścātpragalbhā satī he devi devanaśīle iyakṣamāṇaṃ yaṣṭumicchantamabhimataṃ dātumicchantaṃ vā devaṃ dyotanasvabhāvaṃ sūryarūpaṃ priyameṣi gacchasi | tataḥ paścāt yuvatiryauvanopetā satī purastātpratyuta sūryasya purataḥ saṃsmayamānā samīpadaṃśaṃ [?] hāsyaṃ kurvatī vibhātī atyantaṃ bhāsamānā vakṣāṃsi vakṣaso 'lakṣitāni nānāvarṇānyāviṣkṛṇuṣe | prakaṭīkaroṣi | yadvā | yuvatiriti luptopamā | yathā loke pragalbhā yoṣit purastāt priyatamasya purataḥ saṃsmayamānā dantapradarśanāya īṣadasanaṃ kurvatī vakṣāṃsi vakṣasopalakṣitāni gosthāni bāhumūlastanādīnyāviṣkaroti tathā tvamityarthaḥ | yadvā | purastāt pūrvasyāṃ diśi saṃsmayamānā smitoṣamaprakāśaṃ kurvatī yuvatiḥ sarveṣu bhāveṣu miśraṇaśīlā vakṣāṃsi | vakṣa iti rūpanāma | vantsthānīyāni nīlapītādīni rūpāṇyāviṣkaroṣi ‖*

*(Read from the image and checked against the OCR; the small-type words in the middle — "samīpadaṃśaṃ", "vakṣaso 'lakṣitāni", "gosthāni", "vantsthānīyāni" — are doubtful in the print and are given as I read them; the OCR text there is badly garbled.)* "*Tanvā* — with the body; *śāśadānā* — becoming visible, attaining clarity. '*Śāśadānaḥ* means *śāśadyamānaḥ*' (Ni. 6-16, as read by the OCR), says Yāska. *Kanyeva* — like a lovely maiden. '*Kanyā* is lovely; or [it is said] "by whom is she to be led?"' (Ni. 4-15, as read by the OCR), says Yāska. As such a maiden goes about near people in scanty dress, so, O Uṣas, you, a lovely maiden not yet bold, are seen becoming clear with your body. Afterwards, grown bold, O goddess (*devi*, of the shining nature), you go to the god (*devam*, of the shining nature, of the form of the Sun) who is dear to you, who wishes to sacrifice, or who wishes to give you what is desired. Thereafter, a young woman (*yuvatiḥ*) endowed with youth, in front of the Sun, smiling (*saṃsmayamānā*) a little, shining (*vibhātī*) exceedingly, you make manifest (*āviḥ kṛṇuṣe*) the breasts, the many-coloured [forms] [?] seen on the bosom. Or else: *yuvatiḥ* is a simile with the particle omitted. As in the world a bold woman, in front of her beloved, smiling, lightly laughing to show her teeth, reveals the parts of the bosom — the hollow of the arm, the breasts and the like — so you: that is the sense. Or else: *purastāt* — in the eastern quarter, smiling and making a light like a gentle smile, a young woman mingling in all existences, you reveal the *vakṣāṃsi* — '*vakṣa*' is a name for form — the forms such as blue and yellow, that take the place of [the parts of the body] [?]."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Devi* — O goddess; *kanyā iva* — like a maiden; *tanvā* — with the body; *śāśadānā* — having attained clarity; *iyakṣamāṇam* — wishing to give (what is desired); *devam* — the shining (the Sun, who is dear); *eṣi* — you approach; (*tataḥ* — afterwards); *yuvatiḥ* — endowed with youth (you); *purastāt* — in front of the beloved; *saṃsmayamānā* — with a slight smile; *vibhātī* — of special brilliance; *vakṣāṃsi* — the chest and all the other limbs; *ā kṛṇuṣe* — you make manifest. *Purastāt* — in the eastern quarter; *saṃsmayamānā* — spreading a brilliance like a gentle smile; *yuvatiḥ* — showing many colours; *vibhātī* — of special light; *vakṣāṃsi* — the forms (blue, yellow and the like); *āviḥ kṛṇuṣe* — you make manifest.

### Printed p. 114  (PDF 135)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Like a maiden, having a clearly visible body, O goddess, you approach the resplendent (Sun, who is your dear one) and who is minded to give what is desired; then, like a young woman, in the presence of your husband you spread a gentle smile, and being of special radiance you make manifest all your limbs, beginning with the bosom; (or) in the eastern quarter, spreading a brilliance like a gentle smile, of special light, you make manifest many forms — blue, yellow and the like.

**Printed English (as printed):** *Goddess, manifest in person like a maiden, you go to the resplendent and munificent (sun); and, like a youthful bride (before her husband), you uncover, smiling, your bosom in his presence.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 10.**

In this ṛk Uṣas is compared to a woman who first has the state of a maiden (*kanyā*) and afterwards the state of a grown (*prauḍha*) woman.

***kanyeva tanvā śāśadānā*** — *kamanīyā kanyeva | sā yathā janāntike vivasanā saṃcarati | tathā uṣaḥ tvaṃ kamanīyā apragalbhā satī kanyā tanvā śarīreṇa śāśadānā spaṣṭatāṃ gacchantī dṛśyase | śāśadānā śāśadyamānā spaṣṭatāṃ prāpnuvatī.* The Kannada comment: Uṣas is like a beautiful girl, like a small child knowing nothing, who goes about unclothed near people; that is, as soon as the time of dawn arises it is described as a beautiful girl.

***Yāska*** — *kanyā kamanīyā bhavati | kaineyaṃ netavyeti vā | kamanenānīyata iti vā kanater vā syāt kāntikarmaṇaḥ* (Ni. 4-15, as printed "೪-೧೫"; the OCR agrees): the word *kanyā* is used with beauty as its cause. *Iyam* — this girl; either "*kai netavyā*": where is she to be led, [i.e. to join]; or *kamanena* — by the quality that attracts others she is led — she is taken along; or, from the root *kan* with the sense of "beautiful, shining", the word *kanyā* is derived. Following this, Sāyaṇa explains *kamanīyā* as "lovely with the beauty of the body".

***śāśadānaḥ*** — *śāśadyamānaḥ* (Ni. 6-16, as printed "೬-೧೬"): since Yāska has so explained it, the sense is "possessing the manner of being perceived by everyone".

### Printed p. 115  (PDF 136)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6.)*

***devi iyakṣamāṇaṃ devam eṣi*** — by this sentence it is described that Uṣas, whose nature is to spread light, goes to the Sun, the giver of light who fulfils the wishes of the sacrificer who wishes to sacrifice — like a girl choosing her husband, who obtains him as her husband.

***saṃsmayamānā yuvatiḥ vakṣāṃsi āvir kṛṇuṣe*** — Sāyaṇa explains two meanings by this sentence. In the first meaning he explains the word *yuvatiḥ* as *yuvatir iva*, a case of the dropped simile-particle (*lupta-upamā*): thus, a mature woman, that is one with an age and bodily strength fit to enjoy pleasure, a beautiful woman, in front of her beloved displays the desire for enjoyment she has, shows a gentle smile and her own grace; so Uṣas acts in front of the Sun — this is the purport.

In the second meaning, in the eastern quarter, spreading her own light that is like a gentle smile, and making her light and the objects in the world visible to all, Uṣas acts so that the beauty of the world becomes visible to all — this is the purport.

> उपो अदर्शि शुन्ध्युवो न वक्षो नोधा इवाविरकृत प्रियाणि ।
> अद्मसन्न ससतो बोधयन्ती शश्वत्तमागात्पुनरेयुषीणाम् ॥

> *upo adarśi śundhyuvo na vakṣo nodhā ivāvirakṛta priyāṇi |*
> *admasanna sasato bodhayantī śaśvattamāgātpunareyuṣīṇām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-124-4 [?] — as printed; the last numeral is doubtful in my reading, and the OCR shape "n-nge-V" gives only the first two groups.) *(Verse read letter by letter from the image; the OCR agrees except for "puna-reyuṣīṇām".)* Gloss: "[She] has been seen, like the bosom of a (self-)cleansing woman; as a Nodhas-like [poet] she has made her dear [forms] manifest; waking the sleepers who lie down for food, she has come, the most continual of those who return" — mine and tentative.

In this ṛk the word *vakṣaḥ* is explained as *rūpāṇi* ("forms"). Sāyaṇa: *vakṣāṃsi — vakṣa iti rūpanāma | vantsthānīyāni nīlapītādīni rūpāṇi*: the word *vakṣaḥ* conveys the meaning "form". As a young woman makes manifest the parts of her body, her bosom and so on, so Uṣas makes manifest the forms of the objects — blue, yellow and so on; thus the meaning is explained.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar pages pp. 115–117; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *tanvā* — instrumental singular, the ending *ṭā*; the *yaṇ* substitution in the place of the acute; since the ending follows that, *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya* (Pā. 8-2-4) gives the ending the *svarita*. *śāśadānā* — root *śada śātane*; *dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ* (Pā. 3-1-22) gives *yaṅ* in the sense of intensity; *śānac* after it in the sense of laṭ; *chandasy ubhayathā* (Pā. 3-4-117) gives it ārdhadhātuka designation, hence *ato lopaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-48) elides the preceding *a* and *yasya halaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-49) the *y*; *dīrgho 'kitaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-83) lengthens the reduplication; since the preceding sūtra also gives the *sārvadhātuka* designation, *abhyastānām ādiḥ* (Pā. 6-1-189) gives the accent on the first syllable (so the word is not final-acute); in the feminine, *ajādyataṣṭāp* gives *ṭāp*; *aco 'prāgṛhya-* [the rule on nasalised ā] makes the ā nasalised.

*eṣi* — root *iṅ* (*i gatau*); second person singular *sip*; *śap* with *luk*; guṇa of the root-vowel on account of *sip*; since it stands at the head of a pāda there is no *nighāta* accent; since *sip* is *pit* it is unaccented, so the root's accent remains; *ādeśapratyayayoḥ* gives *ṣatva* of the ending.

*iyakṣamāṇam* — root *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu*; in the sense of wish, *dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā* (Pā. 3-1-7) gives *san*; *san-yaṅoḥ* (the reduplication of the root); for the reduplicative syllable the initial consonant remains, and in the Veda *saṃprasāraṇa* occurs; *pūrvarūpa*; *cojaḥ kuḥ* gives *ku* (guttural) for the *j* of the root; *khari ca* gives *ca*[r]; *ādeśapratyayayoḥ* gives *ṣa* for the *s* of *san*; *āne muk* (Pā. 7-2-82) gives the augment *muk* to the stem; *ṇatva* of the *n* of *śānac* on account of the *ṣ*; *abhyastānām ādiḥ* (Pā. 6-1-189) gives acute on the first syllable; accusative singular.

*saṃsmayamānā* — root *ṣmiṅ īṣadhasane*; *śānac* in that sense, *śap* augment; guṇa and *ayādeśa* with that; *āne muk* gives *muk* to the stem ending in *a*; since the ending follows the *upadeśa* the *sārvadhātuka* occurs, so by *tāsyanudāttet* (Pā. 6-1-186) it is unaccented and the root-accent remains; in the compound *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* gives the accent of the final member; in the feminine, because it ends in *a*, *ṭāp*.

*yuvatiḥ* — the word *yuvan*; when the feminine is intended, *yūnas tiḥ* (Pā. 4-1-77) gives the suffix *ti*; *nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya* gives the loss of the *n*; by the accent of the suffix it is final-acute.

*purastāt* — *pūrvādharāvarāṇāṃ purdhavaś caiṣām* (Pā. 5-3-39) gives the suffix *astāti*; for *pūrva*, *pur* is substituted; the suffix has the acute on its first syllable.

*kṛṇuṣe* — root *kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca*; laṭ second person singular, the ending *thās*; *thāsaḥ se* (Pā. 3-4-80) gives it the substitute *se*; *dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca* (Pā. 3-1-80, as read by the OCR) gives the *u*-suffix, with the *a* (the vowel *a* of the root-end); since it has the marker *i*, the augment *num*; *ato lopaḥ* gives the loss of the *a*; the *nighāta* accent of a verb-ending. ‖ 10 ‖

#### Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> सुसंकाशा मातृमृष्टेव योषाविस्तन्वं कृणुषे दृशे कम् ।
> भद्रा त्वमुषो वितरं व्युच्छ न तत्ते अन्या उषसो नशन्त ॥ ११ ॥

> *susaṃkāśā mātṛmṛṣṭeva yoṣāvistanvaṃ kṛṇuṣe dṛśe kam |*
> *bhadrā tvamuṣo vitaraṃ vyuccha na tatte anyā uṣaso naśanta ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सुऽसंकाशा । मातृमृष्टाऽइव । योषा । आविः । तन्वम् । कृणुषे । दृशे । कम् ।
> भद्रा । त्वम् । उषः । वितरम् । वि । उच्छ । न । तत् । ते । अन्याः । उषसः । नशन्त ॥ ११ ॥

> *su 'saṃkāśā | mātṛmṛṣṭā 'iva | yoṣā | āviḥ | tanvam | kṛṇuṣe | dṛśe | kam |*
> *bhadrā | tvam | uṣaḥ | vitaram | vi | uccha | na | tat | te | anyāḥ | uṣasaḥ | naśanta ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे उषोदेवि मातृमृष्टा मातृभिर्जननीभिः शुद्धीकृता योषेव सुसंकाशात्यर्थं प्रकाशमाना त्वं तन्वं स्वकीयां तनुं दृशे सर्वेषां दर्शनायाविः कृणुषे । प्रकटयसि । यथा लोके मात्रादिना स्वलंकृतात्यन्तं शोभना सती स्वकीयं लावण्योपेतं सर्वशरीरं दर्शनायाविष्करोति तद्वत्त्वमित्यर्थः । अत्र कमिति पादपूरणोऽत्र विशेषस्याभावात् शिशिरं जीवनाय कमिवत् । तथा च यास्काचार्यः । मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिदु इति । नि. १-९ । इति । यद्वा । कमिति सुखवचनः । सुखं यथा भवति तथाविष्कृणुष इत्यर्थः । हे उषः यत एवं करोषि अतो भद्रा कल्याणशीला स्तुत्या त्वं वितरं व्युच्छ । आवरकमन्धकारं विप्रकृष्टं यथा भवति तथा विवासय । अत्र यद्यपि विशेषो न श्रुतस्तथापि प्रकाशनिवर्त्यत्वात्परिहरणीयत्वाच्च विवासनीयं तम एवेति गम्यते । किंच ते तव तद्विवसनमन्या उषसोऽतीता आगामिन्यश्च न नशन्त । न व्याप्नुवन्ति । तथा व्युच्छेति भावः । नशतिर्व्याप्तिकर्मा । इन्नति नक्षतीति व्याप्तिकर्मसु पाठात् ॥

> *he uṣodevi mātṛmṛṣṭā mātṛbhirjananībhiḥ śuddhīkṛtā yoṣeva susaṃkāśātyarthaṃ prakāśamānā tvaṃ tanvaṃ svakīyāṃ tanuṃ dṛśe sarveṣāṃ darśanāyāviḥ kṛṇuṣe | prakaṭayasi | yathā loke mātrādinā svalaṃkṛtātyantaṃ śobhanā satī svakīyaṃ lāvaṇyopetaṃ sarvaśarīraṃ darśanāyāviṣkaroti tadvattvamityarthaḥ | atra kamiti pādapūraṇo 'tra viśeṣasyābhāvāt śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kamivat | tathā ca yāskācāryaḥ | mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmidu iti | ni. 1-9 | iti | yadvā | kamiti sukhavacanaḥ | sukhaṃ yathā bhavati tathāviṣkṛṇuṣa ityarthaḥ | he uṣaḥ yata evaṃ karoṣi ato bhadrā kalyāṇaśīlā stutyā tvaṃ vitaraṃ vyuccha | āvarakamandhakāraṃ viprakṛṣṭaṃ yathā bhavati tathā vivāsaya | atra yadyapi viśeṣo na śrutastathāpi prakāśanivartyatvātpariharaṇīyatvācca vivāsanīyaṃ tama eveti gamyate | kiṃca te tava tadvivasanamanyā uṣaso 'tītā āgāminyaśca na naśanta | na vyāpnuvanti | tathā vyuccheti bhāvaḥ | naśatirvyāptikarmā | innati nakṣatīti vyāptikarmasu pāṭhāt ‖*

*(Read from the image and compared with the OCR; the OCR's Devanagari is badly garbled in the middle ("tanvaṃ", "śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kamivat" are read from the image). A few words in the middle of the passage are small and doubtful, e.g. "mitākṣareṣv anarthakāḥ kam īm id u", and the numeral of the Nirukta reference, which I read as "1-9" ("೧-೯"; the OCR "१-९").)* "O goddess Uṣas, *mātṛmṛṣṭā* — purified by her mothers, the mothers who bore her — like a young woman (*yoṣā iva*), *susaṃkāśā* — shining exceedingly: you make your own body (*tanvam*) manifest for all to see (*dṛśe*). As in the world a woman well adorned by her mother and others, being exceedingly beautiful, reveals her whole body, full of loveliness, to be seen — so you: that is the sense. Here the word *kam* is merely a pāda-filler, since no special meaning is found — like *kam* in *śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kam*. And Yāska says: 'In the metres of limited syllables, [the particles] *kam, īm, id, u* are without meaning' (Ni. 1-9). Or else *kam* means 'happiness': you make [your body] manifest so that there is happiness. O Uṣas, since you do thus, therefore, auspicious and praiseworthy, *vitaraṃ vi uccha* — dispel (*vivāsaya*) the darkness that covers, so that it goes far. Although it is not stated here what is to be dispelled, it is understood to be darkness itself, since it is removed by light and must be got rid of. Moreover, this dispelling of yours — other dawns, past and future, *na naśanta* — do not reach it (do not pervade it); so *vi uccha*: that is the sense. The root *naś* has the sense of pervading, since it is read among the verbs of pervading: *innati, nakṣati*."

### Printed p. 118  (PDF 139)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Uṣaḥ* — O goddess Uṣas; *mātṛmṛṣṭā* — adorned by her mother (made pure); *yoṣā iva* — like a woman; *susaṃkāśā* — exceedingly radiant; *tvam* — you; *tanvam* — (your) own body; *dṛśe* — for (everyone's) seeing; *kam* — so that it be pleasant; *āviḥ kṛṇuṣe* — you make manifest; (*ataḥ* — therefore); *bhadrā* — auspicious (therefore praiseworthy); (*tvam* — you); *vitaram* — the covering darkness; *vi uccha* — drive away; *te* — your; *tat* — that (work of dispelling the darkness); *anyāḥ atītāḥ ca anāgatāḥ ca uṣasaḥ* — other dawns, past and future; *na naśanta* — do not attain.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O goddess Uṣas, like a woman adorned by her mother, being of special radiance, you make your body to be seen (by all). Therefore, being auspicious (and praiseworthy), dispel the darkness that covers the world, in a manner that none of the dawns, past or future, can imitate.

**Printed English (as printed):** *Radiant as a bride decorated by her mother, you willingly display your person to the view. Do you, auspicious Ushas, remove the investing (gloom), for other dawns than you do not disperse it.*

**Special topics, Ṛk 11.**

***mātṛmṛṣṭā yoṣā iva susaṃkāśā*** — *mātṛbhiḥ jananībhiḥ śuddhīkṛtā yoṣā iva atyantaṃ prakāśamānā. yathā loke mātrādinā svalaṅkṛtā atyantaṃ śobhanā satī svakīyaṃ lāvaṇyopetaṃ sarvaśarīraṃ darśanāyāviṣkaroti tadvat tvam ity arthaḥ.* A woman who has been prepared (or adorned) by her mother and other intimate women, a loving woman, being very beautiful, shows to others her body, full of loveliness, so that it comes within the sight of her beloved; so Uṣas too shows her form in front of the Sun — thus it is described.

Yāska explains the word *yoṣā*: it is derived from the root *yu miśraṇe*, "*yoṣā yauteḥ*" (Ni. 3-15, as read by the OCR; the print "೩-೧೫"). The commentator (*vṛttikāra*) explains: *sā hi miśrayaty ātmānaṃ puruṣeṇa sākam* — a woman unites with a man in order to have union of bodies with him.

### Printed p. 119  (PDF 140)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 6.)*

***dṛśe kam*** — *atra kam iti pādapūraṇaḥ viśeṣasyābhāvāt śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kam iti vat | yadvā kam iti sukhavacanaḥ sukhaṃ yathā bhavati tathā āviṣkṛṇuṣe.* Here, because the word *kam* is an indeclinable, for want of any other special meaning it is, in one way, a mere pāda-filler; Sāyaṇa has explained it so. And Yāska:

> अथ ये प्रवृत्तेऽर्थेऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रन्थेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छन्ति पदेपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिद्धितेति

> *atha ye pravṛtte 'rthe 'mitākṣareṣu grantheṣu vākyapūraṇā āgacchanti padepūraṇāste mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmiddhiteti*

(Ni. 1-9, as printed "೧-೯", the shape in the image; read letter by letter, the last words doubtful.) Particles (indeclinables) used in sentences serve to fill out words. Since verses are bound by metres of measured syllables, the indeclinables *kam, īm, it, u* in them convey no meaning — so they are without meaning (*anarthaka*).

> निष्टक्राः [?] भूरितोका वृकादिव । बिभ्यस्यन्तो वनाशिरे । शिशिरं जीवनाय कम् ॥

> *niṣṭakrāḥ [?] bhūritokā vṛkādiva | bibhyasyanto vanāśire | śiśiraṃ jīvanāya kam ‖*

(Ni. 1-[?]; the numerals "೧-೧೮" or similar are not clear to me.) In this quotation the word *kam* is, though it is absent, used without any purpose as if for the completion of the sense — thus an example is given.

Moreover both words *kam* and *īm* are recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]4, numerals unclear), and *kam* is also recorded among the names of happiness (Ni. 3-[?]9, unclear). Following this explanation of Yāska, Sāyaṇa explains the word *kam* in the sense of happiness: Uṣas displays her own body to all in a manner that gives happiness — this is the second meaning.

***bhadrā tvaṃ vyuccha*** — *kalyāṇaśīlā stutyā āvarakam andhakāraṃ viprakṛṣṭaṃ yathā bhavati tathā vivāsaya.* Since Uṣas is praised, she is prayed to destroy the dense darkness. Uṣas is described as the bringer of auspiciousness. Since Uṣas is always engaged in the act of bringing light, in the matter of the work of Uṣas there is no particular thing to be prayed for. Hence the addition (*upasaṃhāra*) is stated: of those past and future dawns pervading and destroying the covering darkness...

### Printed p. 120  (PDF 141)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)*

***naśanta*** — *innati, nakṣati* — among these ten verbs of pervading, '*naśat*' is read (Ni. 3-10, as read by the OCR); so *naśanta* means 'they pervade'.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page; noted briefly, numbers as read).** *susaṃkāśā* — root *kāśṛ dīptau*; since it belongs to the *pacādi* class, the suffix *aṭ*; *ṭāp* in the feminine; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. 6-2-139 as read by the OCR) gives the accent of the final member of the kṛt-compound; nominative singular. *mātṛmṛṣṭā* — *mātṛbhiḥ mṛṣṭā*; root *mṛjū śuddhau*; in the passive, *niṣṭhā* (Pā. 3-2-102) gives *kta*; *vraśca-bhrasja-…-ṣaḥ* (Pā. 8-2-36) gives *ṣa* for the root's *j*; *ṣṭutva* of the *t* of the ending following that; *tṛtīyā karmaṇi* (Pā. 6-2-48) gives the accent of the first member; then *ṭāp* in the feminine as before. *tanvam* — the word *tanu*; the accusative *am* following, *tanvādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam* gives *yaṇ*; the *yaṇ* stands at the place of the acute; since the ending follows it, *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya* (Pā. 8-2-4) gives the ending the *svarita*. *dṛśe* — root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*; *dṛśe vikhye ca* (Pā. 3-4-11) records it as a *tumarthe* form in the Veda; since it ends in *e* and is a kṛdanta, *kṛnmejantaḥ* (Pā. 1-1-39) gives it the indeclinable designation. *bhadrā* — root *bhadi kalyāṇe sukhe ca*; the Uṇādi suffix *rak* (*bhadrā* nominative singular); final-acute by the accent of the suffix. *vitaram* — root *tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ*; pacādi *aṭ*; guṇa and *raparatva* with that; in the compound *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the accent of the final member; the final member is final-acute by the suffix-accent. *uccha* — root *uchī vivāse*; loṭ second singular, *sip* with *hi* substituted; *ato heḥ* (Pā. 6-4-105) elides *hi*; the verb-accent *nighāta* after a non-verb.

*naśanta* — root *naś adarśane*; here used in the sense of motion ('going'); recorded as *innati nakṣati* among the verbs of pervading. By *vyatyayo bahulam* the *ātmanepada* ending (Chāndasa) …

#### Ṛk 12

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अश्वावतीर्गोमतीर्विश्ववारा यतमाना रश्मिभिः सूर्यस्य ।
> परा च यन्ति पुनरा च यन्ति भद्रा नाम वहमाना उषासः ॥ १२ ॥

> *aśvāvatīrgomatīrviśvavārā yatamānā raśmibhiḥ sūryasya |*
> *parā ca yanti punarā ca yanti bhadrā nāma vahamānā uṣāsaḥ ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अश्वऽवतीः । गोऽमतीः । विश्वऽवाराः । यतमानाः । रश्मिऽभिः । सूर्यस्य ।
> परा । च । यन्ति । पुनः । आ । च । यन्ति । भद्रा । नाम । वहमानाः । उषासः ॥ १२ ॥

> *aśva 'vatīḥ | go 'matīḥ | viśva 'vārāḥ | yatamānāḥ | raśmi 'bhiḥ | sūryasya |*
> *parā | ca | yanti | punaḥ | ā | ca | yanti | bhadrā | nāma | vahamānāḥ | uṣāsaḥ ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अश्वावतीरश्ववत्यः बहुभिरश्वैस्तद्वत्यः । तथा गोमतीर्बहुभिर्गोभिस्तद्वत्यः । विश्ववारा विश्वे वारा वरणीयाः कालाः यासां ताः । सार्वकालीना इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । विश्वे वरितारो यासु ताः विश्ववाराः । विश्वैर्वरणीया इत्यर्थः । सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्यतमानाः सूर्यरश्मिभिः साकं तमोनिवारणाय प्रयत्नं कुर्वाणाः । यद्यपि सूर्यरश्मय एव जगत्प्रकाशनाय प्रभवन्ति तथापि सूर्योदयात्पूर्वं तमोनिवारणस्यापेक्षितत्वात्तासामपि प्रयत्नमविरुद्धम् । रश्मिदेवता अपि प्रकाशिका इत्यर्थः । किंच भद्रा भद्रं कल्याणं स्तुत्यं वा नाम नमनं सर्वजनानुकूल्यं वहमाना धारयमाणा उषास उषोदेवताः परा च यन्ति । परायन्ति च । तथा पुनरा च यन्ति । पुनरायन्ति च । परस्परापेक्षयोभयत्र चशब्दः । या एवातीतेषु दिनेषु गतास्ता एव पुनः पुनर्दिनान्तरेष्वस्माकमायन्तीति [?] । जगन्निर्वाहाय प्रतिदिनं गतागतं कुर्वन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

### Printed p. 122  (PDF 143)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Ṛk 12).** *Aśvāvatīḥ* — possessed of horses; *gomatīḥ* — possessed of cows; *viśvavārāḥ* — belonging to all times (desired by all); *sūryasya* — of the Sun; *raśmibhiḥ* — with the rays; *yatamānāḥ* — striving (to dispel the darkness); *bhadrā* — auspicious; *nāma* — favour (to all people); *vahamānāḥ* — bringing about; (the) *uṣāsaḥ* — Uṣas deities; *parā yanti* — depart; *punaḥ ca ā yanti* — and come again.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Possessed of horses and cows, at all times striving at the work of dispelling darkness together (in concert) with the rays of the Sun, and bringing auspiciousness to all, the Uṣas deities keep going and keep coming.

**Printed English (as printed):** *Possessed of horses, possessed of cows, existing through all time, vying with the rays of the sun (in dissipating darkness) auspicious Dawns, sending down benefits (on mankind), pass away and again return.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 12.**

***viśvavārāḥ*** — *viśve vārāḥ varaṇīyāḥ kālā yāsāṃ tāḥ | sārvakālīnāḥ | yadvā viśve varitāro yāsu tāḥ | viśvair varaṇīyāḥ.* The word *vāra* is derived from the root *vṝ* (*vṛñ varaṇe*) which conveys "choose, desire", so it means "desired"; thus the word *viśvavārāḥ*, used as an epithet of the word *uṣāsaḥ*, is explained in one way as "for them all the times of dawn are desired", and Sāyaṇa explains it in another way as "all desire the times of dawn" (*viśvaiḥ varaṇīyāḥ*). By both these meanings the beauty of the times of dawn, and its being a benefit to all, becomes evident.

***sūryasya raśmibhir yatamānāḥ*** — *sūryaraśmibhiḥ sākaṃ tamonivāraṇāya prayatnaṃ kurvāṇāḥ.* The sense: the dawns, joining with the rays of the Sun, strive to remove the darkness. The darkness is removed by the Sun's rays themselves; but before the Sun rises, in order to destroy darkness by making the Sun's rays manifest, Uṣas spreads her own light and is a helper — this is the sense.

In *gomatīḥ* also *matup* and *pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*; since it follows a long *ā*… [no] *matup*'s *m* is not changed to *v*; since *matup* has the marker *p* it is unaccented. *viśvavārāḥ* — *viśve vārāḥ yāsāṃ tāḥ*; *bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām* (Pā. 6-2-106) gives the final-acute of the first member; nominative plural.

*yatamānāḥ* — root *yatī prayatne*; *śānac* in the sense of laṭ, *śap* augment; *āne muk* (Pā. 7-2-82) gives *muk* to a stem in *a*; since the *sārvadhātuka* follows the *upadeśa*, *tāsyanudāttet* (Pā. 6-1-186) makes it unaccented, and the root-accent remains.

*sūryasya* — root *ṣū gatau* [as printed "ಸೃ ಗತೌ"]; *rājasūyasūrya…* (Pā. 3-1-114) records the form as ending in *kyap*; since the suffix has the marker *p* it is unaccented; genitive singular.

*yanti* — root *iṇ gatau* (Adādi); laṭ third person plural *jhi*; *jhor antaḥ* gives *ant*; *iṇo yaṇ* (Pā. 6-4-81) gives *yaṇ* to the root; since *ca* stands before it, *cavāyoge prathamā* (Pā. 8-1-59) prohibits the *nighāta* accent in the first [verb]; the suffix is acute (? accent as printed: "ಪ್ರತ್ಯಯದ ಆದ್ಯುದಾತ್ತ"); in the second verb there is no prohibition, so the *nighāta* accent applies.

*vahamānāḥ* — root *vaha prāpaṇe*, ubhayapadī; *śānac* in the sense of laṭ, *śap* augment; as before *muk* is added to a stem in *a*, and the *sārvadhātuka* is unaccented since it follows the *upadeśa*, so the root accent remains. ‖ 12 ‖

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे उषः ऋतस्य सत्यभूतादित्यस्य रश्मिं रश्मीननुयच्छमानानुकूल्येन प्रवर्तमाना त्वं भद्रं भद्रं क्रतुं तत्तत्कल्याणं स्तुत्यं वा लौकिकं वैदिकं कर्म तद्विषयां प्रज्ञां वा धेहि । स्थापय । हे उषः नोऽस्मदर्थं सुहवा सुष्ठ्वाहूता सती व्युच्छ । तमो विवासय । प्रकाशं कुर्वित्यर्थः । किमर्थमिति तदुच्यते । मघवत्सु । मघमिति धननाम । हविर्लक्षणधनयुक्तेष्वस्मासु यजमानेषु रायश्च स्युः । बहुविधानि धनानि संभवन्तीति पूर्वोक्तेन क्रतुना सह समुच्चयार्थश्चशब्दः ॥

> *he uṣaḥ ṛtasya satyabhūtādityasya raśmiṃ raśmīnanuyacchamānānukūlyena pravartamānā tvaṃ bhadraṃ bhadraṃ kratuṃ tattatkalyāṇaṃ stutyaṃ vā laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ karma tadviṣayāṃ prajñāṃ vā dhehi | sthāpaya | he uṣaḥ no 'smadarthaṃ suhavā suṣṭhvāhūtā satī vyuccha | tamo vivāsaya | prakāśaṃ kurvityarthaḥ | kimarthamiti taducyate | maghavatsu | maghamiti dhananāma | havirlakṣaṇadhanayukteṣvasmāsu yajamāneṣu rāyaśca syuḥ | bahuvidhāni dhanāni saṃbhavantīti pūrvoktena kratunā saha samuccayārthaścaśabdaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; checked against the OCR, which is garbled in several words.)* "O Uṣas, following (*anuyacchamānā*) the ray (*raśmim* — the rays) of the true Āditya (*ṛtasya*) — acting in accord with them — place (*dhehi*, establish) in us each auspicious *kratu*, that is, each auspicious and praiseworthy action, worldly or Vedic, or the wisdom concerned with it. O Uṣas, well invoked for us (*suhavā*), *vi uccha* — dispel the darkness; make light: that is the sense. For what? That is said: *maghavatsu* — *magha* is a name for wealth: in us the sacrificers possessed of wealth in the form of oblations, may *rāyaḥ* (riches) — of many kinds — arise; the word *ca* has the sense of conjunction with the *kratu* mentioned before."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *He uṣaḥ* — O goddess Uṣas; *ṛtasya* — of the true (Āditya); *raśmim* — the rays; *anuyacchamānā* — acting in accord with all (you); *bhadraṃ bhadraṃ kratum* — each auspicious action (and the knowledge of it); *asmāsu* — in us; *dhehi* — establish; (*uṣaḥ* — O goddess Uṣas;) *suhavā* — well (with praise) invoked (by us); *naḥ* — for us; *vi uccha* — dispel the darkness; *maghavatsu* — those possessed of wealth in the form of oblations; *asmāsu* — (among us) the sacrificers; *adya* — now; *rāyaḥ ca syuḥ* — may many kinds of wealth arise.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O goddess Uṣas, directing the rays of Āditya to suit us, make each of (our) auspicious [works] firm; well praised (by us) dispel the darkness for us; grant many kinds of prosperity to the sacrificers who are possessed of oblations and the like.

**Printed English (as printed):** *Co-operating with the rays of the true (sun), confirm in us every propitious act : earnestly invoked by us to-day, disperse, Ushas, (the darkness), that wealth may devolve upon us, (already) affluent (in sacrificial treasures).*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 13.**

***ṛtasya — satyabhūtādityasya*** — The word *ṛta* is used in the senses *udaka* (water) (Ni. 2-24, as printed, the OCR agrees), *muhūrta* (a particular division of time) (Ni. 2-25), *satya* or *yajña* (Ni. 4-19)…

### Printed p. 126  (PDF 147)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 18 Sū. 123".)*

…thus the word *ṛta* has many meanings; here it is an epithet of the word *Āditya*. It is described that Uṣas follows the ray of the true Āditya and spreads light.

***bhadraṃ bhadraṃ kratuṃ dehi*** [as printed; the bhāṣya reads *dhehi*] — *tattat kalyāṇaṃ stutyaṃ vā laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ karma tadviṣayāṃ prajñāṃ vā sthāpaya.* In the world, skill in carrying out acts related to conduct that is praiseworthy and auspicious in various ways, or proficiency in doing the actions prescribed in the Veda — this Uṣas is prayed to bring about for us.

Yāska records the word *kratu* among the names of *karma* (Ni. 3-2) and among the names of *prajñā* (Ni. 3-13):

> उतस्य वाजी क्षिपणिं तुरण्यति ग्रीवायां बद्धो अपिकक्ष आसनि ।
> क्रतुं दधिक्रा अनु संतवीत्वत्पथामङ्कांस्यन्वापनीफणत् ॥

> *utasya vājī kṣipaṇiṃ turaṇyati grīvāyāṃ baddho apikakṣa āsani |*
> *kratuṃ dadhikrā anu saṃtavītvatpathāmaṅkāṃsyanvāpanīphaṇat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-40-4, as printed "೪-೪೦-೪".) — citing this ṛk he has stated for *kratu* the meaning "action or wisdom". Sāyaṇa too has explained the word *kratu* in both these ways.

***suhavā*** — *suṣṭhu āhūtā*: the sense is that Uṣas is invoked in the sacrifices, in the order prescribed by the Veda, in the proper way.

***vyuccha*** — *tamo vivāsaya, prakāśaṃ kuru.* The root *uchī* conveys "removal" (*vivāsana*, meaning "destroy"), with the prefix *vi*; so Uṣas is prayed to root out the darkness and spread the light exceedingly.

***asmāsu rāyaḥ maghavatsu ca syuḥ*** — by this sentence Uṣas is prayed that to us who perform the sacrifice there may be wealth in the form of oblations, to offer to the various deities, and that the various rites may be completed.

The word *rāyaḥ* and the word *magha* in *maghavatsu* also convey the meaning "wealth", being recorded among the twenty-eight names of wealth (Ni. 3-9, as read by the OCR): "*magham*, *reknaḥ*" and so on.

> परिषद्यं हिरण्यस्य रेक्णो नित्यस्य रायः पतयः स्याम ।
> न शेषो अग्ने अन्यजातमस्त्यचेतानस्य मा पथो वि दुक्षः ॥

> *pariṣadyaṃ hiraṇyasya rekṇo nityasya rāyaḥ patayaḥ syāma |*
> *na śeṣo agne anyajātamastyacetānasya mā patho vi dukṣaḥ ‖*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (pp. 127–128; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *raśmim* — by *vyatyaya* the singular ending for a plural. *anuyacchamānā* — to the root *yam*, when *śānac* comes in the sense of laṭ, *iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ* (Pā. 7-3-77) gives the substitute *cha* for the root; *āne muk* (Pā. 7-2-82) gives *muk* to a stem in *a*; since the *sārvadhātuka* follows the *upadeśa*, *tāsyanudāttet* (Pā. 6-1-186) makes it unaccented and the root-accent remains; in the kṛt-compound with *uttarapada* the natural accent arises; in the feminine *ṭāp*, since it ends in *a*; nominative singular. *bhadraṃ bhadram* — *nityavīpsayoḥ* (Pā. 8-1-4) gives doubling; since the latter has the designation *āmreḍita*, *anudāttaṃ ca* (Pā. 8-1-3) gives it the all-unaccented accent. *dhehi* — root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; loṭ second person singular, *sip* replaced by *hi*, *śnu*-augment (*śluḥ*) [as printed "ಶ್ಲು ವಿಕರಣ"]; taking that as its cause the root is doubled; *snasor allopaḥ* — the elision of the reduplicative syllable and the change of the root's *ā* to *e* (*ghvasor eddhāv abhyāsalopaś ca*, Pā. 6-4-119); since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta* accent. *suhavā* — *śobhanaṃ havaḥ yasyāḥ sā suhavā*; the root *hvaiñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *bhāve 'nupasargasya* (Pā. 3-3-75) gives the suffix *ap* in the sense of the action… *(page ends; continues on p. 128)*

…by *saṃprasāraṇa* and *pūrvarūpa* of the root, taking which as its cause *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* gives the guṇa of the root's *u*, and the *av*-substitution; as the *ap*-suffix has the marker *p* it is unaccented, so the root accent remains; in the compound the accent of the final member's own nature arises.

*maghavatsu* — *magham asya asti iti maghavān*; the suffix *matup* [rendered by the print as *matuṣ*] comes after a stem ending in *a*; *mādupadhāyāś ca* gives *va* for the *m* of *matup*; being *pit* it is unaccented; locative plural.

*rāyaḥ* — the word *rai*; its nominative plural with *jas* following; *echo 'yavāyāvaḥ* gives *āy* [as printed "ಏಚೋಽಯವಾಯಾವಃ"]. *syuḥ* — root *as bhuvi*; *liṅ* third person plural, the suffix *jhi*; for it the substitute *us*; the augment *yāsuṭ*; since it has the marker *p* [*pit*? as read], *śnasor allopaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-111) elides the *a* of the root; since it follows a non-verb word, the *nighāta* accent. ‖ 13 ‖

## Sūkta 124 — *uṣā ucchantī* (begins at the foot of printed p. 128)

**ನೂರ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra ippattanālkaneya sūktavu** (the one hundred and twenty-fourth Sūkta).

**॥ भूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, from the Sāyaṇa text):**

> उषा उच्छन्तीति त्रयोदशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसः कक्षीवत आर्षं त्रैष्टुभमुषस्यम् । उषा उच्छन्तीत्यनुक्रान्तम् । विनियोगस्तु पूर्वसूक्त एवोक्तः ॥

> *uṣā ucchantīti trayodaśarcaṃ caturthaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasaḥ kakṣīvata ārṣaṃ traiṣṭubhamuṣasyam | uṣā ucchantītyanukrāntam | viniyogastu pūrvasūkta evoktaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; the last word, "evoktaḥ", is given as read.)* "The fourth sūkta, of thirteen ṛks, beginning *uṣā ucchantī*, of Kakṣīvat Dairghatamasa, in the Triṣṭubh metre, addressed to Uṣas. It is listed in the Anukramaṇī as *uṣā ucchantī*; its application (*viniyoga*) has been stated in the preceding sūkta itself."

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This Sūkta, beginning *uṣā ucchantī*, is the fourth Sūkta in the eighteenth Anuvāka. It has thirteen ṛks. The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Kakṣīvān Dairghatamasa; the deity is Uṣas; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated as *uṣā ucchantī*; its *viniyoga* has been stated before.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उषा उच्छन्ती समिधाने अग्ना उद्यन्त्सूर्य उर्विया ज्योतिरश्रेत् ।
> देवो नो अत्र सविता न्वर्थं प्रासावीद्द्विपत्प्र चतुष्पदित्यै ॥ १ ॥

> *uṣā ucchantī samidhāne agnā udyantsūrya urviyā jyotiraśret |*
> *devo no atra savitā nvarthaṃ prāsāvīddvipatpra catuṣpadityai ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उषाः । उच्छन्ती । सम्ऽइधाने । अग्नौ । उत्ऽयन् । सूर्यः । उर्विया । ज्योतिः । अश्रेत् ।
> देवः । नः । अत्र । सविता । नु । अर्थम् । प्र । असावीत् । द्विऽपत् । प्र । चतुःऽपत् । इत्यै ॥ १ ॥

> *uṣāḥ | ucchantī | sam 'idhāne | agnau | ut 'yan | sūryaḥ | urviyā | jyotiḥ | aśret |*
> *devaḥ | naḥ | atra | savitā | nu | artham | pra | asāvīt | dvi 'pat | pra | catuḥ 'pat | ityai ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> एषोषाः समिधानेऽग्नौ । अग्निषु सामान्यैकवचनम् । अग्निषु समिध्यमानेषु सत्सु । कर्मार्थे कर्तृप्रयोगः [?] । उषःकाले ह्याहवनीयादयः प्रज्वाल्यन्ते । उच्छन्ती तमो विवासयन्ती उर्विया उरु बहुलं ज्योतिः प्रकाशमश्रेत् । सेवते । प्रकाशते प्रकाशयति वा सर्वम् । किमिव उद्यन्सूर्यः । उपमाप्रधाननिर्देशः ॥

> *eṣoṣāḥ samidhāne 'gnau | agniṣu sāmānyaikavacanam | agniṣu samidhyamāneṣu satsu | karmārthe kartṛprayogaḥ [?] | uṣaḥkāle hyāhavanīyādayaḥ prajvālyante | ucchantī tamo vivāsayantī urviyā uru bahulaṃ jyotiḥ prakāśamaśret | sevate | prakāśate prakāśayati vā sarvam | kimiva udyansūryaḥ | upamāpradhānanirdeśaḥ ‖*

> उदितः सूर्य इव सूर्यो यथा प्रकाशयति तथेत्यर्थः । अत्र त्वदुदयानन्तरमस्मिन्कर्मणि वा सविता देवः सर्वस्य प्रेरकः सूर्यो नोऽस्मदर्थं नु क्षिप्रमर्थमपेक्षितम् । अर्थशब्दोऽत्र विशेषणवाची नपुंसकलिङ्गः । अयन्नर्थानि कृण्वन्नांसीत्यादौ (ऋ. ७-६३-४ [?]) तथादृष्टत्वात् ॥ अरणीयं [?] द्विपत् पादद्वयोपेतं मनुष्यादिरूपं धनं प्रासावीत् । अनुजानातु ददात्वित्यर्थः । तथा चतुष्पत् पादचतुष्टयोपेतं गवादिरूपं धनं प्रासावीत् । किमर्थम् । इत्यै । द्विपदां चतुष्पदां च गमनाय । यद्वा । न इत्यै इति संबन्धः । अस्मद्गमनागमनादिव्यापाराये[त्यर्थः] ॥

> *uditaḥ sūrya iva sūryo yathā prakāśayati tathetyarthaḥ | atra tvadudayānantaramasminkarmaṇi vā savitā devaḥ sarvasya prerakaḥ sūryo no 'smadarthaṃ nu kṣipramarthamapekṣitam | arthaśabdo 'tra viśeṣaṇavācī napuṃsakaliṅgaḥ | ayannarthāni kṛṇvannāṃsītyādau (ṛ. 7-63-4 [?]) tathādṛṣṭatvāt ‖ araṇīyaṃ [?] dvipat pādadvayopetaṃ manuṣyādirūpaṃ dhanaṃ prāsāvīt | anujānātu dadātvityarthaḥ | tathā catuṣpat pādacatuṣṭayopetaṃ gavādirūpaṃ dhanaṃ prāsāvīt | kimartham | ityai | dvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ ca gamanāya | yadvā | na ityai iti saṃbandhaḥ | asmadgamanāgamanādivyāpārāye[tyarthaḥ] ‖*

*(Read from the image; the first half of the passage is doubtful in the print — "atra tvad-udayānantaram asminkarmaṇi vā" and "araṇīyam [?]" are my readings; the OCR garbles them. The Ṛg reference "7-63-4" is read from the image "೭-೬೩-೪" (the OCR agrees on the shape).)* Sense: "This Uṣas, when the fires (the Āhavanīya and the others) are being kindled — for the Āhavanīya and the other fires are kindled at the time of Uṣas — *ucchantī*, driving away the darkness, *urviyā* — abundantly — has resorted to (*aśret*, 'serves', 'shines' or 'illumines') the light (*jyotiḥ*, brightness), like the rising Sun (*udyan sūryaḥ*), that is, as the Sun illuminates when risen. Here, after your rising, the god Savitṛ, the impeller of all, the Sun, for us — *nu*, quickly — *artham* (the desired): the word *artha* here, as an epithet, is a neuter noun, as seen in such places as *ayann arthāni kṛṇvann ajāsīt* … Let him bestow (*prāsāvīt*, let him permit, let him give) wealth in the form of men and the like, 'two-footed' (*dvipat*, possessed of two feet); and likewise wealth in the form of cattle and the like, 'four-footed' (*catuṣpat*). For what? *Ityai* — for the going of the two-footed and the four-footed. Or else, the connection is: *na ityai* — for our activity of going and coming and the like."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Agnau* — when the fire (the fires); *samidhāne* — are kindled; *uṣāḥ* — the goddess Uṣas; *udyan sūryaḥ* — like the rising Sun; *ucchantī* — driving away (the darkness); *urviyā* — abundantly; *jyotiḥ* — light; *aśret* — attains (she illumines everything); *atra* — after this (in this rite); *savitā devaḥ* — the god Savitṛ (the impeller of all); *naḥ* — for us; *nu* — quickly; *artham* — the desired; *dvipat* — beings with two feet (wealth in the form of men and the like); *ityai* — for (our) going and coming; *(pra asāvīt)* — may he grant; *catuṣpat* — beings with four feet (wealth in the form of cattle and the like); *(pra asāvīt)* — may he grant.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** While the Āhavanīya and other fires are kindled, the goddess Uṣas, driving away the darkness with her (own) boundless brilliance, like the Sun, shines; after her rising, may the god Savitṛ, the Sun, for the sake of our going and coming and other works, quickly favour us with two-footed and four-footed beings.

**Printed English (as printed):** *When the (sacred) fire is kindled, Ushas sheds abundant light, dispersing (the darkness) like the rising sun; may the divine Savitri bestow upon us for our use, wealth of both bipeds and quadrupeds.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 1.**

***ucchantī*** — For this word one may give, by way of the root *uchī* ("driving away"), the meaning "destroying", or, in another way, "shining with brilliance". The derivation of the word *uṣāḥ* is also from *ucchati*: *uṣāḥ kasmād ucchatīti satyā rātrer aparaḥ kālaḥ*…

### Printed p. 131  (PDF 152)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7.)*

— with this sentence the author of the Nirukta states this etymology (Ni. 2-18, as printed "೨-೧೮"; the OCR agrees). But by the sentence *uṣā vaṣṭeḥ kāntikarmaṇa ucchater itarā mādhyamikā* (Ni. 12-7, as read by the OCR; the print "೧೨-೭") the word *ucchati* may be derived either from the root *vaś kāntau* or from the root *uchī vivāse*. *Ucchantī uṣāḥ* means "Uṣas who, driving away the darkness, appears outside", or "Uṣas who shines".

***nu*** — *nu ity eṣo 'nekakarmā | idaṃ nu kariṣyatīti hetvapadeśe | kathaṃ nu kariṣyatīty anupraśne* (Ni. 1-4, as printed "೧-೪"). The indeclinable *nu* has many meanings. When one says *idaṃ nu kariṣyati* the *nu* means "therefore", "because of this" (the sense of a reason); when one says *kathaṃ nu kariṣyati* the *nu* is an inquiry, "how?". Likewise *athāpy upamārthe bhavati*: even in indicating a comparison the word *nu* is used. For example —

> अक्षो न चक्र्योः शूर बृहन्ते महना रिरिचे रोदस्योः ।
> वृक्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वया व्यूतयो रुरुहुरिन्द्र पूर्वीः ॥

> *akṣo na cakryoḥ śūra bṛhante mahanā ririce rodasyoḥ |*
> *vṛkṣasya nu te puruhūta vayā vyūtayo ruruhurindra pūrvīḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-24-? — numerals "೬-೨೪-೯" as I read the print; doubtful [?].) — citing this ṛk, the author of the Nirukta (1-4) gives *vṛkṣasyeva te puruhūta śākhāḥ* — "like a tree, or like the branches of a tree" — for the word *nu*, with the sense of comparison. Likewise it also has the sense "quickly", "in a hurry".

> नू मर्तो दयते सनिष्यन्यो विष्णव उरुगायाय दाशत् ।
> प्र यः सत्राचा मनसा यजात एतावन्तं नर्यमाविवासात् ॥

> *nū marto dayate saniṣyanyo viṣṇava urugāyāya dāśat |*
> *pra yaḥ satrācā manasā yajāta etāvantaṃ naryamāvivāsāt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-100-1, as I read the print "೭-೧೦೦-೧"; the OCR "2-100-1" is letter-shaped.) — in such ṛks *nu* has the sense "quickly" (*kṣipram*).

> नू इन्द्र शूर स्तवमान ऊती ब्रह्मजूतस्तन्वा वावृधस्व ।
> उप नो वाजान्मिमीह्युप स्त्रीन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

> *nū indra śūra stavamāna ūtī brahmajūtastanvā vāvṛdhasva |*
> *upa no vājānmimīhyupa strīnyūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-98-11 [?], as I read the print.) *(Read letter by letter; "upa stīn / strīn" — the print shows "ಉಪ ಸ್ತ್ರೀನ್ಯೂಯಂ", given as "upa strīn yūyam" without completing it from memory.)* In these and other places *adya*, that is, "now", "at once" is the meaning; likewise, as the author of the Nirukta says, *nu ity eṣo 'nekakarmā* (Ni. 1-4) — "this *nu* has many meanings" — in the present ṛk it means "quickly, soon".

***ityai*** — this word means "going": "for going and coming", that is, for moving about. Here one connection is *dvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ ca gamanāya* — "for the going of the two-footed and the four-footed"…
