### Printed p. 250  (PDF 271)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 127".)*

> अभ्यासे भूयांसमर्थं मन्यन्ते यथाहो दर्शनीयाहो दर्शनीयेति । तत्परुच्छेपस्य शीलम् ॥

> *abhyāse bhūyāṃsamarthaṃ manyante yathāho darśanīyāho darśanīyeti | tatparucchepasya śīlam ‖*

(Ni. 10-43 [?], as printed "೧೦-೪೩".) That is, in the ṛks seen by this ṛṣi *abhyāsa*, that is, repetition, is seen specially. Ordinarily in ṛks of metres such as Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh and Jagatī there are only two parts, a first half and a second half. But in ṛks seen by Paruccheṣa, of Atyaṣṭi and other metres, there are three halves. At the end of the first and third of these three halves one or two words recur like a refrain (*pallavi*). For example —

> अग्निं होतारं मन्ये दास्वन्तं वसुं सूनुं सहसो जातवेदसं विप्रं न जातवेदसम् ।

> *agniṃ hotāraṃ manye dāsvantaṃ vasuṃ sūnuṃ sahaso jātavedasaṃ vipraṃ na jātavedasam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-127-1, the first ṛk of this very Sūkta, as printed; the OCR agrees.) In this ṛk the word *jātavedasam* is repeated; between this repetition stand the words *vipraṃ na*. This repeating word is always at the end of a sentence.

> निष्षहमाणो यमते नायते धन्वासहा नायते ।

> *niṣṣahamāṇo yamate nāyate dhanvāsahā nāyate |*

*(Read letter by letter; the sense is "he who overpowers restrains, does not move away; he who surpasses in the bow does not move away" — I give no gloss for the unclear words.)* In this ṛk the words *na āyate* are repeated, and between them stands the word *dhanvāsahā*. Yāska states this subject of repetition: *abhyāse bhūyāṃsam arthaṃ manyante yathāho darśanīyāho darśanīyeti*, and explains its meaning. The commentator on this sentence of the Nirukta (Durga) —

> अभ्यासे भूयांसमर्थं मन्यन्ते । शब्दाभ्यासे यत्रान्यो विशेषो नास्ति शिष्टं विशेषमाचार्या मन्त्रार्थचिन्तका मन्यन्ते — यदुतार्थभूयस्त्वमिति । न ह्येकस्मात्स एव शब्दः पुनरभ्यस्यते । लोकेऽपि चैतद्दृष्टम् — शब्दाभ्यासेऽर्थभूयस्त्वमिति । यथा — अहो दर्शनीयः ! अहो दर्शनीयः ! इति । गुणातिशये हि स्त्रियाः शब्दाभ्यासः । तस्मान्मन्त्रेष्वपि तद्वदेवेति न्यायम् ॥

> *abhyāse bhūyāṃsamarthaṃ manyante | śabdābhyāse yatrānyo viśeṣo nāsti śiṣṭaṃ viśeṣamācāryā mantrārthacintakā manyante — yadutārthabhūyastvamiti | na hyekasmātsa eva śabdaḥ punarabhyasyate | loke 'pi caitaddṛṣṭam — śabdābhyāse 'rthabhūyastvamiti | yathā — aho darśanīyaḥ ! aho darśanīyaḥ ! iti | guṇātiśaye hi striyāḥ śabdābhyāsaḥ | tasmānmantreṣvapi tadvadeveti nyāyam ‖*

*(Read letter by letter from the print; "mantrārthacintakāḥ" and "stṛiyāḥ" [?] are doubtful.)* That is, when a word is uttered twice in a sentence, in the case where the word has no two different senses, the repetition of the word indicates excess of meaning; that is, it is used in order to give prominence to the matter said, or to say it so that it is well fixed in the mind. For example, when describing the beauty of women, the repeated "*aho darśanīyā, aho darśanīyā*" — "what a lovely one! what a lovely one!" —

### Printed p. 251  (PDF 272)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12.)*

— there is a custom in the world of speaking so, to make clear the idea of surpassing beauty; as there, so it must be thought here too, he has said. But Sāyaṇa has in general explained the repeated words in these ṛks by giving them different meanings.

This kind of repetition has another purpose. Many ṛks of the Ṛgveda have been composed so as to be fit for singing. It is well known to all in the world that when a composition set to a *rāga* and the like is sung, the *pallavi* and the *anupallavi* are sung again and again. Therefore these ṛks, and many other ṛks, must have been composed with the purpose of being sung so as to be pleasing to hear. For this very reason, it is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa that these Pārucchepa mantras are laid down for the recitation of the *śastra*; and for this very reason the greater part of the Sāmaveda consists of Ṛgveda ṛks.

When the Vedic mantras are understood with their meaning and recited or sung with devotion and faith, with the accents, there arises, for those who recite and for the audience who hear such Vedic chanting, an indescribable joy; this has come into the experience of many. Some modern scholars, such as Westerners, look at the Vedic mantras only from the point of view of meaning, and therefore have no chance of understanding fully the musical nature of the Vedic mantras; so they do not take pains for it. Some say that, though these ṛks are metrical, there are many dropped syllables (*lopa*) and violations of grammar in them, and that they are not suited to mature poetry. But their opinion is not tenable. For at that time there was no written language; everything had to be learnt by heart; therefore it is natural that attention should be given to pronunciation more than to meaning. And, there being no written language and no grammar, it is natural that words and the style of language current at that time were used. It must not be forgotten that grammatical treatises such as Pāṇini's were composed on the basis of Vedic words. Grammar comes out of language, not language out of grammar; language is the root; grammar is made to follow it. Therefore, it is not appropriate to apply grammatical rules strictly to the forms of words and so on that are seen in the Vedic mantras.

As was said before, many ṛks may have been composed from the point of view of singing. For that reason, in many contexts short syllables are used as long ones and long ones as short; this is seen here and there. For example, words such as *ādha*, *ghā*, *sma* and others are long in the Saṃhitā text. In the same way *ṛtavṛdhā* is pronounced as *ṛtāvṛdhā*.

### Printed p. 252  (PDF 273)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 127".)*

…and so on. In many contexts one or two syllables of words are dropped; for example, *tmanā* in place of *ātmanā*, and *bhāvyasya* in place of *bhāvayavyasya*. Such defects of dropping are not new in the modern languages either. For example, singers, when they sing compositions, sing *Kṛṣṇā mūruti* in place of *Kṛṣṇamūrti*, and *kīruti* for *kīrti*. Such drops are many. Since the Vedic mantras have come down handed on by pronunciation alone through tradition, such small drops (which are not drops at all) are natural.

There is no doubt that the sūktas seen by Paruccheṣa belong to very ancient mantras. Because the meaning of some words and sentences in these ṛks is very difficult and unclear, the meaning does not fit well in many contexts. A large part of these mantras has been included in the *śastra* mantras. Their explanation is in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows:

> देवासुरा वा एषु लोकेषु समयतन्त ते वै देवाः षष्ठेनैवाह्ना [?] लोकेभ्योऽसुरान्प्राणुदन्त तेषां यान्यन्तर्हस्तीनानि [?] वसून्यासंस्तान्यादाय समुद्रं प्रौहन् [?] ते वा एतेनैव छन्दसानुहायान्तर्हस्तीनानि [?] वसून्यादत्त तद्यदेतत्पदं पुनःपदं स एनान्कुत आसञ्जनाय [?] । आ द्विषतो वसु दत्ते निरेनमेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यो लोकेभ्यो नुदते य एवं वेद ॥

> *devāsurā vā eṣu lokeṣu samayatanta te vai devāḥ ṣaṣṭhenaivāhnā [?] lokebhyo 'surānprāṇudanta teṣāṃ yānyantarhastīnāni [?] vasūnyāsaṃstānyādāya samudraṃ prauhan [?] te vā etenaiva chandasānuhāyāntarhastīnāni [?] vasūnyādatta tadyadetatpadaṃ punaḥpadaṃ sa enānkuta āsañjanāya [?] | ā dviṣato vasu datte nirenamebhyaḥ sarvebhyo lokebhyo nudate ya evaṃ veda ‖*

(Ai. Br. 22-6, as printed "ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. ೨೨-೬".) *(Read letter by letter; this long passage is in small type and I have marked the words I could not make out reliably. The words *antarhastīnāni*, *prauhan* and *kuta āsañjanāya* are the doubtful ones.)* The gods and the Asuras once fought a great battle in this world. Then the gods, performing the rites on the sixth day (of the *dvādaśāha* sacrifice) and conquering the Asuras, drove them out of this world. Then the Asuras, being defeated, took the wealth — gold and the like — that had come into their hands, and went away from the battlefield and threw it into the sea. Afterwards the gods, pursuing the Asuras, recovered, by the power of reciting the ṛks seen by Paruccheṣa, the riches the Asuras had thrown into the sea. In this recovery, the repeated seventh *pāda* of the Paruccheṣa ṛks (the *pāda* like *sumṛḷīko na ā gahi* — "be gracious, come to us") helped them. In the world it is natural that people draw out with a hook (*hook* in the print, in Latin letters) a thing that has fallen into a depth, with a rod joined to it. In the same way, the repeated seventh *pāda* of ṛks seen by this ṛṣi has the intent that, drawing the wealth lying in the midst of the sea so as to make it return to the gods, one … Understanding this matter well, and reciting the mantra accordingly and performing the rite, a man conquers enemies and drives them out of this world, and himself gets their wealth.

### Printed p. 253  (PDF 274)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12.)*

The use (*viniyoga*) of the ṛks seen by Paruccheṣa and the explanation of their inner meaning is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa thus (Ai. Br. 22-5 [?]):

> पारुच्छेपीरुपदधाति पूर्वयोः सवनयोः पुरस्तात्प्रस्थितयाज्यानां रोहितं वै नामैतच्छन्दो यत्पारुच्छेपमेतेन वा इन्द्रः सप्त स्वर्गान्लोकानरोहत् । रोहति सप्त स्वर्गान्लोकान्य एवं वेद । तदाहुर्यत्पञ्चपदा एव पञ्चमस्याह्नो रूपं षट्पदाः षष्ठस्याथ कस्मात्सप्तपदाः पारुच्छेपीः षष्ठेऽहन्नुच्यन्त इति । षड्भिरेव पद्भिः षष्ठमहराप्नुवन्ति । अथ यदेतत्सप्तमं पदं तदेव सप्तमेन पदेनाभ्यारभ्य वसन्ति वाचमेव तत्सप्तरूपां संतन्वन्ति ॥

> *pārucchepīrupadadhāti pūrvayoḥ savanayoḥ purastātprasthitayājyānāṃ rohitaṃ vai nāmaitacchando yatpārucchepametena vā indraḥ sapta svargānlokānarohat | rohati sapta svargānlokānya evaṃ veda | tadāhuryatpañcapadā eva pañcamasyāhno rūpaṃ ṣaṭpadāḥ ṣaṣṭhasyātha kasmātsaptapadāḥ pārucchepīḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hannucyanta iti | ṣaḍbhireva padbhiḥ ṣaṣṭhamaharāpnuvanti | atha yadetatsaptamaṃ padaṃ tadeva saptamena padenābhyārabhya vasanti vācameva tatsaptarūpāṃ saṃtanvanti ‖*

*(Read letter by letter from the print and from the OCR, which is garbled here; the numbers and a few syllables are doubtful and I give the passage as read, marked as unverified.)* In the morning pressing and the midday pressing (*savana* means the act of pressing and extracting the Soma from the creeper) of the sixth day of the *dvādaśāha* or *daśarātra* sacrifice, the seven priests belonging to the *hotṛ* group recite the *prasthita-yājyā* mantras. That is, one must first recite the Pārucchepa ṛks one by one, and then recite the *prasthita-yājyā* mantras one by one. Which Pārucchepa mantras are to be recited in this context? —

The ṛks from *vṛṣaṃ indra vṛṣapāṇāsa indavaḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-139-6, as printed) up to the last ṛk of this [139th] sūkta (1-139-11), and from *pibā somam indra suvānam adribhiḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-2) up to the last ṛk of that sūkta (1-130-[?]) — these ṛks are to be recited one by one. The ṛks seen by Paruccheṣa are called "*rohita*" ("ascending"), because by reciting these ṛks Indra once mounted the seventh heaven. Here the "seven heavens" are the seven divisions of heaven, differing in excellence and inferiority; whoever recites these mantras thus and performs the sacrifice, he too ascends the seven heavens.

Here there is a special matter. It is the custom that on the fifth day of this sacrifice, at the times of pressing, ṛks of five *pādas* (Paṅkti metre) are recited; and on the sixth day, ṛks of six *pādas*. Yet why are the seven-*pāda* Pārucchepa ṛks recited on that day? — They say: on all six days one goes beyond the six heavens by the six *pādas* of the ṛk, and mounts the seventh heaven by the seventh *pāda*. Because the seventh *pāda* is a repetition, in the ṛk there are counted only six *pādas*; the seventh *pāda* is [also] praised, and by reciting it one obtains…

…the excellent seventh heaven: so it is said; this is the main idea.

What the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says on the use of the Paruccheṣa sūktas in the *śastra* mantras is explained here —

> द्यौर्हैव देवता षष्ठमहर्वहति त्रयस्त्रिंशस्तोमो रैवतं साम अतिच्छन्दा छन्दो यथादेवतमेतेन यथास्तोमं यथासाम यथाच्छन्दसं राध्नोति य एवं वेद ॥

> *dyaurhaiva devatā ṣaṣṭhamaharvahati trayastriṃśastomo raivataṃ sāma aticchandā chando yathādevatametena yathāstomaṃ yathāsāma yathācchandasaṃ rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ‖*

(Ai. Br. 22-? [?], as printed "ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. ೨೨-೭" (?), numerals small.) In the programme of the sixth day of the *daśarātra* sacrifice mentioned above, the details of the deity and others are thus: on the sixth day *dyauḥ* is the deity; one must praise with the *trayastriṃśa* stoma; one must sing with the Sāman named *Raivata*; one must recite ṛks of an *atichandas* metre (for the *śastra* mantras). These are the special rites of the sixth day.

We have explained the *trayastriṃśa* stoma before. Yet the description of this stoma in the Tāṇḍya Brāhmaṇa, as follows —

> एकादश हिंकरोति स तिसृभिः स सप्तभिः स एकया । एकादश हिंकरोति स एकया स तिसृभिः स सप्तभिः । एकादश हिंकरोति स सप्तभिः स एकया स तिसृभिः ॥

> *ekādaśa hiṃkaroti sa tisṛbhiḥ sa saptabhiḥ sa ekayā | ekādaśa hiṃkaroti sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ sa saptabhiḥ | ekādaśa hiṃkaroti sa saptabhiḥ sa ekayā sa tisṛbhiḥ ‖*

*(Read letter by letter from the print; the second and third cycles are as printed and I give them without correcting.)* [that is, eleven *hiṅkāras*, of three, seven and one; and so on] — the *tṛca* (three ṛks) to be recited: in the first round the first ṛk three times and the second ṛk seven times (by which eleven ṛks [verses] are recited, as the print has "೧೧" [?]); in the second round the first ṛk once, the second ṛk three times, the third ṛk seven times (in all 11 ṛks); in the third round the first ṛk seven times, the second once, the third three times (in all 11 ṛks). In this way the number of ṛks recited in three rounds comes to 33, [and] for this reason this stoma is called *trayastriṃśa*. The Sāman produced from the ṛk *revatīr naḥ sadhamāde* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-30-13, as printed) is called *Raivata*. Metres with more syllables than Gāyatrī are called *Atichandas*. On this sixth day the deities are Vāk, Go and Dyaus. One must praise with the *trayastriṃśa* stoma; one must sing with the Sāman called Raivata; one must recite ṛks of the *atichandas* metres (as *śastra* mantras). These are the special rites of this sixth day.

The *ājya-śastra* mantra to be recited on the sixth day must be the ṛks of the sūkta *ayaṃ jāyata manuṣo dharīmaṇi* [Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-128], seen by Paruccheṣa. All these are special rites of the sixth day.

Among the metres Utkṛti, Abhikṛti, Saṃkṛti, Vikṛti, Ākṛti, Prakṛti, Kṛti, Atikṛti, [Dhṛti, Atidhṛti, Aṣṭi, Atyaṣṭi], beginning at one hundred and four syllables and dropping four each time, each metre comes about; thus Atidhṛti would have the stated count. All this is stated in the metre-treatise in the sūtras beginning *catuḥśataṃ utkṛtiḥ* (Piṅgala 4-1 [?]). And so the Anukramaṇī says: 'Agni — eleven; Paruccheṣa Daivodāsi; Āgneya; Pārucchepa; all Atyaṣṭi; in it the first Atidhṛti; the sixth …'. The special application of the sūkta is by *liṅga*: in the sixth day of the Daśarātra, in the morning pressing, one should sacrifice with other ṛks first before the *prasthita-yājyās*, together with the *prākṛta* ones. Of these, the first, addressed to Agni, is this one; it is laid down in the section 'of the sixth day, in the morning pressing' [Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra]: '*agniṃ hotāraṃ manye dāsvantaṃ dadharṣajña ha me januṣaṃ pūrvo aṅgirāḥ*' (Āś. 8-1 [?])."

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** With this Sūkta the nineteenth Anuvāka of the first Maṇḍala begins. In this Anuvāka there are seven Sūktas. Of these seven Sūktas, the Sūkta beginning *agniṃ hotāram* is the first; it has eleven ṛks. The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Paruccheṣa, the son of Divodāsa; the deity is Agni; the metre is Atyaṣṭi. The ṛk *sa hi śardhaḥ* is of the metre Atidhṛti, of 76 syllables. In the metres Utkṛti, Abhikṛti, Saṃkṛti, Vikṛti, Ākṛti, Prakṛti, Kṛti, Atidhṛti [as printed: "ಅತಿಧೃತಿ"], Dhṛti, Atyaṣṭi, Aṣṭi, the syllable-count of each ṛk goes down by four syllables from 104, and the last, the Aṣṭi, has 64 syllables. That is, from Utkṛti to Aṣṭi the counts are 104, 100, 96, 92, 88, 84, 80, 76, 72, 68, 64 (as printed: "೧೦೪, ೧೦೦, ೯೬, ೯೨, ೮೮, ೮೪, ೮೦, ೭೬, ೭೨, ೬೮, ೬೪" — I give the series as consistent with the printed pattern; the printed digits are small). Therefore the metres Atyaṣṭi and Atidhṛti are of 68 and 76 syllables. All this has been established in the metre-treatise by the sūtras beginning *catuḥśatam utkṛtiḥ* (Piṅ. 4-1 [?]). In the Anukramaṇī: *agnim ekādaśa paruccheṣo daivodāsir āgneyaṃ tu pārucchepaṃ sarvam atyaṣṭaṃ tatrātidhṛtiḥ ṣaṣṭhīti*. The special application of the sūkta is *liṅga*-based: on the sixth day of the Daśarātra sacrifice, in the morning pressing, in the rite of the *prasthita-yājyā* mantras, it is the custom to recite a ṛk before each *yājyā* mantra; of these the first, *agniṃ hotāram*, is to be recited by the Agni-priest. This matter is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the section *ṣaṣṭhasya prātaḥsavane*, in the sūtra *agniṃ hotāraṃ manye dāsvantaṃ dadharṣajña ha me januṣaṃ pūrvo aṅgirāḥ* (Āś. 8-1).

### Printed p. 259  (PDF 280)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 13.)*

"[I think of] Agni — the leader of all the divine armies, or, in sacrifices, the one led first — the *hotṛ*, who calls the gods to this sacrifice; or else, the *hotṛ*, the performer of the oblation: '*juhoter hotety aurṇavābhaḥ*', says Yāska (Ni. 7-15). By the text 'he chose Agni today as *hotṛ*' [TB, as read], and *agnim agna āvaha* ('Agni, bring [the gods]'), the calling of the gods by Agni is well known. *Agniṃ hotāraṃ manye* — thus, *manye* ('I think') is connected with each epithet. Or else, since the performance of the sacrifice alone is desired, this alone is the predicate-epithet; the other epithets that follow are for praise. *Dāsvantam* — most generous; *vasum* — the cause of everyone's dwelling; *sahasaḥ sūnum* — the son of strength: at the time of the kindling by friction he is born, being churned with force; hence 'son' is figuratively said. *Jātavedasam* — the knower of what is born, one whose knowledge or strength is born; the word *jātavedas* has been explained in many ways by Yāska (Ni. 7-19). An illustration of *jātavedas*-ness: *vipraṃ na jātavedasam* — like a Brahmin, learned, intelligent, whom people hold in high esteem; so I too hold you: I praise [you]. The god endowed with the qualities stated — *svadhvaraḥ*, having a good sacrifice, well conducting the sacrifice — with *ūrdhvayā* — lofty, excellent — *devāc'yā*, that goes to the gods or worships the gods, *kṛpā* — with compassion, characterised by capacity: 'to the gods, one's own compassion' says Yāska (Ni. 6-8 [?]); endowed with the intent of carrying the oblation to them, *ājuhvānasya* — of the ghee being offered all round, *sarpiṣaḥ* — flowing, *ghṛtasya* — of the ghee that is melted and shining, *vibhrāṣṭim anu* — following specially its glow, he himself *vaṣṭi* — desires, accepts, the ghee with his flame."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Yaḥ devaḥ* — which god Agni; *svadhvaraḥ* — endowed with a sacrifice beautified by him (one who conducts the sacrifice well); *ūrdhvayā* — excellent; *devāc'yā* — worshipping the gods; *kṛpā* — with compassion (being endowed with the power of carrying the oblation); *ājuhvānasya* — of (the sacrificer) who is invoking; *sarpiṣaḥ* — liquid; *ghṛtasya* — of the ghee; *vibhrāṣṭim anu* — following the flame; *śociṣā* — with (his own) flame; *vaṣṭi* — accepts; *(taṃ* — that); *agnim* — Agni (the leader of all the gods); *hotāram* — the one who calls the gods to our sacrifice (and the priest who performs the oblation); *dāsvantam* — the generous; *vasum* — the cause of dwelling (for all); *sahasaḥ sūnum* — the son of strength (necessarily produced in the kindling); *jātavedasam* — the intelligent; *vipraṃ na* — like a Brahmin; *jātavedasam* — one who knows everything that has been born; *manye* — I know (I praise).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Agni, who adorns (our) sacrifice, with excellent power that worships the gods (in the form of carrying the oblations), accepts, with his flames, the liquefied ghee offered by the sacrificer who invokes [the gods]; I know (I praise) such an Agni as the *hotṛ* who calls the gods to our sacrifice, as generous, as the cause of dwelling for all, and as omniscient like a wise Brahmin.

### Printed p. 260  (PDF 281)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 127".)*

**Printed English (as printed):** *I venerate Agni, the invoker (of the gods), the munificent, the giver of dwellings, the son of strength : he who knows all that exists, like a sage who is endowed with knowledge : who, the divine regenerator of sacrifices, through his lofty and reverential devotion, covets for the gods the blaze of the liquefied butter which is offered in oblation with his flames.* *(Printed as such; "regenerator" and "sacrfices"/"sacrifices" are as the print has them.)*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 1.**

***agniṃ*** — *sarvāsāṃ devasenānām agraṇyaṃ yajñeṣv agraṃ nīyamānaṃ vā*: The word *agni* is used in two senses. In the first sense, "one who is the foremost of the divine armies, the army of the gods"; in the second, "the one who is led first, in sacrifices, before all, being invoked". On this Yāska says —

> अग्निः पृथिवीस्थानस्तं प्रथमं व्याख्यास्यामः । अग्रणीर्भवति । अग्रं यज्ञेषु प्रणीयते । अङ्गं नयति सन्नममानः ॥

> *agniḥ pṛthivīsthānastaṃ prathamaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | agraṇīrbhavati | agraṃ yajñeṣu praṇīyate | aṅgaṃ nayati sannamamānaḥ ‖*

(Ni. 7-14 [?], as printed "೭-೧೪".) Agni has three places. Agni's work is spread through the three places — atmosphere, heaven and earth. Among these, since he pervades most the place of the earth, beginning with the terrestrial Agni he first explains, and gives three derivations of the form of the word *agni*. For the first, *agraṇīr bhavati*, Durgācārya says: *sarveṣv artheṣu asāv ātmānam agraṃ nayati, sarvatra tathopakaroti yathā agraṃ sampadyate* [?] — "in all matters he leads himself in front; he helps everywhere in such a way that the foremost place is attained", [or:] he is the chief (principal) one in Vedic rites and in worldly acts. Therefore *agraṇīḥ*, or — since it is said *agnir vai devānāṃ senānīḥ*, "Agni is the general of the gods' army" — because Agni himself, going first, is first for leading the gods to the sacrifices and so on, he is *agraṇīḥ*; and because he makes eminence for those who serve him he is also *agraṇīḥ*: thus the meaning is explained by the derivation *agraṃ nayati iti agraṇīḥ*.

Second: among the duties that must necessarily be done first in sacrifices, since no rite is done before the carrying forward (*praṇayana*) of Agni, [it is said] *yajñeṣu agraṃ praṇīyate* ("in sacrifices he is first led forward").

### Printed p. 261  (PDF 282)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 13.)*

*(Special topics, Ṛk 1, continued — **agniṃ**:)* The second explanation [is that he is] the one who, among sacrifices, is made ready first; *agraṃ praṇayanāt* — since he is first made ready (or: brought forward) and carried: so the word *agni* is appropriately [explained as] "one who is called by the word *agni*".

The third derivation of the word *agni* is *aṅgaṃ nayati sannamamānaḥ* [as printed; read in the Nirukta as *aṅgaṃ nayati sannamamānaḥ*]. This god, in all rites, worldly or Vedic, is himself the chief; he makes everything else (that is inferior to himself) subordinate to himself; or, when he takes up a blade of grass or a piece of firewood, he makes it subordinate to himself and keeps it so; therefore he is called *agni*.

*Agraṃ nayatīty agniḥ, agraṃ nīyata ity agniḥ, aṅgaṃ nayatīty agniḥ* — thus Yāska has described the derivation of the word *agni* in three ways. The teacher Sthaulāṣṭhīvi [as printed "ಸ್ಥೌಲಾಷ್ಠೀವಿ"; the OCR "राज्यपि"] describes the nature of Agni as "one who makes whatever he receives ugly (burns it black)"; and the teacher Śākapūṇi —

> त्रिभ्य आख्यातेभ्यो जायते । इताद्अक्ताद्दग्धाद्वा नीतात् । स खल्वेतेरकारमादत्ते गकारमनक्तेर्वा दहतेर्वा नीः परः ॥

> *tribhya ākhyātebhyo jāyate | itādaktāddagdhādvā nītāt | sa khalveterakāramādatte gakāramanaktervā dahatervā nīḥ paraḥ ‖*

(Ni. 7-14 [?], as printed "೭-೧೪"; the OCR reads "२-१४".) *(Read letter by letter; "itād aktād dagdhād vā nītāt" and the second half are small and doubtful.)* — gives the derivation of the word *agni*: [it is formed] from three verbs — from *i* ("goes"), from *añj* ("anoints") or *dah* ("burns"), and from *nī* ("leads"); he takes the *a* from *eti* (he goes), the *g* from *anakti* or *dahati*, and *nī* after it. Durgācārya describes Agni's nature by his actions: *eti ca nayati ca havīṃṣi dahati ca* — or *eti*, *vyanakti*: he comes (*eti*), he carries oblations (*nayati*), he burns (*dahati*), he transforms (*vyanakti*). Sāyaṇa, explaining the word *agni* as one who is in front of the divine army, or one who is chief in the sacrifices, gives only two meanings.

***hotāram*** — *asmadyāgaṃ prati devānām āhvātāraṃ yadvā homaniṣpādakaṃ hotāram*: "the one who calls the gods to our sacrifice, or the *hotṛ* who performs the oblation (and recites the mantra)": thus he explains two senses. The derivation of the word *hotṛ* is from the root *hu dānādanayoḥ*. The *śruti* "*agnim adya hotāram avṛṇīta*" (Tai. Brā. 2-6-15-1) shows that Agni is to be chosen as the *hotṛ* in the sacrifice; and the *śruti* "*agnim agna āvaha*" (Tai. Brā. 3-5-[?]) shows that one should first invoke Agni to call the gods. Hence both senses are possible. Therefore here too [Sāyaṇa] has said *agniṃ hotāraṃ manye*, and explained *hotāram* as the predicate-epithet of the word *agni*, the second-case words as the epithets of the word *agni*.

### Printed p. 262  (PDF 283)

— the one sense. *Yadvā yāganiṣpatter evāpekṣitatvād etad eva vidheyaviśeṣaṇam, itarāṇi tu vakṣyamāṇaviśeṣaṇāni stutiparāṇi*: since the sacrifice must necessarily be completed, the word *hotāram* is the predicate-epithet and the other epithets are for praising Agni: this is the second explanation. By this the meaning arises that Agni himself is meant by the word *hotṛ*. Yāska, in the Nirukta, citing

> अग्निमीळे पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवमृत्विजम् । होतारं रत्नधातमम् ॥

> *agnimīḷe purohitaṃ yajñasya devamṛtvijam | hotāraṃ ratnadhātamam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-1, as printed.) says *hotāraṃ hvātāraṃ juhoter hotā ity aurṇavābhaḥ* (Ni. 7-15): the view of Aurṇavābha, that *hotā* derived from the root *hu* is "one who calls the gods to the sacrifice".

***dāsvantam*** — *atiśayena dānavantam*: "the one who gives to the sacrificers in great quantity wealth and the like".

***vasum*** — *sarveṣāṃ nivāsahetum*: "the cause of dwelling at ease for all". The word *vasu* is recorded among the names of rays (Ni. 1-[?]5, as printed "೨-೧೫" [?]) and among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). And in

> सुगुरसत्सुहिरण्यः स्वश्वो बृहदस्मे वय इन्द्रो दधाति ।
> यस्त्वायन्तं वसुना प्रातरित्वो मुक्षीजयेव पदिमुत्सिनाति ॥

> *sugurasatsuhiraṇyaḥ svaśvo bṛhadasme vaya indro dadhāti |*
> *yastvāyantaṃ vasunā prātaritvo mukṣījayeva padimutsināti ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-125-2, as printed.) *vasunā* is explained as *annena*, so the meaning "food" too arises.

> देवी जोष्ट्री वसुधिती ययोरन्या ... [?] द्वेषांसि युयवदन्याव [?] ... ।
> वार्याणि यजमानाय सुन्वते वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज ॥

> *devī joṣṭrī vasudhitī yayoranyā ... [?] dveṣāṃsi yuyavadanyāva [?] ... |*
> *vāryāṇi yajamānāya sunvate vasuvane vasudheyasya vītāṃ yaja ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?], as printed "೨-೫-೧"? — doubtful; the middle of the first line I cannot read.) Here the word *vasu* is explained with the sense "wealth".

> जम्या अत्र वसवो रन्त देवा उरावन्तरिक्षे मर्जयन्त शुभ्राः ।
> अर्वाक्पथ उरुज्रयः कृणुध्वं श्रोता दूतस्य जग्मुषो नो अस्य ॥

> *jamyā atra vasavo ranta devā urāvantarikṣe marjayanta śubhrāḥ |*
> *arvākpatha urujrayaḥ kṛṇudhvaṃ śrotā dūtasya jagmuṣo no asya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-62-5 [?], as printed "೬-೬೨-೬"? — numerals small.) *(Read letter by letter; *jamyā* / *jmayā* — the first word is doubtful in the print.)* Here the word *vasavaḥ* is explained as "gods". But Sāyaṇa explains the word *vasu* as "cause of dwelling".

***sahasaḥ sūnum*** — *balasya putram*: "the son of strength": at the sacrifice, men churn in the *araṇi* with strength and thereby produce Agni; since Agni is born by strength, the figurative usage "son of strength" is here.

The word *sahas* is recorded among the one hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-[?]4, as printed "೨-೩೪" [?]) and among the twenty-eight names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [?]).

> एता विश्वा सवना तूतुमा कृषे स्वयं सूनो सहसो यानि दधिषे ।
> वराय ते पात्रं धर्मणे तना यज्ञो मन्त्रो ब्रह्मोद्यतं वचः ॥

> *etā viśvā savanā tūtumā kṛṣe svayaṃ sūno sahaso yāni dadhiṣe |*
> *varāya te pātraṃ dharmaṇe tanā yajño mantro brahmodyataṃ vacaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-6 [?], as printed "೧೦-೮೦-೬"? — numerals small.) *(Read letter by letter; the second half is as printed and I do not claim it.)* In this ṛk, *sahasaḥ sūno* "O son of strength" is said to be addressed to Agni, and Durgācārya has described [it as] "some say (*sutam*) his son".

***jātavedasam*** — *jātānāṃ veditāraṃ jātaprajñaṃ jātabalaṃ vā*: "the knower of all that is born; or one whose knowledge is born; or one whose strength is born": Sāyaṇa explains the word *jātaveda*, which teaches the nature of Agni, in three ways: he who knows all that has come into being; he who has the power of intelligence by which everything natural can be known; he who has abundant power. Yāska in the Nirukta says —

> जातानि वेद । जातानि वैनं विदुः । जाते जाते विद्यत इति वा । जातवित्तो वा जातधनः । जातविद्यो वा जातप्रज्ञानः ॥

> *jātāni veda | jātāni vainaṃ viduḥ | jāte jāte vidyata iti vā | jātavitto vā jātadhanaḥ | jātavidyo vā jātaprajñānaḥ ‖*

(Ni. 7-19, as printed "೭-೧೯"; the OCR reads "२-१०".) Nothing in this world that is born is unknown to him; hence Agni is omniscient; all beings that are born know Agni; hence he is fit to be known by all.

> यत्र ज्ञातः पशूनविन्देति तद्ज्ञातवेदसो जातवेदस्त्वमिति ब्राह्मणं तस्मात्सर्वान्पशवोऽग्निमभि सर्पन्तीति च ॥

> *yatra jñātaḥ paśūnavindeti tadjñātavedaso jātavedastvamiti brāhmaṇaṃ tasmātsarvānpaśavo 'gnimabhi sarpantīti ca ‖*

*(The Brāhmaṇa passage is small and the OCR garbles it; I give it as read and mark it uncertain.)* — this *śruti* sentence clearly says that Agni pervades everything that is born.

Describing the nature of Agni as one who has wealth and who by nature has wisdom, [Yāska cites]

> जातवेदसे सुनवाम सोममरातीयतो नि दहाति वेदः ।
> स नः पर्षदति दुर्गाणि विश्वा नावेव सिन्धुं दुरितात्यग्निः ॥

> *jātavedase sunavāma somamarātīyato ni dahāti vedaḥ |*
> *sa naḥ parṣadati durgāṇi viśvā nāveva sindhuṃ duritātyagniḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-99-1, as printed "೧-೯೯-೧".)

and

> प्र नूनं जातवेदसमश्वं हिनोत वाजिनम् । इदं नो बर्हिरासदे ॥

> *pra nūnaṃ jātavedasamaśvaṃ hinota vājinam | idaṃ no barhirāsade ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-188-1, as printed "೧೦-೧೮೮-೧".) — in these ṛks he explains the praise of Agni called *jātavedas*. And:

> तदेतदेकमेव जातवेदस्यं गायत्रं तृचं दशतयीषु विद्यते । यत्तु किंचिदाग्नेयं तज्जातवेदसानां स्थाने युज्यते ॥

> *tadetadekameva jātavedasyaṃ gāyatraṃ tṛcaṃ daśatayīṣu vidyate | yattu kiṃcidāgneyaṃ tajjātavedasānāṃ sthāne yujyate ‖*

(Ni. 7-20 [?], as printed "೭-೨०"?; the OCR reads "८-२०".) *(Read letter by letter; "daśatayīṣu vidyate" and the second sentence are in small type and doubtful.)* "The *Pra nūnam* is the one *gāyatra tṛca* connected with Jātavedas that is found in the ten books; whatever else is Āgneya is employed in the place of the Jātavedas [hymns]"; thus there is no other Gāyatrī-verse connected with Jātavedas that is used in ritual; Agni himself is indicated by the word *jātavedāḥ*. Therefore —

> स न मर्त्यायैवाग्निरित्येशे उत्तरे ज्योतिषी जातवेदसी उच्येते ततो नु मध्यमः । अभि प्रवन्त समनेव योषा इति तत्पुरस्ताद्व्याख्यातम् । अथासावादित्य उदुत्यं जातवेदसमिति तदुपरिष्टाद्व्याख्यास्यामः ॥

> *sa na martyāyaivāgnirityeśe uttare jyotiṣī jātavedasī ucyete tato nu madhyamaḥ | abhi pravanta samaneva yoṣā iti tatpurastādvyākhyātam | athāsāvāditya udutyaṃ jātavedasamiti tadupariṣṭādvyākhyāsyāmaḥ ‖*

(Ni. 7-[?], as printed.) *(Read letter by letter; the first words, "sa na martyāyaivāgnir iti" [?], are doubtful.)* Though the nature of Agni is described also by the mantra *abhi pravanta samaneva yoṣā*, when one discusses the sense of the word *jātavedas*, the word *agni* [in that mantra] is an epithet of the sense of *jātavedas*; and by the mantra *ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam* it is understood that the Sun too is denoted by the word *jātavedas*. Durgācārya —

> जातवेदसं सूर्यमुद्वहन्तीति तु विशेषणविशेष्यसामानाधिकरण्यैकवाक्यप्रसिद्धाभिः स्वनिगमसिद्धमस्मिन्मन्त्रे जातवेदाः सूर्य इति ॥

> *jātavedasaṃ sūryamudvahantīti tu viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasāmānādhikaraṇyaikavākyaprasiddhābhiḥ svanigamasiddhamasminmantre jātavedāḥ sūrya iti ‖*

*(Read letter by letter; the Durga passage is small type and doubtful.)* — in the mantra *ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam*, in order to show the identity of the Sun and the Agni called Jātavedas, he accepts a single sentence through the relation of qualifier and qualified, and explains that the Sun is also Jātavedas. And —

> यस्तु सूक्तं भजते यस्मै हविर्निरुप्यते [?] अयमेव सोऽग्निर्जातवेदा निपातमेवैते उत्तरे ज्योतिषी इत्येन नामधेयेन भजेते ॥

> *yastu sūktaṃ bhajate yasmai havirnirupyate [?] ayameva so 'gnirjātavedā nipātamevaite uttare jyotiṣī ityena nāmadheyena bhajete ‖*

(Ni. 7-?? [?], as printed.) — the Agni of terrestrial form, indicated by the word *jātavedas*, is invoked in sacrifices by various sūktas and mantras and accepts the oblations; Vaidyuta Agni (lightning), Vaiśvānara Agni and the Sun are varieties of Agni; but the word *jātavedas*, though it can denote them too, by its established usage denotes the terrestrial Agni: so he has explained.

### Printed p. 265  (PDF 286)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 13.)*

***vipraṃ na jātavedasam*** — *jātavidyaṃ medhāvinaṃ brāhmaṇam iva*: "like a Brāhmaṇa of wisdom born, intelligent". Yāska —

> नेति प्रतिषेधार्थीयो भाषायाम् । उभयमन्वध्यायम् ॥

> *neti pratiṣedhārthīyo bhāṣāyām | ubhayamanvadhyāyam ‖*

(Ni. 1-4, as printed "೧-೪".) The word *na* is known in the sense of negation in the language; in the Veda it is used in both senses, negation and *upamā* (comparison): he has explained; in the phrase *vipraṃ na*, since the word *na* is used in the sense of comparison, Sāyaṇa says "like a Brāhmaṇa". The sense: the seer, the seer of the mantra, as one respectfully honours a learned Brāhmaṇa, so with respect and regard I praise Agni too.

***ūrdhvayā devāc'yā kṛpā*** — *utpannayā utkṛṣṭayā devān pūjayantyā devān pratyaktayā vā kṛpayā sāmarthyalakṣaṇayā*: the word *ūrdhva* conveys by usage the meaning "high"; here, as an epithet of the word *kṛpā*, it means "excellent" or "exceeding". The *kṛpā* that Agni has toward the gods is [his power of] sending the oblations offered in the sacrifice to each god, and of honouring the gods.

Yāska, in the Nirukta, *devo devāc'yā kṛpā* (Ni. 6-8) — *devo devān pratyakṣayā* [as printed "ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ತಯಾ"] *kṛpā kṛpater vā kalpater vā* — explains thus. Durgācārya, citing the same ṛk *agniṃ hotāraṃ manye* (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-12-1 [?], as printed), says that because the word *kṛpā* is formed from the root *kṛp* (*kṛpū sāmarthye*) or from the root *kalp*, it means: by power Agni has a mind directed towards the gods.

***śociṣā vaṣṭi*** — *jvālayā kāmayate svīkarotīty arthaḥ*: "with the flame he desires, accepts": it is described that Agni, following the spreading of the ghee that is offered all round and abundantly flows about him, himself shining, accepts with his flames the burning ghee. The words *śocati*, *śociḥ* are recorded among the names of burning, among the names of the burning (Ni. 1-[?]8, as printed "೨-೨೮" [?]); the sense is "flames".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *hotāram* — root *hu dānādanayoḥ*; *tṛn* in the agent sense; guṇa of the root vowel; since it has the marker *n*, first-syllable acute; accusative singular. *manye* — root *manu avabodhane*; laṭ first person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta*.

### Printed p. 266  (PDF 287)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 127".)*

*dāsvantam* — root *ḍudāñ dāne*; *sarvadhātubhya asun* gives *asun*, the form *dāś*; *dāḥ dānaṃ yasya saḥ dāsvān*; *tad asyāsty* gives *matup*; *mādupadhāyāś ca…* gives *va* for *m*; *tasau matvarthe* (Pā. 1-4-19) gives *bha*-designation to the ending in *s*, so no *rutva*; since *matup* is unaccented, the first-syllable acute remains. *jātavedasam* — root *vida jñāne*; with *jāta* as upapada, *gatikārakopapadayoḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca* (Uṇ. 4-?, as printed "೪-೬೬೦" [?]) gives the suffix *asi*; the accent of the first member as an exception to the natural accent of the final member; guṇa of the short penultimate of the root; accusative singular. *svadhvaraḥ* — *śobhanaḥ adhvaraḥ yasya saḥ svadhvaraḥ*; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the final-acute of the latter member. *devāc'yā kṛpā* — *supāṃ sulug…* (Pā. 7-1-39) gives *luk* to the instrumental ending. *vibhrāṣṭim* — root *bhrāja dīptau*; *striyāṃ ktin* (Pā. 3-3-94) gives *ktin*; *vraśca…* gives *ṣa* for the *j*; taking it as cause, *ṣṭutva*; *tādau ca niti kṛty ati* (Pā. 6-2-50) gives the natural accent of the *gati* (*vi*). *vaṣṭi* — root *vaś kāntau* (to desire); laṭ third person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *śociṣā* — root *śuca śoke*; *arciśuciḥ* (Uṇ. 2-?, as printed "೨-೨೬೫") gives *isi*; guṇa of the short penultimate; first-syllable acute of the suffix. *ājuhvānasya* — root *hu dānādanayoḥ*; in the passive, *śānac* in the laṭ sense; in the Veda no *yak*; *śluḥ* [print: *śluvikaraṇa*]; doubling of the root; *abhyastānām ādiḥ* (Pā. 6-1-189) gives the first-syllable acute; in the *prādi*-compound the accent of the final member; genitive singular. *sarpiṣaḥ* — root *sṛp gatau*; *arciśuciḥ* gives *isi*; guṇa of the short penultimate; genitive singular. ‖ 1 ‖

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यजिष्ठं त्वा यजमाना हुवेम ज्येष्ठमङ्गिरसां विप्र मन्मभिर्विप्रेभिः शुक्र मन्मभिः ।
> परिज्मानमिव द्यां होतारं चर्षणीनाम् ।
> शोचिष्केशं वृषणं यमिमा विशः प्रावन्तु जूतये विशः ॥ २ ॥

> *yajiṣṭhaṃ tvā yajamānā huvema jyeṣṭhamaṅgirasāṃ vipra manmabhirviprebhiḥ śukra manmabhiḥ |*
> *parijmānamiva dyāṃ hotāraṃ carṣaṇīnām |*
> *śociṣkeśaṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ yamimā viśaḥ prāvantu jūtaye viśaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यजिष्ठम् । त्वा । यजमानाः । हुवेम । ज्येष्ठम् । अङ्गिरसाम् । विप्र । मन्मऽभिः ।
> विप्रेभिः । शुक्र । मन्मऽभिः ।
> परिज्मानम्ऽइव । द्याम् । होतारम् । चर्षणीनाम् ।
> शोचिःऽकेशम् । वृषणम् । यम् । इमाः । विशः । प्र । अवन्तु । जूतये । विशः ॥ २ ॥

> *yajiṣṭham | tvā | yajamānāḥ | huvema | jyeṣṭham | aṅgirasām | vipra | manma 'bhiḥ |*
> *viprebhiḥ | śukra | manma 'bhiḥ |*
> *parijmānam 'iva | dyām | hotāram | carṣaṇīnām |*
> *śociḥ 'keśam | vṛṣaṇam | yam | imāḥ | viśaḥ | pra | avantu | jūtaye | viśaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे विप्र मेधाविन् शुक्र दीप्तज्वालाग्ने यजिष्ठमतिशयेन यष्टृतमं त्वा त्वां यजमाना वयं यष्टारो हुवेम । आह्वयामः । यतो वयं यजमानाः यतश्च त्वं यजिष्ठः अतो हुवेमेत्यभिप्रायः । कीदृशं त्वाम् । अङ्गिरसामङ्गिरोगोत्रोत्पन्नानां मध्ये ज्येष्ठं । यद्वा । अङ्गाराणां मध्ये ज्येष्ठं ज्वालायुक्तत्वात् । अङ्गिरा अङ्गारा इति यास्कः । नि. ३-१७ । ये अङ्गारा आसंस्तेऽङ्गिरसोऽभवन्निति श्रुतेः । केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । मन्मभिर्मननसाधनैर्विप्रेभिर्विशेषेण प्रीणयितृभिर्मन्मभिर्मन्त्रैः । यद्वा । विप्रेभिर्मेधाविभिर्ऋत्विग्भिर्मन्मभिर्मन्त्रैश्च सहिता वयमिति संबन्धः । त्वदाह्वानानन्तरं परिज्मानं परितो गच्छन्तं द्यामिव सूर्यमिव होतारं देवानामाह्वातारम् । केषामर्थम् । चर्षणीनां मनुष्यनामैतत् । मनुष्याणां यजमानानामर्थे । यद्वा । चर्षणीनां पूर्वं मनुष्याणामेव सतां पश्चाद्यागादिसाधनेन देवत्वमापन्नानां देवानामाह्वातारम् । तथा शोचिष्केशं केशवदत्यन्तायतातेजोज्वालोपेतं वृषणं वर्षितारमेवं रूपं यं त्वां विशः त्वामेव निविशमाना इमा विशो यजमानरूपाः प्रजा जूतये स्वर्गाद्यभिमतफलप्राप्तये प्रावन्तु । प्रकर्षेण प्रीणयन्तु । तादृशं त्वां हुवेमेति संबन्धः ॥

> *he vipra medhāvin śukra dīptajvālāgne yajiṣṭhamatiśayena yaṣṭṛtamaṃ tvā tvāṃ yajamānā vayaṃ yaṣṭāro huvema | āhvayāmaḥ | yato vayaṃ yajamānāḥ yataśca tvaṃ yajiṣṭhaḥ ato huvemetyabhiprāyaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ tvām | aṅgirasāmaṅgirogotrotpannānāṃ madhye jyeṣṭhaṃ | yadvā | aṅgārāṇāṃ madhye jyeṣṭhaṃ jvālāyuktatvāt | aṅgirā aṅgārā iti yāskaḥ | ni. 3-17 | ye aṅgārā āsaṃste 'ṅgiraso 'bhavanniti śruteḥ | kena sādhaneneti taducyate | manmabhirmananasādhanairviprebhirviśeṣeṇa prīṇayitṛbhirmanmabhirmantraiḥ | yadvā | viprebhirmedhāvibhirṛtvigbhirmanmabhirmantraiśca sahitā vayamiti saṃbandhaḥ | tvadāhvānānantaraṃ parijmānaṃ parito gacchantaṃ dyāmiva sūryamiva hotāraṃ devānāmāhvātāram | keṣāmartham | carṣaṇīnāṃ manuṣyanāmaitat | manuṣyāṇāṃ yajamānānāmarthe | yadvā | carṣaṇīnāṃ pūrvaṃ manuṣyāṇāmeva satāṃ paścādyāgādisādhanena devatvamāpannānāṃ devānāmāhvātāram | tathā śociṣkeśaṃ keśavadatyantāyatātejojvālopetaṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ varṣitāramevaṃ rūpaṃ yaṃ tvāṃ viśaḥ tvāmeva niviśamānā imā viśo yajamānarūpāḥ prajā jūtaye svargādyabhimataphalaprāptaye prāvantu | prakarṣeṇa prīṇayantu | tādṛśaṃ tvāṃ huvemeti saṃbandhaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; checked against the OCR, which is garbled in places. The words "tvadāhvānānantaram" and "ātivāyatā-" are small and doubtful.)* "O *vipra*, wise, O *śukra*, O Agni of shining flames, you *yajiṣṭha* — the most worthy of sacrifice — we the sacrificers *huvema* — call. Since we are sacrificers and you are most sacrificed-to, therefore we call: that is the intention. What sort are you? *Jyeṣṭham aṅgirasām* — the eldest among those born in the Aṅgiras lineage; or the eldest among the *aṅgāras* (embers), since he has flame: '*aṅgirā aṅgārāḥ*' says Yāska (Ni. 3-17); '*ye aṅgārā āsaṃs te 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan*' — by the *śruti* [Ai. Br.]. By what means? That is said: *manmabhiḥ* — with means of thought, *viprebhiḥ* — with the specially pleasing, *manmabhiḥ* — mantras. Or else: we, together with *viprebhiḥ* — wise priests — and *manmabhiḥ* — mantras. *Parijmānam iva dyām* — like the Sun going all round the sky, *hotāram* — the caller of the gods; for whose sake? *Carṣaṇīnām* — this is a name for men: for men, the sacrificers; or, for those who were first merely men and afterwards, by the means of sacrifice, attained godhood — the caller of the gods. Likewise *śociṣkeśam* — having hair, that is, extremely long flames of radiance, *vṛṣaṇam* — the showerer; whom, being such, *imā viśaḥ* — these people, in the form of sacrificers, resting in you alone, *jūtaye* — for the attainment of the desired fruit, such as heaven, *pra avantu* — may they greatly please. Such a you we call: so it is connected."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(He) vipra* — O wise Agni; *parijmānam iva dyām* — like the Sun that moves around the sky; *carṣaṇīnām* — for the sacrificers; *hotāram* — the one who calls the gods; [*carṣaṇīnām* — for those who were first men and afterwards attained godhood, the gods; *hotāram* — the one who calls them]; *śociṣkeśam* — one with hair of shining flame (flames spread out like hair); *vṛṣaṇam* — the showerer of desires; *yam* — whom (you); *viśaḥ* — people; *imāḥ viśaḥ* — these (sacrificer) people; *jūtaye* — for the attainment of the fruit desired, such as heaven; *pra avantu* — may they please well; *he śukra* — O blazing Agni; *taṃ* — such; *yajiṣṭham* — most worthy of worship; *aṅgirasām* — among the Aṅgirases (among the embers); *jyeṣṭham* — the eldest (the eldest by his flame); *tvā* — you; *manmabhiḥ* — with the means of thought (and); *viprebhiḥ* — with special pleasing; *manmabhiḥ* — mantras; [*manmabhiḥ* — with praising; *viprebhiḥ* — priests; *manmabhiḥ* — with mantras]; *yajamānāḥ* — we the sacrificers; *huvema* — call.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O wise and blazing Agni, you call the gods, like the Sun that goes all round the sky, for the sake of men, the sacrificers; the people approach you, most worthy of worship, with hair-like flames, the giver of desired ends, for the attainment of the fruits such as heaven; to you, who are the eldest of all the Aṅgirases, we the sacrificers call, together with priests (the praisers) and mantras (the means of praise).

**Printed English (as printed):** *We, the institutors of the ceremony, invoke you Agni, who are most deserving of worship, and are the eldest of the Angirasas, with*

### Printed p. 269  (PDF 290)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 13.)*

*(acceptable) prayers; and with prayers (recited) by the priests, (we adore) you, who, like the traverser of the sky, (the sun), are the invoker (of the gods on behalf) of men, and whom, the bright-haired showerer (of blessings), many people approaching propitiate for the attainment of felicity.*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 2.**

***śukra — dīptajvālāgne*** — the word *śukra* is recorded among the hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-[?]4 [as printed "೨-೩೪"; doubtful]).

> आ सुष्वयन्ती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ ।
> दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥

> *ā suṣvayantī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yonau |*
> *divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142-7, as printed "೧-೧೪೨-೭".) *(Read letter by letter; "suṣvayantī" and "śukrapiśaṃ" as printed.)* In this ṛk, the word *śukra* is explained: "*śukrapeśasaṃ śriyaṃ, śukraṃ śocateḥ jvalatikarmaṇaḥ*" (Ni. 8-11 [?] as printed "೮-೧೧"), the word *śukra*, derived from *śuc* (burning), meaning "shining", is made an epithet of Agni, and Agni is addressed as "one with bright flames".

***vipra — medhāvin*** — the word *vipra* is explained as "wise, intelligent"; as it is used as an epithet of Agni, Agni is addressed as "wise one".

***yajiṣṭhaṃ tvā yajamānā huvema*** — *atiśayena yaṣṭṛtamaṃ tvāṃ vayaṃ yaṣṭāraḥ āhvayāmaḥ*: In this sentence the sacrificer is called both *yajamāna* and *yaṣṭṛ*; Agni, being necessarily required by the sacrificers (as the chief), is addressed as the most worthy of sacrifice, and the sacrificers invoke Agni for the purpose of the sacrifice, it is explained.

***aṅgirasāṃ jyeṣṭham*** — *aṅgirogotrotpannānāṃ madhye jyeṣṭhaṃ yadvā aṅgārāṇāṃ madhye jyaiṣṭhaṃ jvālāyuktatvāt aṅgirā aṅgārāḥ* (Ni. 3-17), says Yāska: *ye 'ṅgārā āsaṃs te 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan* (Ai. Br. 3-34, as printed "ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. ೩-೩೪"), by the *śruti*. The meaning is that Agni is the first of all those born in the lineage of the seer Aṅgiras; or that, by the connection with flames, he is the chief among the embers.

> त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरा ऋषिर्देवो देवानामभवः शिवः सखा ।

> *tvamagne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣirdevo devānāmabhavaḥ śivaḥ sakhā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-1, as printed.)

> त्वमग्ने प्रथमोऽङ्गिरस्तमः कविर्देवानां परिभूषसि व्रतम् ॥

> *tvamagne prathamo 'ṅgirastamaḥ kavirdevānāṃ paribhūṣasi vratam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-2, as printed.)

### Printed p. 270  (PDF 291)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 127".)*

In these ṛks it is described that Agni, first of all the Aṅgirases, was born under the name of the ṛṣi Aṅgiras and was the best among those ṛṣis. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, "*ye 'ṅgārā āsaṃs te 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan*" (Ai. Br. 3-34): the embers (*aṅgāra*) that arose when Agni burned became the name of the ṛṣis Aṅgiras: thus the derivation of the word *aṅgiras* is also given.

> प्रियमेधवदत्रिवज्जातवेदो विरूपवत् ।
> अङ्गिरस्वन्महिव्रत प्रस्कण्वस्य श्रुधी हवम् ॥

> *priyamedhavadatrivajjātavedo virūpavat |*
> *aṅgirasvanmahivrata praskaṇvasya śrudhī havam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-45-3, as printed "೧-೪೫-೩".) Citing this ṛk, Yāska (Ni. 3-17), "*arciṣi bhṛguḥ saṃbabhūva bhṛgur bhrajyamāno na dehe | aṅgāreṣv aṅgirā aṅgārā añcanāḥ aṅkanāḥ*": has explained. Durgācārya, explaining its meaning —

> भृगुर्भ्रज्यमानो न देहे प्रजापतिना किल शुक्रमाक्षीयमादाय अग्नौ हुतम् । ततः अर्चिषि ज्वालायां भृगुर्नाम महर्षिः संबभूव । व्यपगते अर्चिषि यः अङ्गारेषु संबभूव सः अङ्गिराः नाम अभवत् । अङ्गाराः अङ्कनाः । ते हि यत्र निधीयन्ते तदङ्कितं भवति ॥

> *bhṛgurbhrajyamāno na dehe prajāpatinā kila śukramākṣīyamādāya agnau hutam | tataḥ arciṣi jvālāyāṃ bhṛgurnāma maharṣiḥ saṃbabhūva | vyapagate arciṣi yaḥ aṅgāreṣu saṃbabhūva saḥ aṅgirāḥ nāma abhavat | aṅgārāḥ aṅkanāḥ | te hi yatra nidhīyante tadaṅkitaṃ bhavati ‖*

*(Read letter by letter; "śukram ākṣīyam ādāya" [?] is small and doubtful.)* "[It is said that] Bhṛgu, as if being fried in a body, [arose] when Prajāpati offered his seed in the fire; thence in the flame (*arciṣi*) the great seer called Bhṛgu came into being; when the flame had gone, he who came into being among the embers was called Aṅgirā. *Aṅgārāḥ* are *aṅkanāḥ* — marking: for where they are laid down, that place is marked." When Brahmā (Prajāpati) offered his seed in the fire, flames arose; from them the seer Bhṛgu was born; when all the flames had subsided, the embers remained; he who was born from these became the seer called Aṅgiras; since those that are touched are marked (*aṅkana*), these were named *aṅgāras*: so the meaning is explained. From this Sāyaṇa has described Agni, being endowed with flame, as the best among embers.

***manmabhir viprebhir manmabhiḥ*** — *mananasādhanaiḥ viśeṣeṇa prīṇayitṛbhiḥ mantraiḥ | yadvā viprair medhāvibhir ṛtvigbhiḥ manmabhir mantraiś ca sahitā vayam iti saṃbandhaḥ*. The word *manma* is repeated here twice; by this two kinds of meanings are described. The first meaning is "means of thought", as an epithet of the word *mantra*. In the second, the word *manma* [means mantra]. For the word *vipra* too two meanings are explained: first, *vi* = special, *pra* = pleasing (*prīṇayitā*, "the satisfier"); the second meaning of the word *vipra* is "wise priest" (*ṛtvij*).

### Printed p. 271  (PDF 292)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 13.)*

The meaning is that, in sum, wise priests who are accompanied by mantras that please Agni, and we the sacrificers, invoke [Agni]. Sāyaṇa has explained this in two ways. Through the different meanings stated for *vipra*, a variation of sense is described here. The meaning of the word *manma* has been explained in the ṛk 1-[?] [as printed "೧-೧೪೪-೨"?; doubtful].

***hotāraṃ carṣaṇīnām*** — *yajamānānām arthe devānām āhvātāraṃ yadvā pūrvaṃ manuṣyāṇām eva satāṃ paścād yāgādisādhanena devatvam āpannānāṃ devānām āhvātāram*: In explaining the meaning of the word *hotṛ*, derived from the root *hve*, it was described before that Agni himself is the *hotṛ*, and that he calls the gods to receive the oblations offered in the sacrifice to the various gods, by reciting their mantras. By this two kinds of meaning are explained here too. In the first, it is said that Agni calls all the gods for the sacrifice. In the second, to explain the word *carṣaṇī* — Yāska in the Nirukta cites *manuṣyāḥ, naraḥ* [and so on], among the twenty-five names of men (Ni. 3-8 [?], as printed "೩-೮"). And —

> विश्वानरस्य वस्पतिमनानतस्य शवसः । एवैश्च चर्षणीनामूती हुवे रथानाम् ॥

> *viśvānarasya vaspatimanānatasya śavasaḥ | evaiśca carṣaṇīnāmūtī huve rathānām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-6-? [?], as printed "೮-೬-೪"? — numerals small.) *(Read letter by letter; I do not complete the words from memory; "vaspatim" is doubtful.)* In this ṛk, *carṣaṇīnām* is explained as *manuṣyāṇām* (Ni. 12-22 [?] as read by the OCR). Following this, Sāyaṇa explains the word *carṣaṇī*, since it is recorded among the names of men, as *yajamānānām arthe* — "for the sacrificers" — in the first explanation; and in the second, those who were first mere men and, by performing sacrifice, attained the state of gods, are called *carṣaṇī*; Agni calls them to the sacrifice, he said.

***parijmānam iva dyām*** — *sūryam iva parito gacchantam*: explaining *dyām* as "the sun", Sāyaṇa says that Agni, like the Sun, moves about everywhere (pervades). But Yāska —

> न नूनमस्ति नो श्वः कस्तद्वेद यदद्भुतम् ।
> अन्यस्य चित्तमभि संचरेण्यमुताधीतं वि नश्यति ॥

> *na nūnamasti no śvaḥ kastadveda yadadbhutam |*
> *anyasya cittamabhi saṃcareṇyamutādhītaṃ vi naśyati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-120-3 [?], as printed "೧-೧೨೦-೩".) citing this ṛk, [says] *na nūnam asty adyatanaṃ, adyāsmin daivi dyur ity ahno nāmadheyaṃ dyotata iti sataḥ* (Ni. 4-[?]; as read) — he explains the word *dyu* as *ahas*, "day". Durgācārya, since the ṛk says "not now … tomorrow does not exist", explains it by supplying the word *adyatanam* ("of today") to Yāska's statement.

### Printed p. 272  (PDF 293)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 127".)*

Since the day (*ahas*) arises from a particular motion of the Sun, and is a particular time, [Sāyaṇa seems to] explain that "he who gives light to the day, who moves about like the Sun that is ever moving" — the general meaning "shining" belongs to both day and Sun.

***śociṣkeśam*** — *keśavad atyantāyatatejojvālopetam*: the word *śocis* is recorded among the eleven names of burning beginning with *jvalat* (Ni. 1-[?]8 [as printed "೨-೨೮"; doubtful]); *jvalataḥ* means flames. As the hairs on the bodies of men are long, so are the flames of Agni long. One having such flames is Agni: that is the sense.

***imāḥ viśaḥ viśaḥ jūtaye prāvantu*** — in this sentence the word *viśaḥ* is used twice. The author of the Nirukta says that the word *viśaḥ* is recorded among the twenty-five names of men, beginning with *manuṣyāḥ*, *naraḥ* (Ni. 3-8). And —

> जराबोध तद्विविड्ढि विशेविशे यज्ञियाय । स्तोमं रुद्राय दृशीकम् ॥

> *jarābodha tadviviḍḍhi viśeviśe yajñiyāya | stomaṃ rudrāya dṛśīkam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-114-4, as printed "೧-೧೧೪-೪" [?].) *(Read letter by letter.)* In this ṛk, *viśe viśe* is explained as *manuṣyasya manuṣyasya*, "for each and every man". Sāyaṇa says of the two words *viśaḥ* … *viśaḥ*: for the one, "those who rest in you alone, taking Agni alone as their support"; for the second *viśaḥ*, "people in the form of sacrificers"; and since Agni, the god, is the fulfiller of what is desired, may the people who serve him, in the form of sacrificers, be satisfied by offering oblations for their respective desired ends, such as heaven: thus he prays. And — such an Agni we call and give oblations to: this is what is said.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR).** *yajiṣṭham* — root *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu*; *tṛc* in the agent sense; when the sense "most worshipping" is intended, *tuśchandasi* (Pā. 5-3-59) gives *iṣṭhan*; with it following, *turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu* (Pā. 6-4-154) elides the *tṛc*; *ñnityādir nityam* (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the first-syllable acute; accusative singular.

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 13.)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, continued; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR and the page.)* *yajamānāḥ* — the root as before; *śānac* in the laṭ sense, *śap*; *āne muk* (Pā. 7-2-82) gives *muk* to the stem in *a*; since the *sārvadhātuka* follows the *upadeśa*, *tāsyanudāttet* makes it unaccented, so the root-accent remains. *huvema* — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; liṅ first person plural, *mas*; *nityaṃ ṅitaḥ* elides its *s*; *śap*; the augment *yāsuṭ* …; *iyaṅ*-substitution; *loponyoḥ* [print: "ಲೋಪೋವೋರ್ವ್ಯೋಃ"] elides the *y*; guṇa; *bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pā. 1-1-34 [?]) gives *saṃprasāraṇa*; by *vyatyaya* the *uvaṅ* substitution; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *jyeṣṭham* — *atiśayena praśasyaḥ jyeṣṭhaḥ*; when *iṣṭhan* comes in the sense of excess, *jya ca* (Pā. 5-3-61) gives *jya* for *praśasya*; since *prakṛtyaikāc* gives *prakṛtibhāva*, the *ā*-elision does not occur; guṇa; since the suffix has the marker *n*, first-syllable acute; accusative singular. *manmabhiḥ* — root *mana jñāne*; *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante* (Pā. 3-2-75) gives *manin*; since *n*-marked, first-syllable acute; instrumental plural. *viprebhiḥ* — *vipra* + *bhis*; since *bahulaṃ chandasi* applies, *bhis* does not become *ais*; by the *jhal* rule, *e* in the plural. *parijmānam* — *pari jāyate iti parijmā*; recorded as formed with *kanin* (Uṇ. 1-[?]), accusative singular. *carṣaṇīnām* — final-acute by the *prātipadika* accent; *nāmany atarasyām* [print: *nāmanyatarasyām*] (Pā. 6-1-177) gives the acute to the case-ending (genitive plural). *avantu* — root *ava rakṣaṇe*; loṭ third person plural; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *jūtaye* — *ūtijūtisātihetiḥ…* (Pā. 3-3-97) records the form formed with *ktin* as acute; dative singular. ‖ 2 ‖

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स हि पुरू चिदोजसा विरुक्मता दीद्यानो भवति द्रुहन्तरः ।
> परशुर्न द्रुहन्तरः ।
> वीळु चिद्यस्य समृतौ श्रुवद्वनेव यत्स्थिरम् ।
> निःषहमाणो यमते नायते धन्वासहा नायते ॥ ३ ॥

> *sa hi purū cidojasā virukmatā dīdyāno bhavati druhantaraḥ |*
> *paraśurna druhantaraḥ |*
> *vīḷu cidyasya samṛtau śruvadvaneva yatsthiram |*
> *niḥṣahamāṇo yamate nāyate dhanvāsahā nāyate ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । हि । पुरु । चित् । ओजसा । विरुक्मता । दीद्यानः । भवति । द्रुहःऽतरः ।
> परशुः । न । द्रुहःऽतरः ।
> वीळु । चित् । यस्य । सम्ऽऋतौ । श्रुवत् । वना ऽइव । यत् । स्थिरम् ।
> निःऽसहमानः । यमते । न । आयते । धन्वऽसहा । न । आयते ॥ ३ ॥

> *saḥ | hi | puru | cit | ojasā | virukmatā | dīdyānaḥ | bhavati | druhaḥ 'taraḥ |*
> *paraśuḥ | na | druhaḥ 'taraḥ |*
> *vīḷu | cit | yasya | sam 'ṛtau | śruvat | vanā 'iva | yat | sthiram |*
> *niḥ 'sahamānaḥ | yamate | na | āyate | dhanva 'sahā | na | āyate ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> स हि स एव पूर्वं स्तुत एवाग्निर्विरुक्मता विशेषेण रोचनवता ओजसा ज्वालारूपेण बलेन पुरु चित् अत्यधिकमेव दीद्यानो दीप्यमानो द्रुहन्तरो द्रोग्ध्ऋणां तरिता निवारयिता भवति । अस्मासु द्रोहं कुर्वतां शत्रूणां हिंसको भवतीत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । द्रुहन्तरः द्रुमाणां छेदनाय प्रयुक्तः परशुर्न परशुरिव । स यथा द्रुमं हिनस्ति तथायमपि । किंच यस्याग्नेः समृतौ संगतौ संयोगे वीळु चित् दृढमपि पाषाणादिकं श्रुवत् गच्छेत् क्षीयेत । तथा यत्स्थिरं पर्वतादि स्थिरमचलितं तदपि श्रुवत् । वीळिति दृढनाम वीळु च्छौतमिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वनेव उदकमिव । उदकं यथाग्निसंयोगे शुष्यति तथेत्यर्थः । अत्यन्तदृढं स्थिरमपि हिनस्ति । अस्मद्द्रोग्धॄणामग्न्यादिरूपं शत्रुं हिंसतीति किमुतवक्तव्यमित्यभिप्रायः । किंचायमग्निर्निःषहमाणः शत्रून्नितरामभिभवन् यमते । उपरमते । शत्रुषु मध्ये क्रीडति । तानेव नाशयति । कथं कुर्वन्नायते । न गच्छति । शत्रोः सकाशात्पलायते । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । धन्वसहा न । धनुषा शत्रूनभिभवतीति धान्वष्कः । सहतेरसुन् छान्दसोऽन्त्यलोपः । स यथा शत्रुमभिमुखं विध्यति न पलायते तद्वदित्यर्थः । यद्वा । दृढधनुर्वहनक्षमो धन्वसहः । अस्मिन्पक्षे पचाद्यच् । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । दृढधन्वा सन्नायते न चलति ॥

> *sa hi sa eva pūrvaṃ stuta evāgnirvirukmatā viśeṣeṇa rocanavatā ojasā jvālārūpeṇa balena puru cit atyadhikameva dīdyāno dīpyamāno druhantaro drogdhṛṇāṃ taritā nivārayitā bhavati | asmāsu drohaṃ kurvatāṃ śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsako bhavatītyarthaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | druhantaraḥ drumāṇāṃ chedanāya prayuktaḥ paraśurna paraśuriva | sa yathā drumaṃ hinasti tathāyamapi | kiṃca yasyāgneḥ samṛtau saṃgatau saṃyoge vīḷu cit dṛḍhamapi pāṣāṇādikaṃ śruvat gacchet kṣīyeta | tathā yatsthiraṃ parvatādi sthiramacalitaṃ tadapi śruvat | vīḷiti dṛḍhanāma vīḷu cchautamiti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vaneva udakamiva | udakaṃ yathāgnisaṃyoge śuṣyati tathetyarthaḥ | atyantadṛḍhaṃ sthiramapi hinasti | asmaddrogdhṝṇāmagnyādirūpaṃ śatruṃ hiṃsatīti kimutavaktavyamityabhiprāyaḥ | kiṃcāyamagnirniḥṣahamāṇaḥ śatrūnnitarāmabhibhavan yamate | uparamate | śatruṣu madhye krīḍati | tāneva nāśayati | kathaṃ kurvannāyate | na gacchati | śatroḥ sakāśātpalāyate | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | dhanvasahā na | dhanuṣā śatrūnabhibhavatīti dhānvaṣkaḥ | sahaterasun chāndaso 'ntyalopaḥ | sa yathā śatrumabhimukhaṃ vidhyati na palāyate tadvadityarthaḥ | yadvā | dṛḍhadhanurvahanakṣamo dhanvasahaḥ | asminpakṣe pacādyac | supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | dṛḍhadhanvā sannāyate na calati ‖*

*(Read from the image; checked against the OCR. The Nirukta citation "vīḷu cautam" is as printed and doubtful.)* "*Sa hi* — that same Agni praised before, with *virukmatā* — specially shining — *ojasā*, might in the form of flame, *puru cit* — most abundantly, *dīdyānaḥ* — blazing — *druhantaraḥ* — he becomes the one who crosses over, who wards off, those who injure (*drogdhṛṇām*): the destroyer of enemies who do harm to us. An illustration: *paraśur na druhantaraḥ* — like an axe used for cutting trees; as it destroys the tree, so he too. Moreover, *yasya samṛtau* — at whose contact, *vīḷu cit* — even the hard stone and the like *śruvat* — goes, wastes away; and likewise whatever is firm, a mountain and the like, immovable, also [wastes away]. (*Vīḷu* is a word for 'hard': '*vīḷu cautam*' is read among those names.) An illustration: *vaneva* — like water; as water dries up on contact with fire, so [they waste]. He destroys even the very hard and firm; what then need be said of enemies, in the form of fire and the rest, of those who harm us? That is the intention. Moreover, this Agni, *niḥṣahamāṇaḥ* — overpowering enemies, *yamate* — stays [amid them], sports among enemies; he destroys them. How does he act? *Nāyate* — he does not go; he does not flee from the enemy. An illustration: *dhanvasahā na* — as the one who overcomes enemies with the bow, an archer; *sahas*… the suffix *asun*, the last letter dropped in the Veda; as he, facing the foe, shoots and does not flee, so [Agni]. Or else *dhanvasaha* is one capable of bearing a strong bow; here the suffix *ac* in the *pacādi* sense; the augment *ā* by *supāṃ sulug*. Being one with a strong bow he does not go, does not waver."

### Printed p. 275  (PDF 296)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 13.)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *Yasya* — of which Agni; *saṃṛtau* — at the contact; *vīḷu cit* — even the very hard (mountains and the like); *yat sthiram (tat ca)* — whatever is firm (other things, whatever they are); *vaneva* — like water (as water is dried up by contact with fire); *śruvat* — go to destruction; *sa hi* — that Agni, praised before; *virukmatā* — specially shining; *ojasā* — with the strength in the form of flame; *puru cit* — most abundantly; *dīdyānaḥ* — blazing; *druhantaraḥ* — used for the destruction of enemies; *paraśuḥ na* — like an axe; *druhantaraḥ* — the destroyer of (our) enemies; *bhavati* — becomes; (*kiṃ ca* — moreover; *ayam agniḥ* — this Agni); *niḥsahamānaḥ* — wholly defeating the enemies; *yamate* — plays [among them] (destroys them); *yathā* — as; *dhanvasahā* — a hero who overcomes enemies as the bearer of a bow; *na āyate* — does not flee from enemies; (*tathā* — so); *na āyate* — does not run away (stays firm).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** In contact with Agni even the very hard and immovable mountains and the like, like water [dried by fire], perish; the same Agni, like an axe used to cut the enemies, shining especially with his flames, destroys our enemies; defeating them completely, he plays among them; like a hero bearing a bow, he does not flee, but stands firm.

**Printed English (as printed):** *Verily, that Agni, far shining with brilliant vigour, is the destroyer of foes, like a hatchet that cuts down trees : whatever is most solid and stable dissolves like water at his contact : unsparing, he sports (amidst enemies), nor desists (from their destruction), like an archer who retreats not (from battle).*

### Printed p. 276  (PDF 297)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 127".)*

**Special topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu), Ṛk 3.**

In this ṛk there are three sentences: (1) *sa dīdyānaḥ druhantaraḥ paraśur na druhantaraḥ*; (2) *yasya saṃṛtau vīḷu cid yat sthiraṃ vaneva śruvat*; (3) *niṣṣahamāṇaḥ yamate dhanvasahā na nāyate nāyate*.

In the first sentence the word *druhantaraḥ* is used twice. For this word the meaning "one who destroys" is explained. By this it is said that Agni, shining abundantly, destroys even those who do harm to sacrificers, or enemies, or makes them submerged. In this matter, by the second *druhantaraḥ* an illustration is cited: as the axe that is used for cutting down trees destroys them, so Agni too, it is compared, destroys like the axe.

***puru*** — this word is recorded among the twelve names of "many" (Ni. 3-13 [?]); it gives the meaning "much".

***cit*** — the author of the Nirukta records this word among the particles, explaining *cid iti ... anekakarmā* [as printed "ಚಿದಿತ್ಯೇಷೋऽನೇಕಕರ್ಮಾ", Ni. 1-4]: (the indeclinable *cit* conveys many meanings); *ācāryaḥ cid idaṃ brūyāt iti pūjāyām* — in the sentence "the teacher may say this" *cit* means respect; and in *caturdaśadamānāt* (Ni. 3-[?]) [as printed] *cit* is a word of comparison.

> चिदिति निपातोऽनुदात्तः । अथापि पशुनामेह भवत्युदात्तः ॥

> *ciditi nipāto 'nudāttaḥ | athāpi paśunāmeha bhavatyudāttaḥ ‖*

(Ni. 5-[?] as printed.) *(Read letter by letter; the second half is doubtful.)* The indeclinable *cit* is used with an unaccented tone and is a sign of an unaccented sense; but when accented it conveys an animal [name, *cit* ... ]. In *sadyaś cid yaḥ śavasā pañca kṛṣṭīḥ* *cit* is a sign of the unaccented tone; in *cid asi manāsi dhīr asi* it is a sign of the accented tone; thus they say.

In the second sentence it is explained that even the hard stones and the like, merely through contact with Agni, dissolve [or: waste away]; the mountain that is exceedingly strong and the like are made soft; as water is dried by contact with Agni: so he gives the example. By this illustration it is said that Agni is a wonder of capacity in destroying the enemies or the injurers of those who have performed the sacrifice, who cause difficulty to the firm mountain and (rock).

***vīḷu*** — the meaning is "hard"; the word *vīḷu* is recorded in the twenty-eight names of strength: *vīḷu cautam* (Ni. 2-[?]).

### Printed p. 277  (PDF 298)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 13.)*

***vaneva*** — Sāyaṇa explains this as "like water". Yāska has recorded the word *vana* also among the names of rays (Ni. 1-[?]5 [as printed "೧-೧೫"? doubtful]) —

> नियश्वश्नक्षि श्वसनस्य मूर्धनि कुष्ठस्य चिद्वनिनो रोरुवद्वना ॥

> *niyaśvaśnakṣi śvasanasya mūrdhani kuṣṭhasya cidvanino roruvadvanā ‖*

*(Read letter by letter; the first words are small and I cannot confirm them: I give the pāda as printed in the Kannada, "niyaśvaśnakṣi …", unverified.)* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as printed "೧-೫೪-೫"?) — in this ṛk the word *vanā* is explained as *vanāni udakāni*, "waters".

> मेद्यन्तु ते वह्नयो येभिरीयसेऽरिषण्यन्वनस्पते ।
> आयूया धृष्णो अभिगूर्या त्वं नेष्ट्रात्सोमं द्रविणोदः पिब ऋतुभिः ॥

> *medyantu te vahnayo yebhirīyase 'riṣaṇyanvanaspate |*
> *āyūyā dhṛṣṇo abhigūryā tvaṃ neṣṭrātsomaṃ draviṇodaḥ piba ṛtubhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-37-3 [?], as printed "೨-೩೭-೩"; the first words are doubtful in my reading.) Citing this ṛk, in explaining the word *vanaspate* — *vanaspatir ity eṣa hi vanānāṃ pātā vā pālayitā vā vanaṃ vanoteḥ* — he explains that the word *vana*, derived from the root *van* meaning "to ask", conveys the meaning "forest".

In the third sentence it is described: *nāyate* — Agni does not flee, does not run in fear from enemies when they come against him; *niṣṣahamāṇaḥ yamate* — he, overcoming the enemies greatly and sporting in their midst, destroys them.

And here, in this matter, the illustrative sentence *dhanvāsahā nāyate nāyate* is cited. The word *dhanvasaha* is used here. For *dhanvasaha* the meaning is *dhanuṣā śatrūn abhibhavati iti dhānuṣkaḥ* — "since he overcomes enemies by the bow, a bearer of a bow as weapon"; or, in the second explanation, "one who is able to bear a strong bow". By this Agni is compared to a hero who, bearing a bow or bearing a strong bow and fighting, does not move away from enemies but stays firm, facing them, or who, bending the bow firmly, fights without moving.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; noted briefly, numbers as read by the OCR and page).** *puru* — *nipātasya ca* (Pā. 6-3-136) lengthens the final vowel in the Saṃhitā. *virukmatā* — *viśiṣṭā ruk virukmā*, *tadvān virukmān*; when *matup* comes, since *ayasmayādīni* (Pā. 1-4-20) read it as having *pada* status, there is no *kutva*, and since it is *bha* there is no *jaś*-saṃdhi; instrumental singular. *dīdyānaḥ* — root *dīdī dīptidevanayoḥ*; this is a *sautra* root; by *vyatyaya* *śānac*; since it follows the *upadeśa* it is unaccented, so the root-accent remains.

*druhantaraḥ* — *drogdhṛṇāṃ taritā druhantaraḥ*; root *tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ*; *saṃjñāyāṃ bhṛtvṛjidhārisahitapidamaḥ* [print: "ಸಂಜ್ಞಾಯಾಂ ಭೃತ್ಯ…", Pā. 3-2-46] gives the suffix *khac*; with it as cause guṇa of the root vowel; the form *tara*; from *druha jighāṃsāyām* — since it has *it* [penultimate], *igupadhajñāprīkirakaḥ* (Pā. 3-1-135) gives *ka*; *lakṣaṇe*… *aruddviṣad-ajantasya mum* (Pā. 6-3-67) gives the augment *mum* to the preceding word; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* gives the accent of the final member. *paraśuḥ* — *paraṃ śṛṇāti iti paraśuḥ*; root *śṝ hiṃsāyām*; *ājjaraśaraṇikhaniśyabhyāṃ ḍiccha* [print: "ಆಜ್ಜಪರಯೋಃ ಖನಿಕ್ಷ್ಯಭ್ಯಾಂ ಡಿಚ್ಚ", Uṇ. 1-[?]] gives *ku* ; by *ḍit* the *ṭi* of the root is elided; final-acute by the suffix accent. *śruvat* — root *śru śru gatau*; Bhvādi; leṭ third person singular *tip*; *itaś ca lopaḥ* (Pā. 3-4-97) elides *i*; *leṭo 'ṭāṭau* (Pā. 3-4-94) gives *aṭ*; *śap*; by the rule "*saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ*" no guṇa; *ācchinnu…* gives *uvaṅ* [*śruvaḥ*]; the form *śruvat*; since *yat* is connected, no *nighāta*; the root-accent remains. *vanā iva* — *supāṃ sulug…* (Pā. 7-1-39) gives *ā* to the ending. *niṣṣahamāṇaḥ* — root *saha marṣaṇe*; *śānac* in the place of *laṭ*; *śap*; *āne muk* gives *muk* to the stem in *a*; *tāsyanudāttet* makes the *sārvadhātuka* unaccented and the root-accent remains; in the *prādi* compound the accent of the final member. *yamate* — root *yama uparame*; laṭ third person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta* after a non-verb word. *āyate* — root *aya paya gatau*; laṭ third person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *dhanvasahā* — root *saha marṣaṇe*; *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* gives *s*; *sarvadhātubhya asun* gives *asun*; in the Veda the end of the root (*ha*) is dropped; since *n*-marked, first-syllable acute; in the compound the accent of the final member. In the second explanation, *ac* after *nandigrahapacādibhyaḥ* (Pā. 3-1-134); *supāṃ sulug…* gives *ā* to the case-ending. ‖ 3 ‖
