### Printed p. 346  (PDF 367)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 128".)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** All the sacrificers, by their excellent rites, in the powerful flames of Agni, for his satisfaction, offer *puroḍāśa* and the like, as grains belonging to the wind (the wind splits the clouds and brings rain, and through that grain arises) and as food is given to a guest who has come; the sacrificer too, by the strength of the wealth given by Agni, makes the gift of oblation; (Agni accepts the oblation by the strength of the flames fit to receive it, or grants the sacrificer the gift he desires); Agni, thus satisfied, protects us from the sin and sorrow that harass and overcome us.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Inasmuch as (all men) offer in holy rite (food) for his satisfaction in the blazing (flames) of Agni, like (the grains that) are to be enjoyed by the winds, and like the viands that are to be given to him who solicits them: therefore the worshipper presents gifts to him, according to the extent of his opulence; and he preserves us, when oppressed (by sin), from wickedness; from overpowering malevolence and sin."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 5).**

***taviṣīṣu avena pṛñcate*** — *prabalāsu jvālāsu tṛptinimittena bhojyā bhakṣyāṇi puroḍāśādīni miśrayanti*: the sacrificer, as an offering of the oblations, throws into the powerful flames, so that Agni may be satisfied, the *puroḍāśa* and other suitable foods. The word *taviṣī* is recorded among the twenty-eight names of strength (Ni. 3-9 [?]). And —

> पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीम् ।
> यस्य त्रितो व्योजसा वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् ॥

> *pituṃ nu stoṣaṃ maho dharmāṇaṃ taviṣīm |*
> *yasya trito vy ojasā vṛtraṃ viparvam ardayat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-187-1, as read.) Here, "*taviṣīti balanāma tavater vṛddhikarmaṇaḥ*" — the word *taviṣī* is used in the sense of strength; Sāyaṇa explains it with the same sense as the Niruktakāra intended.

***marutāṃ na bhojyā*** — *vāyūnāṃ sambandhīni vrīhyādīnīva*: since the wind, splitting the clouds, brings about rain, from that rain crops arise, and in them the foods fit to be eaten…

[*the Special Topics continue on p. 347*]

### Printed p. 347  (PDF 368)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 15 [as read].)*

(Continuing from p. 346:) "…the grains and the like, fit to be eaten, are spread out (*vyāpta*), occupying the field. As these grains, in the form of food, spread out to the wind and the other gods as oblations through Agni, so the offering of the oblation spreads in the flame of Agni": this is given as the illustration.

***iṣirāya na bhojyā*** — *eṣaṇayuktāya yajamānāya arthine bhojyā bhogyāni bhakṣyādīni yathā dīyante tadvat*: "as edibles and the like are given to a petitioner who is seeking": this sentence is cited as an example (*upamāna-vākya*) in the matter of giving the oblation to Agni. It is compared that Agni gives the sacrificer who has a purpose in view the enjoyable things according to his wish. The Niruktakāra cites —

> इषिरेण ते मनसा सुतस्य भक्षीमहि पित्र्यस्येव रायः ।
> सोम राजन् प्र ण आयूंषि तारीरहानीव सूर्यो वासराणि ॥

> *iṣireṇa te manasā sutasya bhakṣīmahi pitryasyeva rāyaḥ |*
> *soma rājan pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tārīr ahānīva sūryo vāsarāṇi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-48-2, as printed "೮-೪೮-೨".) — and explains *īṣaṇena vā eṣaṇena vā ṛṣaṇena vā* (Ni. 4-7 [?]). Durgācārya: "*iṣireṇa* — *sarvātmanā gatena*, [i.e. taking refuge] with all one's being, with mind, speech and body; *eṣaṇena* — *icchāvatā phalaprārthanāvatā*, who prays for the fruit, desiring it; or who performs rites with the fruit in view and prays that the fruit should come; *ṛṣaṇena* — *darśanavatā*, one who has seen the favoured god": thus the meanings. Sāyaṇa accepts only the meaning "with an eye to the fruit".

***dānam invati*** — *haviḥpradānaṃ tasmai vyāpnoti | yadvā svayam abhimataṃ dānam*: "the sacrificer, who wishes Agni to accept the oblation, makes the oblation pervade Agni by himself offering it": so the meaning. Since the word *invati* is recorded among the ten names of "pervading" (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೩-೧೦"), the meaning "makes it pervade" is given. In the second meaning, the sacrificer himself makes what he desires accessible to Agni for the sake of Agni's pleasure, by giving him the oblations Agni wants.

***vasūnām*** — *nivāsayogyānāṃ dhanānām*: the word *vasu* is recorded among the names of rays (Ni. 1-[?]) and among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೧೫" and "೩-೯"); here *vasunā annena* (Ni. 5-[?]; as read "೫-೧೯") — the word denotes food. —

> वसवो यद्विवसते सर्वमग्निर्वसुभिर्वासव इति समाख्या तस्मात् पृथिवीस्थानाः । इन्द्रो वसुभिर्वासव इति समाख्या तस्मान्मध्यस्थानाः । वसव आदित्यरश्मयो विवासनात् तस्माद्द्युस्थानाः ।

> *vasavo yad vivasate sarvam agnir vasubhir vāsava iti samākhyā tasmāt pṛthivīsthānāḥ | indro vasubhir vāsava iti samākhyā tasmān madhyasthānāḥ | vasava ādityaraśmayo vivāsanāt tasmād dyusthānāḥ |*

### Printed p. 348  (PDF 369)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 128".)*

(Ni. 12-41 [?], as read "೧೨-೪೧"; the passage as I read it from the small Kannada type: the Vasus are of the earth, of the middle region and of heaven.) Since the root *vas* is explained as "to dwell much" or "to pervade everything", the word *vasu* has several meanings, for Agni, Indra and the rays of the sun all dwell by pervading everything. Sāyaṇa here explains: "wealth fit for dwelling".

***majmanā*** — *balena*: since this word is recorded among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [?]), the meaning is "strength".

***vasūnāṃ ca majmanā dānam invati*** — two kinds of meaning are given for this sentence. The first, *nivāsayogyānāṃ dhanānām agninā labdhānāṃ balenaiva*: that the sacrificers serve Agni with offered oblations by the strength of the wealth, fit for comfortable dwelling, which they have obtained through Agni's grace. The second, *yadvā so 'gnir vasūnāṃ havirnivāsayogyānāṃ jvālārūpāṇāṃ dhanānāṃ majmanā balena*: that Agni, by the strength of his wealth-like rays — his flames, fit for receiving the oblations — pervades the oblations offered by the sacrificers.

***abhihrutaḥ duritāt trāsate*** — *ābhimukhyena pāpaiḥ hriyamāṇān pāpāt trāyate*: "Agni protects us from the evil deeds that violently harm us".

***śaṃsāt abhihrutaḥ aghāt*** — *atiprabhūtatvena śaṃsanīyāt yadvā hiṃsakāt abhito hriyamāṇāt duḥkhāt tatkāraṇāt pāpād vā trāyate*: "since evil deeds, practised in great number, bring great harm and then suffering, Agni protects from these sins": so the meaning.

Since *śaṃsati* is read among the names of "praising" (Ni. 3-19 [?]), the meaning "praiseworthy" is given for *śaṃsāt* here; but Sāyaṇa has explained it as "destroyer".

***aghāt*** — *duḥkhāt tatkāraṇād vā pāpāt*: the word *agha* means "pain, or the sin that causes pain". —

> इन्द्रासोमा समघशंसमभ्यघं तपुर्ययस्तु चरुरग्निवाँ इव [?] ।
> ब्रह्मद्विषे क्रव्यादे घोरचक्षसे द्वेषो धत्तमनवायं किमीदिने ॥

> *indrāsomā samaghaśaṃsam abhy aghaṃ tapur yayastu carur agnivām̐ iva [?] |*
> *brahmadviṣe kravyāde ghoracakṣase dveṣo dhattam anavāyaṃ kimīdine ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-104-2, as read "೭-೧೦೪-೨"; the first line has doubtful letters in the print: "*tapur yayastu*" [?].) The Niruktakāra in this Ṛk says: "*aghaṃ hanti nirhasitopasarga āhantīti*": the word *agha* is formed from the root *han* (to harm, to go) even though there is no prefix, and it conveys the sense "*āhanti*", "strikes."

### Printed p. 349  (PDF 370)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 15 [as read].)*

— so he explains; the meaning is that the word *agha* denotes both what produces harm and what exists in the form of harm.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *pṛñcate* — root *pṛcī saṃparke*; *rudhādi*; by *vyatyaya* it takes the ātmanepada; *laṭ* third person plural, the suffix *jha*; *ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ* (Pā. 7-1-5) gives *ata*; *ṭeḥ* the substitution *e*; *rudhādibhyaḥ śnam* (Pā. 3-1-78) the *śnam* affix, which, because of *m*, comes after the last vowel; *śnasor allopaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-111) drops its *a*; the *n* becomes *anusvāra*/*parasavarṇa*; because of *yad* there is no *nighāta*; the acute of the suffix's first vowel makes the middle *anudātta*. *bhojyā* — root *bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ*; *bhojyaṃ bhakṣye* (Pā. 7-3-69) gives the form in *ṇyat*; *śeś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. 6-1-70) drops *śi*. *iṣirāya* — root *iṣu icchāyām*; *iṣimadimudi…* (Uṇ. 1-51) gives *kirac*; no guṇa since *k*-marked; since *c*-marked (*citaḥ*, Pā. 6-1-163) the acute on the last syllable; dative singular. *dānam* — root *ḍudāñ dāne*; *lyuṭ* in the abstract sense; *yuvor anākau* gives *ana*; *liti* gives the acute before the suffix. *invati* — root *ivi vyāptau*; Yāska reads *invati* among the verbs of pervading (Ni. 2-18 [?]); *idito num dhātoḥ* (Pā. 7-1-58) gives the augment *nuṁ*; *laṭ* third person singular; because of *hi*, *hi ca* (Pā. 8-1-34) forbids *nighāta*; the root's accent remains since *śap* and *tip* are unaccented. *trāsate* — root *trai pālane*, *laṭ* third person singular; by the power of *bahulagrahaṇa* here too *sip*(?) [as printed]; *ādeca upadeśe 'śiti* (Pā. 6-1-45) gives *ā* to the root; *tiṅ-nighāta*, since it follows a non-finite word. *duritāt* — root *iṇ gatau*; the suffix *kta*; no guṇa since *k*-marked; *kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara*. ‖ 5 ‖

***(ornamental rule)***

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> विश्वो विहाया अरतिर्वसुर्दधे हस्ते दक्षिणे तरणिर्न शिश्रथच्छ्रवस्यया न शिश्रथत् ।

> विश्वस्मा इत्सुकृते वारमृण्वत्यग्निर्द्वारा व्यृण्वति ॥ ६ ॥

> *viśvo vihāyā aratirvasurdadhe haste dakṣiṇe taraṇirna śiśrathacchravasyayā na śiśrathat |*

> *viśvasmā itsukṛte vāramṛṇvatyagnirdvārā vyṛṇvati ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> विश्वः । विऽहायाः । अरतिः । वसुः । दधे । हस्ते । दक्षिणे । तरणिः । न । शिश्रथत् ।
> श्रवस्यया । न । शिश्रथत् ।
> विश्वस्मै । इत् । इषुध्यते । देवऽत्रा । हव्यम् । आ । ऊहिसे ।
> विश्वस्मै । इत् । सुऽकृते । वारम् । ऋण्वति । अग्निः । द्वारा । वि । ऋण्वति ॥ ६ ॥

> *viśvaḥ | vi 'hāyāḥ | aratiḥ | vasuḥ | dadhe | haste | dakṣiṇe | taraṇiḥ | na | śiśrathat |*

> *viśvasmai | it | iṣudhyate | deva 'trā | havyam | ā | ūhise |*
> *viśvasmai | it | su 'kṛte | vāram | ṛṇvati | agniḥ | dvārā | vi | ṛṇvati ‖ 6 ‖*

*(Read from the image. The Saṃhitā prints the first *pāda* in one line "…śiśrathac chravasyayā na śiśrathat"; the Pada repeats *ṛṇvati* twice.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अयमग्निर्दक्षिणेऽभिमतं प्रदातुमुत्साहयुक्ते हस्ते वामेतरे यजमानाय दातव्यं धनं दधे । धारयति । कीदृशोऽयम् । विश्वः सर्वगन्तव्यः । यद्वा विश्वात्मकः । विहाया महान् । विहाया इति महन्नाम विहाया यह्व इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । अरतिरीश्वरोऽरममाणो वा प्रीतिः [?] ॥ अत्र वह्निवस्यर्तिभ्यश्चित् [?] अतिप्रत्ययः चिद्वद्भावादन्तोदात्तः [?] ॥ धृत्वा च शिश्रथत् । धृतं हस्तं यजमानार्थं श्रथयति । ददाति ॥ श्लथयतेर्लुङि चङि रूपम् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । तरणिर्न तरणिरिव तारकः सूर्य इव । स यथा स्वोपासकायाभिमतं हस्ते धृत्वा वितरति तद्वत् । यद्वा । तरणिः सर्वस्य तारको न शिश्रथत् । यजमानं न श्रथयति न मुञ्चति । किंच श्रवस्यया न शिश्रथत् । हविरूपान्नेच्छयैव न शिश्रथत् । न विमुञ्चति । अयमनुग्रहेणैव पालयते हविःस्वीकारस्तु व्यपदेशमात्रेणेति भावः । इदानीं प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे अग्ने देवत्रा देवेषु मध्ये अतिशयेन त्वं विश्वस्मै सर्वस्मा इषुध्यते हविरात्मन इच्छते इन्द्रादये ॥ इषुध्यतिः कण्ड्वादिः ॥ हव्यं तत्तद्देवतामुद्दिश्य प्रत्तं पुरोडाशा

> *ayamagnirdakṣiṇe 'bhimataṃ pradātumutsāhayukte haste vāmetare yajamānāya dātavyaṃ dhanaṃ dadhe | dhārayati | kīdṛśo 'yam | viśvaḥ sarvagantavyaḥ | yadvā viśvātmakaḥ | vihāyā mahān | vihāyā iti mahannāma vihāyā yahva iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | aratirīśvaro 'ramamāṇo vā prītiḥ [?] ‖ atra vahnivasyartibhyaścit [?] atipratyayaḥ cidvadbhāvādantodāttaḥ [?] ‖ dhṛtvā ca śiśrathat | dhṛtaṃ hastaṃ yajamānārthaṃ śrathayati | dadāti ‖ ślathayaterluṅi caṅi rūpam | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | taraṇirna taraṇiriva tārakaḥ sūrya iva | sa yathā svopāsakāyābhimataṃ haste dhṛtvā vitarati tadvat | yadvā | taraṇiḥ sarvasya tārako na śiśrathat | yajamānaṃ na śrathayati na muñcati | kiṃca śravasyayā na śiśrathat | havirūpānnecchayaiva na śiśrathat | na vimuñcati | ayamanugraheṇaiva pālayate haviḥsvīkārastu vyapadeśamātreṇeti bhāvaḥ | idānīṃ pratyakṣakṛtaḥ | he agne devatrā deveṣu madhye atiśayena tvaṃ viśvasmai sarvasmā iṣudhyate havirātmana icchate indrādaye ‖ iṣudhyatiḥ kaṇḍvādiḥ ‖ havyaṃ tattaddevatāmuddiśya prattaṃ puroḍāśā*

*(Read from the image; the bhāṣya continues on p. 351. Several small-type letters, especially in the grammatical tail on *arati*, are doubtful: [?]. What kind? *viśvaḥ* — to be approached by all, or all-formed; *vihāyāḥ* — great (the word *vihāyāḥ* is recorded among the names of 'great': *vihāyā yahva*…); *aratiḥ* — the lord, or the delight; *vasuḥ*. ### Printed p. 351  (PDF 372)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 15 [as read].)*

(Continuing the bhāṣya of Ṛk 6 from p. 350:)

> दिकमोहिसे । सर्वतो वहसि ॥ वहेर्लिटि यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं ॥ किंचायमग्निर्विश्वस्मै सुकृते शोभनयज्ञकर्त्रे यजमानाय वारं सर्वैर्वरणीयं क्षुदादिनिवारकं वान्नादिकम् [?] ऋण्वति । गच्छति । करोतीत्यर्थः । किंचायमग्निर्द्वारा स्वर्गाद्यभिमतद्वाराणि व्यृण्वति । विवृणोति । प्रतिबन्धकपापासनेनद्वाराभिमतानि साधयतीत्यर्थः ॥ ऋण्वतिर्गतिकर्मा । यद्वा रिणिर्गत्यर्थः । इदित्त्वान्नुम् । छान्दसं रेफस्य संप्रसारणम् ॥

> *dikamohise | sarvato vahasi ‖ vaherliṭi yajāditvātsaṃprasāraṇaṃ ‖ kiṃcāyamagnirviśvasmai sukṛte śobhanayajñakartre yajamānāya vāraṃ sarvairvaraṇīyaṃ kṣudādinivārakaṃ vānnādikam [?] ṛṇvati | gacchati | karotītyarthaḥ | kiṃcāyamagnirdvārā svargādyabhimatadvārāṇi vyṛṇvati | vivṛṇoti | pratibandhakapāpāsanenadvārābhimatāni sādhayatītyarthaḥ ‖ ṛṇvatirgatikarmā | yadvā riṇirgatyarthaḥ | idittvānnum | chāndasaṃ rephasya saṃprasāraṇam ‖*

*(Read from the image: "*(ā) ūhise*" — the beginning is the end of "*ā ūhise*"; *havyam…puroḍāśā* of p. 350 + "*dikam ohise*" [sic?]; the fragment is read as printed: "*puroḍāśādikam ohise | sarvato vahasi*" ["you carry it from everywhere"]. A few letters in the small-type grammar tail are doubtful: [?].)* Sense: "…the *puroḍāśa* and the rest, you carry; that is, you carry from all sides. [Grammar: in the *liṭ* of *vah* the *saṃprasāraṇa* by *yajādi*.] And this Agni, to every doer of good sacrifice, the sacrificer, grants a *vāra* — food and the like, to be chosen by all, which keeps off hunger and the like — *ṛṇvati*, goes, makes: so the meaning. And this Agni *dvārā vy ṛṇvati* — opens the gates to heaven and other desired places; by removing the obstructing sins he accomplishes the sacrificer's desires: so the meaning. [Grammar: *ṛṇvati* is a verb of motion; or *riṇi* in the sense of motion; *idittvān num*; the Vedic *saṃprasāraṇa* of the *r*.]"

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *viśvaḥ* — reached by all (the all-formed); *vihāyāḥ* — of great form; *aratiḥ* — the lord; *vasuḥ* — (this Agni, the lord of) wealth fit for dwelling; *dakṣiṇe* — able to give what is desired; *haste* — in the (right) hand; *dadhe* — holds; *taraṇiḥ na* — like the Sun the saviour; *śiśrathat* — gives (the wealth held in his hand) to the sacrificer [or: *taraṇiḥ* — Agni the saviour; *na śiśrathat* — does not let go the sacrificer]; *śravasyayā* — merely by desire for the oblation-food; *na śiśrathat* — does not let go; *devatrā it* — among the gods you in particular; *viśvasmai* — for all; *iṣudhyate* — for Indra and others who desire the oblation; *havyam* — the oblation offered to each deity; *ā ūhise* — you carry everywhere; *viśvasmai sukṛte it* — to all the doers of good works; *vāram* — the food to be desired by all; *ṛṇvati* — grants; *agniḥ* — Agni; *dvārā* — the gates to heaven and the like, as wished; *vi ṛṇvati* — opens.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Agni, who is approached by all, venerable and lord, holds in his right hand — able to grant the desired gift — wealth fit to be given, and gives it (to the sacrificer) like the Sun, the saviour; he does not let go the performers of the sacrifice, even out of desire for the oblations (that is, the oblations are only a pretext; his grace is the chief cause of his protection). Among the gods Agni alone carries to Indra and the others, who desire oblations, the *puroḍāśa* and other oblations offered by the sacrificers; he provides food that removes hunger to all who do good rites; and he opens the gates of the desired heaven and other worlds.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"The universal, mighty and imperious (Agni) holds riches in his right hand; but, like the sun, he loosens his grasp (in favour af* [sic] *his worshipper),*

### Printed p. 352  (PDF 373)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 128".)*

*although he relaxes not from his desire of the (sacrificial) food. Verily, Agni, you bear the oblation to every one of the gods who desires it; Agni grants blessings to every pious (worshipper), and opens for him the gates (of heaven)."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 6).**

***dakṣiṇe*** — *abhimataṃ pradātum utsāhayukte haste vāmetare*: Sāyaṇa explains the word *dakṣiṇa* in two ways: "full of the eagerness of a generous mind", and "the hand other than the left, that is, the right hand".

***viśvaḥ*** — *sarvair gantavyaḥ yadvā viśvātmakaḥ*: "he who should be approached and worshipped by all", or "he who exists in the nature of all things": two meanings are given. The word *viśva* is recorded among the twelve names of "much" — *uru, tuvi* and so on (Ni. 3-13 [?]). In the sense "all" this word is used in very many places.

***vihāyāḥ*** — since it is recorded among the "great" names (Ni. 3-13 [?]), here Sāyaṇa explains *vihāyāḥ* as "great, filled with greatness": this Agni.

***taraṇir na dhṛtvā ca śiśrathat*** — *taraṇiḥ tārakaḥ sūrya iva dhṛtaṃ hastaṃ yajamānārthaṃ śrathayati dadāti yathā saḥ svopāsakāya abhimataṃ haste dhṛtvā vitarati tadvat | yadvā taraṇiḥ sarvasya tārakaḥ na śiśrathat yajamānaṃ na śrathayati na muñcati*: "as the Sun, the saviour, loosens the held hand for the sacrificer, that is, gives, so Agni; or the saviour Agni of all does not let go the sacrificer." The word *taraṇi* is recorded among the names of the swift (Ni. 3-9 [?]); here it is explained as "the Sun". One meaning is that, as the Sun holds in his hand what his worshipper wants and gives it to him, Agni too holds what the sacrificer desires in his own hand and gives it; the second, that as the Sun brings all to a good state, so Agni makes those who serve him — not leaving them in trouble — possess a good state: so it is described.

***śravasyayā na śiśrathat*** — *na vimuñcati*: "Agni does not leave the sacrificers out of pride that they offer him the oblations, nor out of the desire that the oblations will come from them; one should not so understand it. *ayam anugraheṇaiva pālayate haviḥsvīkāras tu vyapadeśamātreṇa*": that Agni accepts oblations is merely a pretext; Sāyaṇa explains that he always protects the sacrificer only by favour.

### Printed p. 353  (PDF 374)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 15 [as read].)*

The word ***śravaḥ*** is recorded among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೩-೯"). —

> अमन्दान्त्स्तोमान् प्र भरे मनीषा सिन्धावधि क्षियतो भाव्यस्य ।
> यो मे सहस्रममिमीत सवानतूर्तो राजा श्रव इच्छमानः ॥

> *amandān stomān pra bhare manīṣā sindhāv adhi kṣiyato bhāvyasya |*
> *yo me sahasram amimīta savān atūrto rājā śrava icchamānaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-126-1, as printed "೧-೧೨೬-೧".) Here the word *śravaḥ* is used in the sense of "fame". And —

> आसश्रासः [?] शवसानमच्छेन्द्रं सुचक्रासो रथ्यासो अश्वाः ।
> अभि श्रव ऋज्यन्तो वहेयुर्नू चिन्नु वायोरमृतं वि दस्येत् ॥

> *āsaśrāsaḥ [?] śavasānam acchendraṃ sucakrāso rathyāso aśvāḥ |*
> *abhi śrava ṛjyanto vaheyur nū cin nu vāyor amṛtaṃ vi dasyet ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-62-3 [?], as read; the numerals are doubtful. The first word is printed "āsaśrāsaḥ"; I give the letters as read.) Here the Niruktakāra explains "*śrava iti annanāma śrūyata iti sataḥ*" — "*śravaḥ* is a name of food; it is heard (*śrūyate*) as something existing". Sāyaṇa explains the word *śravasyā*, in which the suffix *kyac* arises in the sense *śravaḥ ātmana icchati* ("who desires *śravas* for himself"), as "desire for food in the form of an oblation".

***viśvasmai sukṛte vāram ṛṇvati*** — *śobhanayajñakartre yajamānāya sarvair varaṇīyaṃ kṣudādinivārakaṃ vānnādikaṃ karoti*: "Agni grants to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice food that quells hunger": so the meaning.

***agniḥ dvārā vy ṛṇvati*** — "since Agni destroys the sins that obstruct the desired aims such as heaven, he accomplishes the sacrificer's desires": so the meaning.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as read).** *dadhe* — root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; the root with the hidden causal sense; the Vedic *liṭ* in the present sense, third person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *aratiḥ* — root *ṛ gatau*; *vahivasyarti…* (Uṇ. 4-[?]) gives the suffix *ati*; because of it guṇa of the root with *raparatva*; since *cit* is prescribed, *citaḥ* gives the acute on the last syllable. *taraṇiḥ* — root *tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ*; *ārtisṛdhy…* (Uṇ. 2-[?]) gives *ani*; guṇa of the root; acute on the first syllable of the suffix. *śiśrathat* — root *śrath mokṣaṇe*; after *ṇic*, *luṅ* third person singular, *tip*; *itaś ca* drops *i*; *ṇiśridrusubhyaḥ kartari caṅ* (Pā. 3-1-48) the *caṅ* for *cli*; *caṅi* the root is doubled; shortening of the penult; in *sanvadbhāva* [as printed], though there is no [cause]…

### Printed p. 354  (PDF 375)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 128".)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 6, concluded; numbers as printed.)* *śiśrathat* (cont.) — by *bahulaṃ chandasi* the reduplicative takes *i*; and by *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi* the augment *aṭ* does not occur; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *śravasyayā* — when *śravaḥ annam ātmana icchati* is intended, *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. 3-1-8) gives *kyac*; after the *kyac*-ending root, *apratyayāt* (Pā. 3-3-102) gives the suffix *a* in the abstract sense; then *ṭāp*; instrumental singular. *iṣudhyate* — root *iṣudha śaradhāraṇe*, *kaṇḍvādi*; *kaṇḍvādibhyo yak* (Pā. 3-1-27) gives *yak* in the proper sense; *śatṛ* in the present sense; dative singular; since *śatṛ* is without *num* and the ending follows it, *śatur anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. 6-1-173) gives the acute to the ending. *devatrā* — *devamanuṣyapuruṣapurumartyebhyo dvitīyāsaptamyor bahulam* (Pā. 5-4-56) gives *trā*; acute on the last syllable by the accent of the suffix. *ohise* — root *vah prāpaṇe*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* gives *liṭ* in the present sense; in the second person *thāsaḥ se* gives *se*; *vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti* (Pā. 6-1-15) gives *saṃprasāraṇa* of the root's *v*; reduplication; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *sukṛte* — *śobhanaṃ karotīti sukṛt*; root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; after *kvip*, *hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk* (Pā. 6-1-71) the augment *tuk*; *kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara*. *ṛṇvati* — this is a *sautra* root, used in the sense of motion; or *riṇvi gatau*; *idito num dhātoḥ* (Pā. 7-1-58) gives *num*; the Vedic *saṃprasāraṇa* of the *r* of the root; the *n* of *num*, made so by that, becomes *ṇ*; *laṭ* third person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *dvārā* — the form *dvārāṇi*; *śeś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. 6-1-70) drops *śi* in the neuter. ‖ 6 ‖

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स मानुषे वृजने शंतमो हितोऽग्निर्यज्ञेषु जेन्यो न विश्पतिः ।
> प्रियो यज्ञेषु विश्पतिः ।
> स हव्या मानुषाणामिळा कृतानि पत्यते ।
> स नस्त्रासते वरुणस्य धूर्तेर्महो देवस्य धूर्तेः ॥ ७ ॥

> *sa mānuṣe vṛjane śaṃtamo hito 'gniryajñeṣu jenyo na viśpatiḥ |*
> *priyo yajñeṣu viśpatiḥ |*
> *sa havyā mānuṣāṇāmiḷā kṛtāni patyate |*
> *sa nastrāsate varuṇasya dhūrtermaho devasya dhūrteḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । मानुषे । वृजने । शम्ऽतमः । हितः । अग्निः । यज्ञेषु । जेन्यः । न । विश्पतिः ।
> प्रियः । यज्ञेषु । विश्पतिः ।
> सः । हव्या । मानुषाणाम् । इळा । कृतानि । पत्यते ।
> सः । नः । त्रासते । वरुणस्य । धूर्तेः । महः । देवस्य । धूर्तेः ॥ ७ ॥

> *saḥ | mānuṣe | vṛjane | śam 'tamaḥ | hitaḥ | agniḥ | yajñeṣu | jenyaḥ | na | viśpatiḥ |*
> *priyaḥ | yajñeṣu | viśpatiḥ |*
> *saḥ | havyā | mānuṣāṇām | iḷā | kṛtāni | patyate |*
> *saḥ | naḥ | trāsate | varuṇasya | dhūrteḥ | mahaḥ | devasya | dhūrteḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

*(Read from the image. The Pada divides *śaṃ-tamaḥ* as "śam-tamaḥ"; the Saṃhitā is "*śaṃtamo*", as printed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> सोऽग्निर्मानुषे मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य सम्बन्धिनि वृजने वर्जनीये पापे निमित्तभूते सति यज्ञेषु निमित्तेषु शन्तमोऽत्यन्तं सुखतमः अरिष्टस्य निवारकत्वात् अत एव हितः स्वर्गाद्यभिमतसाधकत्वात् । किंचायं यज्ञेषु विश्पतिर्ऋत्विग्रूपाणां प्रजानामतिशयेन पालकः ॥ पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ अत एव प्रियश्च भवति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । जेन्यो न विश्पतिर्जयशीलो राजेव । स यथा परसेनाद्युपद्रवपरिहारेण सम्यक्परिपालनेन च प्रजानां प्रियो भवति । किंचायमग्निर्मानुषाणां मनुष्याणां यजमानानां सम्बन्धीनि हव्या हवींषीळा कृतानीलायां वेद्यां कृतानि सम्पादितान्युद्दिश्य पत्यते । पतति । आगच्छति । किंच सोऽग्निर्नोऽस्मान्यजमानान्वरुणस्य वारकस्य धूर्तेर्हिंसकस्य भयात्त्रासते । त्रायते । यद्वा । धूर्तेरिति पञ्चमी । वरुणस्य पापदेवस्य धूर्तेर्हिंसकात् । किंच महो महतो देवस्य

> *so 'gnirmānuṣe manuṣyasya yajamānasya sambandhini vṛjane varjanīye pāpe nimittabhūte sati yajñeṣu nimitteṣu śantamo 'tyantaṃ sukhatamaḥ ariṣṭasya nivārakatvāt ata eva hitaḥ svargādyabhimatasādhakatvāt | kiṃcāyaṃ yajñeṣu viśpatirṛtvigrūpāṇāṃ prajānāmatiśayena pālakaḥ ‖ patyāvaiśvarya iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvare prāpte parādiśchandasi bahulamityuttarapadādyudāttatvam ‖ ata eva priyaśca bhavati | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | jenyo na viśpatirjayaśīlo rājeva | sa yathā parasenādyupadravaparihāreṇa samyakparipālanena ca prajānāṃ priyo bhavati | kiṃcāyamagnirmānuṣāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ yajamānānāṃ sambandhīni havyā havīṃṣīḷā kṛtānīlāyāṃ vedyāṃ kṛtāni sampāditānyuddiśya patyate | patati | āgacchati | kiṃca so 'gnirno 'smānyajamānānvaruṇasya vārakasya dhūrterhiṃsakasya bhayāttrāsate | trāyate | yadvā | dhūrteriti pañcamī | varuṇasya pāpadevasya dhūrterhiṃsakāt | kiṃca maho mahato devasya*

> धूर्तेर्हिंसातस्त्रासते । पालयते । आयष्वारमग्निर्हिनस्तीति प्रसिद्धम् [?] । यद्वा । एकमेव वाक्यम् । धूर्तेर्हिंसकस्य महो महतो वरुणस्य देवस्य वरुणाख्यायाः पापदेवताया धूर्तेर्हिंसातो नोऽस्मान् सोऽग्निस्त्रासते । त्रायते ॥

> *dhūrterhiṃsātastrāsate | pālayate | āyaṣvāramagnirhinastīti prasiddham [?] | yadvā | ekameva vākyam | dhūrterhiṃsakasya maho mahato varuṇasya devasya varuṇākhyāyāḥ pāpadevatāyā dhūrterhiṃsāto no 'smān so 'gnistrāsate | trāyate ‖*

*(Read from the image: "…*dhūrter hiṃsātas trāsate | pālayate |* [a doubtful phrase "*āyaṣvāram agnir hinastīti prasiddham*" — I give the letters as read: [?]] *| yadvā | ekam eva vākyam |*…")* Sense: "…of the great god's destruction (or of the destroyer) he protects; or as one sentence: from the great Varuṇa, the god who is the sin-deity named Varuṇa, from his harm, Agni protects us."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *mānuṣe* — belonging to man; *vṛjane* — in the matter of sin (its removal); *yajñeṣu* — in the sacrifices; *śaṃtamaḥ* — the great giver of happiness; *hitaḥ* — (therefore) the benefactor; *yajñeṣu* — in the sacrifices; *viśpatiḥ* — protector of the people (in the form of the priests); *jenyaḥ* — victorious; *viśpatiḥ na* — like a king; *priyaḥ* — trusted; *saḥ agniḥ* — that Agni; *iḷā kṛtāni* — prepared on the altar; *mānuṣāṇām* — belonging to man; *havyā* — the oblations (for them); *patyate* — comes; *(kiṃ ca* — and); *saḥ* — he; *naḥ* — us (the performers of the sacrifice); *varuṇasya* — of Varuṇa, who obstructs the rites; *dhūrteḥ* — from the harming one; *trāsate* — protects; *(and)* *mahaḥ devasya* — of the powerful (sin-)god named Varuṇa; *dhūrteḥ* — from the harm; *(trāsate* — protects) [or: *dhūrteḥ* — the harmful; *mahaḥ* — and mighty; *varuṇasya devasya* — of the god named Varuṇa (of sin); *dhūrteḥ* — from the harm; *naḥ* — us; *saḥ* — that Agni; *trāsate* — protects].

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Agni, who gives happiness in the sacrifices by removing the sin of men and is therefore beneficent; who is the protector of the priests who are the subjects in the sacrifices, and who is dear like a victorious king, comes for the oblations that men have prepared on the altar; and, having come, saves us the sacrificers from the harm of the sin (deity) who harms and obstructs the sacrifice.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Agni is a most amiable friend in human infirmity through the means of sacrifices; the beloved protector of all in sacrifices, like a victorious prince, he alights upon the oblations of men when placed upon the altar: he preserves us from the malignity of Varuna; from the malignity of the mighty deity (of sin.)"*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 7) — begun.** ***agniḥ mānuṣe vṛjane yajñeṣu śaṃtamaḥ hitaḥ*** — *yajamānasya sambandhini varjanīye pāpe nimittabhūte sati yajñeṣu atyantaṃ sukhatamaḥ ariṣṭanivārakatvāt*: "when the sacrificer's sin, which is to be shunned, has arisen, Agni is the giver of the greatest happiness in the sacrifices, since he removes harm…" *(the entry continues on p. 357).*

### Printed p. 357  (PDF 378)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 15 [as read].)*

(Continuing the Special Topics of Ṛk 7:) "…*ata eva hitaḥ svargādyabhimatasādhakatvāt*" — "therefore he is *hita*, beneficial, since he accomplishes desired things such as heaven." When sin arises that brings the sacrificer to a bad state, Agni, worshipped with oblations and the like in the sacrifice, which is the means of removing it, removes the sins one by one and so gives great happiness; and by removing the undesired and bringing about heaven and the other desired things for the sacrificers, this Agni also brings what is beneficial: so the meaning.

***yajñeṣu viśpatiḥ jenyo na viśpatiḥ*** — *ayaṃ yajñeṣu ṛtvigrūpāṇāṃ prajānām atiśayena pālakaḥ ata eva priyaś ca | jayaśīlaḥ rājā parasenādyupadravaparihāreṇa samyak paripālanena ca prajānāṃ priyo bhavati iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ.* "Agni is like a king": by this sentence he is compared to a king. As a victorious king, by warding off the troubles that come from the armies of enemies, who bring harm to the people and to himself, is beneficial to his people, and as he is dear to the people because he guards them well, so Agni, by removing the troubles of the people (the priests) in the sacrifices, protects them and is thus dear to them: so the meaning.

***viśpatiḥ*** — *prajānām atiśayena pālakaḥ*: "he who protects the people very well": so the meaning. The word *viśpati* is explained by the Niruktakāra as *sarvasya pātā pālayitā vā*: "the protector of all or one who makes all protected." As illustrations —

> अस्य वामस्य पलितस्य होतुस्तस्य भ्राता मध्यमो अस्त्यश्नः ।
> तृतीयो भ्राता घृतपृष्ठो अस्यात्रापश्यं विश्पतिं सप्तपुत्रम् ॥

> *asya vāmasya palitasya hotus tasya bhrātā madhyamo asty aśnaḥ |*
> *tṛtīyo bhrātā ghṛtapṛṣṭho asyātrāpaśyaṃ viśpatiṃ saptaputram ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-1, as printed "೧-೧೬೪-೧".) and —

> प्र वावृजे सुप्रया बर्हिरेषामा विश्पतीव बीरिट इयाते ।
> विशामक्तोरुषसः पूर्वहूतौ वायुः पूषा स्वस्तये नियुत्वान् ॥

> *pra vāvṛje suprayā barhir eṣām ā viśpatīva bīriṭa iyāte |*
> *viśām aktoruṣasaḥ pūrvahūtau vāyuḥ pūṣā svastaye niyutvān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?], as read "೨-೪೧-೨" [?]; small type, doubtful letters: [?].) — in these Ṛks the word *viśpati* is used in the sense "protector or one who makes protected, of the whole world".

***mānuṣāṇāṃ havyā iḷā kṛtāni patyate*** — *manuṣyāṇāṃ yajamānānāṃ sambandhīni havīṃṣi vedyāṃ sampāditāny uddiśya ayam agnir āgacchati*: "Agni comes to accept the oblations which the sacrificers have prepared and placed on the altar": so the meaning.

### Printed p. 358  (PDF 379)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 128".)*

The word ***iḷā*** is recorded among the names of the earth (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೩"), of speech (Ni. 1-[?]; "೧-೩೩"), of food (Ni. 2-[?]; "೨-೯") and of the cow (Ni. 2-[?]; "೨-९") [numerals as read from the page; doubtful], and is used in the senses earth, speech, food and cow. Durgācārya explains that the word *iḷā* is formed from the root *īḍ* of the sense "praise" (*īḍa stutikarmaṇaḥ*) and so has the sense "praise"; Sāyaṇa alone explains it as "sacrificial altar".

***varuṇasya dhūrteḥ trāsate maho devasya dhūrteḥ*** — Sāyaṇa explains the meaning both by dividing it into two sentences (*varuṇasya dhūrteḥ trāsate* and *mahaḥ devasya dhūrteḥ trāsate*) and as one sentence: *dhūrteḥ mahaḥ devasya varuṇasya dhūrteḥ naḥ agniḥ trāsate*.

In the first way: Agni protects us from the harm of the harmer named Varuṇa (or from the fear of the harmer), and Agni *dhūrvati* — brings to harm — those who do not sacrifice. In the second way: the sin-deity named Varuṇa, being endowed with greatness, is harmful through causing harm, and from the harm of that deity Agni protects us: so the meaning is described.

For the word *dhūrti* two kinds of meaning are given: "harm" and "the harmer".

***mahaḥ*** — *mahataḥ*; the word *mahaḥ* is recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೩-೨೪"[?]). And —

> पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीम् ।
> यस्य त्रितो व्योजसा वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् ॥

> *pituṃ nu stoṣaṃ maho dharmāṇaṃ taviṣīm |*
> *yasya trito vy ojasā vṛtraṃ viparvam ardayat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-187-1, as printed.) Here *mahaḥ* is explained as *mahataḥ*.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *vṛjane* — root *vṛjī varjane*; *kyap ca vṛñ…* [as read: Uṇ. 2-[?]] gives *ana*; no guṇa since *k*-marked; *yuvor anākau* (Pā. 7-1-1) gives *ana*; acute on the first syllable of the suffix; locative singular. *śaṃtamaḥ* — *atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau* (Pā. 5-3-55) gives *tamap* in the sense of excess; since *p*-marked it is unaccented. *jenyaḥ* — root *ji jaye*; by the power of *bahulagrahaṇa* in *kṛtyuṭo bahulam* (Pā. 3-3-113), *yat* in the agent sense by *āto yat* [as read, doubtful: Pā. 3-1-97], *ṇyat* (?)…

### Printed p. 359  (PDF 380)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 15 [as read].)*

*(Grammar, continued.)* *jenyaḥ* (cont.) — the augment *nuṭ* [as read]; because of it guṇa of the root's *i*; *yato nāvaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-213) the acute on the first syllable. *viśpatiḥ* — *viśāṃ patiḥ*; though *patyāvaiśvaryeṇe* (Pā. 6-2-18) would give the accent of the first member, by *parādiś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. 6-2-199) the acute falls on the first syllable of the latter member. *havyā* — the form *havyāni*; by *śeś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. 6-1-70) *śi* is dropped. *iḷā* — *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. 7-1-39) the locative ending is dropped. *patyate* — root *patḷ gatau*; by *vyatyaya* with the ātmanepada; or the root *tasa aiśvarye*, *divādi* — by the transposition the variant reading is accepted, so that the form in *laṭ* is *patyate*; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *trāsate* — root *trai pālane*, *bhvādi*, *laṭ* third person singular; *ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e* (Pā. 3-4-79) gives *e*; *śap*; because *ac* follows, *ayādeśa*; the change of letters is Vedic; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *dhūrteḥ* — root *dhurvī hiṃsāyām*; *ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām* (Pā. 3-3-174) gives *ktic*; *titutratatha…* (Pā. 7-2-9) forbids *iṭ*; *upadhāyāś ca* (Pā. 8-2-78) lengthens the penult; where *lopo vyor vali* would give loss of the *v*, *rālopaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-21) gives loss of the root's *v*; since the suffix has *c*-marker, the acute on the last syllable; the ablative and genitive have the same form. *mahaḥ* — *mahataḥ*, with the Vedic loss of *ti*; or the root *maha pūjāyām*, *kvip*; genitive singular; *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ* (Pā. 6-1-168) gives the acute to the ending. ‖ 7 ‖

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अग्निं होतारमीळते वसुधितिं प्रियं चेतिष्ठमरतिं न्येरिरे ।
> हव्यवाहं न्येरिरे ।
> विश्वायुं विश्ववेदसं होतारं यजतं कविम् ।
> देवासो रण्वमवसे वसूयवो गीर्भी रण्वं वसूयवः ॥ ८ ॥

> *agniṃ hotāramīḷate vasudhitiṃ priyaṃ cetiṣṭhamaratiṃ nyerire |*
> *havyavāhaṃ nyerire |*
> *viśvāyuṃ viśvavedasaṃ hotāraṃ yajataṃ kavim |*
> *devāso raṇvamavase vasūyavo gīrbhī raṇvaṃ vasūyavaḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अग्निम् । होतारम् । ईळते । वसुऽधितिम् । प्रियम् । चेतिष्ठम् । अरतिम् । नि । एरिरे ।
> हव्यऽवाहम् । नि । एरिरे ।
> विश्वऽआयुम् । विश्वऽवेदसम् । होतारम् । यजतम् । कविम् ।
> देवासः । रण्वम् । अवसे । वसुऽयवः । गीःऽभिः । रण्वम् । वसुऽयवः ॥ ८ ॥

> *agnim | hotāram | īḷate | vasu 'dhitim | priyam | cetiṣṭham | aratim | ni | erire |*
> *havya 'vāham | ni | erire |*
> *viśva 'āyum | viśva 'vedasam | hotāram | yajatam | kavim |*
> *devāsaḥ | raṇvam | avase | vasu 'yavaḥ | gīḥ 'bhiḥ | raṇvam | vasu 'yavaḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

*(Read from the image: *vasu-dhitim*, *vasu-yavaḥ*, *gīḥ-bhiḥ*; the Saṃhitā "*gīrbhī raṇvaṃ*".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अमुमग्निं होतारमाह्वातारं होमनिष्पादकं वेळते । ऋत्विजः स्तुवन्ति । तथा वसुधितिं धनस्य धारयितारं दातारं वा अत एव प्रियं सर्वेषां प्रियतमं चेतिष्ठमतिशयेन यजमानानां चेतयितारं यद्वा प्रकृष्टचेतनवन्तम् ॥ चेतिशब्दात्तृश्छन्दसीष्ठन् । तुरिष्ठेमेयःस्विति तृलोपः ॥ अरतिमीश्वरं तादृशं देवं न्येरिरे । नितरां प्राप्ताः । प्राप्तिरेव विशेष्यते । हव्यवाहं न्येरिरे । निःशेषेण प्राप्ताः । इतरदेवेभ्यो हव्यं वोढुं यथा प्रभवति तथा नितरां प्राप्ताः । पुनः कीदृशं विश्वायुं सर्वत्र प्राणिजीवनं विश्ववेदसं सर्वप्रज्ञं होतारं देवानामाह्वातारं यजतं यजनीयं कविं सर्वज्ञम् ॥ ईर प्रेरणे ईर गतौ [?] लिट् रूपम् [?] ॥ किंच देवासो देवनशीला ऋत्विजो रण्वमतिप्रवृद्ध्या शब्दयन्तमवसे रक्षणाय वसूयवो वसुकामाः सन्तः । पुनः कीदृशाः । गीर्भिः स्तुतिभी रण्वं रणयन्तं रमणीयं वा वसूयवो वसु हविरूपमन्नमग्नये प्रदातुमात्मन इच्छन्तो न्येरिरे । प्रीतो यथा धनं प्रयच्छति तथा हविरादिना प्राप्ता इत्यर्थः ॥

> *amumagniṃ hotāramāhvātāraṃ homaniṣpādakaṃ veḷate | ṛtvijaḥ stuvanti | tathā vasudhitiṃ dhanasya dhārayitāraṃ dātāraṃ vā ata eva priyaṃ sarveṣāṃ priyatamaṃ cetiṣṭhamatiśayena yajamānānāṃ cetayitāraṃ yadvā prakṛṣṭacetanavantam ‖ cetiśabdāttṛśchandasīṣṭhan | turiṣṭhemeyaḥsviti tṛlopaḥ ‖ aratimīśvaraṃ tādṛśaṃ devaṃ nyerire | nitarāṃ prāptāḥ | prāptireva viśeṣyate | havyavāhaṃ nyerire | niḥśeṣeṇa prāptāḥ | itaradevebhyo havyaṃ voḍhuṃ yathā prabhavati tathā nitarāṃ prāptāḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ viśvāyuṃ sarvatra prāṇijīvanaṃ viśvavedasaṃ sarvaprajñaṃ hotāraṃ devānāmāhvātāraṃ yajataṃ yajanīyaṃ kaviṃ sarvajñam ‖ īra preraṇe īra gatau [?] liṭ rūpam [?] ‖ kiṃca devāso devanaśīlā ṛtvijo raṇvamatipravṛddhyā śabdayantamavase rakṣaṇāya vasūyavo vasukāmāḥ santaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśāḥ | gīrbhiḥ stutibhī raṇvaṃ raṇayantaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ vā vasūyavo vasu havirūpamannamagnaye pradātumātmana icchanto nyerire | prīto yathā dhanaṃ prayacchati tathā havirādinā prāptā ityarthaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; a few small letters are doubtful ("*ṛtvijaḥ stuvanti*", the grammatical tail on *ira*, "*tuṣṭeme…*"): [?].)* Sense: "This Agni, the Hotṛ, the invoker, the accomplisher of the oblation, the priests praise (*īḷate*). Also *vasudhitim* — the holder or giver of wealth, therefore *priyam* — dearest of all; *cetiṣṭham* — that makes the sacrificers aware to the highest degree, or possessing excellent awareness; *aratim* — the lord; such a god they approach (*nyerire*) — completely reached; the reaching itself is qualified: *havyavāham nyerire* — thoroughly reached, as the one who is able to carry oblations to the other gods. Again what kind of one: *viśvāyum* — the life of creatures everywhere; *viśvavedasam* — all-knowing; *hotāram* — the invoker of the gods; *yajatam* — worthy of worship; *kavim* — omniscient. And the *devāsaḥ* — the playful priests — *raṇvam* (sounding loudly, with excess of vigour), for protection, desirous of wealth (*vasūyavaḥ*); *gīrbhiḥ* — with praises, the sounding (*raṇvam*) or delightful one — wishing to give Agni the wealth, the food in the form of oblations, they approach him: as one pleased gives wealth, so they have come with oblations and so on."

### Printed p. 361  (PDF 382)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 16 [as read: "೧೬"].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *hotā-m* — the invoker of the gods; *agnim* — Agni; *īḷate* — they praise; *vasudhitim* — the support of wealth (the giver of wealth); *priyam* — dear (to all); *cetiṣṭham* — endowed with great intelligence (who awakens the sacrificers); *aratim* — the lord, Agni; *ni erire* — approached; *havyavāham* — the bearer of oblations to the gods; *viśvāyum* — the life (in the form of life) of all creatures; *viśvavedasam* — the all-knowing; *hotāram* — the invoker of the gods (the accomplisher of the oblation); *yajatam* — to be worshipped (by sacrifices and the like); *kavim* — the knower of the three times; *ni erire* — they reached; *(kiṃ ca* — and); *devāsaḥ* — the priests given to worship; *raṇvam* — Agni, who sounds (blazing); *avase* — for the protection (of this sacrificer); *vasūyavaḥ* — desirous of wealth; *gīrbhiḥ* — with words of praise; *raṇvam* — the delightful; *vasūyavaḥ* — those desiring food in the form of oblations in order to offer it in Agni; *(nyerire* — reached).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** The priests praise Agni, who invokes the gods to the sacrificial place; the support of wealth (the giver of wealth), dear to all, the one who warns the sacrificers in the matter of the sacrifice, the lord, the life of all creatures, the all-knowing, the *hotṛ* (the accomplisher of the oblation, or the one who calls the gods), the one to be worshipped in the sacrifices, who knows the three times; the priests approached him; the priests, being devoted to worship, desirous of wealth for the protection of the sacrificer, and desiring the delightful food in the form of oblations by their praise-words, approached the blazing, sounding Agni.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"They, (the devout), praise Agni, the invoker (of the gods), the possessor of wealth, the beloved, the thoughtful; they have recourse to him as to a sovereign; they have recourse to him as the bearer of oblations; to him, who is the life (of all living beings), who knows all things, the offerer of oblations, the object of worship, the sage: the sacred (priests), desirous of affluence, murmur (his praises) to obtain his protection; desirous of affluence, they murmur (his praises) in their hymns."*

### Printed p. 362  (PDF 383)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 128".)*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 8).**

***hotāram īḷate*** — *homaniṣpādakam āhvātāraṃ vā*: "Agni accomplishes the oblation, or he calls the gods to accept the oblations offered as homa; the priests praise such an Agni."

***vasudhitim*** — *dhanasya dhārayitāraṃ dātāraṃ vā*: "Agni holds wealth, or gives wealth": so the meaning. The Niruktakāra says that the words *vasudhiti* and *vasudhī* do not convey different meanings; he explains *vasudhītī vasudhānyau — vasūnāṃ nidhānabhūte* ("in the form of a store of wealth": the support of riches) (Ni. 9-42 [?], as read "೯-೪೨").

***cetiṣṭham*** — *atiśayena yajamānānāṃ cetayitāraṃ yadvā prakṛṣṭacetanavantam*: "Agni grants great knowledge to the sacrificers; or he himself has great wisdom."

***havyavāhaṃ nyerire*** — *niḥśeṣeṇa prāptāḥ*: "Agni is able, with delight, to bear the oblations to the other gods; they serve such an Agni": so it is described.

***raṇvam*** — *atipravṛddhatayā śabdayantaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ vā*: "when he blazes well he makes a sound; or he is delightful."

***vasūyavaḥ*** — *vasukāmāḥ | vasu haviḥrūpam annam agnaye pradātum ātmana icchantaḥ*: "those who want wealth, or the sacrificers who wish to obtain from Agni abundant food in order to offer food in the form of oblations to Agni; the sacrificers who, having obtained plenty of food and wealth from Agni, satisfy Agni with oblations, so that Agni, content, may grant wealth, serve Agni in this way": so it is described. —

> कारुरहं ततो भिषगुपलप्रक्षिणी नना ।
> नानाधियो वसूयवोऽनु गा इव तस्थिमेन्द्रायेन्दो परि स्रव ॥

> *kārur ahaṃ tato bhiṣag upalaprakṣiṇī nanā |*
> *nānādhiyo vasūyavo 'nu gā iva tasthimendrāyendo pari srava ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-112-3, as printed.) Here *vasūyavaḥ* is explained as *vasukāmāḥ* (Ni. 6-[?]; as read "೬-೫"?). And —

> इन्द्रो अश्रायि सुध्यो निरेके पज्रेषु स्तोमो दुर्यो न यूपः ।
> अश्वयुर्गव्यू रथयुर्वसूयुरिन्द्र इद्रायः क्षयति प्रयन्ता ॥

> *indro aśrāyi sudhyo nireke pajreṣu stomo duryo na yūpaḥ |*
> *aśvayur gavyū rathayur vasūyur indra id rāyaḥ kṣayati prayantā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-14 [?], as read "೧-೩೧-೧೪"; the first line has doubtful letters in the print: [?].)

### Printed p. 363  (PDF 384)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 16 [as read].)*

In this Ṛk *vasūyuḥ* is explained as *vasumān*, "possessing wealth". From this the word *vasūyavaḥ* is explained as "those who desire wealth" or "those who possess wealth".

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as read).** *hotāram* — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *tṛn* in the agent sense; Vedic *saṃprasāraṇa* and *pūrvarūpa*; guṇa of *u* because of the suffix; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable; accusative singular. *īḷate* — root *īḍa stutau*, *adādi*; *laṭ* third person plural; *ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ* (Pā. 7-1-5) gives *at* for *jha*; *luk* for *śap*; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *vasudhitim* — *vasunaḥ dhitiḥ*; root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; by the power of *bahulagrahaṇa* the suffix *ktin* in the agent sense; the root takes *i*; *pūrvapadaprakṛtisvara*. *cetiṣṭham* — root *citī saṃjñāne*; *tṛc* in the agent sense; when *atiśayena cetayitā* is meant, *tuśchandasi* [as read: Pā. 5-3-59] gives *iṣṭhan* after its own kind; with *iṣṭhan* following, *turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu* (Pā. 6-4-154) drops *tṛc*; since *n*-marked, the acute on the first syllable. *aratim* — root *ṛ gatau*; the Uṇādi suffix *ati*; since *cit* is continued from the previous sūtra, the acute on the last syllable; accusative singular. *erire* — root *īra preraṇe* or *īr gatau*; *liṭ* third person plural; because it follows a non-finite word, *nighāta*. *havyavāham* — root *vah prāpaṇe*; *vahaś ca* (Pā. 3-2-64) gives *ṇi* [as read]; since *ṇ*-marked, *ata upadhāyāḥ* (Pā. 7-2-116) gives *vṛddhi* of the penult; everything drops in the suffix; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the accent of the latter member; accusative singular. *viśvavedasam* — *viśvaṃ vedo yasya saḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. 6-2-1) gives the accent of the first member. *yajatam* — root *yaja devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadāneṣu*; *bhṛmṛśiyajiparvi…* (Uṇ. 3-110) gives *atac*; *citaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the acute on the last syllable. *devāsaḥ* — *ājjasera suk* (Pā. 7-1-50) gives the augment *asuk* to *jas*. *raṇvam* — root *raṇa gatau*; *idito num dhātoḥ* gives *num*; suffix *k*; *aṭkupvāṅ…* gives *ṇ* for the *n*; acute on the last syllable by the accent of the suffix.

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *avase* — root *av rakṣaṇe*; Uṇādi *asun*; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable. *vasūyavaḥ* — *vasum ātmana icchantaḥ vasūyavaḥ*; *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. 3-1-8) gives *kyac*; *kyāc chandasi* (Pā. 3-2-170) gives *u* after the *kyac*-ending; *ato lopaḥ* drops the *a* of *kyac*; by the suffix's accent, the acute on the last syllable; nominative plural. ‖ 8 ‖

## Sūkta 129 — *yaṃ tvaṃ ratham indra* (begins on printed p. 364; Anuvāka 19, third Sūkta)

### Printed p. 364 (continued; PDF 385, lower part)

**ನೂರ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂಭತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra ippattoṃbhattaneya sūktavu** (the one hundred and twenty-ninth Sūkta).

**॥ सूक्तभूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, small type; read from the image; several letters doubtful [?]).**

> यं त्वं रथमित्येकादशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं पारुच्छेपं सर्वमात्यष्टमित्युक्तत्वादत्यष्टिच्छन्दस्कम् [?] । अनुक्तत्वादैन्द्रम् । प्रप्रा वो अस्मे इत्यादिके द्वे अतिशक्वर्यौ षष्ट्यक्षरोपेतत्वात् [?] । पाहि न इत्यन्त्याष्टिः चतुःषष्ट्यक्षरोपेतत्वात् । प्र तद्वोचेयमिति षष्ठीन्दुदेवत्या । तथा चानुक्रमणिका । यं त्वमेकादश षष्ठैन्दवी प्रप्रा वोऽतिशक्वर्यावष्टिरन्त्येति । दशरात्रस्य षष्ठेऽहनि मरुत्वतीये शस्त्र एतत्सूक्तं षष्ठस्येति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । यं त्वं रथमिन्द्र स यो वृषा । आ. ८-१ [?] इति ॥

> *yaṃ tvaṃ rathamityekādaśarcaṃ tṛtīyaṃ sūktaṃ pārucchepaṃ sarvamātyaṣṭamityuktatvādatyaṣṭicchandaskam [?] | anuktatvādaindram | praprā vo asme ityādike dve atiśakvaryau ṣaṣṭyakṣaropetatvāt [?] | pāhi na ityantyāṣṭiḥ catuḥṣaṣṭyakṣaropetatvāt | pra tadvoceyamiti ṣaṣṭhīndudevatyā | tathā cānukramaṇikā | yaṃ tvamekādaśa ṣaṣṭhaindavī praprā vo 'tiśakvaryāvaṣṭirantyeti | daśarātrasya ṣaṣṭhe 'hani marutvatīye śastra etatsūktaṃ ṣaṣṭhasyeti khaṇḍe sūtritam | yaṃ tvaṃ rathamindra sa yo vṛṣā | ā. 8-1 [?] iti ‖*

**Kannada anuvāda (translated).** *Anuvāda* — This Sūkta *yaṃ tvaṃ ratham* is the third Sūkta in the nineteenth Anuvāka. It has eleven ṛks. The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Paruccheṣa; since it is said that all the Sūktas seen by this ṛṣi are in the Atyaṣṭi metre, this Sūkta too is in the Atyaṣṭi metre. Of the two ṛks that begin *pra prā vo asme* (the eighth and ninth ṛks) there are sixty syllables each [as read], and so they have the metre Atiśakvarī; the last ṛk *pāhi na indra* has sixty-four syllables, so its metre is Aṣṭi; the sixth ṛk, *pra tad voceyam*, has Indu (Soma) for deity; Indra is the deity of the remaining ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "*yaṃ tvam ekādaśa ṣaṣṭhaindavī prapra vo 'tiśakvaryāv aṣṭir antyā*". On the sixth day of the *daśarātra* sacrifice this Sūkta is used in the *marutvatīya śastra*, as stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the section *ṣaṣṭhasya*: *yaṃ tvaṃ ratham indra sa yo vṛṣā* (Āś. 8-1 [?], as read "೮-೧-೧").

**ಸೂಕ್ತ—೧೨೯ — Sūkta 129.** *Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 19 ‖ Sūkta 129 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 1 ‖ Varga 16, 17 ‖ Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 11 ‖ Ṛṣi: Paruccheṣa Daivodāsi ‖ Devatā: Ṛks 1–5 and 7–11 Indra; Ṛk 6 Indu (Soma) ‖ Chandas: Ṛks 1–7 and 10 Atyaṣṭi; Ṛks 8, 9 Atiśakvarī; Ṛk 11 Aṣṭi.* *(Numerals of the ṛk-groups as printed; "೧-೭, ೧೦" for the Atyaṣṭi ṛks.)*

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यं त्वं रथमिन्द्र मेधसातयेऽपाका सन्तमिषिर प्रणयसि प्रानवद्य नयसि ।
> सद्यश्चित्तमभिष्टये करो वशश्च वाजिनम् ।
> सास्माकमनवद्य तूतुजान वेधसामिमां वाचं न वेधसाम् ॥ १ ॥

> *yaṃ tvaṃ rathamindra medhasātaye 'pākā santamiṣira praṇayasi prānavadya nayasi |*
> *sadyaścittamabhiṣṭaye karo vaśaśca vājinam |*
> *sāsmākamanavadya tūtujāna vedhasāmimāṃ vācaṃ na vedhasām ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यम् । त्वम् । रथम् । इन्द्र । मेधऽसातये । अपाका । सन्तम् । इषिर । प्रऽनयसि । प्र । अनवद्य । नयसि ।
> सद्यः । चित् । तम् । अभिष्टये । करः । वशः । च । वाजिनम् ।
> सः । अस्माकम् । अनवद्य । तूतुजान । वेधसाम् । इमाम् । वाचम् । न । वेधसाम् ॥ १ ॥

> *yam | tvam | ratham | indra | medha 'sātaye | apākā | santam | iṣira | pra 'nayasi | pra | anavadya | nayasi |*
> *sadyaḥ | cit | tam | abhiṣṭaye | karaḥ | vaśaḥ | ca | vājinam |*
> *saḥ | asmākam | anavadya | tūtujāna | vedhasām | imām | vācam | na | vedhasām ‖ 1 ‖*

*(Read from the image. The Saṃhitā prints *prānavadya* with a long *ā*; the Pada divides *pra-nayasi*, *pra*, *anavadya*, *nayasi*; and *medha-sātaye*.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्रेषिर यज्ञगमनशील त्वं मेधसातये यज्ञस्य दानाय लाभाय वा यं यजमानं प्रति रथं प्रणयसि प्रापयसि ॥ द्विकर्मकोऽयम् ॥ कीदृशं यजमानम् । अपाका अपाकमनल्पप्रज्ञयाधिकारवन्तम् । पाकः पक्वो भवतीति यास्कः ।

> *he indreṣira yajñagamanaśīla tvaṃ medhasātaye yajñasya dānāya lābhāya vā yaṃ yajamānaṃ prati rathaṃ praṇayasi prāpayasi ‖ dvikarmako 'yam ‖ kīdṛśaṃ yajamānam | apākā apākamanalpaprajñayādhikāravantam | pākaḥ pakvo bhavatīti yāskaḥ |*

*(Read from the image; the bhāṣya continues at the head of p. 366. "*indreṣira*" is printed as one word, i.e. *he indra iṣira*.)*

### Printed p. 366  (PDF 387)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 129".)*

> नि. ३-१२ [?] । अत एव सन्तं पण्डितं सन्तम् । किंच हे अनवद्यानिन्दित यं यजमानं धनविद्यादिना प्रणयसि प्रकृष्टं नयसि । तं यजमानं सद्यश्चित् तदानीमेव तदनुग्रहकाल एवाभिष्टये आभिमुख्येन यागायाभिमतप्राप्तये वा ॥ अभिपूर्वादिषेः क्रिन् । शकन्ध्वादित्वात्पररूपत्वम् [?] । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥ करः । समर्थं करोषि । लेटि व्यत्ययेन शप् ॥ एवं कृत्वा च वाजिनं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं तद्वन्तं वा वशः । कामयसे च । वष्टेर्लेट्यडागमः । तिङः परत्वान्निघातः ॥ यजमानेनाहूतः सन् शीघ्रमेवागत्य हविः स्वीकृत्य यागं साधु निर्वर्त्य तं चाभिमतफलेन संयोज्य पुनर्हविः करोषीत्यर्थः । हे इन्द्रानवद्यानिन्दित सर्वैः स्तूयमान तूतुजानात्मानमनुग्रहीतुं त्वरमाण ॥ तुजेः प्रेरणार्थात्कानच् । तुजादीनां दीर्घोऽभ्यासस्येत्यभ्यासस्य दीर्घत्वम् ॥ स त्वम् ॥ सोचि लोपे चेदिति संहितायां सोर्लोपः ॥ वेधसां विविधफलकर्तॄणां मध्ये श्रेष्ठतया वेधसां मेधाविनामस्माकं सम्बन्धि हविः स्वीकुर्वित्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । इमां वाचं नास्मदीयां स्तुतिरूपां वाचमिव । स्तुतिं यथा स्वीकरोषि तथा हविरपीत्यर्थः ॥

> *ni. 3-12 [?] | ata eva santaṃ paṇḍitaṃ santam | kiṃca he anavadyānindita yaṃ yajamānaṃ dhanavidyādinā praṇayasi prakṛṣṭaṃ nayasi | taṃ yajamānaṃ sadyaścit tadānīmeva tadanugrahakāla evābhiṣṭaye ābhimukhyena yāgāyābhimataprāptaye vā ‖ abhipūrvādiṣeḥ krin | śakandhvāditvātpararūpatvam [?] | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam ‖ karaḥ | samarthaṃ karoṣi | leṭi vyatyayena śap ‖ evaṃ kṛtvā ca vājinaṃ havirlakṣaṇamannaṃ tadvantaṃ vā vaśaḥ | kāmayase ca | vaṣṭerleṭyaḍāgamaḥ | tiṅaḥ paratvānnighātaḥ ‖ yajamānenāhūtaḥ san śīghramevāgatya haviḥ svīkṛtya yāgaṃ sādhu nirvartya taṃ cābhimataphalena saṃyojya punarhaviḥ karoṣītyarthaḥ | he indrānavadyānindita sarvaiḥ stūyamāna tūtujānātmānamanugrahītuṃ tvaramāṇa ‖ tujeḥ preraṇārthātkānac | tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasyetyabhyāsasya dīrghatvam ‖ sa tvam ‖ soci lope cediti saṃhitāyāṃ sorlopaḥ ‖ vedhasāṃ vividhaphalakartṝṇāṃ madhye śreṣṭhatayā vedhasāṃ medhāvināmasmākaṃ sambandhi haviḥ svīkurvityarthaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | imāṃ vācaṃ nāsmadīyāṃ stutirūpāṃ vācamiva | stutiṃ yathā svīkaroṣi tathā havirapītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; the Nirukta reference "३-१२" at the head is small and doubtful [?]; the grammar tail is characterized, not completed: *abhi + iṣ* with *kri*; the *pararūpa* by *śakandhvādi* [doubtful]; *tuj* with *kānac* and lengthening of the reduplicative; *so 'ci lope ced* — the loss of *sa*.)* Sense: "O Indra, *iṣira* — quick-going to the sacrifices — for the giving or obtaining of the sacrifice (*medhasātaye*) you drive your chariot to the sacrificer, who is *apākā* — of not small, i.e. mature, wisdom and fitness — (*pāka* = ripe, Yāska); therefore *santam* — learned; and, O blameless one, the sacrificer whom you *pra-nayasi*, lead forward with wealth and learning, him you at once (*sadyaś cit*), at the very time of favouring him, *abhiṣṭaye* — turning toward him, for the sacrifice or for the attainment of the desired; *karaḥ* — you make capable (*laṭ* by *vyatyaya*); having done so, you desire (*vaśaḥ*) the oblation-food or the one who has it. Called by the sacrificer, you come quickly, accept the oblation, complete the sacrifice well, unite him with the desired fruit, and again make an oblation… O blameless, praised by all, *tūtujāna* — hastening to favour us: you, as the best among the makers of various fruits (*vedhasām*), accept the oblation of us the wise, as you accept this our speech in praise."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *he indra* — O Indra; *iṣira* — whose nature is to go to sacrifices; *tvam* — you; *medhasātaye* — for the giving (obtaining) of the sacrifice; *apākā* — of mature knowledge, qualified; *santam* — wise; *yam* — whichever sacrificer; *ratham* — the chariot; *pra nayasi* — you drive (to him); *he anavadya* — O faultless (praised by all); *(yam* — whom); *pra nayasi* — you lead forward (with wealth and learning); *tam* — that sacrificer; *cit* — at once; *abhiṣṭaye* — to turn toward the sacrifice (for the attainment of the desired); *karaḥ* — you make able; *vājinam* — the food in the form of an oblation; *vaśaḥ ca* — you desire and desire; *anavadya* — O faultless; *tūtujāna* — eager to favour us; *saḥ* — you; *vedhasām* — (among) makers of various fruits (as best); *vedhasām* — of the wise; *asmākam* — our (oblation); *imām vācaṃ na* — as this praise; *(svīkuru* — accept).

### Printed p. 367  (PDF 388)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 17 [as read].)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha** *(its first lines are at the foot of p. 366, the end on p. 367).* O Indra, whose nature is to go to sacrifices: to the house of whichever sacrificer, mature in knowledge and learned, you drive your chariot; O faultless Indra, whomever you lead forward with wealth and learning — make that man at once able to obtain the fruit he desires, intent on the sacrifice; and you, faultless one, eager to favour me, accept our oblations, as you accept my praise, being the best among the givers of various fruits.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Indra, frequenter of sacrifices, quickly enable him to attain his desires, to whom you repair in your car to receive the oblation; and for whom, as he is mature (in understanding) and devout, you who are without fault, entertain regard. Accept his offering, for you who are without fault, are prompt to favour us (among) the pious (offerers of oblations), as (you accept) this our praise."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 1).**

***medhasātaye*** — *yajñasya dānāya lābhāya vā*: since the Niruktakāra gives the word *medha* the sense "sacrifice" (Ni. 3-19 [?], as read "೩-೧೯"), Sāyaṇa follows the same meaning: Indra drives his chariot to the sacrificial hall in order to complete the sacrificer's sacrifice, or to receive the oblations himself.

The Niruktakāra explains the word *indra* in many ways: *indra irāṃ dṛṇātīti vā* — "because he splits [the cloud and] sends rain, he makes the seeds of rice and the like sprout and shoot"; *irāṃ dadātīti vā* — "because he sends rain he gives food"; *irāṃ dadhātīti vā* — "he gives or holds food for creatures"; *irāṃ dhārayate, dārayate iti vā* (the sense is as above); *indave dravatīti vā* — "he hastens to the drinking of Soma"; *indau ramata iti vā* — "he delights in the drinking of Soma"; *indhe bhūtānīti vā* — "he kindles creatures", as said in the Brāhmaṇa sentence, "*tad yad enaṃ prāṇaiḥ samaindhaṃs tad indrasya indratvam iti vijñāyate*" ("because the gods kindled him with the vital breaths, that is the Indra-ness of Indra") — he is within creatures in the spiritual form, makes them brilliant and causes them to grow, or is the one made brilliant by the breaths. The Niruktakāra then gives other views: "*idaṃ karaṇād ity āgrāyaṇaḥ*" — the teacher Āgrāyaṇa says that he is Indra because he makes all this; "*idaṃ darśanād ity aupamanyavaḥ*" — Aupamanyava, the ṛṣi, says that he is Indra because he looks upon all this to protect it; "*indater aiśvaryakarmaṇaḥ*" — from *ind* in the sense "to be lord"; and "*indraḥ śatrūṇāṃ dārayitā vā drāvayitā vā ādārayitā*" — "Indra is the one who splits the enemies, or makes them run, or tears them apart". *(Read from the image; the Sanskrit of these Nirukta passages is in small Kannada type and is given as read, doubtful in places: [?]; the passage continues on p. 368.)*

### Printed p. 368  (PDF 389)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 129".)*

(Continuing the Nirukta etymologies of *indra*, from p. 367: "…*ādārayitā*" — one who tears apart: "he who splits the enemies, or makes them flee, honours those who perform the sacrifice": so they say.)

***apākā*** — *apākam analpaprajñayādhikāravantam*: "Indra, who is full of such greatness, shows his favour to the sacrificer who is very wise and fit for the sacrifice, bestowing wealth and knowledge on him and making him honourable": so the meaning. —

> यत्रा सुपर्णा अमृतस्य भागमनिमेषं विदथाभिस्वरन्ति ।
> इनो विश्वस्य भुवनस्य गोपाः स मा धीरः पाकमत्रा विवेश ॥

> *yatrā suparṇā amṛtasya bhāgam animeṣaṃ vidathābhisvaranti |*
> *ino viśvasya bhuvanasya gopāḥ sa mā dhīraḥ pākam atrā viveśa ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-21 [?], as read "೧-೧೬೪-೨೧"; small type.) Citing this Ṛk, Yāska explains *pākaḥ pakvo bhavati* (Ni. 3-12 [?]); Durgācārya says: "*pākaḥ pakvaprajñaḥ asamyagdarśī*" … *apakvaprajñaḥ* — "one who has not seen rightly, who has no right understanding", and *niruktaprajñaḥ samagradarśī sarvajñaḥ* — "the one who has perfect knowledge, who has seen everything, the all-knowing: he is called *vipakva*-minded"; so the meaning is stated. [Doubtful in the small print: [?].]

***abhiṣṭaye*** — *ābhimukhyena yāgāya abhimataprāptaye vā*: "Indra makes the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice capable of undertaking the sacrifice; or he makes the sacrificer, who is skilful in the rite by which he can obtain his wish, able to perform the sacrifice": so the meaning.

***vājinaṃ havirlakṣaṇam annaṃ tadvantaṃ vā vaśaḥ — kāmayase ca*** — "Indra, called by the sacrificer for the sacrifice, comes quickly to the sacrifice, accepts the oblation, shows favour so that the sacrifice is completed, and by fulfilling the desires the sacrificer wants, makes him eager to sacrifice again": so it is explained.

The word *vāja* is recorded among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯") and, as *vāje*, among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?], "೨-೯"). —

> हिरण्यस्तूपः सवितर्यथा त्वाङ्गिरसो जुह्वे वाजे अस्मिन् ।
> एवा त्वार्चन्नवसे वन्दमानः सोमस्येवांशुं प्रति जागराहम् ॥

> *hiraṇyastūpaḥ savitar yathā tvāṅgiraso juhve vāje asmin |*
> *evā tvārcann avase vandamānaḥ somasyevāṃśuṃ prati jāgarāham ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-149-5, as read "೧೦-೧೪೯-೫".) Here *vāje* is explained as *anne saṃskṛte haviṣi* — "in the prepared food, the oblation prepared for the sacrifice". And —

> पावका नः सरस्वती वाजेभिर्वाजिनीवती । यज्ञं वष्टु धियावसुः ॥

> *pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī vājebhir vājinīvatī | yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-10, as read "೧-೩-೧೦".) Here *vājebhir vājinīvatī* — "*annena haviṣā udakena vā tadvatī*", i.e. possessed of food, oblation, water — Durgācārya explains thus.

### Printed p. 369  (PDF 390)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 17 [as read].)*

***anavadya*** — *anindita sarvaiḥ stūyamāna*: "Indra, who is not a place of blame and is fit to be praised by all": so it is addressed.

***tūtujāna*** — *asmān anugrahītuṃ tvaramāṇa*: the word *tūtujāna* is recorded among the names of the quick (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೩-೯"): "Indra comes quickly where he must favour us who depend on him"; the form arises with a suffix after the root *tuj* in the sense of impelling.

The word ***vedhasām*** is used twice. The first *vedhasām* is explained as "among those able to produce many kinds of fruit", the second as "of the wise ones". "O Indra, accept the oblations we offer, we the wise": so he is prayed.

***imāṃ vācaṃ na*** — *asmadīyāṃ stutirūpāṃ vācam iva*: "as Indra accepts the words in which we praise him, so may he accept the oblations": so it is compared.

***vācam*** — the word *vāc* is recorded among the fifty-seven names of speech (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೧೧"); here the sense "praise" is given.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *medhasātaye* — *medhasya sātiḥ medhasātiḥ*; root *ṣaṇu dāne*, suffix *kriṇ*; *janasanakhanāṃ sañjhalośh* (Pā. 6-4-42) gives *ā* to the root; *pūrvapadaprakṛtisvara*; dative singular. *apākā* — *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. 7-1-39) gives *ā* in place of the ending. *santam* — root *as bhuvi*; *śatṛ* in the present sense; *śnasor allopaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-111) drops the *a*; acute on the first syllable of the suffix; accusative singular. *iṣira* — root *iṣa gatau*; Uṇādi *kirac* [as printed "*rak*"]; *āmantritasya ca* gives *nighāta*. *praṇayasi* — root *ṇīñ prāpaṇe*; this is a verb with two objects; *laṭ* second person singular; *upasargād asamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya* [as read] gives *ṇ* for the *n* of the root. *anavadya* — *na avadyaḥ anavadyaḥ*; vocative; *āmantrita-nighāta*. *abhiṣṭaye* — the root *iṣa* with the prefix *abhi*, suffix *kriṇ*; because of *s*, *ṣṭutva* for the *t*; when *abhi + iṣṭi*, by the vārttika *śakandhvādiṣu pararūpaṃ vācyam* the *pararūpa* occurs; *tāddau ca niti kṛtyatau* (Pā. 6-2-50) gives the prefix (*abhi*) its natural accent; dative singular.

### Printed p. 370  (PDF 391)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 129".)*

*(Grammar, continued.)* *karaḥ* — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *leṭ* second person singular, *sip*; *itaś ca lopaḥ* (Pā. 3-4-97) drops *i*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *luk* of *śap*; *āṭo 'ḍāṭau* [as read: *leṭo 'ḍāṭau*] gives the augment *aṭ*; because of the suffix guṇa of the root's *i* [i.e. *u*] with *raparatva*; since *cet* is connected, *nighāta* is forbidden (*nipātair yad yadi…*, Pā. 8-1-30); the suffix is *p*-marked so the root's accent remains. *vaśaḥ* — root *vaśa kāntau*, *adādi*; as in *karaḥ*, the augment *aṭ* in the *leṭ*, loss of *i*; since it follows a finite verb there is no *nighāta*; the accent of the root remains. *vājinam* — *vājo 'syāsti iti vājī*; *ata iniṭhanau* (Pā. 5-2-115) gives *ini* in the possessive sense; by the suffix's accent the *ī* is acute. *tūtujāna* — root *tuja preraṇe*; when *liṭ* follows, *liṭaḥ kānajvā* gives *kānac*; because of it the root is doubled; *tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya* lengthens the reduplicative; in the vocative *āmantrita-nighāta*. *vācam* — root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; *kvip vaci…* [Pā. 3-2-[?]] gives *kvip*; lengthening. ‖ 1 ‖

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स श्रुधि यः स्मा पृतनासु कासु चिद्दक्षाय्य इन्द्र भरहूतये नृभिरसि प्रतूर्तये नृभिः ।
> यः शूरैः स्वः सनिता यो विप्रैर्वाजं तरुता ।
> तमीशानास इरधन्त वाजिनं पृक्षमत्यं न वाजिनम् ॥ २ ॥

> *sa śrudhi yaḥ smā pṛtanāsu kāsu ciddakṣāyya indra bharahūtaye nṛbhirasi pratūrtaye nṛbhiḥ |*
> *yaḥ śūraiḥ svaḥ sanitā yo viprairvājaṃ tarutā |*
> *tamīśānāsa iradhanta vājinaṃ pṛkṣamatyaṃ na vājinam ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । श्रुधि । यः । स्म । पृतनासु । कासु । चित् । दक्षाय्यः । इन्द्र । भरऽहूतये । नृऽभिः । असि । प्रऽतूर्तये । नृऽभिः ।
> यः । शूरैः । स्वरिति स्वः । सऽनिता । यः । विप्रैः । वाजम् । तरुता ।
> तम् । ईशानासः । इरधन्त । वाजिनम् । पृक्षम् । अत्यम् । न । वाजिनम् ॥ २ ॥

> *saḥ | śrudhi | yaḥ | sma | pṛtanāsu | kāsu | cit | dakṣāyyaḥ | indra | bhara 'hūtaye | nṛ 'bhiḥ | asi | pra 'tūrtaye | nṛ 'bhiḥ |*
> *yaḥ | śūraiḥ | svariti svaḥ | sa 'nitā | yaḥ | vipraiḥ | vājam | tarutā |*
> *tam | īśānāsaḥ | iradhanta | vājinam | pṛkṣam | atyam | na | vājinam ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(small type; read from the image, many letters doubtful: [?]).*

> हे इन्द्र स वक्ष्यमाणगुणविशिष्टस्त्वं श्रुधि । अस्माकमाह्वानं स्तोत्रं वा शृणु ॥ हेर्धिभावः ॥ यः स्म यः खलु त्वं नृभिर्मनुष्यैरेव सद्भिः पश्चाद्देवैर्मरुद्भिः [?] । पुनस्त एव विशेष्यन्ते । नृभिः सङ्ग्रामनयनशीलैः । इन्द्रस्य मरुतां साहाय्यमिन्द्रो मरुद्भिः । तै. सं. २-३-१-१ [?] । मरुतो ह्येनं वाजहुः । ऐ. ब्रा. २-२० [?] इत्यादिषु प्रसिद्धम् । तैः सहितः सन् कासु चित्पृतनासु सर्वासु प्रवृत्तासु सङ्ग्रामेषु भरहूतये भरणहविष्प्राह्वानायुक्ताय प्रतूर्तये प्रकृष्टहिंसनाय । यद्वा । भरहूतये शूरो भव प्रहरेत्येवमादिभरणयुक्ताह्वानाय च शूराणां प्रकृष्टवधाय च । दक्षाय्योऽसि प्रवर्धनशीलोऽसि । यद्वा । नृभिर्नेतृभिर्यजमानैः प्रार्थितः सन् प्रतूर्तये शत्रूणां प्रकृष्टहिंसनाय दक्षाय्योऽसि समर्थोऽसि । किंच यस्त्वं शूरैः शौर्योपेतैर्मरुद्भिर्नृभिर्भर्तृभिः सहितः सन् स्वः स्वयमेव सनिता सङ्ग्रामयस्य [?] अस्यान्यस्य वा मनीषितस्य सनिता सम्भक्तासि [?] । सत्स्वपि तेषां साहित्येऽन्यैरनपेक्ष्येव [?] । तरुतासीत्यर्थः । तरतेस्तृनि ग्रसितस्कभितेति वा निपात्यते ॥ यस्त्वं विप्रैर्मेधाविभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः स्तुतः सन् वाजं तरुता तेभ्यो ऽन्नस्य दातासि । विप्रैर्मरुद्भिः सहित इति सम्बन्धः । तं तादृशं वाजिनं गमनवन्तं पृक्षं हविर्लक्षणान्नवन्तमिन्द्रमीशानासः सम्यग्गभ्यर्थयितुं समर्था ऋत्विज इरधन्त । संराधयन्ति । सेवन्ते । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वाजिनं वेजनवन्तं गमनवन्तं पृक्षं घासाद्यन्नवन्तमत्यं न नाश्वमिव । तं यथा समर्थाः स्वादुघासप्रदानादिना पोषयन्ति तद्वत् ॥ अत्य इत्यश्वनाम अत्यो हय इति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥

> *he indra sa vakṣyamāṇaguṇaviśiṣṭastvaṃ śrudhi | asmākamāhvānaṃ stotraṃ vā śṛṇu ‖ herdhibhāvaḥ ‖ yaḥ sma yaḥ khalu tvaṃ nṛbhirmanuṣyaireva sadbhiḥ paścāddevairmarudbhiḥ [?] | punasta eva viśeṣyante | nṛbhiḥ saṅgrāmanayanaśīlaiḥ | indrasya marutāṃ sāhāyyamindro marudbhiḥ | tai. saṃ. 2-3-1-1 [?] | maruto hyenaṃ vājahuḥ | ai. brā. 2-20 [?] ityādiṣu prasiddham | taiḥ sahitaḥ san kāsu citpṛtanāsu sarvāsu pravṛttāsu saṅgrāmeṣu bharahūtaye bharaṇahaviṣprāhvānāyuktāya pratūrtaye prakṛṣṭahiṃsanāya | yadvā | bharahūtaye śūro bhava praharetyevamādibharaṇayuktāhvānāya ca śūrāṇāṃ prakṛṣṭavadhāya ca | dakṣāyyo 'si pravardhanaśīlo 'si | yadvā | nṛbhirnetṛbhiryajamānaiḥ prārthitaḥ san pratūrtaye śatrūṇāṃ prakṛṣṭahiṃsanāya dakṣāyyo 'si samartho 'si | kiṃca yastvaṃ śūraiḥ śauryopetairmarudbhirnṛbhirbhartṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ san svaḥ svayameva sanitā saṅgrāmayasya [?] asyānyasya vā manīṣitasya sanitā sambhaktāsi [?] | satsvapi teṣāṃ sāhitye 'nyairanapekṣyeva [?] | tarutāsītyarthaḥ | taratestṛni grasitaskabhiteti vā nipātyate ‖ yastvaṃ viprairmedhāvibhirṛtvigbhiḥ stutaḥ san vājaṃ tarutā tebhyo 'nnasya dātāsi | viprairmarudbhiḥ sahita iti sambandhaḥ | taṃ tādṛśaṃ vājinaṃ gamanavantaṃ pṛkṣaṃ havirlakṣaṇānnavantamindramīśānāsaḥ samyaggabhyarthayituṃ samarthā ṛtvija iradhanta | saṃrādhayanti | sevante | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vājinaṃ vejanavantaṃ gamanavantaṃ pṛkṣaṃ ghāsādyannavantamatyaṃ na nāśvamiva | taṃ yathā samarthāḥ svādughāsapradānādinā poṣayanti tadvat ‖ atya ityaśvanāma atyo haya iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt ‖*

*(Sense. "O Indra, such as is described, hear (*śrudhi*; the *hi* becomes *dhi*) our invocation or praise. You, who with men — *nṛbhiḥ* — in whatever battles, and afterwards with the gods, the Maruts [?] — the leaders of battle, the Maruts, helpers of Indra — 'Indra with the Maruts' (Tai. Saṃ. [?], Ait. Br. [?]: 'the Maruts called him to the contest') — in all engagements, for the call to battle (*bharahūti*) and for the great slaying (*pratūrti*) of the enemies, you are *dakṣāyya* — of growing power; or, asked by the sacrificers, the leaders, you are able to slay foes greatly. And you who, together with the heroic Maruts, are the winner (*sanitā*) of heaven and of what is desired — *tarutā* — are the giver of food (*vājam*) to the sages, the priests praising you: that Indra, swift, with food (*pṛkṣam*) in the form of oblation, the lords (*īśānāsaḥ*), the priests able to seek well, serve (*iradhanta*); as people nourish a swift horse (*atyam*) with sweet fodder: 'the word *atya* is a name for horse', since it is read among those names." The grammar tail on *tarutā*, *hedhibhāva*, etc., is only characterized.)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (begins at the foot of p. 371).** *indra* — O Indra; *saḥ* — you, of the qualities stated; *śrudhi* — hear (our praise) or (pardon our invocation); *yaḥ sma* — you who; *nṛbhiḥ* — with men [the print continues on p. 372].

### Printed p. 372  (PDF 393)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 129".)*

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 2, continued from p. 371:)* "…*nṛbhiḥ* — with men; being men first, then having obtained divinity [i.e. the Maruts]; *nṛbhiḥ* — with the leaders (in battle), the Maruts; *kāsu cit pṛtanāsu* — in various battles; *bharahūtaye* — with cries of encouragement (calling to battle); *pratūrtaye* — for the very great slaying (of enemies); *dakṣāyyaḥ asi* — you are capable [for encouraging the call, and for slaying the enemies]; or, *nṛbhiḥ* — being prayed to by the sacrificers; *pratūrtaye* — to destroy enemies or sins; *dakṣāyyaḥ asi* — you are capable; *(kiṃ ca* — and); *yaḥ (tvam)* — you who; *śūraiḥ* — with the brave (Maruts or other warriors), *svaḥ* — by yourself; *sanitā* — can give victory in battle or other desired things; *yaḥ (tvam)* — you who; *vipraiḥ* — praised by the wise priests, or endowed with the wise Maruts; *vājam* — food (to those priests); *tarutā* — can give; *tam* — such; *vājinam* — swift; *pṛkṣam* — possessed of food in the form of oblation, Indra; *īśānāsaḥ* — the priests able in prayer; *vājinam* — swift (and possessed of fodder, grass and so on); *atyam* — a horse; *na* — as (people able to) nourish; *iradhanta* — worship (serve)."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, hear our praise (grant our invocation): you, first men and afterwards gods, are able to destroy the enemies through the encouraging cries made by the Maruts, the leaders of battle; accompanied by the brave (the Maruts or warriors), or yourself, without the help of others, giving victory in battle; prayed to by the wise priests, giving them food; such you, endowed with these qualities, going to sacrifices, giver of food in the form of oblations — the priests skilled in prayer serve, as brave men tend a swift horse with grass and the like.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Hear our invocation, Indra: you, who in various battles (associated with the Maruts, are animated through their encouragement; (and are able), with the Maruts, to destroy (your foes): (for you are) he, who, (aided) by heroes, are of yourself the giver (of victory); or, (when praised) by the pious, the giver of food, and whom the lords (of prayer) celebrate, as swift-moving and eager (for sacrificial food), like a fleet courser (eager for forage)."* *(The printed parentheses are unbalanced here, as printed.)*

### Printed p. 373  (PDF 394)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 17 [as read].)*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 2).**

***nṛbhiḥ*** — *manuṣyair eva sadbhiḥ paścāt devatvam āpannair marudbhiḥ*; *nṛbhiḥ — saṅgrāmanayanaśīlaiḥ*: "Indra's help from the Maruts; 'Indra with the Maruts' (Tai. Saṃ. 6-5-5-1 [?], as read; numerals doubtful); 'for the Maruts called him to the contest' (Ait. Br. 3-20 [?])" — thus well known. The word *nara* is recorded among the names of horse (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೨೭") and among the names of man (Ni. 3-[?], "೩-೭"). So Indra is with the Maruts — the groups of gods who, though they were men, performed the sacrifice and obtained, as its fruit, the state of gods; or, he grows in company of the groups of gods who help him in fighting: so the meaning. That the Maruts help Indra is well known from the Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence "*indro marudbhiḥ*" and the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence "*maruto hainaṃ vājahuḥ*" [as read: *vāja-*, doubtful].

***pṛtanāsu bharahūtaye pratūrtaye dakṣāyyaḥ*** — *sarvāsu prauḍhāsv api saṅgrāmeṣu bharaṇaviśiṣṭāhvānayuktāya prakṛṣṭahiṃsanāya | yadvā śūro bhava prahara ity evamādi bharaṇayuktāhvānāya śūrāṇāṃ prakṛṣṭavadhāya ca pravardhanaśīlaḥ asi*: one meaning is that in the places where fierce battles go on, Indra is called by the others, "protect us, kill the enemies"; in another sense: "O Indra, be brave, subdue the enemies" — to the call of all the brave soldiers worthy of protection and for the great slaying of the enemies Indra, competent, is by nature one who grows. For *nṛbhiḥ pṛtanāsu* Sāyaṇa gives another meaning: "following the prayer of the sacrificer, Indra is able to subdue enemies and evil-doers": thus Indra's greatness is described.

Following the explanation of the word *indra* given by Yāska, Durgācārya says, "*irādāro 'ndra iti parokṣeṇocyate*" [reading doubtful: [?]]: though Indra does not show his form directly, he is recognized by his work. In all words that name deities, though the several deities are the thing denoted, they remain unseen to those who serve them and accomplish their respective works; and the deities hide their own true forms and greatness: "*parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ pratyakṣadviṣaḥ*" (as read) — "the gods are, as it were, fond of the unseen and averse to the seen"; for this reason the gods are not willing to show themselves in their own visible form; the Śruti also says their attachment is greater to the unseen. The wise, knowing this secret of the gods, from the derivations of the words that denote the deities,

### Printed p. 374  (PDF 395)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 129".)*

learn well the nature, qualities, greatness and works of the several deities, serve them, meditate on them, and by identification with them accomplish their respective desires. From this, all deities have both an inner (*ādhyātmika*) and a divine (*ādhidaivata*) form; Yāska describes how these become manifest to the worshippers of the several deities. Indra too, being very powerful in this matter, performs protection and the like: so his nature and greatness are described.

***yaḥ śūraiḥ svaḥ sanitā tarutā*** — "Indra, accompanied by the heroic Maruts or by other soldiers, accomplishes his desire, either himself in battle or in some other way. Though there may be much help to assist him, he does not depend on it but, by his greatness, can accomplish the works alone": so the meaning is stated.

***vipraiḥ vājaṃ tarutā*** — *medhāvibhir ṛtvigbhiḥ stutaḥ sann tebhyo 'nnasya dātāsi | vipraiḥ marudbhiḥ iti sambandhaḥ*: the word *vipra* is recorded among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19 [?]). By repeating the word *vipraiḥ* he gives one meaning "by the wise priests" and another "by the Maruts": Indra, accompanied by the Marut gods and praised by the priests, gives food to the priests: so it is described.

***pṛkṣaṃ havirlakṣaṇānnavantam indram*** — the word *pṛkṣa* is recorded among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?], "೨-೯"); used as an epithet of Indra: "Indra is the possessor of food in the form of oblations."

***atyaṃ na*** — *aśvam iva*: the word *atya* is recorded among the names of horse (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೨೨"). The word *na* is recorded among the particles of comparison; in "*nendraṃ devam amaṃsata*" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3 [?], numerals unreadable) it is used in the sense of negation, and in —

> हृत्सु पीतासो युध्यन्ते दुर्मदासो न सुरायाम् ।
> ऊधर्न नग्ना जरन्ते ॥

> *hṛtsu pītāso yudhyante durmadāso na surāyām |*
> *ūdhar na nagnā jarante ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-2-12, as printed "೮-೨-೧೨".) in the sense of comparison, as Yāska explains; so in *atyaṃ na* the word *na* is a particle of comparison: "like a horse".

***vājinaṃ pṛkṣam atyaṃ na*** — *vejanavantaṃ ghāsādyannavantam aśvam iva*: this sentence is used as an illustration (*upamāna-vākya*) for the sentence *vājinaṃ pṛkṣam īśānāsaḥ*: as people in the world nourish a swift horse by giving it palatable grass, so the priests able to serve Indra, who moves with food in the form of oblation, serve him: so it is compared. Since this usage is in the Veda, there is no room for the charge that it is a base comparison.

### Printed p. 375  (PDF 396)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 17 [as read].)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *śrudhi* — root *śru śravaṇe*; *loṭ* second person singular; the *hi* by *śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi* (Pā. 6-4-102) becomes *dhi*; by the Vedic *luk* the *śnu*-suffix is dropped; *tiṅ-nighāta* since it follows a finite word. *sma* — *nipātasya ca* (Pā. 6-3-136) gives the long vowel in the Saṃhitā. *dakṣāyyaḥ* — root *dakṣa vṛddhau*; Uṇādi *āyyac* (Uṇ. 3-[?]); the acute on the first syllable of the suffix. *bharahūtaye* — *bharo hūtir yasyāṃ sā bharahūtiḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* gives the accent of the first member; dative singular. *pratūrtaye* — root *turvī hiṃsāyām*; *striyāṃ ktin* gives *ktin*; *upadhāyāś ca* (Pā. 7-1-101) lengthens *u*; where *lopo vyor vali* would drop the *v*, *rāllopaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-21) prevents it; *tāddau ca niti* (Pā. 6-2-50) gives the prefix (*pra*) its natural accent. *śūraiḥ* — *śū* is a sautra root; root *śū gatau*; *kuśīsyamīnāṃ…* (Uṇ. 2-[?]) gives *ran*, lengthening; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable. *svaḥ* — *svar* becomes *svarit* (Phiṭ-sūtra 4 [as read]). *sanitā* — root *ṣaṇa sambhaktau*; *tṛn* in the agent sense, with the augment *iṭ*; the acute on the first syllable. *tarutā* — root *tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ*; *tṛn* in the agent sense, *grasitaskabhita…* (Pā. 6-2-[?]) gives the irregular form *tarutṛ*. *īśānāsaḥ* — root *īśa aiśvarye*; *śānac* in the present sense; *citaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the acute on the last syllable; with *jas* following, *ājjaser asuk* (Pā. 7-1-50) gives the augment *asuk*.
