> *cidetyantaṃ kutsitaṃ hiṃsantamapi śatruṃ ririṣeḥ | bādhasva ‖ riṣa hiṃsāyām | chāndasaḥ śap śluḥ | punarvyatyayena śaḥ | ririkṣantam | asmādeva sani halantācceti sanaḥ kidbhāvaḥ [?] | cidityakutsitaḥ [?] | kulmāṣāṅki [?] … iti yāskenoktatvāt | ni. 1-4 [?] | yadvā | samuccayārthaḥ | kaṃcidityena saha samuccīyate ‖*

*(Read from the image; the clauses on *adrivaḥ* and on *ririkṣantam* are small and in parts illegible: I give them as read with [?]. Sense: "O Indra, bring us across [calamity] with wealth that is *tarūṣasā* — skilled in carrying across, able to take us across distress — you be [the one that gives it]. O Indra, you, the fierce (*ugra*), of mighty strength, this greatness of yours, produced by praise-hymns, *sakṣat* — serves you, i.e. exalts you. For what? for *avase* — for pleasing: example: *mahe avase mitraṃ na* — as the sun, the friend of all people, whose form is light and so on, for the great protection (*mahe avase*): as they join him to greatness, so; or like a friend who is dear and beneficial, as they approach him with delight in greatness. And O most mighty (*ojiṣṭha*) protector (*trātaḥ*), O immortal Indra, satisfying us by protection, mount a swift chariot and come quickly to our place of worship. O *adrivaḥ* — possessing the thunderbolt — harass (*ririșeḥ*) any other than us; O *adrivaḥ* — devourer of enemies — harass any enemy (small or great) who wishes to hurt us (*ririkṣantam*) even if base (*cit*)…")*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he indra* — O Indra); *tvam* — you; *naḥ* — us; *tarūṣasā* — able to carry us over calamities; *rāyā* — with wealth (supply us); *ugram* — fierce; *tvā cit* — you yourself; *mahinā* — by greatness (produced by our praises); *mahe* — great; *avase* — for pleasing (for health and the like, for the sake of affection); *mitram na* — like the Sun (the friend); *avase* — for your pleasure; *sakṣat* — serves; *(kiṃ ca* — and); *ojiṣṭha* — most mighty; *trātaḥ* — protector; *amartya* — immortal, O Indra; *avitaḥ* [as printed: *avite*] — you who gratify (us with wealth and the like); *kaṃ cit ratham* — any chariot; *(ārohya* — mounting); *adrivaḥ* — O destroyer (devourer) of enemies; *indra* — O Indra; *asmat* — us; *anyam ririkṣantam cit* — any other who wishes to harm; *ririṣeḥ* — harass; *he adrivaḥ* — O mountain-wielder; *kaṃ cit* — any (harmful) one; *(ririṣeḥ* — harass: *bādhasva*).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, raise us with wealth that is able to remove calamities (the greatness that arises from our praise); we serve you, the fierce, for health and the like, with affection, as we serve the Sun, our friend, for great well-being; O mightiest, protector, immortal one, gratifying us with wealth and the like — mount any swift chariot and come to our place of sacrifice; and likewise destroy whoever else, other than us, wishes to harm us. O Indra, O wielder of the mountain, destroy our enemies.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; begins at the foot of p. 409):** *"Indra, (sustain us) with wealth that transports (man beyond calamity); for, (enhanced) greatness accrues to you, however mighty (from our thanks) for (your) protection, as it does to Mitra for his powerful,"* [continues on p. 410]

### Printed p. 410  (PDF 431)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 129".)*

**Printed English (continued, Ṛk 10):** *"…protection, most potent and immortal (Indra) our defender and preserver, (ascend) some chariot, (and come hither): devourer (of foes), repel any one assailing us; any one assailing us, devourer (of foes)."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 10).**

***tarūṣasā*** — *taraṇakuśalena asmān āpadbhya uttārayituṃ śaktena*: "Indra is prayed to favour and protect us with wealth, with strength able to protect us from calamities."

***ugraṃ cit mahinā sakṣat*** — *udgūrṇabalam asmat stotrajanitaḥ kaścid atiśayaḥ utkarṣayati*: "By abundant strength, a certain growth, produced by the praises that the sacrificers recite at the sacrifice offered to the all-pervading Indra, raises him": so the meaning.

***avase*** — the word is read twice. For the first *avase* the meaning is "for Indra's pleasure"; for the second, "the protection in the form of splendour and health that Indra grants the sacrificers".

***mitraṃ na*** — *sarvajanamitraṃ sūryam iva*: "as people, in order to grow, praise the greatness of the Sun, who is venerable to all": one meaning; and, as people serve a friend who always does what is dear and good: so the second; Indra is compared to be one filled with greatness. Even though Mitra has nothing to gain from it, in doing good to others he is the dwelling-place of surpassing love, is the sense.

***ojiṣṭha*** — *atiśayena ojasvitama balavān*: the word *ojas* is recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೩೪") and of strength (Ni. 2-[?]; "೨-೯"). Indra is addressed as "very strong".

***adrivaḥ*** — this word is repeated. For the first *adrivaḥ* the meaning is "destroyer of enemies in excess"; for the second, *adrer ādartṛbhakṣakaḥ vā śatrūṇām* ("the devourer of the enemies, or the tearer"). The word *adri* is recorded among the names of cloud (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೩-೧೦"), and *adrivān* is explained by Yāska as *adrir ādṛṇāter ātteḥ [?] api vātreyī syāt* (Ni. 4-4 [?]), i.e. from *ā-dṝ* (to split) or from *ad* (to eat); the cloud (*adri*) is split or struck by him; or it is derived from destruction. Indra is described as having such strength that he repels even the enemy who harms by many wicked means, so as to repel our enemies, the performers of sacrifice.

### Printed p. 411  (PDF 432)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 18 [as read].)*

***cit*** — this (preposition-like) indeclinable is explained by the Niruktakāra: *cid ity eṣo 'nekakarmā | cit* (Ni. 1-4 [?]) — that it conveys many kinds of meaning. *ācāryaḥ kṣīdiṃ [?] bruyāt* — in this example the word *cit* denotes the greatness of the teacher and is used in the sense of "reverence" (*pūjāyām*); and in *dadhi cit* (a curd-like food) it is used in the sense of comparison (*upamā*); and in *kulmāṣān kṣīdā harety evaṃ kutsite* [as read, doubtful: [?]] in this sentence *cit* is used in the sense of "abuse, base". Sāyaṇa explains: *cit* is a particle (*cidityakutsitaḥ* [?]); the word *cit* conveys the sense of "very blameworthy", or *samuccayārthaḥ* — "it conveys the sense of 'also'".

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *tarūṣasā* — root *tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ*; Uṇādi *usin*; *ñnityādir nityam* (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the acute on the first syllable; lengthening is Vedic; instrumental singular. *ugram* — root *uca samavāye*; *ujjer ndra* [as read; Uṇ. 2-[?]] gives *ran*; by *vyatyaya* the acute on the last syllable. *mahinā* — the stem *mahat*; in the abstract sense the suffix *imanic*; *ṭi* drops; *citaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the acute on the last syllable; nominative singular. *sakṣat* — root *saha marṣaṇe*; *itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pā. 3-4-97) drops the *i* of the suffix; *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* gives the augment *aṭ*; *sibbahulaṃ leṭi* (Pā. 3-1-34) gives *sip*; *h* of the root becomes *ḍh*, *k*, *ṣ*; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *ojiṣṭha* — *ojo 'sya asti iti ojasvī*; since *asun* ends it, the suffix *vini*; then, for excess, *iṣṭhan*; *vinmator luk* (Pā. 5-3-65) drops *vin*; *ṭeḥ* (Pā. 6-4-155) drops *as*; by *nityādi* the acute on the first syllable; at the beginning of the *pāda*, there is no *āmantrita-nighāta*; *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. 6-1-198) gives the acute on the first syllable. *trātaḥ* — root *trai pālane*; *tṛn* in the agent sense; *ādeca upadeśe 'śiti* (Pā. 6-1-45) gives *ā* to the root; in the vocative *trātaḥ*;

### Printed p. 412  (PDF 433)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 129".)*

*(Grammar, continued.)* since by *āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat* the preceding word is as if not present, there is no *āmantrita-nighāta*; the acute on the first syllable, as in the earlier. *avitā* — root *ava rakṣaṇe*; *tṛc* as before; the augment *iṭ*; accent as before. *riṣeḥ* — root *riṣa hiṃsāyām*; *liṭ* second person singular, *sip*; *itaś ca* drops *i*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *śap*… *ślau* (Pā. 6-1-10) gives doubling of the root; again by *vyatyaya* the *vikaraṇa* [as read]; since *p*-marked, no guṇa of the penult; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *adrivaḥ* — *adriḥ vajram*; when "he who has it" is meant, the suffix *matup*; after the *a*-ending it comes after *i*, so *chandasīraḥ* (Pā. 8-2-15) gives *va* for the *m* of *matup*; in the vocative singular *ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ* (Pā. 7-1-70) gives *num*; *hal ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal* (Pā. 6-1-68) drops *s*; *saṃyogāntalopa* drops the *t*; *matuvasoru sambuddhau chandasi* (Pā. 8-3-1) gives *ru*; *āmantritasya ca* gives *nighāta*. *ririkṣantam* — root *riṣa hiṃsāyām*; *san* in the sense of desire; since *san* follows a root ending in a consonant, *halantāc ca* (Pā. 1-2-10) makes it *kit*; because of *san* the root is doubled; *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si* (Pā. 8-2-41) gives *k*; because of that *ṣatva* of the *s* of *san*; after the *san*-ending the suffix *śatṛ* in the present sense; accusative singular; *abhyastānām ādiḥ* (Pā. 6-1-189) gives the acute on the first syllable. ‖ 10 ‖

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पाहि न इन्द्र सुष्टुत स्रिधोऽवयाता सदमिद्दुर्मतीनां देवः सन्दुर्मतीनाम् ।
> हन्ता पापस्य रक्षसस्त्राता विप्रस्य मावतः ।
> अधा हि त्वा जनिता जीजनद्वसो रक्षोहणं त्वा जीजनद्वसो ॥ ११ ॥

> *pāhi na indra suṣṭuta sridho 'vayātā sadamiddurmatīnāṃ devaḥ sandurmatīnām |*
> *hantā pāpasya rakṣasastrātā viprasya māvataḥ |*
> *adhā hi tvā janitā jījanadvaso rakṣohaṇaṃ tvā jījanadvaso ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पाहि । नः । इन्द्र । सुऽस्तुत । स्रिधः । अवऽयाता । सदम् । इत् । दुःऽमतीनाम् । देवः ।
> सन् । दुःऽमतीनाम् ।
> हन्ता । पापस्य । रक्षसः । त्राता । विप्रस्य । मावतः ।
> अध । हि । त्वा । जनिता । जीजनत् । वसो इति । रक्षःऽहनम् । त्वा । जीजनत् । वसो इति ॥ ११ ॥

> *pāhi | naḥ | indra | su 'stuta | sridhaḥ | ava 'yātā | sadam | it | duḥ 'matīnām | devaḥ |*

> *hantā | pāpasya | rakṣasaḥ | trātā | viprasya | māvataḥ |*
> *adha | hi | tvā | janitā | jījanat | vaso iti | rakṣaḥ 'hanam | tvā | jījanat | vaso iti ‖ 11 ‖*

*(Read from the image: *su-stuta*, *ava-yātā* [print "avyayātā"?, doubtful: [?]], *duḥ-matīnām*, *rakṣaḥ-hanam*; *vaso iti* twice.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र सुष्टुत शोभनस्तुत त्वं स्रिधो दुःखात् तदुत्पादकात्पापाद्वा नोऽस्मान्पाहि । रक्ष । यतस्त्वं दुर्मतीनां दुर्मनस्कानां रक्षःप्रभृतीनाम् ॥ नामन्यतरस्यामिति नाम उदात्तत्वम् ॥ सदमित् सर्वदैवावयाता अपयायितापायिता [?] असि । अतः पाहि । अत एव हे इन्द्र देवो द्योतमानः सन् त्वं दुर्मतीनां दुष्टमनस्कानां यज्ञविघातकानामवयातासि [?] । तथा रक्षसः रक्षणनिमित्तभूतस्य । रक्षो रक्षितव्यमस्मादिति यास्कः । नि. ४-१८ [?] । तादृशस्य पापस्य फलप्रतिबन्धरूपस्य हन्ता घातकोऽसि । यद्वा । पापस्य पापिनो रक्षसो राक्षसादेर्हन्तासि । तथा मावतो मत्सदृशस्य विप्रस्य मेधाविनो यजमानस्य त्राता रक्षकोऽसि । अधातो हेतोर्हे इन्द्र वसो सर्वेषां निवासभूत त्वा त्वां जनिता सर्वस्य जनयिता कर्ता परमेश्वरो जीजनत् । अजनयत् । उत्पादितवान् । तथा हे वसो नासयितः [?] त्वा त्वां रक्षोहणं जीजनत् । रक्षोहननायोत्पादितवान् । जनयतेर्लुङि चङि रूपम् ॥ यज्ञादिविघातिनां रक्षःप्रभृतीनां विघाताय हीन्द्रस्यावतारः । तमिन्द्रो देवतास्मृष्टज्येत्यादिप्रसिद्धम् [?] । द्योतनार्थो हि शब्दः ॥

> *he indra suṣṭuta śobhanastuta tvaṃ sridho duḥkhāt tadutpādakātpāpādvā no 'smānpāhi | rakṣa | yatastvaṃ durmatīnāṃ durmanaskānāṃ rakṣaḥprabhṛtīnām ‖ nāmanyatarasyāmiti nāma udāttatvam ‖ sadamit sarvadaivāvayātā apayāyitāpāyitā [?] asi | ataḥ pāhi | ata eva he indra devo dyotamānaḥ san tvaṃ durmatīnāṃ duṣṭamanaskānāṃ yajñavighātakānāmavayātāsi [?] | tathā rakṣasaḥ rakṣaṇanimittabhūtasya | rakṣo rakṣitavyamasmāditi yāskaḥ | ni. 4-18 [?] | tādṛśasya pāpasya phalapratibandharūpasya hantā ghātako 'si | yadvā | pāpasya pāpino rakṣaso rākṣasāderhantāsi | tathā māvato matsadṛśasya viprasya medhāvino yajamānasya trātā rakṣako 'si | adhāto hetorhe indra vaso sarveṣāṃ nivāsabhūta tvā tvāṃ janitā sarvasya janayitā kartā parameśvaro jījanat | ajanayat | utpāditavān | tathā he vaso nāsayitaḥ [?] tvā tvāṃ rakṣohaṇaṃ jījanat | rakṣohananāyotpāditavān | janayaterluṅi caṅi rūpam ‖ yajñādivighātināṃ rakṣaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ vighātāya hīndrasyāvatāraḥ | tamindro devatāsmṛṣṭajyetyādiprasiddham [?] | dyotanārtho hi śabdaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; small type, a number of places doubtful: [?]. Sense: "O Indra, well praised (*sustuta*), protect us from pain (*sridhaḥ*) or from the sin that causes it; for you are of the ill-minded, the Rākṣasas and the like; always [their] repeller, so protect us; therefore, being a god, shining, you are the repeller of the ill-minded, those who spoil sacrifices; and of *rakṣas* — what is protected from (Yāska, Ni. 4-18 [?]) — you are the killer of that sin that obstructs the fruit; or the killer of sinners, of Rākṣasas and the like; and of one like me — the wise sacrificer — the protector. Therefore, O Indra, *vaso*, abode of all, the creator, the Supreme Lord, the begetter of all, *jījanat* — begot you, gave you birth; and, O *vaso*, he begot you as the slayer of Rākṣasas, for the slaying of the Rākṣasas. [Grammar: aorist *caṅ* of *janayati*.] Indra's descent is for the destruction of the obstructors of sacrifice, the Rākṣasas and others — as is well known from 'Indra, the god' and the like. **॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he indra* — O Indra); *(tvam* — you); *durmatīnām* — of the ill-minded (the Rākṣasas and the like); *sadam it* — always; *avayātā* — the repeller; *(ataḥ* — therefore); *sustuta* — well praised; *sridhaḥ* — from pain (from the sin that causes pain); *naḥ* — us; *pāhi* — protect; *devaḥ san* — being a god (pleased by our praise); *durmatīnām* — of the evil-minded (who obstruct the sacrifice); *(avayātā* — the one who drives them away); *(kathā* — likewise); *pāpasya* — of the sinful; *rakṣasaḥ* — of the Rākṣasas;

### Printed p. 414  (PDF 435)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 129".)*

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 11, continued from p. 413:)* "…*(pāpasya rakṣasaḥ* — of the sinful Rākṣasas, *hantā* — the slayer); *māvataḥ* — (of the sacrificer) like me; *viprasya* — of the wise sacrificer; *trātā* — the protector; *adha* — for this very reason; *vasoḥ* — O Indra, the abode (of all); *tvā* — you; *janitā* — the creator; *jījanat hi* — begot; *vaso* — O Indra, the support (of all); *tvā* — you; *rakṣohaṇam* — for slaying the Rākṣasas; *jījanat* — begot."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, who always repels the Rākṣasas, well praised (by us), protect us from sin (from sorrow); pleased by our praise, you destroy the ill-minded, those who spoil the sacrifice and the sinful Rākṣasas, and protect the sacrificer who is wise like me; for this reason the Creator, who makes all things, begot you, the abode of all; O Indra, the support of all, he brought you into being for the destruction of the Rākṣasas.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Deservedly-lauded Indra, preserve us from suffering; for you are always verily the chastiser of the malevolent: you, being divine, (are the chastiser) of the malevolent: (you are) the slayer of the wicked Rakshas, the preserver of a pious (worshipper), such as I am: for, asylum (of all men), the progenitor has begotten you (for this purpose); has begotten you, asylum (of all men), the destroyer of the Rakshasas."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 11).**

***sridhaḥ*** — *duḥkhāt tadutpādakāt pāpād vā*: "Indra is prayed to protect us from sorrows or from the sins that produce sorrow."

***durmatīnāṃ sadamit avayātā*** — *durmanaskānāṃ rakṣaḥ-prabhṛtīnāṃ sadaiva adhaḥ prāpayitā*: "he who always makes the Rākṣasas and the other ill-minded beings go downward, as a thing thrown from above falls": so the meaning is given.

The word ***durmatīnām*** is used twice. For the second *durmati* he gives the sense *duṣṭamanavatāṃ yāgavighātakānām* — "of the evil-minded, who spoil the sacrifice, who hinder it", and the prayer is that Indra destroy them.

***rakṣasaḥ pāpasya hantā*** — *rakṣaṇanimittabhūtasya phalapratibandharūpasya ghātakaḥ | yadvā pāpinaḥ rākṣasādeḥ hantā asi*: "the slayer of what is the cause of protection [needed] and obstructs the fruit; or: you are the slayer of sinful Rākṣasas and the like. Because such an ill-effect as sin arises, protection is wanted; for this reason Indra destroys the sin." This is one meaning given; or another, "the destroyer of the Rākṣasas who practise sinful acts (acts that harm others)". Yāska too —

> वि ज्योतिषा बृहता भात्यग्निराविर्विश्वानि कृणुते महित्वा ।
> प्रादेवीर्मायाः सहते दुरेवाः शिशीते शृङ्गे रक्षसे विनिक्षे ॥

> *vi jyotiṣā bṛhatā bhāty agnir āvir viśvāni kṛṇute mahitvā |*
> *prādevīr māyāḥ sahate durevāḥ śiśīte śṛṅge rakṣase vinikṣe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-2-9, as read "೫-೨-೯".) Explaining the word *rakṣase* in this Ṛk, Yāska says: *rakṣo rakṣitavyam asmāt, rahasi kṣaṇotīti vā, rātrau nakṣata iti vā* (Ni. 4-18 [?]): "*rakṣas* — he from whom one must be protected; or one who harms in secret; or one who walks about at night": so the word *rakṣas* is explained; it means one who inflicts harm on the body, or one who injures in a secluded place, or one who moves about greatly at night. Indra is described as the destroyer of such Rākṣasas in order to protect from them.

***viprasya trātā*** — *yajamānasya medhāvinaḥ rakṣitā*: "the protector of the wise sacrificer": the word *vipra* is recorded among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೯"). —

> यो अनिध्मो दीदयदप्स्वन्तर्यं विप्रास ईळते अध्वरेषु ।
> अपां नपान्मधुमतीरपो दा याभिरिन्द्रो वावृधे वीर्याय ॥

> *yo anidhmo dīdayad apsv antar yaṃ viprāsa īḷate adhvareṣu |*
> *apāṃ napān madhumatīr apo dā yābhir indro vāvṛdhe vīryāya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-30-4, as read "೧೦-೩೦-೪".) In this Ṛk *viprāsaḥ* is explained as *medhāvinaḥ*, "the wise".

Here *vaso janitā* is used twice; as stated in the Śruti sentence "*tam indro devatā asṛjyata*" (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-1-1 [?], as read), the Supreme Lord who creates all is said to be the support of all, and Indra is said to have been created for the destruction of the Rākṣasas and others who are thorns to the sacrifice.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 11; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *sustuta* — root *ṣṭuñ stutau*; *kta* in the passive; *śobhanaṃ stutaḥ sustutaḥ*; in the vocative *āmantrita-nighāta*. *sridhaḥ* — root *sridha śoṣaṇe* [as read; *sridha* with the sense of *śoṣaṇa*]; *kvip*; ablative singular; *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ* gives the acute to the ending. *avayātā* — prefix *ava*; root *yā prāpaṇe*; *tṛc* in the agent sense; *kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara*.

*(Grammar, continued.)* *durmatīnām* — *duṣṭā matiḥ yeṣāṃ te durmatayaḥ*; genitive plural; *nāmanyatarasyām* (Pā. 6-1-177) gives the acute to the ending. *hantā* — root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *tṛc* in the agent sense; since the suffix is not *aniṭ*... [as read], the augment *iṭ* does not occur; since *c*-marked, the acute on the last syllable. *māvataḥ* — *matsadṛśasya māvataḥ*; *vatup prakaraṇe yuṣmadasmadbhyāṃ chandasi sādṛśya upasaṅkhyānam* (vārttika on Pā. 4-3-1 [?]) gives *vatup* after *asmad*; *pratyayottarapadayoś ca* (Pā. 7-2-98) gives *ma* for the *asmad* ending up to the last letter; *ato guṇe* (Pā. 6-1-97) gives *pararūpa*; *dṛgdṛśavatuṣu* [as read: *tyadādīnām aḥ* …] with its continuation the *ā* [Pā. 6-3-91] becomes the substitute *ā* for the pronoun *ā*; the form *māvat* results; since *vatup* is *p*-marked the stem's accent remains; genitive singular. *janitā* — root *janī prādurbhāve*; the causative sense hidden in it; *tṛc* in the agent sense; the augment *iṭ*; since *c*-marked the acute on the last syllable. *jījanat* — the same root with *ṇic*; *hetumati ca* (Pā. 3-1-26); *luṅ* after the *ṇic*-ending; third person singular, *tip*; *ṇiśridrusrubhyaḥ kartari caṅ* (Pā. 3-1-48) gives *caṅ* for *cli*; *caṅi* (Pā. 6-1-11) gives doubling of the root; *sanvallaghuni caṅpare…* (Pā. 7-4-93) gives *sanvadbhāva*, and *sanyataḥ* (Pā. 7-4-79) gives *i* to the reduplicative; *dīrgho laghoḥ* (Pā. 7-4-94) lengthens it; *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi* gives no augment *aṭ*; *hi ca* (Pā. 8-1-34) forbids *nighāta*; *abhyastānām ādiḥ* (Pā. 6-1-189) gives the acute on the first syllable. *vaso* — root *vasa nivāse*; *śvasyasnihi…* (Uṇ. 1-[?]) gives *u*; in the vocative, *hrasvasya guṇaḥ* (Pā. 7-3-108) gives guṇa; *eṅ hrasvāt sambuddheḥ* (Pā. 6-1-69) drops the *s*; *āmantritasya ca* gives *nighāta*. *rakṣohaṇam* — root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *kvip*; *kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara*; in the accusative singular *inhanpūṣāryamṇāṃ śau* (Pā. 6-4-12) prescribes lengthening. ‖ 11 ‖

## Sūkta 130 — *indra yāhy upa naḥ* (begins on printed p. 417; Anuvāka 19, fourth Sūkta)

### Printed p. 417  (PDF 438)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 18 [as read].)*

**ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra mūvattaneya sūktavu** (the one hundred and thirtieth Sūkta).

**॥ सूक्तभूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, small type; read from the image; several letters doubtful [?]).**

> इन्द्र याह्युप न इति दशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं पारुच्छेपमैन्द्रम् । अन्त्या स नो नव्येभिरित्येषा त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टा अत्यष्टयः । अत्र त्रिष्टुबन्ते परिभाषा नात्रेयते [?], सर्वमात्यष्टमिति विशेषेण प्रतिज्ञातत्वात् । इन्द्र याहि दशान्त्या त्रिष्टुबित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ पृष्ठ्यषडहस्य षष्ठेऽहनि निष्केवल्यशस्त्र एतत्सूक्तम् । षष्ठस्येति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । इन्द्र याह्युप नः प्रघान्यस्य [?] । आ. ८-१ [?] इति ॥ महाव्रते माध्यन्दिनसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनोऽनुरूपतृचे प्रथमम् । इन्द्र याहीत्येषा । महाव्रतस्य पञ्चविंशीति खण्डे शौनकेन सूत्रितम् । इन्द्र याह्युप नः परावत इन्द्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नत । ऐ. आ. ५-१-१ [?] इति ॥

> *indra yāhyupa na iti daśarcaṃ caturthaṃ sūktaṃ pārucchepamaindram | antyā sa no navyebhirityeṣā triṣṭup śiṣṭā atyaṣṭayaḥ | atra triṣṭubante paribhāṣā nātreyate [?], sarvamātyaṣṭamiti viśeṣeṇa pratijñātatvāt | indra yāhi daśāntyā triṣṭubityanukramaṇikā ‖ pṛṣṭhyaṣaḍahasya ṣaṣṭhe 'hani niṣkevalyaśastra etatsūktam | ṣaṣṭhasyeti khaṇḍe sūtritam | indra yāhyupa naḥ praghānyasya [?] | ā. 8-1 [?] iti ‖ mahāvrate mādhyandinasavane brāhmaṇācchaṃsino 'nurūpatṛce prathamam | indra yāhītyeṣā | mahāvratasya pañcaviṃśīti khaṇḍe śaunakena sūtritam | indra yāhyupa naḥ parāvata indrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnata | ai. ā. 5-1-1 [?] iti ‖*

**Kannada anuvāda (translated).** *Anuvāda* — This Sūkta *indra yāhy upa naḥ* is the fourth Sūkta in the nineteenth Anuvāka. It has ten ṛks. The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Paruccheṣa; the deity is Indra. The last ṛk, beginning *sa no navyebhiḥ*, is in the Triṣṭubh metre; the other ṛks are in Atyaṣṭi metres. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "*indra yāhi daśāntyā triṣṭubh*". On the sixth day of the *pṛṣṭhya ṣaḍaha* sacrifice this Sūkta is used for the *niṣkevalya śastra*, as expounded in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the section *ṣaṣṭhasya* by the sūtra *indra yāhy upa naḥ praghānyasya* [as read: [?]] (Āś. 8-1 [?]). In the *mahāvrata* sacrifice, at the midday pressing, when the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin priest (the *udgātṛ*, the one who chants) recites for the Sāman-mantras, the three ṛks beginning *indra yāhi* are to be recited as the *anurūpa* hymn; in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, in the section *mahāvratasya pañcaviṃśī*, the sage Śaunaka states this by the sūtra *indra yāhy upa naḥ parāvata indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata* (Ait. Ār. 5-1-1, as read "೫-೧-೧").

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> एन्द्र याह्युप नः परावतो नायमच्छा विदथानीव सत्पतिरस्तं राजेव सत्पतिः ।

> *endra yāhyupa naḥ parāvato nāyamacchā vidathānīva satpatirastaṃ rājeva satpatiḥ |*
> *havāmahe tvā vayaṃ prayasvantaḥ sute sacā |*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । इन्द्र । याहि । उप । नः । पराऽवतः । न । अयम् । अच्छ । विदथानिऽइव । सत्ऽपतिः । अस्तम् । राजाऽइव । सत्ऽपतिः ।

> *ā | indra | yāhi | upa | naḥ | parā 'vataḥ | na | ayam | accha | vidathāni 'iva | sat 'patiḥ | astam | rājā 'iva | sat 'patiḥ |*
> *havāmahe | tvā | vayam | prayasvantaḥ | sute | sacā |*

*(Read from the image. The Saṃhitā prints *endra yāhy upa naḥ* (*ā indra*), *nāyam acchā*; the Pada: *parā-vataḥ*, *vidathāni-iva*, *rājā-iva*, *vāja-sātaye*.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र परावतो दूरदेशात् स्वर्गलक्षणान्नोऽस्मानुप सामीप्येन याहि । अस्मत्समीपं प्रत्यागच्छ । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अयं न पुरोवर्त्यग्निरभिषुतः सोमो वा प्रस्तुतेऽस्मिन् निर्दिश्यते । स इव । यद्यपि पुरस्तादुपाचारानिषेधार्थीयो नकारः सर्वत्र तथास्य प्रैतिकेनोपमार्थीयो गृह्यते [?] । यद्वा । परावतो न दूरदेशादिव । यद्यपि यज्ञे सर्वदा सन्निहितस्तथापि स्वर्गाख्याद्दूरदेशादिवास्मिन् यज्ञे ॥ आयमिति विभक्तिव्यत्ययः । अमुं देवयजनदेशमच्छाभिप्राप्तुं मायाहीति शेषः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । सत्पतिः सतां सर्वदा वर्तमानानामृत्विजां पालको यजमान इव । पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । स यथा विदथानि वेदनान्युपेयुर्ज्ञानानि [?] । यद्वा । सतां विद्यमानानां फलानां पालकोऽग्निः । स यथा विदथानि यज्ञगृहाण्यागच्छति तद्वत्त्वमपि यज्ञगृहानागच्छ । यद्वा । सतां नक्षत्राणां पतिः राजा चन्द्रमा अस्तमिव । स यथा स्वधामस्थानमागच्छति तद्वत् । किंच प्रयस्वन्तो हविर्लक्षणान्नवन्तो वयं यजमानास्त्वां हवामहे । आह्वयामः । किमर्थम् । सुतेऽभिषुते सोमे निमित्तभूते सति । कीदृशा वयम् । सचा ऋत्विग्भिः सहिताः । सचा सहेत्यर्थ इति यास्कः । नि. ५-५ [?] । आह्वाने दृष्टान्तः । पुत्रासः पुत्राः पितरं न पालकं जनकमिव तं यथा वाजसातयेऽन्नस्य सम्भजनायाह्वयन्ति तथा वयमपि त्वां तदर्थमाह्वयामः । किंच मंहिष्ठं मंहनीयं त्वां वाजसातये सङ्ग्रामप्राप्तये तज्जयाय हविःस्वीकाराय वाह्वयामः ॥

> *he indra parāvato dūradeśāt svargalakṣaṇānno 'smānupa sāmīpyena yāhi | asmatsamīpaṃ pratyāgaccha | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | ayaṃ na purovartyagnirabhiṣutaḥ somo vā prastute 'smin nirdiśyate | sa iva | yadyapi purastādupācārāniṣedhārthīyo nakāraḥ sarvatra tathāsya praitikenopamārthīyo gṛhyate [?] | yadvā | parāvato na dūradeśādiva | yadyapi yajñe sarvadā sannihitastathāpi svargākhyāddūradeśādivāsmin yajñe ‖ āyamiti vibhaktivyatyayaḥ | amuṃ devayajanadeśamacchābhiprāptuṃ māyāhīti śeṣaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | satpatiḥ satāṃ sarvadā vartamānānāmṛtvijāṃ pālako yajamāna iva | patyāvaiśvarya iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | sa yathā vidathāni vedanānyupeyurjñānāni [?] | yadvā | satāṃ vidyamānānāṃ phalānāṃ pālako 'gniḥ | sa yathā vidathāni yajñagṛhāṇyāgacchati tadvattvamapi yajñagṛhānāgaccha | yadvā | satāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ patiḥ rājā candramā astamiva | sa yathā svadhāmasthānamāgacchati tadvat | kiṃca prayasvanto havirlakṣaṇānnavanto vayaṃ yajamānāstvāṃ havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ | kimartham | sute 'bhiṣute some nimittabhūte sati | kīdṛśā vayam | sacā ṛtvigbhiḥ sahitāḥ | sacā sahetyartha iti yāskaḥ | ni. 5-5 [?] | āhvāne dṛṣṭāntaḥ | putrāsaḥ putrāḥ pitaraṃ na pālakaṃ janakamiva taṃ yathā vājasātaye 'nnasya sambhajanāyāhvayanti tathā vayamapi tvāṃ tadarthamāhvayāmaḥ | kiṃca maṃhiṣṭhaṃ maṃhanīyaṃ tvāṃ vājasātaye saṅgrāmaprāptaye tajjayāya haviḥsvīkārāya vāhvayāmaḥ ‖*

*(Read from the image; the small type is partly doubtful: [?] — notably the clause on the particle *na* ("*yady api purastād…*") and "*vidathāni vedanāny upeyur jñānāni*". Sense: "O Indra, come near us from afar (*parāvataḥ*) — from heaven — return to us. The example: like this (*ayam na*) fire before us, or the pressed Soma that is pointed to in the present context — like him; though the particle *na* is generally negative, here it is taken as a particle of comparison. Or: as if from a distant place (*parāvato na*), though you are always present at the sacrifice, as if from far-off heaven to this sacrifice. [Case variation: *āyam* for *amum*.] Come to this place of sacrifice, to reach it. Example: like a *satpati* — the sacrificer, protector of the priests who are always present; [the accent of the first member is from *patyāvaiśvarye*]; as he comes to *vidathāni* — the places of knowledge/of the ceremonies; or, as Agni, the protector of existing fruits, comes to *vidathāni* — the sacrificial houses — so you come to the sacrificial houses; or, as the Moon, king (*rājā*) and lord of the stars, comes to his setting-place (*astam*), his own abode. And we sacrificers, possessed of food in the form of oblations, call you (*havāmahe*), for the pressed Soma, together with the priests (*sacā* — 'together', Yāska, Ni. 5-5 [?]). Example for the invocation: as sons call a father — a protector — for the *vājasāti* — to partake of food; so we also call you for that; and we call you, the most worthy of honour (*maṃhiṣṭha*), for the winning of battle, for the acceptance of oblations.")*

### Printed p. 419  (PDF 440)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 19 [as read].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he indra* — O Indra); *parāvataḥ* — from a very distant place (from heaven); *ayaṃ na* — like this (the fire before us) [or: (this pressed) Soma]; *naḥ* — us; *upa yāhi* — approach; or, *parāvataḥ na* — as if from a distant place; *naḥ* — to us; *ā* — here, at this sacrificial hall; *upa yāhi* — come near; *satpatiḥ* — the sacrificer who is the protector of the priests who are always present, or Agni, protector of existing fruits; *vidathāni iva* — as one comes to rites that are to be known, or as to the sacrificial houses; or *satpatiḥ* — the lord of the stars; *rājā iva* — like the Moon; *astam* — to his own setting-place; *(ayam* — to this sacrificial entry); *accha ā (yāhi)* — come, facing us; *(kiṃ ca* — and); *prayasvantaḥ* — possessed of food in the form of oblations; *sacā* — together with the priests; *vayam* — we (the sacrificers); *putrāsaḥ* — sons; *pitaram na* — as a father is called; *sute* — for the pressed Soma; *tvā* — you; *havāmahe* — we invoke; *maṃhiṣṭham* — you, the most worthy of honour; *vāja-sātaye* — for the winning of battle (for victory in battle) or for the acceptance of oblations; *(havāmahe* — we invoke).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha** *(its first part is at the foot of p. 419, the rest on p. 420).* O Indra, (though you are always near) as if from a distant place, or like this fire that came from afar — come to us; as the sacrificer goes to the priests, as Agni goes to the sacrificial halls, as the Moon, lord of the stars, goes to his abode, set out facing us toward the sacrificial hall; we, the sacrificers, with the priests, having prepared the Soma, as sons call a father to share food, call you, the most worthy, for the winning of battle or for the acceptance of the oblation.

### Printed p. 420  (PDF 441)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Come to us, Indra, from afar: not as this (fire) which is before us, (but) like the pious instituter of sacrifices, or like the royal lord of the constellations (when going) to his setting. Bearing oblations, we, along with (the priests), invoke you to accept the effused (juices), as sons (invite) a father to partake of food: (we invoke) you, who are most entitled to reverence, to (accept of) the sacrificial viands."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 1).**

***parāvataḥ naḥ upa yāhi ayaṃ na*** — *svargalakṣaṇāt dūradeśāt asmatsamīpaṃ pratyāgaccha | purovartī agnir iva*: the word *parāvat* is recorded among the names of "far" (Ni. 3-20 [?]; as read "೩-೩೦"). "From heaven, far away, Indra is prayed to come near us for the sacrifice." By the sentence *ayaṃ na* — "like this" — the ṛṣi directly points out, before the priests and the sacrificers, that Indra should come near to us, like another fire, or like the Soma-juice that has been prepared and brought near. The particle *na* always denotes a prohibition; but here, it is explained in one meaning that it is used only in the sense of comparison (*upamārthe*).

In the second meaning it is said together with the word *parāvataḥ* in the sense "as from a distant place": whether it be Agni or Indra, those who are always present in the places where sacrifice is going on, are thought of by those who call them as living far away in heaven; so it is customary that they are prayed, "come to the place where the sacrifice is going".

***satpatiḥ*** — *satāṃ sarvadā vartamānānām ṛtvijāṃ pālakaḥ yajamāna iva*: "As the sacrificer, who always protects the priests present at the sacrifice when it is performed in the sacrificial hall, is near them, so may Indra be near the sacrificer": and the meaning is given that "the sacrificer, having knowledge of the duties to be performed at the sacrifice, protects the sacrifice"; by the sentence *vidathānīva satpatiḥ*, the first meaning is described.

### Printed p. 421  (PDF 442)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 19 [as read].)*

In the second meaning: *satāṃ vidyamānānāṃ phalānāṃ pālako 'gniḥ vidathāni yajñagṛhāṇi āgacchati tadvat* — "as Agni, who protects the fruits of sacrificial acts so that the fruit be certain, comes to the sacrificial hall, so may Indra come to protect the sacrifice."

In the matter of Indra's coming to the sacrificial hall, the sentence *astaṃ rājeva satpatiḥ* is used as a comparison. The words *gayaḥ, kṛdaraḥ* [as read, doubtful: [?]] — *asta* is recorded among the two names of "house" (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೩"); "*house*" is the meaning: as the Moon, king of the stars, comes to his own abode, so Indra too may come to the sacrificial hall.

***prayasvantaḥ*** — *havirlakṣaṇānnavantaḥ*: the word *prayas* is recorded among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"): "the sacrificers who have prepared the food in the form of oblation."

***sacā*** — this word, which has the meaning "together" (*saha*), is explained by Yāska (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೩೨" [?]): here the meaning "with the priests" is given.

***putrāsaḥ pitaraṃ na vājasātaye*** — *putrāḥ pitaraṃ janakaṃ pālakam iva annasya sambhajanāya āhvayanti tadvat*: "as sons call a father — the protector — to share food, so the sacrificers, having prepared the Soma-pressing, call Indra to accept it": so the meaning.

***maṃhiṣṭhaṃ vājasātaye*** — *maṃhanīyaṃ tajjayāya saṅgrāmaprāptaye havissvīkārāya vā āhvayāmaḥ*: "we call Indra, who deserves honour or worship, to bring about victory in battle, or to accept the oblation": so the meaning. The word *vājasātau* is recorded among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯").

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *yāhi* — root *yā prāpaṇe*; *loṭ* second person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *āyam* — by the statement *supāṃ suluk…* the first case ending becomes the second. *accha* — *nipātasya ca* (Pā. 6-3-136) gives the long vowel in the Saṃhitā. *satpatiḥ* — *satāṃ patiḥ satpatiḥ*; though *patyāvaiśvaryeṇe* (Pā. 6-2-18) gives the accent of the first member remains.

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, continued; numbers as printed.)* *satpatiḥ* (cont.) — *patyāvaiśvaryeṇe* (Pā. 6-2-18) gives the accent of the first member. *vidathāni* — root *vida jñāne*; *rudhivididhyām…* [as read: *ruditviditam*…; Uṇ. 3-[?]] gives the suffix *athac*; since *j*-marked, no guṇa of the penult; acute on the first syllable of the suffix. *havāmahe* — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *laṭ* first person plural; because at the beginning of the *pāda*, no *nighāta*; *tāsyanudāttenṅidvidāder…* (Pā. 6-1-186): the *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented, so the root's accent remains. *prayasvantaḥ* — *prayaḥ yeṣām asti iti prayasvantaḥ*; suffix *matup*; since *p*-marked it is unaccented. *sute* — root *ṣuñ abhiṣave*; *kta* in the passive by *niṣṭhā*; acute on the last syllable by the suffix's accent; locative singular. *putrāsaḥ* — root *pūñ savane*; *puvaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ…* [as read: *puvo hrasvaś ca*, Uṇ. 4-[?]] gives *kran* [as read: *tran*]; the root is shortened; since *k*-marked no guṇa; with *jas* following, *ājjaser asuk* (Pā. 7-1-50) gives the augment *asuk*. *vājasātaye* — root *ṣaṇa sambhaktau*; *ūtiyūtijūti…* (Pā. 3-3-97) gives *ktic* by irregular formation; a *bahuvrīhi* [as printed]; the accent of the first member; dative singular. *maṃhiṣṭham* — *atiśayena maṃhitā maṃhiṣṭhaḥ*; *tuścchandasi* (Pā. 5-3-59) gives, when excess is meant, *iṣṭhan* after the *tṛc* ending; with it following, *turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu* (Pā. 6-4-154) drops *tṛc*; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable. ‖ 1 ‖

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; small type, a few doubtful places [?]).*

> षष्ठेऽहनि माध्यन्दिने सवने प्रस्थितयाज्यानां पुरस्तादेन्या ऋचः प्रक्षेपणीययोः । तत्र होतुः पुरस्तात् पिबा सोममिन्द्रेत्येषा । षष्ठस्य प्रातःसवन इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । पिबा सोममिन्द्र सुवानमद्रिभिरिन्द्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नतेति । आ. ८-१ [?] इति ॥

> *ṣaṣṭhe 'hani mādhyandine savane prasthitayājyānāṃ purastādenyā ṛcaḥ prakṣepaṇīyayoḥ | tatra hotuḥ purastāt pibā somamindretyeṣā | ṣaṣṭhasya prātaḥsavana iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | pibā somamindra suvānamadribhirindrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnateti | ā. 8-1 [?] iti ‖*

> हे इन्द्र वंसगो वननीयगमनस्त्वं सोमं पिब ॥ द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति दीर्घः ॥ कीदृशं तम् । अद्रिभिरभिषवसाधनैर्ग्रावभिः सुवानं सूयमानम् ॥ कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः ॥ कोशेन सिक्तं कोशस्थानीयेन दशापवित्रेण शोधितम् । यद्वा । अवतमित्यनेन सह सम्बन्धः । कोशेनेति लक्षणेन सिक्तं स्वोचितजलेन पूरितमवतं नाहावलक्षणमवटमिव । तं यथा वंसगो वननीयगमनस्तृषा शीघ्रगामी वृषभः पिबति तद्वत् । तत्तृषाणो न वंसगः । यथात्यन्तं तृषितो वंसगो वननीयगमनः शीघ्रगामी पुरुष अहावादिमागत्य पिबति तद्वत् । किमर्थं पानमिति तत्राह । ते तव मदाय तृप्तये हर्यताय विक्रान्तिहेतवे कान्त्यर्थं वा ॥ हर्य गतिकान्त्योः । भृमृदृशीत्यादिनातच् ॥ तुविष्टमाय महत्त्वाय प्रवृद्धत्वाय धायसे यदर्थं मद उपजायते तदर्थाय ॥ धाञ् वहिपाधाञ्भ्य इत्यसुनि नित्त्वात् [?] ॥ यद्वा । ते तव तुविष्टमाय धायसे इति प्रभूताय पानाय । त्वा त्वामश्वा यच्छन्तु । अभिमुख्येन गमयन्तु । अश्वा इति शेषः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । हरितो न सूर्यं हरिद्वर्णविशिष्टा एतन्नामका अश्वाः सूर्यमिव । तं यथा चित्रैराभिमतदेशमभिप्रेरिता वहन्ति तद्वत् । किंचाहा विश्वा सर्वाण्यहानि सूर्यमिव । तं यथा त एव प्रतिदिनं वहन्ति तथास्माद्यागादिषेषु प्रतिदिनमावहन्तु ॥

> *he indra vaṃsago vananīyagamanastvaṃ somaṃ piba ‖ dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti dīrghaḥ ‖ kīdṛśaṃ tam | adribhirabhiṣavasādhanairgrāvabhiḥ suvānaṃ sūyamānam ‖ karmaṇi kartṛpratyayaḥ ‖ kośena siktaṃ kośasthānīyena daśāpavitreṇa śodhitam | yadvā | avatamityanena saha sambandhaḥ | kośeneti lakṣaṇena siktaṃ svocitajalena pūritamavataṃ nāhāvalakṣaṇamavaṭamiva | taṃ yathā vaṃsago vananīyagamanastṛṣā śīghragāmī vṛṣabhaḥ pibati tadvat | tattṛṣāṇo na vaṃsagaḥ | yathātyantaṃ tṛṣito vaṃsago vananīyagamanaḥ śīghragāmī puruṣa ahāvādimāgatya pibati tadvat | kimarthaṃ pānamiti tatrāha | te tava madāya tṛptaye haryatāya vikrāntihetave kāntyarthaṃ vā ‖ harya gatikāntyoḥ | bhṛmṛdṛśītyādinātac ‖ tuviṣṭamāya mahattvāya pravṛddhatvāya dhāyase yadarthaṃ mada upajāyate tadarthāya ‖ dhāñ vahipādhāñbhya ityasuni nittvāt [?] ‖ yadvā | te tava tuviṣṭamāya dhāyase iti prabhūtāya pānāya | tvā tvāmaśvā yacchantu | abhimukhyena gamayantu | aśvā iti śeṣaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | harito na sūryaṃ haridvarṇaviśiṣṭā etannāmakā aśvāḥ sūryamiva | taṃ yathā citrairābhimatadeśamabhipreritā vahanti tadvat | kiṃcāhā viśvā sarvāṇyahāni sūryamiva | taṃ yathā ta eva pratidinaṃ vahanti tathāsmādyāgādiṣeṣu pratidinamāvahantu ‖*

*(Sense. At the sixth day, at the midday pressing, the ṛks before the *prasthita-yājyās* are the *praṣepaṇīyas* [?]; in this, before the Hotṛ, *pibā somam indra* is recited: as stated in the section *ṣaṣṭhasya prātaḥsavane*: "*pibā somam indra suvānam adribhir indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata*" (Āś. 8-1 [?]). "O Indra, *vaṃsagaḥ* — of desirable going — drink the Soma. [Lengthening by *dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ*.] What kind? *suvānam* — being pressed (*adribhiḥ*) by the pressing-stones; *kośena siktam* — purified by the *daśāpavitra* (the ten-fold strainer) that serves as a receptacle; or taken with the following *avatam*: as a well (*avata*) filled with the water suitable for it, like a well at the watering-place; as the swift bull, of desirable going (*vaṃsaga*), drinks it when thirsty; or the man who is very thirsty and swift going to the watering-place and drinks: so. For what purpose? For your exhilaration (*madāya*), for *haryatāya* (heroism or splendour) [root *hary* in the sense of going and desire], for *tuviṣṭamāya* — greatness, growth, for *dhāyase* — for that for which the exhilaration arises. Or: *tuviṣṭamāya dhāyase* — for much drinking. May the horses bring you, bring you facing us (*ā yacchantu*); example: *harito na sūryam* — as the horses called *harit*, of golden-green colour, bring the sun; as they carry him impelled toward the desired place; and *ahā viśvā* — all days — as the same horses carry the sun every day, so may they bring you every day to our sacrifices and the like.")*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he indra* — O Indra); *vaṃsagaḥ* — you who go swiftly; *adribhiḥ* — by the stones (the means of pressing); *suvānam* — being pressed; *kośena* — by the ten-fold strainer; *siktam* — made pure (and); *somam* — the Soma-juice; *(kośena siktam* — filled with water as with a vessel); *avatam* — [as] a well; *vaṃsagaḥ na* — as a swift bull drinks water [or] — *tātṛṣāṇaḥ* — very thirsty; *vaṃsagaḥ na* — as a swift man (reaching the well and drinking); *piba* — drink; *te* — for your; *madāya* — satisfaction; *haryatāya* — for valour (splendour); and *tuviṣṭamāya* — for growth (greatness) — *dhāyase* — drink; (or: *tuviṣṭamāya* — very great; *dhāyase* — for drinking); *tvā* — you; *haritaḥ* — the sun's horses; *sūryam na* — as they bring the sun; *ā yacchantu* — may (your horses) bring you facing (the sacrifice); *(kiṃ ca* — and); *viśvā ahā* — on all days; *sūryam iva* — as the sun (they bring); (may they bring you) every day to the sacrificial hall.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, drink the Soma-juice, pressed with the stones and purified by the ten-fold strainer, as a swift bull, or a man exceedingly thirsty, goes to a well and drinks; drink it for your satisfaction, for valour and splendour, and for growth (greatness); may your horses bring you, facing the place of sacrifice, as the sun's horses bring the sun to the place he desires; and may they bring you every day to our sacrificial hall as they bring the sun every day.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Drink, Indra, the Soma juice, that has been expressed by the stones, and sprinkled with the sacred grass, as a thirsty ox or a thirsty man hastens to a well. (Drink) for your exhilaration, for your invigoration, for your exceedingly great augmentation: let your horses bring you hither, as his steeds convey the sun; as they carry him (through heaven) day by day."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 2).**

*(The first sentence of this section is the Kannada introduction (to the use of the Ṛk in the sacrifice):)* "In the *ṣaṣṭha* (sixth) day of the sacrifice, at the time of the midday pressing, certain ṛks are recited as the preliminary (*pūrvabhāvi*) for the *prasthitayājyā* mantras. Then the Hotṛ recites this Ṛk *pibā somam* as a preliminary to the *yājyā* mantra — as explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, section *ṣaṣṭhasya prātaḥsavane*, by the sūtra *pibā somam indra suvānam adribhir indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata* (Āś. 8-1-… [as read "೮-೧-೧"?])."

### Printed p. 425  (PDF 446)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 19 [as read].)*

***vaṃsagaḥ*** — *vananīyagamanaḥ*: "one whose going is desirable": the going of Indra is described as to be desired.

***adribhiḥ*** — *abhiṣavasādhanair grāvabhiḥ*: "with the stones used to press out the Soma-creeper." The word *adri* is recorded among the names of cloud (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೧೦") and is explained as *adrir ādṛṇāter ātter vātreyaḥ syāt* (Ni. 4-4 [?]). And —

> स्यै ते वदन्तु प्र वयं वदाम ग्रावभ्यो वाचं वदता वदद्भ्यः ।
> यदद्रयः पर्वताः साकमाशवः श्लोकं घोषं भरथेन्द्राय सोमिनः ॥

> *syai te vadantu pra vayaṃ vadāma grāvabhyo vācaṃ vadatā vadadbhyaḥ |*
> *yad adrayaḥ parvatāḥ sākam āśavaḥ ślokaṃ ghoṣaṃ bharathendrāya sominaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-1, as read "೧೦-೯೪-೧"; the first line is printed differently from what I give and the letters are doubtful — I record it as read from the small type: [?].) In this Ṛk *adrayaḥ* is explained as *ādaraṇīyāḥ* — "worthy of respect".

***kośena siktam*** — *kośasthānīyena daśāpavitreṇa śodhitam | yadvā svocitajalena pūritam*: "the Soma-juice, purified by the strainer which acts as its receptacle, or filled with its own water." *Kośa* means a large (wooden) vessel that holds the Soma-juice. Or this word is connected with *avatam*: "the Soma-juice mixed with water in the proper proportion."

***avatam na*** — *ahāvalakṣaṇam avaṭam iva*: "as a swift ox, drinking from a well (a trough, a pit) filled with water to drink, Indra is prayed to drink the Soma-juice purified by the strainer that is taken out with stones."

***tatṛṣāṇo na vaṃsagaḥ*** — *atyantaṃ tṛṣitaḥ*: "one who is very thirsty": "As a man very thirsty goes quickly to a well and the like and drinks water, so Indra is prayed to drink Soma."

***haryatāya*** — *vikrāntihetave kāntyarthāya vā*: since the root *hary* conveys the two meanings "going" and "desire", it is said that by the drinking of Soma valour and splendour grow, and that for this very purpose Indra drinks Soma-juice.

***tuviṣṭamāya dhāyase*** — two kinds of meaning are given: the word *tuvi* is recorded among the names of "much" (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೩"). "In order that very great exhilaration arise, the drinking of Soma is for Indra"; this is the first meaning. In the second meaning, *tvā*

### Printed p. 426  (PDF 447)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

*(continued:)* …*ā yacchantu* — since "bring" is the verb used here, the sense is that Indra's horses bring him and that he may come, called, for much drinking of Soma.

***harito na sūryam*** — this sentence is given as a comparison here. The word *harit* is recorded among the names of the quarters (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೩-೧೬") and of rivers (Ni. 1-[?]; "೩-೩೨"). And —

> हरी इन्द्रस्य रोहिता अग्नेः हरित आदित्यस्य रासभावश्विनोः । अजाः पूष्णः पृषत्यो मरुतामरुणो गावः उषसः श्यावाः सवितुः विश्वरूपा बृहस्पतेः नियुतो वायोः ।

> *harī indrasya rohitā agneḥ harita ādityasya rāsabhāv aśvinoḥ | ajāḥ pūṣṇaḥ pṛṣatyo marutām aruṇo gāvaḥ uṣasaḥ śyāvāḥ savituḥ viśvarūpā bṛhaspateḥ niyuto vāyoḥ |*

(Ni. 1-[?], as read "೩-೧೪", a list of the vehicles of the gods; the passage is in small type and doubtful in places: [?].) In this and other passages, the word *harit* is used for the "vehicle" of the sun. For this reason Sāyaṇa explains *harit* as *haridvarṇaviśiṣṭāḥ* — "horses called *harit* by name, of golden-green colour". As these horses, driven by the charioteer, carry the sun, who has many horses, to the place he must go, so may Indra's horses bring him to the sacrifice: so it is described.

***ahā viśvā sūryam iva — sarvāṇy ahāni iva | yathā ta eva pratidinaṃ vahanti tathā asmadyāgādiṣeṣu pratidinam āvahantu*** — this sentence is given as a comparison in the matter of Indra's coming. As the horses carry the sun every day to the place he must go, so they should carry Indra to the sacrificial hall every day: so he is compared.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *piba* — root *pā pāne*; *loṭ* second person singular, *sip*; its substitute *hi*; *śap*; *pāghrādhmā…* (Pā. 7-3-78) gives *piba* for the root; *ato he* (Pā. 6-4-105) drops *hi*; at the beginning of the *pāda* there is no *nighāta*; since *śap* is *p*-marked the root's accent remains; *dyaucotas… [as read: dyubhyo… ]* gives the long vowel in the Saṃhitā. *suvānam* — root *ṣuñ abhiṣave*; *vyatyayo bahulam* (Pā. 3-1-85) gives the agent-suffix in the passive; *śānac* in the present sense; by Vedic usage the *vikaraṇa* has *luk*; since *j*-marked [as read] no guṇa; the substitute *uvaṅ*; *citaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the acute on the last syllable. *siktam* — root *ṣiñc kṣaraṇe*; *kta* in the passive; since *k*-marked, no guṇa of the penult; *coḥ kuḥ* gives *k* for *c*; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. *avatam* — in *avaṭam* the *ṭ* becomes *t* by Vedic letter-interchange; the stem's accent on the last syllable.

### Printed p. 427  (PDF 448)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 19 [as read].)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 2, concluded; numbers as printed.)* *vaṃsagaḥ* — *upasarga*-less; *prṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam* (Pā. 6-3-109) gives the desired form and accent. *tātṛṣāṇaḥ* — root *ñitṛṣā pipāsāyām*; when *liṭ* follows, *liṭaḥ kānajvā* (Pā. 3-2-106) gives *kānac*; because of it the root is doubled; *urat* (Pā. 7-4-66) gives *at* to the reduplicative, *ṛ*-ending, and by *ādir ṇiṭuḍavaḥ* [as read: *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*] the initial consonant remains; *āṭ kupvāṅ…* gives *ṇ* for the *n* of the suffix; the long vowel in the Saṃhitā is Vedic; *citaḥ* gives the acute on the last syllable. *madāya* — root *madī tṛptiyoge*; *mado 'nupasarge* (Pā. 3-3-67) gives *ap*; since *p*-marked the root's accent remains; dative singular. *haryatāya* — root *harya gatikāntyoḥ*; *bhṛmṛdṛśi…* (Uṇ. 3-110) gives *atac*; *citaḥ* gives the acute on the last syllable. *dhāyase* — root *dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *vahihādhāñbhyaś chandasi* (Uṇ. 4-[?]) gives *asun*; by *ñit* [continued] *āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ* (Pā. 7-3-33) gives the augment *yuk*; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable. *yacchantu* — root *yam uparame* [as printed "vāṅ dāne"]; *loṭ* third person plural; *pāghrādhmā…* (Pā. 7-3-78) gives *yaccha*; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *ahā viśvā* — neuter plural; *śeś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. 6-1-70) drops *śi*. ‖ 2 ‖

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; small type, partly doubtful: [?]).*

> अयमिन्द्रो दिवो द्युलोकादानीतं सोममविन्दत् । अलभत । लब्धवान् । द्युलोकाद्गायत्र्या पक्षिरूपयोपहृतं भूमावानीतं स्वीकृतवानित्यर्थः । द्युलोकादानयनं कृत्स्नत्रयीये तृतीयस्यामितो दिवि सोम आसीत्तं गायत्र्याहरत् । तै. ब्रा. ३-२-१-१ [?] इत्यादिषु प्रसिद्धम् । स एव विशेष्यते । गुहा गुहायां निहितमतिगोप्ये प्रदेशे पर्वताद्यौ स्थापितम् । अत एव निधिं निधिस्थानीयम् । अनाशमित्यर्थः । आनयने दृष्टान्तः । वेर्न गर्भं पक्षिणो गर्भं न शिशुमिव । यथा कपोतादिः स्त्री पक्षिणी स्वशिशुं व्याधादिभयात्कस्मिंश्चिद्दुर्गमे स्थापयित्वा तत्स्थानमनुजानाति परिभ्रम्य विन्दते तद्वत् । कीदृशे स्थाने ... अश्मनि पाषाणे । अतिमहति विस्तृतेऽनन्तेऽपरिमितपाषाणे पर्वतादौ परिवीतं लताकण्टकादिना परितो वेष्टितम् । सत्स्वपीतरेषूदेशेषु कोस्याति शय इति तत्राह । अयमिन्द्रो वज्री वज्रवान् गवां व्रजमिव पणिनासुरेणापहृतं भूमौ खनित्वा पाषाणेन पिहितद्वारं गवां व्रजं यथा तमसुरं जित्वा द्वारमुद्घाट्य लब्धवान् तद्वत् सोमं सिषासन् सम्भक्तुमिच्छन् । सनीवन्तर्धेति विकल्पनादिडभावो जनसनेत्यादिः । अविन्दत् । अयमर्थः पणिनेव गावः । ऋ. १-३२-११ [?] इत्यादिषु प्रसिद्धः । तथायमिन्द्रः परिवृताः परितो मेघेनावृता इषोऽन्नहेतुभूतस्योदकस्य द्वारो द्वाराण्यपावृणोत् । अपवृतान्यकरोत् । उद्घाटितवानित्यर्थः । तथा कृषेष्विष्यमाणानि व्रीह्याद्यन्नानि परिवृता भूमावुपरि परितो व्याप्त्यान्यकरोत् । वज्रेण मेघं भित्त्वा जलवर्षणेन सस्यादिसमृद्धिं कृत्वा व्रीह्यादिकं भूमौ व्याप्तमकरोदित्यर्थः । यतोऽयमेवं कृतवान् अतः सोमस्वीकारो युक्तः ॥

> *ayamindro divo dyulokādānītaṃ somamavindat | alabhata | labdhavān | dyulokādgāyatryā pakṣirūpayopahṛtaṃ bhūmāvānītaṃ svīkṛtavānityarthaḥ | dyulokādānayanaṃ kṛtsnatrayīye tṛtīyasyāmito divi soma āsīttaṃ gāyatryāharat | tai. brā. 3-2-1-1 [?] ityādiṣu prasiddham | sa eva viśeṣyate | guhā guhāyāṃ nihitamatigopye pradeśe parvatādyau sthāpitam | ata eva nidhiṃ nidhisthānīyam | anāśamityarthaḥ | ānayane dṛṣṭāntaḥ | verna garbhaṃ pakṣiṇo garbhaṃ na śiśumiva | yathā kapotādiḥ strī pakṣiṇī svaśiśuṃ vyādhādibhayātkasmiṃściddurgame sthāpayitvā tatsthānamanujānāti paribhramya vindate tadvat | kīdṛśe sthāne ... aśmani pāṣāṇe | atimahati vistṛte 'nante 'parimitapāṣāṇe parvatādau parivītaṃ latākaṇṭakādinā parito veṣṭitam | satsvapītareṣūdeśeṣu kosyāti śaya iti tatrāha | ayamindro vajrī vajravān gavāṃ vrajamiva paṇināsureṇāpahṛtaṃ bhūmau khanitvā pāṣāṇena pihitadvāraṃ gavāṃ vrajaṃ yathā tamasuraṃ jitvā dvāramudghāṭya labdhavān tadvat somaṃ siṣāsan sambhaktumicchan | sanīvantardheti vikalpanādiḍabhāvo janasanetyādiḥ | avindat | ayamarthaḥ paṇineva gāvaḥ | ṛ. 1-32-11 [?] ityādiṣu prasiddhaḥ | tathāyamindraḥ parivṛtāḥ parito meghenāvṛtā iṣo 'nnahetubhūtasyodakasya dvāro dvārāṇyapāvṛṇot | apavṛtānyakarot | udghāṭitavānityarthaḥ | tathā kṛṣeṣviṣyamāṇāni vrīhyādyannāni parivṛtā bhūmāvupari parito vyāptyānyakarot | vajreṇa meghaṃ bhittvā jalavarṣaṇena sasyādisamṛddhiṃ kṛtvā vrīhyādikaṃ bhūmau vyāptamakarodityarthaḥ | yato 'yamevaṃ kṛtavān ataḥ somasvīkāro yuktaḥ ‖*

*(Sense. "This Indra obtained (*avindat*) the Soma brought from heaven (*divaḥ*): having it carried by the Gāyatrī in the form of a bird, brought to the earth: this is well known from the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa and others ('the Soma was in heaven; the Gāyatrī brought it'). It was *guhā nihitam* — placed in a hiding-place on a mountain etc., thus a treasure, without loss. The example of fetching: *vor na garbham* — like the young of a bird: as a hen pigeon or other bird hides its young in some inaccessible place for fear of the hunter, goes round, and finds the place again, so [Indra finds Soma], *aśmani anante* — in a vast rock, the mountain without measure, covered all round by creepers and thorns. In what condition? *aśmani* — in the stone. Though there were other places, why this one? He says: this Indra, the thunderer (*vajrī*), *gavāṃ vrajam iva* — as one finds a cow-pen hidden by the demon Paṇi in the earth with a stone over its door: conquering the demon, opening the door, and obtaining it; so, *sisāsan* — desiring to partake, [he found Soma]; ... And so this Indra opened (*apāvṛṇot*) the doors (*dvāraḥ*) of the waters (*iṣaḥ*, the water that is the cause of food) enclosed (*parivṛtāḥ*) by clouds all round; he made the grains and the like, desired in the fields, spread out over the earth; splitting the cloud with the thunderbolt, he gave abundance of crops by the rain: thus he did; therefore the acceptance of Soma is proper.")*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *aṅgirastamaḥ* — the best (of the Aṅgirases) among those who go against enemies; *(ayam) indraḥ* — this Indra; *vajrī* — the bearer of the thunderbolt; *gavāṃ vrajam iva* — like the cow-pen (shut by the Paṇi demon); *sisāsan* — desiring to get; *aavindat* — found; *tathā* — likewise; *(ayam* — this one); *pari-vṛtāḥ* — covered all round (by clouds); *iṣaḥ* — the food (cause: water); *dvāraḥ* — the doors; *apa avṛṇot* — opened (and); *iṣaḥ* — the grains; *parivṛtāḥ* — spread over the earth (he made); *ayam indraḥ* — this Indra; *aśmani antaḥ* — in the middle of the rocks; *guhā* — in a secret place; *nihitam* — hidden; *nidhim* — like a treasure; *anante aśmani* — in the boundless stones, the mountains etc.; *parivītam* — surrounded (by creepers and thorns); *divaḥ* — (the Soma-juice) from the world of heaven; *vaḥ* — a bird; *garbham na* — as the young one (found after a long search); *avindat* — found.

### Printed p. 429  (PDF 450)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 19 [as read].)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Indra, the foremost among those who advance against enemies, with the thunderbolt in hand, broke open the door of the cow-pen (shut by the demon Paṇi) and, as one obtains cows, found the Soma-juice; and he opened the doors of the food-giving waters covered by clouds all round, and caused the rice and other grains to spread over the earth. Therefore, as one finds, after long search, the young of a pigeon hidden by the bird, he found the Soma-juice, brought from heaven, hidden in a secret place amidst boundless rocks, in the mountains surrounded by creepers and thorns, as a treasure.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"He (Indra) found the (Soma) treasure (that had been brought) from heaven, and hidden like the nestlings of a bird in a rock; amidst (a pile of) vast rocks inclosed (by bushes): desiring to partake (of the beverage), the thunderer (found it), as the chief of the Angirasas (discovered), the hiding-place of the cows: he opened the doors (of the waters, the sources of) food, when shut up (in the clouds; the sorcerer of) food that were spread (over the earth)."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 3).**

***divaḥ avindat*** — *dyulokāt anītaṃ somam aindro labdhavān*: "Soma was at first only in heaven. The goddess Gāyatrī, in the form of a bird, brought it to the earth": this is said in the Śruti *tṛtīyasyām ito divi soma āsīt taṃ gāyatry āharat* (Tai. Br. 3-2-1-1 [?], as read "೩-೨-೧-೧" or "೩-೧-೧-೧": doubtful). "This is explained as Indra's getting it at the sacrifice."

### Printed p. 430  (PDF 451)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

***guhā nidhim*** — *atigopye parvatādau pradeśe sthāpitaṃ nidhisthānīyam*: "the Soma-creeper grows in the mountains; as a person hides a treasure (money) in a secret place, so that no one comes to know it, it is hidden, and to bring it out from there, very great effort is required": such is the idea.

***vor garbhaṃ na*** — *pakṣiṇaḥ śiśum iva*: "as the pigeon, in order that its young may not be destroyed by hunters and others, places them in a place unknown to anybody but accessible to itself, and afterwards, itself searching, finds the place with effort, so they seek this Soma": so he compares.

***aśmani anante aśmani parivītam*** — *atimahati vistṛte pāṣāṇe, aparimitapāṣāṇe parvatādau latākaṇṭakādinā parivītam*: "in places abounding with thorns and thorny shrubs, in the mountains filled with many stones, other creepers and thorn-bushes surround the Soma creeper". The word *aśman* is recorded among the names of cloud (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೩-೩೧").

> त्वमग्ने द्युभिस्त्वमाशुशुक्षणिस्त्वमद्भ्यस्त्वमश्मनस्परि ।
> त्वं वनेभ्यस्त्वमोषधीभ्यस्त्वं नृणां नृपते जायसे शुचिः ॥

> *tvam agne dyubhis tvam āśuśukṣaṇis tvam adbhyas tvam aśmanas pari |*
> *tvaṃ vanebhyas tvam oṣadhībhyas tvaṃ nṛṇāṃ nṛpate jāyase śuciḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-1, as read "೨-೧-೧".) In this Ṛk *aśmanaḥ pari* is explained as *paritaḥ sarvataḥ itaretarābhighātāt jāyase* — "Agni is born from the mutual striking of stones": hence the sense "stone" is given for *aśman*. And —

> यो हत्वाहिमरिणात्सप्त सिन्धून्यो गा उदाजदपधा वलस्य ।
> योऽश्मनोरन्तरग्निं जजान संवृक्समत्स जनास इन्द्रः ॥

> *yo hatvāhim ariṇāt sapta sindhūn yo gā udājad apadhā valasya |*
> *yo 'śmanor antar agniṃ jajāna saṃvṛk samatsu sa janāsa indraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-12-3, as read "೨-೧೨-೩".) Here he explains *aśmanoḥ* as *aśanavatyoḥ dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ* — "heaven and earth that have the thunderbolt": the word *aśman* is given the sense "heaven and earth that give food".

***vajrī gavāṃ vrajam iva sisāsan*** — *paṇinā asureṇāpahṛtaṃ bhūmau khanitvā pāṣāṇena pihitadvāraṃ gavāṃ vrajaṃ yathā tam asuraṃ jitvā dvāram udghāṭya labdhavān tadvat somaṃ sisāsan saṃbhaktum icchan*: "Indra, who bears the thunderbolt, as he found, by conquering the demon called Paṇi, who had carried off the cows and hidden them, digging in the earth and closing the door with a stone, and opening the door, the cow-pen —"

### Printed p. 431  (PDF 452)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 19 [as read].)*

(Continuing the *vajrī gavāṃ vrajam iva sisāsan* entry from p. 430:) "…as one finds the cow-pen, so Indra strove to obtain Soma": thus it is described. —

> दासपत्नीरहिगोपा अतिष्ठन्निरुद्धा आपः पणिनेव गावः ।
> अपां बिलमपिहितं यदासीद्वृत्रं जघन्वाँ अप तद्ववार ॥

> *dāsapatnīr ahigopā atiṣṭhan niruddhā āpaḥ paṇineva gāvaḥ |*
> *apāṃ bilam apihitaṃ yad āsīd vṛtraṃ jaghanvām̐ apa tad vavāra ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-11, as read "೧-೩೨-೧೧".) In this Ṛk it is told how Indra protected the cows carried off by the demon.

***aṅgirastamaḥ*** — *atiśayena śatrūn gamanaśīlaḥ aṅgāravat tejasvī vā*: "Indra is of the nature of going quickly against the enemies, or is brilliant like the sparks of Agni": so the meaning.

***indraḥ parivṛtāḥ iṣaḥ dvāraḥ apāvṛṇot*** — "Indra, by opening the waterways of the clouds that block rain on the earth, causes food to grow": so the meaning.

***iṣaḥ parivṛtāḥ*** — *iṣyamāṇāni vrīhyādyannāni bhūmau parito vyāptāny akarot*: "by splitting the cloud with the thunderbolt and making rain on the earth, he makes the rice and other grains grow and fill the earth; since Indra does this, it is proper for Indra to accept the Soma in the form of oblation at the sacrifice." The word *iṣ* is recorded among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"). In this Ṛk *iṣaḥ* is used twice; it is explained as "food, which is desired by all".

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *avindat* — root *vidḷ lābhe*; *laṅ* third person singular, *tip*; *itaś ca* drops *i*; *śa*-vikaraṇa; *śemuchadīnām* (Pā. 7-1-59) gives the augment *num*; the augment *aṭ*; since at the beginning of the *pāda*, no *nighāta*; the acute on the first syllable. *divaḥ* — *ūḍidaṃ padādi…* (Pā. 6-1-171) gives the acute to the ending. *nihitam* — root *ḍudhāñ*; *kta* in the passive; *dadhāter hiḥ* (Pā. 7-4-42) gives *hi* to the root; *gatir anantaraḥ* (Pā. 6-2-49) gives the prefix its accent. *guhā* — *supāṃ sulug* — loss of the locative ending.

### Printed p. 432  (PDF 453)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

*(Grammar, continued.)* *nidhim* — *upasarge ghoḥ kiḥ* (Pā. 3-3-92) gives the suffix *ki* after *ḍudhāñ*; *ādgholopa iṭi ca* (Pā. 6-4-64) drops the *ā*; *kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara*. *parivītam* — root *vī gatyādiṣu*; the suffix *kta* in the passive; *gatir anantaraḥ* gives the accent of the prefix (*pari*). *anante* — *na vidyate antaḥ yasya tasmin*; *nañsubhyām* gives the acute on the last syllable of the latter member. *vajrī* — *vajro 'syāsti iti vajrī*; *ata iniṭhanau* gives *ini* in the possessive sense. *sisāsan* — root *ṣaṇa sambhaktau*; *dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā* (Pā. 3-1-7) gives *san* in the sense of desire; *sanīvantardha…* (Pā. 7-2-49) by the optional rule gives no augment *iṭ*; *janasanakhanāṃ sañjhalośh* (Pā. 6-4-42) gives *ā* to the root; *sanyaṅoḥ* (Pā. 6-1-9) gives doubling; *sanyataḥ* (Pā. 7-4-79) gives *i* to the reduplicative; after it *śatṛ*; *abhyastānām ādiḥ* gives the acute on the first syllable. *avṛṇot* — root *vṛñ varaṇe*; *laṅ* third person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *parivṛtāḥ* — the root as above; *kta* in the passive; *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* (Pā. 6-3-137) gives the lengthening of the prior member; *gatir anantaraḥ* gives the prefix (*pari*) its accent. ‖ 3 ‖

> संशिशदहिहत्याय सं श्यत् [?] ।

> *dādhṛhāṇo vajramindro gabhastyoḥ kṣadmeva tigmamasanāya saṃ śyat |*
> *saṃśiśadahihatyāya saṃ śyat [?] |*
> *saṃvivyāna ojasā śavobhirindra majmanā |*
> *taṣṭeva vṛkṣaṃ vanino ni vṛścasi paraśveva ni vṛścasi ‖ 4 ‖*

### Printed p. 433  (PDF 454)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 19 [as read].)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> दाधृहाणः । वज्रम् । इन्द्रः । गभस्त्योः । क्षद्माऽइव । तिग्मम् । असनाय । सम् । श्यत् ।
> अहिऽहत्याय । सम् । श्यत् ।
> सम्ऽविव्यानः । ओजसा । शवःऽभिः । इन्द्र । मज्मना ।
> तष्टाऽइव । वृक्षम् । वनिनः । नि । वृश्चसि । परश्वाऽइव । नि । वृश्चसि ॥ ४ ॥

> *dādhṛhāṇaḥ | vajram | indraḥ | gabhastyoḥ | kṣadmā 'iva | tigmam | asanāya | sam | śyat |*
> *ahi 'hatyāya | sam | śyat |*
> *sam 'vivyānaḥ | ojasā | śavaḥ 'bhiḥ | indra | majmanā |*
> *taṣṭā 'iva | vṛkṣam | vaninaḥ | ni | vṛścasi | paraśvā 'iva | ni | vṛścasi ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अयमिन्द्रो गभस्त्योर्बाह्वोर्वज्रं दाधृहाणो दृढं गृह्णन् ॥ दृह दृहि वृद्धौ । लिटः कानच् । गभस्तिरिति बाहुनाम गभस्ती बाहू इति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥ किमर्थम् । असनाय शत्रोरुपरि क्षेपणाय । तिग्ममत्यन्ततीक्ष्णं वज्रं सं श्यत् । सम्यक् तीक्ष्णं करोति ॥ शो तनूकरणे । ओतः श्यनि लोपः । छान्दसोऽडभावः । यद्वा । लेटीतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः ॥ तत्र दृष्टान्तः । क्षद्मेव उदकमिव । उदकं यथा शत्रूणां निरसनायाभिमन्त्रणादिसंस्कारेण तीक्ष्णीक्रियते तद्वत् । क्षद्मेत्युदकनामसु क्षद्म नभ इति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥ पुनरपि तदेव विशेष्यते । अहिहत्यायाहेर्वृत्रस्य मेघस्य वा हननाय । हन्तेर्हननस्य चेति क्यप् तकारान्तादेशश्च । सं श्यत् । पूर्वमेव तीक्ष्णं सत् पुनरपि वधाय तीक्ष्णयति । हे इन्द्र ओजसा बलेन पराभिभवनसामर्थ्येन शवोभिः सेनालक्षणैर्बलैर्मज्मना शारीरेण च बलेन संविव्यानः । सम्यग्युक्तः सन् । व्येञ् संवरणे । लिटः कानच् । ग्रहिज्येति सम्प्रसारणम् । तष्टेव वृक्षम् । यथा कश्चित्तष्टा वृक्षाणां तक्षणस्य साधु कर्ता वनिनो वनसम्बन्धिनो वृक्षान्निवृश्चति स्तोपयोगाय नितरां छिनत्ति तक्षणेन तनूकरोति तथा त्वमप्यस्मान् वक्रनूचरन्तं शत्रुं नि वृश्चसि । किंच परश्वेव नि वृश्चसि । यथा परशुना कश्चिच्छैनत्ति वृक्षं तथा त्वमप्यस्मत्कृत्सिविद्वेषिर्मर्हलैर्निरामस्मद्द्वेषिणं वृश्चसि ॥

> *ayamindro gabhastyorbāhvorvajraṃ dādhṛhāṇo dṛḍhaṃ gṛhṇan ‖ dṛha dṛhi vṛddhau | liṭaḥ kānac | gabhastiriti bāhunāma gabhastī bāhū iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ kimartham | asanāya śatrorupari kṣepaṇāya | tigmamatyantatīkṣṇaṃ vajraṃ saṃ śyat | samyak tīkṣṇaṃ karoti ‖ śo tanūkaraṇe | otaḥ śyani lopaḥ | chāndaso 'ḍabhāvaḥ | yadvā | leṭītaśca lopa itīkāralopaḥ ‖ tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | kṣadmeva udakamiva | udakaṃ yathā śatrūṇāṃ nirasanāyābhimantraṇādisaṃskāreṇa tīkṣṇīkriyate tadvat | kṣadmetyudakanāmasu kṣadma nabha iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ punarapi tadeva viśeṣyate | ahihatyāyāhervṛtrasya meghasya vā hananāya | hanterhananasya ceti kyap takārāntādeśaśca | saṃ śyat | pūrvameva tīkṣṇaṃ sat punarapi vadhāya tīkṣṇayati | he indra ojasā balena parābhibhavanasāmarthyena śavobhiḥ senālakṣaṇairbalairmajmanā śārīreṇa ca balena saṃvivyānaḥ | samyagyuktaḥ san | vyeñ saṃvaraṇe | liṭaḥ kānac | grahijyeti samprasāraṇam | taṣṭeva vṛkṣam | yathā kaścittaṣṭā vṛkṣāṇāṃ takṣaṇasya sādhu kartā vanino vanasambandhino vṛkṣānnivṛścati stopayogāya nitarāṃ chinatti takṣaṇena tanūkaroti tathā tvamapyasmān vakranūcarantaṃ śatruṃ ni vṛścasi | kiṃca paraśveva ni vṛścasi | yathā paraśunā kaścicchainatti vṛkṣaṃ tathā tvamapyasmatkṛtsividveṣirmarhalairnirāmasmaddveṣiṇaṃ vṛścasi ‖*

*(Read from the image; the passages on *kṣadmeva*, the *kyap*-grammar on *ahihatyāya* and the last sentence are small and partly doubtful: [?]. Sense: "This Indra, *dādhṛhāṇaḥ* — firmly holding the thunderbolt in both his arms (*gabhastyoḥ*; *gabhasti* is a name of arm) — for what? for *asanāya* — for hurling upon the enemy — makes the sharp (*tigmam*) thunderbolt sharper still, *saṃ śyat* (root *śo* 'to sharpen'): as water (*kṣadma* — water; in the list of names of water) is made sharp by charming, to repel the enemies; again for *ahihatyāya* — for the slaying of Ahi, Vṛtra, or the cloud, he sharpens it a second time. O Indra, endowed fully (*saṃvivyānaḥ*) with strength (*ojas*), the armies (*śavobhiḥ*) and bodily strength (*majmanā*): as a carpenter cuts the trees of a forest to make them useful, so you cut the enemy who walks crooked [?] among us; and as with an axe one cuts a tree, so you cut our enemies.")*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(ayam) indraḥ* — this Indra; *gabhastyoḥ* — in both arms; *tigmam* — the sharp; *vajram* — thunderbolt; *dādhṛhāṇaḥ* — firmly holding; *asanāya* — to hurl on the enemy; *kṣadmā iva* — as water (is made sharp by charming); *(vajram* — the thunderbolt); *saṃ śyat* — makes well sharp; *ahihatyāya* — to slay Vṛtra (the cloud), to split it; *saṃ śyat* — makes sharp. *(he indra* — O Indra); *ojasā* — with the strength (of overcoming); *śavobhiḥ* — with the strength of the army; *majmanā* — and with bodily strength; *saṃvivyānaḥ* — fully endowed; *vṛkṣam* — a tree; *taṣṭā iva* — as a carpenter; *vaninaḥ* — [cuts] those of the forest; *ni vṛścasi* — you cut (our enemies); *paraśvā iva* — as with an axe (one cuts a tree); *ni vṛścasi* — you cut well (the enemies).

### Printed p. 434  (PDF 455)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Indra, holding in both hands his sharp thunderbolt in order to hurl it at the enemy, whets it, like water (made sharp by charms), and sharpens it again in order to kill Vṛtra (the cloud). O Indra, endowed with the strength that overcomes, with the strength of an army, and with the strength of body: as one cuts the trees of a forest, cut our enemies; as with an axe one cuts down a tree, cut them well.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Grasping his sharp thunderbolt with both hands, Indra whetted it to hurl it (on his foes), like the water (of an imprecation): he whetted it for the destruction of Ahi. Indra, you are fully endowed with strength, with energy, with might, you cut (our enemies) to pieces, as a woodcutter the trees of a forest; you cut them to pieces as if with a hatchet."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 4).**

***gabhastyoḥ*** — *bāhvoḥ*: the word *gabhasti* is recorded among the names of rays (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೩-೧೪") and among the names of arm (Ni. 2-[?]; "೨-೯"); the meaning "arm" is given here.

***tigmam*** — *atyantatīkṣṇam*: the word *tigma* is recorded among the names of the thunderbolt (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೧೧"). —

> इमा रुद्राय स्थिरधन्वने गिरः क्षिप्रेषवे देवाय स्वधावने ।
> अषाळ्हाय सहमानाय वेधसे तिग्मायुधाय भरता शृणोतु नः ॥

> *imā rudrāya sthiradhanvane giraḥ kṣipreṣave devāya svadhāvane |*
> *aṣāḷhāya sahamānāya vedhase tigmāyudhāya bharatā śṛṇotu naḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-33-[?], as read "೨-೩೩-೧"; the first line is printed differently and I give it as read: [?].) In this Ṛk *tigmāyudhāya* is explained as "to him whose weapon is sharp"; *tigmaṃ tejateḥ utsāhakarmaṇaḥ* (Ni. 10-[?]; as read "೧೦-೭") is the explanation: here the word is used as an epithet of the thunderbolt, in the sense "very sharp".

### Printed p. 435  (PDF 456)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 19 [as read].)*

***kṣadmeva*** — *udakam iva*: the word *kṣadma* is recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೩೪"?) and among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?]; "೨-೯"?). "*udakaṃ yathā śatrūṇāṃ nirasanāyābhimantraṇādisaṃskāreṇa tīkṣṇīkaroti tadvat*" — "as water is made sharp by being charmed with mantras for destroying the enemies, so Indra, holding in his hands the thunderbolt, makes it very sharp when destroying enemies": this is the illustration given.

***ahihatyāya*** — *aher vṛtrasya meghasya vā hananāya*: the Niruktakāra explains the meaning with the explanation: *ahir ayanād eti, ā-hanter vā*; *ahir ayam apīta iro 'hir eti*, *ahir meghaḥ nirhrasitopasarga āhantīti* (as read; small type, doubtful: [?]): from the root *iṇ* (to go) "*ayanāt*" (because it moves), or the root *han* with *ā*: *āhanti*, "strikes". The word *ahi* is recorded among the names of cloud (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೧೦") and of water (Ni. 1-[?], "೧-೩೪"). Sāyaṇa explains the meaning "Indra makes the thunderbolt sharper, in order to slay the demon Vṛtra, the enemy, or to destroy the cloud, which is naturally sharp [?]".

***ojasā, majmanā, śavobhiḥ*** — *parābhibhavasāmarthyena śārīreṇa balena senālakṣaṇair balaiḥ*: the word *ojas* is recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; "೧-೩೪") and of strength (Ni. 2-[?]; "೨-೯"); *majmanā* among the names of strength (Ni. 2-[?], "೨-೯"); and *śavas* among the names of water and strength. Since these three words are recorded among the names of strength and convey the same sense "strength", Sāyaṇa distinguishes among them: *ojas* is the power of overcoming others, *majman* is bodily strength, and *śavas* is the strength of an army (as warriors and the like). Indra is described as being endowed with these three strengths.

***taṣṭeva vṛkṣaṃ vanino ni vṛścasi*** — *vṛkṣāṇāṃ takṣaṇasya sādhukartā vanasambandhino vṛkṣān stopabhogāya yathā nitarāṃ chinatti*: "as a carpenter, who cuts the trees of the forest so that they may be used, does the work of cutting the tree; and *paraśveva nivṛścasi* — as with an axe one cuts the trees; so Indra, by his three kinds of strength, destroys the enemies of the sacrificers": the carpenter's work is the comparison.

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *dādhṛhāṇaḥ* — root *dṛha dṛhi vṛddhau*; when *liṭ* follows, *liṭaḥ kānajvā* (Pā. 3-2-106) gives *kānac*; the root is doubled; since *ur* ends, *urat* gives *at*; *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* leaves the first consonant; the long vowel of the reduplicative is Vedic; since the suffix has *k*-marker the *n* [as read]; *citaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the acute on the last syllable. *vajram* — root *vaja gatau*; *ujjer…* [as read: *ṛjendrāgravajra…* Uṇ. 2-28] gives *ran* by irregular formation; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable. *tigmam* — root *tija niśāne*; *yujirucitijāṃ kuś ca* (Uṇ. 1-[?]) gives *mak*; *ku* for the final *j* of the root; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. *asanāya* — root *asu kṣepaṇe*; *lyuṭ* in the abstract sense; *yuvor anākau* (Pā. 7-1-1) gives *ana*; *liti* gives the acute before the suffix. *śyat* — root *śo tanūkaraṇe*, *divādi*; *laṅ* third person singular, *tip*; *itaś ca* drops *i*; *divādibhyaḥ śyan* (Pā. 3-1-69) gives *śyan*; *ote śyani* (Pā. 7-3-71) drops the *o* of the root; *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi* gives no augment *aṭ*; or by *leṭi*, *itaś ca lopaḥ* drops *i*. *ahihatyāya* — *aher hatyaṃ tasmai*; root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *hanas ta ca* (Pā. 3-1-97) gives *kyap*; *t* replaces the root's end; since *p*-marked the root's accent remains; *kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara*. *saṃvivyānaḥ* — root *vyeñ saṃvaraṇe*; when *liṭ* follows, *liṭaḥ kānac* gives *kānac*; since *k*-marked, *grahijyāvayi…* (Pā. 6-1-16) gives *saṃprasāraṇa*, *pūrvarūpa*; *vi + āna* by *yaṇ*; *citaḥ* gives the acute on the last syllable; in the compound *kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara*. *taṣṭā* — root *takṣū tanūkaraṇe*; *tṛn* in the agent sense; *skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca* (Pā. 8-2-29) drops the *k*; *ṣatva* of the suffix; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable. *vaninaḥ* — *vanam asyāsti iti vanī, tasya*; *ini* in the possessive sense; genitive singular.

### Printed p. 437  (PDF 458)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 19 [as read].)*

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *vṛścasi* — root *oścū chedane*; *laṭ* second person singular; because it follows a finite verb, *nighāta*. *paraśvā* — *paraṃ śṛṇāti iti paraśuḥ*; root *śṝ hiṃsāyām*; *ajiśṛbhyāṃ…* [as read: *ājñāsarayoḥ khanibhyāṃ ḍit*, Uṇ. 1-[?]] gives *u* after *śṝ* with the *ḍit* marker; because of *ḍit* the *ṭi* (*ṛ*) drops; the acute on the last syllable by the suffix; by the statement *jasādiṣu chandasi vā vacanam* [as read] the instrumental singular following does not give *nā*; *yaṇ* substitution; *udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt* (Pā. 6-1-174) gives the acute to the ending. ‖ 4 ‖

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वं वृथा नद्य इन्द्र सर्तवेऽच्छा समुद्रमसृजो रथाँ इव वाजयतो रथाँ इव ।
> इतः ऊतीरयुञ्जत समानमर्थमक्षितम् ।
> धेनूरिव मनवे विश्वदोहसो जनाय विश्वदोहसः ॥ ५ ॥

> *tvaṃ vṛthā nadya indra sartave 'cchā samudramasṛjo rathā~ iva vājayato rathā~ iva |*
> *itaḥ ūtīrayuñjata samānamarthamakṣitam |*
> *dhenūriva manave viśvadohaso janāya viśvadohasaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वम् । वृथा । नद्यः । इन्द्र । सर्तवे । अच्छ । समुद्रम् । असृजः । रथान्ऽइव । वाजयतः । रथान्ऽइव ।
> इतः । ऊतीः । अयुञ्जत । समानम् । अर्थम् । अक्षितम् ।
> धेनूःऽइव । मनवे । विश्वऽदोहसः । जनाय । विश्वऽदोहसः ॥ ५ ॥

> *tvam | vṛthā | nadyaḥ | indra | sartave | accha | samudram | asṛjaḥ | rathān 'iva | vājayataḥ | rathān 'iva |*
> *itaḥ | ūtīḥ | ayuñjata | samānam | artham | akṣitam |*
> *dhenūḥ 'iva | manave | viśva 'dohasaḥ | janāya | viśva 'dohasaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

*(Read from the image. The Saṃhitā prints "*itaḥ ūtīr ayuñjata*"; the Pada gives *itaḥ | ūtīḥ | ayuñjata*; *rathān-iva*, *vājayataḥ*.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; small type, partly doubtful: [?]).*

> हे इन्द्र त्वं वृथा प्रयत्नेनैव । अनायासेनैवेत्यर्थः । नद्यो नदीः समुद्रमच्छाभिमुख्येन सर्तवे प्रसर्तुमसृजः । मेघं निर्भिद्योत्पादितवानसि । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । रथानिव । यथा त्वं रथानस्मद्यागं प्रत्येतुं सर्तवे अभिमुखेन प्रासृजः सृष्टवानसि तद्वत् । किंच वाजयतो रथानिव । सङ्ग्रामं वा वाजमन्नमभिलषन्तो राजादयो रथान् यथा सृजन्ति तद्वत् । कृ . ... जन्तात् शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ किंचेतोऽस्मत्सन्निधिदेशम् ॥ द्वितीयार्थे तसिल् । अस्मान् प्रत्योतीरूतयो गमनवत्यो रक्षणवत्यो वा नद्यः समानमर्थं समानप्रयोजनवदक्षितमुदकमयुञ्जत । योजितवत्यः । त्वत्प्रसादादिति भावः ॥ अर्थशब्द उदकविशेषः सन्नपुंसकलिङ्गः । अक्षितमित्युदकनामसु अक्षितं बर्हिरिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । मनवे मनोरर्थाय धेनूरिव धेनवो यथा विश्वदोहसः सर्वार्थं दोग्ध्र्यो भवन्ति । यथा वा जनाय यस्मै कस्मै चिज्जनायार्थाय तदर्थं विश्वदोहसो भवन्ति सर्वक्षीरप्रदा भवन्ति । यद्वा । जनाय सर्वजनार्थं सस्यादीनभिलक्ष्य नद्यो विश्वदोहसः सम्पूर्णदोग्ध्र्यो भवन्ति । सर्वत्र प्रवहन्ति । अत्र नद्यः प्रीणनादिदोहस इत्युपचर्यते । ऊर्ध्वगग्रामनुपकारिवृष्टिप्रद इतीन्द्रस्यैव स्तुतिः ॥

> *he indra tvaṃ vṛthā prayatnenaiva | anāyāsenaivetyarthaḥ | nadyo nadīḥ samudramacchābhimukhyena sartave prasartumasṛjaḥ | meghaṃ nirbhidyotpāditavānasi | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | rathāniva | yathā tvaṃ rathānasmadyāgaṃ pratyetuṃ sartave abhimukhena prāsṛjaḥ sṛṣṭavānasi tadvat | kiṃca vājayato rathāniva | saṅgrāmaṃ vā vājamannamabhilaṣanto rājādayo rathān yathā sṛjanti tadvat | kṛ . ... jantāt śaturanuma iti vibhakterudāttatvam ‖ kiṃceto 'smatsannidhideśam ‖ dvitīyārthe tasil | asmān pratyotīrūtayo gamanavatyo rakṣaṇavatyo vā nadyaḥ samānamarthaṃ samānaprayojanavadakṣitamudakamayuñjata | yojitavatyaḥ | tvatprasādāditi bhāvaḥ ‖ arthaśabda udakaviśeṣaḥ sannapuṃsakaliṅgaḥ | akṣitamityudakanāmasu akṣitaṃ barhiriti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | manave manorarthāya dhenūriva dhenavo yathā viśvadohasaḥ sarvārthaṃ dogdhryo bhavanti | yathā vā janāya yasmai kasmai cijjanāyārthāya tadarthaṃ viśvadohaso bhavanti sarvakṣīrapradā bhavanti | yadvā | janāya sarvajanārthaṃ sasyādīnabhilakṣya nadyo viśvadohasaḥ sampūrṇadogdhryo bhavanti | sarvatra pravahanti | atra nadyaḥ prīṇanādidohasa ityupacaryate | ūrdhvagagrāmanupakārivṛṣṭiprada itīndrasyaiva stutiḥ ‖*

*(Sense: "O Indra, *vṛthā* — without effort — you released the rivers to flow (*sartave*) toward the sea, splitting the cloud. The example: as you released chariots toward our sacrifice, so; and as kings and others eager for battle or food send forth chariots. And hence the flowing rivers (*ūtīḥ*) — those that go or protect — yoked (*ayuñjata*) to the common purpose water that does not diminish (*akṣitam*): by your grace. *Artha* is a kind of water [neuter]. *Akṣita* is recorded among the names of water and of *barhis*. The example: as cows, for Manu or for any person whomever, are *viśvadohasaḥ* — yielding all milk — so, or: the rivers, for all people, looking to the crops and so on, yield fully and flow everywhere; here the rivers are said, figuratively, to 'milk' through gratification. This is a praise of Indra alone, the giver of rain beneficial to all.")*

### Printed p. 438  (PDF 459)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he) indra* — O Indra; *tvam* — you; *vṛthā* — without effort; *nadyaḥ* — the rivers; *samudram accha* — toward the sea; *sartave* — to flow; *rathān iva* — as chariots (are sent toward our sacrifice); *(kiṃ ca* — and); *vājayataḥ* — (kings and others) desiring battle or food; *rathān iva* — as chariots (are sent); *asṛjaḥ* — you released (splitting the clouds); *(kiṃ ca* — and also); *itaḥ* — here (toward the place near us); *ūtīḥ* — the rivers that flow (and protect us); *samānam* — equal; *arthaṃ* — in purpose; *akṣitam* — water; *manave* — for the sake of Manu; *dhenūḥ iva* — as cows; *viśvadohasaḥ* — milking all things; *janāya* — for any man; *(dhenūr iva viśvadohasaḥ* — cows give milk fully); or *janāya* — for the people; *viśvadohasaḥ (iva)* — the rivers (flow and make crops grow, bringing the desired fruits); *ayuñjata* — [by your favour] have yoked.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, you, effortlessly, send the rivers toward the sea by splitting the clouds, as one sends chariots to our sacrifice, or as kings eager for battle or food send chariots; and here, the rivers that flow close to us (protecting us) are united in one purpose with the water that does not waste away; for Manu, as cows yield all things, and for all people as cows yield milk in full, all the rivers, flowing everywhere, make crops grow and bring all desired fruits.
