### Printed p. 439  (PDF 460)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 19 [as read].)*

*(Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 5, concluded from p. 438:)* "…as cows give all things to Manu, or as they are milked for all men, so the rivers (as if milked) join their water (in a single purpose)."

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"You have without effort created the rivers (that are) to flow to the sea, like chariots (bearing you to sacrifices), as those (construct) chariots who are desirous of (going to) battle: (the streams) flowing hither have gathered together their water for a common purpose, like the cows that yielded all things to Manu; that yield all things to man."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 5).**

***rathān iva vājayato rathān iva*** — *tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ yathā tvaṃ rathān asmadyāgaṃ prati abhimukhyena prāptuṃ asṛṣṭavān asi tadvat | saṅgrāmam annaṃ vā icchanto rājādayo rathān iva | te yathā saṅgrāmaṃ prati oṣadhyādikaṃ vātisartuṃ rathān sṛjanti tadvat*: "Indra, whatever effort he makes, causes the rivers to bring together their water to the sea — splitting the cloud and giving abundant water in the rivers. In this matter two comparisons are given: the first sentence means 'as a chariot is built to bring us to the sacrifice of those who sacrifice'; in the second, kings and others who wish to fight, or to collect grain and the like, prepare chariots and cause them to run swiftly to the various places: so" is the meaning.

The word ***vāja*** is recorded among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯") and among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?]); *ṛbhukṣā viśvā vāja iti* (Ni. 11-[?]; as read "೧೧-೧೭") is said also of a certain name [?]. —

> पावका नः सरस्वती वाजेभिर्वाजिनीवती । यज्ञं वष्टु धियावसुः ॥

> *pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī vājebhir vājinīvatī | yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-10, as read.) In this Ṛk *vājebhiḥ* is explained as *annena haviṣā udakena vā tadvatī* — hence the word *vāja* is used in the senses "food" and "water". Sāyaṇa too, for *vājayataḥ*, gives the meaning "battle or food".

***ūtīḥ akṣitam ayuñjata*** — *gamanavatyo rakṣaṇavatyo vā nadyaḥ udakaṃ yojitavatyaḥ*: the word *akṣita* is recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೩೪"). The word *ūti*

### Printed p. 440  (PDF 461)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

(continued:) …is explained: —

> आ त्वा रथं यथोतये सुम्नाय वर्तयामसि ।
> तुविकूर्मिमृतीषहमिन्द्र शविष्ठ सत्पते ॥

> *ā tvā rathaṃ yathotaye sumnāya vartayāmasi |*
> *tuvikūrmim ṛtīṣaham indra śaviṣṭha satpate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-68-1, as read "೮-೬೮-೧"; small type, doubtful: [?].) In this Ṛk *ūtaye* is explained as *avanāt* (Ni. 11-[?]; as read "೧೧-೨") — "protection". Here the sense "flowing or protecting" is given and is used as an epithet of the rivers.

"That the rivers join their water, to be of use to those who perform the sacrifice, is through Indra's favour": so he describes.

***manave dhenūr iva viśvadohasaḥ, janāya viśvadohasaḥ*** — these two sentences are also stated in the form of an illustration. The rivers are compared to cows: as cows give a person such as Manu all that is needed, so the rivers are useful. And that the rivers flow so as to be favourable to all people and be useful to the life of crops and so on, and do many benefits, is compared; thus he praises Indra, who gives the rain that causes the rivers to do such services.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *sartave* — root *sṛ gatau*; when *tumartha* is intended, *tumarthe sese…* (Pā. 3-4-9) gives *tavai*; [the form *tavenn*]; guṇa of the root with *raparatva* by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*; *jñityādir nityam* (Pā. 6-1-197) gives the acute on the first syllable; *kṛn mejantaḥ* (Pā. 1-1-39) gives the name of an indeclinable. *accha* — *nipātasya ca* (Pā. 6-3-136) gives the long vowel in the Saṃhitā. *asṛjaḥ* — root *sṛja visarge*, *tudādi*; *laṅ* second person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta* since it follows a finite verb. *vājayataḥ* — *vājam ātmana icchanti vājayanti*; *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. 3-1-8) gives *kyac*; *na chandasy apuṭrasya* (Pā. 7-4-35) forbids lengthening and the like; after the *kyac*-ending, *śatṛ* in the present sense; accusative plural; since *num*-less, the case-ending after *śatṛ* gets *catur…* [as read: *śatur anumo nadyajādī*, Pā. 6-1-173] the acute. *ūtīḥ* — *ūtiyūtijūti…* (Pā. 3-3-97) gives *ktic* with the acute on the last syllable, irregular; the plural following, *supāṃ sulug…* (Pā. 7-1-39) lengthens the previous vowel.

### Printed p. 441  (PDF 462)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 19 [as read].)*

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *ayuñjata* — root *yujir yoge*, *rudhādi*; *laṅ* third person plural; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *artham* — root *ṛ gatau*; *uṣikuṣigarbhibhyaḥ than* (Uṇ. 2-[?]) gives *than*; guṇa of the root; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable; though masculine, here, being an epithet of the neuter *akṣitam*, it is neuter. *viśvadohasaḥ* — *viśvaṃ dohaḥ yāsāṃ tāḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* gives the accent of the first member. ‖ 5 ‖

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> इमां ते वाचं वसूयन्त आयवो रथं न धीरः स्वपा अतक्षिषुः ।
> सुम्नाय त्वामतक्षिषुः ।
> शुम्भन्तो जेन्यं यथा वाजेषु विप्र वाजिनम् ।
> अत्यमिव शवसे सातये धना विश्वा धनानि सातये ॥ ६ ॥

> *imāṃ te vācaṃ vasūyanta āyavo rathaṃ na dhīraḥ svapā atakṣiṣuḥ |*
> *sumnāya tvāmatakṣiṣuḥ |*
> *śumbhanto jenyaṃ yathā vājeṣu vipra vājinam |*
> *atyamiva śavase sātaye dhanā viśvā dhanāni sātaye ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सुम्नाय । त्वाम् । अतक्षिषुः ।
> शुम्भन्तः । जेन्यम् । यथा । वाजेषु । विप्र । वाजिनम् ।

### Printed p. 442  (PDF 463)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; small type, doubtful places [?]).*

> हे इन्द्र ते त्वदर्थं वसूयन्तो धनमात्मन इच्छन्त आयवो दातव्यहविरूपान्नवन्त ऋत्विजः ॥ आयव इति मनुष्यनामसु पाठात् ॥ इमां क्रियमाणां स्तुतिरूपां वाचमतक्षिषुः । सम्पादितवन्तः । स्वपाः शोभनकर्मवान् कुशली ॥ बहुव्रीहौ सोर्मनसी इत्यत्र पदाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ धीरो धीमान् रथं न रथमिव । तं यथा प्रयत्नेन साधु करोति तद्वत् । एवं कृत्वा त्वां सुम्नाय सुखायातक्षिषुः । अनुकूलमुत्पादयन्ति । सुम्नमिति सुखनाम । सुम्नं सुग्मियमिति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥ किंच हे विप्र मेधाविन्निन्द्र वाजेषु सङ्ग्रामेषु वाजिनं वेगवन्तं त्वां शुम्भन्तो गुणैर्दीपयन्त उत्कृष्टं कुर्वन्तो ऋत्विजः स्तुत्या प्रीणयन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । जेन्यं यथा जयशीलं शूरं यथा भटाः स्तुवन्ति तद्वत् । यद्वा । जेन्यं जयशीलं वाजिनं वेगवन्तमश्वं वाजेषु सङ्ग्रामेषु यथोत्साहयन्ति तद्वत् । किंच शवसे बलाय धना धनानां सातये लाभाय च स्तुम इति शेषः । ऊतियूतिजूतिसातीत्यादिना क्तिन उदात्तत्वम् ॥ न केवलं धनमात्रं किंतु विश्वा धनानि सातये कृत्स्नानि प्रीणनसाधनानि गवादिधनानि । षष्ठ्यर्थे द्वितीया । तेषां लाभाय । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । धना धने सङ्ग्रामे शवसे वैरिजयसाधनबलाय सातये तेषामेव धनानां प्राप्तये चात्यमिवाश्वमिव सततगामिनमश्वमिव । तं यथा स्तुवन्ति तद्वत् ॥

> *he indra te tvadarthaṃ vasūyanto dhanamātmana icchanta āyavo dātavyahavirūpānnavanta ṛtvijaḥ ‖ āyava iti manuṣyanāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ imāṃ kriyamāṇāṃ stutirūpāṃ vācamatakṣiṣuḥ | sampāditavantaḥ | svapāḥ śobhanakarmavān kuśalī ‖ bahuvrīhau sormanasī ityatra padādyudāttatvam ‖ dhīro dhīmān rathaṃ na rathamiva | taṃ yathā prayatnena sādhu karoti tadvat | evaṃ kṛtvā tvāṃ sumnāya sukhāyātakṣiṣuḥ | anukūlamutpādayanti | sumnamiti sukhanāma | sumnaṃ sugmiyamiti tannāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ kiṃca he vipra medhāvinnindra vājeṣu saṅgrāmeṣu vājinaṃ vegavantaṃ tvāṃ śumbhanto guṇairdīpayanta utkṛṣṭaṃ kurvanto ṛtvijaḥ stutyā prīṇayanti | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | jenyaṃ yathā jayaśīlaṃ śūraṃ yathā bhaṭāḥ stuvanti tadvat | yadvā | jenyaṃ jayaśīlaṃ vājinaṃ vegavantamaśvaṃ vājeṣu saṅgrāmeṣu yathotsāhayanti tadvat | kiṃca śavase balāya dhanā dhanānāṃ sātaye lābhāya ca stuma iti śeṣaḥ | ūtiyūtijūtisātītyādinā ktina udāttatvam ‖ na kevalaṃ dhanamātraṃ kiṃtu viśvā dhanāni sātaye kṛtsnāni prīṇanasādhanāni gavādidhanāni | ṣaṣṭhyarthe dvitīyā | teṣāṃ lābhāya | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | dhanā dhane saṅgrāme śavase vairijayasādhanabalāya sātaye teṣāmeva dhanānāṃ prāptaye cātyamivāśvamiva satatagāminamaśvamiva | taṃ yathā stuvanti tadvat ‖*

*(Sense: "O Indra, for you the *āyavaḥ* — priests, who desire wealth and have food in the form of oblation to give (*āyu* is recorded among the names of man) — have fashioned (*atakṣiṣuḥ*) this praise-speech being made; *svapāḥ* — skilled, doing good work, wise — as a skilful man makes a chariot well by effort, so they made it. Having done so, they have made you favourable for *sumna*, happiness (*sumna* is a name of happiness). And, O wise Indra, the priests adorn you with qualities, glorify you, swift in battles, as soldiers praise a conquering hero; or as one encourages a swift horse in battle. And we praise you for strength, for the gaining of wealth; not wealth alone but all kinds of wealth such as cows, the means of satisfaction. The example: as one praises a swift horse that always runs, for victory in battle, for the gaining of that very wealth.")*

### Printed p. 443  (PDF 464)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read: "೨೦"].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he indra* — O Indra); *vasūyantaḥ* — desirous of wealth; *āyavaḥ* — the priests who have food in the form of oblation to give; *svapāḥ* — skilful; *dhīraḥ* — wise (man); *rathaṃ na* — as (he prepares) a chariot (with effort); *te* — for you; *imāṃ* — this; *vācam* — word (of praise); *atakṣiṣuḥ* — have fashioned; *tvām* — you; *sumnāya* — for their happiness; *atakṣiṣuḥ* — have made favourable; *(he vipra* — O wise Indra); *vājeṣu* — in battles; *vājinam* — the swift; *śumbhantaḥ* — adorning (with qualities in praise); *jenyaṃ yathā* — as a victorious hero (is praised by soldiers) or as a swift horse is encouraged in battle; *(ātakṣiṣuḥ* — they please with words of praise); *(kiṃ ca* — and); *śavase* — for strength; *dhanā* — of wealth; *sātaye* — for gaining; *viśvā dhanāni* — all kinds of wealth such as cows; *sātaye* — for gaining; *atyam iva* — as (they praise) the best horse (that wins battle); *(stumaḥ* — we praise you).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, the priests who desire wealth and have food in the form of oblation, have fashioned this praise for you, as a wise and skilful man makes a chariot, to make you favourable to their happiness; O wise one, the sages praise you, swift in battle, as soldiers praise a victorious hero; we too praise you for strength, wealth and all kinds of affluence, as they praise an excellent horse for victory in battle.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Men who are desirous of wealth have recited this your praise, as a resolute and provident man (prepares) a chariot (for a journey): they have propitiated you for their good: glorifying you, sage Indra, as impetuous in conflicts, they have praised you (as men praise) a conqueror. We praise you for (the acquirement of) strength, wealth, and every kind of affluence; as (they commend) a courser (for his good qualities) in battle."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 6).**

***vasūyantaḥ āyavaḥ*** — *dhanamātmana icchantaḥ dātavyahavirūpānnavantaḥ ṛtvijaḥ*: the word *āyu* is recorded among the names of man (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೩"): "the priests who have food in the form of oblations to be given to the gods in the sacrifice". Also it is described that these priests praise Indra with these Ṛks with the wish that wealth may come to them.

***svapāḥ dhīraḥ rathaṃ na*** — *śobhanakarmavān kuśalī dhīmān rathamiva | taṃ yathā prayatnena sādhu karoti tadvat*: the word *svapāḥ* —

> आ नो यज्ञं भारती तूयमेत्विळा मनुष्वदिह चेतयन्ती ।
> तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं स्योनं सरस्वती स्वपसः सदन्तु ॥

> *ā no yajñaṃ bhāratī tūyam etv iḷā manuṣvad iha cetayantī |*
> *tisro devīr barhir edaṃ syonaṃ sarasvatī svapasaḥ sadantu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-8, as read "೧೦-೧೧೦-೮".) is used in this Ṛk in the sense "doing good deeds".

"One who does good work, who is wise, by his own effort prepares the chariot"; the meaning of this is that

---

### Printed p. 444  (PDF 465)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

(Special Topics of Ṛk 6, continued from p. 443:) "…"; so Indra is compared to one whom the priests make favourable to themselves, turned toward them.

***sumnāya*** — *sukhāya*: the word *sumna* is recorded among the twenty-[?] names of happiness, *śambaḥ* and the others (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೪"): "the priests praise Indra in order that Indra may give them happiness."

***vipra*** — *medhāvin indra*: the word *vipra* is recorded among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19 [?]; as read "೩-೧೯"); addressing Indra as *vipra*, he explains it as "O wise one".

***jenyaṃ yathā*** — *jayaśīlaṃ śūraṃ yathā bhaṭāḥ stuvanti tadvat | yadvā | jenyaṃ jayaśīlaṃ vegavantam aśvaṃ saṅgrāmeṣu yathotsāhayanti tadvat*: "as soldiers praise a victorious hero, or as one encourages a swift horse that gives victory in battle; as the young soldiers praise Indra with praises that make known his qualities, and so give him joy": the meaning is explained by comparing him both to the hero and to the horse.

***atyam iva viśvā dhanāni sātaye*** — *kṛtsnāni prīṇanasādhanāni gavādidhanāni teṣāṃ lābhāya | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ atyam iveti*: the word *atya* is recorded among the names of horse (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೩೨"). In the sentence before it, *śavase dhanā sātaye stumaḥ*, Indra is praised in order that he may grant strength and wealth; in this sentence Indra is praised that the priests may obtain the cows and wealth that are the means of performing the sacrifices that please Indra: so the meaning is given. "As, in order to have strength and wealth in battle, and also to obtain the wealth of enemies by victory, one praises and encourages a swift horse that always runs, here Indra is praised": so the meaning is described by comparison to the horse.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *vasūyantaḥ* — *vasum ātmana icchantaḥ*; *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. 3-1-8) gives *kyac*; *akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ* (Pā. 7-4-25) lengthens the previous vowel; after the *kyac*-ending *śatṛ* in the present sense; the accent of *kyac* remains. *āyavaḥ* — root *iṇ gatau*; *chandasīṇaḥ* (Uṇ. 1-3 [?]) gives *uṇ*; *ac oñciñ…* [as read: *aco ñṇiti*, Pā. 7-2-115] gives *vṛddhi*; *ayādeśa*; acute on the last syllable.

### Printed p. 445  (PDF 466)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

*(Grammar, continued.)* *dhīraḥ* — root *dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *susūdhāgṛdhibhyaḥ kran* (Uṇ. 2-[?]) gives *kran*; *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali* (Pā. 6-4-66) gives *ī*; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable. *svapāḥ* — *śobhanam apaḥ yasya saḥ svapāḥ*; since *su* is not accented [as read] *soḥ manasī aloma-ṣoṣasī* (Pā. 6-2-117) gives, against the accent of *su*, the acute on the first syllable of the latter member. *atakṣiṣuḥ* — root *takṣū tanūkaraṇe*; *luṅ* third person plural; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *śumbhantaḥ* — root *śubha śobhārthe*; *śatṛ* in the present sense; *tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ* (Pā. 3-1-77) gives *śa*; the accent of the *vikaraṇa* remains; nominative plural. *jenyam* — root *ji jaye*; *ṇyat* [as read *enya*] by *āto yat* [?], with the Uṇādi sense; acute on the first syllable of the suffix. *vipra* — root *ḍuvap bījasantāne*; *ujjendrāgrā…* (Uṇ. 2-[?]) gives *ran* by irregular formation; in the vocative *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. 8-1-19) gives *nighāta*. *sātaye* — root *ṣaṇa dāne*; *ūtiyūtijūti…* (Pā. 3-3-97) gives *ktin* acute irregularly; dative singular. *dhanā viśvā* — neuter plural; *śeś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. 6-1-70) drops *śi*; by the suffix [*ā*], the accusative is used in the sense of the genitive. ‖ 6 ‖

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> भिनत्पुरो नवतिमिन्द्र पूरवे दिवोदासाय महि दाशुषे नृतो वज्रेण दाशुषे नृतो ।
> अतिथिग्वाय शम्बरं गिरेरुग्रो अवाभरत् ।
> महो धनानि दयमान ओजसा विश्वा धनान्योजसा ॥ ७ ॥

> *bhinatpuro navatimindra pūrave divodāsāya mahi dāśuṣe nṛto vajreṇa dāśuṣe nṛto |*
> *atithigvāya śambaraṃ girerugro avābharat |*
> *maho dhanāni dayamāna ojasā viśvā dhanānyojasā ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> भिनत् । पुरः । नवतिम् । इन्द्र । पूरवे । दिवःऽदासाय । महि । दाशुषे । नृतो इति । वज्रेण । दाशुषे । नृतो इति ।
> अतिथिऽग्वाय । शम्बरम् । गिरेः । उग्रः । अव । अभरत् ।
> महः । धनानि । दयमानः । ओजसा । विश्वा । धनानि । ओजसा ॥ ७ ॥

> *atithi 'gvāya | śambaram | gireḥ | ugraḥ | ava | abharat |*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; small type, partly doubtful: [?]).*

> हे इन्द्र नृतो रणे नर्तनशीलस्त्वं दाशुषे हविर्दात्रे पूरवे [?] । मनुष्यनामैतत् । महि महते दिवोदासायैतन्नाम्ने राज्ञे ॥ दिवो दासे षष्ठ्या अलुक् । का. ६-३-२१-२४ [?] इत्यलुक् ॥ दिवोदासादीनां छन्दसीति पूर्वपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ नवतिमेतत्सङ्ख्याकानि पुरः शत्रूणां पुराणि भिनत् भिन्नवानसि । तथा हे नृतो गात्रविक्षेपणकुशल हस्तपादादिप्रक्षेपेण शत्रूणां हिंसक वज्रेण क्षेपणसमर्थेनायुधेन दाशुषे हविर्दात्रे दिवोदासायान्यस्मै वा भिनत् । कंसमपि शत्रुं भिन्नवानसि । इदानीं परोक्षमाह । अतिथिग्वाय पूजार्थमतिथिं गच्छते दिवोदासाय तदर्थम् ॥ गमेरौणादिको ड्वप्रत्ययः ॥ उग्र उद्गूर्णबल इन्द्रः पूर्वं पुरभेदनसमये विद्धमुष्मिन् [?] म्रियमाणं गिरिनारूढं शम्बरमेतन्नामानमसुरं गिरेर्दुर्गमात्पर्वतादेः सकाशादोजसा स्वकीयेन बलेनावाभरत् । अवाङ्मुखमवक्षस्य [?] प्राणं हृतवान् । किं कुर्वन् । महो महान्ति धनानि तदीयगवाश्वादीनि दयमानो दिवोदासाय राज्ञे साधयन् । दय दानगतिहिंसादानेषु । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे शानचो लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः ॥ न केवलमल्पं धनं किंतु विश्वा धनानि सर्वाण्यपि तेषां मणिमुक्तादीन्योजसा स्वकीयेन बलेन दयमानः साधयन्नावाभरत् ॥

> *he indra nṛto raṇe nartanaśīlastvaṃ dāśuṣe havirdātre pūrave [?] | manuṣyanāmaitat | mahi mahate divodāsāyaitannāmne rājñe ‖ divo dāse ṣaṣṭhyā aluk | kā. 6-3-21-24 [?] ityaluk ‖ divodāsādīnāṃ chandasīti pūrvapadādyudāttatvam ‖ navatimetatsaṅkhyākāni puraḥ śatrūṇāṃ purāṇi bhinat bhinnavānasi | tathā he nṛto gātravikṣepaṇakuśala hastapādādiprakṣepeṇa śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsaka vajreṇa kṣepaṇasamarthenāyudhena dāśuṣe havirdātre divodāsāyānyasmai vā bhinat | kaṃsamapi śatruṃ bhinnavānasi | idānīṃ parokṣamāha | atithigvāya pūjārthamatithiṃ gacchate divodāsāya tadartham ‖ gamerauṇādiko ḍvapratyayaḥ ‖ ugra udgūrṇabala indraḥ pūrvaṃ purabhedanasamaye viddhamuṣmin [?] mriyamāṇaṃ girinārūḍhaṃ śambarametannāmānamasuraṃ girerdurgamātparvatādeḥ sakāśādojasā svakīyena balenāvābharat | avāṅmukhamavakṣasya [?] prāṇaṃ hṛtavān | kiṃ kurvan | maho mahānti dhanāni tadīyagavāśvādīni dayamāno divodāsāya rājñe sādhayan | daya dānagatihiṃsādāneṣu | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatve śānaco lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvaraḥ ‖ na kevalamalpaṃ dhanaṃ kiṃtu viśvā dhanāni sarvāṇyapi teṣāṃ maṇimuktādīnyojasā svakīyena balena dayamānaḥ sādhayannāvābharat ‖*

*(Sense: "O Indra, *nṛto* — dancing (with delight) in battle — for *pūrave* — [a man] — the giver of oblations, for the great *Divodāsa* (a king by that name) you *bhinat* — broke ninety (*navatim*) cities (*puraḥ*) of enemies; and, O dancer, skilful at the movement of limbs, destroyer of enemies by the throwing of hands and feet, with the thunderbolt (the weapon able to be cast) for the giver of oblations Divodāsa or another, you split … Now he speaks indirectly: for Divodāsa, *atithigva* — who goes to guests with worship — [Indra] fiercely (*ugra*), of mighty strength, in the earlier time of splitting the cities, threw down (*avābharat*) from the mountain, hard to reach, the demon named Śambara, who had gone up the mountain, with his own strength, head downward; he took his life. Doing what? *mahaḥ* — giving great riches, his cows, horses and the like, to king Divodāsa; and *viśvā dhanāni* — all his treasures, jewels, pearls and the like, by his strength.")*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he) indra* — O Indra; *nṛto* — dancing (in the field of battle); *dāśuṣe* — who offered oblations; *pūrave* — for Puru (a man); *mahi* — the great; *divodāsāya* — for the king named Divodāsa; *navatim* — ninety; *puraḥ* — cities (of enemies); *bhinat* — you broke; *(kathā* — likewise); *nṛto* — O dancer (who destroys enemies by throwing the limbs in battle); *vajreṇa* — with the thunderbolt; *dāśuṣe* — for the one who offered oblations (Divodāsa); *bhinat* — you destroyed; *atithigvāya* — for him who goes to guests to honour them (Divodāsa); *ugraḥ* — the terrible (Indra); *śambaram* — the demon Śambara; *ojasā* — by his own strength; *mahaḥ* — greater; *dhanāni* — Śambara's cows and other wealth; *giroḥ ava abharat* — brought down headlong from the mountain, and killed him; *(kiṃ ca* — and); *viśvā dhanāni* — all his rich possessions; *ojasā* — by his strength; *(dayamānaḥ* — giving to Divodāsa); *avābharat* — he took away (and killed).

### Printed p. 447  (PDF 468)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, dancer on the field of battle, for the sake of Puru and for the great man Divodāsa, who offered oblations to you, you broke the ninety cities of the enemy; O slayer of enemies, for the giver of oblations you destroyed [the enemies] with the thunderbolt; for Divodāsa, who honours guests, the terrible Indra threw Śambara down from the mountain, gave Divodāsa his wealth of cows and so on, and by his strength killed Śambara (giving Divodāsa all his rich possessions).

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"For Puru, the giver of offerings, for the mighty Divodasa, you, Indra, the dancer (with delight in battle), have destroyed ninety cities; dancer (in battle), you have destroyed them with (your thunderbolt), for (the sake of) the giver of offerings. For (the sake of) Atithigwa, the fierce (Indra) hurled Shambara from off the mountain, bestowing (upon the prince) immense treasure, (acquired) by (his) prowess; all kinds of wealth (acquired) by (his) prowess."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 7).**

In this Ṛk it is briefly told how Indra, pleased with the sacrifice and other offerings of the king Divodāsa, subdued his enemies, protected Divodāsa, and gave him the wealth of his enemies.

***nṛto*** — this word is said twice. For the first *nṛto* the meaning *raṇe nartanaśīla* — "he who dances in battle" — is given, describing Indra's joy and eagerness for the battle, as one dances, being filled with enthusiasm, in the fighting.

---

### Printed p. 448  (PDF 469)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

(Special Topics of Ṛk 7, continued:) For the second *nṛto* it is described that, in the fighting, Indra, being skilled in the movements of hands and feet and in the use of his body in the proper manner at the right moment — the wonderful mantras (*yuddhacamatkāra*) fit for subduing enemies at the time of battle — protects himself and slays enemies; this is explained by the sentence *gātravikṣepaṇakuśala hastapādādipraksepeṇa śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsaka* — "skilled in moving the limbs, the destroyer of enemies by throwing hands, feet and so on".

***dāśuṣe*** — the word, formed as *dāśvān sāhvān* [Pā. 6-1-12] — though it also has the meaning "inclined to give" — is here explained as *havirdātre* — "to one who gives oblations".

***pūrave*** — *abhimatapūrakāya*: the word *pūravaḥ* is recorded among the twenty-five names of man (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೮"), *manuṣyāḥ naraḥ*; and is explained as *kāmyaiḥ pūrayitavyāḥ* — "those fit to have their desires fulfilled". Here the word *pūru* is given as an epithet of *divodāsāya*: the king named Divodāsa pleased Indra by offerings of oblations, following Indra's wishes; for that, Indra destroyed the cities of his enemies and helped the king: so it is described. By this example it is indicated that to the man who pleases Indra by oblations Indra accomplishes his wishes.

***atithigvāya*** — *pūjārtham atithiṃ gacchate divodāsāya*: "Indra subdues the enemies of Divodāsa, the king who honours guests and gratifies them, or of any other man who does so." The word *atithi* is explained by Yāska: *atithir abhyeti tithiṣu parakulānīti vā pargṛhān eti iti vā* — "he goes, on days other than *tithi*-days, to others' houses; or a person who comes seeking houses at midday" (Ni. 4-[?]; as read "೪-೬"): one who goes to the houses of others, or of the sacrificers, on particular days, is a guest.

***ugraḥ śambaraṃ ojasā avābharat*** — in this sentence Sāyaṇa alludes to a story. While Indra was destroying the ninety cities of the enemy, the demon Śambara, struck by Indra, hid on the mountain. The mighty Indra climbed the mountain, which none could ascend, seized the demon there and by his own strength killed him, head downward (*avāṅmukha*).

***mahaḥ*** — *mahānti*: the word *mahaḥ* is recorded among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೩-೩೪"). —

### Printed p. 449  (PDF 470)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

> पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीम् ।
> यस्य त्रितो व्योजसा वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् ॥

> *pituṃ nu stoṣaṃ maho dharmāṇaṃ taviṣīm |*
> *yasya trito vy ojasā vṛtraṃ viparvam ardayat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-187-1, as printed.) Here *mahaḥ* is explained as *mahataḥ*. Sāyaṇa has explained the word *mahas* as "abundant".

***dhanāni ojasā viśvā dhanāni ojasā*** — in this sentence the words *dhanāni ojasā* are used twice. The first *dhana* is explained as "cows, horses and the like": "Indra, out of pity for king Divodāsa, brought the cows, horses and so on of the demon Śambara and gave them to him". For the second *dhanāni* he gives, other than the wealth in the form of cows and so on already mentioned, "chariots, jewels, pearls and the like", and explains that by his strength he protected the king for the sake of those and gave them out of pity.

The word *ojas* is used in the sense of "strength", as it was used many times before.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *bhinat* — root *bhidir vidāraṇe*; *laṅ* third person singular, *tip*; *itaś ca* drops *i*; *rudhādibhyaḥ śnam* gives *śnam*, which, being *m*-marked, comes after the last vowel; *hal ṅyābbhyo…* (Pā. 6-1-68) drops the ending; *dakāra* of the root becomes *c*, *car* [*coḥ kuḥ*…]; no augment *aṭ* (Vedic); at the beginning of the *pāda* no *nighāta*; the accent of the *vikaraṇa* remains. *divodāsāya* — *divaḥ dāsaḥ* — a *ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa*; *divo dāse ṣaṣṭhyā aluk* (Kāśikā 6-3-21 [?], as read "೬-೩-೨೧-೨೪"?) gives no loss of the genitive of *divaḥ*; by the vārttika *divodāsādīnāṃ chandasi* the first member is acute on the first syllable; dative singular. *dāśuṣe* — root *dāś dāne*; *dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca* (Pā. 6-1-12) gives it as irregularly formed with the suffix *kvasu*; since *bha* in the dative singular, *vasoḥ samprasāraṇam* (Pā. 6-4-131) gives *saṃprasāraṇa*, *pūrvarūpa*; *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca* (Pā. 8-3-60) gives *ṣ* for the *s* of the suffix. *nṛto* — root *nṛtī gātravikṣepe*; the Uṇādi *ku* [?]; since *k*-marked, no guṇa of the penult; in the vocative, *hrasvasya guṇaḥ* (Pā. 7-3-108) gives guṇa; *āmantritasya ca* gives *nighāta*.

### Printed p. 450  (PDF 471)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *atithigvāya* — *atithiṃ gacchati iti ātithigvaḥ* [as read]; root *gamḷ gatau*; *ḍvan* [as read: *ḍva*] by Uṇādi; because *ḍit*, the *ṭi* (*am*) drops; *kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara*; dative singular. *abhārat* — root *bhṛñ bharaṇe*, *bhvādi*; *laṅ* third person singular; because it follows a finite verb, *nighāta*. *mahaḥ* — root *maha pūjāyām*; *kvip ca* gives *kvip*; accusative plural; *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ* gives the acute to the ending. *dayamānaḥ* — root *daya dānagatihiṃsādāneṣu*; *śānac* in the present sense; *śap*; *āne muk* (Pā. 7-2-82) gives the augment *muk* to the stem ending in *a*; *tāsyanudāttenṅidvidāder…* makes the *lasārvadhātuka* unaccented so that the root's accent remains. *ojasā* — root *ubja ārjave*; *ubjer balope ca* [as read: *ubjer balope ca*, Uṇ. 4-[?]] gives *asun*; the *b* of the root drops; because of the suffix guṇa of the penult; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable; instrumental singular. ‖ 7 ‖

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; small type, a few doubtful places: [?]).*

> अयमिन्द्रः समत्सु रणेषु प्रहारनिमित्तेषु यजमानं यष्टारमार्यमरणीयं सर्वैर्गन्तव्यं प्रावत् । रक्षति ॥ समत्सु समरणे [?] सङ्ग्रामनाम समत्स्विति सङ्ग्रामनामसु पाठात् ॥ किंच शतमूतिः स्वभक्तरक्षणेषु बहुविधरक्षण इन्द्रो विश्वेषु ॥ लिङ्गव्यत्ययः ॥ आजिषु सर्वेषु स्पर्धानिमित्तेषु सङ्ग्रामेषु यजमानं प्रावत् । तथा स्वर्मीळ्हेषु स्वर्गदेशेषु सुखस्य सेचयत्सु वाजिषु महासङ्ग्रामेषु प्रावत् । स्वर्गप्रदानेन रक्षति । रण अभिमुखेन हतानां वीराणां स्वर्गे परारूढेन [?] श्रूयते । द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके सूर्यमण्डलभेदिनौ । परिव्राड्योगयुक्तश्च रणे चाभिमुखो हतः । पराशर [?] इति । अश्रूतेहासमाचक्षते । अंशुमती नाम नदी । तस्यास्तीरे कृष्णनामासुरो वर्णतश्च कृष्णो दशसहस्रैरनुचरैरुपेतस्त्रेषा वर्णिनः पीडयन्नास्ते । तत्रेन्द्रो बृहस्पतिना प्रेरितः सन् मरुद्भिः सहितः कृष्णां त्वचमुत्कृत्य सानुचरमवधीत् । आयमर्थोव्य ... द्रप्सो अंशुमतीमतिष्ठत् । ऋ. ८-९६-१३ [?] इत्यादिनोपरिष्टाद्द्रष्टव्यम् । तदत्रोच्यते । अयमिन्द्रो मनवे मनुष्याय । विभक्तिव्यत्ययः । मनुष्याणामर्थायाव्रतान् । व्रतमिति कर्मनाम तद्रहितान् । यागविद्वेषिणः शासत् शिक्षितवान् । हिंसितवान् । शासेर्लेट्यडागमः । तथा कृष्णां त्वचं कृष्णनाम्नोऽसुरस्य कृष्णवर्णां त्वचमुत्कृत्यारन्धयत् । हिंसितवान् । रध हिंसायां रधिजभोरचि नुम् । केन प्रकारेणेति तदुच्यते । दक्षन्न विश्वम् । तत्तृषाणं ततृषाणमोषति । सर्वमपि हिंसकं तदनुचरसंघं दहति । यत्किंचिदनिशिष्टमिति नेत्याह । अर्कसानं हिंसारुचिं [?] दशावशिष्टं सर्वमपि न्योषति । निःशेषेण दहति ॥

*(Sense: "This Indra protects (*prāvat*) in *samatsu* — battles — the worshipper, the Ārya, worthy of being approached by all; (*samatsu* is among the names of battle). And *śatamūtiḥ* — of hundredfold protections for his own devotees — Indra protects the sacrificer in all contests (*ājiṣu*) and in the great battles (*svarmīḷheṣu*) that sprinkle happiness [lead to heaven]; he protects by granting heaven; of heroes slain facing the enemy it is heard in the world: 'These two men pierce the orb of the sun: the ascetic joined in yoga, and the one slain facing the enemy.' (Parāśara [?]). It is told in history: on the bank of the river Aṃśumatī the black demon Kṛṣṇa, with ten thousand followers, was afflicting the (respectable people) of the (four) castes: there Indra, urged by Bṛhaspati, with the Maruts, stripped the black skin and killed him with his followers: 'the drop (*drapsa*) stood on the Aṃśumatī' (Ṛ. 8-96-13 [?]) etc. — to be seen later. Here it is said: this Indra, for Manu (for men), punished (*śāsat*) the *avratān* — those without *vrata* (rites), who hate the sacrifice; and he destroyed (*arandhayat*) the black skin of the demon Kṛṣṇa; and as to how: *dakṣan na viśvam* — he burns the whole of them, the entire host of followers; not leaving anything: he burns (*oṣati*) all the harming ones, whatever is left of the sinful *arśasāna* [the wicked], utterly.")*

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 8, continued from p. 451:)* "…*viśveṣu* — in all; *ājiṣu* — in battles; *(pra āvat* — protects the sacrificer); *(tathā* — likewise); *svarmīḷheṣu* — in those that lead to heaven; *ājiṣu* — in battles; *(prāvat* — protects); *(kiṃ ca* — and); *(ayam) indraḥ* — this Indra; *manave* — for the sake of men; *avratān* — the people without rites (haters of the sacrifice); *śāsat* — punishes; *(tathā* — likewise); *kṛṣṇām* — the black (of the demon named Kṛṣṇa); *tvacam* — skin; *(utkṛtya* — having stripped); *dakṣat na* — as if burning to ashes; *arandhayat* — destroyed; *tatṛṣāṇam* — the harming; *viśvam* — all (his followers); *oṣati* — burns; *arśasānam* — the one who delights in cruelty, or [one who has] whatever is left of sin — everything; *ni oṣati* — utterly burns."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Indra, who protects his devotees in many ways, protects the sacrificer who worships him in all battles; in all battles that give the happiness of heaven he protects; he punishes for the sake of men those who hate the sacrifice; stripping the black skin of the demon named Kṛṣṇa, he destroyed those Rākṣasas; like fire, blazing, he destroys all the harmful (with his followers); he destroys utterly those who delight in cruelty.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Indra, the manifold protector (of his votaries) in battles, defends his Arya worshipper in all conflicts; in conflicts that confer heaven: he punished for (the benefit of) man the neglecters of religious rites: he tore off the black skin (of the aggressor): as if burning (with flame), he consumes the malignant; he utterly consumes him who delights in cruelty."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 8).**

***samatsu*** — *raṇeṣu prahāranimittṛeṣu*: "in places where harm may happen — in places of danger or in battles". The word *samatsu* is recorded among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯").

***yajamānam āryam*** — *araṇīyaṃ yaṣṭāram*: "the sacrificer who is an object of honour to all".

***śatamūtiḥ viśveṣu ājiṣu prāvat*** — *sarveṣu spardhānimitteṣu indro yajamānaṃ prāvat*: "In all the contests in which people dispute with one another, Indra, expert in many kinds of protection, protects the sacrificer, who seeks to increase his prosperity, in every way": so the meaning. The word *āji* is recorded among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯").

### Printed p. 453  (PDF 474)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

***svarmīḷheṣu ājiṣu prāvat*** — *svargadeśeṣu sukhasya secayatsu vā mahāsaṅgrāmeṣu svargapradānena rakṣati*: "In this Ṛk the word *āji* is used twice. The Niruktakāra explains it as 'battle'; Sāyaṇa, from the connection with the adjectives, explains *āji* as 'the great battle that makes heaven attainable (*svargaprāpaka*), the contest that is the occasion of rivalry'. The word *svarmīḷha* denotes what gives the happiness of heaven." To those who fight in battles with courage — and who, by indifference, take no care of their lives — Indra gives the comfort of heaven and so protects them: so he says. Parāśara —

> द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके सूर्यमण्डलभेदिनौ ।
> परिव्राड्योगयुक्तश्च रणे चाभिमुखो हतः ॥

> *dvāv imau puruṣau loke sūryamaṇḍalabhedinau |*
> *parivrāḍ yogayuktaś ca raṇe cābhimukho hataḥ ‖*

(Parāśara-smṛti 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೨" [?]) — the sage in yoga, who in the contemplation of the self constantly dwells in detachment from the happiness of this world and the warrior who gave up hope for his life in great battles and, not turning back, fought and fell in battle, both are said by the Parāśara-smṛti to reach, on the birth cycle ceasing, the state of passing through the orb of the sun. By this it is indicated that the happiness of heaven too, which has the form of non-return (*apunarāvṛtti*) according to the Śāstra, is attainable for them. And Indra, by honouring such heroes, gives them the happiness of heaven and protects them; so the greatness of Indra's protection is described.

***manave śāsad avratān tvacaṃ kṛṣṇām arandhayat*** — *manuṣyāṇām arthāya yāgavidveṣiṇaḥ hiṃsitavān | kṛṣṇanāmno 'surasya kṛṣṇavarṇāṃ tvacam utkṛtya hiṃsitavān*: the word *manu* is explained as "men". "To bring about the welfare and happiness of men, Indra [punishes] the thorns of the sacrifice and destroys them; stripping the black skin of the demon named Kṛṣṇa, he killed him": so it is explained. On this Sāyaṇa cites a legend:

> अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । अंशुमती नाम नदी । तस्यास्तीरे कृष्णनामासुरो वर्णतश्च कृष्णो दशसहस्रैरनुचरैरुपेतस्तद्देशवर्तिनः पीडयन्नास्ते । तत्रेन्द्रो बृहस्पतिना प्रेरितस्सन् मरुद्भिः सहितः कृष्णां तदीयां त्वचमुत्कृत्य सानुचरमवधीत् । अयमर्थः ॥

> *atretihāsam ācakṣate | aṃśumatī nāma nadī | tasyās tīre kṛṣṇanāmāsuro varṇataś ca kṛṣṇo daśasahasrair anucarair upetas taddeśavartinaḥ pīḍayann āste | tatrendro bṛhaspatinā preritas san marudbhiḥ sahitaḥ kṛṣṇāṃ tadīyāṃ tvacam utkṛtya sānucaram avadhīt | ayam arthaḥ ‖*

### Printed p. 454  (PDF 475)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

> अव द्रप्सो अंशुमतीमतिष्ठदियानः कृष्णो दशभिः सहस्रैः ।
> आवत्तमिन्द्रः शच्या धमन्तमप स्नेहितीर्नृमणा अधत्त ॥

> *ava drapso aṃśumatīm atiṣṭhad iyānaḥ kṛṣṇo daśabhiḥ sahasraiḥ |*
> *āvat tam indraḥ śacyā dhamantam apa snehitīr nṛmaṇā adhatta ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-13, as read "೮-೯೬-೧೩".) "Etc.; this will be seen later": so it is told. "On the bank of the well-known river called Aṃśumatī, in the region of the Yamunā [as read: *hariyuttaravuḍa*, doubtful: [?]], there lived an asura named Kṛṣṇa. He was black in colour, and with ten thousand followers he afflicted the people of that country, doing violence to the inhabitants and killing them. Bṛhaspati, the priest of all the gods, learned of this, and informed Indra that the demon and his followers, thorns of the sacrifice, must be subdued quickly. Then Indra, accompanied by the Marut gods, fought against that demon, stripped off the black skin of Kṛṣṇa, killed him and his followers and protected all the people of that country": it is explained that this story is told in the interpretation of the Ṛk "*ava drapso aṃśumatīm atiṣṭhat*".

***dakṣat*** — *bhasmīkaroti*: "Indra kills the thorns of the sacrifice who harm others in the world."

***tatṛṣāṇam oṣati — nyarśasānam oṣati*** — the word *oṣati* is used twice. *Sarvam api hiṃsakaṃ tadanucarasaṅghaṃ dahati* — "Indra destroys both those who do violence and their followers"; and *arśasānaṃ hiṃsārucim hatāvaśiṣṭaṃ sarvam api niḥśeṣeṇa dahati* — "he destroys all who delight in violence, without leaving any remainder".

***āryam*** — *araṇīyaṃ, sarvair gantavyam*: "worthy of being attained by all". The Niruktakāra —

> युवं वृकेणाश्विना वपन्तेषं दुहन्ता मनुषाय दस्रा ।
> अभि दस्युं बकुरेणा धमन्तोरु ज्योतिश्चक्रथुरार्याय ॥

> *yuvaṃ vṛkeṇāśvinā vapanteṣaṃ duhantā manuṣāya dasrā |*
> *abhi dasyuṃ bakureṇā dhamantoru jyotiś cakrathur āryāya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-21, as read "೧-೧೧೭-೨೧".) — explains *āryāya* in this Ṛk as "the son of Īśvara [?]" [as read]; Sāyaṇa explains *āryāya* as "to the one who knows".

### Printed p. 455  (PDF 476)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *āryam* — root *ṛ gatau*; *ṛhaloṇyat* (Pā. 3-1-124) gives *ṇyat*; *ñit*-marked, so *vṛddhi*, and *raparatva*. *āvat* — root *ava rakṣaṇe*; *laṅ* third person singular; because it follows a finite verb, *nighāta*. *śatamūtiḥ* — *śatam aparimitam ūtiḥ rakṣaṇaṃ yasya saḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* gives the accent of the first member. *viśveṣu* — as an epithet of *ājiṣu* the feminine would be required by the rule *yal liṅgaṃ yad vacanam…*; but by *vyatyaya* it is used in the masculine. *svarmīḍheṣu* — root *mihaḥ secane*; *kta*; *hoḍhaḥ* gives *ḍh* for *h*; *jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ* (Pā. 8-2-40) gives *dh* for the *t* of the suffix; *ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ* (Pā. 8-3-13) drops the earlier *ḍh*; *ḍhralope pūrvasya dīrgho 'ṇaḥ* (Pā. 6-3-111) lengthens the *i*; *pūrvapadaprakṛtisvara*. *śāsat* — root *śāsu anuśiṣṭau*; *leṭ* third person singular, *tip*; *itaś ca lope* (Pā. 3-4-97) drops *i*; *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* gives the augment *aṭ*; *cādilope vibhāṣā* (Pā. 8-1-63) forbids *nighāta*; the root's accent remains. *avratān* — *na vidyate vrataṃ yeṣāṃ te avratāḥ*; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. 6-2-172) gives the acute on the last syllable. *kṛṣṇām* — root *kṛṣa vilekhane*; *kṛṣer varṇe* [as read: Uṇ. 3-[?]] gives *naka*; *ṣṇu*… the *n* replaces the *k* of the suffix; the acute on the last syllable; feminine *ṭāp* since it ends in *a*; accusative singular. *manave* — by *vyatyaya* the dative is used for the genitive. *arandhayat* — root *radha hiṃsāyām*; after *ṇic*, *luṅ* third person singular, *tip*; *itaś ca lopaḥ*; *śap* [as read]; *radhijabhor aci* (Pā. 7-1-61) gives the augment *num* to the root; since *m*-marked it comes after the last vowel; guṇa because of *śap*, *ayādeśa*; the augment *aṭ*; because it follows a finite verb, *nighāta*. *dakṣat* — root *daha bhasmīkaraṇe*; *leṭ* third person singular, *tip*, loss of *i*, augment *aṭ*; *sibbahulaṃ leṭi* (Pā. 3-1-34) gives *sip*; *dādher dhātor ghaḥ* [as read: *dādhe… ḥaḥ*] gives…

### Printed p. 456  (PDF 477)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 8, concluded; numbers as printed.)* *dakṣat* (cont.) — the *h* of the root becomes *gh*/*k*… by *dādher ghoḥ* [as read]; *ṣatva* of the *s* following the *k*; *ekāco baśo bhaṣ jhaṣantasya sdhvoḥ* (Pā. 8-2-37) gives *bh* for the root-initial; the form *dakṣat*; because it follows a finite verb *nighāta* is not applied; the root's accent remains since the suffix is *p*-marked. *tatṛṣāṇam* — root *ñitṛṣā pipāsāyām*; when *liṭ* follows, *kānac* replaces it; *citaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-163) gives the acute on the last syllable; accusative singular. *oṣati* — root *uṣa dāhe*; *laṭ* third person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *arśasānam* — root *ṛ gatau*; *arter guṇaḥ śuṭ ca* (Uṇ. 3-[?]) gives the suffix *āsānac*; guṇa of the root; the augment *śuṭ*; because *ṭ*-marked the augment comes at the beginning of the suffix; *citaḥ* gives the acute on the last syllable. ‖ 8 ‖

#### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> सूरश्चक्रं प्र वृहज्जात ओजसा प्रपित्वे वाचमरुणो मुषायति ।
> ईशान आ मुषायति ।
> उशना यत्परावतोऽजगन्नूतये कवे ।
> सुम्नानि विश्वा मनुषेव तुर्वणिरहा विश्वेव तुर्वणिः ॥ ९ ॥

> *sūraścakraṃ pra vṛhajjāta ojasā prapitve vācamaruṇo muṣāyati |*
> *īśāna ā muṣāyati |*
> *uśanā yatparāvato 'jagannūtaye kave |*
> *sumnāni viśvā manuṣeva turvaṇirahā viśveva turvaṇiḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सूरः । चक्रम् । प्र । वृहत् । जातः । ओजसा । प्रऽपित्वे । वाचम् । अरुणः । मुषायति ।
> ईशानः । आ । मुषायति ।
> उशना । यत् । पराऽवतः । अजगन् । ऊतये । कवे ।
> सुम्नानि । विश्वा । मनुषाऽइव । तुर्वणिः । अहा । विश्वाऽइव । तुर्वणिः ॥ ९ ॥

> *sūraḥ | cakram | pra | vṛhat | jātaḥ | ojasā | pra 'pitve | vācam | aruṇaḥ | muṣāyati |*
> *īśānaḥ | ā | muṣāyati |*
> *uśanā | yat | parā 'vataḥ | ajagan | ūtaye | kave |*
> *sumnāni | viśvā | manuṣā 'iva | turvaṇiḥ | ahā | viśvā 'iva | turvaṇiḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; small type, many places doubtful: [?]).*

> अत्रापीतिहासमाचक्षते । केचनासुराः पूर्वमिन्द्रवज्रेण वधो मा भूदिति ब्रह्मणो वरं लब्ध्वेन्द्रमगणयित्वोद्वृत्ता आसन् । तान् हन्तुमिन्द्रः सूर्यरथस्य चक्रमादायावधीदिति । तदिदमुच्यते । अयमिन्द्रः सूरः सूर्यस्य षष्ठ्यर्थे प्रथमा । चक्रं रथस्य चक्रमादायौजसा शारीरेण बलेन जातः सम्वृद्धः सन् प्र वृहत् । प्रकृष्टं वृक्णवान् । वृहू उद्यमने । तौदादिकः । किंचारुणोऽरुणवर्णोऽत्यन्तं तेजोयुक्तः सन् यद्वा गमनशीलः सन् प्रपित्वे तेषां समीपे [?] तेषामुपगम्य वाचं वागुपलक्षितं प्राणं मुषायति । मुमोष मुष्णाति वा । प्रपित्व इत्याद्यनामाम [?] । यद्वा । वाचं तेषां प्रहारध्वनिं मुषायति । तेषु हतेषु ध्वनिः स्वयमेव विश्रान्तो भवति । अवधीदित्यर्थः । अथवा । इन्द्र एव द्युस्थानः सन्नादित्यात्मना स्तूयते । सूरः सूर्यो जाते उदिते सन्नोजसा स्वकीयेन तेजसा युक्तश्चक्रं प्र वृहत् । तमोनिवारणार्थमसुरजयाय वा चक्रोपलक्षितं रथं प्रकर्षेणोद्यतं करोति । ततः पूर्वमरुणस्सूरथयन्ता प्रपित्वे मन्देहादीनामसुराणां प्रपित्वे समीपे वाचं तेषां जहद्भिन्दतीति दध्यनिं मुषायति । मुष्णाति । मुषेरुत्तरस्य क्ष्णोऽवानः । श्छन्दसि शायजपीति शायजादेशः ॥ तदनन्तरं सूर्य ईशानः सर्वाणि तमांस्यसुरान्वा निराकर्तुं समर्थः सन् आ मुषायति । समन्तान्मुष्णाति । अथ प्रकृतम् ॥ हे कवे क्रान्तदर्शिन् यद्यस्मात्त्वमुशनोऽनसा [?] युक्तः सन् परावतो दूरात्स्वर्गस्थानादजगन् [?] । उशना कविः तदुपेतमूतये रक्षणाय । परावतो दूरात्स्वर्गस्थानादजगन् गतवानसि प्राप्तवानसि ॥ गमेर्लुङि सिचि छान्दसः शपः श्लुः । हल्ङ्यादिलोपे [?] इति सलोपः ॥ यद्वा । उशना उशनसा ऋषिणा युक्तः सन् जगन् आगच्छ । आगत्य च विश्वा विश्वानि सुम्नानि सुखसाधनानि धनान्यादायास्माकं तुर्वणिः शीघ्रं सम्भक्ता भवेति शेषः । तुर्वणिः शीघ्रं सम्भक्तेति निरुक्तम् । नि. ६-१४ [?] । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । मनुषेव मनुष्येण । स यथा सम्भक्त्रेण [?] । यद्वा । मनुष्येण मनुष्याणामिव । इतरेषामृत्विजां विश्वा सुम्नानि सर्वाणि धनान्यादाय तुर्वणिर्भवसि । तद्वदस्माकमपि । न केवलमेकस्मिन्नेव यागादिने किंत्विहा विश्वेव विश्वस्यान्यहानि [?] सर्वेष्वप्यहःसु तुर्वणिर्भव । यद्वा । तुर्वणिस्त्वमहा विश्वेव विश्वस्यान्यहानीव । यथा दीर्घायुष्यं यथा ददासि तथा सुम्नान्यपि । उभयमपि देहीत्यर्थः ॥

> *atrāpītihāsamācakṣate | kecanāsurāḥ pūrvamindravajreṇa vadho mā bhūditi brahmaṇo varaṃ labdhvendramagaṇayitvodvṛttā āsan | tān hantumindraḥ sūryarathasya cakramādāyāvadhīditi | tadidamucyate | ayamindraḥ sūraḥ sūryasya ṣaṣṭhyarthe prathamā | cakraṃ rathasya cakramādāyaujasā śārīreṇa balena jātaḥ samvṛddhaḥ san pra vṛhat | prakṛṣṭaṃ vṛkṇavān | vṛhū udyamane | taudādikaḥ | kiṃcāruṇo tejasā yuktaścakraṃ pra vṛhat | tamonivāraṇārthamasurajayāya vā cakropalakṣitaṃ rathaṃ prakarṣeṇodyataṃ karoti | tataḥ pūrvamaruṇassūrathayantā prapitve mandehādīnāmasurāṇāṃ prapitve samīpe vācaṃ teṣāṃ jahadbhindatīti dadhyaniṃ muṣāyati | muṣṇāti | muṣeruttarasya kṣṇo 'vānaḥ | śchandasi śāyajapīti śāyajādeśaḥ ‖ tadanantaraṃ sūrya īśānaḥ sarvāṇi tamāṃsyasurānvā nirākartuṃ samarthaḥ san ā muṣāyati | samantānmuṣṇāti | atha prakṛtam ‖ he kave krāntadarśin yadyasmāttvamuśano 'nasā [?] yuktaḥ san parāvato dūrātsvargasthānādajagan [?] | uśanā kaviḥ tadupetamūtaye rakṣaṇāya | parāvato dūrātsvargasthānādajagan gatavānasi prāptavānasi ‖ gamerluṅi sici chāndasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | halṅyādilope [?] iti salopaḥ ‖ yadvā | uśanā uśanasā ṛṣiṇā yuktaḥ san jagan āgaccha | āgatya ca viśvā viśvāni sumnāni sukhasādhanāni dhanānyādāyāsmākaṃ turvaṇiḥ śīghraṃ sambhaktā bhaveti śeṣaḥ | turvaṇiḥ śīghraṃ sambhakteti niruktam | ni. 6-14 [?] | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | manuṣeva manuṣyeṇa | sa yathā sambhaktreṇa [?] | yadvā | manuṣyeṇa manuṣyāṇāmiva | itareṣāmṛtvijāṃ viśvā sumnāni sarvāṇi dhanānyādāya turvaṇirbhavasi | tadvadasmākamapi | na kevalamekasminneva yāgādine kiṃtvihā viśveva viśvasyānyahāni [?] sarveṣvapyahaḥsu turvaṇirbhava | yadvā | turvaṇistvamahā viśveva viśvasyānyahānīva | yathā dīrghāyuṣyaṃ yathā dadāsi tathā sumnānyapi | ubhayamapi dehītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Sense: "Here also they relate an itihāsa: certain demons formerly, having obtained from Brahmā the boon 'let there be no death by Indra's thunderbolt', became arrogant, disregarding Indra. To kill them Indra took the wheel of the Sun's chariot and slew them. That is told here: this Indra — *sūraḥ*, 'the Sun', the first case for the genitive — taking the wheel (*cakram*) of the chariot, grown (*jātaḥ*) in bodily strength (*ojasā*), *pra vṛhat* — tore out. Further, *aruṇaḥ* — reddish, exceedingly brilliant, or moving — at *prapitve*, near them, comes up and *muṣāyati* — takes away their breath marked by speech; or he stops the sound of their blows. Or: Indra himself, standing in heaven, is praised in the form of the Sun. When *sūra* the sun has risen, endowed with his own splendour, he lifts the wheel-marked chariot to dispel darkness or to conquer the demons. Then, before, *aruṇa* — the sun's charioteer — near the demons … *īśānaḥ* — able to remove all darknesses or the demons — *ā muṣāyati*, carries off all around. Now to the context: O sage (*kave*, far-seeing), since you came (*ajagan*) from afar (*parāvataḥ*), from the heavenly abode, for protection (*ūtaye*), joined with Uśanā [or: *uśanā kaviḥ* — the sage Uśanas]; coming, bring all (*viśvā*) the means of happiness (*sumnāni*), wealth, and be quick (*turvaṇiḥ* — 'quickly sharing', Nirukta) for us; as for man (*manuṣeva*) — as for other priests you bring all wealth, so for us too; and not only on one day of the sacrifice but on all days (*ahā viśveva*): or as you give long life, so give happiness: give both.")* *(Doubtful readings in the small type are marked [?]; the grammar tail on *muṣāyati* and *ajagan* is characterized only.)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(ayam) indraḥ* — this Indra; *sūraḥ* — of the Sun; *cakram* — the wheel of the chariot (taking it); *ojasā* — by bodily strength; *jātaḥ* — grown; *pra vṛhat* — tore out against (the demons' bodies); *(kiṃ ca* — and); *aruṇaḥ* — reddish or moving; *prapitve* — near (them, going to them); *vācam* — speech or breath; *muṣāyati* — takes away [or: *(athavā) sūraḥ* — Indra in the form of the Sun; *jātaḥ* — risen; *ojasā* — with his own splendour; *cakram* — the wheel (chariot); *pra vṛhat* — lifts up (to remove darkness); *aruṇaḥ* — the sun's charioteer, named Aruṇa; *prapitve* — near the demons (Mandeha and the rest); *vācam* — their voice (the sound of demons, by the wheel); *muṣāyati* — makes them silent; *īśānaḥ* — able to remove darkness (or the demons); *ā muṣāyati* — destroys them entirely]; *(he) kave* — O sage; *uśanā* — joined with the sage named Uśanas; *ūtaye* — for our protection; *parāvataḥ* — from a very distant place (from the world of heaven); *ajagan* — came (or: *yat* — that you; *uśanā* — to Uśanas' protection; *parāvataḥ* — from heaven; *ajagan* — you came); *viśvā sumnāni* — all the means of happiness (taking); *manuṣā iva* — as (from a distant place) for a man the desired things are brought, or as for the other priests [wealth is granted]; *turvaṇiḥ (bhava)* — be quick to favour; *viśvā ahā iva* — on all days; *turvaṇiḥ (bhava)* — be quick to favour [or: *turvaṇiḥ* — you who give; *viśvā ahā iva* — as long life; *viśvā sumnāni* — all the means of happiness; *turvaṇiḥ (bhava)* — be one who favours quickly].

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Indra, endowed with extraordinary bodily strength, took up the wheel of the Sun's chariot and slew the demons; reddish, he destroyed them completely, being able (to destroy the Rākṣasas) — he made them lifeless; O wise Indra, as you came from the heavenly world, from far away, for the protection of Uśanas, so come and bring all the means of happiness for us and for the other priests; be quick to favour us, giving the means of happiness, every day.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed; begins here and continues on p. 459):** *"Endowed with augmented vigour, he hurled (against the foes) the wheel (of the chariot) of the sun; and, ruddy of hue, deprived them of existence; he, the sovereign lord, deprived them of existence. As you, sage Indra, come from afar to the succour of Ushanas, so do you come quickly, bearing all good things (to us), as you bear to (other) men; come quickly (to us) every day."*

### Printed p. 459  (PDF 480)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 9).**

***sūraś cakraṃ ojasā pravṛhat*** — *sūryasya rathasya cakram ādāya śārīreṇa balena samṛddhaḥ san prakṛṣṭavān*: "taking the wheel of the Sun's chariot, strong in body, Indra tore it out." Here too a legend is told: *kecana asurā indrasya vajrāyudhena asmākaṃ vadho mā bhūd iti brahmaṇā varaṃ labdhvā indram āgaṇayitvā uddhṛttāḥ sthitāḥ | tān hantum indraḥ sūryarathasya cakram ādāyāvadhīt iti* — "some demons, having obtained from Brahmā the boon that they should not die by Indra's thunderbolt, became arrogant, disregarding Indra, and Indra, taking the wheel of the Sun's chariot as his weapon, slew them all."

> यमेन दत्तं त्रित एनमायुनगिन्द्र एणं प्रथमो अध्यतिष्ठत् ।
> गन्धर्वो अस्य रशनामगृभ्णात्सूरादश्वं वसवो निरतष्ट ॥

> *yamena dattaṃ trita enam āyunag indra eṇaṃ prathamo adhyatiṣṭhat |*
> *gandharvo asya raśanām agṛbhṇāt sūrād aśvaṃ vasavo nir ataṣṭa ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-163-2, as read "೧-೧೬೩-೨"; the first line has a doubtful word at its start: *yamena* [?]. The numerals "1-163-2" are my reading of the small type and are not confirmed by the numeral tool.) In this Ṛk Durgācārya has explained the word *sūrāt* as "from the Sun". Here Sāyaṇa explains *sūraḥ* as *sūryasya*, and for *ojasā*, recorded among the names of strength in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"), the meaning "bodily strength".

***aruṇaḥ prapitve vācaṃ muṣāyati*** — *aruṇavarṇaḥ atyantatejoyuktaḥ | yadvā gamanaśīlaḥ san prapitve teṣāṃ samīpam upāgatya vāgupalakṣitaṃ prāṇaṃ mumoṣa muṣṇāti vā* — three kinds of meaning are given by Sāyaṇa. In the first, Indra, very radiant and reddish in colour, or constantly moving, approaches the demons and takes away their very breath (so that they cannot even speak); the explanation is that he kills them.

In the second meaning: *vācaṃ teṣāṃ prahāradhvaniṃ muṣāyati | teṣu hateṣu dhvaniḥ svayam eva viśrānto bhavati | avadhīd ity arthaḥ* — "Indra, at the time of battle, strikes the demons with his weapon so that they do not utter even a sound; and their breath, along with the sound of their blows, ceases": thus it is described. In the third meaning: *athavā indra iva dyusthānaḥ sann ādityātmanā stūyate* — "Indra, who is the deity of the heaven-region, is praised in the form of the Sun". The description of Indra's greatness is explained in this way. *(The remainder of this page and the explanation of the third meaning continue on p. 460.)*

### Printed p. 460  (PDF 481)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 9, continued — the third meaning:)* *sūraḥ sūryo jātaḥ udita san ojasā svakīyena tejasā yukta ś cakraṃ pravṛhat | tamo nivāraṇārtham asurajayāya vā cakropalakṣitaṃ rathaṃ prakarṣeṇa udyataṃ karoti | tataḥ pūrvam aruṇaḥ sūrathayantā prapitve mandehādyasurāṇāṃ samīpe vācaṃ teṣāṃ jahad bhindati ity ādidhvaniṃ muṣāyati muṣṇāti*: "As soon as the Sun has risen, endowed with his own splendour, he makes the chariot, marked by its wheel, speed along, to dispel darkness or to conquer the demons; before that, Aruṇa, the Sun's charioteer, near the demon-hosts such as Mandeha, silences the sound of their words — he breaks it": so it is explained. The Niruktakāra —

> यदुदञ्चो वृषाकपे गृहमिन्द्राजगन्तन ।
> क्वस्य पुल्वघो मृगः कमगञ्जनयोपनो विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ॥

> *yad udañco vṛṣākape gṛham indrājagantana |*
> *kvasya pulvagho mṛgaḥ kam agañ janayopano viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-[?], as read "೧೦-೮೬-೨೩" [?]; the small type is hard to read: [?].) — citing this Ṛk, he explains *kam agam uddiśya janayopanaḥ sarvasmād indra uttaraḥ*, and (Ni. 12-[?]) says that Indra is invisible, while Āditya (the Sun) is visible; the wise know the identity of the two from the "knowledge of the form of the Sun" in the sacrificer; among the gods Indra is the foremost; therefore it is described that Indra is called by the name Āditya.

***prapitve*** — *teṣāṃ samīpe prapitve abhīke ity āsannasya | prapitve prāpte*: the Niruktakāra reads *prapitve prāpte, abhīke abhyakte* (Ni. 3-30 [?]) and explains *prapitve abhīke ity āsannasya* — both words denote nearness. And —

> यथा गौरो अपा कृतं तृष्यन्नेत्यवेरिणम् ।
> आपित्वे नः प्रपित्वे तूयमा गहि कण्वेषु सु सचा पिब ॥

> *yathā gauro apā kṛtaṃ tṛṣyann ety averiṇam |*
> *āpitve naḥ prapitve tūyam ā gahi kaṇveṣu su sacā piba ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-4-3, as read "೮-೪-೩".) From this Ṛk the word *prapitve* is explained as *prāpte*; by this it is stated that a word meaning "near" is used without a gap.

***īśānaḥ ā muṣāyati*** — *sarvāṇi tamāṃsi asurān vā nirākartuṃ samarthaḥ san samantāt muṣṇāti*: "the Sun is able to remove all darkness, or the demons."

### Printed p. 461  (PDF 482)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

(…) "while he is risen, the Sun destroys the darkness or the demons entirely, as one endowed with the means and power to subdue them."

***kave yat uśanā ūtaye parāvataḥ ajagan*** — *krāntadarśin uśanas iti nāmnaḥ maharṣeḥ rakṣaṇāya dūrāt svargasthānāt prāptavān asi*: two kinds of meaning are given. Indra is addressed as *kavi*, "one who sees everything directly". "When the sage named Uśanas prayed to Indra for protection, Indra came from the far-off heaven and protected him": this story is alluded to; one meaning. In the second, the word *uśanā* is explained as *uśanasā* — together with Bhārgava (Śukrācārya), the coming of Indra is prayed for, and his protection.

***viśvā sumnāni turvaṇiḥ*** — *sarvāṇi sukhasādhanāni dhanāni ādāya asmākaṃ kṣipraṃ saṃbhaktā bhava*: the word *sumna* is recorded among the names of happiness (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೪"); *turvaṇi* is explained as *turvaṇis tūrṇavaniḥ* (Ni. 6-[?]; as read "೬-೧೪"). "Indra is prayed to bring wealth, the means of happiness, to us and to give us happiness carefully."

***manuṣeva turvaṇiḥ*** — *manuṣyeṇeva yathā tvoteṇa parivṛḍhāya deśāntarād abhimataṃ dhanam ānīyate tadvat | yadvā manuṣeva manuṣyāṇām iva itareṣām ṛtvijāṃ viśvā sumnāni sarvāṇi dhanāny ādāya turvaṇir bhavasi tadvad asmākam api*: "as a man goes to another country and brings the wealth he needs, so Indra is asked to bring wealth for the sacrificers; or, as Indra brings all the wealth that the other priests desire, so for us".

***ahā viśveva turvaṇiḥ*** — *sarveṣv apy ahaḥsu turvaṇir bhava | yadvā turvaṇis tvam ahā viśveva atidīrghāyuṣyaṃ yathā dadāsi tathā sumnāny api ubhayam api dehi*: "on all days be the quick giver; or, as you give very long life, give happiness too — give both": so it is prayed that when the sacrifice is being performed Indra give wealth and, on all other days, favour us.

### Printed p. 462  (PDF 483)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *sūraḥ* — root *ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane* [as read], suffix *kran* by *susūdhāgṛdhibhyaḥ kran* (Uṇ. 2-[?]); no guṇa since *k*-marked; by *n*-marker the acute on the first syllable; first case in the sense of the genitive. *bṛhat* — root *vṛhū udyamane*, *tudādi*; *laṅ* third person singular; *itaś ca* drops *i*; *tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ* gives *śa*; since *sārvadhātukam apit* no guṇa of the penult; *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi* gives no augment *aṭ*; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *muṣāyati* — root *muṣa steye*; by the statement *ghuṇarthakaviṣaya* [as read] *ṇic*…; *muṣam ātmana icchati*, *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. 3-1-8); *na chandasy aputrasya* (Pā. 7-4-35) forbids lengthening, but by *vyatyaya* the preceding lengthening occurs; after the *kyac*-ending *laṭ* third person singular; or by *bahulaṃ chandasi* the *ṇic* as *vikaraṇa*; by the statement *sañjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ* no guṇa of the penult; *tiṅ-nighāta*; or when *śāyac* … *chandasi śāyajapi* (Pā. 3-1-84) gives *śāyac*. *īśānaḥ* — root *īśa aiśvarye*; *śānac* in the present sense; *citaḥ* gives the acute on the last syllable. *uśanā* — root *vaśa kāntau*; *vaśeḥ kanasi* (Uṇ. 4-[?]) gives *kanasi*; *grahijyāvayi…* (Pā. 6-1-16) gives *saṃprasāraṇa*, *pūrvarūpa*; the stem *uśanas*; acute on the first syllable by the suffix; by *vyatyaya* the first case. *ajagan* — root *gamḷ gatau*; *luṅ* second person singular, *sip*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *śap*→*śluh*; *ślau* doubles the root; *kuhoś cuḥ* (Pā. 7-4-62) gives *j* for the reduplicative *g*; *hal ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt…* drops *sip*; *no no dhātoḥ* [as read: Pā. 8-2-64?] gives *n* for the *m*; since *yad* is connected, *nighāta* does not occur; the augment *aṭ* is acute so that the first syllable is acute.

### Printed p. 463  (PDF 484)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *turvaṇiḥ* — root *turvī hiṃsāyām*; Uṇādi *ani*; the acute on the first syllable of the suffix. *ahā* — in the neuter plural *śeś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. 6-1-70) drops *śi*. ‖ 9 ‖

***(ornamental rule)***

#### Ṛk 10

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स नो नव्येभिर्वृषकर्मन्नुक्थैः पुरां दर्तः पायुभिः पाहि शग्मैः ।
> दिवोदासेभिरिन्द्र स्तवानो वावृधीथा अहोभिरिव द्यौः ॥ १० ॥

> *sa no navyebhirvṛṣakarmannukthaiḥ purāṃ dartaḥ pāyubhiḥ pāhi śagmaiḥ |*
> *divodāsebhirindra stavāno vāvṛdhīthā ahobhiriva dyauḥ ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । नः । नव्येभिः । वृषकर्मन् । उक्थैः । पुराम् । दर्तः । दर्तरिति दर्तः । पायुऽभिः । पाहि । शग्मैः ।
> दिवःऽदासेभिः । इन्द्र । स्तवानः । ववृधीथाः । अहःऽभिःऽइव । द्यौः ॥ १० ॥

> *saḥ | naḥ | navyebhiḥ | vṛṣakarman | ukthaiḥ | purām | dartaḥ | dartariti dartaḥ | pāyu 'bhiḥ | pāhi | śagmaiḥ |*
> *divaḥ 'dāsebhiḥ | indra | stavānaḥ | vavṛdhīthāḥ | ahaḥ 'bhiḥ 'iva | dyauḥ ‖ 10 ‖*

*(Read from the image: the Saṃhitā's first line is printed over two lines; the Triṣṭubh metre of the last ṛk is as stated in the table.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; small type, a few places doubtful: [?]).*

> हे इन्द्र वृषकर्मन्नभिमतवर्षणव्यापारवन् पुरां दर्तरसुरपुराणां दारयिता ॥ सुबामन्त्रिते [?] इति षष्ठ्याः पराङ्गवद्भावात्षष्ठ्यामन्त्रितसमुदायस्य पादादित्वादाष्टमिकमाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ स तादृशो महानुभावस्त्वं नोऽस्मत्सम्बन्धिभिर्नव्येभिर्नूतनैरुक्थैरिदानीं प्रतिपादितप्रकारैः स्तोत्रैस्तुष्टः सन् पायुभिः पालनप्रकारैः शग्मैः सुखैश्चैहिकामुष्मिकरूपैः पाहि । पालय । किंच हे इन्द्र दिवोदासेभिर्दिवोदासगोत्रोत्पन्नैरस्माभिः पारुच्छेपैः ॥ अश आदिभ्योऽच् । यद्वा । पूजार्थं बहुवचनम् ॥ स्तवानः स्तूयमानः कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः । वावृधीथाः प्रवृद्धो भव । वृधेर्लिङि छान्दसः शपः श्लुः । किमिव । अहोभिरिव द्यौः । द्योतनशीलः आदित्योऽहोभिः प्रसिद्धैर्यथा प्रवृद्धो भवति । तथास्मत्स्तुत्या त्वमपि प्रवृद्धो भवेत्यर्थः ॥

> *he indra vṛṣakarmannabhimatavarṣaṇavyāpāravan purāṃ dartarasurapurāṇāṃ dārayitā ‖ subāmantrite [?] iti ṣaṣṭhyāḥ parāṅgavadbhāvātṣaṣṭhyāmantritasamudāyasya pādāditvādāṣṭamikamādyudāttatvam ‖ sa tādṛśo mahānubhāvastvaṃ no 'smatsambandhibhirnavyebhirnūtanairukthairidānīṃ pratipāditaprakāraiḥ stotraistuṣṭaḥ san pāyubhiḥ pālanaprakāraiḥ śagmaiḥ sukhaiścaihikāmuṣmikarūpaiḥ pāhi | pālaya | kiṃca he indra divodāsebhirdivodāsagotrotpannairasmābhiḥ pārucchepaiḥ ‖ aśa ādibhyo 'c | yadvā | pūjārthaṃ bahuvacanam ‖ stavānaḥ stūyamānaḥ karmaṇi kartṛpratyayaḥ | vāvṛdhīthāḥ pravṛddho bhava | vṛdherliṅi chāndasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | kimiva | ahobhiriva dyauḥ | dyotanaśīlaḥ ādityo 'hobhiḥ prasiddhairyathā pravṛddho bhavati | tathāsmatstutyā tvamapi pravṛddho bhavetyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Sense: "O Indra, *vṛṣakarman* — whose work is the showering of the desired — *purāṃ dartaḥ* — the splitter of the cities of demons: you, such a great one, pleased by our new (*navyebhiḥ*) hymns (*ukthaiḥ*) as now stated, protect us with protections (*pāyubhiḥ*) and with the happiness (*śagmaiḥ*) of this world and the next. And, O Indra, praised by us, the Paruccheṣas, born in the line of Divodāsa — the plural is of respect — increase (*vāvṛdhīthāḥ*): as *dyauḥ* — the shining Sun — grows by the days, so you grow by our praise.")*

### Printed p. 464  (PDF 485)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 130".)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he) indra* — O Indra; *vṛṣakarman* — shower of the desired; *puraṃ dartaḥ* — destroyer of the cities of enemies (and so); *saḥ* — that (great one); *naḥ* — us; *navyebhiḥ ukthaiḥ* — pleased with new praises; *pāyubhiḥ* — with protective acts; *śagmaiḥ* — with happiness in this world and the next; *pāhi* — protect; *(he indra* — O Indra); *divodāsebhiḥ* — by us of the line of Divodāsa (Paruccheṣa) or by Divodāsa; *stavānaḥ* — praised; *dyauḥ* — the Sun; *ahobhiḥ iva* — as by days; *vāvṛdhīthāḥ* — increase.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, giver of the desired, destroyer of the cities, great one: pleased by our new praises, protect us with protective acts and with happiness in this world and the next; and, as the Sun grows by days, so, praised by us of Divodāsa's line, grow and increase.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Showerer of benefits, destroyer of cities, propitiated by our new songs, reward us with gratifying blessings: glorified, Indra, by the descendants of Divodasa, increase (in power), like the sun in (revolving) days."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 10).**

***vṛṣakarman*** — *abhimatavarṣaṇavyāpāravān*: "Indra performs the work of showering rain that is desired by the world."

***purāṃ dartaḥ*** — *asurapurāṇāṃ dārayitā*: "the destroyer of the cities where the demons live."

***navyebhir ukthaiḥ pāyubhiḥ śagmaiḥ pāhi*** — "Indra, satisfied by praises recited in a new manner by the ṛṣi who saw the mantra, is prayed to protect us by the various kinds of protective acts and by the happiness of this world and the next."

### Printed p. 465  (PDF 486)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

***ahobhir iva dyauḥ*** — *dyotanaśīla ādityo 'hobhiḥ prasiddhair yathā pravṛddho bhavati kathā asmatstutyā tvam api pravṛddho bhava*: "as the Sun grows through days, so may Indra, praised by Paruccheṣa, who is born in the line of Divodāsa, grow through the days and become mighty": so he wishes.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *navyebhiḥ* — *bhave chandasi* (Pā. 4-4-110) gives *yat*; *yato nāvaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-213) gives the acute on the first syllable; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives no *ais* for *bhis*; *bahuvacane jhaly et* (Pā. 7-3-103) gives *e*. *vṛṣakarman* — *ṇaja sambuddhyoḥ* (Pā. 8-2-8) gives no loss of *n* in the vocative; *āmantritasya ca* gives *nighāta*. *ukthaiḥ* — root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; *pātṛtudivaci…* (Uṇ. 2-[?]) gives *thak*; since *k*-marked, *vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti* (Pā. 6-1-15) gives *saṃprasāraṇa*, *pūrvarūpa*; *coḥ kuḥ* gives *k* for *c*; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. *purāṃ dartaḥ* — root *dṝ vidāraṇe*; *tṛc* in the agent sense; guṇa of the root because of it; in the vocative *dartaḥ*; by *subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare* (Pā. 2-1-2) the word *purām* is treated as part of the following so that, being at the beginning of the *pāda*, the *aṣṭamika* [i.e. *āmantrita*] *nighāta* does not occur; *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. 6-1-198) gives the acute on the first syllable. *pāyubhiḥ* — root *pā rakṣaṇe*; *kṛvāpā…* (Uṇ. 1-1) gives *uṇ*; *ato yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ* (Pā. 7-3-33) gives the augment *yuk*; acute on the last syllable by the suffix; instrumental plural. *pāhi* — as before: a *loṭ* second person singular; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *divodāsebhiḥ* — *divodāse ṣaṣṭhyā aluk* (Kāśikā 6-3-21 [?], as read "೬-೩-೨೧-೨೫") gives no loss of the genitive of *divaḥ*; *divodāso 'sya asti iti divodāsaḥ*; *arśa ādibhyo 'c* (Pā. 5-2-127) gives *ac* in the possessive sense; *yasyeti ca* drops *a*; by the suffix's accent the acute on the last syllable; by the optional rule *bhis* → *ais* for the *a*-ending is not required, hence *ebhiḥ*.

### Printed p. 466  (PDF 487)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131" [as read: "೧೩೧"].)*

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *stavānaḥ* — root *ṣṭuñ stutau*; *vyatyayo bahulam* gives the suffix of the agent in the passive; *śānac* in the present sense; guṇa; *avādeśa*; because it follows a [word with] *anudātta* [as read], the *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented and the root's accent remains. *vāvṛdhīthāḥ* — root *vṛdhu vṛddhau*; *liṅ* second person singular, suffix *thās*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *śluḥ* for *śap*; *ślau* doubles the root; *urat* gives *at*, *raparatva*, *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*; *liṅaḥ sīyuṭ* (Pā. 3-4-102) gives *sīyuṭ*; *sutiṅopor…* [as read: *suṭ tithoḥ*, Pā. 3-4-107] gives *suṭ*; *liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya* (Pā. 7-2-79) drops both *s*; *lopo vyor vali* drops *y*; because at the beginning of the *pāda* no *nighāta*; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. ‖ 10 ‖

Here ends the 130th Sūkta. *(Kannada closing line: "ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತನೇ ಸೂಕ್ತ ಮುಗಿದುದು".)*

## Sūkta 131 — *indrāya hi dyaur asuro* (begins on printed p. 466; Anuvāka 19, fifth Sūkta)

### Printed p. 466 (continued; PDF 487, lower part)

**ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra mūvattoṃdaneya sūktavu** (the one hundred and thirty-first Sūkta).

**॥ सूक्तभूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, small type; read from the image; several letters doubtful [?]).**

> इन्द्राय हि सप्तर्चं पञ्चमं सूक्तम् । इन्द्राय सप्तेत्यनुक्रमणिका । पारुच्छेपमात्यष्टिच्छन्दः । इन्द्रो देवता ॥ पृष्ठ्यस्य षष्ठेऽहनि माध्यन्दिनसवने होत्रकाः सस्स्तशस्त्रे एतत्सूक्तं तृचत्रयं कृत्स्नारम्भणीयाभ्य ऊर्ध्वं मावपेयुः । आश्रायणं विभागः । आद्यास्तिस्त्रो मैत्रावरुणस्य । तृतीयाद्यास्तिस्रो ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः । पञ्चम्याद्यास्तिस्र उक्थावाकस्य । एतच्चतुर्थेऽहनीति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । पष्ठेऽहनीन्द्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नतेत्येवमेव । आ. ८-११ [?] इति ॥ शस्त्रेऽहनि तस्मिन्नेव सवने प्रशास्त्रादीनां प्रस्थितयाज्याभ्यः पुरस्ताद्यादिते [?] … पष्ठस्येति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । इन्द्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नतेति षट् । आ. ८-१ [?] इति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये इन्द्राय हीति तृचो नैकल्पिकानुरूपत्पद्यतीयः [?] । महाव्रतस्येति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । इन्द्रं याह्युप नः परावत इन्द्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नत । ऐ. आ. ५-१-१ [?] इति ॥

> *indrāya hi saptarcaṃ pañcamaṃ sūktam | indrāya saptetyanukramaṇikā | pārucchepamātyaṣṭicchandaḥ | indro devatā ‖ pṛṣṭhyasya ṣaṣṭhe 'hani mādhyandinasavane hotrakāḥ sasstaśastre etatsūktaṃ tṛcatrayaṃ kṛtsnārambhaṇīyābhya ūrdhvaṃ māvapeyuḥ | āśrāyaṇaṃ vibhāgaḥ | ādyāstistro maitrāvaruṇasya | tṛtīyādyāstisro brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ | pañcamyādyāstisra ukthāvākasya | etaccaturthe 'hanīti khaṇḍe sūtritam | paṣṭhe 'hanīndrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnatetyevameva | ā. 8-11 [?] iti ‖ śastre 'hani tasminneva savane praśāstrādīnāṃ prasthitayājyābhyaḥ purastādyādite [?] … paṣṭhasyeti khaṇḍe sūtritam | indrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnateti ṣaṭ | ā. 8-1 [?] iti ‖ mahāvrate niṣkevalye indrāya hīti tṛco naikalpikānurūpatpadyatīyaḥ [?] | mahāvratasyeti khaṇḍe sūtritam | indraṃ yāhyupa naḥ parāvata indrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnata | ai. ā. 5-1-1 [?] iti ‖*

*(The Sanskrit introduction is small and in several places unreadable to me; I give what is legible and mark [?]; the sense follows.)*

**Kannada anuvāda (translated).** *Anuvāda* — This Sūkta *indrāya hi dyaur asuraḥ* is the fifth Sūkta in the nineteenth Anuvāka. It has seven ṛks; the Anukramaṇikā says "*indrāya sapta*". The ṛṣi is Paruccheṣa; the deity is Indra; the metre is Atyaṣṭi. On the sixth day of the *pṛṣṭhya* ṣaḍaha sacrifice, at the midday pressing, the ṛks seen by this ṛṣi, which the *hotrakas* recite as *sasta-śastra* mantras, are used; of these ṛks the first three are for the Maitrāvaruṇa priest, the next three for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and the last three for the Ukthāvāka [as read; the allotment is doubtful: [?]]. This is expounded in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section beginning "*ṣaṣṭhe 'hani*", by the sūtra *indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata* (Āś. 8-1 [?]; as read "೮-೧೧" in one place and "೮-೧" in another). In the *mahāvrata* sacrifice, in the *niṣkevalya śastra*, the three ṛks beginning *indrāya hi* are used as *anurūpa* — as stated by Śaunaka in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, in the section *mahāvratasya*, by the sūtra *indraṃ yāhy upa naḥ parāvata indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata* (Ait. Ār. 5-1-1 [?]).

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read: "೨೦"].)*

*(The Kannada anuvāda of the introduction, continued from p. 466: at the midday pressing this Sūkta is made into three *tṛcas* (groups of three ṛks) and recited, and the *stomāvāpa* is done after them; the division is: the first three ṛks for the Maitrāvaruṇa priest, the next three for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and the last for the Acchāvāka — as stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section *caturthe 'hani*, by the sūtra *ṣaṣṭhe 'hani indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata* (Āś. 8-11 [?], as read). On the same day, at the same pressing, the six ṛks of this Sūkta are recited one by one by the Praśāstṛ and others as preliminary to the *prasthitayājyā* mantras, by the sūtra *indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnateti ṣaṭ* in the section *ṣaṣṭhasya* (Āś. 8-1 [?]). In the *mahāvrata*, at the *niṣkevalya śastra*, the three ṛks beginning *indrāya hi* are recited as alternative *anurūpa* ṛks, by Śaunaka's Aitareya Āraṇyaka sūtra *indraṃ yāhy upa naḥ parāvata indrāya hi dyaur asuro anamnata* (Ait. Ār. 5-1-1 [?]).)*

**ಸೂಕ್ತ—೧೩೧ — Sūkta 131.** *Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 19 ‖ Sūkta 131 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 1 ‖ Varga 20 ‖ Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 7 ‖ Ṛṣi: Paruccheṣa Daivodāsi ‖ Devatā: Indra ‖ Chandas: Atyaṣṭi.*

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> इन्द्राय हि द्यौरसुरो अनम्नतेन्द्राय मही पृथिवी वरीमभिः ।
> द्युम्नसाता वरीमभिः ।
> इन्द्रं विश्वे सजोषसो देवासो दधिरे पुरः ।
> इन्द्राय विश्वा सवनानि मानुषा रातानि सन्तु मानुषा ॥ १ ॥

> *indrāya hi dyaurasuro anamnatendrāya mahī pṛthivī varīmabhiḥ |*
> *dyumnasātā varīmabhiḥ |*
> *indraṃ viśve sajoṣaso devāso dadhire puraḥ |*
> *indrāya viśvā savanāni mānuṣā rātāni santu mānuṣā ‖ 1 ‖*

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

> इन्द्राय । हि । द्यौः । असुरः । अनम्नत । इन्द्राय । मही । पृथिवी । वरीमऽभिः ।
> द्युम्नऽसाता । वरीमऽभिः ।
> इन्द्रम् । विश्वे । सऽजोषसः । देवासः । दधिरे । पुरः ।
> इन्द्राय । विश्वा । सवनानि । मानुषा । रातानि । सन्तु । मानुषा ॥ १ ॥

> *indrāya | hi | dyauḥ | asuraḥ | anamnata | indrāya | mahī | pṛthivī | varīma 'bhiḥ |*
