> *indram | viśve | sa 'joṣasaḥ | devāsaḥ | dadhire | puraḥ |*
> *indrāya | viśvā | savanāni | mānuṣā | rātāni | santu | mānuṣā ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; small type, a few places doubtful: [?]).*

> द्यौर्द्योतनशीलो द्युलोकस्तन्निवासी देवसंघो वा स चासुरो निरसनशीलः शत्रूणां पुण्यकृतामेव तन्निवासात् । इन्द्रायै हीन्द्रायैवानम्नत । स्वयमेव प्रह्वीभवति ॥ नमेश्छान्दसे लुङ् [?] कर्मकर्तर्यात्मनेपदम् । न दुहस्नुनमामिति यगभावः । पा. ३-१-८९ ॥ छान्दसः शपः श्लुः । हलादिशेषाभावश्च । अनुनासिकलोपः ॥ हिशब्दः प्रसिद्ध्यर्थो वा । तथेन्द्रायेन्द्रार्थं मही महती पृथिवी भूमिस्तत्रत्यः सर्वो जनो वानम्नत । उभयत्राश्रयवाचिशब्देनाश्रया लक्ष्यन्ते ग्राम आगत इतिवत् । केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । वरीमभिर्वरणीयैः स्तोत्रैर्हविर्भिर्वा । किंच द्युम्नसाता द्युम्नसातावन्नस्य यशसो वा लाभे सति वरीमभिर्वरणीयैर्हविर्भिर्युक्ता यजमानाः प्रह्वा भवन्ति । किंचेन्द्रमेव विश्वे सर्वे देवासो देवाः सजोषसः समानप्रीतियुक्ता ऐकमत्यभाजः पूर्वमसुरजयार्थं पुरो दधिरे । पुरतः स्थापितवन्तः । इन्द्रमुखेनैवासुराञ्जितवन्त इत्यर्थः । तथा मानुषा सवनानि मनुष्याणां सम्बन्धीन्यभिषवयुक्तानि प्रातरादिसवनानीन्द्रायैव सन्तु । इन्द्रायैव भवन्तु । तथा मानुषा मनुष्याणामृत्विजां सम्बन्धीनि रातानि दातव्यानि पुरोडाशादीनीन्द्रायैव सन्तु । इन्द्रं प्रीणयितुं समर्थानि भवन्तित्यर्थः ॥

> *dyaurdyotanaśīlo dyulokastannivāsī devasaṃgho vā sa cāsuro nirasanaśīlaḥ śatrūṇāṃ puṇyakṛtāmeva tannivāsāt | indrāyai hīndrāyaivānamnata | svayameva prahvībhavati ‖ nameśchāndase luṅ [?] karmakartaryātmanepadam | na duhasnunamāmiti yagabhāvaḥ | pā. 3-1-89 ‖ chāndasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | halādiśeṣābhāvaśca | anunāsikalopaḥ ‖ hiśabdaḥ prasiddhyartho vā | tathendrāyendrārthaṃ mahī mahatī pṛthivī bhūmistatratyaḥ sarvo jano vānamnata | ubhayatrāśrayavāciśabdenāśrayā lakṣyante grāma āgata itivat | kena sādhaneneti taducyate | varīmabhirvaraṇīyaiḥ stotrairhavirbhirvā | kiṃca dyumnasātā dyumnasātāvannasya yaśaso vā lābhe sati varīmabhirvaraṇīyairhavirbhiryuktā yajamānāḥ prahvā bhavanti | kiṃcendrameva viśve sarve devāso devāḥ sajoṣasaḥ samānaprītiyuktā aikamatyabhājaḥ pūrvamasurajayārthaṃ puro dadhire | purataḥ sthāpitavantaḥ | indramukhenaivāsurāñjitavanta ityarthaḥ | tathā mānuṣā savanāni manuṣyāṇāṃ sambandhīnyabhiṣavayuktāni prātarādisavanānīndrāyaiva santu | indrāyaiva bhavantu | tathā mānuṣā manuṣyāṇāmṛtvijāṃ sambandhīni rātāni dātavyāni puroḍāśādīnīndrāyaiva santu | indraṃ prīṇayituṃ samarthāni bhavantityarthaḥ ‖*

*(Sense: "Heaven (*dyauḥ*, the shining heaven-world, or the host of gods who dwell there) and the *asura* (the repeller of enemies, because the dwellers there are the righteous) bows (*anamnata*) to Indra alone, of its own accord. [Grammar: the Vedic *luṅ* of *nam*, the ātmanepada in the intransitive sense; *na duhasnunamām yag abhāvaḥ* (Pā. 3-1-89 [?]); *śluḥ* for *śap*; no *halādiśeṣa*; loss of the nasal.] *hi* is for emphasis. So for Indra the great earth (*mahī pṛthivī*) — or all people dwelling on it — bows; the words naming the support stand for the supported, as in 'the village has come'. By what means? *varīmabhiḥ* — by choice praises or oblations. And when there is *dyumnasātā* — winning food or fame — the sacrificers, furnished with choice oblations, bow. And all the gods (*viśve devāsaḥ*), united in affection (*sajoṣasaḥ*), of one mind, formerly put Indra in front (*puro dadhire*) to conquer the demons: they conquered the demons through Indra. Likewise may the human pressings (*mānuṣā savanāni*), the morning and other pressings, be for Indra alone; and the offerings to be given by the human priests, the *puroḍāśa* and the rest, be for Indra, able to please him.")*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *asuraḥ* — the repeller of enemies (that gives no room for enemies); *dyauḥ* — the heaven-world; *indrāya hi* — to Indra only; *anamnata* — bows [becomes submissive]; *indrāya* — to Indra; *mahī* — the great; *pṛthivī* — the earth (the people on it); *varīmabhiḥ* — by praises (oblations); *anamnata* — bow; *dyumnasātā* — for food or the winning of fame; *varīmabhiḥ* — with oblations; *(anamnata* — they bow); *viśve devāsaḥ* — all the gods; *sajoṣasaḥ* — with equal affection (in unity, for conquering the demons); *puraḥ dadhire* — placed in front (made Indra the leader and conquered the demons by him); *mānuṣā* — belonging to men; *viśvā savanāni* — all pressings (connected with extraction, the morning and others); *indrāya santu* — be for Indra; *mānuṣā* — belonging to men (the priests); *rātāni* — offerings to be given (the *puroḍāśa* and the rest); *(indrāya santu* — be for Indra).

### Printed p. 469  (PDF 490)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** The heaven-world, that gives no room to the wicked, is subject to Indra alone; with offerings that have no equal this great earth is submissive to Indra; for food or fame, the sacrificers worship Indra; the gods, united in affection (in agreement, for conquering the demons), gave Indra the first place; may the pressings of men be for Indra; may the *puroḍāśa* and other offerings made by men be for Indra.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"To Indra heaven, that excludes the wicked, verily has bowed: to Indra the wide-spread earth (has offered homage) with acceptable (praises); with acceptable praises (the worshipper has propitiated Indra) for the sake of food: all the gods well pleased have given precedence to Indra: let all the sacrifices of men (be appropriated) to Indra; let all the offerings of men be (presented to him)."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 1).**

***dyauḥ*** — *dyotanaśīlaḥ dyulokaḥ tannivāsī devasaṅgho vā*: "the shining heaven-world, or the company of gods who dwell there." The word *dyauḥ* is recorded among the twelve names of day (*vastoḥ, dyauḥ, bhānuḥ* etc.; Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೨೦" [?]). And —

> त्वमग्ने द्युभिस्त्वमाशुशुक्षणिस्त्वमद्भ्यस्त्वमश्मनस्परि ।
> त्वं वनेभ्यस्त्वमोषधीभ्यस्त्वं नृणां नृपते जायसे शुचिः ॥

> *tvam agne dyubhis tvam āśuśukṣaṇis tvam adbhyas tvam aśmanas pari |*
> *tvaṃ vanebhyas tvam oṣadhībhyas tvaṃ nṛṇāṃ nṛpate jāyase śuciḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-1, as read "೨-೧-೧"; the same Ṛk was cited on p. 430.) Here *dyubhiḥ* is explained as *ahobhiḥ* ("by days").

### Printed p. 470  (PDF 491)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

> उप श्वासय पृथिवीमुत द्यां पुरुत्रा ते मनुतां विष्ठितं जगत् ।
> स दुन्दुभे सजूरिन्द्रेण देवैर्दूराद्दवीयो अप सेध शत्रून् ॥

> *upa śvāsaya pṛthivīm uta dyāṃ purutrā te manutāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ jagat |*
> *sa dundubhe sajūr indreṇa devair dūrād davīyo apa sedha śatrūn ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-29, as read "೬-೪೭-೨೯".) In this Ṛk *dyām* is explained as *divam*. Sāyaṇa explains *dyauḥ* as "the heaven-world", very bright, or as "the company of the gods who live in the heaven-world".

***asuraḥ indrāya hi anamnata*** — *śatrūṇāṃ nirasanaśīlaḥ indrāyaiva svayam eva prahvo bhavati*: the word *asura* is recorded among the names of cloud (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೩೧"). The Niruktakāra —

> तदिद्ध्यस्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीयं येनासुरां अभि देवा असाम ।
> ऊर्जादः उत यज्ञियासः पञ्च जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वम् ॥

> *tad id dhy asya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīyaṃ yenāsurām̐ abhi devā asāma |*
> *ūrjādaḥ uta yajñiyāsaḥ pañca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-4, as read "೧೦-೫೩-೪".) — citing this Ṛk, explains *asurāḥ asuratāḥ sthāneṣu sthāneṣu* [?] — "the *asuras* are so called because (*asu* = breath) or because they are 'not set' (*a-sthita*)": "*asuḥ prāṇaḥ tena tadvantaḥ*", and by *so 'deva*… *sa devān asṛjata tat surāṇāṃ suratvam*: "he created the gods; that is the god-hood of the gods; *asor asurān asṛjata tad asurāṇām asuratvam*": so it is known (Ni. 3-[?]). Durgācārya says, "one who stands in one place, firm, as persons of fickle mind who flee to other places, are gods or ... ; because they stand firmly (*asthitāḥ*) they are asuras"; or, as stated in the Śruti "*ūrdhvam udait pūrvapakṣaḥ … tena sa devān asṛjata tat surāṇāṃ suratvam*": "Brahmā, by his excellent self, created gods; therefore they are *suras*"; "*arvāñjyotir … aparapakṣaḥ … tenāsurān asṛjata*": "the later half [of the day] has the name *asu*, hence he created the asuras": so he explains (see Ṛg-Saṃhitā vol. 10, pp. 8–9 in this edition).

Sāyaṇa explains *asura* as "one who is cast out by the company of the gods", and so as "one who is not suited to dwell in the heaven-world, where only the righteous have a place"; thus he points out the greatness of Indra, to whom the great heaven-world is itself subservient.

***indrāya mahī pṛthivī anamnata*** — *indrārthaṃ mahatī pṛthivī tatratyaḥ sarvo jano vā anamnata | ubhayatrāśrayavācī śabdenāśrayā lakṣyate | grāmaḥ āgata itivat*: "heaven and the earth, the dwelling-places of the gods and of men, are named by the words *dyauḥ* and *pṛthivī*; here the dwellers are meant by these words."

### Printed p. 471  (PDF 492)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

(…) As one says, "the village has come" — when what comes is the people of the village; so here the people living on the earth are meant by the word "earth". The gods too are subject to Indra; the people on the earth also are submissive to Indra of their own accord; and the earth is subject to Indra in every way.

***varīmabhiḥ dyumnasātā varīmabhiḥ*** — *stotraiḥ havirbhir vā annasya yaśaso vā lābhe sati havirbhir yuktāḥ yajamānāḥ prahvā bhavanti*: "the sacrificers, who are fit to propitiate the god they desire, by praises or by oblations bow down again to the gods, to offer oblations, because they have obtained food and fame." The words *varīmabhiḥ* are used twice; in the one the meaning is *varaṇīya*, "to be chosen"; in the second *varaṇīyair havirbhiḥ*, "with oblations that are choice".

The word *dyumna* is recorded among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯") and in *dyumnam adhiraṣmaṃ ca dhehi* [as read] *dyumnaṃ dyoter yaśo vā annaṃ vā* (Ni. 5-[?]; as read "೫-೬") the word is explained: *dyumna* from the root *dyut* gives the many senses "fame" or "food", as Yāska says.

***sajoṣasaḥ puro dadhire*** — *samānaprītiyuktā aikamatyabhājaḥ*: "gods, united in affection for each other, in agreement, to conquer the demons, made Indra their leader and by him obtained victory". The word *sajoṣas* is explained in the Nirukta as "joined" (Ni. 8-[?]; as read "೮-೮"). —

> आजुह्वान ईड्यो वन्द्यश्चा याह्यग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः ।
> त्वं देवानामसि यह्व होता स एनान्यक्षीषितो यजीयान् ॥

> *ājuhvāna īḍyo vandyaś cā yāhy agne vasubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ |*
> *tvaṃ devānām asi yahva hotā sa enān yakṣīṣito yajīyān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-[?], as read "೧೦-೧೧೦-೩".) Here *sajoṣāḥ* is explained as *saha joṣaṇaḥ samānaprītiyuktaḥ*. And —

> आ रुद्रासः इन्द्रवन्तः सजोषसो हिरण्यरथाः सुविताय गन्तन ।
> इयं वो अस्मत्प्रति हर्यते मतिस्तृणाजे [?] न दिव उत्सा उदन्यवे ॥

> *ā rudrāsa indravantaḥ sajoṣaso hiraṇyarathāḥ suvitāya gantana |*
> *iyaṃ vo asmat prati haryate matis tṛṇāje [?] na diva utsā udanyave ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-[?] as read "೫-೩-೧-೧"? [?]; small type, doubtful.) Here, *indreṇa saha joṣaṇāḥ sajoṣasaḥ*, "served together with Indra in the greatness of lordship": as the reading in small type is unclear, the explanation is given only as read.

### Printed p. 472  (PDF 493)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

***mānuṣā savanāni indrāya santu*** — "May the pressings (extracting the Soma-juice), by which men bring the Soma and grind it and prepare the morning libation, be for Indra."

***mānuṣā rātāni*** — "The mantra-seer prays, in a fit of inspiration, that the *puroḍāśa* and other offerings made by the priests may be able to please Indra alone."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *asuraḥ* — root *asu kṣepaṇe*; *āser uraN* (Uṇ. 1-[?]) gives *uran*; *jñityādir nityam* gives the acute on the first syllable. *anamnata* — root *ṇamu prahvatve śabde ca*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pā. 3-4-6) gives *laṅ* in the present sense; since the agent of the middle-sense is intended, *karmavat karmaṇā tulyakriyaḥ* (Pā. 3-1-87) gives the ātmanepada; third person singular *ta*; *namatiśapo…* [as read: *na duhasnunamāṃ yag* …] — no *yak*; *śluḥ* in place of *śap*; the root is doubled; no *halādiśeṣa* in the reduplicative; *anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti* (Pā. 6-4-37) drops the nasal; the augment *aṭ*; because *hi* is connected, *hi ca* (Pā. 8-1-34) forbids *nighāta*; the augment being acute, the first syllable is acute. *pṛthivī* — root *pratha prakhyāne*; *pratheḥ ṣivan saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca* (Uṇ. 1-[?]) gives *ṣivan*; in the feminine *ṣidgaurādibhyaś ca* (Pā. 4-1-41) gives *ṅīṣ*; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. *varīmabhiḥ* — root *vṛñ varaṇe*; Uṇādi *īman* with *ninc*; guṇa of the root by the suffix with *raparatva*; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable. *dadhire* — root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *liṭ* third person plural; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *savanāni* — root *ṣuñ abhiṣave*; *lyuṭ*; *yuvor anākau* gives *ana*; *liti* gives the acute before the suffix.

### Printed p. 473  (PDF 494)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 20 [as read].)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 1, concluded; numbers as printed.)* *mānuṣā* — *manuṣyasya imāni mānuṣāṇi*; the suffix *aṇ* in the sense of relation; acute on the last syllable by the suffix; in the neuter plural *śeś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. 6-1-70) drops *śi*. *rātāni* — root *rā ādāne*; *kta*; accent by the suffix. *santu* — root *as bhuvi*; *loṭ* third person plural; *tiṅ-nighāta*. ‖ 1 ‖

***(ornamental rule)***

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> विश्वेषु हि त्वा सवनेषु तुञ्जते समानमेकं वृषमण्यवः ।
> पृथक् स्वः सनिष्यवः पृथक् ।
> तं त्वा नावं न पर्षणिं शूषस्य धुरि धीमहि ।
> इन्द्रं न यज्ञैश्चितयन्त आयवः स्तोमेभिरिन्द्रमायवः ॥ २ ॥

> *viśveṣu hi tvā savaneṣu tuñjate samānamekaṃ vṛṣamaṇyavaḥ |*
> *pṛthak svaḥ saniṣyavaḥ pṛthak |*
> *taṃ tvā nāvaṃ na parṣaṇiṃ śūṣasya dhuri dhīmahi |*
> *indraṃ na yajñaiścitayanta āyavaḥ stomebhirindramāyavaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> विश्वेषु । हि । त्वा । सवनेषु । तुञ्जते । समानम् । एकम् । वृषऽमन्यवः । पृथक् ।
> स्वः । सनिष्यवः । पृथक् ।
> तम् । त्वा । नावम् । न । पर्षणिम् । शूषस्य । धुरि । धीमहि ।
> इन्द्रम् । न । यज्ञैः । चितयन्तः । आयवः । स्तोमेभिः । इन्द्रम् । आयवः ॥ २ ॥

> *viśveṣu | hi | tvā | savaneṣu | tuñjate | samānam | ekam | vṛṣa 'manyavaḥ | pṛthak |*
> *svaḥ | saniṣyavaḥ | pṛthak |*
> *tam | tvā | nāvam | na | parṣaṇim | śūṣasya | dhuri | dhīmahi |*
> *indram | na | yajñaiḥ | citayantaḥ | āyavaḥ | stomebhiḥ | indram | āyavaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

*(Read from the image: the Pada gives *vṛṣa-manyavaḥ*, *svar iti svaḥ*, *sanisyavaḥ*; the Saṃhitā's first line prints "*tuñjate samānam ekaṃ vṛṣamaṇyavaḥ*", and in the Pada "*vṛṣamanyavaḥ*" — the Saṃhitā spelling with *ṇ* is as printed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; small type, doubtful places [?]).*

> हे इन्द्र त्वा त्वामेकमेकमेव सन्तं विश्वेषु सर्वेषु सवनेषु तद्वत्सु स्वैः [?] काहाहीनसत्ररूपेषु सर्वेषु सोमयागेषु यजमानास्तुञ्जते । त्वरयन्ति । हविरादीनि ददते । कीदृशं त्वाम् । समानं सर्वेषामेकरूपम् । कीदृशा यजमानाः । वृषमण्यवो वृषमन्यवः । अभिमतवर्षणाय त्वामेव मन्यमानाः । पृथग्भिन्नरूपैः [?] । पृथगेव त्वरयन्ति । पृथक् प्रत्येकं तत्तद्यागेषु हविरादीनि दद्युः । तुञ्जतिर्दानार्थः । शिक्षति तुञ्जत इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तं तादृशं त्वा त्वां शूषस्य बलस्य सेनारूपस्य धुरि वहने तज्जयाय धीमहि । स्थापयामः । यद्वा । शूषस्य सुखस्य । शरीरबलस्य [?] धुरि धीमहि । शूषमिति बलनाम । शूषं सह इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । पर्षणिं नावं न पारस्य सम्भक्त्रीं पूरयित्रीं वा फलस्य नावमिव । तां यथा भारवहने स्थापयन्ति । पारतीरं कर्मसमाप्तौ [?] । छन्दसि वनसनेति सनेरिन्प्रत्ययः । पृषोदरादित्वाद् [?] । पिपर्तेर्वौणादिकः सनिप्रत्ययो वा ॥ कीदृशा वयम् । आयवो मनुष्या यजमाना यज्ञैः साधनैरिन्द्रं न चितयन्तः परमेश्वरमिव त्वां चेतयन्तः । परमेश्वरबुद्ध्या भावयन्त इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । नशब्द उपमार्थः । इन्द्रमेव त्वां जानन्तः । तथा स्तोमेभिः स्तोत्रैरिन्द्रमिन्द्रमेवायवो गच्छन्तो वयं धीमहि ॥ दधातेर्लिङि [?] छान्दसः शपो लुक् ॥

> *he indra tvā tvāmekamekameva santaṃ viśveṣu sarveṣu savaneṣu tadvatsu svaiḥ [?] kāhāhīnasatrarūpeṣu sarveṣu somayāgeṣu yajamānāstuñjate | tvarayanti | havirādīni dadate | kīdṛśaṃ tvām | samānaṃ sarveṣāmekarūpam | kīdṛśā yajamānāḥ | vṛṣamaṇyavo vṛṣamanyavaḥ | abhimatavarṣaṇāya tvāmeva manyamānāḥ | pṛthagbhinnarūpaiḥ [?] | pṛthageva tvarayanti | pṛthak pratyekaṃ tattadyāgeṣu havirādīni dadyuḥ | tuñjatirdānārthaḥ | śikṣati tuñjata iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | taṃ tādṛśaṃ tvā tvāṃ śūṣasya balasya senārūpasya dhuri vahane tajjayāya dhīmahi | sthāpayāmaḥ | yadvā | śūṣasya sukhasya | śarīrabalasya [?] dhuri dhīmahi | śūṣamiti balanāma | śūṣaṃ saha iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | parṣaṇiṃ nāvaṃ na pārasya sambhaktrīṃ pūrayitrīṃ vā phalasya nāvamiva | tāṃ yathā bhāravahane sthāpayanti | pāratīraṃ karmasamāptau [?] | chandasi vanasaneti sanerinpratyayaḥ | pṛṣodarāditvād [?] | pipartervauṇādikaḥ sanipratyayo vā ‖ kīdṛśā vayam | āyavo manuṣyā yajamānā yajñaiḥ sādhanairindraṃ na citayantaḥ parameśvaramiva tvāṃ cetayantaḥ | parameśvarabuddhyā bhāvayanta ityarthaḥ | yadvā | naśabda upamārthaḥ | indrameva tvāṃ jānantaḥ | tathā stomebhiḥ stotrairindramindramevāyavo gacchanto vayaṃ dhīmahi ‖ dadhāterliṅi [?] chāndasaḥ śapo luk ‖*

*(Sense: "O Indra, in all pressings (*savaneṣu*) — the Soma sacrifices of all kinds, the one-day, the several-day, the long sessions — the sacrificers, regarding you alone, *samānam ekam* — the same for all, of one form — urge (*tuñjate*) and give oblations; they are *vṛṣamanyavaḥ*, thinking of you as the showerer of the desired; *pṛthak* — each separately, in their own several sacrifices, giving oblations (*tuñj* is a verb of giving: 'śikṣati tuñjate' in the lists of its names); *svaḥ sanisyavaḥ* — each desiring heaven. Such as you are we place (*dhīmahi*) at the yoke of *śūṣa* — strength, in the form of an army — for victory over it; or *śūṣa* is happiness or bodily strength (the word *śūṣa* is recorded among the names of strength). The example: like a boat (*nāvaṃ na parṣaṇim*) that carries one across — a ferry that is placed to bear the burden to the other bank, or fills the fruit; we the *āyavaḥ*, men, sacrificers, by sacrifices thinking of you as the Supreme Lord, or *na* is a word of comparison: knowing you as Indra alone; and with *stomas*, going to Indra alone, we meditate."*)

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he indra* — O Indra); *viśveṣu savaneṣu* — in all Soma sacrifices; *(yajamānāḥ* — the sacrificers); *pṛthak* — each separately (in their own sacrifices); *vṛṣamanyavaḥ* — thinking of you as the showerer of desires; *samānam* — the same for all; *ekam* — one; *tvā* — you; *tuñjate* — urge (and give oblations); *hi* — indeed; *svaḥ* — heaven; *sanisyavaḥ* — those desiring to obtain; *pṛthak* — separately (urge you); *tam* — such; *tvā* — you; *śūṣasya* — of strength (of the army); *dhuri* — at the yoke (to bear it, for victory); *parṣaṇim* — one who carries across; *nāvaṃ na* — like a boat (put to bear the load); *dhīmahi* — we place; *āyavaḥ* — we men (sacrificers); *yajñaiḥ* — by sacrifices; *indraṃ na* — as the Supreme Lord; *citayantaḥ* — meditating; *kathā* — likewise; *stomebhiḥ* — with hymns; *indram* — Indra; *āyavaḥ* — going to him (we place, delighting him).

### Printed p. 474  (PDF 495)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** Your worshippers, regarding you alone as the showerer of the desired, offer oblations to you in all the sacrifices, each separately, in their several sacrifices; each, desiring heaven (happiness), regards you; we too, regarding you as the Supreme Lord, thinking of you — you who are the support of our strength, like a boat that carries men across — we please you with hymns and with the means of sacrifice; we, the sacrificers, regarding you as Indra, meditate on you, going to you alone with hymns.

*(The Kannada bhāvārtha as printed is rendered above: "(Your worshippers), regarding you alone as the bestower of what is wished, each separately in each sacrifice regard you; each desiring heaven, seeking your protection; we, regarding you as Indra, praise you only, as the support of our strength, like a ferry-boat that carries (people) across…")*

### Printed p. 475  (PDF 496)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 21 [as read: "೨೧"].)*

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Hoping to partake of your bounties, (your worshippers) hasten severally in every rite to (adore) you, who ask one and all; each severally seeking heaven. We meditate on you, the sustainer of our strength, like a boat that bears (passengers) across (a stream): mortals, indeed, knowing Indra, propitiate him with sacrifices: mortals (propitiate him) with hymns."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 2).**

***vṛṣamanyavaḥ samānam ekaṃ viśveṣu savaneṣu tuñjate*** — *abhimatavarṣaṇāya tvām eva manyamānāḥ sarveṣām ekarūpam ekam eva santam ekāhīnasatrarūpeṣu somayāgeṣu tvarayanti havirādīni dadate*: "regarding you alone as the one who gives what is wished, the sacrificers, in the one-day (*ekāha*), several-day (*ahīna*) and long (*satra*) Soma sacrifices, urge you and give you oblations. In the matter of fulfilling their desires every one is equally partial to Indra: they believe he is the only one. In the Soma sacrifices of one day etc., consisting of the three pressings in morning and the rest, they offer oblations to Indra": so the meaning.

The Niruktakāra says that *tuñjati* is recorded among the ten verbs of giving beginning *dāti, dāśati* (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೯"). And —

> तुञ्जेतुञ्जे य उत्तरे स्तोमा इन्द्रस्य वज्रिणः ।
> न विन्धे अस्य सुष्टुतिम् ॥

> *tuñje-tuñje ya uttare stomā indrasya vajriṇaḥ |*
> *na vindhe asya suṣṭutim ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೭-೭" [?]; small type.) citing this, he explains *tuñje tuñje* as *dāne dāne*; Durgācārya says the word *tuj* is a synonym of *dāna*, "giving".

***pṛthak svaḥ sanisyavaḥ*** — "the sacrificers, who perform the sacrifices separately, each offering oblations to Indra in their own sacrifices, desire heaven or extraordinary happiness". The word *svaḥ* is recorded among the six common names *svaḥ, pṛśniḥ* (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೧೩") and is explained: *svar ādityo bhavati, su araṇaḥ, su īraṇaḥ, svato rasān, svato bhāsaṃ jyotiṣām, svato bhāsety vā* (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೧೪"), recorded also among the hundred and one names of water (Ni. 1-[?]; "೧-೩೪"). And —

### Printed p. 476  (PDF 497)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

> परं मृत्यो अनु परेहि पन्थां यस्ते स्व इतरो देवयानात् ।
> चक्षुष्मते शृण्वते ते ब्रवीमि मा नः प्रजां रीरिषो मोत वीरान् ॥

> *paraṃ mṛtyo anu parehi panthāṃ yas te sva itaro devayānāt |*
> *cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate te bravīmi mā naḥ prajāṃ rīriṣo mota vīrān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-18-1, as read "೧೦-೧೮-೧".) In this Ṛk the word *sva* is explained as "your own".

***śūṣasya dhuri dhīmahi*** — *senārūpasya balasya vahane jayāya sthāpayāmaḥ | yadvāsmadīyaśārīrabalasya dhuri dhīmahi*: two meanings are given for the word *śūṣa*. In the first, the strength in the form of an army; that we the sacrificers may be in the front in conquering the army; in the second, to increase greatly the strength of our body, as sacrificers, Indra is first prayed to. Since the word *śūṣa* is recorded among the eight names of strength (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"), Sāyaṇa gives two meanings of "strength": army, or bodily strength.

***parṣaṇiṃ nāvaṃ na*** — *pārasya sambhaktrīṃ pūrayitrīṃ vā phalasya nāvam iva*: "as a boat that carries a heavy load and countless things is placed to bring it to the far shore of the sea, and gives the fruit": so Indra is compared; he gives the sacrificer the completion of the sacrifice and its fruit.

***āyavaḥ indraṃ na citayantaḥ*** — *manuṣyāḥ yajamānāḥ parameśvaram iva tvāṃ bhāvayantaḥ | yadvā na śabda upamārthaḥ | indram eva tvāṃ jānantaḥ*: "men, sacrificers, regarding you as the Supreme Lord; or *na* is in the sense of emphasis: knowing you, the very Indra." The word *āyavaḥ* is used twice. The Niruktakāra reads *āyavaḥ* among the names of men (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೮"). In the first meaning, "sacrificers"; "regarding Indra as the Supreme Lord, they satisfy him by sacrifices". *Indater aiśvaryakarmaṇaḥ* (Ni. 10-[?]; as read "೧೦-೮") — the word *indra* is formed from the root *ind*, expressing lordship, so that *indra* gives the sense "one who has lordship and gives it"; and, since those who sacrifice regard him as the Supreme Lord, it is explained. Or, when the Niruktakāra explains the word *indra*: *idaṃ bhūtānīti vā* [as read: *indhe bhūtāni*], "*tad yad enaṃ prāṇaiḥ samaindhaṃs tad indrasyendratvam iti vijñāyate*" — "he kindles creatures; because the gods kindled him with the vital breaths, that is Indra's Indra-ness": it is explained that he makes living beings brilliant. Durgācārya: "*bhūtāni hy asya adhidevatvena adhyātmatvena abhyavahārayan vibhajamānaś ca dīpayati dyumantaṃ karoti*" — he is within beings as presiding deity and within the self, and, dividing, kindles and makes them brilliant. Therefore, the meaning of the word *indra* is stated: that he is the Supreme Lord.

### Printed p. 477  (PDF 498)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 21 [as read].)*

In the second meaning the word *āyavaḥ* is explained as "those who know"; Indra, who has the nature of supreme lordship, is known as the Supreme Lord, and we, the sacrificers, meditate on him by sacrifices and by hymns. And since particles have many meanings, *na* is explained as having the sense of comparison and of emphasis.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *tuñjate* — *tuja* is a *sautra* root of the sense "giving"; *śikṣati tuñjate* (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೨೦-೮"?) is read among the verbs of giving; *laṭ* third person plural; *hi ca* (Pā. 8-1-34) forbids *nighāta*; acute on the first syllable of the suffix. *vṛṣamanyavaḥ* — root *mana jñāne*; *yaji-mani…* (Uṇ. 3-[?]) gives *yuc*; in the compound the acute on the first syllable; nominative plural. *svaḥ* — *svar* becomes *svarita* by Phiṭ-sūtra 4 [as read]. *sanisyavaḥ* — root *ṣaṇu dāne*; *in sarvadhātubhyaḥ* [as read: *iṇ sarvadhātubhyaḥ*, Uṇ. 4-[?]] gives *iṇ*; when "desiring to give" is intended, *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. 3-1-8) gives *kyac*; *sarvaprātipadikebhyo lālasāyām asuk vaktavyaḥ…* [as read: Kāś. 3-1-8 vārttika] gives *suk*; after the *kyac*-ending, *kyāc chandasi* (Pā. 3-2-170) gives *u*; *ato lopaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-48) drops the *a* of *kyac*; acute on the last syllable by the suffix. *parṣaṇim* — root *pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ* or *paṇa sambhaktau*; *chandasi vanasana…* (Pā. 3-2-27) gives *in*; with *pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam* the form is obtained; the acute on the first syllable by the suffix. *dhīmahi* — root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *liṅ* first person plural, *mahiṅ*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *luk* of the *vikaraṇa*; since the suffix is *j*-marked, *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali* (Pā. 6-4-66) gives *ī*; *tiṅ-nighāta*.

### Printed p. 478  (PDF 499)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *citayantaḥ* — root *citī saṃjñāne*; *satyāpapāśa…* (Pā. 3-1-25) gives *ṇic* in the proper sense; by the statement *saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ* no guṇa; after the *ṇic*-ending, *śatṛ* in the present sense; guṇa, *ayādeśa* of the *ṇic*; the acute of *ṇic*. *āyavaḥ* — root *iṇ gatau*; *chandasīṇaḥ* (Uṇ. 1-[?]) gives *uṇ*; *aco ñṇiti* gives *vṛddhi*; *ayādeśa*; nominative plural. *stomebhiḥ* — by *bahulaṃ chandasi*, *bhis* takes *ais* optionally; since it is optional, *bahuvacane jhaly et* (Pā. 7-3-103) gives *e*. ‖ 2 ‖

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> वि त्वा ततस्रे मिथुना अवस्यवो व्रजस्य साता गव्यस्य निःसृजः ।
> सक्षन्त इन्द्र निःसृजः ।
> यद्गव्यन्ता द्वा जना स्वर्यन्ता समूहसि ।
> आविष्करिक्रद्वृषणं सचाभुवं वज्रमिन्द्र सचाभुवम् ॥ ३ ॥

> *vi tvā tatasre mithunā avasyavo vrajasya sātā gavyasya niḥsṛjaḥ |*
> *sakṣanta indra niḥsṛjaḥ |*
> *yadgavyantā dvā janā svaryantā samūhasi |*
> *āviṣkarikradvṛṣaṇaṃ sacābhuvaṃ vajramindra sacābhuvam ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> वि । त्वा । ततस्रे । मिथुनाः । अवस्यवः । व्रजस्य । साता । गव्यस्य । निःऽसृजः । सक्षन्तः ।
> इन्द्र । निःऽसृजः ।
> यत् । गव्यन्ता । द्वा । जना । स्वःऽयन्ता । सम्ऽऊहसि ।
> आविः । करिक्रत् । वृषणम् । सचाऽभुवम् । वज्रम् । इन्द्र । सचाऽभुवम् ॥ ३ ॥

> *vi | tvā | tatasre | mithunāḥ | avasyavaḥ | vrajasya | sātā | gavyasya | niḥ 'sṛjaḥ | sakṣantaḥ |*
> *indra | niḥ 'sṛjaḥ |*
> *yat | gavyantā | dvā | janā | svaḥ 'yantā | sam 'ūhasi |*
> *āviḥ | karikrat | vṛṣaṇam | sacā 'bhuvam | vajram | indra | sacā 'bhuvam ‖ 3 ‖*

*(Read from the image; in the Saṃhitā's third line the print has "*gavyantā dvā janā svaryantā samūhasi*"; the Pada writes *dvā* as a separate word. Doubtful letters in the Saṃhitā: "*ततस्रे*" is the form as printed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; very small and dense type — I transcribe the opening and then give the sense; doubtful places [?]).*

### Printed p. 480  (PDF 501)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

*(he) indra* — O Indra; *tvam* — you; *vṛṣaṇam* — rainer of desires; *sacābhuvam* — born together with you; *vajram* — the thunderbolt, [armed with] *sacābhuvam* (born together, with the power of killing enemies and the like); *āviḥ karikrat* — you make manifest; *(tat* — therefore); *(he indra* — O Indra); *avasyavaḥ* — those who desire (for themselves, or for you) satisfaction; *niḥ sṛjaḥ* — those who give oblations abundantly; *sakṣantaḥ* — going to you (to serve); *niḥ sṛjaḥ* — those who drive out sin that obstructs the fruit; *mithunāḥ* — the sacrificers together with their wives; *tvā* — you; *gavyasya* — related to cattle; *vrajasya* — of the herd; *sātā* — for the winning; *vi tatasre* — perform the sacrifice (or, with milk and the like, extend/strain the vows).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, to the couples who desire cattle and heaven you grant the fruit of heaven and the like; and you reveal the thunderbolt born with you, which rains desires, with its power to kill enemies; therefore the sacrificers, husband and wife, who both desire your satisfaction, offering oblations abundantly, coming to you and driving out the sin that obstructs the fruit, perform the sacrifice (with milk-vows and the like) for the winning of cattle-herds.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"The (married) couples, anxious to satisfy you, and presenting (oblations) together, celebrate (your worship), for the sake of (obtaining) herds of cattle; presenting (you), Indra, (oblations): you well know that these two persons are desirous of cattle, are desirous of heaven, and (you abide), displaying your thunderbolt, the shower (of benefits), your constant companion, ever Indra, associated (with you)."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 3).**

***mithunāḥ … vi tatasre*** — a long discussion follows on whether wives have a right to take part in Vedic sacrifices. It runs: "*na ca agnihotrādinityavākyeṣu kārīrīcitrādikāmyavākyeṣu yasyodayaṃ yasya gṛhān ity ādinaimittikavākyeṣu puruṣasyaiva arthitvādeḥ sadbhāvāt tasyaivādhikāraḥ, striyās tu satyapi arthitve adhyayanābhāvena vidvattvāyā abhāvāt … nāsty adhikāra iti vācyam*" — "In the *nitya* (constant) injunctions such as the Agnihotra, in the *kāmya* (optional, for a wish) ones such as the *kārīrī* and *citrā* sacrifices, and in the *naimittika* (occasional) ones such as 'yasyodayaṃ…', 'yasya gṛhān…', only the man has the right, since he alone has the wish and the like; the woman, though she wishes, being without Vedic study, has no learning and therefore no capacity; so it must be said she has no right." Sāyaṇa answers: though the *Pūrvamīmāṃsā* (Adhyāya 6, adhikaraṇas 3 and 4) shows that the wife does have the right to the sacrifice, because of the śruti "*jāyāpatī agnim ādadhīyātām*" ("let husband and wife set up the fire") (Taittirīya [?]); and the sūtra of Manu "*nāsti strīṇāṃ pṛthag yajño na vratam*" (Manu 5-155 [?], as read "೫-೧೫೫"), which forbids a separate right, shows that her right is together with her husband's. The wife has no independent right to the vow or the sacrifice; she may perform the rites together with her husband.

### Printed p. 481  (PDF 502)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 21 [as read].)*

(Continuing:) The Śruti statements "*kurvīta*" and the like make the *nitya* injunctions binding even on those who live by it; the *kāmya* injunctions such as "*vṛṣṭikāmaḥ kārīryā yajeta*" ("one desiring rain should sacrifice with the *kārīrī*") teach that those who have the respective desires should perform the respective sacrifices; the *naimittika* ones such as "*yasyodayaṃ yasya gṛhān*" teach that they are to be performed at the respective occasions. In performing these three kinds of sacrifice the man alone has the wish; it is understood that he alone has the right. The wife too, because she shares his wish, has a right; but since she has not studied the mantras and is not learned, she lacks the capacity: therefore it is said in the Śāstra that she has no right to the performance of the sacrificial rite.

*yadyapi striyāḥ nāsti pṛthag adhikāraḥ tathāpi pūrvamīmāṃsāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe adhikārādhyāye tṛtīyacaturthābhyām adhikaraṇābhyām asty eva striyā adhikāraḥ | sa ca patyā saheti prapañcitatvāt "jāyāpatī agnim ādadhīyātām" ity ādhānavidhānāt* — "Though a woman has no separate right, yet in the sixth Adhyāya of the Pūrvamīmāṃsā, called the *adhikārādhyāya*, by the third and fourth *adhikaraṇas* a woman has the right; and that is together with her husband, as it is explained at length, from the injunction about setting up the fire: 'let husband and wife set up the fire'." *(Read from the image; the references to sūtras are in small type and are given as read.)* And in the Manu-smṛti "*nāsti strīṇāṃ pṛthag yajño na vrataṃ nāpy upoṣaṇam*" (Manu 5-155 [?]) it is the separate right alone that is denied: the wife has a right only with her husband.

*adhyayanābhāve 'pi vedaṃ patnyai pradāya vācayet* (Āś. Śrauta-sūtra 1-11 [?]) — by this sūtra of the Sūtrakāra *patnyā nyasyate* [as read] ... *ity ādividhiṣu suprajasas tvayaṃ* (Tai. Saṃ. 1-1-10-1 [?]): "in the absence of study, the husband, giving the Veda [mantra] to his wife, should make her recite it."

### Printed p. 482  (PDF 503)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

"…In injunctions such as this, where there is a statement, the wife has an authority in the mantra (*yatra vacanam asti tatra asyaiva mantre 'dhikāraḥ*); what is the use of a statement? — By the maxim *nāsti vacanasyātibhāraḥ* ('a statement can bear any weight'), therefore *mithunā yajñaṃ tatasre* is proper: couples, together with their wives, perform the sacrifice, as said in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā with the 'prajā' [*suprajasas tvayam*]. In the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra the husband is ordered to give the *darbha* to his wife's hand and make her recite the mantra; from this it is evident that she has the right to Vedic rites; and in accordance with the statement of the Śruti the right of the wife is seen in the recitation of the mantras; and the statement has a purpose; as in the statement of a *prāk-prokṣaṇa* — by *anvādhāna* and the like, since a wife has the right with her husband, it is said here in this mantra: 'couples perform the sacrifice'." So Sāyaṇa explains.

***avasyavaḥ niḥsṛjaḥ*** — *indrasya ātmane vā tṛptim icchantaḥ niḥśeṣeṇa havīṃṣi sṛjantaḥ*: "desiring Indra's satisfaction or their own satisfaction through the sacrifice done as they wish, they offer oblations in abundance." The word *niḥsṛjaḥ* is used twice. For the second, *phalapratibandhakaṃ pāpaṃ nirgamayantaḥ* — "driving away by the performance of sacrifice the sins that obstruct the fruit they desire."

***gavyantā svaryantā dvā janā samūhasi*** — *gām ātmana icchantau svargaṃ gantum udyuktau jāyāpatirūpau janau abhimataṃ svargaṃ prāpayasi | yadvā samyaggamanuṣṭhitavantau āviṣkaroṣi niṣkṛṣya* [?]: "since the sacrificers with their wives wish to obtain cows and also to obtain heaven, Indra is said to carry out the wishes of both; or, he is the one who, when both have properly performed the sacrifice, brings it to fruition": so the performance of the sacrifice together by husband and wife is described.

***vṛṣaṇaṃ sacābhuvam*** — *kāmānāṃ varṣakam avinābhūtam*: "Indra is always occupied in fulfilling desires, as he fulfils those of his followers."

***sacābhuvaṃ vajram āviṣkarikrat*** — *śatruvadhādivyāpārasāmarthyena sahaivotpannaṃ vajraṃ prakaṭayan varteṣe*: "Indra constantly carries the thunderbolt, endowed with the power to kill enemies": his unlimited greatness is described.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *tatasre* — root *tasu upakṣaye*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pā. 3-4-6) gives *liṭ* in the present sense; third person plural, *litas tājjhayor eśirec* (Pā. 3-4-81) gives *ire*; *iraya ire* [as read: Pā. 6-4-76] gives *re*; the root is doubled; because it follows a finite verb *nighāta*. *avasyavaḥ* — *avāḥ devāḥ tān icchanti* [as read; the root *av*]; *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. 3-1-8); *sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ lālasāyām asuk vaktavyaḥ* gives *suk*; after *kyac*, *kyāc chandasi* (Pā. 3-2-170) gives *u*; the *a* of *kyac* drops; acute on the last syllable. *sātā* — root *ṣaṇu dāne*; *ūtiyūtijūti…* (Pā. 3-3-97) gives *ktin* irregularly, acute; locative singular *supāṃ sulug* gives *ḍā*; the *ṭi* drops as *ḍit*; the *udāttanivṛtti* accent gives the acute to the ending. *gavyasya* — *gopayasor yat* [as read: Pā. 4-3-160] gives *yat* in the sense of relation; *vānto yi pratyaye* (Pā. 6-1-79) gives *av*; *yato nāvaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-213) gives the acute on the first syllable. *niḥsṛjaḥ* — root *sṛja visarge*; *kvip ca* gives *kvip*; since a prefix compound, *kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara*; nominative plural. *sakṣantaḥ* — root *sakṣa gatau* [as read]; *śatṛ* in the present sense; *tāsyanudāttenṅid…* — the *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented so the root's accent remains. *gavyantā* — *gām ātmana icchantau*; *supa ātmanaḥ kyac*; *vānto yi pratyaye* gives *av*; after the *kyac*-ending *śatṛ*; *kṛt* accent remains; for the dual, *ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ* gives *num*; *supāṃ sulug* gives *ā* for the dual; likewise in *dvā janā*, *svaryantā*. *yantā* — root *iṇ gatau*; *laṭ*… *śatṛ*; *iṇo yaṇ* (Pā. 6-4-81) gives *yaṇ* to the root; the dual as before; acute on the first syllable of the suffix.

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *saṃ ūhasi* — root *ūha vitarke*; *laṭ* second person singular; because *yad* is connected, *nighāta* does not occur; since *śap* and *sip* are unaccented the root's accent remains; *tiṅ codāttavati* (Pā. 8-1-71) gives the unaccented *saṃ* [as read: the prefix *sam* gets the *anudātta*]. ‖ 3 ‖

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> विदुष्टे अस्य वीर्यस्य पूरवः पुरो यदिन्द्र शारदीरवातिरः ।
> ससहानो अवातिरः ।
> शासस्तमिन्द्र मर्त्यमयज्युं शवसस्पते ।
> महीममुष्णाः पृथिवीमिमा अपो मन्दसान इमा अपः ॥ ४ ॥

> *viduṣṭe asya vīryasya pūravaḥ puro yadindra śāradīravātiraḥ |*
> *sasahāno avātiraḥ |*
> *śāsastamindra martyamayajyuṃ śavasaspate |*
> *mahīmamuṣṇāḥ pṛthivīmimā apo mandasāna imā apaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> विदुः । ते । अस्य । वीर्यस्य । पूरवः । पुरः । यत् । इन्द्र । शारदीः । अवऽअतिरः ।
> ससहानः । अवऽअतिरः ।
> शासः । तम् । इन्द्र । मर्त्यम् । अयज्युम् । शवसः । पते ।
> महीम् । अमुष्णाः । पृथिवीम् । इमाः । अपः । मन्दसानः । इमाः । अपः ॥ ४ ॥

> *viduḥ | te | asya | vīryasya | pūravaḥ | puraḥ | yat | indra | śāradīḥ | ava 'atiraḥ |*
> *sasahānaḥ | ava 'atiraḥ |*
> *śāsaḥ | tam | indra | martyam | ayajyum | śavasaḥ | pate |*
> *mahīm | amuṣṇāḥ | pṛthivīm | imāḥ | apaḥ | mandasānaḥ | imāḥ | apaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

*(Read from the image: Saṃhitā "*viduṣ ṭe*" is printed with the *ṣ* of the Saṃhitā sandhi, Pada *viduḥ | te*.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र ते तव सम्बन्धिनोऽस्य वीर्यस्य ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी । वक्ष्यमाणमेतद्वीर्यं विदुः । ये पूरवो मनुष्या यजमानास्तव महत्त्वं जानानास्त्वामेव यजन्ति ते विदुः । यद्वा । अस्य वीर्यस्य माहात्म्यमिति शेषः । विदुष्ट इत्यत्र युष्मत्तत्तक्षुष्विति विसर्जनीयस्य सत्त्वम् ॥ वीर्यमेव विशेष्यते । हे इन्द्र यद्यस्मात्कारणात् शारदीः संवत्सरसम्बन्धिनीः संवत्सरपर्यन्तं प्राकारपरिखादिभिर्दृढीकृताः पुरः शत्रूणां पुरीरवातिरः । अनाशयः । अवपूर्वस्तिर्नाशनार्थः ॥ किं कुर्वन् । ससहानः सहतेः क्वसुः ससहानः । अभिभवन् धनाद्यपहारेण पीडयन् सहतेर्लुगन्तात्तालेलिकृष्णात् [?] ॥ अवातिरः । किंच हे इन्द्र तं मर्त्यं मरणधर्माणमयज्युमयज्वानं यज्ञविघातिनं राक्षसादिं शासः । निगृहीतवानसि । हे शवसस्पते बलस्य पालकेन्द्र त्वं महीं महतीं पृथिवीमिमा अपश्च समुद्रनद्यात्मकान्युदकानि चामुष्णाः । बलादपहृतवानसि । असुरैर्वा यज्ञविद्वेषिभी राक्रान्तां भूमिं तत्सम्बन्धिनीरपश्च तेषां पुराणि भित्त्वाहृतवानसीत्यर्थः । किं दुःखेन । नेत्याह । मन्दसानो हृष्यन्नेवेमा अप इमान्युपकार्याणि व्रीह्याद्यन्नान्यमुष्णाः । लब्धवानसि ॥

> *he indra te tava sambandhino 'sya vīryasya ‖ karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī | vakṣyamāṇametadvīryaṃ viduḥ | ye pūravo manuṣyā yajamānāstava mahattvaṃ jānānāstvāmeva yajanti te viduḥ | yadvā | asya vīryasya māhātmyamiti śeṣaḥ | viduṣṭa ityatra yuṣmattattakṣuṣviti visarjanīyasya sattvam ‖ vīryameva viśeṣyate | he indra yadyasmātkāraṇāt śāradīḥ saṃvatsarasambandhinīḥ saṃvatsaraparyantaṃ prākāraparikhādibhirdṛḍhīkṛtāḥ puraḥ śatrūṇāṃ purīravātiraḥ | anāśayaḥ | avapūrvastirnāśanārthaḥ ‖ kiṃ kurvan | sasahānaḥ sahateḥ kvasuḥ sasahānaḥ | abhibhavan dhanādyapahāreṇa pīḍayan sahaterlugantāttālelikṛṣṇāt [?] ‖ avātiraḥ | kiṃca he indra taṃ martyaṃ maraṇadharmāṇamayajyumayajvānaṃ yajñavighātinaṃ rākṣasādiṃ śāsaḥ | nigṛhītavānasi | he śavasaspate balasya pālakendra tvaṃ mahīṃ mahatīṃ pṛthivīmimā apaśca samudranadyātmakānyudakāni cāmuṣṇāḥ | balādapahṛtavānasi | asurairvā yajñavidveṣibhī rākrāntāṃ bhūmiṃ tatsambandhinīrapaśca teṣāṃ purāṇi bhittvāhṛtavānasītyarthaḥ | kiṃ duḥkhena | netyāha | mandasāno hṛṣyannevemā apa imānyupakāryāṇi vrīhyādyannānyamuṣṇāḥ | labdhavānasi ‖*

*(Read from the image; small type, a few places doubtful: [?] — notably the grammatical clause on *sasahānaḥ*. Sense: "O Indra, men (*pūravaḥ*), the sacrificers, who know your greatness and sacrifice to you alone, know (*viduḥ*) this heroism of yours, to be told: that you destroyed (*avātiraḥ*) the autumn (*śāradīḥ*) cities of the enemies, fortified for a year with ramparts and moats, overpowering (*sasahānaḥ*) them and afflicting them by seizing their wealth. And you punished (*śāsaḥ*) that mortal who is *ayajyu* — one who does not sacrifice, a spoiler of sacrifice, a Rākṣasa and the like. O lord of strength (*śavasaspate*), you carried off (*amuṣṇāḥ*) by force the great earth and these waters — the rivers and the sea — [seized by] the demons, hostile to the sacrifice, breaking their cities and recovering them: is it with sorrow? No: delighting (*mandasānaḥ*) you carried off these waters, the foods such as rice that benefit [men].")*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha** *(read from p. 485).* *(he) indra* — O Indra; *yat* — because; *śāradīḥ* — of years (strengthened for many years by ramparts and moats); *puraḥ* — the cities of the enemy; *ava atiraḥ* — you destroyed; *sasahānaḥ* — afflicting those who dwelt in those cities by seizing their wealth; *ava atiraḥ* — you destroyed; *(kiṃ ca* — and); *(he) indra* — O Indra; *tam* — that; *martyam* — mortal; *ayajyum* — who does not sacrifice (spoiler of the sacrifice); *śāsaḥ* — you punished; *(he) śavasaspate* — O Indra, protector of strength; *mahīm pṛthivīm* — the great earth; *imāḥ apaḥ* — these waters (of the sea, the rivers); *amuṣṇāḥ* — you took away by force; *mandasānaḥ* — delighting; *imāḥ apaḥ* — these waters, the means of rice and the like; *(amuṣṇāḥ* — you obtained); *tat* — therefore; *te* — your; *asya vīryasya* — this prowess (the deeds, the greatness of the deeds); *pūravaḥ* — men, the sacrificers; *viduḥ* — know.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, you destroyed for many years [the cities] of enemies, fortified by ramparts and moats; afflicting those dwelling in them by seizing their wealth, you destroyed them; you punished the mortals who are spoilers of sacrifice; O Indra, protector of the strong, you won back by force the great earth, taken by the demons, and the waters; delighting, you obtained these waters. The sacrificers know such greatness of your valorous deeds.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"The ancients have known of that your prowess, by which, Indra, you destroy the perennial cities (of the Asuras): you have destroyed them, humiliating (their defenders). You have chastised, Lord of Strength, the mortal who offers not sacrifice: You have rescued this spacious earth and these waters; exulting, (you have recovered) these waters."*

### Printed p. 486  (PDF 507)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 4).**

***pūravaḥ te asya vīryasya viduḥ*** — *manuṣyāḥ yajamānāḥ tava mahattvaṃ jānānāḥ tvām eva yajanti, yadvā asya vīryasya māhātmyaṃ viduḥ*: "the sacrificers, knowing Indra's greatness, offer oblations to him; or, those who sacrifice know well the greatness of Indra's prowess": two meanings are given. The word *pūravaḥ* is recorded among the names of man (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೮"). And —

> प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वृत्रहणं सचन्ते ।
> वैश्वानरो दस्युमग्निर्जघन्वाँ अधूनोत्काष्ठा अव शम्बरं भेत् ॥

> *pra nū mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya vocaṃ yaṃ pūravo vṛtrahaṇaṃ sacante |*
> *vaiśvānaro dasyum agnir jaghanvām̐ adhūnot kāṣṭhā ava śambaraṃ bhet ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-59-6, as read "೧-೫೯-೬".) In this Ṛk *pūravaḥ* is explained as *pūrayitavyāḥ*: "men are those fit to have their desires fulfilled".

***śāradīḥ*** — *saṃvatsarasambandhinīḥ*: "Indra, working so that even rival warriors cannot enter, destroys the walls and moats guarded by the enemies' cities that stand through the year": so the meaning.

***pṛthivīm imā apaḥ amuṣṇāḥ*** — *mahīṃ pṛthivīṃ samudranadyātmakāni udakāni ca balād apahṛtavān asi | asurair vā yajñavidveṣibhir ākrāntāṃ bhūmiṃ tatsambandhinīr apaś ca teṣāṃ purāṇi bhittvāhṛtavān*: "whether by *asuras* or by other enemies of the sacrifice who forcibly took the earth and the waters of the seas, Indra broke their cities and recovered them": thus Indra is described as having protected them.

***amuṣṇāḥ*** — the word is used twice. In the first meaning, Indra split the cities of the enemies and protected them. For the second *amuṣṇāḥ*, *udakasambandhikāryāṇi vrīhyādīni bhūmau belaydu annādigaḷu uṇṭāguvante kāryagaḷannu indranu līleyiṃdale ācarisiruvanu* — "Indra effortlessly brought about the conditions by which the grains such as rice grow on the earth, through the waters": so he explains.

### Printed p. 487  (PDF 508)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 21 [as read].)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *viduḥ* — root *vida jñāne*; *laṭ* third person plural, *jhi*; *vido laṭo vā* (Pā. 3-4-83) gives *jus* for *jhi*; since *j*-marked, no guṇa of the penult; since at the beginning of the *pāda* no *nighāta*; the acute on the last syllable by the suffix. *vīryasya* — *kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti* (Pā. 2-3-65) gives the genitive for the object. *viduṣ ṭe* — when *viduḥ te*, *yuṣmattatakṣuṣu* (Pā. 8-3-103) gives *ṣatva* of the visarga and so *ṣ*. *avātiraḥ* — *ava* a preposition; *tira* a root with the sense of destroying; *laṅ* second person singular; because *yad* is connected there is no *nighāta*; the augment *aṭ* being acute, the first syllable is acute; *tiṅ codāttavati* (Pā. 8-1-71) gives the preposition (*ava*) the unaccented tone. *sasahānaḥ* — root *saha marṣaṇe*; *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* gives *s*; *dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kvasur…* [as read: *chandasi liṭ*]; *liṭaḥ kānajvā* (Pā. 3-2-106) gives *kānac*; since *c*-marked [as read: *yajoc ca*]; the root is doubled; *dīrgho 'kitaḥ* (Pā. 7-4-83) lengthens the reduplicative; after the *yañluk*-ending [?] *tācchīlyavayovacanaśaktiṣu cānaś* (Pā. 3-2-129) gives *cānaś*; *citaḥ* gives the acute on the last syllable. *śāsaḥ* — root *śāsu anuśiṣṭau*; *laṅ* second person singular, *sip*; *itaś ca* drops *i*; *śap*'s *luk* is not applied by Vedic usage; the *s* of the suffix becomes *ru*, visarga; *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi* — no augment *aṭ*; at the beginning of the *pāda* no *nighāta*; *śap* unaccented so the root's accent remains. *ayajyum* — root *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu*; *yaji-mani-śundhi…* (Uṇ. 3-[?]) gives *yuc*; in the *tatpuruṣa*, *tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…* (Pā. 6-2-2) gives the accent of the first member (the indeclinable *a*). *śavasaspate* — *subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare* (Pā. 2-1-2) treats the genitive as part of the following; so the whole has the *āmantrita-nighāta*. *amuṣṇāḥ* — root *muṣa steye*, *kryādi*; *laṅ* second person singular, *sip*; *itaś ca* drops *i*; *kryādibhyaḥ śnā* (Pā. 3-1-81) gives *śnā*; *ṛṣābhyāṃ ṇo naḥ* [as read: *raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade*] gives *ṇ* for the *n*; the *s* becomes *ru*, visarga; the augment *aṭ*; because it follows a finite verb, *nighāta*.

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *āpaḥ* — accusative plural; *ūḍidaṃ padādi…* (Pā. 6-1-171) gives the acute to the ending. *mandasānaḥ* — root *madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu*; the suffix *āsānac* continued by *ṛñji-vṛdhi-mandi…* [as read: *ṛñji-vṛdhimandi-…*, Uṇ. 2-[?]]; *citaḥ* gives the acute on the last syllable. ‖ 4 ‖

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आदित्ते अस्य वीर्यस्य चर्किरन्मदेषु वृषन्नुशिजो यदाविथ ।
> सखीयतो यदाविथ ।
> चकर्थ कारमेभ्यः पृतनासु प्रवन्तवे ।
> ते अन्यामन्यां नद्यं सनिष्णत श्रवस्यन्तः सनिष्णत ॥ ५ ॥

> *āditte asya vīryasya carkiranmadeṣu vṛṣannuśijo yadāvitha |*
> *sakhīyato yadāvitha |*
> *cakartha kāramebhyaḥ pṛtanāsu pravantave |*
> *te anyāmanyāṃ nadyaṃ saniṣṇata śravasyantaḥ saniṣṇata ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आत् । इत् । ते । अस्य । वीर्यस्य । चर्किरन् । मदेषु । वृषन् । उशिजः । यत् । आविथ ।
> सखिऽयतः । यत् । आविथ ।
> चकर्थ । कारम् । एभ्यः । पृतनासु । प्रऽवन्तवे ।
> ते । अन्याम्ऽअन्याम् । नद्यम् । सनिष्णत । श्रवस्यन्तः । सनिष्णत ॥ ५ ॥

> *āt | it | te | asya | vīryasya | carkiran | madeṣu | vṛṣan | uśijaḥ | yat | āvitha |*
> *sakhi 'yataḥ | yat | āvitha |*
> *cakartha | kāram | ebhyaḥ | pṛtanāsu | pra 'vantave |*
> *te | anyām 'anyām | nadyam | saniṣṇata | śravasyantaḥ | saniṣṇata ‖ 5 ‖*

*(Read from the image: the Pada's last line prints "*te anyām-anyām*" as one compound; Saṃhitā "*cakartha kāram ebhyaḥ*".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image).*

> हे इन्द्र आदित्ते आदित्त एव ते वीर्यस्य तव सम्बन्धिने वीर्याय तवाभिवृद्धये चर्किरन् । पुनः पुनः सोमं विकिरन्ति । किरतेर्यङ्लुगन्ताल्लट्यभ्यासस्य रुगागमः ॥ सर्वेषु सवनेषु विकिरन्ति यजमानाः । आदित्युत्कृतं कुत इत्याह । मदेषु वृषन् सोमजनितमदेषु सत्सु हे कामानां वर्षितः उशिजस्त्वां कामयमानान्यजमानान् यद्यस्मात्कारणादाविथ रक्षसि । किंच सखीयतस्त्वं सखित्वमात्मन इच्छतोऽस्मान् यद्यस्मादाविथ तर्पयसि अभिमतेन प्रीणयसि । अत एव कारणादेभ्यो यजमानेभ्यः कारं शब्दं सिंहनादलक्षणं चकर्थ करोषि । पृतनासु सङ्ग्रामेषु । किमर्थम् । प्रवन्तवे प्रकर्षेण वनितुं सम्भक्तुं युद्धाय हि धीराः सम्भजन्ते । वनतेस्तुमर्थे तवेन्प्रत्ययः ॥ ताडा चेति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । किंच ते तव सङ्ग्रामवासिनस्त्वय्यासन्नाः अन्यामन्यां नद्यं नदीं सन्तोषं सम्बृद्धिं तुनदि सम्बृद्धौ [?] ॥ पूर्वरूपं बाधित्वा भावेसो यणादेशः ॥ सनिष्णत सम्भजन्ते । सनेर्लेटि सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् इट् । व्यत्ययेन पुनः श्नाप्रत्ययः । आत्मनेपदेष्वनत इत्यादेशे श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातो लोप इत्यकारलोपः ॥ छान्दसस्तेरेत्वाभावः ॥ तथा श्रवस्यन्तोऽन्नमिच्छन्तो जयालब्धमन्नं काङ्क्षन्तः सनिष्णत सम्भजन्ते ॥

> *he indra āditte āditta eva te vīryasya tava sambandhine vīryāya tavābhivṛddhaye carkiran | punaḥ punaḥ somaṃ vikiranti | kirateryaṅlugantāllaṭyabhyāsasya rugāgamaḥ ‖ sarveṣu savaneṣu vikiranti yajamānāḥ | ādityutkṛtaṃ kuta ityāha | madeṣu vṛṣan somajanitamadeṣu satsu he kāmānāṃ varṣitaḥ uśijastvāṃ kāmayamānānyajamānān yadyasmātkāraṇādāvitha rakṣasi | kiṃca sakhīyatastvaṃ sakhitvamātmana icchato 'smān yadyasmādāvitha tarpayasi abhimatena prīṇayasi | ata eva kāraṇādebhyo yajamānebhyaḥ kāraṃ śabdaṃ siṃhanādalakṣaṇaṃ cakartha karoṣi | pṛtanāsu saṅgrāmeṣu | kimartham | pravantave prakarṣeṇa vanituṃ sambhaktuṃ yuddhāya hi dhīrāḥ sambhajante | vanatestumarthe tavenpratyayaḥ ‖ tāḍā ceti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | kiṃca te tava saṅgrāmavāsinastvayyāsannāḥ anyāmanyāṃ nadyaṃ nadīṃ santoṣaṃ sambṛddhiṃ tunadi sambṛddhau [?] ‖ pūrvarūpaṃ bādhitvā bhāveso yaṇādeśaḥ ‖ saniṣṇata sambhajante | sanerleṭi sibbahulamiti sip iṭ | vyatyayena punaḥ śnāpratyayaḥ | ātmanepadeṣvanata ityādeśe śnābhyastayorāto lopa ityakāralopaḥ ‖ chāndasasteretvābhāvaḥ ‖ tathā śravasyanto 'nnamicchanto jayālabdhamannaṃ kāṅkṣantaḥ saniṣṇata sambhajante ‖*

*(Sense: "O Indra, thereafter (*ād it*) they strew (*cakiran*) Soma again and again in all the pressings for your vigour (*vīryasya*), i.e. for your increase. [*kir* in the intensive with *luk*: the reduplicative takes *ruk*.] When, *madeṣu*, in the exhilarations produced by Soma, O showerer of desires, you protect (*āvitha*) the *uśijaḥ* — sacrificers who desire you — and since you favour us who seek your friendship, satisfying us with what is wished: for that reason you utter (*cakartha kāram*) for them the lion-roar in battles (*pṛtanāsu*): for what? *pravantave* — to win, since the brave seek battle. And those who dwell in your battles, near you, obtain one enjoyment after another (*anyām-anyāṃ nadyam*, the Vedic sense 'satisfaction, growth'); *saniṣṇata* — they partake; and, desiring food, wishing for food won by victory, they partake.")*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he) indra* — O Indra; *(tvam* — you); *yat* — because; *madeṣu* — when exhilaration arises from Soma; *vṛṣan* — O showerer of desires; *uśijaḥ* — the sacrificers desiring you; *āvitha* — you protect; *(kiṃ ca* — and); *sakhīyataḥ* — us, desiring your friendship; *yat āvitha* — because you favour (and satisfy); *āt it* — therefore indeed; *te* — your; *asya vīryasya* — for this increase of valour; *cakiran* — they strew Soma again and again; *ebhyaḥ* — for them (the sacrificers); *pṛtanāsu* — in battles; *kāram* — the lion-roar; *pravantave* — to encourage; *cakartha* — you make; *(kiṃ ca* — and); *te* — your (worshippers); *anyām-anyām* — various, or successive; *nadyam* — satisfaction; *saniṣṇata* — obtain; *(tathā* — likewise); *śravasyantaḥ* — desiring food (won by victory); *saniṣṇata* — obtain (from you).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, satisfied with Soma, you protect the sacrificers who desire you and seek your friendship; therefore, to increase your valour, they pour out Soma again and again; in battles you make a lion's roar to encourage them; through you they obtain various kinds of satisfaction, and, desiring food, they obtain it from you.

### Printed p. 490  (PDF 511)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Thenceforth have your worshippers scattered (libations) for the augmentation of your vigour, that in your exhilaration, showerer (of benefits), you may defend those who are solicitous (of your favour); that you may defend those who are desirous of (your) friendship: for them you have uttered a shout to encourage them in combats; from you they obtain many and many an enjoyment; anxious for food, they obtain it (from you)."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 5).**

***te vīryasya cakiran*** — *tava sambandhine vīryāya tadabhivṛddhaye punaḥ punaḥ somaṃ vikiranti*: "the sacrificers pour out Soma in all the pressings, often, for the increase of Indra's strength, or so that his power may grow."

***uśijaḥ āvitha*** — *tvāṃ kāmayamānān yajamānān rakṣasi*: the word *uśij* is recorded among the eighteen names of "radiance-acts" beginning *vaṣṭi*, *uśnasi* (Ni. 3-[?]; as read "೩-೯") and among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-[?]; "೩-೧೯"). *Uśik* is formed from the root *vaś kāntau*, with the sense of desire; "Indra protects the sacrificers who have much desire to please him".

***āvitha*** — the word is used twice. For the first, "protect"; in the second meaning, "Indra gratifies the sacrificers who seek his friendship by satisfying them".

***pṛtanāsu pravantave kāraṃ cakartha*** — *saṅgrāmeṣu prakarṣeṇa sambhaktuṃ siṃhanādalakṣaṇaṃ śabdaṃ karoṣi*: the word *pṛtanā* is recorded among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"). "When fighting, Indra makes a lion-roar to defeat the enemies": so the meaning. Since the root *vana* with the prefix *pra* has the sense of begging, the meaning of the verb differs; so the wise (*dhīrāḥ*) always get ready for battle with enthusiasm: thus it is described.

### Printed p. 491  (PDF 512)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 21 [as read].)*

***anyām-anyāṃ nadyaṃ saniṣṇata*** — *tava saṅgrāmavāsinaḥ tvayi anyam-anyaṃ prati santoṣaṃ saṃvṛddhiṃ sambhajante*: "in battle the soldiers of Indra's army, wishing to gain superiority one over another, or to bring about each other's greater increase, work with enthusiasm": so the meaning. Here the word *anya* is, by Vedic usage, an adjective of the word *nadyam*; it is repeated. The Niruktakāra —

> न नूनमस्ति नो श्वः कस्तद्वेद यदद्भुतम् ।
> अन्यस्य चित्तमभि सञ्चरेण्यमुताधीतं वि नश्यति ॥

> *na nūnam asti no śvaḥ kas tad veda yad adbhutam |*
> *anyasya cittam abhi sañcareṇyam utādhītaṃ vi naśyati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-170-1, as read "೧-೧೭೦-೧".) — in this Ṛk explains the word *anyasya* as *nānāgatasya* (Ni. 4-[?]). Here Sāyaṇa explains *anyām-anyām* as *anyam anyaṃ prati*, "toward one another".

***śravasyantaḥ saniṣṇata*** — *annam icchanto jayālabdham annaṃ kāṅkṣanto sambhajante*: "the warriors of Indra desire food, or, having obtained victory, desire the food obtained by it from the enemies, and join Indra." The word *śravas* is recorded by the Niruktakāra among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯") and is used also in the sense "fame" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1-11-1; 6-[?]). —

> आसश्रासः शवसानमच्छेन्द्रं सुचक्रासो रथ्यासो अश्वाः ।
> अभि श्रव ऋज्यन्तो वहेयुर्नू चिन्नु वायोरमृतं वि दस्येत् ॥

> *āsaścāsaḥ śavasānam acchendraṃ sucakrāso rathyāso aśvāḥ |*
> *abhi śrava ṛjyanto vaheyur nū cin nu vāyor amṛtaṃ vi dasyet ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?], as read "೫-೬೨-೩" [?]; same Ṛk as on p. 353.) Here *śravaḥ* is explained, by *śravaḥ annanāma śrūyata iti sataḥ*, as "food". Since the word *śravas* has many senses — wealth, fame, food — Sāyaṇa explains the word *śravasyantaḥ* as "those desiring food": and, further, it is described that they enjoy the food obtained by conquering and subduing enemies.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *cakiran* — root *kṝ vikṣepe*; when the intensive sense is shown, *yaṅ*; after it, in the sense of an *aiśvarya* [as read], the *luk* of *yaṅ*; *kuhoś cuḥ* (Pā. 7-4-62) gives *c* in the reduplicative; the Vedic *laṭ*, third person plural, *jhi*; *ant* by the substitution *ant*; *i*-elision; by *vyatyaya* the *śa*-vikaraṇa; *pararūpa*; because it follows a finite verb, *nighāta*.

### Printed p. 492  (PDF 513)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

*(Grammar, continued.)* *vṛṣan* — root *vṛṣu secane*; *kanin yuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanidyuprākṣāṇām* [as read: *kanin yuvṛṣi…*, Uṇ. 1-[?]] gives *kanin*; *ṇaja sambuddhyoḥ* (Pā. 8-2-8) — no loss of *n* in the vocative; *āmantrita-nighāta*. *uśijaḥ* — root *vaś kāntau*; *vaśeḥ kit* (Uṇ. 2-[?]) gives *iji*; since *kit*, *saṃprasāraṇa*; acute on the first syllable of the suffix; accusative plural. *āvitha* — root *ava rakṣaṇe*; the Vedic *liṭ*, second person singular; since *yad* is connected, no *nighāta*; *thal*; because of *liti* (Pā. 6-1-193) the acute falls on the syllable before the suffix. *sakhīyataḥ* — *sakhāyam ātmana icchantaḥ*; *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. 3-1-8); the long vowel by Vedic usage; after the *kyac*-ending *śatṛ*; accusative plural; *śatur anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. 6-1-173) gives the acute to the ending. *cakartha* — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *liṭ* second person singular; at the beginning of the *pāda*, no *nighāta*; *liti* gives the acute before the suffix. *kāram* — the root as before; the suffix *ghañ* in the object sense; *aco ñṇiti* gives *vṛddhi*, with *raparatva*; *kṛṣāv…* [as read: *kharṣāt* …] gives the acute on the last syllable. *pravantave* — root *vana sambhaktau*; when the sense of *tumun* is shown, *tumarthe sesenase…* (Pā. 3-4-9) gives *tavenn*; *tāḍau ca niti* (Pā. 6-2-50) gives the prefix (*pra*) the acute; the form is an indeclinable. *anyām-anyām* — in reciprocity, *sarvanāmno dve vācye* (Pā. 8-1-12 [?]), by *samāsavac ca bahulam* the doubling in the sense of *kriyāvinimaya*; by the power of the *bahulagrahaṇa* the compound-like state does not occur, so *suṭ* and the like do not; the second member takes the name *āmreḍita*; *anudāttaṃ ca* (Pā. 8-1-3) makes it all unaccented. *nadyam* — root *ṭunadi samṛddhau*; Uṇādi *iya*; with *am* following, *ami pūrvaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-107) would give *pūrvarūpa*, which is set aside by Vedic *yaṇ*-substitution; *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ* (Pā. 8-2-4) gives the *svarita* to the ending.

### Printed p. 493  (PDF 514)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 21 [as read].)*

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *saniṣṇata* — root *paṇa sambhaktau* [as printed: the root is *ṣaṇa*]; *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* gives *s*; *leṭ* third person plural, *ru* [?]; *sibbahulaṃ leṭi* (Pā. 3-1-34) gives *sip*; *ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ* gives *iṭ*; by *vyatyaya* again *śnā* as the *vikaraṇa*; *ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ* (Pā. 7-1-5) gives *at* for the ending; since it is *j*-marked [as read], *śnābhyastayor ātaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-112) drops the *ā* of the *śnā*; Vedically the *ṭi* does not take *e*; *ādeśapratyayayoḥ* (Pā. 8-3-59) gives *ṣatva* of the *s* of the *sic*, and because of this the *n* of the *vikaraṇa* becomes *ṇ*; the form *saniṣṇata*; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *śravasyantaḥ* — *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* after *śravas*; *śatṛ* after the *kyac*-ending; the *kyac*'s accent remains. ‖ 5 ‖

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उतो नो अस्या उषसो जुषेत ह्यर्कस्य बोधि हविषो हवीमभिः ।
> स्वर्षाता हवीमभिः ।
> यदिन्द्र हन्तवे मृधो वृषा वज्रिञ्चिकेतसि ।
> आ मे अस्य वेधसो नवीयसो मन्म श्रुधि नवीयसः ॥ ६ ॥

> *uto no asyā uṣaso juṣeta hyarkasya bodhi haviṣo havīmabhiḥ |*
> *svarṣātā havīmabhiḥ |*
> *yadindra hantave mṛdho vṛṣā vajriñciketasi |*
> *ā me asya vedhaso navīyaso manma śrudhi navīyasaḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उतो इति । नः । अस्याः । उषसः । जुषेत । हि । अर्कस्य । बोधि । हविषः । हवीमऽभिः ।
> स्वःऽसाता । हवीमऽभिः ।
> यत् । इन्द्र । हन्तवे । मृधः । वृषा । वज्रिन् । चिकेतसि ।
> आ । मे । अस्य । वेधसः । नवीयसः । मन्म । श्रुधि । नवीयसः ॥ ६ ॥

> *uto iti | naḥ | asyāḥ | uṣasaḥ | juṣeta | hi | arkasya | bodhi | haviṣaḥ | havīma 'bhiḥ |*
> *svaḥ 'sātā | havīma 'bhiḥ |*
> *yat | indra | hantave | mṛdhaḥ | vṛṣā | vajrin | ciketasi |*
> *ā | me | asya | vedhasaḥ | navīyasaḥ | manma | śrudhi | navīyasaḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; small type, a few places doubtful: [?]).*

> अयमिन्द्रो नोऽस्माकं सम्बन्धिनीमस्या उषसः ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ विशामुषसं सुक्याः सम्बन्धिनीमुषःकालमुतो जुषेत । अपि नाम सेवेत । उपस्येसुवास्माकमयमिन्द्रो यज्ञं गच्छेदित्यर्थः ॥ हि पूरणार्थः । गत्वा चार्कस्य हविषः ॥ पूर्ववत्कर्मणि षष्ठी । अर्चनसाधनं हविर्हवीमभिर्हवनप्रकारविशेषैर्दत्तं हविरुतो बोधि । अपि नाम जानीहि । किंच स्पर्धाता स्वर्गस्यान्यस्य सुखविशेषस्य वा सम्भजनस्थाने यज्ञे हवीमभिराह्वानैराहूतो भवेति शेषः । अस्माभिराहूतः सन्नुपस्यैवागत्य हविः स्वीकरोतीत्यर्थः ॥ कस्मादिदमुच्यते । यद्यस्मात्कारणात् हे वज्रिन् वज्रयुक्तेन्द्र मृधो हिंसकाञ्छत्रून् हन्तवे हन्तुं वृषा वर्षिता सन् कामानां चिकेतसि अवबुध्यसे । कित ज्ञाने । जौहोत्यादिकः । लेट्यडागमः । नाभ्यस्तस्याचि पिति सार्वधातुके [?] इत्यत्र छन्दसि बहुलमिति वचनाल्लघूपधगुणप्रतिषेधाभावः । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ तस्माद्ब्रूमः । हे इन्द्र मे मम मन्म मननीयं स्तोत्रमा श्रुधि । सर्वतः शृणु । कीदृशस्य मे । वेधसो मेधाविनः नवीयसो नवतरस्य । दीक्षितसंस्कारैः संस्कृतत्वान्नवीयस्त्वं पुनर्विशेष्यते । नवीयसोऽतिशयेन नवनवतोत्साधारणस्तुतिमतः । अत्र यजमानविशेषणत्वेऽपि तत्कर्तृकं स्तोत्रमेव विशिष्टं भवति ॥

> *ayamindro no 'smākaṃ sambandhinīmasyā uṣasaḥ ‖ karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī ‖ viśāmuṣasaṃ sukyāḥ sambandhinīmuṣaḥkālamuto juṣeta | api nāma seveta | upasyesuvāsmākamayamindro yajñaṃ gacchedityarthaḥ ‖ hi pūraṇārthaḥ | gatvā cārkasya haviṣaḥ ‖ pūrvavatkarmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī | arcanasādhanaṃ havirhavīmabhirhavanaprakāraviśeṣairdattaṃ haviruto bodhi | api nāma jānīhi | kiṃca spardhātā svargasyānyasya sukhaviśeṣasya vā sambhajanasthāne yajñe havīmabhirāhvānairāhūto bhaveti śeṣaḥ | asmābhirāhūtaḥ sannupasyaivāgatya haviḥ svīkarotītyarthaḥ ‖ kasmādidamucyate | yadyasmātkāraṇāt he vajrin vajrayuktendra mṛdho hiṃsakāñchatrūn hantave hantuṃ vṛṣā varṣitā san kāmānāṃ ciketasi avabudhyase | kita jñāne | jauhotyādikaḥ | leṭyaḍāgamaḥ | nābhyastasyāci piti sārvadhātuke [?] ityatra chandasi bahulamiti vacanāllaghūpadhaguṇapratiṣedhābhāvaḥ | abhyastānāmādirityādyudāttatvam ‖ tasmādbrūmaḥ | he indra me mama manma mananīyaṃ stotramā śrudhi | sarvataḥ śṛṇu | kīdṛśasya me | vedhaso medhāvinaḥ navīyaso navatarasya | dīkṣitasaṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtatvānnavīyastvaṃ punarviśeṣyate | navīyaso 'tiśayena navanavatotsādhāraṇastutimataḥ | atra yajamānaviśeṣaṇatve 'pi tatkartṛkaṃ stotrameva viśiṣṭaṃ bhavati ‖*

*(Sense: "This Indra may enjoy (*juṣeta*) this dawn (*uṣasaḥ*) of ours — the time of dawn belonging to the *sūkta* — i.e. may come to our sacrifice early. [*hi* is a filler.] And having come, *bodhi* — know (accept) the oblation of the one who praises (*arkasya haviṣaḥ*), given with the particular kinds of invocations (*havīmabhiḥ*); and be called by invocations at the sacrifice, the place of enjoyment of heaven or other happiness (*svarsātā*): called by us, he comes early and accepts the oblation. Why this? Because, O thunderer, you are aware (*ciketasi*), as the showerer, of desires, for the slaying of the injuring enemies (*mṛdhaḥ*). Therefore we say: O Indra, hear (*śrudhi*) my praise (*manma*), the praise worthy of thought, of the new — consecrated by initiation — wise *vedhas*, of the extraordinary newest praiser.")*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(ayam) indraḥ* — this Indra; *naḥ* — our; *asyāḥ uṣasaḥ* — this dawn (the morning rite); *juṣeta hi* — may serve; *(he indra* — O Indra); *havīmabhiḥ* — by invocations of various kinds (given); *arkasya* — for worship; *haviṣaḥ* — the oblation; *bodhi* — know; *(kiṃ ca* — and); *svarṣātā* — at the sacrifice (a place of the enjoyment of heaven or happiness); *havīmabhiḥ* — by invocations; *(āhūtaḥ bhava* — be called); *yat* — because; *vajrin* — O wielder of the thunderbolt; *indra* — O Indra; *tvam* — you; *vṛṣā* — showerer of desires; *mṛdhaḥ* — enemies who harm; *hantave* — to slay; *cikētasi* — you are aware; *tat* — therefore; *vedhasaḥ* — of the wise; *navīyasaḥ* — made new by initiation and other rites (extraordinary in praise); *asya me* — this my; *manma* — praise; *ā śrudhi* — hear.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha** *(begins at the foot of p. 494).* Indra comes early in the morning to our rite. O Indra, accept the oblations of various kinds, offered for worship, and [come] to the heavenly

### Printed p. 495  (PDF 516)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 21 [as read].)*

*(Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 6, concluded from p. 494:)* "…heaven and the like, when you are called by the invocations at the sacrifice; O thunderer, showerer of desires: you know that the spoilers of the sacrifice are to be killed; therefore hear the praise of me, who am new (consecrated by rites), unique and highly distinguished in praise, wise."

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Will (Indra) be present at this our morning rite: be apprized, (Indra), of the oblation offered with (due) observances; offered with (due) observances for the sake of (obtaining) heaven: and since, wielder of the thunderbolt, showerer (of benefits), you know how to destroy the malevolent, therefore, listen to my acceptable (praise) intelligent, though a novice; (hear it from me) a novice."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 6).**

***asyāḥ uṣasaḥ uto juṣeta*** — *viśām uṣasaṃ sūktyāhaḥ sambandhinīm uṣaḥkālam api nāma sevetā*: "Indra is prayed to come and accept the oblations at dawn, on the day of the sacrifice (the *sūkta*-day) that the sacrificers perform."

***havīmabhiḥ*** — *havanaprakāraviśeṣaiḥ*: "the ways in which the *homa* of oblations, prepared for acceptance at the sacrifice, is performed in the fire, according to the order of the various injunctions".

***svarṣātā havīmabhiḥ*** — *svargasyānyasya sukhaviśeṣasya vā sambhajanasthāne yajñe āhvānair āhūto bhava*: "since the sacrifice gives heaven or another special happiness, Indra is called at it by the sacrificers and priests, and comes to accept the oblation at dawn."

***mṛdhaḥ hantave vṛṣā ciketasi*** — *śatrūn hantuṃ kāmānāṃ varṣitā avabudhyase*: "the sacrificers know that Indra destroys the enemies who harm and fulfils the wishes of the sacrificers."

***navīyasaḥ*** — the word is used twice. For the first, as an epithet *navīyasaḥ vedhasaḥ*, it is explained as "wise, consecrated by the rites that a person initiated (*dīkṣita*) must undergo".

### Printed p. 496  (PDF 517)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 131".)*

For the second *navīyasaḥ* he explains "one who offers extraordinary praise, such as no one else can utter", as an epithet of the sacrificer.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *uṣasaḥ* — the genitive is used for the object; likewise *arkasya haviṣaḥ*. *juṣeta* — root *juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*, *tudādi*; *liṅ* third person singular; *cādilope vibhāṣā* (Pā. 8-1-63) forbids *nighāta*, the *vikaraṇa*'s accent remains; so *madhyodātta*. *bodhi* — root *budha avagamane*; *loṭ* second person singular, *sip*, replaced by *hi*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *luk* of the *vikaraṇa*; *vā chandasi* (Pā. 3-4-88) gives *apit* when not [required]; since *j*-marked and not *p*-marked the guṇa of the penult occurs because of the suffix; *hurhaldher dhiḥ* (Pā. 6-4-101) gives *dhi* for *hi*; the final drops by Vedic usage; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *havīmabhiḥ* — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante* (Pā. 3-2-75) gives *manin* in the agent sense (where the independence of the instrument is intended); by Vedic usage the augment *iḍ*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pā. 6-1-34) gives *saṃprasāraṇa* of the root; *pūrvarūpa*; guṇa because of the suffix, *avādeśa*; *jñityādir nityam* gives the acute on the first syllable. *svarṣātā* — root *paṇa saṃbhaktau* [as printed; the root is *ṣaṇu*]; *ktin*; *janasanakhanāṃ sañjhalośh* (Pā. 6-4-42) gives *ā*; locative singular; *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. 7-1-39) gives *ḍā*. *hantave* — root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; when *tumun* sense is shown, *tumarthe sesenase…* (Pā. 3-4-9) gives *tavenn*; the acute on the first syllable since *n*-marked. *mṛdhaḥ* — root *mṛdhu undane*; *kvip ca* gives *kvip*; accusative plural. *ciketasi* — root *kita jñāne*, *juhotyādi*; *leṭ* second person singular, *sip*; *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* gives the augment *aṭ*; *ślau* doubles the root; *kuhoś cuḥ* (Pā. 7-4-62) gives *c* for the *k*;

### Printed p. 497  (PDF 518)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 21 [as read].)*

*(Grammar, concluded.)* …*nābhyastasyāci piti sārvadhātuke* (Pā. 7-3-87) — by the statement *bahulaṃ chandasi* the prohibition of guṇa of the light penult does not apply; *abhyastānām ādiḥ* (Pā. 6-1-189) gives the acute on the first syllable; because *yad* is connected, no *nighāta*. *navīyasaḥ* — when the sense of excess is shown, the suffix *īyasun*; *yasyeti ca* drops the *a*; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable; genitive singular. *manma* — root *mana jñāne*; Uṇādi *manin*; since *n*-marked the acute on the first syllable. *śrudhi* — root *śru śravaṇe*; *loṭ* second person singular, *sip*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *luk* of the *vikaraṇa*; *śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi* (Pā. 6-4-102) gives *dhi* for *hi*; since *apit*, no guṇa; *tiṅ-nighāta*. ‖ 6 ‖

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> वज्रेण शूर मर्त्यम् ।
> जहि यो नो अघायति शृणुष्व सुश्रवस्तमः ।
> रिष्टं न यामन्नप भूतु दुर्मतिर्विश्वाप भूतु दुर्मतिः ॥ ७ ॥

> *tvaṃ tamindra vāvṛdhāno asmayuramitrayantaṃ tuvijāta martyam |*
> *vajreṇa śūra martyam |*
> *jahi yo no aghāyati śṛṇuṣva suśravastamaḥ |*
> *riṣṭaṃ na yāmannapa bhūtu durmatirviśvāpa bhūtu durmatiḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> वज्रेण । शूर । मर्त्यम् ।
> जहि । यः । नः । अघऽयति । शृणुष्व । सुश्रवःऽतमः ।
> रिष्टम् । न । यामन् । अप । भूतु । दुःऽमतिः । विश्वा । अप । भूतु । दुःऽमतिः ॥ ७ ॥
