### Printed p. 530  (PDF 551)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 132".)*

> हे इन्द्रापर्वता । इन्द्रः प्रसिद्धः । पर्वतः पर्ववान्मेघः । तदभिमानिनौ देवौ । तौ युवं युवां पुरोयुधा सङ्ग्रामे पुरतो योद्धारौ नोऽस्माकं यः शत्रुः पृतन्यात् अस्मान् हन्तुं पृतनामात्मन इच्छति तं तमिद् सर्वमपि शत्रुमपहतम् । नाशयतम् । हन्तेर्लोट्यनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यनुनासिकलोपः ॥ केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । तं तस्मिन् सर्वमपि शत्रुं हन्तुं वज्रेण साधनेन प्राप्नुतम् । ईदृक् सामर्थ्यमस्तीति दर्शयति । यद्वोऽवज्रः । लिङ्गव्यत्ययः ॥ दूरे चत्तायोत्यन्तदूरदेशे गताय ॥ चतायतेर्वा नाशकर्मणः । निष्प्रायः । आदर्शनमापन्नायेत्यर्थः । ग्रसितस्कभितेत्यादौ निपातनादिडभावः ॥ ताद्दृशं शत्रुं छन्त्सत् छन्दयति कामयते हन्तुम् । छन्देः कान्तिकर्मण इदं रूपम् । किंच गहनं दुरवगाहं स्थानमतिकठिनं हृदयं शत्रुसमीपे वेनक्षत् व्याप्नोति । नक्ष गतौ । छान्दस इकारोपजनः । इनक्षतीर्वा प्रकृत्यन्तरम् ॥ इदानीमिन्द्र एव स्तूयते । हे शूर शौर्योपेतेन्द्र अस्माकं विरोधिनः शत्रून् विश्वतो विश्वान् । सार्वविभक्तिकस्तसिल् ॥ परि परितो विश्वतो विश्वरूपायैर्दर्षीष्ट । दारयसि । किंच दर्मा शत्रूणां दारकः । दारयतेर्मेन्भ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति मनिन् । णिलोप उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण मनिन उदात्तत्वम् ॥ दृ भये । घटादित्वान्मितां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वत्वम् ॥ कव पूर्वोक्तो वज्रो विश्वतः सर्वान्शत्रून् सर्वरूपायैर्वा दर्षीष्ट । दारयति । यद्वा । दर्मा शत्रूणां दारक इन्द्रो दर्षीष्ट । काष्ठ्स्नर्येन दारयति शत्रून् ॥

> *he indrāparvatā | indraḥ prasiddhaḥ | parvataḥ parvavānmeghaḥ | tadabhimāninau devau | tau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ puroyudhā saṅgrāme purato yoddhārau no 'smākaṃ yaḥ śatruḥ pṛtanyāt asmān hantuṃ pṛtanāmātmana icchati taṃ tamid sarvamapi śatrumapahatam | nāśayatam | hanterloṭyanudāttopadeśetyanunāsikalopaḥ ‖ kena sādhaneneti taducyate | taṃ tasmin sarvamapi śatruṃ hantuṃ vajreṇa sādhanena prāpnutam | īdṛk sāmarthyamastīti darśayati | yadvo 'vajraḥ | liṅgavyatyayaḥ ‖ dūre cattāyotyantadūradeśe gatāya ‖ catāyatervā nāśakarmaṇaḥ | niṣprāyaḥ | ādarśanamāpannāyetyarthaḥ | grasitaskabhitetyādau nipātanādiḍabhāvaḥ ‖ tāddṛśaṃ śatruṃ chantsat chandayati kāmayate hantum | chandeḥ kāntikarmaṇa idaṃ rūpam | kiṃca gahanaṃ duravagāhaṃ sthānamatikaṭhinaṃ hṛdayaṃ śatrusamīpe venakṣat vyāpnoti | nakṣa gatau | chāndasa ikāropajanaḥ | inakṣatīrvā prakṛtyantaram ‖ idānīmindra eva stūyate | he śūra śauryopetendra asmākaṃ virodhinaḥ śatrūn viśvato viśvān | sārvavibhaktikastasil ‖ pari parito viśvato viśvarūpāyairdarṣīṣṭa | dārayasi | kiṃca darmā śatrūṇāṃ dārakaḥ | dārayatermenbhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti manin | ṇilopa udāttanivṛttisvareṇa manina udāttatvam ‖ dṛ bhaye | ghaṭāditvānmitāṃ hrasva iti hrasvatvam ‖ kava pūrvokto vajro viśvataḥ sarvānśatrūn sarvarūpāyairvā darṣīṣṭa | dārayati | yadvā | darmā śatrūṇāṃ dāraka indro darṣīṣṭa | kāṣṭhsnaryena dārayati śatrūn ‖*

*(Sense: "O Indra and Parvata — Indra the well-known; Parvata, the *parvavat* cloud — the deities presiding over them: you two, *purojudhā* — fighting in front in battle — whichever enemy of ours (*yaḥ pṛtanyāt*) wishes an army against us in order to kill us — destroy (*apa hatam*) each and every such enemy. With what? With the thunderbolt (*vajreṇa*) obtain [him] to kill every enemy; so it shows that such power exists. The enemy gone very far (*dūre cattāya*) [*cata* in the sense 'destroyed', 'out of sight'], or one who wishes to kill (*chantsat*, from *chand*, 'to desire'); the difficult, impenetrable place (*gahanam*), the very hard heart near the enemy, [the thunderbolt] pervades (*inakṣat*). Now Indra alone is praised: O hero Indra, our enemies on all sides (*viśvataḥ*) you tear apart (*dardṛṣṭa*); and *darmā* — the tearer of enemies; or the thunderbolt, mentioned before, tears all enemies completely.")*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he) indrāparvatā* — O Indra and clouds (O Indra and the deity of the clouds); *yuvam* — you two; *puroyudhā* — fighting in front in battle; *naḥ* — our; *yaḥ* — which enemy; *pṛtanyāt* — desires an army to kill us; *tam tam it* — every such enemy; *apa hatam* — destroy; *yat* — which; *dūre* — far away; *cattāya* — gone (out of sight); *tam* — such an enemy; *chantsat* — desires to kill (and); *gahanam* — a very difficult place (the very hard-hearted enemy); *inakṣat* — pervades; *vajreṇa* — with the thunderbolt; *tam tam it hatam* — kill every such one; *he śūra* — O brave Indra; *asmākam* — our; *viśvataḥ* — all; *śatrūn* — enemies; *pari* — completely; *viśvataḥ* — by all means; *dardṛṣṭa* — you tear; *darmā* — the thunderbolt, destroyer of enemies [of Indra]; *(śatrūn* — enemies); *viśvataḥ* — completely; *dardṛṣṭa* — tears apart.

### Printed p. 531  (PDF 552)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 22 [as read].)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra and Parvata (the cloud), you who are in front in all battles: kill all those who wish to fight us; to destroy the enemies, with the thunderbolt that pursues them however far, in whatever dense place, and kills them; O brave Indra, destroy completely our enemies by all means; and may the thunderbolt, the tearer of enemies, kill them.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Indra and Parvata, who are foremost in battles, slay every one who is arrayed against us; slay every such (adversary) with the thunderbolt — (the shaft that) bent upon his destruction pursues him, however far, or to whatever hiding-place he may have fled. You, hero, (tear) our enemies entirely to pieces; the tearer (of foes, the thunderbolt), rends them entirely asunder."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 6).**

***indrāparvatā*** — by this word Indra and the cloud (or the deity presiding over the cloud) are addressed. This word is found in the Ṛgveda only in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-132-6; 1-[?]-[?]; 3-[?]-[?]; and nowhere else. In explaining Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-132-6, the commentator explains this word: *indrāparvatā — indraḥ prasiddhaḥ, parvataḥ parvavān vṛṣṭyādipūraṇavān parjanyaḥ* — "Indra, the well known; *parvata*, the one who has parts, *parvavān* — Parjanya, the deity who fills the earth with rain and the like". In the present Ṛk: *parvataḥ parvavān meghaḥ* — "the cloud with its parts". Yāska, in his Nirukta: *parvavān parvataḥ | parva pṛṇāteḥ prīṇāteḥ vā* (Ni. 1-[?]; as read "೧-೨೦"): "*parvata* means 'having joints'; *parva* is from *pṛ* 'to fill' or *prī* 'to please'": the name *parvata* (mountain) is given because (stones) lie in heaps, or because it covers the earth and fills it, or because it pleases people; *parvataṃ meghaṃ* — a cloud (Ni. 1-[?] and 10-[?]; as read "೧-೩೧", "೧೦-೧೦"); *parvatānāṃ meghānām* (Ni. 11-[?]; as read "೧೧-೧೭"): the word *parvata* is thus explained as "cloud". —

> बळित्था पर्वतानां खिद्रं बिभर्षि पृथिवि ।
> प्र या भूमिं प्रवत्वति महना जिनोषि महिनि ॥

> *baḷitthā parvatānāṃ khidraṃ bibharṣi pṛthivi |*
> *pra yā bhūmiṃ pravatvati mahnā jinoṣi mahini ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-84-1; Tai. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?], as read "೫-೮೪-೧", "೩-೨-೧೧-೨" [?].) and others are given as illustrations.

### Printed p. 532  (PDF 553)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 132".)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 6, continued from p. 531:)*

***puroyudhā*** — *saṅgrāme puratao yoddhārau*: "those who fight in front of all in battle", is the meaning.

***pṛtanyāt*** — *raṇaḥ vivāk* [as read] and the like are the forty names of battle in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-[?]; as read "೨-೯"); since the word *pṛtanā* is recorded among them, *pṛtanā* means "war"; *pṛtanām ātmana icchatīti pṛtanyati* — "one who desires war against us": the enemy who wishes to fight us. "Destroy such enemies": so he is prayed.

***taṃ-tam it vajreṇa hatam*** — "whichever enemy wishes to kill us in battle, kill him, every one, with the thunderbolt."

***cattāya*** — *gatāya | cātayater vā nāśakarmaṇaḥ | niṣprāyaḥ | adarśanam āpannāyety arthaḥ*: "to the enemy who has hidden himself in a hiding place, so as to be invisible to the eye": Indra is prayed to destroy such an enemy.

***asmākaṃ śatrūn pari śūra viśvataḥ darmā dardṛṣṭa viśvataḥ*** — "O Indra, the hero, the destroyer of enemies: kill our enemies everywhere by all means" — so the immeasurable power of Indra is described.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *indrāparvatā* — *indraś ca parvataś ca indrāparvatau*, *devatādvandve ca* (Pā. 6-3-26) gives *ānaṅ* to the first member; *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. 7-1-39) gives *ā* in place of the dual ending; *āmantritasya ca* gives *nighāta*. *puroyudhā* — root *yudha saṃprahāre*; *kvip ca* gives *kvip*; *kṛd-uttarapadaprakṛtisvara*; as before, a dual-ending change to *ā*. *pṛtanyāt* — *pṛtanām ātmana icchati pṛtanyati*; *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. 3-1-8); *kavyadhvaropapṛtanasya…* [as read: *lopaḥ kyaci*, Pā. 7-4-39] drops the *a*; after the *kyac*-ending, *liṅ* third person singular [as read: *laṭ*]; hence the form; because *yad* is connected no *nighāta*; *yāsuṭ* is acute so the *ā* is acute; *chandasy ubhayathā* (Pā. 3-4-117) makes the suffix *ārdhadhātuka*-named so *kyac* drops. *taṃ-tam* — by *nityavīpsayoḥ* (Pā. 8-1-4) doubling; since the second has the name *āmreḍita*, *anudāttaṃ ca* (Pā. 8-1-3) makes it unaccented.

### Printed p. 533  (PDF 554)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 22 [as read].)*

*(Grammar, continued.)* *hatam* — root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *loṭ* second person dual, *tam* [replaced]; since *t*-marked [as read: *ṅit*], *anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām…* (Pā. 6-4-37) drops the nasal; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *cattāya* — root *cate yācane* [as read]; here used in the sense of destroying; by *grasitaskabhita…* (Pā. 7-2-34) the suffix *kta* is irregularly formed (without *iṭ*); acute on the last syllable by the suffix; dative singular. *chantsat* — root *chadi kāntau*; *leṭ* third person singular, *tip*; *itaś ca lopaḥ* (Pā. 3-4-97) drops *i*; *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* gives the augment *aṭ*; by Vedic usage *luk* of the *vikaraṇa*; *sibbahulaṃ leṭi* (Pā. 3-1-34) gives *sip*; because *it*-marked the root gets *num*; *khari ca* gives *car* for the *d*; *tiṅ-nighāta*. *inakṣat* — root *nakṣa gatau*; as before, *leṭ* third person singular; the prefix *i* comes in as an augment by Vedic usage; or the root *inakṣa*, as one infers, in the *bhvādi* [list], is established as *ākṛtigaṇa*; because *yad* is connected no *nighāta*; the first syllable acute by *vyatyaya*. *viśvataḥ* — in the sense of the second case, the suffix *tasil*; *liti* gives the acute before the suffix. *darmā* — root *dṝ vidāraṇe*; when *ṇic* follows, *aco ñṇiti* gives *vṛddhi*, giving the form *dār*; *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante* (Pā. 3-2-75) gives *manin* after the *ṇic*-ending; *ner aniṭi* (Pā. 6-4-51) drops *ṇic*; since *manin* is *n*-marked [as read: *nit* / unaccented] and follows, the loss of *ṇic* — the accent rule *anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-161) gives the acute to *manin*; by Vedic usage the root is shortened. Or the root *dṝ bhaye*; since it is read in the *ghaṭādi* group, *mitāṃ hrasvaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-92) shortens the penult when *ṇic* follows; nominative singular.

### Printed p. 534  (PDF 555)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 133" [as read: "೧೩೩"].)*

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *dardṛṣṭa* — root *dṝ vidāraṇe*; after the *ṇic*-ending *liṅ* third person singular, *ta*; *liṅaḥ sīyuṭ* (Pā. 3-4-102) gives *sīyuṭ*; *suṭ tithoḥ* (Pā. 3-4-107) gives *suṭ*; *chandasy ubhayathā* (Pā. 3-4-117) gives the suffix both names, so *ṇic* drops; as before the penult is shortened; *tiṅ-nighāta*. ‖ 6 ‖

Here ends the 132nd Sūkta. *(Kannada closing line: "ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತೆರಡನೇ ಸೂಕ್ತ ಮುಗಿದುದು".)*

## Sūkta 133 — *ubhe punāmi* (begins on printed p. 534; Anuvāka 19, seventh and last Sūkta)

### Printed p. 534 (continued; PDF 555, lower part)

**ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತಮೂರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra mūvattamūraneya sūktavu** (the one hundred and thirty-third Sūkta).

**॥ सूक्तभूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, small type; read from the image; several letters doubtful [?]).**

> उभे पुनामीति सप्तर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं पारुच्छेपमैन्द्रम् । आद्या त्रिष्टुप् । अभिल्गेत्याद्यास्तिस्रोऽनुष्टुभः । पिशङ्गभृष्टिमिति षष्ठी गायत्री । अन्वर्महेत्येषा धृतिः । वनोति हीत्यभिधानात्कृत्यः [?] । अत्राह्नुक्रमणिका । उभे सप्तादौ त्रिष्टुप् तिस्रोऽनुष्टुभो गायत्री धृतिरिति ॥ अस्य सूक्तस्य विनियोगमाह शौनकः । उभे पुनामि पुरा रिपुघ्न्यस्तु प्रकीर्तिताः । ता जपन् प्रयतो नित्यमिष्ठान् कामान् समश्नुते । ता जपन् हन्ति रक्षांसि सपत्नांश्च नियच्छति । ऋ. वि. १-३१ [?] इति ॥

> *ubhe punāmīti saptarcaṃ saptamaṃ sūktaṃ pārucchepamaindram | ādyā triṣṭup | abhilgetyādyāstisro 'nuṣṭubhaḥ | piśaṅgabhṛṣṭimiti ṣaṣṭhī gāyatrī | anvarmahetyeṣā dhṛtiḥ | vanoti hītyabhidhānātkṛtyaḥ [?] | atrāhnukramaṇikā | ubhe saptādau triṣṭup tisro 'nuṣṭubho gāyatrī dhṛtiriti ‖ asya sūktasya viniyogamāha śaunakaḥ | ubhe punāmi purā ripughnyastu prakīrtitāḥ | tā japan prayato nityamiṣṭhān kāmān samaśnute | tā japan hanti rakṣāṃsi sapatnāṃśca niyacchati | ṛ. vi. 1-31 [?] iti ‖*

**Kannada anuvāda (translated).** *Anuvāda* — This Sūkta *ubhe punāmi* is the seventh Sūkta in the nineteenth Anuvāka. It has seven ṛks. The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Paruccheṣa; the deity is Indra. The first ṛk of this Sūkta is in the Triṣṭubh metre; the three ṛks beginning *abhilgā* [as read: *abhi-lgya*…] are Anuṣṭubh; the ṛk *piśaṅgabhṛṣṭim* is Gāyatrī; the ṛk *anarmaha* is Dhṛti; and the ṛk *vanoti hi* is Atyaṣṭi [as read: "Atyaṣṭi" here and earlier given "Dhṛti"; the Kannada text prints these as given]. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "*ubhe sapta ādau triṣṭup tisro 'nuṣṭubho gāyatrī dhṛtiḥ*". Śaunaka states the use of this Sūkta as follows: "*ubhe punāmi purā ripughnyas tu prakīrtitāḥ | tā japan prayato nityam iṣṭān kāmān samaśnute | tā japan hanti rakṣāṃsi sapatnāṃś ca niyacchati*" (Ṛgvidhāna 1-[?], as read "೧-೩೨" [?]). *Ubhe punāmi* is a Sūkta that destroys enemies: it is said that, if one recites its mantras with faith and regularly every day, enemies are destroyed and all desires are fulfilled.

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

**ಸೂಕ್ತ — Sūkta 133** [as read]. Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 19; Sūkta 133. Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read]. Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 7. Ṛṣi — Paruccheṣa Daivodāsi. Devatā — Indra. Chandas — [as printed] 1 Triṣṭubh; 2–4 Anuṣṭubh; 5 Gāyatrī; 6 Dhṛti; 7 Atyaṣṭi. *(The printed table gives Ṛk 5 Gāyatrī, 6 Dhṛti, 7 Atyaṣṭi, whereas the Sanskrit introduction on p. 534 as I read it has the Gāyatrī at 6; recorded as printed.)*

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उभे पुनामि रोदसी ऋतेन द्रुहो दहामि सं महीरनिन्द्राः ।
> अभिव्लग्य यत्र हता अमित्रा वैलस्थानं परि तृळ्हा अशेरन् ॥ १ ॥

> *ubhe punāmi rodasī ṛtena druho dahāmi saṃ mahīranindrāḥ |*
> *abhivlagya yatra hatā amitrā vailasthānaṃ pari tṛḷhā aśeran ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उभे इति । पुनामि । रोदसी इति । ऋतेन । द्रुहः । दहामि । सम् । महीः । अनिन्द्राः ।
> अभिऽव्लग्य । यत्र । हताः । अमित्राः । वैलस्थानम् । परि । तृळ्हाः । अशेरन् ॥ १ ॥

> *ubhe iti | punāmi | rodasī iti | ṛtena | druhaḥ | dahāmi | sam | mahīḥ | anindrāḥ |*
> *abhi 'vlagya | yatra | hatāḥ | amitrāḥ | vailasthānam | pari | tṛḷhāḥ | aśeran ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; begins p. 535.)*

> हे इन्द्र ऋतेन त्वदुद्देश्येन यज्ञेन बलेनोभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ पुनामि । लोकद्वयं हिंसकानां तवायज्ञ्यानां [?] पापागमनेन पावयामि । किंचित् भूलोकेऽनिन्द्रा इन्द्रविरहितानामाश्रयभूता महीः उर्वीः अत एव द्रुहो द्रोहिणामाधारभूतत्वात्तल्लक्षणा द्रोग्ध्रीः सं दहामि । संभूयैकहेलया दहामि । पुनस्ता एव विशेष्यन्ते । यत्र यासु भूमिष्वमित्राः शत्रवोऽभिव्लग्याभितो गत्वा हताः सर्वतः प्राप्ता अस्माभिर्घातिता वा । व्लगतिर्गतिकर्मा । छान्दसो धातुः । ते सर्वे परि तृळ्हा हिंसिताः ॥ तृहू हिंसार्थः । ऊदित्त्वादस्य विभाषेट्प्रतिषेधः । हिंसिताः संतोऽशेरन् । शयनं प्राप्ताः । शेतेर्व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं ।

> *he indra ṛtena tvaduddeśyena yajñena balenobhe rodasī dyāvāpṛthivyau punāmi | lokadvayaṃ hiṃsakānāṃ tavāyajñyānāṃ [?] pāpāgamanena pāvayāmi | kiṃcit bhūloke 'nindrā indravirahitānāmāśrayabhūtā mahīḥ urvīḥ ata eva druho drohiṇāmādhārabhūtatvāttallakṣaṇā drogdhrīḥ saṃ dahāmi | saṃbhūyaikahelayā dahāmi | punastā eva viśeṣyante | yatra yāsu bhūmiṣvamitrāḥ śatravo 'bhivlagyābhito gatvā hatāḥ sarvataḥ prāptā asmābhirghātitā vā | vlagatirgatikarmā | chāndaso dhātuḥ | te sarve pari tṛḷhā hiṃsitāḥ ‖ tṛhū hiṃsārthaḥ | ūdittvādasya vibhāṣeṭpratiṣedhaḥ | hiṃsitāḥ saṃto 'śeran | śayanaṃ prāptāḥ | śetervyatyayena parasmaipadaṃ |*

*(Sense, with doubtful words as read: "O Indra, by the sacrifice (*ṛta*, i.e. force) aimed at you I purify both heaven and earth; I cleanse the two worlds of the misfortune that comes from the wicked [?]. Those wide lands that lack Indra (*anindrāḥ*) and are the support of the malicious, I burn up together. The lands are further described: in which the enemies, having gone about on every side, were slain — reached on all sides by us or struck by us (*vlagati* is a verb of motion, a Vedic root); all these, utterly (*pari*) crushed, lie asleep (*aśeran*)." Grammar: *tṛhū hiṃsāyām*; because of the *ū*-marker the *iṭ* is optionally forbidden; *śete* has the Parasmaipada by *vyatyaya*.)*

### Printed p. 536  (PDF 557)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 133" [as read].)*

> शीङो रुट् । पा. [?] । शीङः सार्वधातुके गुणः ॥ वैलस्थानं । बिलशब्दो गर्तसमानार्थः । स च गर्तः श्मशानवचनः । आकोऽयमपि श्मशानवाची । अथवा बिलसंबन्धिस्थानं नागलोकः । तत्र वाशेरन् । यद्वा बिल क्षेपे इति धातुः । घञर्थे कः । स्वार्थिकोऽयन् । तत्र शवाः क्षिप्यन्ते इति वैलस्थानं श्मशानं । तत्र त्वयोहता भूमिं श्मशानवत्कृत्वा सर्वत्र शेरते । तान् दहामीत्यर्थः ॥

> *śīṅo ruṭ | pā. [?] | śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ ‖ vailasthānaṃ | bilaśabdo gartasamānārthaḥ | sa ca gartaḥ śmaśānavacanaḥ | āko 'yamapi śmaśānavācī | athavā bilasaṃbandhisthānaṃ nāgalokaḥ | tatra vāśeran | yadvā bila kṣepe iti dhātuḥ | ghañarthe kaḥ | svārthiko 'yan | tatra śavāḥ kṣipyante iti vailasthānaṃ śmaśānaṃ | tatra tvayohatā bhūmiṃ śmaśānavatkṛtvā sarvatra śerate | tān dahāmītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Grammar tail of *aśeran*: *śīṅo ruṭ* (Pā. [?], number not legible to me), *śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ*. Then on *vailasthānam*: "The word *bila* means the same as *garta* (pit); and *garta* is a word for a cemetery; the word *āka* also means cemetery. Or: the place connected with a *bila* is the Nāga-world (serpent world); either of these may be meant by 'they lay there'. Or the root is *bila kṣepe*; *ka* in the sense of *ghañ*, with the selfsame suffix *ayan*; where corpses are thrown is *vailasthāna*, a cemetery. There, those struck by you, making the earth like a cemetery, lie everywhere; these I burn — this is the meaning." The wording of the second half is partly doubtful [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he) indre* — O Indra; *ṛtena* — by the sacrifice aimed at you (by strength); *ubhe rodasī* — both the heaven and earth; *punāmi* — (leaving aside the evil) I purify; *kiṃcit bhūloke* — and in the earth-world; *anindrāḥ* — those without Indra, supporting; *mahīḥ* — wide; *druhaḥ* — (being the support of the malicious) of the malicious, (the lands of the earth); *saṃ dahāmi* — I burn them completely; *yatra* — in whichever lands; *amitrāḥ* — enemies; *abhivlagya* — having gone everywhere; *hatāḥ* — spread over, (or struck by us); *(tatra)* — there; *(te)* — they; *pari tṛḷhāḥ* — completely destroyed; *vailasthāne* — in pits (in cemeteries, or in the Nāga-world); *aśeran* — lie fallen.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, by the sacrifice (by the strength) directed to you I purify both heaven and earth; I burn up the wide lands (portions of the earth) that, lacking Indra, are the very support of the malicious, as the malicious themselves; and in whichever lands enemies are spread and are struck down by us, there they are utterly destroyed and lie in pits (in cemeteries); I make such lands pure also.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"By sacrifice I purify both the heaven and the earth: I burn the wide (realms of earth) that are without Indra, and are (the haunts) of the wicked: wherever the enemies have congregated they have been slain: and, utterly destroyed, they sleep in a deep pit"* (the printed text has a colon after "earth", "wicked" and "slain", no closing full stop).

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 1).**

***ubhe rodasī*** — *rodasī* is one of the twenty-four names of *dyāvāpṛthivī* (Ni. 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೦" [?]), since the word, beginning with *purandhī*, occurs among them; *rodasī* means "the two": heaven and earth, which are in the middle (*patita*). Here, as *rodasī* is a dual-ending word, it indicates two worlds, heaven and earth; the word *ubhe* is thus not necessary [text continues on p. 537].

### Printed p. 537  (PDF 558)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

*(Continuing:)* …the word *ubhe* is superfluous. It has been put in to suit the metre. Yāska, in his Nirukta, explains the word *rodasī* not only as *dyāvāpṛthivī* but also as "*rodasī rudrasya patnī*" — "*rodasī* is the wife of Rudra" (Ni. 11-[?], as read "೧೧-೩೦" [?]); and in support of this meaning he quotes:

> उत ग्ना व्यन्तु देवपत्नीरिन्द्राण्यग्नाय्यश्विनी राट् ।
> आ रोदसी वरुणानी शृणोतु व्यन्तु देवीर्य ऋतुर्जनीनाम् ॥

> *uta gnā vyantu devapatnīrindrāṇyagnāyyaśvinī rāṭ |*
> *ā rodasī varuṇānī śṛṇotu vyantu devīrya ṛturjanīnām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-46-8 [as read; the digits are doubtful].) — as an illustration (Ni. 12-[?], as read "೧೨-೪೬" [?]). In this Ṛk, when naming some of the divine wives, [Yāska says]:

> अपि च ग्ना व्यन्तु देवपत्न्यः । इन्द्राणीन्द्रस्य पत्न्यग्नाय्यग्नेः पत्न्यश्विन्यश्विनोः पत्नी राट् राजते । रोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नी । वरुणानी च वरुणस्य पत्नी ।

> *api ca gnā vyantu devapatnyaḥ | indrāṇīndrasya patnyagnāyyagneḥ patnyaśvinyaśvinoḥ patnī rāṭ rājate | rodasī rudrasya patnī | varuṇānī ca varuṇasya patnī |*

(Ni. 12-[?], as read "೧೨-೪೬" [?].) — that is: the wife of Indra is *indrāṇī*; of Agni, *agnāyī*; of the Aśvins, *aśvinī*; of Rudra, *rodasī*; of Varuṇa, *varuṇānī*, so he explains. In the present Ṛk, *rodasī* means heaven and earth.

***ṛtena*** — the word *ṛta* has many senses (truth, water, etc.), but in the present Ṛk the commentator explains: *yajñena balena* — by the sacrificial act, or by the divine power obtained by performing sacrifice.

***druhaḥ*** — *drohiṇām ādhārabhūtatvāt tadāśrayam api drogdhrīḥ* — "druh" means those that do harm, the wicked; the places that are the support of such wicked, where wicked people dwell, is the meaning. Since the word *anindrāḥ* ("without Indra") is used here as an attribute of this word, the lands without Indra are the dwelling-places of the wicked; the ṛṣi says that, burning such lands, he destroys them.

***abhivlagya yatra hatā amitrāḥ*** — "those who are not friends to us" means enemies, the wicked; in whichever land the wicked assemble, in those lands the wicked are all destroyed.

***ubhe punāmi rodasī*** — As said above, having burned the lands where the wicked who do not worship Indra dwell, and having destroyed their evil, I make heaven and earth pure [text continues on p. 538] — free of the harm done by the wicked.

### Printed p. 538  (PDF 559)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 133" [as read].)*

*(Continuing:)* …I purify, or make clean — this is the purport: to remove the harm done by wicked men is to make [the worlds] pure.

***vailasthānaṃ pari tṛḷhā aśeran*** — "Our enemies, the wicked who do not worship Indra, struck down by us, lie in a *bila*-place, i.e. in a cemetery", is the meaning. Sāyaṇa gives two kinds of meaning for the word *vailasthāna*:

> वैलस्थानं बिलशब्दो गर्तसमानार्थः । स च गर्तः श्मशानवचनः । आकोऽयमपि श्मशानवाची । अथवा बिलसंबन्धिस्थानं नागलोकः । तत्र वाशेरन् । यद्वा बिल क्षेपे इति धातुः । घञर्थे कः । स्वार्थिकोऽयन् । तत्र शवाः क्षिप्यन्ते इति वैलस्थानं श्मशानं । तत्र त्वयोहता भूमिं श्मशानवत्कृत्वा सर्वत्र शेरते । तान् दहामीत्यर्थः ॥

> *vailasthānaṃ bilaśabdo gartasamānārthaḥ | sa ca gartaḥ śmaśānavacanaḥ | āko 'yamapi śmaśānavācī | athavā bilasaṃbandhisthānaṃ nāgalokaḥ | tatra vāśeran | yadvā bila kṣepe iti dhātuḥ | ghañarthe kaḥ | svārthiko 'yan | tatra śavāḥ kṣipyante iti vailasthānaṃ śmaśānaṃ | tatra tvayohatā bhūmiṃ śmaśānavatkṛtvā sarvatra śerate | tān dahāmītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Quoted as on p. 536; the printed text is identical, with *vailasthānam* run into the preceding line.)*

The word *bila* has the meaning of *garta* ("pit"). Though *garta* has the sense of "house" (Ni. 3-[?]), here the commentator gives the meaning "cemetery". Yāska: "*śmaśānasaṃco 'pi garta ucyate | gurater apagūrṇo bhavati | śmaśānaṃ śmayanam*" (Ni. 3-[?], as read "೩-೨೩" [?]) [the quotation's wording partly doubtful, [?]] — by this derivation, he gives *garta* the meaning *śmaśāna* ("cemetery"). Therefore *vailasthāna* means a cemetery-place; or, because *bila* gives the meaning Nāga-world, Pātāla, *vailasthāna* may also be said to mean the Nāga-world. But this meaning is not current in Vedic literature. On this point the English scholar Wilson says as follows —

"*vailasthānaṃ aśeran*" — *They have slept or irregularly 'they sleep' in a place which is of the nature of a bila* (विल [sic]), *a hole, a cavern, a pit; the Scholiast considers the expression in this and in the third stanza to be equivalent to* śmaśāna, *a place where dead bodies are burned, or, as it would have seem [sic] to imply, a place where they were buried; as if it was the practice to bury the dead when this hymn was composed. Sayana also suggests, as an alternative, the translation of* vailasthānaṃ *by* nāgaloka, *the serpent-world;* pātāḷa, *the region below the earth; but this is ratter [sic] Pauranik, perhaps, than Vaidic.*

*Bala*, i.e. "Nāgaloka, Pātāḷa" is a meaning that occurs only in later Sanskrit and is not current in the Vedas, so that meaning need not be considered here. As Yāska explains the word *garta* by the word *śmaśāna*, the meaning "cemetery" is the appropriate one. Even in a cemetery there are two kinds — a place where corpses are burned and a place where they are buried; which of these is meant here cannot be said. Wilson thinks that at that time the burying of corpses was current; but [text continues on p. 539].

### Printed p. 539  (PDF 560)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued from p. 538.)* …but in this Ṛk the word "*dahāmi*" ("I burn") is used, so, since "burning" the corpse is meant, one may say plainly that at that time corpses were burned and also buried. In the Ṛgveda there are authorities for both of these kinds of corpse-rites:

> मैनमग्ने वि दहो माभि शोचो मास्य त्वचं चिक्षिपो मा शरीरम् ।
> यदा शृतं कृणवो जातवेदोऽथेमेनं प्र हिणुतात्पितृभ्यः ॥

> *mainam agne vi daho mābhi śoco māsya tvacaṃ cikṣipo mā śarīram |*
> *yadā śṛtaṃ kṛṇavo jātavedo 'themenaṃ pra hiṇutāt pitṛbhyaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-16-1 [as read: "೧೦-೧೬-೧"].)

> यं त्वमग्ने समदहस्तमु निर्वापया पुनः ।
> क्याम्बूरत्र [?] रोहतु पाकदूर्वा व्यल्कशा ॥

> *yaṃ tvam agne samadahas tam u nirvāpayā punaḥ |*
> *kyāmbūratra [?] rohatu pākadūrvā vyalkaśā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-16-14 [as read: "೧೦-೧೬-೧೪"].) Such Ṛks support the view that corpses were burned. In the 16th Sūkta of the 10th [Maṇḍala] the Ṛks pray in various ways to Agni that the corpse (the body) should not be burnt [i.e. not harmed], and that the body (its *ātman*) be taken to the Pitṛs and the gods. [Sic sense; as read.]

> उप सर्प मातरं भूमिमेतामुरुव्यचसं पृथिवीं सुशेवाम् ।
> ऊर्णम्रदा युवतिर्दक्षिणावत एषा त्वा पातु निर्ऋतेरुपस्थात् ॥
> उच्छ्वञ्चस्व पृथिवि मा नि बाधथाः सूपायनास्मै भव सूपवञ्चना ।
> माता पुत्रं यथा सिचाभ्येनं भूम ऊर्णुहि ॥
> उच्छ्वञ्चमाना पृथिवी सु तिष्ठतु सहस्रं मित उप हि श्रयन्ताम् ।
> ते गृहासो घृतश्चुतो भवन्तु विश्वाहास्मै शरणाः सन्त्वत्र ॥
> उत्ते स्तभ्नामि पृथिवीं त्वत्परीमं लोगं निदधन्मो अहं रिषम् ।
> एतां स्थूणां पितरो धारयन्तु ते यमः सादना ते मिनोतु ॥

> *upa sarpa mātaraṃ bhūmim etām uruvyacasaṃ pṛthivīṃ suśevām |*
> *ūrṇamradā yuvatir dakṣiṇāvata eṣā tvā pātu nirṛter upasthāt ‖*
> *ucchvañcasva pṛthivi mā ni bādhathāḥ sūpāyanāsmai bhava sūpavañcanā |*
> *mātā putraṃ yathā sicābhyenaṃ bhūma ūrṇuhi ‖*
> *ucchvañcamānā pṛthivī su tiṣṭhatu sahasraṃ mita upa hi śrayantām |*
> *te gṛhāso ghṛtaścuto bhavantu viśvāhāsmai śaraṇāḥ santv atra ‖*
> *ut te stabhnāmi pṛthivīṃ tvat parīmaṃ logaṃ nidadhan mo ahaṃ riṣam |*
> *etāṃ sthūṇāṃ pitaro dhārayantu te yamaḥ sādanā te minotu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-18-10 to 13 [as read: "೧೦-೧೮-೧೦ ರಿಂದ ೧೩"]. The reading of these small words is from the image; doubtful letters in the third and fourth verse are not marked individually.) Such Ṛks introduce the burying of the corpse in the earth, with prayers that the earth protect the dead body as a mother protects her son, and so on. The Ṛks of the 16th and 18th Sūktas [of Maṇḍala 10], as stated above, are used even now in the funeral rite (*antyakriyā*).

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *punāmi* — root *pūñ pavane*; *laṭ*, first person singular *mip*; *kryādibhyaḥ śnā* (Pā. 3-1-81 [as read]) gives *śnā*; *hrasvaḥ* by *prādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ* [?] (Pā. [?]) — the root is shortened (*pu-nā-mi*), and as it is followed by a *pit* ending, the *nighāta* accent comes.

### Printed p. 540  (PDF 561)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 133" [as read].)*

*(Grammar page, noted briefly.)* *druhaḥ* — root *druha jighāṃsāyām*; *kvip*; accusative plural. *dahāmi* — root *dahe bhasmīkaraṇe*; *laṭ*, first person singular; as the verb ends in *tiṅ*, the *nighāta* accent. *anindrāḥ* — *na vidyate indro yāsāṃ tāḥ*; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. 6-2-172 [as read; digits doubtful]) puts the udātta on the last syllable of the following member (*uttarapadāntodātta*); accusative plural. *abhivlagya* — *abhi* a prefix; *vlaga gatau*, a Vedic root; *samāse 'nañpūrve ktvo lyap* (Pā. 7-1-37 [as read]) gives *lyap* for *ktvā*; as it is *pit*, it is *anudātta*, so the root's accent remains; in the compound *kṛdutta rapadaprakṛtisvara* occurs. *hatāḥ* — root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *niṣṭhā* (*kta*) in the passive; *anudāttopadeśa* (Pā. 6-4-37 [as read]) drops the nasal of the root; the suffix accent. *amitrāḥ* — *ñañ…jaramaramitramṛtāḥ* (Pā. 6-2-165 [as read]) gives *ādyudātta* on the last member [sense of the note: the following member has the initial udātta]. *vailasthānam* — *bila kṣepe*; the suffix *ka* by the statement "*ghañarthe kavidhānam*"; because it is *kit* the *laghūpadhaguṇa* does not occur; *bila* itself is *vaila*; *prajñādibhyaś ca* (Pā. 5-4-38 [as read]) gives *aṇ* in the selfsame sense; *yasyeti ca* drops the previous *a*; *taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ* gives *vṛddhi* of the first vowel; *vailasya sthānam*, *vailasthānam*: "*śmaśāna*" is the meaning. *tṛḷhāḥ* — root *tṛha hiṃsāyām*; *kta* in the passive; as it has *ū* as marker, *iṭ* is optional, by *yasya vibhāṣā* (Pā. 7-2-15 [as read]) the *kta* suffix gets no *iṭ*; *hoḍhaḥ* — by the sūtra the root's *ha* becomes *ḍha*; by *jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ* [as read] the *th* of the suffix becomes *dh*; by *ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ* the earlier *ḍh* is dropped; suffix accent as final udātta. *aśeran* — *śīṅ svapne*; *vyatyayo bahulam* (Pā. 3-1-85 [as read]) gives Parasmaipada; *laṅ* by Vedic usage; *jhi* (prathama puruṣa bahuvacana) the suffix *jhi* → *ran*; *ādeśa* by *śīṅo ruṭ* (Pā. 7-1-6 [as read]) the suffix gets *ruṭ*; because it is *ṭit*, the first… [the page continues to the next with the remaining details of *aśeran*].

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

*(Grammar of *aśeran*, concluded.)* …*vikaraṇa* (*śap*) is elided (*luk*); *śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ* (Pā. 7-4-21 [as read]) gives *guṇa* to the *ī* of the root; the *āgama* belongs to the *aṅga*. Since the word *yatra* is connected with it, the *nighāta* accent does not occur. As the *āgama* is udātta, the *ādyudātta* accent arises. ‖ 1 ‖

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अभिव्ल्ग्या चिदद्रिवः शीर्षा यातुमतीनाम् ।
> छिन्धि वटूरिणा पदा महावटूरिणा पदा ॥ २ ॥

> *abhivlgyā cidadrivaḥ śīrṣā yātumatīnām |*
> *chindhi vaṭūriṇā padā mahāvaṭūriṇā padā ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अभिऽव्लग्य । चित् । अद्रिऽवः । शीर्षा । यातुऽमतीनाम् ।
> छिन्धि । वटूरिणा । पदा । महाऽवटूरिणा । पदा ॥ २ ॥

> *abhi 'vlagya | cit | adri 'vaḥ | śīrṣā | yātu 'matīnām |*
> *chindhi | vaṭūriṇā | padā | mahā 'vaṭūriṇā | padā ‖ 2 ‖*

*(Saṃhitā "*abhivlagyā*" as printed with long final ā; the Pada has *abhivlagya*.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; the closing grammatical citations are doubtful [?].)*

> अद्रिवो वैरिणां भक्षक यद्वाद्रेर्मेघस्यादर्तेरिन्द्र त्वं यातुमतीनां हिंसावतीनां सेनानां । यद्वा । यातनासाधनान्यायुधानि यातूनि तद्वतीनाम् । अथवा । यातवो रक्षांसि तद्वतीनां सेनानां ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ शत्रूणां सेनाः । शीर्षा शीर्षाण्यभिव्लग्या चिदभितः प्राप्यैव छिन्धि । चूर्णय । यद्वा । तासां संबन्धीनि रथादीनि छिन्धि । केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । वटूरिणा पदा व्याप्तस्य नशीलेन सर्वव्यापिना त्वदीयपादेन । आविस्तृतेनेत्यर्थः । यद्वा । वटूरिणा पदा वेष्टनशीलेन हस्तिनः संबन्धिना पादेन । ऐरावतपादेनेत्यर्थः । न केवलेन येन केन पादेनेत्याह । महावटूरिणा पदा महावेष्टनवता स्वीयेनैरावतसंबन्धिना वा पादेन छिन्धि । चूर्णय ॥ वट वेष्टने । खर्जिपिञ्जादिभ्य ऊरोलचौ । उ. ४-९० [?] । इत्यूरप्रत्ययः । अतः इनितनौ [?] ॥

> *adrivo vairiṇāṃ bhakṣaka yadvādrermeghasyādarterindra tvaṃ yātumatīnāṃ hiṃsāvatīnāṃ senānāṃ | yadvā | yātanāsādhanānyāyudhāni yātūni tadvatīnām | athavā | yātavo rakṣāṃsi tadvatīnāṃ senānāṃ ‖ karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī ‖ śatrūṇāṃ senāḥ | śīrṣā śīrṣāṇyabhivlagyā cidabhitaḥ prāpyaiva chindhi | cūrṇaya | yadvā | tāsāṃ saṃbandhīni rathādīni chindhi | kena sādhaneneti taducyate | vaṭūriṇā padā vyāptasya naśīlena sarvavyāpinā tvadīyapādena | āvistṛtenetyarthaḥ | yadvā | vaṭūriṇā padā veṣṭanaśīlena hastinaḥ saṃbandhinā pādena | airāvatapādenetyarthaḥ | na kevalena yena kena pādenetyāha | mahāvaṭūriṇā padā mahāveṣṭanavatā svīyenairāvatasaṃbandhinā vā pādena chindhi | cūrṇaya ‖ vaṭa veṣṭane | kharjipiñjādibhya ūrolacau | u. 4-90 [?] | ityūrapratyayaḥ | ataḥ initanau [?] ‖*

*(Sense: "O *adrivaḥ* — devourer of enemies, or [from *adri*, cloud, and *adarti*] possessor of the cloud — O Indra: you, of the *yātumatī* — harming — armies; or of those armies possessing *yātūni*, i.e. weapons that are instruments of torment; or those that have *yātus*, Rākṣasas: [the genitive is in the sense of the object] of the enemies' armies, the heads (*śīrṣā* = *śīrṣāṇi*) having encompassed (*abhivlagya cit*) on all sides — cut off, crush them; or, cut their chariots etc. With what instrument? — with *vaṭūriṇā padā*: with your all-pervading foot, pervading, spread out [?]; or with the foot of the elephant, that wraps (Airāvata's foot); and not with just any foot — with the great (*mahā*) wrapping foot, or your own foot, or the foot of Airāvata: cut, crush." Grammar: root *vaṭa veṣṭane*; *kharjipiñjādibhya ūrolacau* (Uṇ. 4-[?] as read "೪-೯೦" [?]) gives suffix *ūra*; final grammar citation not legible to me.)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *he adrivaḥ* — O devourer of enemies, or O Indra who splits clouds; *yātumatīnām* — of the harming (those that do harm), or of the army possessing weapons, or of those with Rākṣasas, *senānām* — of the armies, *(of the enemies' armies)*; *śīrṣā* — the heads (and the chariots); *abhivlagya cit* — having covered well on all sides, *vaṭūriṇā* — all-pervading *(spread-out)*; *padā* — with your foot, or Airāvata's foot; *chindhi* — crush (or cut); *mahāvaṭūriṇā* — extremely wide; *padā* — with your (or Airāvata's) foot (trample them to dust).

### Printed p. 542  (PDF 563)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 133" [as read].)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued.)* …the armies with weapons; *śīrṣā* — the heads (the chariots too); *abhivlagya cit* — having covered well on all sides; *vaṭūriṇā* — all-pervading (wide); *padā* — with your foot or with Airāvata's; *chindhi* — crush or make [them] crushed; *mahāvaṭūriṇā* — most extensive; *padā* — with your (or Airāvata's) foot, trample [them] to powder.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, destroyer of enemies, covering well on all sides the heads (the chariots) of the armies (of weapons that do harm), trample them to dust with your all-pervading (or Airāvata's) foot; trample them to dust with your (or Airāvata's) very wide foot, which is accustomed to cover well.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Devourer (of foes), having trampled on the heads of the malignant (hosts), crush them with your wide-spreading foot; your vast wide-spreading foot."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 2).**

***adrivaḥ*** — *vairiṇāṃ bhakṣaka | yadvādrermeghasyādarteḥ indra*: Sāyaṇa gives two kinds of meaning to this word. One: from the root *ad*, "eat, destroy" — he who destroys the enemies; or, since the word *adri* is among the names of cloud (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೩೦" [?]) — one who strikes the clouds and makes rain: such a meaning may be made.

***yātumatīnām*** — *hiṃsāvatīnāṃ senānām*: "of the armies that have violence" is the meaning. Or *yātanāsādhanānyāyudhāni yātūni tadvatīnām* — to the weapons that have *yātanā* (torment) or violence the name *yātūni* is given; the enemies that have weapons and the like as instruments of violence, that is, "of warriors having them". Or *yātavo rakṣāṃsi tadvatīnāṃ senānām*: *yātavaḥ* means Rākṣasas; "of armies accompanied by them", or "of the armies of Rākṣasas", may also be the meaning.

> प्र ये गृहादमम दुस्त्मना यो पराचरः शतेयातुर्वशिष्टः ।
> न ते भोजस्य सख्यं मृषन्ताधा सूरिभ्यः सुदिना व्यच्छान् ॥

> *pra ye gṛhād amamadus tmanā yo parācaraḥ śateyāturvaśiṣṭaḥ [?] |*
> *na te bhojasya sakhyaṃ mṛṣantādhā sūribhyaḥ sudinā vyacchān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-[?]-[?], as read "೭-೧೯-೩೨" [?]; the Saṃhitā reading of the first line is doubtful in several places.) In explaining this Ṛk, Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, gives *śateyātuḥ*, *bahūnāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ghātayitā* ("one who has slain many Rākṣasas") — thus he gives to the word *yātu* the meaning "Rākṣasas" (Ni. 6-[?], as read "೬-೩೧" [?]).

### Printed p. 543  (PDF 564)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

***vaṭūriṇā***, ***mahāvaṭūriṇā*** — *veṣṭanaśīlena sarvavyāptena tvadīyapādenātivistṛtenetyarthaḥ*. Sāyaṇa gives two kinds of meaning for these words. One: with your all-pervading, extremely wide foot, cut the heads of the enemies, is a meaning. And *yadvā vaṭūriṇā padā mahāveṣṭanavatā svīyenairāvatasaṃbandhinā vā pādena chindhi cūrṇaya* — another meaning: with the extremely large feet of the elephant called Airāvata, which belongs to you, crush to powder the heads of the enemies. The name of the elephant *Airāvata* is not mentioned in the Vedas; so this sort of explanation, from the Purāṇas and the like, does not appear very appropriate.

In this Ṛk the ṛṣi prays to Indra to trample and destroy, with his wide, large foot, the heads of the enemies who do him harm, and to cut off the heads and destroy the enemies.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *abhivlagya* — its process was explained earlier, in an earlier mantra; in the Saṃhitā, by Vedic usage, a long [vowel] occurs. *adrivaḥ* — *chandasīravaḥ* [as read] (Pā. 8-[?]-[?], as read "೮-೩-೧೮") gives *natva* to the *m* of *matup*; *matuvasoḥ sambuddhau* [as read] (Pā. 8-3-1) gives *ruṭva*; *āmantritasya ca* gives the *nighāta* accent. *śīrṣā* — *śīrṣañ chandasi* (Pā. 6-1-60) gives the *śīrṣan* substitute for the word *śiras*; in the neuter plural *śeś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. 6-1-70) drops the *śi*. *yātumatīnām* — *yātūni āsāṃ santīti yātumatyaḥ, tāsām*; *hrasvanudbhyāṃ matup* [as read] (Pā. 6-1-176 [as read]) gives the udātta to the *matup*. *chindhi* — root *chidir dvaidhīkaraṇe*; *loṭ*, second person singular; as it is the beginning of a pāda, [*chindhi* has] the final udātta. *vaṭūriṇā* — root *vaṭa veṣṭane*; *kharjipiñjādibhya ūrolacau* (Uṇ. [?]) gives the suffix *ūra*; *vaṭūro 'syāsti iti vaṭūrī*; *ata iniṭhanau* (Pā. 5-2-115 [as read]) gives the suffix *ini* in the sense of *matup*; the suffix's first vowel is udātta; instrumental singular. *padā* — *ūḍidaṃ padādi* (Pā. 6-1-171 [as read]) gives the udātta to the case-ending.

### Printed p. 544  (PDF 565)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 133" [as read].)*

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *mahāvaṭūriṇā* — *mahāṃś cāsau vaṭūrī ca*; *anmahataḥ samānādhikaraṇayoḥ* [as read] (Pā. 6-3-46 [as read]) gives *ātva* to the earlier member; the earlier member keeps its natural accent. ‖ 2 ‖

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अवासां मघवञ्जहि शर्धो यातुमतीनाम् ।
> वैलस्थानके अर्मके महावैलस्थे अर्मके ॥ ३ ॥

> *avāsāṃ maghavañjahi śardho yātumatīnām |*
> *vailasthānake armake mahāvailasthe armake ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अव । आसाम् । मघऽवन् । जहि । शर्धः । यातुऽमतीनाम् ।
> वैलस्थानके । अर्मके । महाऽवैलस्थे । अर्मके ॥ ३ ॥

> *ava | āsām | magha 'van | jahi | śardhaḥ | yātu 'matīnām |*
> *vailasthānake | armake | mahā 'vailasthe | armake ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image.)*

> हे इन्द्र मघवन् धनवन् आसां यातुमतीनां । यातनासाधनान्यायुधानि यातूनि तद्वतीनां यातुधानवतां वा सेनानां शर्धो बलमव जहि । चूर्णय । तथा कृत्वा चार्मके कुत्सिते शवैरणीये वैलस्थानके पूर्वोक्तलक्षणे श्मशाने स्वपयेति शेषः । यद्वा । वैलस्थानके बिलसंबन्धिनि कुत्सिते स्थानेन्द्रधकारावृतेऽधोलोके स्थापयेति शेषः । ननु यत्र कुत्रचित्क्षुद्रे नेत्याह । महावैलस्थे सर्वैर्गन्तव्ये महाश्मशाने नागलोके वा । पुनः कीदृशे । अर्मके कुत्सिते गताशुभिरणीये [?] ॥

> *he indra maghavan dhanavan āsāṃ yātumatīnāṃ | yātanāsādhanānyāyudhāni yātūni tadvatīnāṃ yātudhānavatāṃ vā senānāṃ śardho balamava jahi | cūrṇaya | tathā kṛtvā cārmake kutsite śavairaṇīye vailasthānake pūrvoktalakṣaṇe śmaśāne svapayeti śeṣaḥ | yadvā | vailasthānake bilasaṃbandhini kutsite sthānendradhakārāvṛte 'dholoke sthāpayeti śeṣaḥ | nanu yatra kutracitkṣudre netyāha | mahāvailasthe sarvairgantavye mahāśmaśāne nāgaloke vā | punaḥ kīdṛśe | armake kutsite gatāśubhiraṇīye [?] ‖*

*(Sense: "O Indra, Maghavan (wealthy)! Of these *yātumatī* armies — those having *yātūni*, weapons that are instruments of torment, or having Yātudhānas — destroy the strength (*śardhaḥ*), crush it; and, having done so, put [them] to sleep in the wretched (*ārmaka*) cemetery, as described above, fit for corpses, the *vailasthānaka*. Or: put [them] in the despised lower world, connected with a *bila* (hole), covered by darkness. Not in just any small place — in the *mahāvailastha*, the great cemetery which all must go to, or in the Nāga-world. Of what kind? — *ārmaka*: wretched, [fit for those who have gone to their destruction] [?].")*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *maghavan* — O wealthy Indra; *āsām* — of these; *yātumatīnām* — of the armies that have weapons that do violence (of the enemies); *śardhaḥ* — the strength; *ava jahi* — destroy; *(tathā kṛtvā)* — having done so; *ārmake* — in the wretched (fit for corpses); *vailasthānake* — in a cemetery (*śmaśāna*); *(svapaya)* — put [them] to sleep; *ārmake* — in the wretched (that which the dead reach); *mahāvailasthe* — in the great *bila* (in the Nāga-world); *(svapaya)* — put [them] to sleep.

### Printed p. 545  (PDF 566)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Ṛk 3).** O wealthy Indra, destroy the strength of these (armies) that are harmful and bear weapons; (crush them and) cast them into a wretched pit (so that they lie in a cemetery); throw them into the wretched great pit (the Nāga-world).

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Annihilate, Maghavan, the might of malignant (hosts), hurl them into the vile pit; the vast and vile pit"* [sic: no full stop; a semicolon-like mark before "the vast"].

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 3).** In this Ṛk also the ṛṣi prays to Indra to destroy the strength of his enemies, to conquer them, and to throw their dead bodies into a cemetery or the lower world, covered with darkness.

***āsāṃ yātumatīnām*** — "of these armies that are accompanied by instruments of torment" is the meaning. The meaning of this word has been explained in the Special Topics of the previous Ṛk.

***śardhaḥ*** — the word *śardha* is in the names of strength (*bala*) (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೯" [?]). Ordinarily this word is used particularly in the sense of "troop of Maruts"; here it means the strength of the enemy armies.

***vailasthānake, mahāvailasthe*** — *bilasaṃbandhini kutsite sthāne 'ndhakārāvṛte 'dholoke*: "a lower world, extremely deep, covered with darkness and terrifying". As said in the previous Ṛk, [it may mean] the Nāga-world or the cemetery; in either case the ṛṣi prays Indra to cast the enemies into such a place.

***ārmake*** — *kutsite śavairaṇīye | gatāsubhiraṇīye*: "an extremely contemptible place [a cemetery] where the bodies of the dead are put".

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *jahi* — root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *loṭ* second person singular, *sip*, replaced by *hi*; *hanter jaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-36 [as read]) gives *ja* in place of the root; because the *ja*-substitute is regarded as not-effective (*asiddha*) for this purpose, *ato heḥ* does not give *luk* [?]; as it follows a *tiṅanta*, the *nighāta* accent. *śardhaḥ* — root *śṛdhu unnadane [?]*; suffix *asun*; since the suffix conditions it, the *laghūpadha guṇa* of the root; *ñnityādir nityam* (Pā. 6-1-197 [as read]) gives the ādyudātta accent. ‖ 3 ‖

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यासां तिस्रः पञ्चाशतोऽभिव्लङ्गैरपावपः ।
> तत्सु ते मनायति तकत्सु ते मनायति ॥ ४ ॥

> *yāsāṃ tisraḥ pañcāśato 'bhivlaṅgairapāvapaḥ |*
> *tatsu te manāyati takatsu te manāyati ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यासाम् । तिस्रः । पञ्चाशतः । अभिऽव्लङ्गैः । अप । अवपः ।
> तत् । सु । ते । मनायति । तकत् । सु । ते । मनायति ॥ ४ ॥

> *yāsām | tisraḥ | pañcāśataḥ | abhi 'vlaṅgaiḥ | apa | avapaḥ |*
> *tat | su | te | manāyati | takat | su | te | manāyati ‖ 4 ‖*

### Printed p. 546  (PDF 567)

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(read from the image; begins p. 546.)*

> हे इन्द्र यासां पूर्वमन्त्रोक्तलक्षणानां सेनानां तिस्रः पञ्चाशतः त्रिगुणितपञ्चाशत्संख्यां सार्धशतमभिव्लङ्गैरभिगमनैः । व्लङ्गतिर्गतिकर्मा तत्कृतं । अभिगम्यापावपः नाशितवानसि । हे इन्द्र तत्ताद्दृशं सेनावधादिरूपं कर्म सु मनायति । सुष्ठु संभावयतीत्यर्थः । किंच हे इन्द्र ते तवाध्यर्धशतैतत्सेनाजयरूपं महदपि तकदिति सु मनायति । अत्यल्पमिदमिति सुष्ठु मन्यते ॥

> *he indra yāsāṃ pūrvamantroktalakṣaṇānāṃ senānāṃ tisraḥ pañcāśataḥ triguṇitapañcāśatsaṃkhyāṃ sārdhaśatamabhivlaṅgairabhigamanaiḥ | vlaṅgatirgatikarmā tatkṛtaṃ | abhigamyāpāvapaḥ nāśitavānasi | he indra tattāddṛśaṃ senāvadhādirūpaṃ karma su manāyati | suṣṭhu saṃbhāvayatītyarthaḥ | kiṃca he indra te tavādhyardhaśataitatsenājayarūpaṃ mahadapi takaditi su manāyati | atyalpamidamiti suṣṭhu manyate ‖*

*(Sense: "O Indra, of which armies — of the kind described in the previous mantra — thrice fifty, i.e. one hundred and fifty, you destroyed by *abhivlaṅgaiḥ*, 'attacks' (*vlaṅgati* is a verb of motion), going against [them]. O Indra, that deed of yours, of the form of slaying such armies, is *su manāyati* — is well esteemed. And further, O Indra, even this great victory over one hundred and fifty armies [seems] to you *takat* — [it] is well thought of as very small." The grammatical tail is not given here.)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he indre — O Indra)*; *yāsām* — of which (the armies spoken of before); *tisraḥ pañcāśataḥ* — thrice fifty (one hundred and fifty); *abhivlaṅgaiḥ* — by facing (having faced); *apa avapaḥ* — you destroyed; *te tat* — that your (deed); *su manāyati* — is well becoming (although that deed is great); *te* — to you; *takat (iti)* — as small; *su manāyati* — it is well known.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, [to the extent that] you have faced and destroyed one hundred and fifty armies [of those harmful, weapon-bearing ones], it well becomes you; but to a mighty one like you, [that great deed] is known to be very small.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"That you have destroyed, by your assaults, thrice fifty of such (hosts), is a deed that well becomes you, although thought by you of little moment."*

### Printed p. 547  (PDF 568)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 4).**

***tisraḥ pañcāśataḥ*** — "three times fifty", that is, one hundred and fifty. [That is,] it has been prayed to Indra that he destroy a hundred and fifty of the enemies spoken of before, or a hundred and fifty armies of enemies.

***tat su te manāyati takat su te manāyati*** — Here, for the word *manāyati* Sāyaṇa says *sukhu manyate, suṣṭhu saṃbhāvayatītyarthaḥ* — "he thinks it very good, he esteems it highly", is the meaning: "he regards it as a very praiseworthy deed". That is, of this sentence: "O Indra, the act of killing the enemies that you do (spoken of up to now) seems to you very small; but to us who see it, it appears a very great deed. Such a deed we praise greatly" — this is the chief purport.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *tisraḥ* — *tricaturoḥ striyāṃ tisṛcatasṛ* (Pā. 7-2-99 [as read]) gives *tisṛ* for the word *tri*; the *guṇa* attained; *ṛta idhātoḥ* [as read?] / *ṛta ut* [?] — the *ṛ* becomes *ra* [as read]; *udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt* (Pā. 6-1-174 [as read]) gives the udātta to the case-ending. *abhivlaṅgaiḥ* — *vlaṅga gatau*, a root used only in the sūtra [?]; suffix *ac*; final udātta; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. 6-2-139 [as read]) gives the *kṛt*-final the earlier member's own accent [sic: "kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara"]. *apāvapaḥ* — *apa* a prefix; *ḍuvap bījasantāne* [as read]; with the prefix it takes the sense of destruction; *laṅ* second person singular, *avapaḥ* in form; because of its connection with *yatra* [sic: *yāsām*?] there is no *nighāta*; since the *āgama* is udātta, it has the ādyudātta; *tiṅ ca udāttavati* (Pā. 8-1-71 [as read]) the *gati* (*apa*) becomes *anudātta*. *manāyati* — *laṭ* second person [sic] singular; since it follows a *tiṅanta*, *nighāta*. ‖ 4 ‖

### Printed p. 549  (PDF 570)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 5).** *(Note on references: this and the next three pages carry dozens of Ṛgveda references in small numerals; to save effort they are not transcribed here but are to be supplied in the separate numeral pass — each place is marked "[refs]" below. Nothing else is omitted.)*

In the previous Ṛks the ṛṣi prayed that enemies in human form be destroyed; in this Ṛk he prays Indra to destroy the Piśācī, the group of Rākṣasas, and the like.

***piśaṅgabhṛṣṭim*** — "one whose body is of a slightly reddish colour with a little flesh"; the colour of the bodies of the Piśācas and the like looks different from that of men, and, to those who look at them, is extremely frightening — this is the sense. The ancient inhabitants of this country are called in many places by words such as *dāsa* and *dasyu*; this appears to be a usage that has become current. Their dress, ornaments and the colour of their bodies, unlike those of the Āryas, being black, flesh-red and so on, are terrifying; hence it is usual to refer to them by words such as *piśāca*, *rakṣaḥ*.

***ambhṛṇam*** — *atibhayaṃkaraṃ śabdāyamānam | yadvā | mahāntam atipravṛddham ity arthaḥ*: "making a terrible noise" — "one who makes noise with an extremely ugly (terrifying) or distorted voice" is the meaning; or "great, very big": the word *ambhṛṇa* occurs among the twenty-odd [?] names of *mahat*, "great", such as *bṛhat*, *dyumnaḥ* (Ni. 3-[?], [refs]) — so it may also be given the meaning "of a very big form". It is well known that the forms of Piśācas and Rākṣasas are far larger than the forms of men.

***piśācīm, rakṣaḥ*** — Yāska, in his Nirukta, gives the derivation of the word *rakṣaḥ*: "*rakṣo rakṣitavyam asmāt | rahasi kṣaṇoti iti vā | rātrau nakṣata iti vā*" (Ni. 4-[?], [refs]) — "they are to be guarded against, because they injure men, so men have to be protected from them; hence they are called *rakṣaḥ*; or, as they live in lonely places, or as they move about in the night-time, they are called *rakṣaḥ*." In modern Sanskrit the words *piśāca*, *rakṣaḥ* signify non-bodily, evil-natured ones, injurious to men, and they also indicate certain bodiless beings. But in the Ṛgveda such description is not found; yet they are said to be evil-doers, to men, and even among men to those who perform sacrificial acts, to sacrificers; their works are against sacrifice and work of the sacrifice, and they are said to cause distress. Probably they were the dark-skinned people, the original inhabitants of this country. The Āryas used to call them Dasyus. They troubled sacrifices and the like and caused various kinds of injury to people, so there are many Ṛks that pray Indra to destroy and protect from them. The chief among them are described briefly —

The name Piśāca is used commonly together with Dāsa and Dasyu. Among them are many: Śuṣṇa, Śambara, Pipru, Namuci, Dhuni, Cumuri and others. As in the Ṛgveda, their matter is briefly described here.

### Printed p. 550  (PDF 571)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 133" [as read].)*

***Śuṣṇa*** — his name occurs some forty times. The chief enemy is Kutsa. This Kutsa, or rather in company with Kutsa, Indra destroys Śuṣṇa root and all [refs]. He has horns [refs]; "the pot-bellied" [refs] — as "swellings (mounds) made of pots" [?] they compare [refs]; thus Śuṣṇa too may be called a serpent. He is a "hisser" (*busugutta*) — [Ṛ. "*svasanaḥ*", refs]. For him the attribute *aśuṣa* (the "swallower", a name of Agni) is used. He has strong forts [refs] or a fort [refs]; these are moving forts [refs]. Indra, destroying Śuṣṇa's forts, releases the waters [refs]; killing Śuṣṇa he gains the sea [refs, Vāla.?] or, destroying Śuṣṇa's race, he wins the (*svarvatīḥ*) heavenly waters [refs]. Śuṣṇa has the epithet *kuyava* ("one who produces bad grain") four times. These two words *kuyava* probably are used instead of the name Śuṣṇa [refs]. The result of the war of Indra with Śuṣṇa is not only the release of the waters but also the gain of the cows or of the sun [refs]. When Indra fights him, Śuṣṇa runs away into the darkness [refs]. He seizes the demon who is the son of snow [Hima] [refs]. Śuṣṇa is the Dānava who has the nectar placed in himself, (*kāṭaka*) [as read].

From the sentences above it may be said that Śuṣṇa causes drought: the root *śuṣ* of the word *śuṣṇa* means "to dry up, to wither"; this supports his being the cause of drought.

***Śambara*** — this name occurs some twenty-five times. Śambara appears along with the other Piśācas. Especially with Śuṣṇa, Pipru, and Varcin [refs]; and, with Ahi, Śambara is fought against; the Maruts help Indra [refs]; when Śambara was split, Indra made the sky shake [refs]; he sought out Śambara living on the mountain and [Indra] rolled him down from the mountain [refs]. Śambara, a Dāsa, the son of Kulitara, Indra hurled down from the great mountain [refs]; also thinking himself a "small deity" [*as read*], striking Śambara he threw him down from a high place [refs]. *Tombhatta* [as read], in general *tombhatta* (or "one hundred", etc.) fortresses were under his authority. Once, for this word, in the neuter, "Śambara's forts" is the sense. These Bṛhaspati split and entered the mountain regions, [filled] with treasures [refs]. Atithigva [refs]; generally Divodāsa [refs], on one occasion both [refs]; for these two Indra destroys Śambara. Some are of the opinion that Śambara and Divodāsa are the name of one person.

### Printed p. 551  (PDF 572)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

***Pipru*** — Indra's enemy (Vāla. [refs]), the foe of Ṛjiśvan; this Ṛjiśvan, having pressed Soma-juice for Indra, gets Indra's help in the war with Pipru [refs]; having taken Indra with Ṛjiśvan [refs] or with Avanigoṣkara [refs], he defeated Pipru. There are many forts under that one possessed of illusions [māyā]; Indra splits these [refs]. Pipru, a Dāsa, and some others Indra slew and sent the waters out [refs]; when the sun in the middle of the sky stopped his chariot, Āryan saw a suitable *yojana* for Pipru [?]; Indra, together with Ṛjiśvan, destroyed the strong forts of the demon Pipru, who has illusions [refs]. Indra gave the black Pipru, a kind of dark-coloured [?], to Ṛjiśvan; he slew fifty thousand black people, splitting forts [refs]; with Ṛjiśvan, Indra destroyed the black-coloured ones' posterity [refs]. Because he has the two epithets Asura and Dāsa, some are of the opinion that he may also be an enemy among men.

***Namuci*** — in the Ṛgveda this name occurs nine times, and also in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa and Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. The attribute Asura (one of asura nature) occurs [refs; Śa. Brā. refs] and in other Vedas also he is called Asura. He is called "Dāsa" in three or four passages [refs] and once Māyin [refs]. While contending with Namuci, Indra's companions (the Maruts) are in his favour [refs]; with Namuci's party Śakti? [as read]; like many other Piśācas, Namuci is slain by Indra [refs] or: he is struck and thrown [refs]; having slain Vṛtra and Namuci, Indra destroyed a hundred forts [refs]; he splits Vṛtra's head [refs]; but he also strikes Namuci's head with a foam [refs]; Indra twisted off Namuci's head [refs] or purified [it] with foam [refs]. In the Brāhmaṇas it is said he cut off the head. Indra crushed the middle of Namuci's side; then, by the help of the Aśvins, Sarasvatī healed it [refs].

Pāṇini's rule [refs]: *namuci*, i.e. *na-muci*: "one who does not let go", that is, a Piśāca who holds back the waters, may be said.

***Dhuni and Cumuri*** — in general both names occur together. Once Cumuri alone has come. Once they are used as a pair [refs]; from this it appears the connection between the two is very close. Indra made the two sleep and lie in sleep [refs]; the same happened to Cumuri also [refs].

### Printed p. 552  (PDF 573)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 133" [as read].)*

With Śambara, Pipru, Śuṣṇa and others, Indra destroyed these [refs]; and their hundreds of forts [refs]; for Dabhīti, who has prepared Soma, the two were destroyed by Indra or put to sleep [refs]; and Dabhīti by Devas got a fitting reward for his devotion [refs]; for Dabhīti Indra put to sleep thirty thousand Dasyus, and bound the Dasyus for Avani, [so that] they could not move [refs].

*Dhuni* means "the roaring one" [or the shaker].

***Varcin and others*** — [In company] with Śambara Varcin's mention occurs four times. He too is an Asura [refs]; but Śambara and he are called "Dāsa" [refs]. Indra broke Śambara's forts and destroyed the hundred thousand warriors of Varcin [refs]. Varcin means "one who goes in the water" [?].

Vala, Śuṣṇa, Namuci and others, and some other Piśācas' names also occur; they too were destroyed by Indra. Dṛbhīka, Rudhikrā [refs], Anarśani, Svabindu [refs] and Ilībiśa [refs] belong to this group.

***The Piśācas on earth, or the *bhūtas*, the enemies of men.*** — the common-gender name for them is *rakṣaḥ*. [The word] occurs more than that number of times, in singular and plural; commonly with one deity or other, it occurs in prayer-form to destroy Rākṣasas, or in praise-form "[you] have slain Rākṣasas". Their matter occurs in the Sūktas 7-104 and 10-87 [as read, [?]]; here the words *rakṣas*, *yātu*, *yātudhāna* and so on denote them. *Rakṣaḥ* is a name for all Rākṣasas, Piśācas; it may be understood as the generic name and *yātu* as a subsidiary generic name.

These Piśācas or *bhūtas* have the forms of dog, owl, cuckoo, [*kokila* [?]] and other birds [refs]. As bird forms they fly about in the night-time [refs]. They take the form of a brother, a husband or a lover, approach women and wish to destroy their children [refs]. As dog or monkey they wait on the cross-roads [Atharva Veda refs]; they cause trouble to pregnant women and children. At marriage-time they run round the bride; their eyes, small arrows they put in the sky [Mā. Gṛ. Sū. refs]. In the Atharvaveda itself the forms of these and so on are described. They especially take forms like men; their heads, eyes, heart and the like limbs are mentioned; but there is something strange about each. Three heads, two mouths [text continues on p. 553].

### Printed p. 553  (PDF 574)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued from p. 552.)* …four eyes, five feet, toes without feet [?], feet turned backwards, or horns on the hands, and so on (Atharvaveda [refs]; Hiraṇyakeśi Gṛhyasūtra [refs]); the Piśācas are also said to have blue and yellow colours and green [dress?]; among them also are males and females, married households, and kings (Ath. Ved. [refs]); they too are mortal (Ath. Ved. [refs] etc.).

The Yātudhānas eat the flesh of men and horses, and drink cow's milk [refs]. To satisfy their desire for blood and flesh Rākṣasas attack men; this attack is usually through entering them; so Agni is prayed to restrain the Rākṣasas, as one stops those who would enter [refs]. Here and there a Piśāca, a presumed cause of disease, enters men (Ath. Ved. [refs]). These *bhūtas*, *pretas* usually enter us through our mouth, when we eat or drink (Ath. Ved. [refs]); they also enter through other doors (Ath. Ved. [refs]). Having entered inside, they obstruct, cut and eat the flesh of the man, and cause disease; they cause madness and destroy speech (Ath. Ved. [refs]; Hir. Gṛ. Sū. [refs]); they attack the dwellings of men (Kau. Sū. [refs]); some *bhūtas* in the evening hours dance round houses and howl like jackals, or wander about in the forests, or stand about on hills, laugh, and drink out of skulls (Ath. Ved. [refs]; Hir. Gṛ. Sū. [refs]).

Their time of movement is night or evening [refs]. In the east they are not allowed to walk; the sun that rises there drives them away [refs]. [In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā it is said that] the burning brand is thought to be the form of a *bhūta*. (Kau. Sū. [refs]) The new-moon night, the darkness, is favourable for the movement of *pretas*, and also for *bhūtas* (Ath. Ved. [refs]).

From these there is no danger to sacrifices of any kind. In sacrifices fit for gods, the Piśācas cause omission and confusion [?]; and the Yātus eat the offerings, scattering them about [refs]; they are not visible when one looks at praise (Stotra) [refs]. Agni is prayed, as a curse suited to a sacrifice, to burn *bhūtas* and the like ([refs]). There is a mantra which makes the sacrifice of an enemy not effective by the illusion of Yātudhānas and Rākṣasas (Ath. Ved. [refs]). Those who come and obstruct as *pretas* when oblations are given to the dead (Ath. Ved. [refs]; compare Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā [refs]). In the Purāṇas it is common that these Rākṣasa-groups (they are generally spoken of as Rākṣasas) trouble the yogis.

### Printed p. 554  (PDF 575)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 133" [as read].)*

Agni is prayed to burn, to drive away or to destroy those who play with fields [?], and the sacrificer at the sacrifice, and those who have hatred against them [refs]. Because of this work Agni and some other deities have the name "*rakṣohā*" ("destroyer of Rākṣasas").

These *bhūtas* are not harmful merely by nature; they may do harm even when impelled by others. The word *rakṣoyujaḥ* ("those who incite Rākṣasas") is found [refs]. And there are *bhūtas* and Yātus that are sent by mantra-wielders [refs]. A *bhūta*-attack sent by an enemy may be made to fall back, [the sufferer] being a victim, with a plant called *yaviṣṭha* [as read] and the one who sent it be swallowed up — such is also dedicated to the *bhūtas* themselves (Ath. Ved. [refs]).

Among the *bhūtas* the word *rakṣaḥ* is used both in the masculine and feminine; in the neuter it also has the sense of "danger". It may be from the root *rakṣ* ("to guard") — *rakṣa*, [the root] "do trouble", i.e. rākṣasa as harmful (*Ṛkvāṇām*? [as read]); but this usage is very rare. Ordinarily it may be from *rakṣ* "to protect". In this connection *rakṣaḥ* means "to be avoided".

***piśācāḥ*** — the third class of *bhūtas* are the Piśācas. In the Ṛgveda they occur in only one place [refs], the word *piśāca* in the singular, in which Indra is prayed to destroy the *piśācī* of tawny colour and having a crest [?], and the one living in water, striking each *bhūta* and destroying it. Asuras, Rākṣasas and Piśācas are, respectively, enemies of the gods, of men, and of the Pitṛs. With the Piśācas, intercourse is mostly connected with the *pretas*. The *pretas* are called *kravyād* (eater of raw flesh, or of dead bodies) (Ath. Ved. [refs] etc.): the word *piśāca* has a similar meaning. Agni is prayed to restore the flesh of a sick man eaten by Piśācas (Ath. Ved. [refs]); and therefore there may also have been a class of Piśācas who eat the flesh of women [?]; the Piśācas roam in the water of rivers (Ath. Ved. [refs]) or ravage the houses and villages of men, [passing] through forests (Ath. Ved. [refs]).

The feminine word *arāti* (miserliness) and the masculine and feminine word *druh* (harm, causing trouble) are also reckoned as kinds of Piśācas.

*Kimīdin*, etc. — a class of *bhūtas* ([refs]).

Of our daily life there are many Piśācas connected with it. By their names alone, one can know the troubles caused by them. They have no connexion with the Prakṛti [i.e. physical nature]; commonly it is a belief that, being enemies to us, it is the dead themselves who come in this form and cause us harm.

### Printed p. 555  (PDF 576)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

Less often, some powers, with a connexion to the person [i.e. to the dead person?], running about in the air, cause men diseases, childlessness, sin, and the like, and suffering. The chief use of *mantra-vidyā* is to turn these away against those who are not ours.

Some Piśācas that move on the earth are not harmful; [from] them we get help. They give help to those who ask, and long life to brides. Arbuda, one of the chief Piśāca-groups, causes terror to enemies and helps us in battles (Ath. Ved. [refs]).

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *piśaṅgabhṛṣṭim* — *piśaṅgā bhṛṣṭir yasya tam*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. 6-2-1 [as read]) gives the earlier member its own accent. *ambhṛṇam* — root *bhṛṇa śabde*; *yaj* (*yañ*) is used in the sense of intensity; for it the *anyemitrakavāgi* [as read: elision, *luk*]; after *yaj-luk-anta*, *nandigrahapacādibhyaḥ* (Pā. 3-1-134 [as read]) gives the *ac* suffix; the change of the letter *bha* is by Vedic usage [as read]. Or *ambhṛṇa* is a name of "great" (*mahat*), a *prātipadika* without derivation; *ñiti nityam* [as read: *phiṣo 'nta udāttaḥ*, "*phiṣ*"] — the final udātta accent comes. *mṛṇa* — root *mṛṇa hiṃsāyām*, *tudādi*; *loṭ* second person singular; as it follows a *tiṅanta*, the *nighāta*. *barhaya* — root *bṛha hiṃsāyām*, *curādi*; *satyāpapāśa…* (Pā. 3-1-25 [as read]) gives *ṇic* in its own sense; *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* (Pā. 7-3-86 [as read]) gives the *laghūpadha guṇa*; after *ṇijanta*, *loṭ* second person singular, hence the form *barhaya*; after *tiṅanta*, *nighāta*. ‖ 5 ‖

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Ṛk 6, concluded; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].)*

> अतिशयेन बलवान् खलु । अतः कारणादुग्रेभिरुद्गूर्णैर्वधैः [?] सहितस्त्वमीयसे । शत्रून् मेघान्वा गच्छसि ॥ ईङ् गतौ । दैवादिकत्वाच्छ्यन् ॥ यद्वा । शुष्मिभिर्वधैरिति संबन्धः । हे शूर विक्रान्त सत्वभिः सत्त्ववद्भिरप्रतीत अप्रतिगत [?] । अप्रत्यर्थिन [?] इत्यर्थः । रक्षःप्रभृतिभिरप्रतिगतो युद्धे शत्रुभिराक्रान्तः । यद्वा । सत्वभिः प्राणिभिरसंस्कृतमनस्कैरनधिगतः । अपूरुषघ्नः पौरुषोपेतानां यजनसमर्थानामहननस्त्वम् । त्रिसप्तैः सत्वभिस्त्रिभिः सप्तभिर्वा सत्वभिरनुचरैरुपेतः सन् । ईयसे इत्यन्वयः ॥

*(Sense: "You, certainly extremely strong, are on that account [*ī-yase*, from *īṅ gatau*, *śyan* by the Daivādika class] accompanied by fierce (*ugra*) and mighty blows, going to enemies or to clouds. **॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he) adrivaḥ* — O (Indra) joined with clouds; *ghṛṇāt* — of the blazing Tvaṣṭṛ, or of Agni; *bhīṣā na* — as through fear (as heaven and earth formerly were frightened); *(he) adrivaḥ* — O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt; *hi* — for which reason; *kṣā* — of the earth; *bhīṣā na* — through fear [because of the lack of rain] that crops and so on will dry up, as she grieves; *dyauḥ* — the heaven-world also (the support of the gods); *śuśoca* — grieves (through the fear that offerings and so on will cease); *[or: as the earth (*kṣā*) and the heaven (*dyauḥ na*) grieve through fear of the Asuras who encircle the world]*; *(tat)* — for that reason; *naḥ* — our (prayer); *śrudhi* — listen; *(he) indra* — O Indra; *mahaḥ* — the great (the water-bearing cloud, or the demon Vṛtra); *avaḥ* — face downward; *dādṛhi* — split (make it burst); *(he indra tvam)* — O Indra, you; *śuṣmibhiḥ* — with strength; *śuṣmintamaḥ hi* — are exceedingly strong (for which reason); *(he) śūra* — O hero; *sattvabhiḥ* — with beings that have become enemies (Rākṣasas and the like), or with the unrefined; *apratīta* — of the unapproached (the unconquered); *apuruṣaghnaḥ* — and the one who does not kill men [capable of sacrifice]; *trisaptaiḥ* — with three times seven (some twenty-one) [as read]; *sattvabhiḥ* — with followers; *ugrebhiḥ* — extremely fierce; *vadhaiḥ* — with means of slaying; *īyase* — goes (to face enemies or clouds).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, accompanied by clouds and wielder of the thunderbolt, formerly the earth and heaven were frightened at the fear of Tvaṣṭṛ (or of Agni); [now] the earth grieves through fear that the crops and so on will wither for lack of rain, and the heaven-world grieves through fear that the offerings will cease; or: unable to bear the Asura party that has encompassed the two worlds, heaven and earth grieve. [So,] O Indra, listen to our prayer; split the clouds, face downward, and make rain. O hero Indra, you are most heroic. Unapproached by Rākṣasas and the like [so as to be conquered], or by the fools with unrefined minds [sic: *asaṃskṛta-mati*], and slaying not those men [fit for sacrifice] but the Rākṣasas, [you go] against the enemies (the clouds), accompanied by twenty-one (or seven times three) [as read] followers and by very fierce means of slaying.

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 6).**

The Sūkta's first two Ṛks are to be used by the Hotṛ's assistant, the Acchāvāka [?], when reciting the *tṛca* ("three Ṛks") for Indra in the *prauga-śastra* on the sixth day of the *daśarātra* sacrifice; this is stated in Āśvalāyana's Śrautasūtra in the section called "*ṣaṣṭhasya*", by the sūtra "*avarmaha indra vṛṣann indra*" (Āś. [refs] [?]).

***avarmaha indra dādṛhi*** — *maho mahato meghasya | karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī | mahāntaṃ jaladhāriṇaṃ megham mahāntaṃ vṛtraṃ vāvaravastrā…[?] avāñcaṃ dādṛhi vidāraya*. Here the word *mahaḥ* is used in the place of *mahataḥ*; the loss of the *t* is by Vedic usage; and the sense of the third case-ending [*sic*, "accusative"?] has to be said by *ṣaṣṭhī-vibhakti*. Therefore, if *mahaḥ* is taken as *mahāntam*, it must be meant: "the great cloud, full of water, or the Asura Vṛtra". Indra is prayed to break such a cloud, or the Asura Vṛtra (with his thunderbolt), headlong, and destroy [him]. The initial syllable of *dādṛhi* is long by Vedic usage in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha.

***śrudhī naḥ*** — *noʼsmadīyaṃ śrudhi śṛṇu*: "O Indra, listen with attention to our word, which is the prayer-wording to be said hereafter", the ṛṣi prays Indra. The final syllable of *śrudhi* is long in the Saṃhitā text, by Vedic usage.

***śuśoca hi dyauḥ kṣā na bhīṣā adrivaḥ*** — the word *adri* is found among the names of cloud and of thunderbolt (Ni. 1-[?], as read "೨-೩೦"); therefore the word *adrivaḥ* means "O Indra, the one who breaks the clouds or the enemies (with the thunderbolt)". O Indra, as the earth, from lack of rain, undergoes harm in the production and nourishment of crops and so on, so also the heaven-world, the support of the gods, is harmed, as the sacrifices and the like of men [do not occur] — [text continues on p. 559].

### Printed p. 559  (PDF 580)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 23 [as read].)*

*(Continuing:)* …through Agni they obtain satisfaction; if there is no rain there is no growth of crops and so on. For lack of such crops (rice, barley and so on) sacrificial acts will not take place in due order, and therefore even the offerings of oblations to the gods do not occur; as, without rain, the earth is subject to suffering, so, from the lack of rain, the heaven-world is anxious and also suffers — this is the chief meaning. Here the commentator explains the words *dyauḥ*, *kṣā*: *dyaur dyuloko devānām āśrayabhūtaḥ* ("the heaven-world, the support of the gods" — i.e. the heaven where the deities live) and *kṣā*: *kṣeti bhūnāma | kṣāyanti nivasanty asyām iti kṣā | sarvanivāsāśrayabhūmiḥ* — that is, the word *kṣā* is found among the twenty-odd names of earth (Ni. 1-[?], as read "೧-೩") hence "earth"; and as it is derived from the root *kṣā* ("to dwell") the earth, where all dwell, gets the name *kṣā*. The ṛṣi explains that "the Asuras, who have grown strong in the two worlds heaven and earth and have become thorns to the worlds, cause obstruction to sacrifices and the like, and heaven and earth, unable to bear it, suffer: [Indra,] listen to this my prayer".

***ghṛṇāt na bhīṣā adrivaḥ*** — here there is an illustration related to heaven and earth being afraid. The commentator gives, as an example, the old itihāsa related in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [as read "೧-೯೫-೧" [?]] —

> हे अद्रिवः शत्रूणां भक्षक । यद्वा । अद्रिर्वज्रः । तेन तद्वन् । हे इन्द्र घृणाद्भीषा न दीप्तादग्नेर्मूर्त्यन्तरात्त्वष्टृभीत्येव । त्वष्टृभीत्या पूर्वं यथा द्यावापृथिव्यौ शोचतस्तद्वत् । अत्रेतिहासमाहुः । पूर्वं जगति महान्धकारेणावृते सति देवा विचिन्त्याग्निं प्रार्थितवन्तः । स च त्वष्टृरूपेण द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां सकाशात्...[sic] उदपद्यत । तं दृष्ट्वा द्यावापृथिव्यौ बिभ्यतुरिति । स चोभे त्वष्टृबिभ्यतुः —

> *he adrivaḥ śatrūṇāṃ bhakṣaka | yadvā | adrirvajraḥ | tena tadvan | he indra ghṛṇādbhīṣā na dīptādagnermūrtyantarāttvaṣṭṛbhītyeva | tvaṣṭṛbhītyā pūrvaṃ yathā dyāvāpṛthivyau śocatastadvat | atretihāsamāhuḥ | pūrvaṃ jagati mahāndhakāreṇāvṛte sati devā vicintyāgniṃ prārthitavantaḥ | sa ca tvaṣṭṛrūpeṇa dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ sakāśāt...[sic] udapadyata | taṃ dṛṣṭvā dyāvāpṛthivyau bibhyaturiti | sa cobhe tvaṣṭṛbibhyatuḥ —*
>
> उभे त्वष्टुर्बिभ्यतुर्जायमानात्प्रतीची सिंहं प्रति जोषयेते ।

> *he adrivaḥ śatrūṇāṃ bhakṣaka | yadvā | adrir vajraḥ | tena tadvan | he indra ghṛṇād bhīṣā na dīptād agner mūrtyantarāt tvaṣṭṛbhītyeva | tvaṣṭṛbhītyā pūrvaṃ yathā dyāvāpṛthivyau śocatas tadvat | atretihāsam āhuḥ | pūrvaṃ jagati mahāndhakāreṇāvṛte sati devā vicintyāgniṃ prārthitavantaḥ | sa ca tvaṣṭṛrūpeṇa dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ sakāśāt… udapadyata | taṃ dṛṣṭvā dyāvāpṛthivyau bibhyatur iti | sa cobhe tvaṣṭṛbibhyatuḥ —*
> *ubhe tvaṣṭur bibhyatur jāyamānāt pratīcī siṃhaṃ prati joṣayete |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೯೫-೨" [?]. The itihāsa passage is partly illegible in the small type; I read it as above with the break marked.) "In former times, when the whole world was covered with darkness (great darkness), all the gods together considered and prayed to Agni to remove this darkness. Then Agni, taking the form of Tvaṣṭṛ [*sic*: Kannada "Tvaṣṭṛ"], arose in the earth and the middle region and, with his blazing flames, made light everywhere. Seeing the terrible form of Agni, burning in that period, heaven and earth trembled in fear" — this is what is said by the Ṛk *ubhe tvaṣṭur bibhyatuḥ*, which the commentator has now cited as an illustration (or, in this connection, [heaven and earth], having seen Agni in the form of Tvaṣṭṛ, [because] of the lack of rain, trembled).

### Printed p. 560  (PDF 581)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 19 Sū. 133" [as read].)*

*(Continuing:)* …"just as they trembled then, they tremble even now, and suffer" — thus the commentator explained the illustrative sentence. Or the word *ghṛṇa* may be taken as meaning only "Agni": that heaven and earth, in fear of such an Agni, trembled and shook, —

> आरेजेतां रोदसी होतृवूर्ये ऽसघ्न्योर्भारमयजो महो वसो ।

> *ārejetāṃ rodasī hotṛvūrye 'saghnyor bhāram ayajo maho vaso |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೩೧-೩" [?]; the Saṃhitā text of this quotation is doubtful in several letters [?].) — thus, as said in this Ṛk, is quoted as an illustration. Therefore, O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, he is prayed to remove the suffering of heaven and earth by striking the clouds and producing rain.

***śuṣmintamo hi śuṣmibhiḥ vadhair ugrebhir īyase*** — the word *śuṣma* is found among the twenty-eight names of strength, *ojaḥ*, *jaḥ* and so on (Ni. 2-[?], as read "೨-೯"); so "*śuṣma*" means "strength". *Śuṣmo 'syāstīti śuṣmī, taiḥ śuṣmibhiḥ*; *atiśayena śuṣmī śuṣmintamaḥ*: he who is strong is *śuṣmī*, and among such strong ones one who has surpassing strength is called *śuṣmintama*. Indra is the strongest of all the strong. "O Indra, such a strong one, you go near the enemies (to destroy them) endowed with all the means of slaying enemies" is the purport.

***apuruṣaghnaḥ*** — *pauruṣopetānāṃ yajanasamarthānām ahananaḥ*: "one who slays men; *apuruṣaghna* — one who does not slay men", that is, one who slays the Rākṣasas but not men fit for sacrifice and so on, who are endowed with manly valour and heroism: this is the purport [sic: "who do not kill the sacrificers" is the sense].

***apratīta*** — *avasanne rakṣaḥprabhṛtibhir apratigate yudhe śatrubhir ākrānte | yadvā | sattvabhiḥ prāṇibhir asaṃskṛtamanaskair anadhigate*: "in battle one not attained by Rākṣasas and the like — enemies — who are to be conquered; or, one not understood by men of unrefined (or little) intelligence, the dull-witted: for the people of ordinary kind do not know the greatness and the power of Indra; only the wise and those who perform sacrifices and good deeds can know the greatness of Indra", is the purport. [Also:] "how could enemies approach him in battle, and still less conquer him?"

***trisaptaiḥ śūra sattvabhiḥ*** — here the commentator gives for *trisaptaiḥ* the meaning *tribhiḥ saptabhir vā*: "by three or by seven". But the meaning "twenty-one times", *trisaptaiḥ* ("three times seven") fits better, and the meaning is more suited than either [three or seven]. On this point Wilson says —
