**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Ṛk 8; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].)*

> हे इन्द्रवायू अत्राह अस्मिन्नेव यज्ञे । अहेति निग्रहार्थीयः ॥ [?] मध्वो मधुरस्य मधुसदृशस्य वा तत् तस्याहुतिं प्रदेयद्रव्यं वहेथे । धारयतम् । यं सोममश्वत्थं पर्वतादिव्याप्तिप्रदेशे स्थितं जायवो जेतारो यजमाना उपतिष्ठन्त उपेत्य तिष्ठन्ति क्रयार्थम् । किंचास्मे अस्माकं संबन्धिनो जायवो जेतारः कर्मनिर्वाहितारस्ते ऋत्विजः सन्तु । समर्था भवन्तु । यज्ञं निर्वहन्तित्यर्थः । यद्वा । ते प्रसिद्धाः प्रयोगकुशला जायवो जेतार ऋत्विजोऽस्मे सन्तु नान्यस्य । अत्र वहेथ इत्यत्कृतं कोऽत्र निशेष इति तत्राह । हे इन्द्रवायू अस्मिन्यज्ञे गावो धेनवः साकं सह्यैव सुवते । युष्मदर्थमेव क्षीरमुत्पादयन्ति । दोग्ध्र्यो भवन्तीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । गावः साकं सह्यैव सुवते । आपत्यमुत्पादयन्ति त्वद्दोग्धॄणामर्थम् ॥ आदादिकः । जोत्तात्पास्यानुदात्तेदिति लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ॥ किंच यवः । जातावेकवचनम् । उपलक्षणमेतत् । यवादिभिः पुरोडाशादिकं पच्यते इत्यर्थः । किंच हे वायो इन्द्र च यतो गाव एवं सुवते अतस्ते त्वदर्था धेनवो नोप दस्यन्ति । नोपक्षीणा भवन्ति । रोगादिना कृशा न भवन्ति । न केवलमुपक्षीणाः । किंतु धेनवो युष्मत्प्रीणयित्र्यो गावो नाप दस्यन्ति । चौर्याद्युपहार्यैरुपक्षीणा नष्टा न भवन्ति ॥

> *he indravāyū atrāha asminneva yajñe | aheti nigrahārthīyaḥ ‖ [?] madhvo madhurasya madhusadṛśasya vā tat tasyāhutiṃ pradeyadravyaṃ vahethe | dhārayatam | yaṃ somamaśvatthaṃ parvatādivyāptipradeśe sthitaṃ jāyavo jetāro yajamānā upatiṣṭhanta upetya tiṣṭhanti krayārtham | kiṃcāsme asmākaṃ saṃbandhino jāyavo jetāraḥ karmanirvāhitāraste ṛtvijaḥ santu | samarthā bhavantu | yajñaṃ nirvahantityarthaḥ | yadvā | te prasiddhāḥ prayogakuśalā jāyavo jetāra ṛtvijo 'sme santu nānyasya | atra vahetha ityatkṛtaṃ ko 'tra niśeṣa iti tatrāha | he indravāyū asminyajñe gāvo dhenavaḥ sākaṃ sahyaiva suvate | yuṣmadarthameva kṣīramutpādayanti | dogdhryo bhavantītyarthaḥ | yadvā | gāvaḥ sākaṃ sahyaiva suvate | āpatyamutpādayanti tvaddogdhṝṇāmartham ‖ ādādikaḥ | jottātpāsyānudāttediti lasārvadhātukānudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ ‖ kiṃca yavaḥ | jātāvekavacanam | upalakṣaṇametat | yavādibhiḥ puroḍāśādikaṃ pacyate ityarthaḥ | kiṃca he vāyo indra ca yato gāva evaṃ suvate ataste tvadarthā dhenavo nopa dasyanti | nopakṣīṇā bhavanti | rogādinā kṛśā na bhavanti | na kevalamupakṣīṇāḥ | kiṃtu dhenavo yuṣmatprīṇayitryo gāvo nāpa dasyanti | cauryādyupahāryairupakṣīṇā naṣṭā na bhavanti ‖*

*(Sense: "O Indra and Vāyu, here — in this very sacrifice — *aha* [the particle of emphasis]: that *āhuti* — the thing to be offered — of the *madhu* (sweet, or sweet-like) you bear (*vahethe*, you take up), the Soma, the *aśvattha* [a kind of fig-tree — i.e. the Soma-plant growing on mountains and the like [?]], which the *jāyavaḥ* — the victors, the sacrificers — approach (*upatiṣṭhanta*) to buy [?]. Further, for us (*asme*) may those *jāyavaḥ* — victors, sacrifice-accomplishers — the priests, be: let them be capable; they carry out the sacrifice; or, the well-known skilful priests, the victors, be for us and for no one else. Now, "*vahethe*" here — what is special? He says: O Indra and Vāyu, in this sacrifice the cows, the *dhenus*, *sākaṃ suvate* — together bring forth, produce milk only for you; they become milkers [i.e. yield milk] — or the cows together bear offspring for the milkers who serve you. [*suvate* is of the *adādi* class: *jottāt pāsyānudātted* — by the rule that the *lasārvadhātuka* is *anudātta*, the root's accent.] Further *yavaḥ* — barley, generic singular, indicating grains: *puroḍāśa* etc. are cooked with barley and so on. And further, O Vāyu and Indra, since the cows so bear, those cows of yours do not *upadasyanti* — are not wasted: not become emaciated by disease and the like; and not merely not wasted — the *dhenus*, cows pleasing you, *nāpa dasyanti* — are not lost by theft and the like, [by] things to be borne away, nor destroyed." The grammatical remarks are only partly legible [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *(he indravāyū)* — O Indra and Vāyu; *(yuvām)* — you two; *atra aha* — in this very sacrificial hall; *madhvaḥ* — sweet; *tat* — that (Soma-juice); *āhutim* — the offering; *vahethe* — accept; *yam aśvattham* — [the Soma] which, standing on the mountain and the like; *jāyavaḥ* — the victorious sacrificers; *upatiṣṭhanta* — approach [to obtain]; *(kiṃca — and)*; *asme* — [for] us; *jāyavaḥ* — capable ones (accomplishers of the work); *te* — those priests; *santu* — let them be (capable) [or: *jāyavaḥ* — capable; *te* — those priests; *asme* — for us; *santu* — let them be];

### Printed p. 648  (PDF 669)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 135" [as read].)*

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 8, concluded:)* *santu* — let them be [capable of carrying out the rites for us]; *(he indravāyū)* — O Indra and Vāyu; *iha* — in this sacrifice; *gāvaḥ* — the cows; *sākam* — (together for you); *suvate* — (to give milk for you) produce [or: *gāvaḥ* — cows; *sākam* — together; *suvate* — to give you milk, they produce]; *(kiṃca)* — and; *iha* — and here; *yavaḥ* — the barley and the like; *pacyate* — is cooked (for *puroḍāśa* and the like); *he vāyo (indra ca)* — O Vāyu and Indra; *te* — those of you, who are intended for you; *dhenavaḥ* — the cows; *na upa dasyanti* — are not wasted (by disease and the like); *(and)* *dhenavaḥ* — those cows that are pleasing to you; *na apa dasyanti* — are not carried away (by thieves and the like).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** The victorious sacrificers stand round the *aśvattha* tree; O Indra and Vāyu, both of you accept the offering of the sweet Soma-juice in such a sacrificial hall; may the priests be capable of carrying out the sacrifice for us; here the cows give birth [yield milk] at one time, to give you milk; barley is cooked for you; these cows, which are devoted to you, are not wasted by disease and the like; and are not stolen by thieves and the like.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Then, accept the libations of the sweet juice at the sacrifice in which the triumphant priests stand round the rock-born (plant): may they ever be victorious for us: (for you) together the cows distil (their milk); the (offering of) barley is dressed; and never for you, (Vayu), will the cows grow meagre; never will the cows be carried off (by thieves)."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 8).**

***jāyavaḥ aśvatthaṃ yam upatiṣṭhante*** — "the victorious sacrificers surround the Soma, as they stand at the *aśvattha*": here Sāyaṇa has not given a proper explanation of the word *aśvattha*. His explanation, *parvatādivyāptipradeśe sthitam*, "which stands in the mountain and the like, in a pervading place", is not clear. It would not be wrong to say simply "the *aśvattha* tree". Probably, as the Soma-creeper grows resting on the *aśvattha* tree, this identity may be told. In this context the meaning may be either the *aśvattha* tree, or the vessel made from that tree. Then the relation of cause and effect between victory and the Soma-juice that is in the *aśvattha* is clear.

> अथ यदाश्वत्थानि तेजसो वा एष वनस्पतिरजायत यदश्वत्थः साम्राज्यं वा एतद्वनस्पतीनां तेज एवास्मिन् [?] तत्साम्राज्यं च वनस्पतीनां क्षत्रे दधाति ।

> *atha yad āśvatthāni tejaso vā eṣa vanaspatir ajāyata yad aśvatthaḥ sāmrājyaṃ vā etad vanaspatīnāṃ teja evāsmin [?] tat sāmrājyaṃ ca vanaspatīnāṃ kṣatre dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-[?], as read "೭-೩೧" [?]; read from the image, doubtful in the middle [?].) "The *aśvattha* arose from [the *tejas* — splendour]; it is the sovereign of the trees": it is the chief of all trees, and is the basis of the *kṣatriya* energy.

### Printed p. 649  (PDF 670)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24–25 [as read].)*

> एतान्यस्य पुरस्तादुपकल्प्यानि भवन्त्यथ सोमं राजानं क्रीणन्ति ।

> *etāny asya purastād upakalpyāni bhavanty atha somaṃ rājānaṃ krīṇanti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-[?], as read "೭-೩೧" [?].) "When the parts of the *aśvattha* etc. [for the vessel] have been made ready, then the adhvaryu buys the Soma from the *kṣatriya*", is explained in this way: the *kṣatriya* energy and the *aśvattha* are connected. And also:

> ब्रह्मलोके तृतीयस्यामितो दिवि तद्यैरं मदीयं सरस्तदश्वत्थः सोमसवनस्तदपराजिता पूर्ब्रह्मणः प्रभुविमितं हिरण्मयम् ।

> *brahmaloke tṛtīyasyām ito divi tad airaṃ madīyaṃ saras tad aśvatthaḥ somasavanas tad aparājitā pūr brahmaṇaḥ prabhuvimitaṃ hiraṇmayam |*

(Chāndogya Upaniṣad 8-[?]-[?], as read "೮-೫-೩" [?]; this small-type Sanskrit is read from the image and is doubtful throughout [?].) In the *brahmaloka*, an *aśvattha* tree that gives Soma-juice is described in the Chāndogya and other Upaniṣads. Therefore, it appears that the meaning here may be: "the Soma-creepers' juices, which resort to the *aśvattha* trees well known on the mountains and so on". The sacrificer, who desires victory, must press this Soma-juice, perform the sacrifice, and himself drink the juice also.

***jāyavaḥ*** — the word is repeated. For the first, "the sacrificers who desire victory"; for the second, "the priests who have the strength to carry out the sacrifice and to gain victory": it is explained.

***sākaṃ gāvaḥ suvate*** — by the praises of this kind, Indra and Vāyu are shown to be the protectors of cows: [it is said] that, by their protection, cows give milk and the like in abundance, freed from disease, and live well.

> यदाह नियुद्भिर्वायविह ता विमुञ्चेति पशवो वै नियुतस्तत्पशुभिरेवैतत्स्वात्राणि [?] विमुञ्चन्ते ।

> *yad āha niyudbhir vāyav iha tā vimuñceti paśavo vai niyutas tat paśubhir evaitat svātrāṇi [?] vimuñcante |*

(Śa. Brā. 4-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೪-೪-೧-೧೭" [?]; read from the image, partly doubtful [?].) In such sentences, the *niyut*s that are always connected with Vāyu are said to be animals (*paśu*), and Vāyu is said to be the protector and lord of all animals.

> दोहाशं सख्यं तव गौरसि वीर गव्यते । अश्वो अश्वायते भव ॥

> *dohāśaṃ [?] sakhyaṃ tava gaur asi vīra gavyate | aśvo aśvāyate bhava ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೪೫-೩೩" [?]; the first word is doubtful [?].) "For the sacrificer who wants a cow, Indra becomes a cow; for him who wants a horse, he is the horse, and helps him": thus described, one may expect to get wealth of cattle protected by the help of Indra and Vāyu.

### Printed p. 650  (PDF 671)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 135" [as read].)*

***indravāyustavopasaṃhāraḥ*** *(Kannada heading: "ಇಂದ್ರವಾಯುಸ್ತವದ ಉಪಸಂಹಾರ" — "Conclusion of the praise of Indra and Vāyu").*

In this Sūkta, Indra and Vāyu are together invoked to accept the offering of Soma-juice. In this context the matters of the carrying of Soma, the pressing of the juice, the placing of the juice, as prescribed in the Śāstra, in the proper vessels, and the offering as oblation have been described in due course. In making ready and offering the Soma-juice, three portions are made, called the *upāṃśugraha*, *antaryāmagraha* and *aindravāyavagraha*. The *upāṃśu*-pressing is the earlier part of the *mahābhiṣava*; with this the Soma-juice is placed in the *upāṃśugraha*. The juice pressed by the *adhvaryu*, the *pratiprasthātṛ* and the *unnetṛ* is poured into the *ādhavanīya* vessel; mixed with the water there, it is then poured through the *daśāpavitra* into the vessel called *pūtabhṛt*: this was explained before. In the present [Sūkta], the power and greatness of the *upāṃśugraha*, *antaryāmagraha* and *aindravāyavagraha* may be understood. In the sentence *adribhiḥ sutānām* of the first Ṛk [as printed: "೧-೧೩೫" [?]], the order in which the juice is pressed, by the rule *upāṃśusavana*, is shown; this order is described in seven parts. [The Taittirīya Saṃhitā 6-4-1 [as read, [?]], where their power and greatness are stated in the sentences of Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-4 to 6-4-6 [?], is to be understood here at length.]

1. By the mantra *ā dade grāvāsy adhvarakṛt* (Tai. Saṃ. 1-4-1 [as read]) when the *grāvan* is taken the divine power enters the priest — this explanation is given in the Āraṇeya section at length.

> देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इति ग्राणावनादत्ते प्रसूत्या अश्विनोर्बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यामित्याहाश्विनौ हि देवानामध्वर्यू आस्तां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यामित्याह यत्यै ॥

> *devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti grāvāṇam ādatte prasūtyā aśvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām ity āhāśvinau hi devānām adhvaryū āstāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām ity āha yatyai ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-1-[?], as read "೬-೪-೧-೧" [?]; the words *grāṇāvana* and *yatyai* are as printed [?].) The Aśvins were the *adhvaryus* of the gods; therefore, by the help of the arms of the Aśvins, and for support, by the help of Pūṣan, saying "at the impulse of Savitṛ", the *adhvaryu* takes the *grāvan* in his hand.

2. By the mantra *indrāya tvā* the Soma is sprinkled [as read: "is made wet"].

> पशवो वै सोमो व्यान उपांशुसवनो यदुपांशुसवनमभिमिमीते व्यानमेव पशुषु दधाति इन्द्राय त्वेन्द्राय त्वेति मिमीत इन्द्राय हि सोम आ ह्रियते पञ्चकृत्वो यजुषा मिमीते पञ्चाक्षरा पङ्क्तिः पाङ्क्तो यज्ञो यज्ञमेवावरुन्धे पञ्चकृत्वस्तूष्णीं दश संपद्यन्ते दशाक्षरा विराडन्नं विराड् विराजैवान्नाद्यमवरुन्धे ।

> *paśavo vai somo vyāna upāṃśusavano yad upāṃśusavanam abhimimīte vyānam eva paśuṣu dadhāti indrāya tvendrāya tveti mimīta indrāya hi soma ā hriyate pañcakṛtvo yajuṣā mimīte pañcākṣarā paṅktiḥ pāṅkto yajño yajñam evāvarundhe pañcakṛtvas tūṣṇīṃ daśa saṃpadyante daśākṣarā virāḍ annaṃ virāḍ virājaivānnādyam avarundhe |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-1-[?], as read "೬-೪-೧-೨" [?]; read from the image; doubtful in details [?].) Soma is animal (*paśu*); the *upāṃśu* pressing is *vyāna* [the breath that pervades]. By beating and offering [Soma] he gives *vyāna* to the animals. As Soma is offered to Indra, he beats it five times with the mantra *indrāya tvā*; five-syllabled is the *paṅkti*; the sacrifice is *pāṅkta*; thus he obtains the sacrifice. Further, [he does] five times silently; in all, ten is the number; the *virāj* has ten syllables; *virāj* is food; with the *virāj* he gets food.

### Printed p. 651  (PDF 672)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24–25 [as read].)*

*(Continuing the Kannada explanation of p. 650:)* …Soma is the animal; the *upāṃśu*-pressing is *vyāna*. By it he gives the animals *vyāna*. Because Soma is offered to Indra, he pours it five times, reciting the mantra *indrāya tvā* ("for Indra, you"); as the five-syllabled [verse] is *paṅkti* and the sacrifice is *pāṅkta*, he gets the power of the sacrifice. And by being silent [five times] the measure increases to ten. The ten-syllabled *virāj* is food; by the *virāj* he gets food.

3. By the mantra *śvātrāḥ stha vṛtraturaḥ* ("you are the strong ones, the conquerors of Vṛtra") he sprinkles water.

> श्वात्राः स्थ वृत्रतुर इत्याहैष वा अपां सोमपीथो य एवं वेदं नाप्सु [?] आर्तिमार्च्छति ॥

> *śvātrāḥ stha vṛtratura ity āhaiṣa vā apāṃ somapītho ya evaṃ veda nāpsv ārtim ārcchati ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-1-[?], as read "೬-೪-೧-೩" [?].) This is the Soma-drinking of the waters; he who knows this does not meet with destruction in [water].

4. By the mantra *yat te soma divi jyotiḥ* he mixes the Soma with water.

> यत्ते सोम दिवि ज्योतिरित्याहेभ्य एवैनं लोकेभ्यः सं भरति ।

> *yat te soma divi jyotir ity āhebhya evainaṃ lokebhyaḥ saṃ bharati |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-1-[?], as read "೬-೪-೧-೩" [?].) Reciting "*antarikṣasthena tava tejasā*" [as read, doubtful [?]] he sprinkles the Soma.

5. By the mantra *dhiṣaṇe vīḍū satī* he touches the boards.

6. *prāg apāk* — this is the *nigrāha* rule; it has been explained before.

> सोमो वै राजा दिशोऽभ्यध्यायत्स दिशोऽनु प्राविशत्प्रागपागुदगधराक्त्वेत्याह दिग्भ्य एवैनं संभरत्यथो दिश एवास्मा अव रुन्धेऽम्ब निष्वरेत्याह कामुका एनं स्त्रियो भवन्ति य एवं वेद ॥

> *somo vai rājā diśo 'bhyadhyāyat sa diśo 'nu prāviśat prāg apāg udag adharāktvety āha digbhya evainaṃ saṃbharaty atho diśa evāsmā ava rundhe 'mba niṣvarety āha kāmukā enaṃ striyo bhavanti ya evaṃ veda ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-1-[?], as read "೬-೪-೧-೩" [?]; doubtful in places [?].) "King Soma reflected on the directions and entered the directions": reciting "*prāg apāg udag adharāk tvā*" ["from east, west, north, south"], he [the adhvaryu] gets Soma from the directions; "*amba niṣvara*" ("Mother, come out") — by this mantra, women become desirous of him who knows this secret.

7. By the mantra *yat te somādābhyaṃ nāma jāgṛvi* the *pratiprasthātṛ* takes up the Soma-stalks.

> यत्ते सोमादाभ्यं नाम जागृवीत्याहैष वै सोमस्य सोमपथो य एवं वेद न सौम्यामार्तिमार्च्छति नार्ध्नोति घ्नन्ति वा एतत्सोमं यदभिषुण्वन्ति सꣳ शूनस्य ग्रहाति त्रायत एवैनं प्राणा वा आꣳशवः पशवः सोमः ।

> *yat te somādābhyaṃ nāma jāgṛvīty āhaiṣa vai somasya somapatho ya evaṃ veda na saumyām ārtim ārcchati nārdhnoti ghnanti vā etat somaṃ yad abhiṣuṇvanti saṃ śūnasya gṛhṇāti trāyata evainaṃ prāṇā vā āṃśavaḥ paśavaḥ somaḥ |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-1-[?], as read "೬-೪-೧-೪" [?]; the last part is doubtful [?].)

### Printed p. 652  (PDF 673)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 135" [as read].)*

*(Quotation 7 of p. 651, concluded; the end of the Sanskrit lines is poorly printed and I read it only in part [?]:)* …*śūnasya gṛhṇāti trāyata evainaṃ prāṇā vā aṃśavaḥ paśavaḥ somaḥ* … *kūśūnam api sṛjati prāṇān eva paśuṣu dadhāti dvidhā vyāvasi sṛjati tasmād dvau prāṇāḥ* [?]. (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-1-[?] [?].)

"*yat te somādābhyaṃ nāma jāgṛvi*" — by this mantra (which is free of delusion and of the nature of waking, and is of Soma) the *pratiprasthātṛ* takes the Soma-stalks, belonging to the Soma-king. He who knows this secret does not meet with ruin from Soma; if they press [the Soma], that is as if they kill it. He [the *pratiprasthātṛ*] places the Soma-stalks aside; therefore he protects it. The Soma-stalks are the breaths (*prāṇa*); Soma is the animals. By holding the stalks he gives breath to the animals. By taking the stalks in two ways, the principal breaths are in two forms.

***upāṃśugrahasya mahimā*** *(Kannada heading "ಉಪಾಂಶುಗ್ರಹದ ಮಹಿಮೆ" — "The greatness of the *upāṃśugraha*").* After describing the nature of the *upāṃśu*-pressing as above, the greatness of the *upāṃśugraha* is praised (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-[?], as read "೬-೪-೩" [?]); the rest of this is the sixth [section] of the Saṃhitā.

1. By the mantra *vācaspataye pavasva vājin* the juice is poured into the vessel.

> प्राणो वा एष यदुपांशुर्यदुपांशुग्रहो गृह्यते प्राणमेवानु प्रयन्ति कृष्ण [?] … । उपांशुपात्रेण सवनं विवाहं यज्ञꣳ संस्थापयामि तेन तत्र संस्थितेन चरामीत्येष्टः [?] कृत्वोऽग्रे [?] अभिपुनीत्यष्टाक्षरा गायत्री गायत्रं प्रातःसवनं प्रातःसवनमेव तेनाप्नोत्येकादशकृत्वो द्वितीयमेकादशाक्षरा त्रिष्टुप् त्रैष्टुभं माध्यंदिनꣳ सवनं माध्यंदिनमेव सवनं तेनाप्नोति द्वादशकृत्वस्तृतीयं द्वादशाक्षरा जगती जागतं तृतीयसवनं तृतीयसवनमेव तेनाप्नोत्येता वा ह वा स यज्ञस्य संस्थितिमुवाचास्कन्दायास्कन्नꣳ हि तद्यज्ञस्य संस्थितस्यास्कन्दति ॥

> *prāṇo vā eṣa yad upāṃśur yad upāṃśugraho gṛhyate prāṇam evānu prayanti kṛṣṇa [?] … | upāṃśupātreṇa savanaṃ vivāhaṃ yajñaṃ saṃsthāpayāmi tena tatra saṃsthitena carāmīty eṣṭaḥ [?] kṛtvo 'gre [?] abhipunīty aṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī gāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ prātaḥsavanam eva tenāpnoty ekādaśakṛtvo dvitīyam ekādaśākṣarā triṣṭup traiṣṭubhaṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ mādhyaṃdinam eva savanaṃ tenāpnoti dvādaśakṛtvas tṛtīyaṃ dvādaśākṣarā jagatī jāgataṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ tṛtīyasavanam eva tenāpnoty etā vā ha vā sa yajñasya saṃsthitim uvācāskandāyāskannaṃ hi tad yajñasya saṃsthitasyāskandati ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೪-೩-೨" [?]; this small-type passage is read from the image and is badly doubtful in the opening and closing portions [?]; only the sense is reliable.) *Sense, from the Kannada:* The *upāṃśu* is the breath of the sacrifice. Taking up the *upāṃśugraha* follows the breath at the beginning. "At the morning pressing I accomplish the sacrifice": he pours it eight times; the *gāyatrī* has eight syllables; the morning pressing belongs to the *gāyatrī*; therefore he who pours eight times accomplishes the morning pressing. At the midday pressing he pours eleven times; the *triṣṭubh* has eleven syllables; the midday pressing belongs to the *triṣṭubh*. At the evening pressing he pours twelve times; the *jagatī* has twelve syllables; the evening pressing belongs to the *jagatī*. By this the third pressing is obtained. This is called the establishment of the sacrifice; by it, any damage that might arise is avoided.

### Printed p. 653  (PDF 674)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24–25 [as read].)*

> अथो खल्वाहुर्गायत्री वाव प्रातःसवने नातिवादोऽत्र रक्षꣳसि [?] नैनं भ्रातृव्यो भवति य एवं वेद तस्मादेष्टव्येष्टव्यः कृत्वो [?] ऽभिपुनात्यथ [?] ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति पवित्रवन्तोऽन्ये ग्रहा गृह्यन्ते किं पवित्र उपांशुरिति वाक्पवित्र इति ब्रूयाद्वाचस्पतये पवस्व वाजिन्नित्याह वाचैवैनं पवयति ॥

> *atho khalv āhur gāyatrī vāva prātaḥsavane nātivādo 'tra rakṣaṃsi [?] nainaṃ bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda tasmād eṣṭavyeṣṭavyaḥ kṛtvo [?] 'bhipunāty atha [?] brahmavādino vadanti pavitravanto 'nye grahā gṛhyante kiṃ pavitra upāṃśur iti vākpavitra iti brūyād vācaspataye pavasva vājinn ity āha vācaivainaṃ pavayati ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೪-೩-೩, ೩" [?]; read from the image; several words doubtful [?].) At the morning pressing [the question is whether the *gāyatrī* is exceeded]; there is no excessive speech there. He who knows this has no enemy for himself. Therefore the rule is that [the cup] be taken [in this way] so many times; and when the *brahmavādins* ask: "the other cups are purified with the *pavitra* (the strainer of ten fringes); what is the strainer for the *upāṃśu*?", [the answer is], "speech is the purifier; he purifies it with speech: *vācaspataye pavasva vājin*." The mantra itself is the purifier.

> वृष्णो अꣳशुभ्यामित्याह वृष्णो ह्येतावꣳशू यौ सोमस्य गभस्तिपूत इत्याह गभस्तिना ह्येनं पवयति देवो देवानां पवित्रमसीत्याह देवो ह्येष सन्देवानां पवित्रं येषां भागोऽसि तेभ्यस्त्वेत्याह येभ्यो ह्येष भागस्तेभ्य एनं गृह्णाति ।

> *vṛṣṇo aṃśubhyām ity āha vṛṣṇo hy etāv aṃśū yau somasya gabhastipūta ity āha gabhastinā hy enaṃ pavayati devo devānāṃ pavitram asīty āha devo hy eṣa san devānāṃ pavitraṃ yeṣāṃ bhāgo 'si tebhyas tvety āha yebhyo hy eṣa bhāgas tebhya enaṃ gṛhṇāti |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೪-೩-೩, ೪" [?].) By such sentences the self-purity of the Soma-stalk is explained.

2. By the mantra *svāṃ kṛto 'si* the vessel is rinsed and purified.

> स्वांकृतोऽसीत्याह प्राणमेव स्वमकृत मधुमतीर्न इषस्कृधीत्याह सर्वमेवास्मा इदꣳ स्वदयति विश्वेभ्यस्त्वेन्द्रियेभ्यो दिव्येभ्यः पार्थिवेभ्य इत्याहोभयेष्वेव देवमनुष्येषु प्राणान्दधाति ॥

> *svāṃkṛto 'sīty āha prāṇam eva svam akṛta madhumatīr na iṣas kṛdhīty āha sarvam evāsmā idaṃ svadayati viśvebhyas tvendriyebhyo divyebhyaḥ pārthivebhya ity āhobhayeṣv eva devamanuṣyeṣu prāṇān dadhāti ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೪-೩-೪" [?].) Saying "*you are made our own*" he makes the breath his own; praying "make our food sweet" he makes all this sweet for him; saying "for all your powers, heavenly and earthly" he places breaths among both gods and men.

3. By mantras such as *manas tvāṣṭūrvantarikṣam anviha svāhā*, the adhvaryu goes to the *āhavanīya* fire and offers the juice in the vessel to the fire.

### Printed p. 654  (PDF 675)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 135" [as read].)*

> मनस्त्वाष्ट्वित्याह मन एवाप्नोत्युरु अन्तरिक्षमन्विहीत्याहान्तरिक्षदेवत्यो [?] हि प्राणः स्वाहा त्वा सुभवः सूर्यायेत्याह प्राणा वै सुभवसो देवास्तेष्वेव परोक्षं जुहोति देवेभ्यस्त्वा मरीचिपेभ्य इत्याहादित्यस्य वै रश्मयो देवा मरीचिपास्तेषां तद्भागधेयं तानेव केन प्रीणाति ।

> *manas tvāṣṭv ity āha mana evāpnoty uru antarikṣam anvihīty āhāntarikṣadevatyo [?] hi prāṇaḥ svāhā tvā subhavaḥ sūryāyety āha prāṇā vai subhavaso devās teṣv eva parokṣaṃ juhoti devebhyas tvā marīcipebhya ity āhādityasya vai raśmayo devā marīcipās teṣāṃ tad bhāgadheyaṃ tān eva kena prīṇāti |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-3-[?], as read "೬-೪-೩-೩" [?]; read from the image, doubtful in places [?].) *Kannada sense:* "May the mind pervade you" — saying this, he gains the mind himself. Since the breath belongs to the *antarikṣa*-deity, he says "go along the *antarikṣa*". "You, well-born, offered to Sūrya" — by this a *homa* is made indirectly [*parokṣa*]. Saying "*prāṇebhyaḥ svāhā*" he leaves the *prāṇa*s — the breaths — since the deities seated in the body are themselves directly [*pratyakṣa*] the objects of the *homa*; so he makes the *homa* to Sūrya, indirectly: "*sūryāya tvā*". Then the rays of the Sun are the breaths; those conscious rays, satisfied, protect the unconscious *marīci*s.

> यदि कामयेत वर्षुकः पर्जन्यः स्यादिति नीचा हस्तेन नि मृज्याद्वृष्टिमेव नि यच्छति यदि कामयेतावर्षुकः स्यादित्युत्ताानेन नि मृज्याद्वृष्टिमेवोद्यच्छति ।

> *yadi kāmayeta varṣukaḥ parjanyaḥ syād iti nīcā hastena ni mṛjyād vṛṣṭim eva ni yacchati yadi kāmayetāvarṣukaḥ syād ity uttānena ni mṛjyād vṛṣṭim evod yacchati |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-3-[?], as read "೬-೪-೩-೩" [?].) If the sacrificer desires that Parjanya may rain, with the hand downward he wipes the vessel [i.e. holds it face down]; then rain falls. If he desires that it should not rain, with the hand upward he wipes it; then there is no rain.

> यद्यभिचरेदमुं जहि [?] त्वा होष्यामीति ब्रूयादाहुतिमेवैनं प्रेप्सन्तं हन्ति यदि दूरे स्यादा तमितोऽस्तीत्येव [?] प्राणमेवास्यानुगत्क [?] पन्ति ।

> *yady abhicaredam umaṃ jahi [?] tvā hoṣyāmīti brūyād āhutim evainaṃ prepsantaṃ hanti yadi dūre syād ā tam ito 'stīty eva [?] prāṇam evāsyānugatka [?] panti |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-3-[?], as read "೬-೪-೩-೩" [?]; this sentence is read with doubt in several words [?].) If a [rite of] *abhicāra* is performed, [the sacrificer] says "kill so-and-so, [and] I will offer to you"; then the deity, desirous of the *āhuti*, harms that enemy.

4. By the mantra *eṣa te yoniḥ prāṇāya tvā* the remainder is poured into the *agrayaṇa* vessel, and a stalk is put into the empty vessel.

> षड्भिरꣳशुभिः पवयति षड्वा ऋतव ऋतुभिरेवैनं पवयति ।

> *ṣaḍbhir aṃśubhiḥ pavayati ṣaḍ vā ṛtava ṛtubhir evainaṃ pavayati |*

"He purifies the Soma with six stalks": there are six seasons; by the seasons he purifies it.

### Printed p. 655  (PDF 676)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24–25 [as read].)*

> त्रिः पवयति त्रय इमे लोका एभिरेवैनं लोकैः पवयति ।

> *triḥ pavayati traya ime lokā ebhir evainaṃ lokaiḥ pavayati |*

"He purifies three times; there are these three worlds; with these worlds he purifies it." Since the number of the worlds is three, he purifies the Soma-juice three times, that is, with two stalks each time.

> ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति कस्मात्सत्यात्त्रयः पशूनाꣳ हस्तादानाः इति यत्त्रिरूपाꣳशुग्रहꣳ हस्तेन वि गृह्णाति तस्मात्त्रयः पशूनाꣳ हस्तादानाः पुरुषो हस्ती मर्कटः ।

> *brahmavādino vadanti kasmāt satyāt trayaḥ paśūnāṃ hastādānāḥ iti yat trir upāṃśugrahaṃ hastena vi gṛhṇāti tasmāt trayaḥ paśūnāṃ hastādānāḥ puruṣo hastī markaṭaḥ |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-3-[?], as read "೬-೪-೩-೬" [?]; read from the image, doubtful in the first words [?].) "Why do three kinds of animals take with the hand?" — so the *brahmavādins* ask; the answer: "Because the *upāṃśugraha* is taken with the hand three times, [so too] man, the elephant and the monkey take [everything] with their hands" (the cow, the buffalo and the like take with the mouth).

The *upāṃśugraha*'s use is summed up by Sāyaṇa in verses:

> वाचोऽह्युपांशुग्रहणं स्वामादत्त्रेऽन्यहस्ततः ।
> उरु गत्वा मनस्त्वेति वेदेर्दक्षिणतः स्थितिः ॥
> स्वाहा जुहोति देवेभ्यो मध्यमे परिधौ तथा ।
> लेपं निमार्ष्टि एषः पात्रं सादयेत्सप्त वर्णिताः ॥

> *vāco 'hy upāṃśugrahaṇaṃ svām ādattre 'nyahastataḥ |*
> *uru gatvā manas tveti veder dakṣiṇataḥ sthitiḥ ‖*
> *svāhā juhoti devebhyo madhyame paridhau tathā |*
> *lepaṃ nimārṣṭy eṣa pātraṃ sādayet sapta varṇitāḥ ‖*

(Read from the image; these two verses are doubtful in several words [?].) With such verses he gives the summary of the *viniyoga* of the *upāṃśugraha*.

***antaryāmagrahasya mahimā*** *(Kannada heading "ಅಂತರ್ಯಾಮಗ್ರಹದ ಮಹಿಮೆಯು" — "The greatness of the *antaryāmagraha*").*

By the mantra *upayāmagṛhīto 'si*, after the rise of the Sun, the *antaryāmagraha* also is to be carried out in the same way as the *upāṃśugraha*: this was told before. The description of this vessel is given in the sixth Kāṇḍa (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-[?], as read "೬-೪-೬" [?]).

> देवा वै यद्यज्ञेऽकुर्वत तदसुरा अकुर्वत ते देवा उपांशौ यज्ञꣳ संस्थाप्यमपश्यन्नुपांशौ समस्थापयन्तेऽसुरा वज्रमुद्यत्य देवान्भ्यायन्त ते देवा बिभ्यत इन्द्रमुपाधावन्नान्तरेन्द्रो ऽन्तर्यामेणान्तरधत्त तदन्तर्यामस्यान्तर्यामत्वं यदन्तर्यामो गृह्यते भ्रातृव्यानेव तद्यजमानोऽन्तर्धत्ते ॥

> *devā vai yad yajñe 'kurvata tad asurā akurvata te devā upāṃśau yajñaṃ saṃsthāpyam apaśyan upāṃśau samasthāpayan te 'surā vajram udyatya devān abhyāyanta te devā bibhyata indram upādhāvann āntarendro 'ntaryāmeṇāntar adhatta tad antaryāmasyāntaryāmatvaṃ yad antaryāmo gṛhyate bhrātṛvyān eva tad yajamāno 'ntardhatte ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-6-1 [as read]; read from the image, doubtful in a few words [?].) *Kannada sense:* Whatever the gods did in the sacrifice, the Asuras did also; the gods saw that the sacrifice could be established in the *upāṃśu* [cup] and established it so, and then the Asuras, taking up the thunderbolt, advanced against the gods. The gods, afraid, approached Indra [who] with the *antaryāma* put them [the Asuras] in between [?]. Hence *antaryāma* is so called: when the *antaryāmagraha* is taken the sacrificer shuts out the enemies.

### Printed p. 656  (PDF 677)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 135" [as read].)*

*(Antaryāmagraha, continued from p. 655:)* …The gods fled to Indra. Indra stopped them [the Asuras] by the help of the *antaryāmagraha*. Therefore this cup became famous by the name *antaryāmagraha*; with its help the sacrificer is able to ward off enemies.

> अन्तस्ते दधामि द्यावापृथिवी अन्तरुर्वन्तरिक्षमित्याहैभिरेव लोकैर्यजमानो भ्रातृव्यानन्तर्धत्ते ।

> *antas te dadhāmi dyāvāpṛthivī antar urv antarikṣam ity āhaibhir eva lokair yajamāno bhrātṛvyān antardhatte |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-6-[?], as read "೬-೪-೬-೨" [?].) "I place heaven and earth and the wide *antarikṣa* within you" — thus he says; by the help of these worlds the sacrificer shuts out his enemy.

> ते देवा अमन्यन्तेन्द्रो वा इदमभूद्यद्वयꣳ स्म इति ते [?] ऽब्रुवन्मघवन्नन्नो न आ भजेति सजोषा देवैरवरैः परैश्चेत्यब्रवीद्ये चैव देवाः परे ये चावरे तानुभयानन्नाभजत्यजोषा देवैरवरैः परैश्चेत्याह ये चैव देवाः परे ये चावरे तानुभयानन्नाभजति ॥

> *te devā amanyantendro vā idam abhūd yad vayaṃ sma iti te [?] 'bruvan maghavann anno na ā bhajeti sajoṣā devair avaraiḥ paraiś cety abravīd ye caiva devāḥ pare ye cāvare tān ubhayān nābhajaty ajoṣā devair avaraiḥ paraiś cety āha ye caiva devāḥ pare ye cāvare tān ubhayān nābhajati ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-6-[?], as read "೬-೪-೬-೩" [?]; read from the image; doubtful in several words [?].) *Kannada sense:* The gods thought, "Indra has become what we were", and they asked, "O Maghavan, give us also a share in your sovereignty." "Let me be united with the lower and with the higher gods": he gave a share to both.

> अन्तर्यामो मघवन्मादयस्वेत्याह यज्ञो देवं यजमानं नान्तरेति ।

> *antaryāmo maghavan mādayasvety āha yajño devaṃ yajamānaṃ nāntareti |*

"O Maghavan, rejoice in the *antaryāma*" — thus the sacrificer, together with the gods, praises Indra; therefore the sacrifice and the sacrificer are not separated.

> प्राणापानौ वा एतौ यदुपाꣳश्वन्तर्यामौ व्यान उपाꣳशुसवनो यं कामयेत प्रमायुकः स्यादिति सꣳस्पृष्टौ तस्य सादयेद्व्यानेनैवास्य प्राणापानौ विच्छिनत्ति ताजक्प्र मीयते यं कामयेत सर्वमायुरियादिति सꣳस्पृष्टौ तस्य सादयेद्व्यानेनैवास्य प्राणापानौ सं तनोति सर्वमायुरेति ॥

> *prāṇāpānau vā etau yad upāṃśv antaryāmau vyāna upāṃśusavano yaṃ kāmayeta pramāyukaḥ syād iti saṃspṛṣṭau tasya sādayed vyānenaivāsya prāṇāpānau vicchinatti tājak pra mīyate yaṃ kāmayeta sarvam āyur iyād iti saṃspṛṣṭau tasya sādayed vyānenaivāsya prāṇāpānau saṃ tanoti sarvam āyur eti ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-6-[?], as read "೬-೪-೬-೪" [?]; read from the image [?].) The *upāṃśugraha* is *prāṇa*; the *antaryāma* is *apāna*; the *upāṃśu*-pressing is *vyāna*. If the sacrificer desires that someone should die early, he places the two [cups] separately, so that the *prāṇa* and *apāna* are not connected with each other; he then at once breaks the breaths with *vyāna*, and the man dies; and if he desires that someone should live his full length of life, he places the two together; by *vyāna* the *prāṇa* and *apāna* are joined, and he lives long. This is the greatness of the *upāṃśu*-pressing, the *upāṃśugraha* and the *antaryāmagraha* taken together.

### Printed p. 657  (PDF 678)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24–25 [as read].)*

***aindravāyavagrahaḥ*** *(Kannada heading "ಐಂದ್ರವಾಯವಗ್ರಹವು" — "The *aindravāyavagraha*").*

By the mantra *ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipāḥ*, the adhvaryu fills the vessel (*lohaka-pātra*) with juice, below the *indravāyava*-graha [?]. The greatness of this *graha* is told in this way:

> वाग्वा एषा यदैन्द्रवायवो यदैन्द्रवायवाग्राः ग्रहा गृह्यन्ते वाचमेवानु प्रयन्ति ।

> *vāg vā eṣā yad aindravāyavo yad aindravāyavāgrāḥ grahā gṛhyante vācam evānu prayanti |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-2-[?], as read "೬-೪-೭-೧" [?].) The *aindravāyava* [cup] is speech. By taking that vessel, one follows speech.

> वायुं देवा अब्रुवन्सोमꣳ राजानꣳ हनामेति सोऽब्रवीद्वरं वृणै मदग्रा एव वो ग्रहा गृह्यन्ता इति तस्मादैन्द्रवायवाग्राः ग्रहा गृह्यन्ते तमघ्नन् ।

> *vāyuṃ devā abruvan somaṃ rājānaṃ hanāmeti so 'bravīd varaṃ vṛṇai mad-agrā eva vo grahā gṛhyantā iti tasmād aindravāyavāgrāḥ grahā gṛhyante tam aghnan |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-2-[?], as read "೬-೪-೭-೧" [?].) When the gods said to Vāyu "Let us kill King Soma", he asked a boon: "Let my cup be taken first, with yours." Therefore all the cups are made ready together; then they killed King Soma. Sāyaṇa explains *abhiṣavaḥ somadevatāyāḥ hananam* — "the pressing is the killing of Soma, who is the deity".

> सोऽपूयत्तं देवा नोपाधृष्णुवन्सोऽब्रवीद्वरं वृणै मद्देवत्यैव वः पात्राण्युच्यन्ता इति तस्मान्ना देवत्यानि सन्ति वायव्यानि [?] उच्यन्ते तमेभ्यो वायुरेवास्वदयत्तस्माद्यः पूयति तत्र वाते वि षजन्ति वायुर्हि तस्य पवयिता स्वदयिता ।

> *so 'pūyat taṃ devā nopādhṛṣṇuvan so 'bravīd varaṃ vṛṇai mad-devatyaiva vaḥ pātrāṇy ucyantā iti tasmān nā devatyāni santi vāyavyāni [?] ucyante tam ebhyo vāyur evāsvadayat tasmād yaḥ pūyati tatra vāte vi ṣajanti vāyur hi tasya pavayitā svadayitā |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-2-[?], as read "೬-೪-೭-೧, ೨" [?]; read from the image, doubtful in places [?].) As soon as Soma was killed, Vāyu became foul-smelling. The gods could not bear his companionship, and said, "Make Soma agreeable [?] to us." Vāyu asked a boon: "Let all your vessels be made for me [as deity]." They agreed. At once the Soma-juice became tasty; therefore when any [food] is spoiled it is the Vāyu that purifies it and makes it taste good.

> तस्य विग्रहणं नाविन्दन्ताः [?] दितिरब्रवीदिन्द्रं वृणा अथ मया वि गृह्णीध्वं मद्देवत्या एव वः सोमाः सन्ना आसन्नित्युपयामगृहीतोऽसीत्याहादितिदेवत्येन यानि हि दारुमयाणि पात्राण्यस्यै तानि योनेः संभूतानि यानि मृन्मयानि साक्षादेव तान्यस्यै तस्मादेवमाह ।

> *tasya vigrahaṇaṃ nāvindan tāḥ [?] ditir abravīd indraṃ vṛṇā atha mayā vi gṛhṇīdhvaṃ mad-devatyā eva vaḥ somāḥ sannā āsann ity upayāmagṛhīto 'sīty āhāditidevatyena yāni hi dārumayāṇi pātrāṇy asyai tāni yoneḥ saṃbhūtāni yāni mṛnmayāni sākṣād eva tāny asyai tasmād evam āha |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-2-[?]-[?], as read "೬-೪-೭-೩-೩" [?]; doubtful in the opening words [?].) *Kannada sense:* They could not find a way to take [Soma] apart from [Vāyu]; Aditi said "choose Indra [as well]; take [the cups] through me, for your Somas are seated as mine"; with "*upayāmagṛhīto 'si*", [the mantra] is addressed to Aditi as deity; for the wooden vessels are born from her womb, and those of clay are directly hers: therefore it is so said.

### Printed p. 658  (PDF 679)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 135" [as read].)*

*(Kannada, continuing the Brāhmaṇa passage on Aditi, from p. 657:)* …the gods did not know the way to arrange the division of the Soma-share. Then Aditi [the Earth] said: "Take [the cups] through me; but your oblations must have Aditi as their deity." So she is the *yoni* (source) of the vessels that were made [in this way]; and those made of clay too are hers, because wooden vessels and the like come out of trees, which come from the earth; those made of clay are directly [the earth's]. Therefore the mantra *upayāmagṛhīto 'si* is recited, common to all the *graha*s.

> वाग्वै पराच्यव्याकृतावदत्ते देवा इन्द्रमब्रुवन्निमां नो वाचं व्याकुर्विति सोऽब्रवीद्वरं वृणै मह्यं चैवैष वायवे च सह गृह्याता इति तस्मादैन्द्रवायवः सह गृह्यते तामिन्द्रो मध्यतोऽवक्रम्य व्याकरोत्तस्मादियं व्याकृता वागुद्यते ।

> *vāg vai parācy avyākṛtāvadat te devā indram abruvann imāṃ no vācaṃ vyākurv iti so 'bravīd varaṃ vṛṇai mahyaṃ caiṣa vāyave ca saha gṛhyātā iti tasmād aindravāyavaḥ saha gṛhyate tām indro madhyato 'vakramya vyākarot tasmād iyaṃ vyākṛtā vāg udyate |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-7-[?], as read "೬-೪-೭-೩" [?]; read from the image [?].) *Kannada sense:* Speech, formerly, was undivided into words and the like, like the sound of the ocean. The gods went to Indra and begged him to divide it [into words] fit for use. Then Indra asked a boon: "this *graha* must be taken for me and for Vāyu together" [hence the name *aindravāyava*]; when the gods agreed, Indra entered the middle of speech and made the division of words and so on, convenient for use.

> तस्मात्सकृदिन्द्राय मध्यतो गृह्यते द्विर्वायवे द्वौ हि स वराववृणीत ।

> *tasmāt sakṛd indrāya madhyato gṛhyate dvir vāyave dvau hi sa varāv avṛṇīta |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-7-[?], as read "೬-೪-೭-೩" [?].) Because Indra asked for one boon, the Soma-taking for Indra is once only; because Vāyu asked for two, there are two takings: once separately, with the mantra *ā vāyo bhūṣa*, and once together with Indra, with *indravāyū ime sutāḥ*. This is the praise of the taking of the *aindravāyava* [cup], found in the Sūkta before us.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *aha* — an *nipāta* in the sense of emphasis; the ādyudātta accent. *vahethe* — root *vaha prāpaṇe*; *laṭ*, second person dual [as printed]; as it follows a *tiṅanta*, *nighāta*. *madhvaḥ* — *jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanam*: *guṇa* and the like are optional; *yaṇ* comes. *āhutim* — root *hu dānādanayoḥ*; *striyāṃ ktin* (Pā. 3-3-94 [as read]) gives the suffix *ktin*; *tādau ca niti kṛty atiḥ* (Pā. 6-2-50 [as read]) gives the *gati* (*ā*) its own accent.

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24–25 [as read].)*

*(Grammar, continued.)* *upatiṣṭhanta* — root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; *upād devapūjā…* (Pā. 1-3-25 [as read]) gives the Ātmanepada, etc.; by Vedic usage *laṅ*; third person plural; by Vedic usage the *āgama* does not occur; since it is connected with *yat*, the *nighāta* does not occur; as the *lasārvadhātuka* is *anudātta* by the sūtra, the accent of the root remains; *tiṅ codāttavati* (Pā. 8-1-71 [as read]) gives the *gati* (*upa*) the *nighāta* [accent]. *jāyavaḥ* — root *ji jaye*; *kṛvāpājimisvadisādhyaśūbhya uṇ* (Uṇ. 1-1 [as read]) gives *uṇ*; because of it, *vṛddhi* [*guṇa*] of the final *i* of the root; *āy*-substitution; the suffix's accent. *asme* — *supāṃ sulug…* (Pā. 7-1-39 [as read]) gives *śe* for the case-ending. *suvate* — root *ṣūṅ prasave* [as read: *ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane*]; *adādi*; *laṭ*, third person plural, the suffix *jha*; *ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ* (Pā. 7-1-5 [as read]) gives *at*; *ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* (Pā. 2-4-72 [as read]) gives *luk* of *śap*; *āti śnudhātubhruvāṃ…* [as read: *aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau* (Pā. 6-4-77 [as read])] gives *uvaṅ*; since it is *jit* [?], and by *tāsyanudāttenṅidvidupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam*, the accent of the root remains. *pacyate* — root *ḍupacaṣ pāke*; in the *karmakartṛ*, *karmavat karmaṇā tulyakriyaḥ* (Pā. 3-1-87 [as read]) gives *yak* [of the passive], the Ātmanepada, etc., because of the *karmavadbhāva*; since it follows a *tiṅanta* [?], there is no *nighāta*; as before, the root's accent remains. *yavaḥ* — the singular, as the purport concerns the genus. *dasyanti* — root *dasu upakṣaye*; *divādi*; *laṭ*, third person plural; *nighāta* after a *tiṅanta*. *dhenavaḥ* — root *dheṭ pāne*; *dhenuṭ icca* (Uṇ. 3-[?], as read "೩-೩೩" [?]) gives the suffix *nu*; *i* is the final-replacement; since the suffix is the cause, *guṇa*; by the suffix accent, the final udātta. ‖ 8 ‖

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Ṛk 9; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].)*

> हे सु वायो शोभनफलप्रद वायुदेव ते तव स्वभूता इमे पुरतो दृश्यमाना येऽश्वाः सन्ति ते नदी नदने द्यावापृथिव्यावन्तस्तयोरन्तराले त्वं त्वां पतयन्ति । पातयन्ति । गमयन्ति । यद्वा । ते तव संबन्धिनोऽश्वाः पतयन्ति । पतन्ति । यज्ञदेशं गच्छन्ति ॥ कीदृशास्ते । बाह्वोजसो बाहुषु प्रकृष्टबलवन्तः । उपलक्षणमेतत् सर्वाङ्गबला इत्यर्थः । किंचोक्षणः सेक्तारः । युवान इत्यर्थः । महि महदतिप्रभूतं व्राधन्तो वर्धमानाः । कथमुक्षण उक्षाणः । तत्सदृशा इत्यर्थः ॥ वा पपूर्वस्य निगम इति दीर्घाभावः ॥ किंच धन्वन् चित् धन्वन्युदकनिर्गमनापादनभूतेऽन्तरिक्षेऽपि निरालम्बेऽनाशवो नाशरहिता अव्याप्ता वा । आकाशे विलम्बमकुर्वाणा इत्यर्थः । अत एव जीराश्चित् जिच्चब्द [?] पूजायाम् [?] । अत्यन्तं क्षिप्रगतयः । यद्वा । अनाशव इत्यनेन सह समुच्चयार्थश्चित् । चित् जीराः । आकाशमार्गेऽक्षीणाः शीघ्रगता यशः [?] इत्यर्थः । किंचागिरौकसः गिरा ओकः स्थानम् [?] । येषां नास्ति ते [?] तापवशाः [?] । भर्त्सनादिना स्थितिमलभमानाः इत्यर्थः ॥ छान्दसस्त्रीतीयाया आलुक् ॥ तदेव स्पष्टयति । सूर्यस्य रश्मय इव दुर्नियन्तवो दुःखेन नियन्तव्याः । ते यथा क्षणेन दश दिशो व्याप्नुवन्ति बहवश्च तद्वदेतेऽपीत्यर्थः । पूर्वं गिरा निग्राह्यत्वमुक्तम् । इदानीं हस्तेनापि निग्राह्यत्वमाह । हस्तयोर्दुर्नियन्तवः उभाभ्यामपि हस्ताभ्यां दुःखेन नियन्तव्याः । देवयजनगमनाय शीघ्रगामिन इत्यर्थः ॥

> *he su vāyo śobhanaphalaprada vāyudeva te tava svabhūtā ime purato dṛśyamānā ye 'śvāḥ santi te nadī nadane dyāvāpṛthivyāvantastayorantarāle tvaṃ tvāṃ patayanti | pātayanti | gamayanti | yadvā | te tava saṃbandhino 'śvāḥ patayanti | patanti | yajñadeśaṃ gacchanti ‖ kīdṛśāste | bāhvojaso bāhuṣu prakṛṣṭabalavantaḥ | upalakṣaṇametat sarvāṅgabalā ityarthaḥ | kiṃcokṣaṇaḥ sektāraḥ | yuvāna ityarthaḥ | mahi mahadatiprabhūtaṃ vrādhanto vardhamānāḥ | kathamukṣaṇa ukṣāṇaḥ | tatsadṛśā ityarthaḥ ‖ vā papūrvasya nigama iti dīrghābhāvaḥ ‖ kiṃca dhanvan cit dhanvanyudakanirgamanāpādanabhūte 'ntarikṣe 'pi nirālambe 'nāśavo nāśarahitā avyāptā vā | ākāśe vilambamakurvāṇā ityarthaḥ | ata eva jīrāścit jiccabda [?] pūjāyām [?] | atyantaṃ kṣipragatayaḥ | yadvā | anāśava ityanena saha samuccayārthaścit | cit jīrāḥ | ākāśamārge 'kṣīṇāḥ śīghragatā yaśaḥ [?] ityarthaḥ | kiṃcāgiraukasaḥ girā okaḥ sthānam [?] | yeṣāṃ nāsti te [?] tāpavaśāḥ [?] | bhartsanādinā sthitimalabhamānāḥ ityarthaḥ ‖ chāndasastrītīyāyā āluk ‖ tadeva spaṣṭayati | sūryasya raśmaya iva durniyantavo duḥkhena niyantavyāḥ | te yathā kṣaṇena daśa diśo vyāpnuvanti bahavaśca tadvadete 'pītyarthaḥ | pūrvaṃ girā nigrāhyatvamuktam | idānīṃ hastenāpi nigrāhyatvamāha | hastayordurniyantavaḥ ubhābhyāmapi hastābhyāṃ duḥkhena niyantavyāḥ | devayajanagamanāya śīghragāmina ityarthaḥ ‖*

*(Sense: "O Vāyu, giver of good fruit, these horses of yours that are seen before us, in the space between the two *nadī*s — the two roarers, heaven and earth — carry you (*patayanti*, make you go; or: your horses fly, go to the place of the sacrifice). Of what kind? *Bāhvojasaḥ* — strong in the arms; this indicates strength in all limbs. *Ukṣaṇaḥ* — sprinklers, i.e. young [like bulls]; *mahi vrādhantaḥ* — growing greatly, like bulls. [The lengthening does not occur, *vā papūrvasya nigame*.] And further *dhanvan cit* — even in the *dhanvan*, the empty *antarikṣa* where rain comes out — *anāśavaḥ* — not lost, not lingering in space; therefore *jīrāḥ cit* — very swift; or with *anāśavaḥ* the particle *cit* is conjunctive; *agiraukasaḥ* — those that have no *gir* (revilement) as their residence [?] — not detained by reviling and the like [?]. [The Vedic *ālug* of the instrumental.] This is clarified: *sūryasyeva raśmayaḥ durniyantavaḥ* — hard to hold, like the rays of the sun, which in a moment pervade the ten directions, and many; so these too. Previously it was said that they cannot be checked by voice; now by hand also: *hastayor durniyantavaḥ* — hard to restrain with both hands; they are swift in going to the sacrificial place." Several words of the middle are doubtful [?].)*

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24–25 [as read].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *he su vāyo* — O Vāyu, giver of good fruit; *te* — joined to you; *ime* — these (that are visible); *ye* — which horses (there are); *te* — those; *bāhvojasaḥ* — strong in the arms; *ukṣaṇaḥ* — young; *mahi* — greatly; *vrādhantaḥ* — growing; *ukṣaṇaḥ* — [like] bulls (the horses); *nadī* — of heaven and earth; *antaḥ* — in the middle region; *(tvām)* — you; *patayanti* — carry (to the place of sacrifice); *dhanvan cit* — in the empty sky also; *anāśavaḥ* — not lost; *(ataeva)* — therefore; *jīrāḥ cit* — very swift; *agiraukasaḥ* — they cannot be held by reviling and the like; *sūryasya* — of the Sun; *raśmayaḥ iva* — like the rays; *durniyantavaḥ* — hard to hold; *hastayoḥ* — with both hands; *durniyantavaḥ* — hard to hold.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O Vāyu, giver of good fruit, these horses before us, of yours, with strong limbs, young and growing, like bulls, carry you to our sacrifice in the space between heaven and earth; they are not lost in the empty sky, are very swift, and are not stopped by reviling and the like; like the rays of the sun they are hard to restrain, and hard to restrain with both hands, even though one holds the reins.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"These your horses, excellent Vayu, strong of limb, youthful and full of vigour, bear you through the space between heaven and earth: growing (are they) in bulk, and strong as oxen: they are not lost in the firmament, but hold on their speed, unretarded by reviling; difficult are they to be arrested as the beams of the sun; difficult are they to be arrested by force."* [The print continues on p. 662; only these lines appear on p. 661.]

### Printed p. 662  (PDF 683)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 135" [as read].)*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 9).**

Here, describing the strength of Vāyu's horses, [the ṛṣi] makes the invitation to come and drink Soma, mounted on such horses, whose carrying power is great. The words *ukṣaṇaḥ* and the like are epithets that describe the nature of the horses.

***ukṣaṇaḥ*** — this word is repeated. Though it is explained twice, the sense is one. The first time it is explained as *sektāraḥ* ("sprinklers") and *yuvānaḥ*: "young, having the ability to sprinkle [semen]" is the meaning, and it comes from the root *ukṣ*, which gives the meaning "to sprinkle". Probably the word is also an epithet of the deities who bestow the desired objects on their devotees. The author of the Nirukta placed the word *ukṣan* among the names of *mahat* ("great") (Ni. 3-[?], as read "೩-೧೪" [?]). And:

> घृतसक्त्र [?] इन्द्र उक्षणः प्रियं काचित्करं हविर्विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ॥

> *ghṛtasaktra [?] indra ukṣaṇaḥ priyaṃ kācitkaraṃ havir viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೮೬-೧೫" [?]; the quotation is doubtful in the first words [?].) Quoting this Ṛk, in explaining the word *ukṣaṇaḥ* used there, [Yāska] says *ukṣaṇa ukṣateḥ vṛddhikarmaṇaḥ ukṣanty udakeneti vā* (Ni. 5-[?], as read "೫-೯೪" [?]) — "from the root *ukṣ*, which gives the sense of increase, or *ukṣanti* by water" — so in that context he gives the meaning "growth, as by water". Ordinarily the word is used only in contexts that show strength and capacity. In the sense of capacity to sprinkle, it has the same purport. As in the Ṛk under discussion,

> ते जज्ञिरे दिव ऋष्वास उक्षणो रुद्रस्य मर्या असुरा अरेपसः ।

> *te jajñire diva ṛṣvāsa ukṣaṇo rudrasya maryā asurā arepasaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೬೪-೨" [?].)

> शृण्वन्तमग्निं घृतपृष्ठमुक्षणं प्रणयन्तं देवं प्रणते सुवीर्यम् ।

> *śṛṇvantam agniṃ ghṛtapṛṣṭham ukṣaṇaṃ praṇayantaṃ devaṃ praṇate suvīryam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೧೩೩-೪" [?]; doubtful [?].) In Ṛks like these also, in the word *ukṣaṇa*, the sense is "sprinkling": since the sense relates to the power of sprinkling, Sāyaṇa explains it as *yuvānaḥ* ("young"). In the Ṛk under discussion, as well, he explains the first word as *yuvānaḥ* and the second as "like bulls that have the ability to sprinkle".

***vrādhantaḥ*** — *vardhamānāḥ*: "growing, increasing". The word *vrādhan* is among the names of *mahat* ("great"); it means "one who is excessively great". This epithet is used also as a synonym of an enemy who possesses abundant strength, a matter of praise. For example,

> स व्राधतो नहुषो दंसुजूतः शर्धस्तरो नरां गूर्तश्रवाः ।
> विश्वस्पराति [?] र्योति वाळ्हसृत्वा विश्वासु पृत्सु सदमिच्छूरः ॥

> *sa vrādhato nahuṣo daṃsujūtaḥ śardhastaro narāṃ gūrtaśravāḥ |*
> *viśvasparātir yoti vāḷhasṛtvā viśvāsu pṛtsu sadam ic chūraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೧೩೩-೧೦" [?]; the quotation is partly doubtful [?].)

### Printed p. 663  (PDF 684)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 24–25 [as read].)*

In this the meaning of the word is "violent, [even those who] cause harm": *himsakān mahataḥ api* — the sense of "enemies that are very strong". Likewise:

> शत्रूयन्तो अभि ये नस्तस्रे मह्ना व्राधन्त ओगणास इन्द्र ।
> अन्धेनामित्रास्तमसा सचन्तां सुज्योतिषो अक्तवस्ताँ अभि ष्युः ॥

> *śatrūyanto abhi ye nas tatsre mahnā vrādhanta ogaṇāsa indra |*
> *andhenāmitrās tamasā sacantāṃ sujyotiṣo aktavas tāṁ abhi ṣyuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೮೪-೧೫" [?]; the first line is doubtful in places [?].) Here too *vrādhantaḥ* means "*asmān bādhamānāḥ*": "those who harm us exceedingly". In the present Ṛk it is an epithet describing the horses' prowess and their growing, [increasing] valour.

***dhanvan cit*** — *dhanvani udakanirgamanāpādānabhūte 'ntarikṣe 'pi nirālambe*: "even in the empty sky, without support": the word *dhanva* is also among the names of *antarikṣa*: *ambaram, viyat, vyoma* and so on, in the list of *antarikṣa* names (Ni. 1-[?], as read "೧-೧೦" [?]). *Dhanvāntarikṣaṃ dhanvanty asmād āpaḥ* — "water runs from it; therefore it is called *dhanva*". The author of the Nirukta, citing:

> यः परस्याः परावतस्तिरो धन्वातिरोचते । स नः पर्षदति द्विषः ॥

> *yaḥ parasyāḥ parāvatas tiro dhanvātirocate | sa naḥ parṣad ati dviṣaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?], as read "೧೦-೬೨-೩" [?].) — has explained, in a sentence, the derivation of the word *dhanva*, as said above.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *bāhvojasaḥ* — *bāhuṣu ojo yeṣāṃ te*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. 6-2-1 [as read]) gives the earlier member its own accent; the *u* [of *bāhu*] becomes udātta; in place of the udātta, *yaṇ* comes, and the following [vowel] is *anudātta*; by *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya* (Pā. 8-2-4 [as read]) the *svarita* accent comes. *patayanti* — root *pata gatau*, *curādi*; by *satyāpapāśa…* (Pā. 3-1-25 [as read]) *ṇic* in its own sense; *aceḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau* (Pā. 1-1-57 [as read]) — since *ṇi*-lopa is *sthānivat*, the lengthening of the penultimate does not occur; *laṭ*, third person plural; since it is connected with *yat* [as read], there is no *nighāta*; the accent of *ṇic* remains. *ukṣaṇaḥ* — root *ukṣa secane*; *śvanukṣan…* (Uṇ. 1-[?], as read "೧-೧೫೭" [?]) gives *kanin* [as read: *kasi*]; the suffix's ādyudātta accent; since *jas* follows, *vā ṣapūrvasya nigame* (Pā. 6-4-9 [as read]) — the lengthening of the penultimate does not occur.

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 136" [as read].)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 9, concluded.)* *vrādhantaḥ* — root *vṛdhu vṛddhau*; by *vyatyaya* *laṭ* with *śatṛ*; by Vedic usage the *ā* augment [for the vowel of the root]; as *mit* etc. follows, *yaṇ* [by the rule *ac*… for the final]; as the *lasārvadhātuka* is *anudātta*, the accent of the root remains; nominative plural. *dhanvan* — *supāṃ sulug…* (Pā. 7-1-39 [as read]) gives *luk* of the locative. *anāśavaḥ* — *na vidyate āśuḥ yeṣāṃ te*; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. 6-2-172 [as read]) gives the final udātta. *jīrāḥ* — root *ju gatau*, *sautra*; *jorīcī* (Uṇ. 2-[?], as read "೨-೨೫೮" [?]) gives the suffix *rak*; *īkāra* as the final-replacement of the root; by the suffix accent, the final udātta. *agiraukasaḥ* — *girā okaḥ sthānaṃ yeṣāṃ te girokasaḥ; na girokasaḥ agirokasaḥ*; by Vedic usage the *luk* of the instrumental does not occur; *tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…* (Pā. 6-2-2 [as read]) gives the *ñañ* its own accent. *durniyantavaḥ* — root *yamu uparame*; *kṛvāpā…* [as read: Uṇ. *tun*] gives the suffix *tun*; *m* of the root becomes anusvāra by *paravarṇa*; as the suffix is *nit*, the ādyudātta; as the prefix *dus* is *prādi* and a *samāsa*, the *kṛduttarapada-prakṛtisvara*. ‖ 9 ‖

Here ends the 135th Sūkta. *(Kannada closing line: "ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತೈದನೇ ಸೂಕ್ತ ಮುಗಿದುದು".)*

## Sūkta 136 — *pra su jyeṣṭham* (begins on printed p. 664; Anuvāka 20, third Sūkta)

**ನೂರ ಮೂವತ್ತಾರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Nūra mūvattāraneya sūktavu** (the one hundred and thirty-sixth Sūkta).

**॥ सूक्तभूमिका ॥ — Introduction (Sanskrit, small type; read from the image; doubtful letters [?]).**

> प्र सु ज्येष्ठमिति सप्तर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं । ऋषिश्चान्यस्मादिति परिभाषया पारुच्छेपः ऋषिः । आत्यष्टिश्छन्दः । ऊती देवानामित्यन्त्या त्रिष्टुप् । अत्र त्रिष्टुबन्तपरिभाषा नाश्रीयते सर्वमात्यष्टमिति विशेषपरिभाषया बाधितत्वात् । मित्रावरुणौ देवता । अन्त्ययोस्तु तन्मन्त्रलिङ्गोक्तदेवता । तथा चानुक्रान्तं । प्र सु सप्त मैत्रावरुणं त्र्यन्त्ये लिङ्गोक्तदेवते अन्त्या त्रिष्टुबिति । तुशब्दप्रयोगादिदमादिके द्वे सूक्ते मैत्रावरुणदेवताके ॥ विनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥

> *pra su jyeṣṭham iti saptarcaṃ tṛtīyaṃ sūktaṃ | ṛṣiś cānyasmād iti paribhāṣayā pārucchepaḥ ṛṣiḥ | ātyaṣṭiś chandaḥ | ūtī devānām ity antyā triṣṭup | atra triṣṭubantaparibhāṣā nāśrīyate sarvam ātyaṣṭam iti viśeṣaparibhāṣayā bādhitatvāt | mitrāvaruṇau devatā | antyayos tu tanmantraliṅgoktadevatā | tathā cānukrāntaṃ | pra su sapta maitrāvaruṇaṃ try antye liṅgoktadevate antyā triṣṭubiti | tuśabdaprayogād idam ādike dve sūkte maitrāvaruṇadevatāke ‖ viniyogo laiṅgikaḥ ‖*

**Kannada anuvāda (translated).** *Anuvāda* — This Sūkta *pra su jyeṣṭham* is the third Sūkta in the twentieth Anuvāka. It has seven ṛks. The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Paruccheṣa. The metre is Atyaṣṭi. The last Ṛk, *ūtī devānām*, is in the Triṣṭubh metre. [To say that the metre of this Sūkta is Atyaṣṭi:] here the general rule [*paribhāṣā*] "that which ends in a Triṣṭubh [is Triṣṭubh]" is not followed, since it is set aside by the special rule "all is Atyaṣṭi". The deities are Mitra and Varuṇa; for the last two ṛks [the deities are] those stated by the signs of the mantras themselves. Thus says the Anukramaṇikā: "*pra su sapta maitrāvaruṇaṃ try antye liṅgoktadevate antyā triṣṭub*". Because of the use of the word *tu* [*pra su*, "su"?], both this Sūkta and the next [as printed: "the two Sūktas beginning from this"] have Mitra and Varuṇa as deities. The use is *laiṅgika*.

### Printed p. 665  (PDF 686)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 26 [as read].)*

*(The Kannada anuvāda, concluded:)* …as the word *tu* is used [in the Anukramaṇikā], this Sūkta is [of the deity] Mitra and Varuṇa [as is also] the next Sūkta. The use is *laiṅgika*.

**ಸೂಕ್ತ — Sūkta 136** [as read: "೧೩೬"]. Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 20; Sūkta 136. Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 26 [as read, [?]]. Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 7. Ṛṣi — Paruccheṣa Daivodāsi. Devatā — 1–5 Mitrāvaruṇau; 6–7 the deities named by the mantra's signs (*liṅgokta*). Chandas — 1–6 Atyaṣṭi; 7 Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्र सु ज्येष्ठं निचिराभ्यां बृहन्नमो हव्यं मतिं भरता मृळयद्भ्यां स्वादिष्ठं मृळयद्भ्याम् ।
> ता सम्राजा घृतासुती यज्ञेयज्ञ उपस्तुता ।
> अथैनोः क्षत्रं न कुतश्चनाधृषे देवत्वं नू चिदाधृषे ॥ १ ॥

> *pra su jyeṣṭhaṃ nicirābhyāṃ bṛhannamo havyaṃ matiṃ bharatā mṛḷayadbhyāṃ svādiṣṭhaṃ mṛḷayadbhyām |*
> *tā samrājā ghṛtāsutī yajñeyajña upastutā |*
> *athainoḥ kṣatraṃ na kutaścanādhṛṣe devatvaṃ nū cidādhṛṣe ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्र । सु । ज्येष्ठम् । निऽचिराभ्याम् । बृहत् । नमः । हव्यम् । मतिम् । भरत । मृळयत्ऽभ्याम् । स्वादिष्ठम् । मृळयत्ऽभ्याम् ।
> ता । सम्ऽराजा । घृतऽआसुती इति घृतऽआसुती । यज्ञेऽयज्ञे । उपऽस्तुता ।
> अथ । एनोः । क्षत्रम् । न । कुतः । चन । आऽधृषे । देवऽत्वम् । नु । चित् । आऽधृषे ॥ १ ॥

> *pra | su | jyeṣṭham | ni 'cirābhyām | bṛhat | namaḥ | havyam | matim | bharata | mṛḷayat 'bhyām | svādiṣṭham | mṛḷayat 'bhyām |*
> *tā | sam 'rājā | ghṛta 'āsutī iti ghṛta 'āsutī | yajñe 'yajñe | upa 'stutā |*
> *atha | enoḥ | kṣatram | na | kutaḥ | cana | ā 'dhṛṣe | deva 'tvam | nu | cit | ā 'dhṛṣe ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Ṛk 1; read from the image; doubtful words marked [?].)*

> हे ऋत्विजः मित्रावरुणाभ्यां ज्येष्ठं प्रशस्यं बृहन्महदतिप्रवृद्धं नमो नमस्कारोपलक्षितं स्तोत्रं तदुपलक्षितं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं वा प्र भरत । संपादयत । नम इत्यन्ननाम । नम आयुरिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । किंच हव्यं हव्यां [?] मतिं तत्तद्दानविषयां [?] बुद्धिं भरत । यद्वा । मतिं पूज्यं हव्यं हविर्भरत । पूर्वत्र पुरोडाशाद्यदनीयमन्नमिदानीं तु सोमाज्यादिरूपं निपेयं हविरिति विवेकः । कीदृशाभ्यां ताभ्याम् । निचिराभ्यां नितरां चिरकालाभ्याम् । नित्याभ्यामित्यर्थः । प्रवाहरूपेणेति भावः । किंच मृळयद्भ्यां स्तुत्या हविःस्वीकारेण स्वयं मृडितः [?] यजमानमपि सुखयद्भ्यां तथा स्वादिष्ठं स्वादुतरं मृळयद्भ्यां हविः सुखयद्भ्यां भक्षयद्भ्यामित्यर्थः । कस्मादेव [?] विशेष इति तत्राह । ता तौ मित्रावरुणौ सम्राजा सम्यग्राजमानौ ॥ राजतेः क्विप् । मो राजि समः क्वाविति सम्मकारस्य मकारः ॥ घृतासुती घृतमासूयते आदीयते याभ्यां तौ ताद्दशौ । यद्वा । घृतमुदकं वृष्टिलक्षणं प्रसूयते सर्वत्रानुज्ञायते याभ्यां तौ । एतयोरहोरात्राभिमानिदेवत्वादहोरात्रद्वारा वृष्ट्युत्पादकत्वात् । अहोरात्रे वै मित्रावरुणावहोरात्राभ्यां खलु वै पर्जन्यो वर्षति । तै. सं. २-१-७-४ [?] इति श्रुतेरेवं वृष्ट्यनुज्ञाप्रदत्वं प्रसिद्धम् । किंचैतौ यज्ञे यज्ञे सर्वेष्वपि यज्ञेषूपस्तुता सर्वैर्ऋत्विग्भिः स्तूयमानौ ॥ गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥ अथापि चैनोः [?] संज्ञापूर्वकस्य विधेरनित्यत्वादोषि [?] च । पा. ६-४-१०९ [?] इति गुणाभावे [?] तो गुण इति पररूपत्वम् ॥ क्षत्रं बलं कुतश्चन कस्मादपि च शत्रो राक्षसादेः सकाशात् कस्मादप्युपायोद्वा [?] नाधृषे अधर्षितुं शक्यं न भवति । कृत्यार्थे तवेकेनिति केन्प्रत्ययः ॥ किंच तयोर्देवत्वं नू चित् देवभावोऽपि नाधृषे अधर्षणायोग्यः । यद्वा । पूर्वमिवेदानीमपि । नू चिदिति निपातः पुराणनवयोरिति यास्केनोक्तत्वात् । नि. ३-१२ [?] । अधृषे न केनाप्याधर्षणीयो भवति । एतयोर्बलं नाधृष्यं किमु तद्देवत्वमिति भावः ॥

> *he ṛtvijaḥ mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ praśasyaṃ bṛhanmahadatipravṛddhaṃ namo namaskāropalakṣitaṃ stotraṃ tadupalakṣitaṃ havirlakṣaṇamannaṃ vā pra bharata | saṃpādayata | nama ityannanāma | nama āyuriti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | kiṃca havyaṃ havyāṃ [?] matiṃ tattaddānaviṣayāṃ [?] buddhiṃ bharata | yadvā | matiṃ pūjyaṃ havyaṃ havirbharata | pūrvatra puroḍāśādyadanīyamannamidānīṃ tu somājyādirūpaṃ nipeyaṃ haviriti vivekaḥ | kīdṛśābhyāṃ tābhyām | nicirābhyāṃ nitarāṃ cirakālābhyām | nityābhyāmityarthaḥ | pravāharūpeṇeti bhāvaḥ | kiṃca mṛḷayadbhyāṃ stutyā haviḥsvīkāreṇa svayaṃ mṛḍitaḥ [?] yajamānamapi sukhayadbhyāṃ tathā svādiṣṭhaṃ svādutaraṃ mṛḷayadbhyāṃ haviḥ sukhayadbhyāṃ bhakṣayadbhyāmityarthaḥ | kasmādeva [?] viśeṣa iti tatrāha | tā tau mitrāvaruṇau samrājā samyagrājamānau ‖ rājateḥ kvip | mo rāji samaḥ kvāviti sammakārasya makāraḥ ‖ ghṛtāsutī ghṛtamāsūyate ādīyate yābhyāṃ tau tāddaśau | yadvā | ghṛtamudakaṃ vṛṣṭilakṣaṇaṃ prasūyate sarvatrānujñāyate yābhyāṃ tau | etayorahorātrābhimānidevatvādahorātradvārā vṛṣṭyutpādakatvāt | ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇāvahorātrābhyāṃ khalu vai parjanyo varṣati | tai. saṃ. 2-1-7-4 [?] iti śruterevaṃ vṛṣṭyanujñāpradatvaṃ prasiddham | kiṃcaitau yajñe yajñe sarveṣvapi yajñeṣūpastutā sarvairṛtvigbhiḥ stūyamānau ‖ gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam ‖ athāpi cainoḥ [?] saṃjñāpūrvakasya vidheranityatvādoṣi [?] ca | pā. 6-4-109 [?] iti guṇābhāve [?] to guṇa iti pararūpatvam ‖ kṣatraṃ balaṃ kutaścana kasmādapi ca śatro rākṣasādeḥ sakāśāt kasmādapyupāyodvā [?] nādhṛṣe adharṣituṃ śakyaṃ na bhavati | kṛtyārthe tavekeniti kenpratyayaḥ ‖ kiṃca tayordevatvaṃ nū cit devabhāvo 'pi nādhṛṣe adharṣaṇāyogyaḥ | yadvā | pūrvamivedānīmapi | nū ciditi nipātaḥ purāṇanavayoriti yāskenoktatvāt | ni. 3-12 [?] | adhṛṣe na kenāpyādharṣaṇīyo bhavati | etayorbalaṃ nādhṛṣyaṃ kimu taddevatvamiti bhāvaḥ ‖*

*(Sense: "O priests, for Mitra and Varuṇa bring forth (*pra bharata*) *jyeṣṭham* — most praiseworthy, and *bṛhat* — great, much-grown, *namaḥ* — praise marked with reverence, or food in the form of oblation marked by it. *Namaḥ* is a name of food: [as in] *nama āyuḥ* in the Naighaṇṭuka lists of names. And bring *matim* — the thought directed to the giving of that [?]; or: bring the reverend oblation (*havya*). Formerly [in the foregoing Ṛks] the food was the cake to be eaten; now it is the oblation to be drunk, in the form of Soma and ghee. Of what kind are these two? *Nicirābhyām* — exceedingly long-lasting, eternal [as a stream]. And *mṛḷayadbhyām* — who by accepting the oblation themselves delighted [?] gladden the sacrificer too, and *svādiṣṭham* — the sweetest oblation [they eat with pleasure]. What is the special reason? *Tā* — those Mitra and Varuṇa, *samrājā* — shining well [*rājate*, *kvip*]; *ghṛtāsutī* — they from whom ghee is received; or from whom the *ghṛta*, water, the rain, is given: since the two are the deities of day and night, they give rain by day and night — as the Śruti says, *ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇāv ahorātrābhyāṃ khalu vai parjanyo varṣati* (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-7-4 [as read, [?]]). And they *yajñe-yajñe* — in every sacrifice — *upastutā* — are praised by all the priests. [Accent notes.] *Kṣatram* — their strength, from anywhere, from enemy or Rākṣasa, *nādhṛṣe* — cannot be overcome (*kena* suffix in the sense of *kṛtya*); further, their divinity *nū cid* — even now — cannot be overcome; or: as before, so now; *nū cit* is a *nipāta* in the sense of 'old and new' [Ni. 3-12 [?]]. Their strength cannot be overcome by anyone — what to say of their divinity." The grammar remarks are partly doubtful [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha.** *he ṛtvijaḥ* — O priests; *nicirābhyām* — [to the two who are] eternal (very ancient); *mṛḷayadbhyām* — who please the sacrificer (satisfied by acceptance of the oblation); *svādiṣṭham* — exceedingly tasty (oblation); *mṛḷayadbhyām* — and who eat (it); *tā* — to those Mitra and Varuṇa both; *su jyeṣṭham* — very praiseworthy; *bṛhat* — great (and the like); *namaḥ* — food [accompanied by reverence]; *pra bharata* — bring forth well (offer abundantly); *(kiṃca)* —

### Printed p. 667  (PDF 688)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 26 [as read].)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued:)* *(kiṃca)* — and; *havyam* — the worshipful; *matim* — [to them] the thought of giving [offerings]; or *[matim — worshipful; havyam — oblation (Soma, ghee, etc.)]*; *pra bharata* — offer; *tā* — those Mitra and Varuṇa both; *samrājā* — shining as sovereigns (emperors); *(kiṃca)* — and; *ghṛtāsutī* — givers of ghee (those who give water as rain); *(kiṃca)* — and; *yajñe-yajñe* — in every sacrifice; *upastutā* — praised (by the priests); *atha* — and; *enoḥ* — of these two; *kṣatram* — strength; *kutaḥ cana* — from anyone (from Rākṣasas or others, by any means); *na ādhṛṣe* — cannot be overcome; *devatvam nū cit* — their divinity also; *(na) ādhṛṣe* — cannot be overcome.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha.** O priests, offer, to Mitra and Varuṇa — the ancient (very old), who delight [the sacrificers] with the oblations — food [of the oblations] that is very sweet, abundant (and given with reverence) [the oblation], [they being] worshipful; offer them the worshipful oblations (ghee and the like): both of them are sovereigns (possessing great splendour), [they] are the givers of ghee (ghee is offered in the fire), by whose command we receive the water of the rain; they are praised in every sacrifice by the priests; they cannot be overcome by anyone (Rākṣasas and the like); likewise their divinity cannot be resisted.

**Printed English (heading "English Translation"; as printed):** *"Offer most excellent and ample adoration, and reverential oblation, to those two deities who have existed from of old; who confer happiness (on their worshippers), and delight in most sweet (libations); for they are both imperial (sovereigns, in whose honour) oblations of butter are poured out, and who are glorified at every sacrifice, whence their might is not in any way to be opposed; their divinity is not to be resisted."*

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Ṛk 1).**

At the time of offering the oblation to Mitra and Varuṇa, their special qualities are praised here. They are of the nature of giving joy to the sacrificer; by the means of rain and the like they give satisfaction to the sacrificers; their strength and divinity cannot be resisted.

***mṛḷayadbhyām*** — *stutyā havissvīkāreṇa svayaṃ mṛḍitvā yajamānam api sukhayadbhyām*: "to Mitra and Varuṇa, who themselves are delighted by accepting the oblation, and give happiness to the sacrificer". Explaining this word, the author of the Nirukta quotes two Ṛks and shows the meaning of the root of this word. First [the Kannada reproduces his quotation, to be read in the next page].

> क्षेत्रस्य पतिना वयं हितेनेव जयामसि । गामश्वं पोषयित्न्वा [?] स नो मृळातीदृशे ॥

> *kṣetrasya patinā vayaṃ hiteneva jayāmasi | gām aśvaṃ poṣayitnv ā [?] sa no mṛḷātīdṛśe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?], as read "೪-೫೭-೨" [?]; the second line is doubtful in several letters [?].) In this Ṛk, for the word *mṛḷāti* he explains [from Ni. 10-[?], as read "೧೦-೧೫" [?], *mṛḷatir dānakarmā*] "the root *mṛḷ* has the meaning 'to give'". "Rudra [also] is one who has a favourable mind in giving cows and the like", and —

> क्षेत्रस्य पते मधुमन्तमूर्मिं धेनुरिव पयो अस्मासु धुक्ष्व ।
> मधुश्चुतं घृतमिव सुपूतमृतस्य नः पतयो मृळयन्तु ॥

> *kṣetrasya pate madhumantam ūrmiṃ dhenur iva payo asmāsu dhukṣva |*
> *madhuścutaṃ ghṛtam iva supūtam ṛtasya naḥ patayo mṛḷayantu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?], as read "೪-೫೭-೩" [?].) — in this Ṛk, the word *mṛḷayantu* is explained, with the explanation that "it means *mṛḷayatiḥ pūjākarmā* [?], i.e. 'to show favour', 'to worship', 'to protect'" (Ni. 10-[?], as read "೧೦-೧೪" [?]). Sāyaṇa too explains it in the second quoted Ṛk as *mṛḷayantu prayacchantu | mṛḷayatir atra dānakarmā*, "let them give; *mṛḷayati* is here a verb of giving". Therefore the root meaning of *mṛḷ* is "to give, worship, protect; to be gracious", and as the result of that the sense of happiness (*sukha*) follows in order. In the present Ṛk it means: Mitra and Varuṇa give rain and the like and make the sacrificer happy.

***havyaṃ matim*** — two kinds of construction are made for this. The first: the word *havya* means "worshipful": "[bring] the worshipful thought [*mati*], the thought of giving to the gods"; and the second, the word *mati* meaning "worshipful": "bring the worshipful oblation".

***ghṛtāsutī*** — *ghṛtam udakaṃ vṛṣṭilakṣaṇaṃ prasūyate yābhyāṃ tau*: "those by whom the water in the form of rain is brought forth" is the meaning. The author of the Nirukta included the word *ghṛta* among the names of water. After that —

> ते आ ववृत्रन्नदनाद्वृतस्य [?] घृतेन पृथिवी व्युद्यते ।

> *te ā vavṛtrann adanād vṛtasya [?] ghṛtena pṛthivī vy udyate |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೧೬೪-೫೧" [?]; the quotation is doubtful [?].) — quoting this Ṛk he shows there the derivation: *ghṛtam ity udakanāma jigharter secanakarmaṇaḥ* (Ni. 7-[?]) — "from the root *ghṛ*, giving the sense of sprinkling". How Mitra and Varuṇa are the cause of rain, is described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa in this way:

> स यदि वृष्टिकामः स्यात् … मित्रावरुणौ त्वा वृष्ट्यावतामिति तद्यो वर्षिष्यन्भवति स त्वा वृष्ट्यावत्विति [?] एतदाहायं वै वर्षिष्यन्भवति योऽयं पवते सोऽयमेकैवेव पवते सोऽयं पुरुषे प्रविष्टः प्राङ्च प्रत्यङ्च तानिमौ प्राणोदानौ प्राणोदानौ वै मित्रावरुणौ तद्य एव वर्षिष्यन्भवति स त्वा वृष्ट्यावत्विति [?] तमेतेनैवाध्वरीते [?] यदा हैव कदा च वृष्टिः समिवा [?] ।

> *sa yadi vṛṣṭikāmaḥ syāt … mitrāvaruṇau tvā vṛṣṭyāvatām iti tad yo varṣiṣyan bhavati sa tvā vṛṣṭyāvatv iti [?] etad āhāyaṃ vai varṣiṣyan bhavati yo 'yaṃ pavate so 'yam ekaiveva pavate so 'yaṃ puruṣe praviṣṭaḥ prāṅ ca pratyaṅ ca tān imau prāṇodānau prāṇodānau vai mitrāvaruṇau tad ya eva varṣiṣyan bhavati sa tvā vṛṣṭyāvatv iti [?] tam etenaivādhvarīte [?] yadā haiva kadā ca vṛṣṭiḥ samivā [?] |*

### Printed p. 669  (PDF 690)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; odd page, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 1, Varga 26 [as read].)*

> … तमेवैतेनैवादीते [?] यदा हैव कदा च वृष्टिः समिवैतं तमनक्त्यार्द्रामेवैतत्कृत्वा [?] आहुतिर्भूत्वा देवलोकं गच्छादिति ॥

> *… tam evaitenaivādīte [?] yadā haiva kadā ca vṛṣṭiḥ samivaitaṃ tam anakty ārdrām evaitat kṛtvā [?] āhutir bhūtvā devalokaṃ gacchād iti ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 1-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೧-೮-೩-೧೩" [?]; this small-type passage is read from the image and is badly doubtful in the second half [?]; the sense is as the Kannada gives.) *Kannada sense:* In the *anuyāja*-section, in the *sūktavāka* and the like, this part is said in praise of Mitra and Varuṇa. He who desires rain should hold the *prastara* [bunch of *darbha*] reciting "*mitrāvaruṇau tvā vṛṣṭyāvatām*" ("may Mitra and Varuṇa protect you with rain"). The wind in the *antarikṣa* is the deity of rain. When this wind moves in the *antarikṣa* it is one form; when it enters man it takes two forms, *prāṇa* and *udāna*. Mitra and Varuṇa are these *prāṇa* and *udāna*; therefore he who wants rain should hold the *prastara* with the mantra "*sa tvā vṛṣṭyāvatu*" — thus the matter that Mitra and Varuṇa are the causes of rain is understood.

> आधारयतं पृथिवीमुत द्यां मित्रराजाना वरुणा महोभिः ।
> वर्धयतमोषधीः पिन्वतं गा अव वृष्टिं सृजतं जीरदानू ॥

> *ādhārayatam pṛthivīm uta dyāṃ mitrarājānā varuṇā mahobhiḥ |*
> *vardhayatam oṣadhīḥ pinvataṃ gā ava vṛṣṭiṃ sṛjataṃ jīradānū ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?], as read "೫-೬೩-೩" [?].) Mitra and Varuṇa, by their splendid power, produce rain, and thereby support heaven and earth; they make the plants grow: so, by many such Ṛks, the quality described may be known from the present Ṛk's epithet *ghṛtāsutī*. Sāyaṇa quotes the sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā:

> अहोरात्रे वै मित्रावरुणावहोरात्राभ्यां खलु वै पर्जन्यो वर्षति ।

> *ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇāv ahorātrābhyāṃ khalu vai parjanyo varṣati |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?]-[?], as read "೨-೧-೭-೩" [?].) and explains the epithet *ghṛtāsutī* by this statement that Parjanya gives rain through Mitra and Varuṇa, who are of the nature of day and night.

***enoḥ kṣatraṃ devatvaṃ na ādhṛṣe*** — "the power and divinity of these two, Mitra and Varuṇa, none can overcome": thus their greatness is described.

> या धर्तारा रजसो रोचनस्योतादित्या दिव्या पार्थिवस्य ।
> न वां देवा अमृता आ मिनन्ति व्रतानि मित्रावरुणा ध्रुवाणि ॥

> *yā dhartārā rajaso rocanasyotādityā divyā pārthivasya |*
> *na vāṃ devā amṛtā ā minanti vratāni mitrāvaruṇā dhruvāṇi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?], as read "೫-೬೯-೪" [?].) As the praise says in many places — that Mitra and Varuṇa, holding the heavens, the earth, the radiant [regions] and so on with their firm commands, cannot be opposed even by the immortal gods — that power is described here also.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar pages, noted briefly; numbers as printed).** *jyeṣṭham* — after the word *praśasya* in the sense of intensity the suffix *iṣṭhan*; *jyāc ca* (Pā. 5-3-61 [as read]) gives *jya* as the substitute for the stem; by *prakṛtyaikāc* (Pā. 6-4-163 [as read]) as an exception to the elision of *ṭi*, the stem-form remains; *guṇa*; since the suffix is *nit*, the ādyudātta. *namaḥ* — root *ṇamu prahvatve śabde ca*; Uṇ. suffix *asun*; since *nit*, the ādyudātta. *matim* — root *mana jñāne*; *mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ* (Pā. 3-3-96 [as read]) gives *ktin* the udātta. *bharata* — root *bhṛñ bharaṇe*; *loṭ*, second person plural, *ta* → *tāta*? [as read: *tādeśa*]; *śap* conditions the *guṇa* of the root's *ṛ*; as it follows a *tiṅanta* [?], *nighāta*. *mṛḷayadbhyām* — root *mṛḍa sukhane*; after the *ṇijanta* the suffix *śatṛ*; *śap* conditions the *guṇa* of *ṇic* and *ay* substitution; dative dual. *svādiṣṭham* — *atiśayena svādu*; *atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau* (Pā. 5-3-55 [as read]) gives *iṣṭhan*; *ṭeḥ* (Pā. 6-4-155 [as read]) drops *u* [of *svādu*]; the ādyudātta. *samrājā* — root *rājṛ dīptau*; the suffix *kvip*; as the root *rāj*, ending in *kvip*, is *para* [?], *mo rājisamaḥ kvau* (Pā. 8-3-25 [as read]) gives *m* for the *m* of *sam*; an exception to the anusvāra; as it is dual, *supāṃ sulug…* gives *ā*; *kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*. *ghṛtāsutī* — *ghṛtam āsūyate yābhyāṃ tau*; root *ṣuñ abhiṣave*; *ktin*; in the *bahuvrīhi*, the earlier member keeps its accent; dual. *yajñe-yajñe* — *nityavīpsayoḥ* (Pā. 8-1-4 [as read]) gives doubling; *anudāttaṃ ca* (Pā. 8-1-3 [as read]) makes the *pararūpa* [second] wholly *anudātta* [?]. *upastutā* — root *ṣṭuñ stutau*; *kta* in the passive; *gatir anantaraḥ* (Pā. 6-2-49 [as read]) gives the *gati* (*upa*) its own accent; as before, *ā* for the dual.

*(Grammar, concluded.)* *enoḥ* — *etad* + *os*; by the *paribhāṣā* "a rule preceded by a *saṃjñā* is non-eternal", *osi ca* (Pā. 6-3-[?], as read "೬-೩-೧೦೩" [?]) does not give *guṇa*; *ato guṇe* (Pā. 6-1-94 [as read]) gives the *pararūpa*; the *s* becomes *ruṭva*, *visarga*. *ādhṛṣe* — root *ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye*; since it has the sense of *śakya*, *kṛtyārthe tavaikenkeniṇtvanaḥ* (Pā. 3-4-14 [as read]) gives the suffix *kena*; as it is *kit*, the *laghūpadha-guṇa* does not occur; *kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvara*; since it ends in *e* [?], it is *avyaya*. *devatvam* — *tasya bhāvas tvatalau* (Pā. 5-1-119 [as read]) gives the suffix *tva* in the sense of state; by the suffix accent, the final udātta. *nu* — *ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām* (Pā. 6-3-133 [as read]) gives the lengthening in the Saṃhitā. ‖ 1 ‖

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अदर्शि गातुरुरवे वरीयसी पन्था ऋतस्य समयंस्त रश्मिभिश्चक्षुर्भगस्य रश्मिभिः ।
> द्युक्षं मित्रस्य सादनमर्यम्णो वरुणस्य च ।
> अथा दधाते बृहदुक्थ्यं वय उपस्तुत्यं बृहद्वयः ॥ २ ॥

> *adarśi gātururave varīyasī panthā ṛtasya samayaṃsta raśmibhiścakṣurbhagasya raśmibhiḥ |*
> *dyukṣaṃ mitrasya sādanamaryamṇo varuṇasya ca |*
> *athā dadhāte bṛhadukthyaṃ vaya upastutyaṃ bṛhadvayaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अदर्शि । गातुः । उरवे । वरीयसी । पन्थाः । ऋतस्य । सम् । अयंस्त । रश्मिऽभिः । चक्षुः । भगस्य । रश्मिऽभिः ।
> द्युऽक्षम् । मित्रस्य । सदनम् । अर्यम्णः । वरुणस्य । च ।
> अथ । दधाते इति । बृहत् । उक्थ्यम् । वयः । उपऽस्तुत्यम् । बृहत् । वयः ॥ २ ॥

> *adarśi | gātuḥ | urave | varīyasī | panthāḥ | ṛtasya | sam | ayaṃsta | raśmi 'bhiḥ | cakṣuḥ | bhagasya | raśmi 'bhiḥ |*
> *dyu 'kṣam | mitrasya | sadanam | aryamṇaḥ | varuṇasya | ca |*
> *atha | dadhāte iti | bṛhat | ukthyam | vayaḥ | upa 'stutyam | bṛhat | vayaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

### Printed p. 672  (PDF 693)
